### cypress-axe v1.7.0 Patterns (Cycle 19)

cypress-axe v1.7.0 (released August 2025) added the `retries` and `interval` options to
`cy.checkA11y()` to handle dynamically-loaded content that is not ready when the axe scan fires.

```typescript
// File: cypress/e2e/accessibility/dashboard.a11y.cy.ts
// cypress-axe v1.7.0 — retry pattern for dynamic content + Cypress 15 compatibility.
// Install: npm install -D axe-core cypress cypress-axe
// Add to cypress/support/e2e.ts: import 'cypress-axe';
// Add to tsconfig.json types: ["cypress", "cypress-axe"]

describe('Dashboard Accessibility — cypress-axe v1.7.0', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.visit('/dashboard');
    cy.injectAxe();  // Must be called after cy.visit()
  });

  it('dashboard has no WCAG 2.1 AA violations', () => {
    // Wait for the data table to be visible before scanning
    cy.get('[role="grid"]').should('be.visible');

    cy.checkA11y(
      undefined,  // context: undefined = scan entire document
      {
        runOnly: {
          type: 'tag',
          values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'],
        },
        // v1.7.0+: retry up to 3 times, 1500ms apart, for dynamic content
        retries: 3,
        interval: 1500,
      }
    );
  });

  it('modal dialog has no violations (scoped scan)', () => {
    cy.get('[data-testid="open-dialog"]').click();
    cy.get('[role="dialog"]').should('be.visible');

    // Scope the scan to the dialog only — exclude page violations outside it
    cy.checkA11y(
      '[role="dialog"]',  // context: scan only the dialog
      {
        runOnly: {
          type: 'tag',
          values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'],
        },
        includedImpacts: ['critical', 'serious'],  // Only fail on critical/serious in E2E
      }
    );
  });

  it('configures axe rules for the test suite', () => {
    cy.configureAxe({
      rules: [
        // Disable color-contrast in JSDOM-rendered components — Playwright handles contrast
        // In Cypress with a real browser, color-contrast IS computed — only disable if justified
        // { id: 'color-contrast', enabled: false },
        // Enable experimental WCAG 2.2 best-practice rules
        { id: 'target-size', enabled: true },
      ],
    });

    cy.checkA11y();
  });
});
```

**cypress-axe v1.7.0 TypeScript setup (`cypress/support/e2e.ts`):**

```typescript
// cypress/support/e2e.ts
import 'cypress-axe';

// Extend Cypress global types for IDE autocomplete
// If using @types/cypress and cypress-axe types together:
declare global {
  namespace Cypress {
    interface Chainable {
      // These are added by cypress-axe — included for clarity
      injectAxe(): Chainable<void>;
      configureAxe(config?: Record<string, unknown>): Chainable<void>;
      checkA11y(
        context?: string | Element | null,
        options?: Record<string, unknown>,
        violationCallback?: (violations: unknown[]) => void,
        skipFailures?: boolean
      ): Chainable<void>;
    }
  }
}
```

**cypress-axe vs @axe-core/playwright — decision guide:**

| Factor | cypress-axe | @axe-core/playwright |
|--------|-------------|----------------------|
| Existing test suite | Already uses Cypress | Already uses Playwright |
| Component-level scanning | Better with Cypress Component Testing | Use jest-axe for components |
| Retry for dynamic content | v1.7.0 native retry option | Use `expect().toPass()` wrapper |
| WCAG 2.2 AA tag support | `wcag22aa` (requires axe-core 4.10+) | `wcag22aa` (native) |
| CI performance | Cypress is slower to start than Playwright | Playwright faster cold-start |
| TypeScript support | Types via `cypress-axe` package | Full TypeScript native |

### WCAG 3.0 Working Draft — What Changes for Test Planning (Cycle 19)

The W3C WCAG 3.0 Working Draft (March 2026) represents a structural restructuring of
accessibility guidance. This section documents the current terminology and architecture so
QA teams can begin familiarising without being blocked by the draft's incomplete state.

**Key architectural changes from WCAG 2.x to WCAG 3.0:**

| WCAG 2.x concept | WCAG 3.0 equivalent | Notes |
|------------------|---------------------|-------|
| Success Criterion | Requirement | Testable condition within a Guideline |
| Guideline | Guideline | Retained but restructured as "outcome statements" |
| Conformance Level (A/AA/AAA) | Core / Extended | Core = most critical; Extended = comprehensive |
| Advisory Technique | Assertion + Method | Assertions are org-level attestations; Methods are tech-specific |
| Accessibility Supported | Technology Support | Requires formal definition of AT + browser support sets |

**Terminology the March 2026 draft finalised** (fixes previous Working Drafts):
- "Outcome" → **"Requirement"** — a testable condition with "applies when"/"except when" syntax
- "Foundational Requirement" → **"Core Requirement"** — the highest-priority subset for minimum conformance

**WCAG 3.0 timeline reality (May 2026):**
- Status: W3C Working Draft — not a Recommendation
- "Several years from completion" — per the March 2026 draft itself
- WCAG 2.2 remains the current standard for all legal compliance contexts (EAA, Section 508, AODA)
- No browser or AT vendor has announced WCAG 3.0 conformance roadmaps yet

**What QA teams should do now:**
1. Continue targeting WCAG 2.2 AA for all legal compliance requirements
2. Track WCAG 3.0 drafts but do not add WCAG 3.0 requirements to test suites yet
3. If writing test plan templates with "WCAG 3.0 Foundational Requirements" sections — update
   the terminology to "WCAG 3.0 Core Requirements" to match the March 2026 draft
4. The new "applies when"/"except when" test structure in WCAG 3.0 is useful as a model for
   writing test preconditions — even for WCAG 2.x test cases

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/wcag30-exploratory.spec.ts
// Exploratory WCAG 3.0 alignment tests — supplemental, not a compliance gate.
// These patterns map to WCAG 3.0 Requirements that are ALSO covered in WCAG 2.2.
// Run as informational — no CI gate until WCAG 3.0 is a W3C Recommendation.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

// WCAG 3.0 "Clear Words" Guideline → maps to WCAG 2.2 3.1.5 (AAA) + 3.1.3 (AAA)
// Not testable automatically — document reading level as a manual check note

// WCAG 3.0 "Text Alternatives" → maps to WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 (A) — fully automated via axe
test('WCAG 3.0 exploratory: text alternatives (maps to 1.1.1)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withRules(['image-alt', 'input-image-alt', 'area-alt', 'svg-img-alt'])
    .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
    .analyze();

  expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
});

// WCAG 3.0 "Pointer Accessible" Guideline → maps to WCAG 2.2 2.5.1-2.5.8
test('WCAG 3.0 exploratory: pointer accessible (maps to 2.5.x)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withRules(['target-size'])  // WCAG 2.5.8
    .withTags(['wcag22aa'])
    .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
    .analyze();

  // Log as informational — WCAG 3.0 alignment tracking
  console.log(`[WCAG 3.0 exploratory] Pointer accessible: ${results.violations.length} violations`);
  expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 19)

99. **[community] WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) is the most-commonly-missed new WCAG 2.2 AA criterion in design system component libraries**: Libraries built before 2022 frequently ship icon buttons with 16×16 or 20×20 bounding boxes because the pre-WCAG 2.2 guidance (WCAG 2.5.5, AAA, 44×44) was treated as optional. The new 2.5.8 AA minimum (24×24) is legally required under EU EAA (EN 301 549 v3.3.2). axe-core's `target-size` rule fires only when the spacing exception clearly does not apply — dense icon toolbars where buttons are 20×20 with 2px gap often pass the automated scan because the rule cannot compute circle intersections reliably. Add the Playwright geometry test from this cycle to catch these. WHY: legal risk under EAA for B2C apps serving EU markets; UX risk for all users on touchscreens where motor precision is naturally lower.

100. **[community] `autocomplete="off"` on login password fields is a WCAG 3.3.8 violation AND a UX anti-pattern that reduces conversion**: Some security-conscious teams set `autocomplete="off"` on password fields to prevent browser-stored credentials. This blocks password managers entirely, which are an "assistance mechanism" under WCAG 3.3.8. Password managers are more secure than remembered passwords — the EU EAA requires that users be allowed to use them. The correct security mitigations are: (1) `autocomplete="current-password"` on login forms (browsers and password managers respect this); (2) server-side rate limiting and MFA; (3) `autocomplete="new-password"` only on sign-up / password-change forms (this prevents autofill of old passwords, which is the correct security intent). WHY: WCAG 3.3.8 + EN 301 549 v3.3.2 are in force under EU EAA. Additionally, blocking autocomplete is on the OWASP ASVS v5.0 list of authentication anti-patterns.

101. **[community] Pa11y's HTMLCS engine detects `<th>` elements without `scope` or `id`/`headers` as WCAG 1.3.1 violations, but axe-core does not flag these if the table structure is otherwise valid**: axe-core's `scope-attr-valid` rule checks that existing `scope` attributes have valid values but does not require `scope` to be present on all `<th>` elements in complex tables. HTMLCS's `WCAG2AA.Principle1.Guideline1_3.1_3_1.H63.3` rule requires explicit `scope` on all `<th>` elements in tables with more than one row or column header level. This creates a gap: a table that passes axe-core CI gates but fails Pa11y HTMLCS may still have unclear header-to-cell associations for screen reader users. WHY: running axe-core alone is insufficient for verifying complex table accessibility — add either Pa11y HTMLCS or manual screen reader testing for data tables with multi-level headers.

102. **[community] IBM Equal Access's `accessibility-checker` reports "potentialviolation" items that are false positives in React + TypeScript projects due to JSX attribute serialisation**: The IBM rule `HAAC_Combobox_Level2` fires as a `potentialviolation` (not a hard violation) when a `role="combobox"` element's `aria-controls` attribute points to an element that is not in the DOM at scan time — which happens when the listbox is conditionally rendered (`{open && <ul>}`). This is not an accessibility defect (the ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern conditionally shows the listbox), but IBM's static analysis cannot distinguish lazy rendering from a missing element. WHY: filter `potentialviolation` items with IBM checker to only those with `level === 'violation'` in your CI gate, and address `potentialviolation` items in a separate manual triage step.

103. **[community] cypress-axe v1.7.0's `retries` option does not retry on passing scans — it only retries when violations are detected**: Teams implement the retry option expecting it to wait for dynamic content to appear before the first scan. That is not how it works. `retries: N` means: if the scan finds violations, wait `interval` ms and scan again — up to N times. If all violations disappear in a subsequent scan, the test passes. If violations persist after all retries, the test fails. For "wait for dynamic content" scenarios, use `cy.get('[role="grid"]').should('be.visible')` before `cy.checkA11y()` — this is the correct synchronisation approach. WHY: the retry option is for catching transient violations in content that changes (e.g., a spinner replaced by actual content), not for initial page load readiness.

104. **[community] Running `axe.run()` without `await page.waitForSelector('[role="main"]')` on server-side rendered Next.js pages with Suspense boundaries causes under-scanning**: With React Suspense, the initial server render includes placeholder `<Suspense>` fallback boundaries (often loading spinners with `aria-busy="true"`). The actual interactive content streams in after hydration. If axe scans before Suspense boundaries resolve, it misses the interactive content entirely and reports zero violations — even on pages with real violations. Always await the primary content boundary: `await expect(page.getByRole('main')).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-busy', 'true')` before `AxeBuilder.analyze()` on Next.js apps using Suspense. WHY: this is a silent failure mode — CI reports green while actual page content is unscanned. Increasingly common as Next.js App Router RSC adoption grows.

105. **[community] WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry is more widely applicable than the checkout example in W3C guidance — it applies to any multi-step wizard, onboarding flow, or settings wizard in SaaS apps**: Teams implementing product onboarding flows (step 1: company info, step 2: team members, step 3: billing — which asks for company name again) often fail 3.3.7 without realising it. The criterion covers any "series of user actions where each action is required in order to complete an activity" within a session — not just e-commerce checkout. Common SaaS failure points: (1) profile setup wizards that ask for full name on step 1 then ask for it again in a billing contact field on step 4; (2) support ticket forms that ask for email address even when the user is logged in with a known email. The simplest fix is to populate fields from session data and allow user overrides. WHY: under-reported category because most QA teams only run axe-core, which has no rule for 3.3.7 (it requires contextual multi-step session analysis that automated tools cannot perform).

### axe-core 4.11.4 (April 28, 2026) — `aria-labelledby` Hidden-Element Fix

axe-core 4.11.4 fixed the `aria-labelledby` accessible name computation to **exclude natively hidden elements** (those with `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, or `hidden` attribute). Previously, if an `aria-labelledby` reference pointed to an element that was hidden with `display:none`, axe would compute the accessible name successfully from the hidden text — masking a real failure. After 4.11.4, the accessible name falls back to empty if all referenced elements are hidden, which correctly triggers a violation.

**Impact on existing test suites:** Teams that used `aria-labelledby` pointing to visually-hidden (but display:none) elements as a workaround for accessible names will now see new `label` or `aria-label` violations after upgrading. The correct accessible name pattern for elements with invisible labels is `aria-labelledby` pointing to a `.sr-only`-classed span (which uses `position:absolute; clip:rect(0,0,0,0)` — visually hidden but NOT `display:none`).

```typescript
// File: src/components/Input/Input.a11y.test.tsx
// Tests for the aria-labelledby hidden-element fix in axe-core 4.11.4
import React from 'react';
import { render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { axe, toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

describe('aria-labelledby hidden element edge cases (axe-core 4.11.4+)', () => {

  // ✅ CORRECT: sr-only class uses clip/position, not display:none
  // axe-core 4.11.4 includes this in accessible name computation
  it('sr-only label (clip pattern) is counted by axe-core', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <div>
        <span
          id="hidden-label"
          style={{
            position: 'absolute',
            width: '1px',
            height: '1px',
            padding: '0',
            overflow: 'hidden',
            clip: 'rect(0,0,0,0)',
            whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
            border: '0',
          }}
        >
          Search
        </span>
        <input
          type="search"
          aria-labelledby="hidden-label"
        />
      </div>
    );
    const results = await axe(container);
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  // ❌ BROKEN after 4.11.4: display:none label is excluded from name computation
  // axe-core now reports a violation — this is the correct behavior
  it('display:none label is NOT counted — triggers violation in 4.11.4+', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <div>
        {/* display:none hides the element from the accessibility tree */}
        <span id="invisible-label" style={{ display: 'none' }}>
          Search
        </span>
        <input
          type="search"
          aria-labelledby="invisible-label"
          // No other accessible name — this is a genuine violation
        />
      </div>
    );
    const results = await axe(container);
    // 4.11.4+: this now correctly flags as a violation
    const hasLabelViolation = results.violations.some(
      (v) => v.id === 'label' || v.id === 'input-field-label-absent'
    );
    // Document the expected failure so reviewers understand what 4.11.4 changed
    expect(hasLabelViolation).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

**Migration checklist when upgrading to axe-core 4.11.4:**
1. Run your full test suite and look for new `label` or accessible-name violations
2. For each, check whether `aria-labelledby` targets a `display:none` element
3. Replace `display:none` hidden labels with `.sr-only` clip-pattern spans
4. Never use `hidden` attribute on an `aria-labelledby` target — it removes the element from the accessibility tree entirely

### Playwright v1.60 `getByRole()` with `description` Parameter

Playwright v1.60 added a `description` option to `getByRole()` that lets tests locate elements by their **accessible description** (the string exposed via `aria-describedby`, `aria-description`, or the element's title attribute) in addition to their accessible name.

This closes a gap where tests had to use complex attribute selectors to distinguish two buttons with the same label but different descriptions.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/getbyrole-description.spec.ts
// Playwright 1.60+: use description option to disambiguate same-name elements.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('getByRole with description (Playwright 1.60+)', () => {

  // Scenario: a data table with multiple "Edit" buttons, each described by row context
  test('can locate Edit button by its accessible description', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/users');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Without description: getByRole('button', { name: 'Edit' }) is ambiguous
    // With description: unambiguous — picks the Edit button described by "Alice"
    const editAliceButton = page.getByRole('button', {
      name: 'Edit',
      description: 'Alice Johnson',
    });

    await expect(editAliceButton).toBeVisible();
    await expect(editAliceButton).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Alice Johnson');
  });

  // Test for correct aria-describedby wiring in a form field
  test('password field is described by its hint text', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings/password');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // aria-describedby connects the hint text to the input
    const passwordField = page.getByRole('textbox', {
      name: 'New password',
      description: /must be at least 8 characters/i,
    });

    await expect(passwordField).toBeVisible();

    // Also verify the description element exists and is not hidden
    const hintText = page.locator('[id][aria-describedby]');
    // Accessible description should be exposed to AT
    await expect(passwordField).toHaveAccessibleDescription(
      /must be at least 8 characters/i
    );
  });

  // Verify the accessible description is correctly configured (no axe violations)
  test('form with aria-describedby has no axe violations', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings/password');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
      .analyze();

    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Why `description` in `getByRole()` matters for accessibility testing:**
- Enables testing the WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) requirement that supplemental instructions are programmatically associated with form controls
- Replaces brittle `aria-describedby` ID-chain assertions with semantic role-based queries
- Works with `aria-describedby` (space-separated list of IDs), `aria-description` (direct string), and `title` attribute (fallback description)

### ARIA APG Widget Keyboard Contracts — Playwright Test Patterns

The W3C ARIA Authoring Practices Guide defines precise keyboard contracts for common widget types. These contracts are not tested by axe-core (which only tests ARIA attribute syntax) — they require Playwright keyboard interaction tests. Below are TypeScript patterns for the three most commonly mis-implemented widgets.

#### Dialog (Modal) Keyboard Contract

Per ARIA APG dialog pattern: Tab/Shift+Tab cycle within the dialog, Escape closes it, and focus must return to the trigger element after close.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/dialog-keyboard.spec.ts
// ARIA APG dialog keyboard contract tests — not covered by axe-core structural scans.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Dialog (modal) ARIA keyboard contract', () => {

  test('Tab key cycles focus within the dialog', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Open the dialog
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /settings/i }).click();
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="dialog"]');

    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();

    // Tab through all focusable elements; verify focus stays inside the dialog
    const focusableSelector =
      'button, [href], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';

    // Get all focusable elements within the dialog
    const focusableCount = await dialog.locator(focusableSelector).count();
    expect(focusableCount).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    // Tab through all elements, then one more — should wrap back inside the dialog
    for (let i = 0; i <= focusableCount; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    }

    // Focus must still be inside the dialog (no escape to page background)
    const activeInsideDialog = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const dialog = document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]');
      return dialog?.contains(document.activeElement) ?? false;
    });
    expect(activeInsideDialog).toBe(true);
  });

  test('Escape closes the dialog', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /settings/i }).click();
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="dialog"]');

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');

    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).not.toBeVisible();
  });

  test('focus returns to trigger element after dialog closes', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    const triggerButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: /settings/i });
    await triggerButton.click();
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="dialog"]');

    // Close via Escape
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).not.toBeVisible();

    // Focus must return to the trigger — ARIA APG requirement
    await expect(triggerButton).toBeFocused();
  });

  // High-consequence action: focus the least destructive button
  test('confirmation dialog focuses Cancel (least destructive) on open', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /delete account/i }).click();
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="alertdialog"]');

    // ARIA APG guidance: for destructive actions, focus the least destructive element
    const cancelButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: /cancel/i });
    await expect(cancelButton).toBeFocused();
  });
});
```

> **[community] Dialog focus-on-open is the most commonly missed keyboard contract**: axe-core validates `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, and `aria-labelledby` but cannot detect whether focus moves INTO the dialog on open. If your modal opens without moving focus (the page background remains focused), keyboard and AT users are stranded. Always call `dialogElement.focus()` or focus the first focusable element programmatically when a dialog opens. WHY: without automatic focus, keyboard users must Tab through the entire page to reach the modal content, which may be many Tab stops away.

#### Tabs Keyboard Contract

Per ARIA APG tabs pattern: Tab moves focus into/out of the tablist; Arrow keys navigate between tabs; Space/Enter activates if not using automatic activation.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/tabs-keyboard.spec.ts
// ARIA APG tabs keyboard contract — Arrow key navigation is NOT tested by axe-core.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Tabs widget ARIA keyboard contract', () => {

  test('Tab key enters the tablist at the active tab', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products/details');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="tablist"]');

    // Tab into the tablist from the element before it
    // (assumes tablist is reachable from start of page via Tab)
    const tablist = page.getByRole('tablist');
    await tablist.focus(); // Simulate Tab into the tablist

    // Focus should land on the currently active tab (aria-selected="true")
    const activeTab = tablist.locator('[role="tab"][aria-selected="true"]');
    await expect(activeTab).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('ArrowRight navigates to the next tab without activating it (manual activation)', async ({
    page,
  }) => {
    await page.goto('/products/details');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="tablist"]');

    const firstTab = page.getByRole('tab').first();
    await firstTab.focus();

    // Arrow navigation — should move focus but NOT change active panel
    // if component uses manual (not automatic) activation
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');

    const secondTab = page.getByRole('tab').nth(1);
    await expect(secondTab).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('Space/Enter activates the focused tab', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products/details');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="tablist"]');

    const firstTab = page.getByRole('tab').first();
    await firstTab.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');

    // Activate with Space (manual activation mode)
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');

    const secondTab = page.getByRole('tab').nth(1);
    await expect(secondTab).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');

    // The corresponding panel should be visible
    const panelId = await secondTab.getAttribute('aria-controls');
    if (panelId) {
      await expect(page.locator(`#${panelId}`)).toBeVisible();
    }
  });

  test('Tab exits the tablist into the active tabpanel content', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products/details');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="tablist"]');

    const activeTab = page.getByRole('tab', { selected: true });
    await activeTab.focus();

    // Tab from the active tab should enter the tabpanel (not move to next tab)
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');

    // Focus should be in the tabpanel, not on another tab
    const activeTabpanel = page.getByRole('tabpanel');
    const focusInPanel = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const panel = document.querySelector('[role="tabpanel"]:not([hidden])');
      return panel?.contains(document.activeElement) ?? false;
    });
    expect(focusInPanel).toBe(true);
  });

  test('tabpanel with no focusable content has tabindex="0" (keyboard reachable)', async ({
    page,
  }) => {
    await page.goto('/products/details');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="tabpanel"]');

    const panels = page.getByRole('tabpanel');
    const panelCount = await panels.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < panelCount; i++) {
      const panel = panels.nth(i);
      const isHidden = await panel.isHidden();
      if (isHidden) continue;

      // Count focusable children
      const focusableCount = await panel
        .locator('button, a[href], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])')
        .count();

      if (focusableCount === 0) {
        // Per ARIA APG: tabpanel with no focusable content must have tabindex="0"
        await expect(panel).toHaveAttribute('tabindex', '0');
      }
    }
  });
});
```

#### Combobox Keyboard Contract (ARIA 1.2)

The ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern differs from ARIA 1.1: DOM focus stays on the combobox input, and `aria-activedescendant` tracks the focused option in the listbox. Arrow keys navigate options without moving DOM focus. This is a common source of implementation bugs that axe-core cannot detect.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/combobox-keyboard.spec.ts
// ARIA 1.2 combobox keyboard contract — aria-activedescendant pattern not checked by axe.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Combobox ARIA 1.2 keyboard contract', () => {

  test('focus remains on the input while ArrowDown navigates listbox options', async ({
    page,
  }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const combobox = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: /search/i });
    await combobox.click();

    // Type to trigger the listbox
    await combobox.fill('app');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="listbox"]');

    // Arrow down — should NOT move DOM focus into the listbox
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');

    // ARIA 1.2: DOM focus must STAY on the combobox
    await expect(combobox).toBeFocused();

    // The combobox input should now have aria-activedescendant pointing to an option
    const activedescendant = await combobox.getAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
    expect(activedescendant).not.toBeNull();
    expect(activedescendant!.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    // That option element must exist in the DOM
    const activeOption = page.locator(`[role="option"][id="${activedescendant}"]`);
    await expect(activeOption).toBeAttached();
  });

  test('Escape closes the listbox and returns to combobox (not cleared)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const combobox = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: /search/i });
    await combobox.fill('app');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="listbox"]');

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');

    // Listbox must close
    await expect(page.getByRole('listbox')).not.toBeVisible();

    // Focus returns to the combobox
    await expect(combobox).toBeFocused();

    // Typed value is preserved (Escape closes but does not clear)
    await expect(combobox).toHaveValue('app');
  });

  test('Enter selects the active option and closes the listbox', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const combobox = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: /search/i });
    await combobox.fill('app');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="listbox"]');

    // Navigate to first option
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');

    // Get the text of the active option before selecting
    const activedescendant = await combobox.getAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
    const optionText = await page
      .locator(`[role="option"][id="${activedescendant}"]`)
      .textContent();

    // Enter selects the option
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

    // Listbox closes
    await expect(page.getByRole('listbox')).not.toBeVisible();

    // Combobox value updates to selected option text
    if (optionText) {
      await expect(combobox).toHaveValue(optionText.trim());
    }
  });

  // ARIA 1.1 vs ARIA 1.2 migration guard
  test('combobox uses ARIA 1.2 pattern (input IS the combobox, not a child)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // ARIA 1.2: the <input> element has role="combobox" directly
    // ARIA 1.1 (deprecated): a <div role="combobox"> wraps the <input>
    const aria12Combobox = page.locator('input[role="combobox"]');
    const aria11Combobox = page.locator('[role="combobox"] input');

    const has12 = (await aria12Combobox.count()) > 0;
    const has11 = (await aria11Combobox.count()) > 0 && !has12;

    expect(
      has11,
      'Combobox uses deprecated ARIA 1.1 pattern (div[role=combobox] wrapping input). ' +
      'Migrate to ARIA 1.2 where the input itself has role="combobox". ' +
      'axe-core 4.4+ reports aria-required-children violations on ARIA 1.1 comboboxes.'
    ).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

### cypress-axe: TypeScript Integration Patterns and Retry Clarification

cypress-axe v1.7.0 (Cypress 15 compatible) provides `cy.checkA11y()` with built-in retry support. The retry mechanism is frequently misunderstood.

```typescript
// File: cypress/e2e/accessibility/full-page.cy.ts
// cypress-axe v1.7.0 TypeScript integration patterns.
// Requires: npm install cypress-axe --save-dev
// tsconfig.json: { "types": ["cypress", "cypress-axe"] }
// cypress/support/e2e.ts: import 'cypress-axe'

// CORRECT retry usage: retries only when violations ARE found
// Purpose: handle transient violations in dynamic content (spinner → content)
describe('Full-page accessibility with cypress-axe', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.visit('/dashboard');
    cy.injectAxe();
  });

  it('dashboard passes WCAG 2.1 AA with no violations', () => {
    // Wait for async content to render BEFORE calling checkA11y
    // (not what retries are for — retries are for transient violations, not initial load)
    cy.findByRole('main').should('be.visible');
    cy.findByRole('heading', { name: /dashboard/i }).should('be.visible');

    cy.checkA11y(
      undefined, // context: undefined = entire page
      {
        runOnly: {
          type: 'tag',
          values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'],
        },
        // retries: only retries when violations are detected (not for load waiting)
        // Use this when content transitions from loading state to loaded state
        retries: 3,
        interval: 500, // wait 500ms between retry scans
      },
      // Violation callback: log violations to CI output before failing
      (violations) => {
        violations.forEach((violation) => {
          const nodes = violation.nodes.map((n) => n.target.join(', ')).join('\n  ');
          cy.log(
            `[${violation.impact?.toUpperCase()}] ${violation.id}: ${violation.description}\n  ` +
            `Nodes: ${nodes}`
          );
        });
      }
    );
  });

  it('scans only critical and serious violations for fast smoke check', () => {
    cy.findByRole('main').should('be.visible');

    cy.checkA11y(
      undefined,
      {
        includedImpacts: ['critical', 'serious'],
        runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'] },
      }
    );
  });

  it('scans a specific component region only', () => {
    cy.findByRole('navigation').should('be.visible');

    // Context selector: scan only the navigation region
    cy.checkA11y('[role="navigation"]', {
      runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'] },
    });
  });

  it('configures custom rules via cy.configureAxe()', () => {
    // Disable color-contrast rule in Cypress (requires real browser rendering —
    // but Cypress runs in real Chromium, so color-contrast IS testable here)
    // Only disable if you have a documented exception approved by a11y team
    cy.configureAxe({
      rules: [
        {
          id: 'color-contrast',
          enabled: true, // Keep enabled in Cypress — real browser can compute contrast
        },
      ],
    });

    cy.checkA11y();
  });
});
```

**cypress-axe vs `@axe-core/playwright` decision matrix:**

| Criterion | cypress-axe | `@axe-core/playwright` |
|-----------|-------------|------------------------|
| Framework | Cypress | Playwright |
| TypeScript support | Via `cypress-axe` types | Native (AxeBuilder class) |
| Retry for dynamic content | `retries` + `interval` options | `expect().toPass()` wrapper or manual `page.waitFor*` |
| Component-level scan | Cypress Component Testing + `injectAxe()` | jest-axe (preferred) or Playwright component testing |
| CI performance | Slower cold start | Faster cold start |
| WCAG 2.2 AA support | `wcag22aa` tag (axe-core 4.10+) | `wcag22aa` tag (native) |
| Violation callback | Third arg to `checkA11y()` | Custom reporter + `testInfo.attach()` |
| Context selector | String CSS selector or locator | `AxeBuilder.include()` / `.exclude()` |

### Axe DevTools Enterprise: Intelligent Guided Testing (IGT) and axe MCP Server

The commercial Axe DevTools ecosystem adds two capabilities beyond open-source axe-core:

**1. Intelligent Guided Testing (IGT):** AI-assisted testing that asks contextual questions for issues automation cannot detect (e.g., "Is this image decorative or informational?"). IGT is reported by Deque to increase detection coverage beyond the ~57% axe-core baseline. IGT results integrate with the same violation schema and reporting pipeline as automated scans.

**2. Axe MCP Server:** A Model Context Protocol server (2025 addition) that exposes axe scanning directly to AI agents and IDEs. This enables Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and other AI coding assistants to run accessibility scans and receive structured violation data during code generation.

```typescript
// File: .claude/mcp-config.ts (illustrative — actual config is JSON)
// Axe MCP Server configuration for Claude Desktop / Claude Code.
// The @axe-core/mcp package provides an MCP server that wraps axe-core.
// Install: npm install -g @axe-core/mcp
// Claude Desktop settings.json:
//   {
//     "mcpServers": {
//       "axe-core": {
//         "command": "npx",
//         "args": ["-y", "@axe-core/mcp"]
//       }
//     }
//   }

// When connected, the axe MCP server exposes tools that Claude Code can invoke:
//   - axe_scan_url: scan a URL and return violations JSON
//   - axe_scan_html: scan an HTML string and return violations JSON
// Results use the standard AxeResults schema (same as AxeBuilder.analyze())
// and can be consumed by test generation or fix pipelines.

// TypeScript type for the MCP tool result (mirrors axe AxeResults):
interface AxeMcpViolation {
  id: string;
  impact: 'minor' | 'moderate' | 'serious' | 'critical';
  description: string;
  help: string;
  helpUrl: string;
  nodes: Array<{
    html: string;
    target: string[];
    failureSummary: string;
  }>;
}

// Example: an AI coding assistant using the axe MCP to check generated HTML
// during a component generation task — violations returned as structured data
// for the AI to include in its fix suggestion.
type AxeMcpScanResult = {
  violations: AxeMcpViolation[];
  passes: number;
  incomplete: number;
  inapplicable: number;
};
```

**When to use axe MCP vs `@axe-core/playwright`:**
- **axe MCP**: During AI-assisted development in Claude Code / Copilot; for scanning arbitrary URLs or HTML snippets without a test file; for real-time accessibility feedback during code generation
- **`@axe-core/playwright`**: For CI gates on user flows; for integrated test suites that run on every PR; for violation baseline management and trend reporting
- **Do not replace CI test gates with axe MCP**: The MCP server is for developer feedback during authoring, not a production quality gate. The `@axe-core/playwright` CI integration remains the authoritative accessibility gate.

### WCAG 2.2 Automated Testing Coverage Table

A practical reference showing which WCAG 2.2 success criteria are covered by axe-core vs require additional test methods:

| SC | Title | Level | axe-core auto | Playwright manual | Notes |
|----|-------|-------|--------------|-------------------|-------|
| 1.1.1 | Non-text Content | A | Yes (image-alt, etc.) | — | axe covers alt text |
| 1.3.1 | Info and Relationships | A | Partial | Yes | axe catches ARIA structure; heading order requires manual |
| 1.3.4 | Orientation | AA | No | Yes | Viewport rotation test |
| 1.3.5 | Identify Input Purpose | AA | Yes (autocomplete) | Supplement | axe `autocomplete-valid` rule |
| 1.4.3 | Contrast Minimum | AA | Partial (not JSDOM) | — | Real browser only; blocked in JSDOM |
| 1.4.10 | Reflow | AA | No | Yes | 320px viewport + scroll test |
| 1.4.11 | Non-text Contrast | AA | Yes | — | `color-contrast` rule covers UI components |
| 1.4.12 | Text Spacing | AA | No | Yes | CSS override injection test |
| 1.4.13 | Content on Hover/Focus | AA | Partial | Yes | axe checks dismissibility ARIA; manual for persistence |
| 2.1.1 | Keyboard | A | No | Yes | Keyboard-only navigation flow test |
| 2.1.2 | No Keyboard Trap | A | No | Yes | Tab/Shift+Tab cycle test in dialog |
| 2.4.3 | Focus Order | A | No | Yes | Tab sequence visual inspection |
| 2.4.7 | Focus Visible | AA | Partial | Yes | axe `focus-order-semantics`; CSS outline check |
| 2.4.11 | Focus Not Obscured (Min) | AA | No | Yes | `scroll-padding` CSS + visibility check |
| 2.5.3 | Label in Name | A | Yes | — | `label-content-name-mismatch` rule |
| 2.5.7 | Dragging Movements | AA | No | Yes | Single-pointer alternative verification |
| 2.5.8 | Target Size (Min) | AA | Partial | Yes | axe `target-size` rule; geometry test for dense toolbars |
| 3.1.1 | Language of Page | A | Yes | — | `html-has-lang` rule |
| 3.2.6 | Consistent Help | A (WCAG 2.2) | No | Yes | DOM order across pages |
| 3.3.1 | Error Identification | A | Partial | Yes | axe `aria-errormessage`; manual for error text quality |
| 3.3.2 | Labels or Instructions | A | Partial | Yes | axe `label`; placeholder-only fields require manual |
| 3.3.7 | Redundant Entry | A (WCAG 2.2) | No | Yes | Multi-step session flow test |
| 3.3.8 | Accessible Authentication | AA (WCAG 2.2) | No | Yes | CAPTCHA + autocomplete tests |
| 4.1.2 | Name, Role, Value | A | Yes | — | Core axe rules; most commonly failed SC |
| 4.1.3 | Status Messages | AA | Yes | — | `aria-live` and `role="alert"` rules |

**Reading the table:**
- "Yes" = axe-core has a rule that reliably detects violations of this SC
- "Partial" = axe-core helps but does not fully cover; supplement with manual/Playwright tests
- "No" = axe-core has no rule for this SC; Playwright test or manual review required
- The "Partial" + "No" rows are where the majority of missed violations occur in projects with axe-only CI gates

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 20)

106. **[community] Deque axe DevTools Enterprise free tier tests only one page at a time — teams using only the browser extension will miss cross-page regressions**: The free Axe DevTools browser extension scans the current page when you click "Analyze." It does not run programmatically across a site or as part of a CI pipeline. Teams who rely on extension-only scanning create a coverage gap for page transitions, multi-step flows, and new pages added after initial audit. WHY: axe-core's npm integration (`@axe-core/playwright`) is free and provides full CI coverage across all pages. The browser extension is a developer tool for investigation; it is not a quality gate. Never count the browser extension as a substitute for CI-integrated axe scanning.

107. **[community] AI-assisted Intelligent Guided Testing (IGT) is billed on a credit model in 2025+ — teams should budget credit consumption before adding IGT to CI pipelines**: Deque's IGT uses an AI-credit model for hosted instances. Unlike the open-source axe-core engine (unlimited runs), IGT calls consume credits per page scan. Running IGT on every PR across 100+ pages in a monorepo can exhaust monthly credits within days. Recommended practice: run axe-core automated scans on every PR (free, unlimited); run IGT only on critical user flows (checkout, login, key forms) on a scheduled basis (nightly or weekly). WHY: teams that move directly from "no accessibility testing" to "IGT on every test run" will hit budget issues before seeing the benefit. The correct adoption order is: axe automated → keyboard testing → IGT → screen reader testing.

108. **[community] `aria-activedescendant` must point to an element that is a DOM descendant of the composite widget OR is owned via `aria-owns` — pointing to elements outside the widget's subtree is an authoring error that NVDA and JAWS handle differently**: Some implementations of combobox or tree widgets render the owned popup in a portal (outside the DOM subtree of the combobox). ARIA 1.2 permits `aria-controls` to reference the popup by ID from outside the DOM tree, but `aria-activedescendant` must reference an element that is either a DOM descendant of the combobox OR linked via `aria-owns`. Without `aria-owns`, screen readers may not navigate to the active descendant correctly. axe-core does not always catch this because it checks that `aria-activedescendant` points to a real element — but not whether that element is in the ownership chain. WHY: NVDA (which checks DOM ancestry) and JAWS (which uses the accessibility tree) may both silently ignore an `aria-activedescendant` that is in a portal without `aria-owns`.

109. **[community] axe-core `color-contrast` rule in Cypress passes with a different threshold than in Playwright if the page uses CSS custom properties (CSS variables) for colors**: Cypress runs in a real Chromium browser (like Playwright), so color-contrast should be consistent — but there is a subtle difference: Cypress opens pages with Cypress's own CSS injection (the spec bridge iframe), which can slightly alter the computed styles in rare cases involving CSS custom properties defined in `:root` or CSS layers. The practical implication: if you see color-contrast discrepancies between your Playwright and Cypress axe scans on the same page, inspect whether the page uses CSS custom properties for colors and whether Cypress's injected styles are interfering. Always confirm contrast violations found by tools with the browser's DevTools computed color values. WHY: CSS custom properties are resolved at computed style time, and any CSS that redefines a custom property higher in the cascade will change what the color-contrast rule measures.

110. **[community] WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) is violated by sticky headers AND sticky footers — both patterns obscure the focused element below/above the viewport edge**: Most teams test for sticky header obscuring (scroll-padding-top fix) but miss sticky footer obscuring. A chat widget fixed to the bottom of the viewport, a cookie consent banner, a sticky "Save" button bar in a form, or a sticky bottom navigation bar can all obscure elements that receive focus via Shift+Tab. The CSS fix is symmetric: use `scroll-padding-bottom: <footer-height>` in addition to `scroll-padding-top`. Playwright verification: after tabbing to an element near the bottom of the page, use `locator.boundingBox()` and compare against the bottom sticky element's bounding box to verify no overlap. WHY: QA checklists often say "check sticky header" without mentioning sticky footer — bottom-fixed elements are equally capable of obscuring focused elements and are often added late in a project (chat widgets, consent banners) without revisiting focus visibility.

### axe.run() resultTypes Performance Optimisation — Deep Dive

The `resultTypes` option on `axe.run()` instructs the engine to skip collecting detailed node data for result categories you do not need. In large SPAs with hundreds of DOM nodes, this can cut analysis time by 40–60% because axe skips serializing element HTML, CSS selectors, and failure summaries for the excluded categories.

**Why this matters for CI pipelines:** The default `axe.run()` collects full data for all four result arrays (`violations`, `passes`, `incomplete`, `inapplicable`). For a CI gate that only needs to assert `violations.length === 0`, collecting `passes` and `inapplicable` is wasted work. Especially on pages with hundreds of images, form fields, or table cells that all *pass*, the serialisation cost dominates scan time.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/optimised-scan.spec.ts
// axe.run() with resultTypes: only collect violations + incomplete.
// Passes and inapplicable arrays will be present but empty — no serialisation cost.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('homepage: violations-only scan (fast CI gate)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // resultTypes limits which categories return full node data.
  // 'violations' is the gate; 'incomplete' surfaces uncertain items for manual triage.
  // 'passes' and 'inapplicable' are omitted — arrays exist but are empty.
  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
    .options({
      resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'],
    })
    .analyze();

  // Fail fast on any violation
  expect(
    results.violations,
    `${results.violations.length} axe violation(s): ${results.violations.map((v) => v.id).join(', ')}`
  ).toEqual([]);

  // Log incomplete items as warnings (require manual triage, not automatic failures)
  if (results.incomplete.length > 0) {
    console.warn(
      'Incomplete (manual review needed):',
      results.incomplete.map((r) => r.id).join(', ')
    );
  }
});
```

**Benchmark guidance (axe-core 4.11.x on a 200-node SPA page):**
| resultTypes | Typical scan time | Use case |
|-------------|-------------------|----------|
| default (all) | ~800 ms | Developer investigation, full audit |
| `['violations']` | ~320 ms | Strict CI gate — pass/fail only |
| `['violations', 'incomplete']` | ~380 ms | CI gate + triage queue |
| `['passes']` | ~700 ms | Audit of passing rules (rarely needed) |

> The numbers above are approximate and depend on page complexity. Profile your specific pages with and without `resultTypes` before committing to a threshold in CI configuration.

### WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) — Playwright Geometry Testing

WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (Level AA) requires interactive targets to be at least 24×24 CSS pixels, or to have sufficient spacing so that a 24px-diameter circle centred on each undersized target does not overlap adjacent targets. The **five exceptions** are: spacing offset, equivalent function, inline text, user-agent-controlled, and essential presentation.

axe-core's `target-size` rule detects clear failures (targets below 24×24 with no spacing buffer) but does not implement the full spacing-offset calculation. Use Playwright geometry assertions for precision:

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/target-size.spec.ts
// Validates WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) for interactive controls.
// Strategy: collect bounding boxes for all buttons/links, check 24×24 minimum
// OR verify the 24-px spacing offset between adjacent undersized targets.
import { test, expect, type Locator } from '@playwright/test';

interface TargetInfo {
  label: string;
  box: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number };
}

async function collectTargets(locator: Locator): Promise<TargetInfo[]> {
  const targets: TargetInfo[] = [];
  const count = await locator.count();
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const el = locator.nth(i);
    const box = await el.boundingBox();
    const label = (await el.getAttribute('aria-label')) ?? (await el.textContent()) ?? `target-${i}`;
    if (box) targets.push({ label: label.trim().slice(0, 40), box });
  }
  return targets;
}

/** Returns true if two targets' 24px-diameter spacing circles overlap. */
function spacingCirclesOverlap(a: TargetInfo, b: TargetInfo): boolean {
  // Circle centre = centre of bounding box
  const cx1 = a.box.x + a.box.width / 2;
  const cy1 = a.box.y + a.box.height / 2;
  const cx2 = b.box.x + b.box.width / 2;
  const cy2 = b.box.y + b.box.height / 2;
  const distance = Math.sqrt((cx2 - cx1) ** 2 + (cy2 - cy1) ** 2);
  // Two circles of radius 12 overlap when their centres are closer than 24px
  return distance < 24;
}

test.describe('WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)', () => {
  test('all interactive targets meet 24×24 or spacing-offset rule', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Collect buttons and links (exclude inline text links — they are exempt)
    const interactiveLocator = page.locator(
      'button:not([hidden]), a[href]:not([hidden]), [role="button"]:not([hidden])'
    );
    const targets = await collectTargets(interactiveLocator);

    const failures: string[] = [];

    for (let i = 0; i < targets.length; i++) {
      const t = targets[i];
      const meetsSize = t.box.width >= 24 && t.box.height >= 24;
      if (meetsSize) continue; // Passes primary criterion

      // Check spacing-offset exception: no adjacent target's circle overlaps
      const adjacentTargets = targets.filter((_, j) => j !== i);
      const hasOverlap = adjacentTargets.some((adj) => spacingCirclesOverlap(t, adj));

      if (hasOverlap) {
        failures.push(
          `"${t.label}": ${t.box.width.toFixed(0)}×${t.box.height.toFixed(0)}px — ` +
          `below 24×24 AND spacing circle overlaps adjacent target`
        );
      }
    }

    expect(failures, `Target size failures:\n${failures.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('icon-only toolbar buttons meet 24×24 minimum', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const toolbarButtons = page.locator('[role="toolbar"] button');
    const count = await toolbarButtons.count();

    if (count === 0) return; // No toolbar on this page

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const btn = toolbarButtons.nth(i);
      const box = await btn.boundingBox();
      expect(box?.width, `Toolbar button ${i} width`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(24);
      expect(box?.height, `Toolbar button ${i} height`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(24);
    }
  });
});
```

**Key testing notes for 2.5.8:**
- CSS pixel sizes do **not** change with page zoom — you cannot rely on users zooming in to meet this requirement
- Targets in overflow/dropdown menus are not assessed until visible — test them in their expanded state
- The `target-size` axe-core rule (added in 4.10.0) catches definitive failures but does not implement the spacing-offset algorithm above; Playwright geometry tests fill this gap
- Inline text links (e.g., "learn more" within a paragraph) are **exempt** — the line-height constraint makes 24px infeasible without breaking text flow

### WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication — Automated Testing Patterns

WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.8 (Level AA) prohibits cognitive function tests (memorisation, transcription, puzzles) in authentication flows unless an alternative path or assistance mechanism is provided. The most common failures are: blocking paste in password fields, using math/logic CAPTCHAs as the sole authentication path, and requiring OTP codes to be typed without allowing paste.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/accessible-auth.spec.ts
// WCAG 3.3.8: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
// Tests: paste is not blocked, autocomplete is present, CAPTCHA has an alternative path.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication', () => {
  test('login form: password field allows paste (autocomplete enabled)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const passwordInput = page.locator('input[type="password"]');
    await expect(passwordInput).toBeVisible();

    // 1. Verify autocomplete attribute is set (enables password managers)
    // Acceptable values: 'current-password', 'new-password'
    const autocomplete = await passwordInput.getAttribute('autocomplete');
    expect(
      autocomplete,
      'Password field must have autocomplete="current-password" or "new-password"'
    ).toMatch(/current-password|new-password/);

    // 2. Verify paste is not blocked (common anti-pattern: onpaste="return false")
    const pasteBlocked = await passwordInput.evaluate((el: HTMLInputElement) => {
      // Check for inline paste event handler that returns false
      const onpaste = el.getAttribute('onpaste');
      return onpaste !== null && onpaste.includes('return false');
    });
    expect(pasteBlocked, 'Password field must not block paste (violates WCAG 3.3.8)').toBe(false);

    // 3. Simulate clipboard paste and verify value is accepted
    await page.evaluate(() => {
      const pw = document.querySelector('input[type="password"]') as HTMLInputElement;
      if (pw) {
        const clipboardEvent = new ClipboardEvent('paste', {
          clipboardData: new DataTransfer(),
          bubbles: true,
        });
        (clipboardEvent.clipboardData as DataTransfer).setData('text/plain', 'TestPass123!');
        pw.dispatchEvent(clipboardEvent);
      }
    });
    // After paste event, the field should have accepted input (or at minimum not thrown)
    // This exercises the paste pathway without requiring actual clipboard access
  });

  test('email/username field has autocomplete attribute', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    const usernameField = page.locator('input[type="email"], input[name="username"], input[name="email"]').first();
    const autocomplete = await usernameField.getAttribute('autocomplete');
    expect(
      autocomplete,
      'Username/email field must have an autocomplete attribute for password manager support'
    ).toBeTruthy();
  });

  test('login page: no axe violations (catches aria-required, label, autocomplete-valid)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
      .withRules(['autocomplete-valid', 'label', 'label-content-name-mismatch'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('CAPTCHA: alternative authentication path exists (no cognitive-only gate)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    // If a CAPTCHA is present, verify there is a bypass or alternative
    const captchaPresent = await page.locator(
      '[class*="captcha"], [id*="captcha"], [title*="captcha" i], iframe[src*="recaptcha"]'
    ).count() > 0;

    if (captchaPresent) {
      // WCAG 3.3.8 AA allows object-recognition CAPTCHAs (click on images of X).
      // It does NOT allow text transcription / math CAPTCHAs without an alternative.
      // Verify a text-only alternative exists (e.g., email OTP, SMS, passkey)
      const hasAlternativeAuth = await page.locator(
        '[data-testid="email-otp"], [data-testid="passkey-button"], text="Use another method"'
      ).count() > 0;
      expect(
        hasAlternativeAuth,
        'CAPTCHA present but no alternative authentication path found — violates WCAG 3.3.8'
      ).toBe(true);
    }
  });
});
```

**3.3.8 compliance checklist for QA teams:**
- Password fields: `autocomplete="current-password"` on login, `autocomplete="new-password"` on registration
- Email/username fields: `autocomplete="username"` or `autocomplete="email"`
- OTP/verification code fields: `autocomplete="one-time-code"` — enables iOS Safari SMS auto-fill
- No `onpaste="return false"` or JS paste-blocking on any authentication field
- If reCAPTCHA v2 image challenge is used, provide an audio challenge as the WCAG-compliant alternative (audio CAPTCHA is object-recognition, not text transcription)
- reCAPTCHA v3 (invisible, score-based) has no user-facing cognitive test — it is 3.3.8-compliant by default

### Playwright locator.normalize() for Accessibility-First Test Authoring

Playwright 1.59 introduced `locator.normalize()`, which converts a locator that uses fragile CSS selectors or `data-testid` attributes into an equivalent locator that uses ARIA roles and accessible names wherever possible. This makes tests resilient to CSS refactors and simultaneously validates that elements have correct accessible names.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/locator-normalize.spec.ts
// locator.normalize() converts implementation-detail selectors to semantic locators.
// This dual-purposes each locator: tests the feature AND validates ARIA semantics.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Locator normalisation for semantic test authoring', () => {
  test('normalize() converts data-testid to role-based locators where possible', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Before normalize(): relies on data-testid — survives HTML changes but doesn't
    // validate ARIA. If the button loses its accessible name, the test still finds it.
    const btnById = page.locator('[data-testid="submit-button"]');

    // After normalize(): if the element has an accessible name, Playwright resolves it to
    // getByRole('button', { name: '...' }) — which FAILS if the accessible name is removed.
    // This makes the test a living accessibility check.
    const btnNormalized = await btnById.normalize();

    // Both locators should resolve to the same element
    await expect(btnById).toHaveCount(1);
    await expect(btnNormalized).toHaveCount(1);
    await expect(btnById).toHaveText(await btnNormalized.textContent() ?? '');
  });

  test('normalize() exposes missing accessible names as test failures', async ({ page }) => {
    // This pattern is used as an accessibility audit pattern:
    // If normalize() cannot resolve a role-based locator, the element likely
    // lacks a proper accessible name.
    await page.goto('/');

    const iconButtons = page.locator('button:has(svg):not(:has-text(""))');
    const count = await iconButtons.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const btn = iconButtons.nth(i);
      const normalizedLocator = await btn.normalize();
      // If normalize() still returns a CSS selector (not role-based), it means
      // the button has no accessible name that Playwright can use for role lookup.
      // This is a WCAG 4.1.2 violation — icon buttons must have aria-label.
      const locatorString = normalizedLocator.toString();
      expect(
        locatorString,
        `Icon button ${i} has no accessible name — add aria-label`
      ).toContain('getByRole');
    }
  });
});
```

**When `locator.normalize()` is NOT appropriate:**
- Components that intentionally use `role="presentation"` or `aria-hidden="true"` — normalize() cannot produce a role-based locator for these, and that is correct
- Complex composite widgets (grids, trees) where the accessible name is context-dependent — use explicit `getByRole()` with `{ name: ... }` instead
- Test files that need to test the *absence* of accessible names (negative tests) — normalize() is useful only when validating presence

### WCAG 3.0 Status Update — April/May 2026

WCAG 3.0 remains in **Working Draft** status as of May 2026. Key updates from the March–April 2026 drafts:

| Change | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Terminology pivot | "Foundational Requirements" renamed to "Core Requirements" in March 2026 draft |
| "Requirements" replaces "Outcomes" | Individual testable items are now "Requirements" within each guideline |
| Conformance model | Still under active development; "more flexible for organisations" than WCAG 2.x binary pass/fail |
| W3C timeline | AG WG projected a timeline in April 2026; final standard still "a few more years" away |
| Impact on WCAG 2.2 testing | **None** — WCAG 2.2 AA remains the current legal and technical standard; do not wait for 3.0 before implementing 2.2 |

**Practical guidance:** QA teams should treat WCAG 3.0 as informational. Target WCAG 2.2 AA as the compliance standard in CI gates for all new projects. WCAG 3.0 will likely not be required by law until several years after it reaches Recommendation status.

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 22)

111. **[community] `locator.drop()` in Playwright v1.60 can test WCAG 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures, but it requires a `sourcePosition` to be specified for drag-from-element tests — omitting it causes the drop to originate from the element centre and can silently skip the drag-start gesture**: WCAG 2.5.1 requires that all multi-point or path-based gestures have a single-pointer alternative. Testing the drag path itself (not just the drop target) requires simulating the full drag from a specific point. The `locator.drop()` API accepts `{ sourcePosition: { x, y } }` to specify where on the source element the drag begins. Omitting `sourcePosition` defaults to the element's bounding box centre, which works for most cases but will fail to detect draggable components whose drag-start zone is a small handle at the top of a card. WHY: Teams implementing WCAG 2.5.1 test coverage for drag-and-drop tend to test only that elements can be dropped onto targets, not that the drag gesture itself starts and tracks correctly. Testing the full drag path validates that `pointer-events` are not accidentally overridden on the drag handle.

112. **[community] `autocomplete="one-time-code"` on OTP input fields is a WCAG 3.3.8 compliance technique but is also a security concern if the OTP is reused — teams must implement short OTP expiry (≤ 5 minutes) to prevent attackers intercepting iOS SMS auto-fill**: Autocomplete attributes on OTP fields enable SMS auto-fill on iOS and reduce cognitive load for users, but this means the OTP is exposed in the iOS pasteboard. If the OTP has a long validity window (some systems allow 30–60 minutes), an attacker who gains access to the device has a larger window to exploit the auto-filled value. The accessibility fix (adding `autocomplete="one-time-code"`) and the security fix (short expiry) are orthogonal — QA must validate both: `autocomplete` attribute presence (accessibility CI gate) AND OTP expiry time (security test). WHY: Treating the autocomplete attribute as purely an accessibility concern leads teams to add it without revisiting the OTP lifetime security policy.

113. **[community] axe-core's `target-size` rule (for WCAG 2.5.8) does NOT implement the spacing-offset algorithm — it only flags targets smaller than 24×24 where it can determine with certainty that the spacing exception does not apply**: The axe-core documentation says the rule "checks that the size of the element's active pointer area is at least 24×24 CSS pixels." However, axe-core cannot always determine the visual positions of neighbouring elements from the accessibility tree alone. The rule will flag clear 24×24 failures (e.g., a 16×16 icon button in a form with plenty of space) but will miss cases where two 20×20 buttons are placed immediately adjacent without the required 24px spacing buffer. The Playwright geometry test pattern in this guide (using `locator.boundingBox()` and spacing circle overlap detection) fills this gap. WHY: Teams that add the `target-size` axe rule to their CI gate believe they have WCAG 2.5.8 coverage, but the partial rule coverage means dense toolbars and icon-heavy interfaces with tiny buttons adjacent to each other may slip through.

114. **[community] The WCAG 2.2 "spacing exception" for 2.5.8 Target Size is calculated from the *minimum bounding box* of the target, not the *activated hit area* — CSS padding extends the hit area but does not always extend the bounding box used for the spacing check**: CSS `padding` on a button extends the clickable area beyond the visible element boundaries. However, the 24×24 spacing check is based on the visual bounding box (the area occupied in the layout), not the hit area. A 12×12 icon inside a button with 6px padding on each side has a 24×24 hit area but a 24×24 visual bounding box only if the padding is included in `offsetWidth`/`offsetHeight`. In practice, browsers report `getBoundingClientRect()` as the full hit box including padding — so padding does help. The nuance: `margin` does NOT contribute to the bounding box for spacing purposes. Only padding (which is inside the border box) counts. WHY: Teams that use `margin` between icon buttons to create visual spacing often assume they are meeting the 2.5.8 spacing exception — but margin is outside the bounding box and does not count. Use `padding` to expand the hit area instead.

115. **[community] The Playwright `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` assertion (v1.50+) validates the `aria-errormessage` attribute but does NOT verify that the referenced error element is currently visible or in the DOM — a detached or hidden error element still passes the assertion**: `aria-errormessage` is a pointer attribute: it contains the `id` of an element that describes the error. `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` checks that the attribute exists and that its value matches the expected string. It does NOT check whether the referenced element is in the DOM, visible, or has `aria-live` configured. A component that sets `aria-errormessage="email-error"` before the `#email-error` element is injected into the DOM will pass this Playwright assertion while simultaneously failing WCAG 4.1.2 (the programmatic relationship exists but the description is inaccessible). WHY: Always pair `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` with a `toBeVisible()` check on the error element itself, and verify that the error element's `id` matches the `aria-errormessage` value. The axe-core `aria-errormessage` rule also checks ID validity — run both.

<!-- sources: WebFetch — axe-core releases (GitHub), WCAG 2.2 Techniques (W3C), Playwright release-notes + emulateMedia docs, Pa11y CI v4 (GitHub), Pa11y v9 README, jest-axe README, forced-colors MDN, ARIA APG combobox pattern, Guidepup README (GitHub), training knowledge for screen reader automation and community patterns -->

### Pattern 1 — Pa11y v9 Node.js 20/22/24 Migration + Dual-Runner Upgrade

Pa11y v9 dropped support for Node.js 18 (end-of-life April 2025) and now requires Node.js 20, 22, or 24. The bundled Puppeteer version was bumped to `^24`, which ships Chromium 124+. The `htmlcs` runner remains the default; the `axe` runner now bundles axe-core from the `@axe-core/puppeteer` package rather than a pinned static copy, so axe rule updates automatically propagate when you upgrade Pa11y. Teams running both runners in parallel get broader coverage: HTML_CodeSniffer catches structural HTML5 violations that axe skips; axe catches ARIA and WCAG 2.2 violations that htmlcs misses.

```typescript
// pa11y.config.ts — Pa11y v9 dual-runner pattern
import pa11y from 'pa11y';

interface Pa11yResult {
  pageUrl: string;
  documentTitle: string;
  issues: Array<{
    code: string;
    type: 'error' | 'warning' | 'notice';
    message: string;
    selector: string;
    context: string;
  }>;
}

async function auditPage(url: string): Promise<Pa11yResult> {
  // Run both runners and merge — axe catches WCAG 2.1/2.2 ARIA violations;
  // htmlcs catches structural HTML5 issues axe overlooks
  const [axeResults, htmlcsResults] = await Promise.all([
    pa11y(url, {
      runners: ['axe'],
      standard: 'WCAG2AA',
      // Pa11y v9 + Puppeteer 24: --no-sandbox required in Docker/CI
      chromeLaunchConfig: { args: ['--no-sandbox', '--disable-setuid-sandbox'] },
      timeout: 30_000,
    }),
    pa11y(url, {
      runners: ['htmlcs'],
      standard: 'WCAG2AA',
      chromeLaunchConfig: { args: ['--no-sandbox', '--disable-setuid-sandbox'] },
      timeout: 30_000,
    }),
  ]);

  // Deduplicate by selector + code (both runners may flag the same element)
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const merged: Pa11yResult['issues'] = [];
  for (const issue of [...axeResults.issues, ...htmlcsResults.issues]) {
    const key = `${issue.selector}::${issue.code}`;
    if (!seen.has(key)) {
      seen.add(key);
      merged.push(issue);
    }
  }

  return { ...axeResults, issues: merged };
}

// CI gate: fail on any errors (not warnings) above threshold
async function ciGate(urls: string[], threshold = 0): Promise<void> {
  for (const url of urls) {
    const result = await auditPage(url);
    const errors = result.issues.filter(i => i.type === 'error');
    if (errors.length > threshold) {
      console.error(`[FAIL] ${url}: ${errors.length} a11y errors`);
      errors.forEach(e => console.error(`  ${e.code}: ${e.message} (${e.selector})`));
      process.exit(2);
    }
  }
  console.log('[PASS] All URLs meet accessibility threshold');
}
```

**When NOT to use Pa11y's dual-runner mode**: When scan time is a bottleneck in CI and both runners' issue lists are stable — pick one runner and set a `threshold` baseline to capture net-new regressions only.

### Pattern 2 — Pa11y CI v4.1.1 Sitemap Testing with Per-URL Overrides

Pa11y CI v4 adds support for per-URL configuration overrides directly in the sitemap URL list, enabling different threshold values for legacy pages that have known, tracked violations without contaminating the zero-tolerance gate on new pages.

```typescript
// .pa11yci.json — Pa11y CI v4.1.1 configuration
{
  "defaults": {
    "standard": "WCAG2AA",
    "runners": ["axe", "htmlcs"],
    "timeout": 30000,
    "threshold": 0,
    "chromeLaunchConfig": {
      "args": ["--no-sandbox", "--disable-setuid-sandbox"]
    }
  },
  "urls": [
    "https://app.example.com/",
    "https://app.example.com/about",
    {
      "url": "https://app.example.com/legacy-dashboard",
      "threshold": 8,
      "runners": ["axe"],
      "ignore": [
        "WCAG2AA.Principle1.Guideline1_4.1_4_3.G18.Fail"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

```bash
# GitHub Actions step — Pa11y CI v4.1.1
- name: Run Pa11y CI
  run: |
    npm install -g pa11y-ci@4
    pa11y-ci --config .pa11yci.json --reporter json > pa11y-results.json
  continue-on-error: false

- name: Upload Pa11y results
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  if: always()
  with:
    name: pa11y-results
    path: pa11y-results.json
```

### Pattern 3 — Playwright `forced-colors` Emulation for Windows High Contrast Mode Testing

Windows High Contrast mode (now called "Contrast Themes" in Windows 11) forces all CSS color properties to system-defined color palette values — `box-shadow`, `text-shadow`, and `background-image` (non-url) are forced to `none`. Components that rely on shadows for visual indication (e.g., a focus ring implemented as `box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px blue`) become invisible to users in High Contrast mode. Playwright's `page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' })` enables automated regression testing.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/high-contrast.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Windows High Contrast mode compatibility', () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
    // Activate forced-colors emulation — simulates Windows High Contrast
    await page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' });
  });

  test('focus indicators remain visible without box-shadow', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const primaryButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' });
    await primaryButton.focus();

    // In forced-colors mode, box-shadow is forced to 'none'.
    // A compliant component MUST use border or outline instead.
    const outline = await primaryButton.evaluate(el =>
      window.getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue('outline-style')
    );
    const border = await primaryButton.evaluate(el =>
      window.getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue('border-style')
    );

    // At least one of outline or border must be non-'none' in forced-colors mode
    expect(
      outline !== 'none' || border !== 'none',
      'Focus indicator must use outline or border — box-shadow is suppressed in High Contrast mode (WCAG 2.4.7 + 2.4.11)'
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  test('icon-only buttons have visible text alternative in high contrast', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings');
    // SVG icons lose their fill color in forced-colors — aria-label is the fallback
    const iconButtons = page.getByRole('button').filter({ has: page.locator('svg') });
    const count = await iconButtons.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      await expect(iconButtons.nth(i)).toHaveAccessibleName(/.+/);
    }
  });

  test('custom checkboxes remain visually distinguishable', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/form');
    // Custom checkbox: background-image-based checkmark is suppressed in forced-colors.
    // The checked state must be conveyed via border change or content property.
    const checkbox = page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Accept terms' });
    await checkbox.check();
    await expect(checkbox).toBeChecked();
    // Verify the aria state is exposed — AT uses this in high contrast mode
    await expect(checkbox).toHaveAttribute('aria-checked', 'true');
  });
});
```

**Key rule**: ARIA roles do NOT inherit forced-colors system color semantics. A `<div role="button">` will NOT get `ButtonText` color automatically — only native `<button>` elements receive system semantic colors. Use native HTML elements where possible; add `forced-color-adjust: none` only as a last resort for components with deliberate color designs that must be preserved.

### Pattern 4 — Playwright `prefers-reduced-motion` Emulation

WCAG 2.3.3 (AAA) requires that animation triggered by interaction can be disabled. Even at AA level, carousels with auto-advance and loading skeletons with perpetual shimmer cause seizure and vestibular disorder issues. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is supported by all major browsers. Playwright can emulate this preference to verify that animations respect the system preference.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/reduced-motion.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('prefers-reduced-motion compliance', () => {
  test('loading skeleton does not animate with reduce preference', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    // Inject CSS to detect if animation is still running despite the preference
    const isAnimating = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const skeletons = document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="skeleton"]');
      return Array.from(skeletons).some(el => {
        const style = window.getComputedStyle(el);
        // animation-duration: 0s or animation: none means the developer respected the preference
        const duration = style.getPropertyValue('animation-duration');
        return duration !== '0s' && duration !== '' && duration !== 'initial';
      });
    });

    expect(
      isAnimating,
      'Skeleton loader must not animate when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is active'
    ).toBe(false);
  });

  test('page transitions do not run with reduce preference', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });

    // Navigate and measure time — animation-free transitions complete in < 100ms
    const start = Date.now();
    await page.goto('/about');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    const elapsed = Date.now() - start;

    // If the page normally has a 600ms transition, < 200ms means it was skipped
    // Adjust threshold to match your expected base page load time
    expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(1500); // reasonable upper bound without animation
  });
});
```
