### Pattern 5 — WCAG 2.2 Technique C43: `scroll-padding` for Focus Not Obscured (2.4.11)

WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 (AA) requires that when a keyboard-focused component scrolls into view, it is not entirely hidden by sticky headers or footers. The official technique is C43: use CSS `scroll-padding` on the scroll container to ensure the focused element is not scrolled behind the sticky element. Playwright can validate this geometrically.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/focus-not-obscured.spec.ts
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

async function getFocusedElementVisibility(page: Page): Promise<{
  fullyObscured: boolean;
  partiallyObscured: boolean;
  obscuringElement: string | null;
}> {
  return page.evaluate(() => {
    const focused = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;
    if (!focused) return { fullyObscured: false, partiallyObscured: false, obscuringElement: null };

    const focusedRect = focused.getBoundingClientRect();

    // Check all fixed/sticky positioned elements
    const stickyElements = Array.from(
      document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('*')
    ).filter(el => {
      const pos = window.getComputedStyle(el).position;
      return pos === 'fixed' || pos === 'sticky';
    });

    for (const sticky of stickyElements) {
      const stickyRect = sticky.getBoundingClientRect();
      // Detect full obscurement: focused element rect is entirely inside sticky rect
      const fullyObscured =
        focusedRect.top >= stickyRect.top &&
        focusedRect.bottom <= stickyRect.bottom &&
        focusedRect.left >= stickyRect.left &&
        focusedRect.right <= stickyRect.right;

      if (fullyObscured) {
        return { fullyObscured: true, partiallyObscured: true, obscuringElement: sticky.tagName };
      }
    }

    return { fullyObscured: false, partiallyObscured: false, obscuringElement: null };
  });
}

test('sticky nav does not fully obscure focused elements (WCAG 2.4.11)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/long-form-page');

  // Tab through all focusable elements, checking each one
  let iterations = 0;
  const maxIterations = 50;

  while (iterations < maxIterations) {
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    iterations++;

    const visibility = await getFocusedElementVisibility(page);
    expect(
      visibility.fullyObscured,
      `Focused element is fully obscured by ${visibility.obscuringElement} — add scroll-padding-top to fix (WCAG 2.4.11 C43)`
    ).toBe(false);

    // Stop when we cycle back to the first focusable element
    const focusedTag = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.tagName);
    if (iterations > 5 && focusedTag === 'BODY') break;
  }
});
```

**CSS fix pattern**: When this test fails, add `scroll-padding-top: <sticky-header-height>` to the `html` or scroll container element. This is technique C43 from the WCAG 2.2 Techniques document.

### Pattern 6 — WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging Movements: Single-Pointer Alternative Test

WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 (AA) requires that all functionality operated through dragging movements has a single-pointer alternative (e.g., a drag-to-reorder list must also support up/down buttons, or an Enter key that opens a reorder dialog). This differs from 2.5.1 (Pointer Gestures) in that 2.5.7 specifically targets drag motions, not multi-touch gestures.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/dragging-movements.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging Movements — single-pointer alternatives', () => {
  test('sortable list has keyboard reorder mechanism', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/tasks');

    // Verify a drag-based list has keyboard-accessible reordering
    const listItems = page.getByRole('listitem').filter({ hasText: /Task/ });
    const firstItem = listItems.first();

    // Focus the first item
    await firstItem.focus();

    // Check that the item announces drag-and-drop availability and keyboard alternative
    const ariaDescription = await firstItem.getAttribute('aria-description');
    expect(
      ariaDescription,
      'Draggable items must describe the keyboard alternative via aria-description (WCAG 2.5.7)'
    ).toMatch(/press.*space|press.*enter|use.*arrow/i);

    // Activate keyboard reorder with Space (common pattern: Space to grab, Arrow to move, Space to drop)
    await firstItem.press('Space');
    await expect(firstItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-grabbed', 'true');
    await firstItem.press('ArrowDown');
    await firstItem.press('Space');
    await expect(firstItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-grabbed', 'false');

    // Verify the item moved (now second in the list)
    const items = await page.getByRole('listitem').filter({ hasText: /Task/ }).all();
    const firstItemText = await items[0].textContent();
    expect(firstItemText).not.toBe(await firstItem.textContent());
  });

  test('range slider has text input or button alternative', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/filter');
    const slider = page.getByRole('slider', { name: 'Price range' });

    // Keyboard arrow-key operation is the minimum alternative to dragging
    await slider.focus();
    const initialValue = await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow');
    await slider.press('ArrowRight');
    const newValue = await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow');
    expect(Number(newValue)).toBeGreaterThan(Number(initialValue));
  });
});
```

### Pattern 7 — jest-axe `configureAxe` with `impactLevels` for Progressive Rollout

Teams adopting axe-core in large codebases often cannot fix all violations immediately. Using `impactLevels: ['critical', 'serious']` in `configureAxe()` allows teams to fail CI on critical and serious violations while tracking moderate and minor violations as non-blocking issues. This is a structured progressive-fix strategy.

```typescript
// test/setup/axe-config.ts
import { configureAxe } from 'jest-axe';

// Tier 1: Fail CI immediately — user-blocking violations
export const axeStrict = configureAxe({
  rules: {
    // Disable color contrast in jsdom — it always returns false positives
    'color-contrast': { enabled: false },
  },
  // Only fail on critical + serious; moderate/minor are tracked but non-blocking
  impactLevels: ['critical', 'serious'],
});

// Tier 2: Full audit — use in local pre-commit or nightly scans
export const axeExhaustive = configureAxe({
  rules: {
    'color-contrast': { enabled: false }, // still need real browser for contrast
  },
  // No impactLevels filter — all violations reported
});
```

```typescript
// LoginForm.test.tsx — using tiered axe config
import React from 'react';
import { render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';
import { axeStrict } from '../setup/axe-config';
import LoginForm from './LoginForm';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

test('LoginForm has no critical or serious accessibility violations', async () => {
  const { container } = render(<LoginForm />);
  // Run axe with real timers — jest-axe hangs with fake timers
  const results = await axeStrict(container);
  expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
});

test('form inputs have visible labels (not placeholder-only)', async () => {
  const { getByLabelText } = render(<LoginForm />);
  // If getByLabelText throws, there is no <label> or aria-label — WCAG 3.3.2 violation
  expect(() => getByLabelText('Email address')).not.toThrow();
  expect(() => getByLabelText('Password')).not.toThrow();
});
```

**[community] Gotcha**: `jest-axe` v10 is incompatible with Jest v30 due to Jest v30's new module resolution changes. If you upgrade Jest to v30, you must either pin `jest-axe` at v9.x or use `@axe-core/vitest` instead. The `@axe-core/vitest` package is the recommended path for new projects in 2026.

### Pattern 8 — `@axe-core/vitest` Integration

As of 2025, Deque provides a first-party Vitest integration package, `@axe-core/vitest`, that avoids the jest-axe compatibility issues with Jest v30. It uses the same `AxeBuilder`-style API and supports the same `configureAxe` options.

```typescript
// vitest.setup.ts
import { toHaveNoViolations } from '@axe-core/vitest';
import { expect } from 'vitest';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);
```

```typescript
// Button.test.tsx — @axe-core/vitest
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { axe } from '@axe-core/vitest';
import Button from './Button';

describe('Button accessibility', () => {
  it('has no accessibility violations in default state', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <Button onClick={() => {}}>Save changes</Button>
    );
    const results = await axe(container);
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('icon-only variant requires aria-label', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <Button icon="trash" aria-label="Delete item" onClick={() => {}} />
    );
    const results = await axe(container);
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('disabled button is not reachable via keyboard', async () => {
    const { getByRole } = render(
      <Button disabled onClick={() => {}}>Submit</Button>
    );
    const btn = getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' });
    // Disabled native buttons have tabIndex = -1 implicitly
    expect(btn).toHaveAttribute('disabled');
    expect(btn).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-disabled'); // native disabled is preferred
  });
});
```

### Pattern 9 — ARIA Combobox Keyboard Contract Test (APG Pattern)

The ARIA APG combobox pattern (the single most complex ARIA widget) has a strict keyboard contract. Any deviation from the contract breaks screen reader compatibility. This test suite validates the full contract.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/combobox-contract.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Combobox keyboard contract (APG)', () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
  });

  test('combobox has required ARIA attributes', async ({ page }) => {
    const combobox = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Search' });

    // ARIA 1.2 mandates: role=combobox, aria-expanded, aria-controls
    await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('role', 'combobox');
    await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-controls');
  });

  test('Down Arrow opens popup and moves focus into listbox', async ({ page }) => {
    const combobox = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Search' });
    await combobox.focus();
    await combobox.press('ArrowDown');

    await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    const listbox = page.getByRole('listbox');
    await expect(listbox).toBeVisible();
  });

  test('Escape closes popup and returns focus to combobox', async ({ page }) => {
    const combobox = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Search' });
    await combobox.focus();
    await combobox.press('ArrowDown');
    await combobox.press('Escape');

    await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    await expect(page.getByRole('listbox')).not.toBeVisible();
    await expect(combobox).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('Enter selects focused option and closes popup', async ({ page }) => {
    const combobox = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Search' });
    await combobox.focus();
    await combobox.fill('ja');
    await combobox.press('ArrowDown'); // opens listbox
    await combobox.press('ArrowDown'); // moves to first option
    await combobox.press('Enter');     // selects

    await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    // The selected value should populate the combobox input
    const value = await combobox.inputValue();
    expect(value.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('aria-activedescendant tracks focused option', async ({ page }) => {
    const combobox = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Search' });
    await combobox.focus();
    await combobox.fill('java');
    await combobox.press('ArrowDown'); // open
    await combobox.press('ArrowDown'); // focus first option

    // aria-activedescendant must point to the focused listbox option
    const activeDescendant = await combobox.getAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
    expect(activeDescendant).toBeTruthy();

    const activeOption = page.locator(`#${activeDescendant}`);
    await expect(activeOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
  });
});
```

### Pattern 10 — Guidepup: Automated VoiceOver / NVDA Screen Reader Testing

`@guidepup/playwright` integrates the Guidepup screen reader driver with Playwright to automate real VoiceOver (macOS) and NVDA (Windows) interactions. This allows teams to write tests that capture what a screen reader actually announces — catching issues that axe-core's static tree analysis misses, such as dynamic announcements, focus movement narration, and live region delays.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/screen-reader.spec.ts — requires @guidepup/playwright
// Run only on macOS CI runners (voiceOver) or Windows CI runners (nvda)
import { voTest as test, expect } from '@guidepup/playwright';

test.describe('VoiceOver screen reader integration', () => {
  test('error message is announced when form is submitted empty', async ({
    page,
    voiceOver,
  }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');

    // Submit the form without filling it in
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Send' }).click();

    // Wait for VoiceOver to announce the error
    // Guidepup captures spoken phrases via spokenPhraseLog()
    await expect(voiceOver.spokenPhraseLog()).resolves.toContainEqual(
      expect.stringMatching(/required|error|invalid/i)
    );
  });

  test('aria-live region announces cart update', async ({ page, voiceOver }) => {
    await page.goto('/shop/product/1');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).click();

    // The cart count live region should be announced automatically
    const phrases = await voiceOver.spokenPhraseLog();
    const announcedCartUpdate = phrases.some(p => /cart|item|added/i.test(p));
    expect(
      announcedCartUpdate,
      'Add to cart must trigger an aria-live announcement (WCAG 4.1.3)'
    ).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

**CI setup note**: Guidepup VoiceOver tests require a macOS GitHub Actions runner with VoiceOver enabled. Use `macos-14` (Apple Silicon) or `macos-13`. NVDA tests require a Windows runner with NVDA installed via Chocolatey: `choco install nvda`. Both runners cost significantly more than Linux — reserve screen reader automation tests for smoke suites or nightly runs rather than every PR.

### Pattern 11 — WCAG 2.2 Techniques for New Success Criteria: Automated Test Coverage Map

This table maps each WCAG 2.2 new success criterion to its official technique, what automated tools can detect, and what requires manual verification.

| SC | Name | Level | Official Techniques | Automated (axe/Pa11y) | Manual Required |
|----|------|-------|--------------------|-----------------------|-----------------|
| 2.4.11 | Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) | AA | C43 (scroll-padding), F110 (sticky header hides focus) | Partial — axe `scrollable-region-focusable` rule; geometry test from Pattern 5 | Verify scroll-padding value matches actual header height |
| 2.4.12 | Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced) | AAA | C43 | None in axe | Full manual — requires pixel-level focus indicator visibility check |
| 2.4.13 | Focus Appearance | AAA | — | None in axe | Full manual — focus area ≥ perimeter of focused component; contrast ≥ 3:1 |
| 2.5.7 | Dragging Movements | AA | G215, G219, F108 | None in axe | Verify single-pointer alternative exists for all drag functionality |
| 2.5.8 | Target Size (Minimum) | AA | C42, C44, G216 | Partial — axe `target-size` rule (see Cycle 22 Gotcha 113 for gaps) | Dense toolbars need geometry testing from Cycle 22 Pattern |
| 3.2.6 | Consistent Help | A | G220 | None in axe | Verify help link/contact appears in same relative order across all pages |
| 3.3.7 | Redundant Entry | A | — | None in axe | Multi-step form: verify previously-entered data is pre-populated |
| 3.3.8 | Accessible Authentication (Minimum) | AA | F109 | Partial — axe checks `autocomplete` attribute | Verify paste is not blocked; verify CAPTCHA has audio/text alternative |
| 3.3.9 | Accessible Authentication (Enhanced) | AAA | F109 | Same as 3.3.8 | Verify no cognitive function test (image recognition, puzzles) in auth flow |

### Pattern 12 — `prefers-contrast: more` Emulation for Enhanced Contrast Mode Testing

macOS and iOS support `prefers-contrast: more` (enabled via Accessibility settings > Increase Contrast). Unlike `forced-colors` (which replaces colors entirely), `prefers-contrast: more` is a hint that applications should voluntarily increase contrast. Playwright v1.51+ exposes this via `page.emulateMedia({ contrast: 'more' })`.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/contrast-preference.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('prefers-contrast: more (macOS Increase Contrast)', () => {
  test('text meets AA contrast ratio when high contrast is requested', async ({ page }) => {
    // Emulate macOS "Increase Contrast" system preference
    await page.emulateMedia({ contrast: 'more' });
    await page.goto('/');

    // The application should respond by applying higher contrast styles.
    // Test that body text meets 4.5:1 contrast (WCAG 1.4.3 AA).
    const { textColor, bgColor } = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const body = document.body;
      const style = window.getComputedStyle(body);
      return {
        textColor: style.getPropertyValue('color'),
        bgColor: style.getPropertyValue('background-color'),
      };
    });

    // Parse RGB values and compute contrast ratio
    function parseRGB(cssColor: string): [number, number, number] {
      const m = cssColor.match(/\d+/g)!;
      return [parseInt(m[0]), parseInt(m[1]), parseInt(m[2])];
    }

    function relativeLuminance([r, g, b]: [number, number, number]): number {
      const toLinear = (c: number) => {
        const s = c / 255;
        return s <= 0.04045 ? s / 12.92 : Math.pow((s + 0.055) / 1.055, 2.4);
      };
      return 0.2126 * toLinear(r) + 0.7152 * toLinear(g) + 0.0722 * toLinear(b);
    }

    const l1 = relativeLuminance(parseRGB(textColor));
    const l2 = relativeLuminance(parseRGB(bgColor));
    const contrast = (Math.max(l1, l2) + 0.05) / (Math.min(l1, l2) + 0.05);

    expect(
      contrast,
      `Body text contrast ratio ${contrast.toFixed(2)} does not meet WCAG AA 4.5:1 under prefers-contrast:more`
    ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4.5);
  });

  test('secondary text color increases when high contrast requested', async ({ page }) => {
    // Without emulation (normal mode)
    await page.goto('/article');
    const normalContrast = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const meta = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.article-meta');
      return meta ? window.getComputedStyle(meta).color : 'rgb(0,0,0)';
    });

    // With high contrast emulation
    await page.emulateMedia({ contrast: 'more' });
    const highContrast = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const meta = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.article-meta');
      return meta ? window.getComputedStyle(meta).color : 'rgb(0,0,0)';
    });

    // Ideally the color should darken (lower R/G/B values on light background)
    // This is a regression test — verify the CSS responds to the media query
    expect(normalContrast).not.toBe(highContrast);
  });
});
```

**Note**: `prefers-contrast: more` was added to Playwright's `emulateMedia` API in v1.51. The `contrast` option accepts `'more'` or `'no-preference'`. Unlike `forced-colors`, this relies on the application voluntarily implementing `@media (prefers-contrast: more)` CSS rules. If the application has no such rules, the test comparing normal vs high-contrast styles will correctly detect the gap.

### Pattern 13 — axe-core `resultTypes` Performance Optimisation for Large SPAs

For applications with many DOM nodes (admin dashboards, data-heavy tables), `axe.run()` with default settings may take 3–8 seconds per scan. The `resultTypes` option limits which result categories are computed, reducing scan time by 40–60% for CI gates that only need violations.

```typescript
// tests/helpers/axe-fast.ts
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';
import { Page, TestInfo } from '@playwright/test';

interface FastAxeOptions {
  /** CSS selectors to include — defaults to entire page */
  include?: string[];
  /** CSS selectors to exclude from scan */
  exclude?: string[];
  /** WCAG tag filters — defaults to wcag2a + wcag2aa + wcag21a + wcag21aa + wcag22aa */
  tags?: string[];
}

/**
 * Runs axe-core with resultTypes optimisation for CI gates.
 * Only computes violations and incomplete results — skips passes and inapplicable.
 * Reduces scan time by ~50% on large SPAs.
 */
export async function fastAxeScan(
  page: Page,
  testInfo: TestInfo,
  options: FastAxeOptions = {}
): Promise<void> {
  const builder = new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(options.tags ?? ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
    .options({
      // Only compute violations and incomplete — skip passes/inapplicable
      resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'],
    } as Parameters<AxeBuilder['options']>[0]);

  if (options.include) {
    options.include.forEach(sel => builder.include(sel));
  }
  if (options.exclude) {
    options.exclude.forEach(sel => builder.exclude(sel));
  }

  const results = await builder.analyze();

  // Attach full results to Playwright test report for debugging
  await testInfo.attach('axe-scan-results', {
    body: JSON.stringify(
      { violations: results.violations, incomplete: results.incomplete },
      null,
      2
    ),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  // Assert — violations that need review go into a separate bucket, not a hard fail
  if (results.violations.length > 0) {
    const summary = results.violations
      .map(v => `[${v.impact}] ${v.id}: ${v.description} (${v.nodes.length} nodes)`)
      .join('\n');
    throw new Error(`axe-core violations found:\n${summary}`);
  }
}
```

**Benchmark guidance**: On a typical React SPA with 800 DOM nodes, default `axe.run()` takes ~4.2 s; with `resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete']` it takes ~2.1 s. On a data-grid page with 3000+ nodes, the reduction can be from 12 s to 4 s.

### Pattern 14 — Testing ARIA Live Region Announcement Timing

ARIA live regions (`aria-live="polite"` and `role="alert"`) announce dynamically injected content to screen readers, but only if: (a) the live region container exists before the content is injected, and (b) the announcement is not suppressed by focus movement happening simultaneously. Teams frequently create the container and inject content in the same render cycle, which browsers ignore.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/aria-live-regions.spec.ts
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

/**
 * Checks that an aria-live region exists before triggering the action that
 * populates it — the container must be pre-rendered, not created dynamically.
 */
async function assertLiveRegionPreExists(
  page: Page,
  regionSelector: string
): Promise<void> {
  const count = await page.locator(regionSelector).count();
  expect(
    count,
    `aria-live region "${regionSelector}" must be pre-rendered in DOM before content is injected — browsers ignore live announcements when the container is created and populated in the same tick`
  ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
}

test.describe('ARIA live region announcement integrity (WCAG 4.1.3)', () => {
  test('status message region exists before form submission', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout');
    // The status region must exist before the Submit button is clicked
    await assertLiveRegionPreExists(page, '[role="status"], [aria-live="polite"]');
  });

  test('alert region fires immediately on validation error', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/register');

    // Pre-check: the alert container exists empty
    await assertLiveRegionPreExists(page, '[role="alert"], [aria-live="assertive"]');

    // Trigger validation
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create account' }).click();

    // The error must appear in the live region within 500ms
    const alertRegion = page.locator('[role="alert"]').first();
    await expect(alertRegion).not.toBeEmpty({ timeout: 500 });
  });

  test('toast notifications use polite not assertive (non-critical messages)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save preferences' }).click();

    // Success toasts are non-critical — they must use polite, not assertive.
    // Assertive interrupts the screen reader's current announcement.
    const toast = page.locator('[data-testid="toast"]');
    await expect(toast).toBeVisible();

    const liveValue = await toast.getAttribute('aria-live');
    const roleValue = await toast.getAttribute('role');

    // Either aria-live="polite" or role="status" (which implies polite)
    const isPolite = liveValue === 'polite' || roleValue === 'status';
    expect(
      isPolite,
      'Non-critical toast notifications must use aria-live="polite" or role="status", not aria-live="assertive" which interrupts screen reader narration (WCAG 4.1.3)'
    ).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

---

### Pattern 15 — Focus Trap Testing for Modal Dialogs (ARIA APG Dialog Pattern)

Modal dialogs must implement a focus trap: Tab and Shift+Tab must cycle through the dialog's focusable elements without escaping to the background page. Escape must close the dialog. Focus must return to the trigger element after close. This is the most-failed interactive component pattern in manual audits.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/focus-trap.spec.ts
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

async function getFocusableElements(page: Page, dialogSelector: string): Promise<string[]> {
  return page.evaluate((selector: string) => {
    const dialog = document.querySelector(selector);
    if (!dialog) return [];
    const focusable = dialog.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(
      'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), ' +
      'textarea:not([disabled]), [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"]), details > summary'
    );
    return Array.from(focusable).map(el => el.tagName + (el.id ? '#' + el.id : ''));
  }, dialogSelector);
}

test.describe('Modal dialog focus trap (WCAG 2.1.2, APG Dialog Pattern)', () => {
  test('Tab key stays within dialog', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open settings' }).click();

    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();

    // Count focusable elements in the dialog
    const focusableCount = await getFocusableElements(page, '[role="dialog"]');
    expect(focusableCount.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    // Tab through all focusable elements plus one extra — should cycle back
    for (let i = 0; i <= focusableCount.length; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    }

    // After cycling through all elements, focus must still be inside the dialog
    const focusIsInsideDialog = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const dialog = document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]');
      return dialog?.contains(document.activeElement) ?? false;
    });

    expect(
      focusIsInsideDialog,
      'Tab must cycle within the dialog — focus escaped to background page (WCAG 2.1.2)'
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  test('Escape closes dialog and returns focus to trigger', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    const trigger = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open settings' });
    await trigger.click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');

    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).not.toBeVisible();
    // Focus must return to the trigger button (WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order)
    await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('dialog is announced with role and accessible name', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open settings' }).click();

    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();

    // Dialog must have an accessible name (aria-labelledby or aria-label)
    await expect(dialog).toHaveAccessibleName(/.+/);
  });
});
```

### Pattern 16 — Keyboard Navigation Audit: Tab Order Snapshot

Tab order deviations (elements that appear visually left-to-right but tab in a different order) are a WCAG 2.4.3 violation that no automated rule catches — axe-core does not know what the expected visual reading order is. A snapshot-based approach captures the current tab order and fails the test when it changes unexpectedly.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/tab-order.spec.ts
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

async function captureTabOrder(page: Page, maxTabs = 30): Promise<string[]> {
  const tabOrder: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < maxTabs; i++) {
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');

    const focusInfo = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
      if (!el || el === document.body) return null;
      const role = el.getAttribute('role') ?? el.tagName.toLowerCase();
      const label =
        el.getAttribute('aria-label') ??
        el.getAttribute('aria-labelledby') ??
        el.getAttribute('placeholder') ??
        el.textContent?.trim().slice(0, 30) ??
        '';
      const testId = el.getAttribute('data-testid') ?? '';
      return `${role}[${label || testId}]`;
    });

    if (!focusInfo) break;
    if (tabOrder.includes(focusInfo)) break; // cycled back to start
    tabOrder.push(focusInfo);
  }

  return tabOrder;
}

test('tab order matches expected reading order on home page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  const tabOrder = await captureTabOrder(page);

  // Update this snapshot when intentional tab order changes are made
  // This is a living accessibility contract
  expect(tabOrder).toMatchSnapshot('home-page-tab-order.txt');
});

test('tab order is not disrupted after modal close', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Capture baseline tab order
  const baselineOrder = await captureTabOrder(page);

  // Open and close a modal
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'View terms' }).click();
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');

  // Tab order must be identical after modal close
  const postModalOrder = await captureTabOrder(page);
  expect(postModalOrder).toEqual(baselineOrder);
});
```

### Pattern 17 — WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry: Multi-Step Form Pre-Population Test

WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7 (Level A) requires that information entered by the user in a previous step is not re-requested in a subsequent step of the same process, unless re-entry is essential (e.g., confirming a password), required for security, or the information is no longer valid.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/redundant-entry.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry — multi-step form', () => {
  test('billing address is pre-populated from shipping address when same-as checkbox is checked', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout/shipping');

    // Step 1: Enter shipping address
    await page.getByLabel('First name').fill('Jane');
    await page.getByLabel('Last name').fill('Doe');
    await page.getByLabel('Address line 1').fill('123 Main St');
    await page.getByLabel('City').fill('Portland');
    await page.getByLabel('State').selectOption('OR');
    await page.getByLabel('ZIP code').fill('97201');

    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue to billing' }).click();

    // Step 2: Billing page — same-as-shipping is the default
    const sameAsShipping = page.getByLabel('Same as shipping address');
    await expect(sameAsShipping).toBeChecked();

    // When same-as is checked, billing fields should be read-only or hidden
    const billingCity = page.getByLabel('Billing city');
    if (await billingCity.isVisible()) {
      // If shown, they must be pre-populated
      await expect(billingCity).toHaveValue('Portland');
    }

    // Uncheck same-as to reveal separate billing form
    await sameAsShipping.uncheck();

    // All fields must be empty (user did not provide billing address yet)
    // — they must NOT ask the user to re-type the shipping address if it's different
    await expect(page.getByLabel('Billing first name')).toHaveValue('');
  });

  test('review page shows all entered data without re-requesting it', async ({ page }) => {
    // Helper: fill all form steps programmatically using saved session
    await page.goto('/checkout/review');

    // The review page should show previously entered data
    await expect(page.getByText('Jane Doe')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.getByText('123 Main St')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.getByText('Portland, OR 97201')).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 23)

116. **[community] Pa11y v9 (Node.js 20+) uses Puppeteer `^24` which changes the default `headless` mode to `'shell'` instead of `true` — on Linux CI without a display server, you must explicitly pass `args: ['--no-sandbox']` in `chromeLaunchConfig` or Puppeteer will crash with "Failed to launch the browser process"**: Pa11y v9 upgraded from Puppeteer 20 to Puppeteer 24. Puppeteer 24 changed the default headless from the old boolean `true` (equivalent to `--headless=old`) to `'shell'` (equivalent to `--headless=new`, Chromium's new headless mode). The new headless mode has stricter sandboxing requirements that fail in Docker/CI without `--no-sandbox`. Teams upgrading Pa11y v8 → v9 in CI often miss this because local macOS development works fine. WHY: The `--no-sandbox` flag is required in all Linux containerized environments (GitHub Actions ubuntu runners, Docker). Omitting it gives a misleading "browser process" error that looks like a general infrastructure problem rather than a configuration issue.

117. **[community] `jest-axe` v10 is incompatible with Jest v30 — Jest v30 changed how `expect` is imported, breaking the `toHaveNoViolations` matcher registration**: Jest v30 moved to a stricter ESM-only import path for `expect` that conflicts with how `jest-axe` v10 registers its custom matchers via `expect.extend()`. The symptom is a runtime error: `TypeError: expect.extend is not a function`. Workarounds: (a) pin `jest-axe` at `^9.0.0` if staying on Jest v30, or (b) migrate to `@axe-core/vitest` if switching to Vitest (the recommended path for new projects in 2026). WHY: Jest v30's `expect` export changed from the global to a module import, and jest-axe's current release does not account for this. Check the `jest-axe` GitHub issues for a v11 release that may resolve this.

118. **[community] Playwright's `forced-colors: 'active'` emulation does not affect CSS `background-image` on elements with `role="img"` — these images remain visible in the browser, but the emulation flag tells CSS engines to suppress background-images, so tests that check image visibility in forced-colors mode may produce false negatives**: The `forced-colors` CSS spec forces `background-image: none` for non-URL images, but Playwright's Chrome DevTools Protocol implementation applies this at the CSS evaluation level. Testing whether a background-image-based icon is visible in forced-colors mode cannot be done purely with `toBeVisible()` — you must check the computed style to confirm the background-image was suppressed. WHY: Teams that add `forced-colors` tests often write `expect(iconElement).toBeVisible()` expecting it to fail when the background image is gone, but `toBeVisible()` checks DOM presence and display properties, not whether background images are rendering with visible content.

119. **[community] `aria-live` regions that are created and populated in the same JavaScript event loop tick are NOT announced by browsers — the container must exist in the DOM (even empty) before the content is injected**: This is the single most common ARIA live region implementation error. Developers add a `<div role="alert">Error message</div>` dynamically to the DOM when an error occurs, expecting the screen reader to announce it. Browsers only announce live region content changes — not live region creation. The fix is to render `<div role="alert" aria-live="assertive"></div>` in the page's initial HTML (empty), then populate it via JavaScript. WHY: The browser observes the live region for mutations. A newly created element has no prior state to compare against, so there is no mutation to announce. Always pre-render live region containers.

120. **[community] `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` in Playwright will fail if the page has dynamic content (timestamps, generated IDs, random numbers) in accessible names — use the `/regex/` YAML template syntax or `expect.stringContaining()` patterns to match variable content**: The `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` assertion performs a deep structural ARIA tree comparison. Any dynamic text in accessible names (e.g., "3 notifications" where 3 changes, or "Item added at 14:32:07") will cause snapshot mismatches on subsequent runs. Use YAML regex templates: `- button "\\d+ notifications"` to match the variable number without hardcoding it. Alternatively, freeze dynamic content with `page.clock.setFixedTime()` before taking the snapshot. WHY: Teams copy-paste the initial snapshot from `npx playwright --update-snapshots` and then discover CI fails randomly whenever the dynamic count changes. The regex template approach makes the snapshot a stable structural contract while still validating the element type and rough content pattern.

121. **[community] The axe-core `target-size` rule ignores elements with `display: inline` because inline elements do not have a defined bounding box in the same way block-level elements do — icon links rendered as `<a>` without `display: block` may be far below the 24×24 minimum and pass the axe scan**: Inline `<a>` elements (such as links within prose text) are exempted by the axe target-size rule because WCAG 2.5.8 provides an exception for targets that are inline within text. However, navigation links and action icons that happen to be in `<a>` tags but are visually standalone buttons may also be treated as inline by axe and exempted. Always use the Playwright geometry-based target-size test (Pattern from Cycle 22) for navigation bar links and icon-heavy interfaces in addition to the axe scan. WHY: The exemption is technically correct for inline text links, but misapplied by developers who do not realize their navigation `<a>` tags render as inline.

122. **[community] Screen reader announcements for `aria-label` on container elements (div, section, nav) are vendor-dependent: NVDA 2024+ no longer announces the `aria-label` of non-interactive containers by default unless the element has a landmark role (`role="region"`, `role="navigation"`, etc.) — test with multiple AT, not just VoiceOver**: A common pattern is `<div aria-label="Product gallery">` used as a section label. VoiceOver announces this when the user enters the group. NVDA 2024 changed its default behavior to only announce labels for elements that are landmarks or interactive controls. A `<div>` with `aria-label` but no role is a "generic" landmark in the ARIA spec, and NVDA skips generic landmark labels by default. The fix: add `role="region"` to the container (`<div role="region" aria-label="Product gallery">`), which upgrades it to a named landmark that all screen readers announce. WHY: Teams test on VoiceOver (macOS) and assume NVDA behaves identically. The behavioral divergence has existed since NVDA 2023.3 and is intentional per the ARIA spec's generic landmark guidance.

### Pattern 1 (Cycle 24) — axe-core 4.10.0: `summary` Element Accessible Name Rule

axe-core 4.10.0 (July 2024) introduced a new rule requiring that `<summary>` elements have an accessible name. A `<details>/<summary>` disclosure widget without a visible label leaves screen reader users unable to understand what will be revealed. Test this rule explicitly in addition to your page-level axe scan, because it targets a narrower element type that broad page scans may deprioritize.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/summary-accessible-name.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('summary element accessible name (axe-core 4.10+ rule)', () => {
  test('all details/summary disclosure widgets have accessible names', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      // Target the specific rule introduced in axe-core 4.10.0
      .withRules(['summary-name'])
      .analyze();

    expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('summary with only icon has explicit aria-label', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');

    // Find all summary elements and verify each has an accessible name
    const summaries = page.locator('summary');
    const count = await summaries.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const summary = summaries.nth(i);
      // Should have either visible text or aria-label/aria-labelledby
      const accessibleName = await summary.evaluate((el) => {
        return (el as HTMLElement).getAttribute('aria-label') ||
               (el as HTMLElement).textContent?.trim() || '';
      });
      expect(accessibleName.length, `summary[${i}] has no accessible name`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });
});
```

### Pattern 2 (Cycle 24) — axe-core 4.10.1: 10× Performance Boost for Repeated-Element Pages

axe-core 4.10.1 fixed a bottleneck when scanning pages with many similar elements (e.g., data tables, lists with 100+ items). The fix allows axe to run up to 10× faster on such pages. Pair this with the `resultTypes` performance option (already documented in Cycle 22) to keep CI scan times under 2 seconds on complex pages.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/performance-optimized-scan.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

// Reusable fast scan fixture for large data pages
const fastAxeScan = async (page: Parameters<typeof AxeBuilder>[0]['page']) => {
  return new AxeBuilder({ page })
    // resultTypes optimization: only collect violations, skip passes/incomplete
    // (axe-core 4.10.1+ processes passes/incomplete even when unrequested — this prevents that)
    .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
    .analyze();
};

test('data table with 200 rows scans in under 3 seconds', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports/all-transactions');

  const start = Date.now();
  const results = await fastAxeScan(page);
  const elapsed = Date.now() - start;

  expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
  // Verify axe 4.10.1+ performance improvement — should be well under limit
  expect(elapsed, `axe scan took ${elapsed}ms — check axe-core version`).toBeLessThan(3000);
});

test('product list with 100+ cards scans efficiently', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products?page_size=100');
  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="product-card"]');

  const results = await fastAxeScan(page);
  expect(results.violations.length).toBe(0);
});
```

### Pattern 3 (Cycle 24) — Pa11y v9.1.0: `--level-cap-when-needs-review` Flag

Pa11y v9.1.0 (February 2025) introduced `--level-cap-when-needs-review` to cap the severity of "needs manual review" issues at a configurable level. This is critical for CI gates: Pa11y's HTML_CodeSniffer runner emits `NOTICE` and `WARNING` items for issues that need human verification (not automated failures). Without this flag, a `WARNING` for a potential contrast issue will fail a gate configured for `error` only. With the flag, you can deliberately treat "needs review" findings as `notice`-level in CI, keeping the gate green while preserving the findings in the report for manual triage.

```typescript
// pa11y.config.js — Node.js configuration file for Pa11y v9.1+
module.exports = {
  standard: 'WCAG2AA',
  // Cap all "needs review" items at NOTICE so they don't trip the CI gate
  // Remove this flag when you want strict mode (all potential issues = CI failure)
  levelCapWhenNeedsReview: 'notice',
  // Use both runners for maximum coverage
  runners: ['htmlcs', 'axe'],
  // Axe-core 4.11 is bundled in Pa11y v9.1
  ignore: [
    // Suppress known false positives from htmlcs on dynamically loaded content
    'WCAG2AA.Principle1.Guideline1_4.1_4_3.G145.Fail',
  ],
  chromeLaunchConfig: {
    args: ['--no-sandbox', '--disable-setuid-sandbox'],
  },
};

// Usage in test suite:
// npx pa11y --config pa11y.config.js https://localhost:3000/
// Or programmatically:
import pa11y from 'pa11y';

const result = await pa11y('http://localhost:3000/', {
  standard: 'WCAG2AA',
  levelCapWhenNeedsReview: 'notice',
  runners: ['htmlcs', 'axe'],
  chromeLaunchConfig: { args: ['--no-sandbox'] },
});

const errors = result.issues.filter((i) => i.type === 'error');
if (errors.length > 0) {
  console.error('Pa11y CI gate FAILED:', errors);
  process.exit(1);
}
```

### Pattern 4 (Cycle 24) — ARIA Accordion Full Keyboard Contract Test (APG Pattern)

The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide defines a specific keyboard contract for accordion widgets: Enter/Space expands the focused header, Tab navigates through page focusable elements normally, and optional arrow keys navigate between accordion headers. The ARIA attributes that must be present are `role="button"` on each header (or a native `<button>`), `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls`. Testing the full contract — not just that the accordion opens — is what distinguishes a compliance test from a smoke test.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/accordion-keyboard-contract.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Accordion keyboard contract (APG)', () => {
  test('Enter key expands collapsed accordion panel', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const firstHeader = page.getByRole('button', { name: /shipping/i }).first();

    // Verify initial collapsed state
    await expect(firstHeader).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

    // Focus the header and press Enter
    await firstHeader.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

    // Panel must be expanded
    await expect(firstHeader).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

    // The controlled panel must be visible
    const panelId = await firstHeader.getAttribute('aria-controls');
    expect(panelId).toBeTruthy();
    await expect(page.locator(`#${panelId}`)).toBeVisible();
  });

  test('Space key toggles collapsed accordion panel', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const firstHeader = page.getByRole('button', { name: /shipping/i }).first();
    await firstHeader.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
    await expect(firstHeader).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

    // Press Space again to collapse
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
    await expect(firstHeader).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  });

  test('accordion headers are wrapped in heading elements with appropriate level', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    // Each accordion button must be inside a heading (h2, h3, etc.)
    const accordionButtons = page.getByRole('button', { expanded: false });
    const count = await accordionButtons.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const btn = accordionButtons.nth(i);
      // Button's parent should be a heading role
      const parentTag = await btn.evaluate((el) =>
        el.parentElement?.tagName.toLowerCase() ?? ''
      );
      expect(['h1','h2','h3','h4','h5','h6']).toContain(parentTag);
    }
  });

  test('accordion does not trap keyboard focus', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const firstHeader = page.getByRole('button').first();
    await firstHeader.focus();

    // Tab twice should move past the accordion into the rest of the page
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');

    // Focused element should be outside the accordion section
    const focusedRole = await page.evaluate(
      () => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role') ?? document.activeElement?.tagName
    );
    // Simply confirm focus has moved (not trapped)
    expect(focusedRole).toBeTruthy();
  });
});
```

### Pattern 5 (Cycle 24) — ARIA Carousel Auto-Rotation Stop on Focus

The WAI-ARIA APG carousel pattern mandates that auto-rotation **stops when any element in the carousel receives keyboard focus** and must not resume until the user explicitly restarts it. This is a critical accessibility requirement often missed in slider/hero implementations. Additionally, the rotation control must appear first in the tab order so users can stop it without needing to Tab through all slides first.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/carousel-auto-rotation.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Carousel auto-rotation (APG 2.2)', () => {
  test('auto-rotation stops when carousel receives keyboard focus', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/home');

    const carousel = page.getByRole('region', { name: /featured/i });
    await expect(carousel).toBeVisible();

    // Note initial slide
    const initialSlide = await page
      .getByRole('group', { name: /slide/i })
      .first()
      .getAttribute('aria-label');

    // Tab into the carousel
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    // Wait and confirm slide did NOT change (auto-rotation stopped)
    await page.waitForTimeout(2500); // longer than typical rotation interval

    const currentSlide = await page
      .getByRole('group', { name: /slide/i })
      .first()
      .getAttribute('aria-label');

    expect(currentSlide).toBe(initialSlide);
  });

  test('rotation control is first focusable element in carousel tab order', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/home');

    // Tab to enter the carousel area
    const carousel = page.getByRole('region', { name: /featured/i });
    await carousel.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();

    // The first focusable element inside the carousel should be the rotation toggle
    const firstFocusable = carousel.locator('button, [href], [tabindex="0"]').first();
    const label = await firstFocusable.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? await firstFocusable.textContent();

    // Rotation control label should contain 'stop' or 'pause' or 'start' wording
    expect(label?.toLowerCase()).toMatch(/stop|pause|start/);
  });

  test('currently displayed slide button has aria-disabled="true"', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/home');

    // In a tabbed carousel, the active tab (current slide picker) should be aria-disabled
    const activeSlideButton = page.locator('[role="tab"][aria-selected="true"], [aria-disabled="true"]').first();
    if (await activeSlideButton.count() > 0) {
      const isDisabledOrSelected =
        (await activeSlideButton.getAttribute('aria-disabled')) === 'true' ||
        (await activeSlideButton.getAttribute('aria-selected')) === 'true';
      expect(isDisabledOrSelected).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test('hidden slides use off-screen technique, not display:none without aria-hidden', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/home');
    // Hidden slides that use visibility:hidden without aria-hidden="true" are still in the AT tree
    const hiddenSlides = page.locator('[role="group"][aria-roledescription="slide"]');
    const count = await hiddenSlides.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const slide = hiddenSlides.nth(i);
      const isHidden = await slide.evaluate((el) => {
        const style = window.getComputedStyle(el);
        return style.display === 'none' || style.visibility === 'hidden';
      });
      if (isHidden) {
        // If visually hidden, must also be hidden from AT
        await expect(slide).toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
      }
    }
  });
});
```

---

### Pattern 6 (Cycle 24) — ARIA Tree View Full Keyboard Contract Test

Tree view widgets have one of the most complex keyboard contracts in the ARIA APG: Right arrow opens nodes, Left arrow closes open nodes or moves to parent, Down/Up arrows navigate visible nodes, Home/End jump to first/last, and multi-select trees use Space/Ctrl+A. Each `treeitem` that is a parent must have `aria-expanded`. The tree container must have `role="tree"` with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Dynamically loaded trees additionally require `aria-level`, `aria-setsize`, and `aria-posinset`.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/treeview-keyboard-contract.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('ARIA Tree View keyboard contract (APG)', () => {
  test('tree container has correct ARIA role and label', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-browser');

    const tree = page.getByRole('tree');
    await expect(tree).toBeVisible();
    // Tree must have an accessible label
    const label = await tree.getAttribute('aria-label') ??
      await tree.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    expect(label).toBeTruthy();
  });

  test('Right arrow opens closed tree node', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-browser');

    // Find a collapsed parent node
    const closedNode = page.getByRole('treeitem', { expanded: false }).first();
    await closedNode.focus();
    await expect(closedNode).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    await expect(closedNode).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
  });

  test('Left arrow closes open node and then moves to parent', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-browser');

    // Find an open node
    const openNode = page.getByRole('treeitem', { expanded: true }).first();
    await openNode.focus();

    // First Left: collapse the node
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft');
    await expect(openNode).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

    // Second Left on a child: should move focus to parent
    // (skip this assertion if we're already at the root level)
  });

  test('Down/Up arrows navigate between visible tree items', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-browser');

    const firstItem = page.getByRole('treeitem').first();
    await firstItem.focus();

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');

    // A different treeitem should now have focus
    const focusedItem = page.locator('[role="treeitem"]:focus');
    await expect(focusedItem).not.toHaveText(await firstItem.textContent() ?? '');
  });

  test('Home/End keys jump to first/last tree item', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-browser');

    const allItems = page.getByRole('treeitem');
    const count = await allItems.count();

    await allItems.first().focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('End');

    const lastItemText = await allItems.nth(count - 1).textContent();
    const focusedText = await page.evaluate(
      () => (document.activeElement as HTMLElement)?.textContent?.trim()
    );
    expect(focusedText).toBe(lastItemText?.trim());
  });

  test('axe-core validates tree widget ARIA structure', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-browser');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include('[role="tree"]')
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

### Pattern 7 (Cycle 24) — ARIA Menubar Full Keyboard Contract Test

Menubar widgets have a specific keyboard contract that differs from tab lists: Tab/Shift+Tab exits the menubar entirely (composite widget semantics), arrow keys navigate within, Escape closes submenus, and Enter/Space activate items. A common implementation error is using Tab to navigate within the menubar instead of arrow keys, which breaks screen reader virtual cursor navigation. Also test that `aria-haspopup="menu"` is present on items that open submenus.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/menubar-keyboard-contract.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('ARIA Menubar keyboard contract (APG)', () => {
  test('menubar has correct role and accessible label', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    const menubar = page.getByRole('menubar');
    await expect(menubar).toBeVisible();
    const label = await menubar.getAttribute('aria-label') ??
      await menubar.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    expect(label).toBeTruthy();
  });

  test('Enter key opens submenu from menubar item', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    const menuTrigger = page.getByRole('menuitem', { name: /file/i }).first();
    await menuTrigger.focus();

    // Verify aria-haspopup before interaction
    expect(await menuTrigger.getAttribute('aria-haspopup')).toBe('menu');
    expect(await menuTrigger.getAttribute('aria-expanded')).toBe('false');

    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

    await expect(menuTrigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    // Submenu should be visible
    await expect(page.getByRole('menu')).toBeVisible();
  });

  test('Escape key closes submenu and returns focus to trigger', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    const menuTrigger = page.getByRole('menuitem', { name: /file/i }).first();
    await menuTrigger.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
    await expect(page.getByRole('menu')).toBeVisible();

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(page.getByRole('menu')).not.toBeVisible();
    // Focus must return to the trigger element
    await expect(menuTrigger).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('Right/Left arrow keys navigate horizontally within menubar', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    const menuItems = page.getByRole('menuitem');
    await menuItems.first().focus();

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    // Second item should now be focused
    const secondItemText = await menuItems.nth(1).textContent();
    const focusedText = await page.evaluate(
      () => (document.activeElement as HTMLElement)?.textContent?.trim()
    );
    expect(focusedText).toBe(secondItemText?.trim());
  });

  test('Tab key exits the menubar entirely (composite widget)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    const menubar = page.getByRole('menubar');
    const menuItems = menubar.getByRole('menuitem');
    await menuItems.first().focus();

    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');

    // Focus should have left the menubar
    const focusIsInsideMenubar = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const menubar = document.querySelector('[role="menubar"]');
      return menubar?.contains(document.activeElement) ?? false;
    });
    expect(focusIsInsideMenubar).toBe(false);
  });

  test('axe validates full menubar ARIA structure', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include('[role="menubar"]')
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

### Pattern 8 (Cycle 24) — WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: CSS `scroll-padding` Automated Test

WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 (Level AA) requires that when a component receives keyboard focus, it is not entirely hidden by author-created content such as sticky headers, footers, or cookie banners. The W3C's primary sufficient technique is CSS `scroll-padding`. While 2.4.11 cannot be fully automated (viewport-dependent, partially hidden is still a pass), the `scroll-padding` configuration and sticky-element Z-index can be verified programmatically.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/focus-not-obscured.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured', () => {
  test('sticky header height is compensated by scroll-padding-top on <html>', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    // Measure the sticky header height
    const headerHeight = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const header = document.querySelector('header[data-sticky], .sticky-header, [style*="position: sticky"]');
      if (!header) return 0;
      return (header as HTMLElement).offsetHeight;
    });

    // Check that scroll-padding-top >= sticky header height
    const scrollPaddingTop = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const style = window.getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
      const val = style.getPropertyValue('scroll-padding-top');
      return parseInt(val, 10) || 0;
    });

    if (headerHeight > 0) {
      expect(
        scrollPaddingTop,
        `scroll-padding-top (${scrollPaddingTop}px) must be >= sticky header height (${headerHeight}px) per WCAG 2.4.11`
      ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(headerHeight);
    }
  });

  test('focused element is not entirely obscured by sticky footer after tab navigation', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/long-form');

    // Tab through several elements to reach content near the sticky footer
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    }

    const obscured = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const focused = document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
      if (!focused || focused === document.body) return false;

      const focusedRect = focused.getBoundingClientRect();
      const footer = document.querySelector('footer[data-sticky], .sticky-footer');
      if (!footer) return false;

      const footerRect = footer.getBoundingClientRect();
      // Check if the focused element's bottom edge is obscured by the footer top
      // WCAG 2.4.11 pass = at least partially visible (not entirely hidden)
      return focusedRect.bottom > footerRect.top &&
             focusedRect.top >= footerRect.top; // entirely hidden
    });

    expect(obscured, 'Focused element is entirely obscured by sticky footer — WCAG 2.4.11 failure').toBe(false);
  });

  test('modal dialog does not fail 2.4.11 — it properly takes focus', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    // Open a modal
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open dialog|learn more/i }).first().click();
    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();

    // Focus should be inside the dialog — not obscured by it
    const focusInsideDialog = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const dialog = document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]');
      return dialog?.contains(document.activeElement) ?? false;
    });
    expect(focusInsideDialog).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

### Pattern 9 (Cycle 24) — axe-core 4.11.0 RGAA Tag Support for French Accessibility Standard

axe-core 4.11.0 (October 2024) added RGAA (Référentiel Général d'Amélioration de l'Accessibilité, France's national accessibility standard) tags to numerous rules. Four best-practice rules became required under RGAA: `focus-order-semantics`, `region`, `skip-link`, and `table-duplicate-name`. Teams building applications for French public-sector clients or EU EAA compliance now need to include RGAA tags in their axe scans or these rules may be silently skipped.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/rgaa-compliance.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('RGAA compliance (axe-core 4.11.0+ RGAA tags)', () => {
  test('page passes WCAG2AA + RGAA required rules', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      // Include both WCAG2AA and RGAA tags (axe-core 4.11.0+)
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa', 'best-practice'])
      .analyze();

    // Filter to show RGAA-related violations separately for triage
    const rgaaViolations = results.violations.filter(
      (v) => v.tags.some((t) => t.startsWith('RGAA'))
    );

    if (rgaaViolations.length > 0) {
      console.warn('RGAA-specific violations found:', rgaaViolations.map((v) => v.id));
    }

    expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('page has a visible skip navigation link (required by RGAA)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    // Skip link must be the first focusable element and become visible on focus
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const skipLink = page.locator(':focus');

    const tagName = await skipLink.evaluate((el) => el.tagName.toLowerCase());
    const href = await skipLink.getAttribute('href');

    expect(tagName).toBe('a');
    expect(href).toMatch(/^#/); // must be an in-page anchor link
    await expect(skipLink).toBeVisible(); // must be visible when focused
  });

  test('page has landmark regions wrapping main content areas (RGAA + WCAG 2.4.1)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    // Required landmarks: main, navigation, and at minimum one region
    await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.getByRole('navigation').first()).toBeVisible();
  });

  test('data tables with both title and caption do not duplicate the name (RGAA table-duplicate-name)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/reports');
    const tables = page.locator('table[aria-label], table[title]');
    const count = await tables.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const table = tables.nth(i);
      const caption = await table.locator('caption').textContent();
      const ariaLabel = await table.getAttribute('aria-label');
      const title = await table.getAttribute('title');

      // If both caption and aria-label/title exist, they must not be identical
      if (caption && (ariaLabel || title)) {
        expect(caption.trim()).not.toBe((ariaLabel ?? title ?? '').trim());
      }
    }
  });
});
```

### Pattern 10 (Cycle 24) — axe-core-npm 4.11.2 WebDriverIO `switchFrame` Compatibility Fix

axe-core-npm 4.11.2 (April 2026) resolved a regression where `AxeBuilder.analyze()` failed silently in WebDriverIO v9 when the test had previously called `browser.switchToFrame()` and the frame context was not properly reset. The fix correctly resets frame context before injecting the axe script. If your WDIO tests scan iframes, always call `browser.switchToParentFrame()` before running `AxeBuilder.analyze()` to guarantee scanning from the top-level document context.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/iframe-axe-wdio.spec.ts
// WebDriverIO v9 + @axe-core/wdio 4.11.2+
import { browser, expect as wdioExpect } from '@wdio/globals';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/wdio';

describe('axe-core iframe scanning (WDIO v9 + axe-core-npm 4.11.2)', () => {
  it('resets frame context before axe scan to avoid 4.11.1 regression', async () => {
    await browser.url('/page-with-iframe');

    // Inspect content inside an iframe
    const iframe = await $('iframe[name="content-frame"]');
    await browser.switchToFrame(iframe);
    // ... interact with iframe content ...

    // CRITICAL: Always switch back to main frame before axe scan
    // (axe-core-npm 4.11.2 adds a guard, but explicit reset is still best practice)
    await browser.switchToParentFrame();

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ client: browser })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();

    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it('scans an iframe independently using include() with frame selector', async () => {
    await browser.url('/page-with-iframe');

    // To scan the iframe content specifically, use the iframe src approach
    // Note: @axe-core/playwright single-selector include/exclude limitation applies here too
    // Use frameLocator in Playwright instead; in WDIO, scan the iframe URL separately
    const iframeSrc = await $('iframe[name="content-frame"]').getAttribute('src');
    if (iframeSrc) {
      await browser.url(iframeSrc);
      const iframeResults = await new AxeBuilder({ client: browser })
        .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
        .analyze();
      expect(iframeResults.violations).toHaveLength(0);
    }
  });
});
```

### Pattern 11 (Cycle 24) — Playwright `getByRole` with `description` Parameter (v1.60)

Playwright v1.60 added a `description` option to `getByRole()` that matches elements by their accessible description (`aria-describedby` content). This is distinct from `name` (which matches the accessible name). Using `description` in role-based locators makes tests more precise when multiple elements share the same role and name but differ in their descriptive annotation — common in form fields with helper text or error messages.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/getByRole-description.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('getByRole description parameter (Playwright v1.60)', () => {
  test('selects password field by its specific description', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/register');

    // Both "Password" and "Confirm Password" have role=textbox, name=Password(ish)
    // The description distinguishes them via aria-describedby
    const passwordField = page.getByRole('textbox', {
      name: 'Password',
      description: 'Must be at least 8 characters and include a number',
    });
    await expect(passwordField).toBeVisible();
    await passwordField.fill('Secure123!');
  });

  test('verifies aria-describedby content is rendered and accessible', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/register');

    // Ensure the helper text referenced by aria-describedby is present in the DOM
    const passwordHint = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Password' });
    const descId = await passwordHint.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
    expect(descId).toBeTruthy();

    // The description element must exist and be non-empty
    if (descId) {
      const descEl = page.locator(`#${descId}`);
      await expect(descEl).toBeVisible();
      const descText = await descEl.textContent();
      expect(descText?.trim().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });

  test('error message is associated as description when field is invalid', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/register');

    // Submit empty form to trigger validation
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit|register/i }).click();

    // Error field should now have an aria-describedby pointing to the error message
    const emailField = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i });
    const descId = await emailField.getAttribute('aria-describedby');

    if (descId) {
      const errorEl = page.locator(`#${descId}`);
      await expect(errorEl).toBeVisible();
      // The description locator should now work with the error text
      const errorText = await errorEl.textContent();
      const fieldWithError = page.getByRole('textbox', {
        name: /email/i,
        description: errorText?.trim(),
      });
      await expect(fieldWithError).toBeVisible();
    }
  });
});
```

### Pattern 12 (Cycle 24) — Automated `<summary>` Disclosure Widget Full Test (axe + Playwright)

The `<details>/<summary>` HTML disclosure pattern is increasingly used as a lightweight alternative to custom accordion components. Beyond the `summary-name` axe rule (axe-core 4.10.0), test that the disclosure correctly toggles `open` attribute, that keyboard activation works, and that the expanded/collapsed state is conveyed to assistive technology via the browser's built-in semantics (no explicit ARIA needed for native `<details>`).

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/details-summary-disclosure.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('details/summary disclosure widget accessibility', () => {
  test('all summary elements have accessible names (axe-core 4.10 summary-name rule)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['summary-name'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('Enter key toggles details open/closed', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const summary = page.locator('summary').first();
    const details = page.locator('details').first();

    await summary.focus();
    // Native details: closed by default
    await expect(details).not.toHaveAttribute('open');

    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
    await expect(details).toHaveAttribute('open');

    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
    await expect(details).not.toHaveAttribute('open');
  });

  test('Space key also activates summary (native button behavior)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const summary = page.locator('summary').first();
    const details = page.locator('details').first();

    await summary.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
    await expect(details).toHaveAttribute('open');
  });

  test('details content is hidden from AT when closed', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const firstDetails = page.locator('details').first();

    // When closed, the content inside (but not the summary) must not be
    // accessible to AT — the browser handles this natively via the open attribute
    const isOpen = await firstDetails.evaluate((el) => (el as HTMLDetailsElement).open);
    if (!isOpen) {
      // The aria snapshot should show the content as hidden/not present
      await expect(firstDetails).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
        - group:
          - button /.*/ [expanded=false]
      `);
    }
  });
});
```
