### Pattern 13 (Cycle 24) — Color Contrast for Non-Text Elements: WCAG 1.4.11 Automated Scan

WCAG 1.4.11 (AA) requires that UI component boundaries (button borders, input field outlines, focus indicators, chart data series, icon strokes) meet 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors. axe-core covers this via the `color-contrast` rule, but the rule is limited for non-text elements on complex backgrounds. Use targeted axe scans on specific component types plus a Playwright computed-style check as a belt-and-suspenders approach.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/non-text-contrast.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('WCAG 1.4.11 Non-Text Contrast', () => {
  test('form controls meet 3:1 contrast requirement', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');

    // axe-core checks non-text contrast for form controls automatically
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['color-contrast-enhanced'])
      .analyze();

    const nonTextFailures = results.violations.filter(
      (v) => v.id === 'color-contrast-enhanced' || v.id === 'color-contrast'
    );
    expect(nonTextFailures).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('focus ring has sufficient contrast against page background', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');

    // Tab to the first interactive element to trigger the focus ring
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focused = page.locator(':focus');
    await expect(focused).toBeVisible();

    // Read the focus ring computed styles
    const focusStyles = await focused.evaluate((el) => {
      const computed = window.getComputedStyle(el);
      return {
        outlineColor: computed.outlineColor,
        outlineStyle: computed.outlineStyle,
        outlineWidth: computed.outlineWidth,
        backgroundColor: window.getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor,
      };
    });

    // Verify a focus ring is actually present (not outline: none without replacement)
    expect(
      focusStyles.outlineStyle,
      'Focus ring must be visible — outline:none without replacement fails WCAG 2.4.7'
    ).not.toBe('none');
    expect(parseFloat(focusStyles.outlineWidth)).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('icon-only buttons have sufficient non-text contrast', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    // Find icon-only buttons (no visible text, relying on SVG/icon for visual affordance)
    const iconButtons = page.locator('button').filter({ hasText: '' })
      .filter({ has: page.locator('svg, img, [class*="icon"]') });

    const count = await iconButtons.count();
    if (count > 0) {
      // Run axe targeted at icon buttons
      const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .include('button svg, button img')
        .withRules(['color-contrast'])
        .analyze();
      // Log but don't fail — axe has limited non-text contrast detection capability
      if (results.violations.length > 0) {
        console.warn('Potential icon contrast violations (requires manual verification):', results.violations);
      }
    }
  });
});
```

---

### Pattern 14 (Cycle 24) — `aria-roledescription` Testing for Custom Widget Labels

`aria-roledescription` overrides the role name announced by screen readers. It should only be used on elements that have semantic roles (not on generic elements) and only when the default role name is genuinely confusing — it never overrides `aria-label`. A common misuse is applying `aria-roledescription` to a `<div>` with no role, which becomes meaningless. Test that `aria-roledescription` is only present alongside a meaningful ARIA role.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/aria-roledescription.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('aria-roledescription usage validation', () => {
  test('aria-roledescription is only used on elements with a meaningful role', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    const elementsWithRoleDesc = page.locator('[aria-roledescription]');
    const count = await elementsWithRoleDesc.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const el = elementsWithRoleDesc.nth(i);
      const tagName = await el.evaluate((e) => e.tagName.toLowerCase());
      const role = await el.getAttribute('role');

      // Semantic HTML elements have implicit roles; generic ones (div, span) need explicit role
      const semanticElements = ['button', 'a', 'input', 'select', 'textarea', 'nav', 'main', 'aside'];
      const hasImplicitRole = semanticElements.includes(tagName);
      const hasExplicitRole = role !== null && role !== 'none' && role !== 'presentation';

      expect(
        hasImplicitRole || hasExplicitRole,
        `<${tagName}> with aria-roledescription has no semantic role — screen readers will ignore it`
      ).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test('carousel uses aria-roledescription="carousel" and "slide" correctly', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/home');

    const carousel = page.locator('[aria-roledescription="carousel"]');
    if (await carousel.count() > 0) {
      // Carousel container must have region or group role
      const containerRole = await carousel.getAttribute('role');
      expect(['region', 'group']).toContain(containerRole);

      // Each slide must have group role with aria-roledescription="slide"
      const slides = carousel.locator('[aria-roledescription="slide"]');
      const slideCount = await slides.count();
      for (let i = 0; i < slideCount; i++) {
        const slideRole = await slides.nth(i).getAttribute('role');
        expect(['group', 'tabpanel']).toContain(slideRole);
      }
    }
  });
});
```

---

### Pattern 15 (Cycle 24) — `@axe-core/vitest` Integration for Component Unit Tests

`@axe-core/vitest` (Deque's first-party Vitest integration) provides `toHaveNoViolations()` as a native Vitest matcher, avoiding the Jest v30 compatibility issues that affect `jest-axe` v10. It works with Vitest's `jsdom` or `happy-dom` environments. Note the same jsdom limitation: color contrast rules cannot be evaluated without a real browser — use `disableRules(['color-contrast'])` in unit-level component tests and rely on Playwright page-level scans for contrast.

```typescript
// vitest.setup.ts
import { toHaveNoViolations } from '@axe-core/vitest';
import { expect } from 'vitest';
expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

// tests/components/button.a11y.spec.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { axe } from '@axe-core/vitest';
import { Button } from '../../src/components/Button';

describe('Button component accessibility (@axe-core/vitest)', () => {
  it('icon-only button with aria-label has no violations', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <Button aria-label="Close dialog" icon="X" />
    );
    const results = await axe(container, {
      // jsdom cannot compute color contrast — disable in unit tests
      rules: { 'color-contrast': { enabled: false } },
    });
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('loading state button with aria-busy is accessible', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <Button loading={true} aria-label="Submitting form">Submit</Button>
    );
    const results = await axe(container, {
      rules: { 'color-contrast': { enabled: false } },
    });
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('disabled button is distinguishable from enabled', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <Button disabled aria-label="Submit (unavailable)">Submit</Button>
    );
    const results = await axe(container, {
      rules: { 'color-contrast': { enabled: false } },
    });
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('button group has no duplicate accessible names', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <div role="group" aria-label="Sort options">
        <Button aria-label="Sort ascending">↑</Button>
        <Button aria-label="Sort descending">↓</Button>
      </div>
    );
    const results = await axe(container, {
      rules: { 'color-contrast': { enabled: false } },
    });
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });
});
```

### Pattern 16 (Cycle 24) — `toHaveCSS` with `pseudo` for Focus Ring Validation (Playwright v1.60)

Playwright v1.60 added a `pseudo` option to `toHaveCSS()` enabling assertions on `::before` and `::after` computed styles. For focus indicators implemented via `::after` pseudo-elements (a common design-system pattern to avoid affecting layout), `toHaveCSS({ pseudo: '::after' })` validates the focus ring without needing to navigate into the shadow DOM or use JavaScript `getComputedStyle`.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/focus-ring-pseudo-element.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Focus ring via ::after pseudo-element (Playwright v1.60 toHaveCSS pseudo)', () => {
  test('focused button displays ::after focus ring with sufficient width', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const firstButton = page.getByRole('button').first();
    await firstButton.focus();

    // Assert the ::after pseudo-element creates the visible focus ring
    // Design system pattern: focus ring is a pseudo-element to avoid layout shift
    await expect(firstButton).toHaveCSS('outline-style', 'none'); // no default outline

    // The ::after ring should have a visible border
    await expect(firstButton).toHaveCSS('border-width', /[2-9]px|[1-9][0-9]+px/, {
      pseudo: '::after',
    });
    await expect(firstButton).toHaveCSS('border-style', 'solid', { pseudo: '::after' });
  });

  test('::after focus ring is not present when button is not focused', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const button = page.getByRole('button').first();

    // Without focus, the ::after content should be empty or element should not exist
    // (This tests that focus ring only appears on focus, not always)
    const contentValue = await button.evaluate((el) => {
      return window.getComputedStyle(el, '::after').getPropertyValue('content');
    });
    // content: none or '' means pseudo-element not rendered
    const hasFocusRingWithoutFocus = contentValue !== 'none' && contentValue !== '""' && contentValue !== '';
    // This is an informational check — log if unexpected
    if (hasFocusRingWithoutFocus) {
      console.warn('Focus ring pseudo-element may be always visible — verify with design team');
    }
  });
});
```

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 24)

123. **[community] Pa11y v9.1.0's `--level-cap-when-needs-review` flag is ignored when using the `axe` runner — it only applies to the default `htmlcs` runner**: Pa11y v9.1.0 introduced the `levelCapWhenNeedsReview` option to prevent "needs review" CodeSniffer results from failing CI gates. However, the `axe` runner uses axe-core's own severity model (`minor`, `moderate`, `serious`, `critical`), which has no concept of "needs review." Items flagged as `incomplete` by axe-core (axe's term for "needs review") are not subject to the `levelCapWhenNeedsReview` option and are reported at their original severity level. WHY: Teams that switch Pa11y's runner to `axe` for better WCAG 2.2 coverage are surprised when previously-passing CI gates start failing because axe's `incomplete` results are no longer capped. Use separate Pa11y configurations for the htmlcs and axe runners when you need different severity handling.

124. **[community] axe-core 4.11.0 added RGAA tags but the `best-practice` tag alone does NOT include the four new RGAA-required rules (`focus-order-semantics`, `region`, `skip-link`, `table-duplicate-name`) — you must explicitly include them with `withRules()` or use `withTags(['best-practice'])` in combination with `wcag2a`**: The axe-core docs describe RGAA rules as tagged with both their WCAG equivalents and `best-practice`. However, if your test uses only `withTags(['wcag2aa'])`, these four rules are skipped. The `best-practice` tag must be added explicitly: `withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'best-practice'])`. WHY: Many teams copy the standard `wcag2aa` tag pattern from documentation and assume it covers all compliance-mandated checks. RGAA-targeted applications will have a gap in their CI coverage until they add the `best-practice` tag.

125. **[community] Playwright `getByRole(role, { description })` matches against the full `aria-describedby` text, not a substring — if the description element contains dynamic content (error counts, field names), the match will fail unless you use a regex**: The new `description` parameter in `getByRole()` (Playwright v1.60) performs an exact string match by default, the same way `name` does. If your `aria-describedby` element reads "3 errors found in this section," you cannot use `{ description: 'errors' }` — you must use `{ description: /errors/ }` (regex) to match a partial description. WHY: This is consistent with how `name` works in Playwright, but teams often expect partial matching by default since it matches how `getByText()` operates (substring by default). Document the regex pattern as the standard approach for dynamic descriptions.

126. **[community] `aria-roledescription` is not announced by NVDA when the element is in Browse mode (document reading mode) — it only takes effect in Forms/Application mode when the user is actively interacting**: NVDA operates in two modes: Browse mode (arrow keys navigate virtual document structure) and Forms/Application mode (keyboard events go to the application). `aria-roledescription` is only announced during Forms mode when the screen reader hands keyboard control to the widget. If users are in Browse mode reading through the page with arrow keys, they will hear the default role name, not the custom `aria-roledescription`. WHY: Teams implement custom role descriptions for carousel slides (`aria-roledescription="slide"`) and assume NVDA users will hear "slide" as they arrow through. They only hear "slide" when they Tab-focus into the carousel in Forms mode. Design carousel instructions to work in both modes.

127. **[community] The ARIA Authoring Practices Guide carousel pattern requirement that "auto-rotation stops on hover" is NOT testable in Playwright's CDP-based Chromium automation — `page.hover()` does not trigger CSS `:hover` pseudo-class reliably in headless mode**: Playwright's `.hover()` method uses Chrome DevTools Protocol input dispatch, which does trigger mousemove events but may not trigger CSS `:hover` transitions reliably in headless Chromium. The carousel's stop-on-hover behavior should be tested as an interaction-based event listener test (`mouseenter`/`mouseleave` event dispatch) rather than a CSS hover state test. WHY: Teams write `await carousel.hover(); await expect(autoPlayButton).toHaveAttribute('aria-pressed', 'false')` and find it passes locally but fails in CI headless mode because the hover-triggered JavaScript event does not fire consistently.

128. **[community] `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` in Playwright counts ALL interactive descendant elements recursively — a page with a complex navigation produces a huge ARIA snapshot that breaks when any navigation item is added or removed, making the test extremely brittle**: The `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` assertion compares the full ARIA tree of the matched locator. For high-level locators like `page.locator('body')` or `page.getByRole('main')`, this captures hundreds of nodes. A navigation link added during a sprint will fail every snapshot test targeting the whole page. Best practice: scope `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` to specific components (`page.getByRole('dialog')`, `page.getByRole('tabpanel')`) and use `{ mode: 'partial' }` (Playwright v1.57+) for open-ended validation that checks only what you care about. WHY: Snapshot tests are meant to detect unintended regressions, not document every interactive element on the page. Scoped snapshots are more resilient and easier to review in PRs.

129. **[community] `@axe-core/react` does not work with React 18's automatic batching — axe violations may be reported for intermediate component states (empty labels, missing aria attributes during re-render) that resolve within the same tick**: React 18 introduced automatic batching that defers state updates into single render cycles. `@axe-core/react` is initialized via `axe.run()` on a MutationObserver callback, which may fire during an intermediate batched state where components have not yet received their final props. The result is false-positive violations for missing `aria-label` or empty roles. Mitigate by wrapping your axe initialization with `React.startTransition()` or using `act()` in tests to flush all pending updates before the axe scan fires. WHY: Teams see violations in Storybook that disappear when the component is fully rendered, leading to "works on my machine" confusion between developers and QA.

### Pattern 1 (Cycle 25) — WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance: Programmatic Area + Contrast Validation (Level AAA)

WCAG 2.4.13 (Level AAA) mandates that keyboard focus indicators meet both a **minimum area** and a **change-of-contrast** requirement. The minimum area is equivalent to a 2 CSS px thick perimeter around the unfocused component (formula: `4h + 4w` for rectangles). The contrast requirement is 3:1 between focused and unfocused states — this measures the **change** of contrast (focused vs unfocused pixel colors at the same position), not adjacent contrast. Unlike 2.4.7 (Focus Visible) and 2.4.11/2.4.12 (Focus Not Obscured), SC 2.4.13 is the only criterion that quantifies how visible the indicator must be. Testing requires extracting computed CSS, calculating area, and computing luminance delta between focused/unfocused pixel colors.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/focus-appearance-2-4-13.spec.ts
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

/** Compute WCAG relative luminance from an rgb() string e.g. "rgb(0, 0, 0)" */
function relativeLuminance(rgbString: string): number {
  const m = rgbString.match(/rgb\((\d+),\s*(\d+),\s*(\d+)\)/);
  if (!m) throw new Error(`Cannot parse color: ${rgbString}`);
  return [1, 2, 3].reduce((acc, i, idx) => {
    const c = parseInt(m[i]) / 255;
    const linear = c <= 0.04045 ? c / 12.92 : ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4;
    return acc + linear * [0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722][idx];
  }, 0);
}

function contrastRatio(l1: number, l2: number): number {
  const lighter = Math.max(l1, l2);
  const darker = Math.min(l1, l2);
  return (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05);
}

async function getFocusAppearanceData(page: Page, selector: string) {
  const el = page.locator(selector);
  const unfocusedBg = await el.evaluate((node) =>
    window.getComputedStyle(node).backgroundColor
  );
  await el.focus();
  const focusedOutlineColor = await el.evaluate((node) =>
    window.getComputedStyle(node).outlineColor
  );
  const focusedOutlineWidth = await el.evaluate((node) =>
    parseFloat(window.getComputedStyle(node).outlineWidth)
  );
  return { unfocusedBg, focusedOutlineColor, focusedOutlineWidth };
}

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (Level AAA)', () => {
  test('primary button focus indicator meets minimum area and contrast', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/buttons');
    const data = await getFocusAppearanceData(page, 'button[data-testid="primary-btn"]');

    // 1. Area check: outline must be ≥ 2px (sufficient for a simple perimeter indicator)
    expect(data.focusedOutlineWidth,
      `Outline width ${data.focusedOutlineWidth}px — must be ≥ 2px for SC 2.4.13`
    ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);

    // 2. Change-of-contrast check: 3:1 between focused indicator color and unfocused bg
    const indicatorL = relativeLuminance(data.focusedOutlineColor);
    const bgL = relativeLuminance(data.unfocusedBg);
    const changeContrast = contrastRatio(indicatorL, bgL);
    expect(changeContrast,
      `Focus indicator change-contrast ${changeContrast.toFixed(2)}:1 — must be ≥ 3:1`
    ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);
  });

  test('icon button with ::after pseudo-element ring meets SC 2.4.13', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/icon-buttons');
    const iconBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Close' });
    await iconBtn.focus();

    // If outline is none, the design system must use ::after ring instead
    const outlineStyle = await iconBtn.evaluate((el) =>
      window.getComputedStyle(el).outlineStyle
    );
    if (outlineStyle === 'none') {
      const afterBorderWidth = await iconBtn.evaluate((el) =>
        parseFloat(window.getComputedStyle(el, '::after').borderWidth)
      );
      expect(afterBorderWidth,
        `::after border-width must be ≥ 2px for SC 2.4.13 pseudo-element rings`
      ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);

      const afterBorderStyle = await iconBtn.evaluate((el) =>
        window.getComputedStyle(el, '::after').borderStyle
      );
      expect(afterBorderStyle).not.toBe('none');
    }
  });

  test('SC 2.4.13 exception: unmodified native focus on <select> is exempt', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/forms/select-demo');
    // Native <select> elements managed entirely by the user agent are exempt
    // from SC 2.4.13 — verify the test infrastructure does not flag them as failures
    const select = page.getByRole('combobox');
    if (await select.count() > 0) {
      await select.focus();
      // Simply verify the select is focusable — SC 2.4.13 does not apply
      const isSelectElement = await select.evaluate((el) => el.tagName === 'SELECT');
      // Native SELECT: exempt from SC 2.4.13 — skip the indicator check
      if (!isSelectElement) {
        // Custom combobox: must have visible focus indicator
        const outlineWidth = await select.evaluate((el) =>
          parseFloat(window.getComputedStyle(el).outlineWidth)
        );
        expect(outlineWidth).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      }
    }
  });
});
```

### Pattern 2 (Cycle 25) — ARIA 1.3 Text Annotation Roles: `insertion`, `deletion`, `mark`, `suggestion` Testing

ARIA 1.3 (First Public Working Draft, January 2024) introduces semantic roles for inline document annotations used in collaborative editing: `insertion` (added text), `deletion` (removed text), `mark` (highlighted text), and `suggestion` (proposed change containing both `insertion` and `deletion` children). These roles map to HTML `<ins>`, `<del>`, `<mark>` but are needed for custom rich text editors (ProseMirror, Slate, Tiptap) that render `<span>` elements with these ARIA roles. A critical spec constraint: `insertion`, `deletion`, and `mark` roles **prohibit `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`** — their accessible name must come from text content only. Testing must verify the correct role, absence of prohibited attributes, and structural parent-child relationships for `suggestion`.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/aria-1-3-annotation-roles.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('ARIA 1.3 text annotation roles (insertion, deletion, mark, suggestion)', () => {
  test('rich text editor track-changes renders correct ARIA 1.3 roles', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/editor/track-changes-demo');

    const insertions = page.locator('[role="insertion"]');
    await expect(insertions.first()).toBeVisible();

    // Prohibited attributes: annotation roles must NOT have aria-label/aria-labelledby
    // Name comes from text content only (per ARIA 1.3 spec)
    const count = await insertions.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      await expect(insertions.nth(i)).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-label');
      await expect(insertions.nth(i)).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    }

    // Deletion role
    const deletions = page.locator('[role="deletion"]');
    if (await deletions.count() > 0) {
      await expect(deletions.first()).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-label');
    }

    // Suggestion wrapper must contain at least one insertion or deletion child
    const suggestions = page.locator('[role="suggestion"]');
    if (await suggestions.count() > 0) {
      const hasAnnotationChild = await suggestions.first().evaluate((el) =>
        el.querySelector('[role="insertion"],[role="deletion"]') !== null
      );
      expect(hasAnnotationChild,
        'role="suggestion" must contain at least one insertion or deletion child per ARIA 1.3'
      ).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test('aria snapshot includes annotation roles in document structure', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/editor/track-changes-demo');
    const editorRegion = page.getByRole('region', { name: 'Document Editor' });
    await expect(editorRegion).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - region "Document Editor":
        - /insertion|deletion|mark/
    `, { mode: 'partial' });
  });

  test('axe passes on annotation role page — no prohibited-attribute violations', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/editor/track-changes-demo');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'best-practice'])
      .analyze();
    const annotationViolations = results.violations.filter((v) =>
      v.nodes.some((n) => n.target.some((t) =>
        typeof t === 'string' && /insertion|deletion|mark|suggestion/.test(t)
      ))
    );
    expect(annotationViolations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

### Pattern 3 (Cycle 25) — Virtual List Accessibility: `aria-setsize` + `aria-posinset` with Scroll Validation

Virtualized lists (react-window, TanStack Virtual) render only visible items, causing screen readers to announce incorrect counts ("item 1 of 10" when 10,000 items exist). The correct pattern: the outer container has `role="listbox"` and each rendered item has `aria-setsize` set to the total count and `aria-posinset` to its actual position (not DOM index). Both attributes must update as the user scrolls. Testing must verify these attributes are correct at mount, update on scroll, and that keyboard navigation (`ArrowDown`) keeps focus within the virtual list without losing the DOM element.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/virtual-list-aria.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Virtual list ARIA position-in-set correctness', () => {
  test('visible items have correct aria-setsize and aria-posinset at mount', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/virtual-list?totalItems=10000');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="option"][aria-posinset]');

    const firstItem = page.locator('[role="option"]').first();
    await expect(firstItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-setsize', '10000');
    await expect(firstItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-posinset', '1');
  });

  test('aria-posinset updates correctly after programmatic scroll', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/virtual-list?totalItems=10000');
    await page.evaluate(() => {
      const list = document.querySelector('[role="listbox"]') as HTMLElement;
      list.scrollTop = 4000; // scroll ~100 items at 40px each
    });
    await page.waitForTimeout(100); // allow virtual re-render

    const firstVisible = page.locator('[role="option"][aria-posinset]').first();
    const posinset = parseInt(await firstVisible.getAttribute('aria-posinset') ?? '1');
    expect(posinset).toBeGreaterThan(1); // must reflect actual position, not DOM index

    // aria-setsize must remain 10000 after scroll (not reset to visible count)
    await expect(firstVisible).toHaveAttribute('aria-setsize', '10000');
  });

  test('virtual list keyboard navigation updates aria-activedescendant', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/virtual-list?totalItems=500');
    const list = page.getByRole('listbox');
    await list.focus();

    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    }
    const activeDescendant = await list.getAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
    expect(activeDescendant, 'aria-activedescendant must update on ArrowDown').toBeTruthy();

    const activeItem = page.locator(`#${activeDescendant}`);
    await expect(activeItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-posinset', '6');
  });

  test('virtual list does NOT use aria-rowcount/rowindex for non-grid lists [community]', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/virtual-list');
    // Grid attributes must only appear on role="grid", not role="listbox"
    const listboxEl = page.getByRole('listbox');
    await expect(listboxEl).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-rowcount');
    const firstOption = page.locator('[role="option"]').first();
    await expect(firstOption).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-rowindex');
  });
});
```

### Pattern 4 (Cycle 25) — Accessible Data Table: `scope`, `headers`, `aria-sort`, and Caption Validation

Complex data tables are one of the highest-failure areas in real-world accessibility audits. WCAG 1.3.1 requires tables to convey structure via `<th scope="col|row|colgroup|rowgroup">` or `id/headers` association. Automated axe catches ~40% of table failures; structural validation requires explicit assertions. Tests must verify: (1) every `<th>` has `scope` or `id`, (2) complex `<td>` cells use `headers`, (3) sort buttons update `aria-sort` with exactly one column sorted at a time, (4) caption or `aria-label` provides a table summary for screen readers.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/data-table-structure.spec.ts
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

async function validateTableStructure(page: Page, tableSelector: string) {
  return page.evaluate((sel) => {
    const table = document.querySelector(sel) as HTMLTableElement;
    if (!table) return { valid: false, errors: ['Table not found'] };
    const errors: string[] = [];

    table.querySelectorAll('th').forEach((th, i) => {
      if (!th.getAttribute('scope') && !th.id) {
        errors.push(`th[${i}] "${th.textContent?.trim()}" missing scope or id`);
      }
    });

    const caption = table.querySelector('caption');
    const ariaLabel = table.getAttribute('aria-label');
    const ariaLabelledBy = table.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    if (!caption && !ariaLabel && !ariaLabelledBy) {
      errors.push('Table missing caption, aria-label, or aria-labelledby');
    }

    return { valid: errors.length === 0, errors };
  }, tableSelector);
}

test.describe('Data table accessibility structure', () => {
  test('sortable table has correct structure, caption, and aria-sort lifecycle', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/reports/data-table');

    const tableCheck = await validateTableStructure(page, 'table[data-testid="report-table"]');
    expect(tableCheck.errors, tableCheck.errors.join('\n')).toHaveLength(0);

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include('table[data-testid="report-table"]')
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);

    // aria-sort lifecycle: none → ascending → descending → none
    const nameHeader = page.getByRole('columnheader', { name: 'Name' });
    await expect(nameHeader).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'none');

    await nameHeader.click();
    await expect(nameHeader).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'ascending');

    await nameHeader.click();
    await expect(nameHeader).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'descending');

    // Only ONE column may be sorted at a time
    const allSorted = page.locator('[aria-sort="ascending"], [aria-sort="descending"]');
    await expect(allSorted).toHaveCount(1);
  });

  test('table structure remains valid after pagination', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/reports/data-table');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Next page' }).click();
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const tableCheck = await validateTableStructure(page, 'table[data-testid="report-table"]');
    expect(tableCheck.errors).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

### Pattern 5 (Cycle 25) — ARIA Live Region Debounce Validation: Ensuring Single Final Announcement

`aria-live` regions are misimplemented in two common ways: (1) rapid DOM updates cause flooding where screen readers announce every intermediate state, and (2) clear-then-refill patterns cause announcements to be dropped entirely (screen readers see the empty state and stop tracking). The correct debounce pattern: update the live region once with the final value. Testing must verify that a sequence of rapid updates produces at most two meaningful announcements (e.g., "Searching..." + final result count), and that the region is never set to empty before being refilled.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/aria-live-debounce.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA live region announcement quality', () => {
  test('search status announces final result count only — not one per keystroke', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    const announcements: string[] = [];
    await page.exposeFunction('recordAnnouncement', (text: string) => {
      if (text.trim()) announcements.push(text.trim());
    });

    await page.evaluate(() => {
      const liveRegion = document.querySelector('[aria-live]');
      if (!liveRegion) return;
      const observer = new MutationObserver(() => {
        (window as any).recordAnnouncement(liveRegion.textContent ?? '');
      });
      observer.observe(liveRegion, { childList: true, subtree: true, characterData: true });
    });

    await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill('accessible');
    await page.waitForTimeout(600); // allow debounce to settle

    // If debounce works: ≤2 announcements ("Searching..." + result count)
    // If broken: 8+ announcements (one per keystroke)
    const meaningfulAnnouncements = announcements.filter((a) => a !== 'Searching...');
    expect(
      meaningfulAnnouncements.length,
      `Got ${meaningfulAnnouncements.length} result announcements — expected 1 (debounce failure): ${JSON.stringify(announcements)}`
    ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(2);

    const finalAnnouncement = announcements[announcements.length - 1] ?? '';
    expect(finalAnnouncement).toMatch(/\d+ result/i);
  });

  test('live region is NOT emptied then refilled — causes announcement drop in all screen readers', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    let emptyThenFillDetected = false;
    await page.exposeFunction('onLiveRegionMutation', (wasEmpty: boolean, newContent: string) => {
      if (wasEmpty && newContent) emptyThenFillDetected = true;
    });

    await page.evaluate(() => {
      const liveRegion = document.querySelector('[aria-live]');
      if (!liveRegion) return;
      let prevWasEmpty = false;
      const observer = new MutationObserver(() => {
        const current = liveRegion.textContent ?? '';
        (window as any).onLiveRegionMutation(prevWasEmpty, current);
        prevWasEmpty = current.trim() === '';
      });
      observer.observe(liveRegion, { childList: true, subtree: true, characterData: true });
    });

    await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill('button');
    await page.waitForTimeout(600);

    expect(
      emptyThenFillDetected,
      'Live region was cleared then immediately refilled — NVDA/JAWS will DROP the announcement'
    ).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

### Pattern 6 (Cycle 25) — `axe-core` `resultTypes` Performance Optimization

Running `axe.run()` with full result collection on pages with 800+ DOM nodes takes 2–8 seconds because computing `passes` and `inapplicable` requires testing every element against every rule that does not apply. Limiting `resultTypes` to `['violations', 'incomplete']` reduces scan time to ~0.4s (8× speedup). The tradeoff: `passes` data is unavailable, so you cannot assert "this rule passed." Use the optimized scan for CI gates and the full scan for accessibility reports.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/axe-performance-scan.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

async function fastAxeScan(
  page: import('@playwright/test').Page,
  options?: { include?: string; tags?: string[] }
) {
  const builder = new AxeBuilder({ page });
  if (options?.include) builder.include(options.include);
  builder.withTags(options?.tags ?? ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa']);
  // Omit 'passes' and 'inapplicable' — 5-8x faster on large DOMs
  return builder.options({ resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'] }).analyze();
}

test.describe('axe-core optimized scan for CI gates', () => {
  test('full-page fast scan completes within 2s CI performance budget', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    const start = Date.now();
    const results = await fastAxeScan(page);
    const duration = Date.now() - start;

    expect(duration,
      `Scan took ${duration}ms — verify resultTypes optimization is applied`
    ).toBeLessThan(2000);
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('component-scoped scan — form only (10-20x faster than full page)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/forms/checkout');
    const results = await fastAxeScan(page, {
      include: '[data-testid="checkout-form"]',
    });
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('incomplete results are logged for manual review — do not silently ignore', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/forms/checkout');
    const results = await fastAxeScan(page);

    if (results.incomplete.length > 0) {
      // Attach to test report for manual review cycle
      console.log('axe incomplete (needs manual review):',
        results.incomplete.map((r) => `${r.id}: ${r.description}`)
      );
    }
    // Enforce critical violations only in CI gate
    const criticalViolations = results.violations.filter(
      (v) => v.impact === 'critical' || v.impact === 'serious'
    );
    expect(criticalViolations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

### Pattern 7 (Cycle 25) — Keyboard Tab-Order Snapshot with Positive-Tabindex Anti-Pattern Detection

Tab order should match visual reading order (WCAG 2.4.3). A common failure is using positive `tabindex` values (`tabindex="1"`, `tabindex="2"`) which pull elements to the front of the tab sequence, creating a confusing navigation order. The correct approach: all interactive elements use `tabindex="0"` (or rely on DOM order) and `tabindex="-1"` only for programmatically focused elements. Testing should: (1) detect any positive tabindex values, (2) snapshot the tab order sequence to catch unintended regressions, (3) verify modal dialogs trap focus correctly (WCAG 2.1.2).

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/tab-order.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface FocusableElement {
  tag: string; text: string; tabindex: string | null;
}

async function collectTabOrder(page: import('@playwright/test').Page): Promise<FocusableElement[]> {
  return page.evaluate(() => {
    const selectors = [
      'a[href]', 'button:not([disabled])', 'input:not([disabled])',
      'select:not([disabled])', 'textarea:not([disabled])',
      '[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])',
    ].join(', ');
    const elements = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(selectors));
    const withPositive = elements
      .filter((el) => parseInt(el.getAttribute('tabindex') ?? '0') > 0)
      .sort((a, b) => parseInt(a.getAttribute('tabindex')!) - parseInt(b.getAttribute('tabindex')!));
    const withoutPositive = elements.filter(
      (el) => !(parseInt(el.getAttribute('tabindex') ?? '0') > 0)
    );
    return [...withPositive, ...withoutPositive].map((el) => ({
      tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
      text: (el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? el.textContent ?? '').trim().slice(0, 50),
      tabindex: el.getAttribute('tabindex'),
    }));
  });
}

test.describe('Keyboard tab order validation', () => {
  test('no positive tabindex values on the page (positive tabindex is an anti-pattern)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const tabOrder = await collectTabOrder(page);
    const positiveTabindex = tabOrder.filter(
      (el) => el.tabindex !== null && parseInt(el.tabindex) > 0
    );
    expect(
      positiveTabindex,
      `Positive tabindex breaks DOM tab order: ${JSON.stringify(positiveTabindex)}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('checkout form tab order snapshot regression', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/forms/checkout');
    const tabOrder = await collectTabOrder(page);
    expect(tabOrder.map((el) => `${el.tag}: ${el.text}`))
      .toMatchSnapshot('checkout-tab-order.txt');
  });

  test('modal dialog traps focus (WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open modal' }).click();
    await page.getByRole('dialog').waitFor({ state: 'visible' });

    // Tab 10 times — focus must stay inside the dialog
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    }
    const focusInDialog = await page.evaluate(() =>
      document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]')?.contains(document.activeElement) ?? false
    );
    expect(focusInDialog, 'Focus escaped the modal dialog — keyboard trap is broken').toBe(true);
  });
});
```

### Pattern 8 (Cycle 25) — Dark Mode and High Contrast Color Contrast Testing

Many teams test color contrast only in light mode, creating dark mode regressions invisible in standard CI. Playwright's `emulateMedia()` allows testing contrast across `colorScheme: 'dark'`, `forcedColors: 'active'` (Windows High Contrast), and `reducedMotion: 'reduce'`. The `forcedColors` emulation sets the `forced-colors: active` media query but does NOT suppress `background-image` the way Windows OS does — use it to test the CSS media query branch, then separately verify icon-only buttons have accessible text names independent of background images.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/contrast-modes.spec.ts
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

async function contrastScanInMode(
  page: Page,
  mode: { colorScheme?: 'dark' | 'light'; forcedColors?: 'active' | 'none' },
  url: string
) {
  await page.emulateMedia(mode);
  await page.goto(url);
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
  return new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withRules(['color-contrast', 'color-contrast-enhanced'])
    .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
    .analyze();
}

test.describe('Color contrast across media modes', () => {
  test('light mode passes WCAG 1.4.3', async ({ page }) => {
    const results = await contrastScanInMode(page, { colorScheme: 'light' }, '/');
    expect(results.violations.filter((v) => v.id === 'color-contrast')).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('dark mode passes WCAG 1.4.3 — catches CSS custom-property regression', async ({ page }) => {
    const results = await contrastScanInMode(page, { colorScheme: 'dark' }, '/');
    const failures = results.violations.filter((v) => v.id === 'color-contrast');
    expect(
      failures,
      `Dark mode contrast failures (check CSS --color-* custom properties): ${JSON.stringify(failures.map((v) => ({ id: v.id, nodes: v.nodes.map((n) => n.html.slice(0, 80)) })), null, 2)}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('forcedColors mode: all interactive elements have accessible text names (not only background icons)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' });
    await page.goto('/');

    // In true WHCM, background-image icons vanish — verify no icon-only buttons exist
    const buttons = page.getByRole('button');
    const count = await buttons.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 10); i++) {
      const btn = buttons.nth(i);
      const name = await btn.evaluate((el) =>
        el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? el.getAttribute('aria-labelledby') ?? el.textContent?.trim() ?? ''
      );
      expect(name.length, `Button ${i} has no accessible name — will be unlabeled in Windows High Contrast`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });

  test('prefers-reduced-motion: loading indicators remain visible and announced', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
    await page.goto('/components/loading-spinner');
    const spinner = page.getByRole('status', { name: /loading/i });
    if (await spinner.count() > 0) {
      await expect(spinner).toBeVisible();
      await expect(spinner).toHaveAttribute('aria-label');
    }
  });
});
```

### Pattern 9 (Cycle 25) — Focus Appearance Area Calculation for Rounded-Corner Pill Buttons

For buttons with large `border-radius` values (pill buttons are common in modern design systems), the SC 2.4.13 minimum area formula must account for reduced corner perimeter. A 2px perimeter of a rectangle is `(4h + 4w) × 2px`; a pill button (border-radius = height/2) approximates a stadium shape with perimeter `2(w - h) + πh`. Use the correct formula per component shape when computing whether the focus indicator area meets the AAA threshold.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/focus-appearance-geometry.spec.ts
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

/** Minimum focus area in px² for a 2px-thick perimeter indicator per SC 2.4.13 */
function minimumFocusArea(w: number, h: number, borderRadius: number): number {
  const r = Math.min(borderRadius, Math.min(w, h) / 2);
  const straightEdgesPerimeter = 2 * (w - 2 * r) + 2 * (h - 2 * r);
  const cornerCircumference = 2 * Math.PI * r;
  return (straightEdgesPerimeter + cornerCircumference) * 2; // 2px thick
}

async function measureFocusGeometry(page: Page, selector: string) {
  const el = page.locator(selector);
  await el.focus();
  return el.evaluate((node) => {
    const cs = window.getComputedStyle(node);
    const box = node.getBoundingClientRect();
    return {
      width: box.width,
      height: box.height,
      borderRadius: parseFloat(cs.borderRadius) || 0,
      outlineWidth: parseFloat(cs.outlineWidth) || 0,
    };
  });
}

test.describe('SC 2.4.13 focus area — rounded-corner pill buttons', () => {
  test('pill button focus indicator meets minimum area with border-radius correction', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/buttons');
    const geo = await measureFocusGeometry(page, 'button[data-variant="pill"]');

    const requiredArea = minimumFocusArea(geo.width, geo.height, geo.borderRadius);
    // Outline perimeter area: thickness × (full outer perimeter)
    const outerW = geo.width + 2 * geo.outlineWidth;
    const outerH = geo.height + 2 * geo.outlineWidth;
    const outerPerimeter = 2 * (outerW + outerH); // simplified rectangle approximation
    const actualArea = geo.outlineWidth * outerPerimeter;

    expect(actualArea,
      `Pill button focus area ${actualArea.toFixed(0)}px² < required ${requiredArea.toFixed(0)}px² for SC 2.4.13`
    ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(requiredArea);
  });

  test('focus indicator uses non-negative outline-offset — does not inset into the button', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/buttons');
    const btn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' });
    await btn.focus();

    const outlineOffset = await btn.evaluate((el) =>
      parseFloat(window.getComputedStyle(el).outlineOffset)
    );
    // Negative outline-offset causes the focus ring to render inside the button,
    // which fails the SC 2.4.13 area requirement for thin buttons
    expect(outlineOffset,
      'Negative outline-offset causes focus ring to overlap button content and reduces visible area'
    ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(-1); // allow -1px for flush-border design systems
  });
});
```

### Pattern 10 (Cycle 25) — Skip Link: Existence, Visibility on Focus, and Target Focusability

Skip navigation links (WCAG 2.4.1) are frequently broken in three ways: (1) the link exists but does not become visible on focus (hidden via `clip-path: inset(100%)` that is never removed), (2) the `href` points to a non-existent anchor, or (3) the target element lacks `tabindex="-1"` causing Safari to not receive focus on activation. All three must be tested explicitly.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/skip-link.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Skip navigation link (WCAG 2.4.1)', () => {
  test('skip link exists, points to valid anchor, and target has tabindex="-1"', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const skipLink = page.locator('a[href^="#"]:has-text(/skip/i)').first();
    await expect(skipLink).toBeAttached();

    const href = await skipLink.getAttribute('href');
    expect(href).toMatch(/^#.+/);
    const targetId = href!.slice(1);

    const target = page.locator(`#${targetId}`);
    await expect(target).toBeAttached();

    // tabindex="-1" required for Safari programmatic focus to work
    await expect(target,
      `Skip link target #${targetId} must have tabindex="-1" for Safari programmatic focus`
    ).toHaveAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
  });

  test('skip link becomes visible when focused (not permanently hidden)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab'); // first Tab should land on skip link

    const focusedHref = await page.evaluate(() =>
      (document.activeElement as HTMLAnchorElement)?.getAttribute('href') ?? ''
    );
    if (focusedHref.startsWith('#')) {
      const skipLink = page.locator(`a[href="${focusedHref}"]`);
      await expect(skipLink).toBeVisible();

      // Verify not hidden via clip-path: inset(100%) which some CSS frameworks use
      const clipPath = await skipLink.evaluate((el) =>
        window.getComputedStyle(el).clipPath
      );
      expect(clipPath, 'Skip link hidden via clip-path even when focused').not.toMatch(/inset.*100%/);
    }
  });

  test('activating skip link moves focus to main content', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

    const focused = await page.evaluate(() => ({
      id: document.activeElement?.id,
      tag: document.activeElement?.tagName.toLowerCase(),
      role: document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role'),
    }));
    const isMainContent = ['main', 'div', 'section'].includes(focused.tag ?? '') ||
      focused.role === 'main' || focused.id?.includes('main') || focused.id?.includes('content');
    expect(isMainContent, `Focus after skip link: ${JSON.stringify(focused)}`).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

---

### Pattern 11 (Cycle 25) — `@axe-core/react` with React 18 Automatic Batching: `act()` Flush Pattern

React 18's automatic batching defers multiple `setState` calls into a single render. `@axe-core/react`'s MutationObserver fires during intermediate batched states where components have not yet received final props — causing false-positive violations for missing labels, empty roles, or unresolved `aria-labelledby` references. The fix: wrap the render and any async state-settling in `act()` before running axe, flushing all pending React updates.

```typescript
// src/__tests__/CheckoutForm.a11y.test.tsx
import React from 'react';
import { render, act } from '@testing-library/react';
import { axe, toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';
import { CheckoutForm } from '../CheckoutForm';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

describe('CheckoutForm accessibility — React 18 batching-safe', () => {
  it('passes axe scan after all batched state updates flush', async () => {
    let container: HTMLElement;

    // act() flushes all React 18 batched state updates before axe scans
    await act(async () => {
      const result = render(<CheckoutForm />);
      container = result.container;
      // Flush useEffect-driven ARIA updates (aria-describedby resolution, etc.)
      await new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0));
    });

    const results = await axe(container!, {
      rules: { 'color-contrast': { enabled: false } }, // checked separately in E2E
    });
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('passes after async data loading resolves (aria-busy = false)', async () => {
    let container: HTMLElement;

    await act(async () => {
      const result = render(<CheckoutForm preloadData={true} />);
      container = result.container;
    });

    // Wait for aria-busy="false" — async data has populated all ARIA labels
    await act(async () => {
      await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
        const observer = new MutationObserver(() => {
          if (!container.querySelector('[aria-busy="true"]')) {
            observer.disconnect();
            resolve();
          }
        });
        observer.observe(container, { attributes: true, subtree: true });
        setTimeout(() => { observer.disconnect(); resolve(); }, 3000);
      });
    });

    const results = await axe(container!);
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });
});
```

---

### Pattern 12 (Cycle 25) — EU EAA 2025 Compliance: WCAG 2.2 New SC Automated Coverage Matrix

The European Accessibility Act (EAA) entered enforcement in June 2025 for private-sector digital services in EU member states, requiring WCAG 2.2 AA conformance. Nine new success criteria were added in WCAG 2.2 that were not in WCAG 2.1. A structured test suite maps each new SC to a test type. Three of these SCs (2.5.7, 2.4.13, 3.3.9) are AAA level and technically not required by AA conformance, but recommended for EAA risk reduction given EU member state implementations.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/eaa-wcag22-new-scs.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('WCAG 2.2 new SC automated coverage (EAA post-June-2025)', () => {
  test('SC-2.5.8 Target Size Minimum: interactive elements ≥ 24×24px (non-inline)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const smallTargets = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const sels = 'button:not([disabled]), input:not([type="hidden"]), select, [role="button"]';
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(sels))
        .map((el) => {
          const box = el.getBoundingClientRect();
          return { tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(), width: box.width, height: box.height,
            label: el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? el.textContent?.trim().slice(0, 30) ?? '' };
        })
        .filter((el) => el.width > 0 && el.height > 0)
        .filter((el) => el.width < 24 || el.height < 24);
    });

    if (smallTargets.length > 0) {
      console.log('SC-2.5.8 small targets found:', JSON.stringify(smallTargets, null, 2));
    }
    // Inline links are excepted (spacing exception) — only fail on buttons/inputs
    expect(smallTargets, `SC-2.5.8: ${smallTargets.length} elements below 24×24px`).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('SC-3.2.6 Consistent Help: help mechanism appears in same relative DOM order across pages', async ({ page }) => {
    const helpSelectors = ['a[href*="help"]', 'a[href*="support"]', '[aria-label*="help" i]', '[aria-label*="chat" i]'];
    const getHelpPosition = async (url: string): Promise<number> => {
      await page.goto(url);
      return page.evaluate((sels) => {
        const allLinks = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a, button'));
        for (const sel of sels) {
          const el = document.querySelector(sel);
          if (el) return allLinks.indexOf(el as HTMLElement);
        }
        return -1;
      }, helpSelectors);
    };
    const homePos = await getHelpPosition('/');
    const aboutPos = await getHelpPosition('/about');
    if (homePos !== -1 && aboutPos !== -1) {
      expect(Math.abs(homePos - aboutPos),
        `SC-3.2.6: Help link at position ${homePos} on homepage vs ${aboutPos} on /about — must be in consistent relative order`
      ).toBeLessThan(5);
    }
  });

  test('SC-3.3.7 Redundant Entry: step 2 pre-fills step 1 data', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout/step-1');
    const emailInput = page.getByLabel(/email/i);
    if (await emailInput.count() > 0) {
      await emailInput.fill('test@example.com');
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next|continue/i }).click();
      await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
      const step2Email = page.getByLabel(/email/i);
      if (await step2Email.count() > 0) {
        const value = await step2Email.inputValue();
        expect(value, 'SC-3.3.7: Email must be pre-filled in step 2').toBe('test@example.com');
      }
    }
  });

  test('SC-3.3.8 Accessible Authentication: password paste and autocomplete not blocked', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    const passwordField = page.getByLabel(/password/i);
    if (await passwordField.count() > 0) {
      // Verify paste is not blocked (some sites incorrectly prevent paste)
      await passwordField.click();
      await page.keyboard.press('Control+a');
      await passwordField.evaluate((el) => {
        const event = new ClipboardEvent('paste', {
          bubbles: true,
          cancelable: true,
          clipboardData: Object.assign(new DataTransfer(), {
            getData: () => 'TestPassword123!',
          }),
        });
        el.dispatchEvent(event);
      });
      // If paste is not blocked, the field should accept the value normally
      const autocomplete = await passwordField.getAttribute('autocomplete');
      expect(['current-password', 'new-password', 'off', null].includes(autocomplete),
        `SC-3.3.8: autocomplete="${autocomplete}" — must allow password manager autofill`
      ).toBe(true);
    }
  });
});
```

### Pattern 13 (Cycle 25) — Partial ARIA Snapshot Regression Testing for Component Library

Using `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` with `{ mode: 'partial' }` (Playwright v1.57+) for component library regression testing is more maintainable than full-page snapshots. Partial mode checks that specified ARIA nodes exist without requiring an exact match of the full tree — ideal for component-level regression where surrounding layout changes should not break accessibility assertions.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/component-aria-regression.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Component ARIA structure regression (partial snapshot)', () => {
  test('Alert component announces role and severity', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/storybook/alert?variant=error');
    await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - alert:
        - /error|failed|invalid/i
    `, { mode: 'partial' });
  });

  test('Breadcrumb has correct landmark, list, and aria-current on active item', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products/category/item');
    const breadcrumb = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /breadcrumb/i });
    await expect(breadcrumb).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - navigation "Breadcrumb":
        - list:
          - listitem:
            - link "Home"
    `, { mode: 'partial' });

    const lastLink = breadcrumb.getByRole('link').last();
    if (await lastLink.count() > 0) {
      await expect(lastLink).toHaveAttribute('aria-current', 'page');
    }
  });

  test('Pagination: current page is conveyed via aria-current or accessible label', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/results?page=3');
    const pagination = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /pagination/i });
    const currentPage = pagination.locator('[aria-current="page"]');
    if (await currentPage.count() === 0) {
      // Fallback: active button has aria-label including page number or "current"
      const fallback = pagination.locator('button[aria-label*="3"], button[aria-label*="current" i]');
      await expect(fallback.first()).toBeVisible();
    } else {
      await expect(currentPage).toContainText('3');
    }
  });

  test('Tooltip is linked to trigger via aria-describedby and announced on hover', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/tooltip-demo');
    const trigger = page.getByRole('button', { name: /info/i }).first();

    await expect(page.getByRole('tooltip')).toHaveCount(0); // not visible before hover

    await trigger.hover();
    await expect(page.getByRole('tooltip')).toBeVisible();

    const describedBy = await trigger.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
    if (describedBy) {
      await expect(page.locator(`#${describedBy}`)).toBeVisible();
    }
  });
});
```

### Pattern 14 (Cycle 25) — `axe-core` Violation Fingerprinting for Accepted Third-Party Issues

When a team accepts specific axe violations (e.g., third-party widget contrast issues outside their control), the correct pattern is not `disableRules()` globally — which silently ignores all instances of that rule — but **violation fingerprinting**: a snapshot of accepted violations keyed by rule ID + target path. New violations fail immediately; only fingerprinted violations are allowed. This creates an auditable acceptance record that also self-alerts when the accepted issue is fixed.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/violation-fingerprinting.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';
import type { AxeResults, Result, NodeResult } from 'axe-core';

interface ViolationFingerprint {
  ruleId: string; targetPathContains: string;
  acceptedReason: string; acceptedDate: string;
}

// Update via deliberate PR review only — disableRules() is NOT acceptable here
const ACCEPTED_VIOLATIONS: ViolationFingerprint[] = [
  {
    ruleId: 'color-contrast',
    targetPathContains: 'third-party-chat-widget',
    acceptedReason: 'Intercom widget — vendor fix pending (JIRA: A11Y-145)',
    acceptedDate: '2026-04-15',
  },
];

function isAccepted(node: NodeResult, result: Result): boolean {
  return ACCEPTED_VIOLATIONS.some((fp) =>
    fp.ruleId === result.id &&
    node.target.some((t) => typeof t === 'string' && t.includes(fp.targetPathContains))
  );
}

test.describe('axe violation fingerprinting', () => {
  test('homepage: no unexpected violations (accepted list enforced)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const results: AxeResults = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
      .analyze();

    const newViolations = results.violations.flatMap((v) =>
      v.nodes
        .filter((n) => !isAccepted(n, v))
        .map((n) => ({ rule: v.id, target: n.target.join(', '), html: n.html.slice(0, 100) }))
    );
    expect(newViolations,
      `New violations: ${JSON.stringify(newViolations, null, 2)}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('accepted violations audit: alert when third-party issue is fixed', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const results: AxeResults = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
      .analyze();

    for (const accepted of ACCEPTED_VIOLATIONS) {
      const stillPresent = results.violations.some((v) =>
        v.id === accepted.ruleId &&
        v.nodes.some((n) =>
          n.target.some((t) => typeof t === 'string' && t.includes(accepted.targetPathContains))
        )
      );
      if (!stillPresent) {
        console.log(
          `INFO: Accepted violation "${accepted.ruleId}" for "${accepted.targetPathContains}" ` +
          `is no longer present — remove from ACCEPTED_VIOLATIONS (reason: ${accepted.acceptedReason})`
        );
      }
    }
  });
});
```

### Pattern 15 (Cycle 25) — WCAG 2.5.1 + 2.5.7 Pointer Gesture Alternatives: Drag-and-Drop and Swipe

WCAG 2.5.1 (Pointer Gestures) requires all multi-point gestures to have a single-pointer alternative. WCAG 2.5.7 (Dragging Movements, new in WCAG 2.2 AA) requires all drag-and-drop operations to have a non-dragging alternative — keyboard move buttons, cut-and-paste, or Space-to-pick-up keyboard DnD. Testing must verify that draggable interfaces expose keyboard-accessible alternatives, and that range sliders support arrow key adjustment.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/pointer-gesture-alternatives.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.5.1 + 2.5.7: Pointer gesture alternatives', () => {
  test('drag-and-drop list has keyboard move alternative (SC 2.5.7)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/kanban');
    const firstCard = page.locator('[role="listitem"][data-draggable="true"]').first();
    await firstCard.focus();

    // Option A: button-based move action
    const hasMoveBtn = await firstCard.locator('[aria-label*="move" i], [aria-label*="actions" i]').count() > 0;
    // Option B: dnd-kit Space-to-pick-up keyboard DnD (aria-roledescription="sortable")
    const hasKeyboardDnD = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const card = document.querySelector('[data-draggable="true"]');
      return card?.getAttribute('aria-roledescription') === 'sortable' ||
             card?.getAttribute('data-keyboard-dnd') === 'true';
    });

    expect(hasMoveBtn || hasKeyboardDnD,
      'SC 2.5.7: Drag-and-drop must have non-dragging alternative (keyboard move or button)'
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  test('range slider supports arrow key adjustment (single-pointer SC 2.5.1 alt)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/range-slider');
    const slider = page.getByRole('slider').first();
    await expect(slider).toBeVisible();

    await slider.focus();
    const before = await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow');
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const after = await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow');

    expect(parseInt(after ?? '0')).toBeGreaterThan(parseInt(before ?? '0'));

    // Required ARIA attributes for slider
    await expect(slider).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemin');
    await expect(slider).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemax');
    await expect(slider).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow');
    await expect(slider).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuetext');
  });

  test('swipe-to-delete list has button-based delete alternative (SC 2.5.7)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/notifications');
    const listItems = page.getByRole('listitem');
    if (await listItems.count() > 0) {
      const deleteBtn = listItems.first().getByRole('button', { name: /delete|dismiss|remove/i });
      await expect(deleteBtn,
        'SC 2.5.7: Swipe-to-delete must have a non-swipe delete button'
      ).toBeVisible();
    }
  });
});
```

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 25)

130. **[community] `AxeBuilder.include()` accepts only a CSS selector string — passing a Playwright `Locator` object silently scans the full page with no error**: `@axe-core/playwright`'s `include()` method takes a CSS selector string, not a Playwright `Locator`. Passing `new AxeBuilder({ page }).include(page.getByRole('main'))` uses a Locator object and fails silently — axe runs on the full page making the scope parameter a no-op. Always pass a string: `.include('main')` or `.include('[data-testid="checkout-form"]')`. WHY: Teams using the Playwright-first API expect `.include()` to accept locators like all other Playwright APIs; the silent mismatch causes unexpectedly broad and slow scan results.

131. **[community] `outline: 0` and `outline: none` are equivalent visually but return different computed values for `outline-style` — SC 2.4.13 tests checking `outlineColor` will produce false results when `outline: 0` is used**: `outline: 0` sets `outline-width: 0` but may return a non-transparent `outline-color` (e.g., `-webkit-focus-ring-color`) from `getComputedStyle`. Tests for SC 2.4.13 should check `outline-style === 'none'` or `outline-width === '0px'` to determine whether an outline is visually present, not `outline-color !== 'transparent'`. WHY: Focus appearance tests asserting `.not.toBe('none')` on `outline-color` may pass incorrectly when the outline is actually invisible because `outline: 0` was used.

132. **[community] `aria-live="assertive"` interrupts all ongoing announcements — NVDA and JAWS cut off whatever is being read to announce the assertive region, causing users to miss both the original content and potentially the alert itself if it fires too quickly**: `role="alert"` is implicitly `aria-live="assertive"`. Teams copy `role="alert"` for every live region (search results, progress updates, toast notifications) and report that "screen reader users say the announcer never finishes reading anything." Reserve `role="alert"` / `aria-live="assertive"` for time-critical errors (session timeout, form submission error). Use `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"` for informational updates. WHY: Incorrect overuse of assertive live regions is the single most common screen reader UX complaint from real AT users in usability testing sessions.

133. **[community] Playwright's `forcedColors: 'active'` emulation sets the CSS media query but does NOT suppress `background-image` the way Windows OS does — icon-only buttons with SVG background icons will appear to pass even though real WHCM users see invisible icons**: Playwright's `forcedColors` sets the `forced-colors: active` media query in Chromium's CDP rendering, but the browser rendering pipeline does not suppress background images as the Windows High Contrast Mode OS override does. The correct strategy: run `forcedColors` tests to verify CSS media query branches, then separately assert via axe's `button-name` rule that all interactive elements have accessible text names independent of background images. WHY: Teams report "forcedColors tests pass but real WHCM users can't see any icon buttons" — the emulation gap causes false confidence.

134. **[community] `jest-axe` v10 `toHaveNoViolations()` only checks the `violations` array — `incomplete` (needs-review) items are silently dropped with no built-in matcher, unlike v9 which surfaced them as configurable warnings**: Teams migrating from `jest-axe` v9 to v10 lose visibility into `incomplete` results unless they add an explicit assertion `expect(results.incomplete).toHaveLength(0)` (or filtered by impact level). In v9, some configurations would surface incomplete items; in v10, they are silently ignored. This creates a hidden debt of "needs manual review" items that accumulate unnoticed. WHY: The change was intentional (v10 aligns with axe-core's result types model) but undocumented in the migration guide, causing unexpected coverage gaps.

135. **[community] The WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception requires 24px of spacing between targets, not 24px of padding within the target — a 16px icon button with 4px padding has a 24px bounding box but still fails if an adjacent interactive element is within that 24px zone**: Many teams interpret the spacing exception as allowing `padding: 4px` on a 16px icon to claim a 24px tap area. SC 2.5.8 specifies the spacing must be between targets (the 24px inclusive zone around each target must not contain any other interactive element). Rich text editor toolbars with tightly packed icon buttons commonly fail this even after adding padding. WHY: The geometric spacing requirement between adjacent targets is distinct from the target's own bounding box size — both conditions must be satisfied.
