## Cycle 28 — 2026-05-14

<!-- sources: WCAG 2.2 Understanding docs (WebFetch) + Playwright accessibility docs (WebFetch) + axe-core API docs (WebFetch) + ARIA APG patterns (WebFetch) + MDN ARIA live regions (WebFetch) + W3C AccName 1.1 spec (WebFetch) + WCAG 2.2 new SC deep-dives (WebFetch) + training knowledge (community patterns) -->

### Pattern 1 (Cycle 28) — Accessible Name Computation Verification with `getByRole` + `toHaveAccessibleName`

WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) requires that every interactive control has a programmatically determinable name. The W3C AccName 1.1 algorithm prioritizes name sources in this order: `aria-labelledby` > `aria-label` > native `<label>` > `title` > placeholder > element contents. Testing must verify that the **computed** accessible name — not just the presence of an attribute — matches what screen readers actually announce. Playwright's `toHaveAccessibleName()` assertion (v1.44+) evaluates the full AccName algorithm in a real browser, catching cases where `aria-labelledby` references a hidden element (which silently produces an empty name in most browsers).

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/accessible-name-computation.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Accessible name computation — WCAG 4.1.2', () => {
  test('button with aria-labelledby pointing to hidden element gets empty name', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setContent(`
      <span id="lbl" style="display:none">Save document</span>
      <button aria-labelledby="lbl">Save</button>
    `);
    // aria-labelledby referencing a CSS-hidden element: browsers disagree on this
    // AccName spec: hidden elements ARE traversed for aria-labelledby (unlike aria-describedby)
    // Test the actual computed name — do NOT rely on the attribute being present
    const btn = page.getByRole('button');
    // Assert the name the browser computes — verify in your actual browser target
    await expect(btn).toHaveAccessibleName(/save/i);
  });

  test('icon button with aria-hidden SVG requires explicit aria-label', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setContent(`
      <button type="button" aria-label="Close dialog">
        <svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" width="16" height="16">
          <path d="M4 4l8 8M12 4l-8 8"/>
        </svg>
      </button>
    `);
    const btn = page.getByRole('button');
    await expect(btn).toHaveAccessibleName('Close dialog');
    // Verify SVG is not independently focusable
    const svgFocusable = await page.locator('svg').getAttribute('focusable');
    expect(svgFocusable).toBe('false');
  });

  test('input with both placeholder and label — label wins', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setContent(`
      <label for="search">Search products</label>
      <input id="search" type="search" placeholder="e.g. shoes, shirts">
    `);
    const input = page.getByRole('searchbox');
    // Computed name must be the label text, not the placeholder
    await expect(input).toHaveAccessibleName('Search products');
  });

  test('landmark with aria-labelledby from heading is announced correctly', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setContent(`
      <section aria-labelledby="section-h2">
        <h2 id="section-h2">User Settings</h2>
        <p>Manage your account preferences.</p>
      </section>
    `);
    // Section becomes a landmark when it has an accessible name
    const region = page.getByRole('region');
    await expect(region).toHaveAccessibleName('User Settings');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `toHaveAccessibleName()` for every interactive element in your smoke accessibility suite. Do NOT rely on attribute presence alone (`expect(btn).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', ...)`) — attributes can be present but produce empty names if the AccName algorithm discards them (e.g., `aria-labelledby` referencing a non-existent ID silently falls back to element content). Alternative: `locator.ariaSnapshot()` to capture the full name+role tree for regression snapshots. When NOT to use: `toHaveAccessibleName()` does not test description — pair with `toHaveAccessibleDescription()` for `aria-describedby` verification. [official]

---

### Pattern 2 (Cycle 28) — ARIA Snapshot Regression Testing for Component Libraries

Playwright's `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` (stable since v1.50) captures the ARIA accessibility tree as a YAML snapshot, providing component-level regression coverage for accessible names, roles, and expanded/checked states. Unlike axe scans (which detect rule violations), ARIA snapshots catch **semantic regressions** — a refactor that accidentally changes a button's accessible name from "Submit order" to "Submit" shows up as a snapshot diff immediately. This is especially valuable for design system components shared across apps.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/aria-snapshots.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA snapshot regression — design system components', () => {
  test('navigation menu ARIA tree matches snapshot', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/navigation');
    const nav = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Main' });

    // First run: creates .aria-snapshots/navigation-main.yml automatically
    // Subsequent runs: fails if the accessibility tree changes
    await expect(nav).toMatchAriaSnapshot({
      name: 'navigation-main',
    });
  });

  test('data table ARIA snapshot captures column headers and sort state', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/data-table');
    const table = page.getByRole('table');

    // Snapshot includes columnheader roles, aria-sort values, and cell content
    // Detects: column header renamed, sort state removed, cell roles changed
    await expect(table).toMatchAriaSnapshot();
  });

  test('modal dialog ARIA tree: role, label, and close button present', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open settings/i }).click();
    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();

    // Partial snapshot: only check structural elements, not dynamic content
    await expect(dialog).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - dialog "Settings":
        - button "Close"
        - heading "Settings" [level=2]
    `);
  });

  test('accordion snapshot captures expanded state correctly', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/accordion');
    const firstItem = page.getByRole('button', { name: /what is/i }).first();
    await firstItem.click();

    const accordion = page.getByRole('region').first().locator('..');
    // Snapshot must include aria-expanded="true" on activated button
    await expect(firstItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    await expect(accordion).toMatchAriaSnapshot();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use ARIA snapshots for component library regression testing where semantic stability is a contract. Update snapshots intentionally via `npx playwright test --update-snapshots`, not by deleting snapshot files. Do NOT use ARIA snapshots for pages with highly dynamic content (timestamps, user-generated text) — the snapshot will fail on every run; use `.toMatchAriaSnapshot()` with inline partial YAML instead to pin only the structural elements. Alternative: axe scans catch rule violations; ARIA snapshots catch name/role regressions — use both. [official]

---

### Pattern 3 (Cycle 28) — `aria-describedby` Error Message Testing with `toHaveAccessibleDescription`

WCAG 3.3.1 (Error Identification) and 3.3.3 (Error Suggestion) require that form errors are described in text. Using `aria-describedby` to link error messages to their input is the standard technique — but it must be tested programmatically, not just by visual inspection. Playwright v1.50 added `toHaveAccessibleDescription()` which evaluates the full `aria-describedby` chain including multi-ID references. This catches the common bug where the error message `id` changes after a framework re-render, breaking the linkage silently.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/form-error-description.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.1 — Form error identification via aria-describedby', () => {
  test('email field: error message linked and announced on invalid submit', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');
    // Submit with empty required fields to trigger validation
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign up/i }).click();

    const emailInput = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i });
    // Input must be invalid and linked to error text
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
    // toHaveAccessibleDescription evaluates the computed aria-describedby chain
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAccessibleDescription(/required|enter.*email/i);
  });

  test('password field: hint and error combined in multi-ID aria-describedby', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');
    const passwordInput = page.getByLabel(/password/i);

    // Before submission: description should contain password requirements
    await expect(passwordInput).toHaveAccessibleDescription(/must be at least/i);

    // After invalid submission: error appended — both IDs must be in aria-describedby
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign up/i }).click();
    await passwordInput.fill('abc');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign up/i }).click();

    // Computed description now concatenates hint + error text
    const description = await passwordInput.evaluate((el) => {
      const ids = el.getAttribute('aria-describedby')?.split(' ') ?? [];
      return ids.map((id) => document.getElementById(id)?.textContent ?? '').join(' ');
    });
    expect(description).toMatch(/must be at least/i);
    expect(description).toMatch(/too short|invalid password/i);
  });

  test('error message element has role="alert" or aria-live for announcement', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /send/i }).click();

    // Error container should be announced without focus movement
    const errorContainer = page.locator('[role="alert"], [aria-live="polite"], [aria-live="assertive"]');
    await expect(errorContainer.first()).toBeVisible();
    await expect(errorContainer.first()).toContainText(/required|error/i);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `toHaveAccessibleDescription()` over manually asserting `aria-describedby` attribute values — the attribute might reference an ID that points to an empty element, which produces an empty description. Test after user interaction (form submission, input blur) not just on page load, since error messages are dynamically injected. Do NOT use `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` (Playwright v1.50+ ARIA ErrorMessage assertion) as a replacement — it checks `aria-errormessage` (a separate ARIA 1.1 attribute), not `aria-describedby`; most forms use `aria-describedby` for errors. [official]

---

### Pattern 4 (Cycle 28) — `axe.run()` with `resultTypes` Performance Optimisation for Large SPAs

On large SPAs with 10,000+ DOM nodes, a full `axe.run()` analyzing all result types (violations, passes, incomplete, inapplicable) can take 3–8 seconds per page. The `resultTypes: ['violations']` option (axe-core 4.7+) skips post-processing of passing rules and cuts scan time by 60–80% in benchmarks. This makes it practical to run axe scans in every E2E test without a CI timeout budget concern. The tradeoff is that `passes` and `incomplete` (needs-review) arrays become empty — acceptable for a gating CI scan, not for a full audit report.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/fast-axe-scan.spec.ts
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';
import type { AxeResults } from 'axe-core';

/**
 * Fast axe scan: violations only, WCAG 2.1 AA + WCAG 2.2 AA tags.
 * 60-80% faster than full scan on large pages.
 * Use for CI gates. Use full scan for audit reports.
 */
async function fastAxeScan(page: Page, selector?: string): Promise<AxeResults> {
  let builder = new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
    .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] });

  if (selector) {
    builder = builder.include(selector);
  }

  return builder.analyze();
}

/**
 * Full audit scan: all result types for detailed compliance reporting.
 * Slower — use for quarterly audits, not every CI run.
 */
async function fullAuditScan(page: Page): Promise<AxeResults> {
  return new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa', 'best-practice'])
    .options({ resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete', 'inapplicable'] })
    .analyze();
}

test.describe('Fast axe scans for CI gates', () => {
  test('checkout page: no WCAG 2.2 AA violations (fast scan)', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const startMs = Date.now();
    const results = await fastAxeScan(page);
    const durationMs = Date.now() - startMs;

    // Attach scan duration to test report for performance monitoring
    await testInfo.attach('axe-scan-duration', {
      body: `${durationMs}ms`,
      contentType: 'text/plain',
    });

    expect(results.violations,
      `Violations: ${JSON.stringify(results.violations.map(v => ({ id: v.id, impact: v.impact })))}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('dashboard: scoped fast scan on main content only', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    // Exclude third-party chat widget and header with known accepted issues
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
      .exclude('#third-party-chat')
      .include('main')
      .analyze();

    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `resultTypes: ['violations']` for all CI gate tests — it is the correct tool for a pass/fail gate. When NOT to use: do NOT use the fast scan for generating compliance audit reports (ACR/VPAT), accessibility debt tracking, or identifying `incomplete` items that need manual review — use the full scan with all result types for those purposes. Alternative: `Pa11y` with `--runner axe` also supports result filtering but lacks the TypeScript integration and Playwright fixture composability. [official]

---

### Pattern 5 (Cycle 28) — Roving `tabindex` Pattern Testing for Composite Widgets

ARIA composite widgets (toolbars, menubars, radio groups, grids, trees) must implement the **roving tabindex** pattern: only one item in the set is in the tab sequence at a time (`tabindex="0"`), all others are removed (`tabindex="-1"`), and arrow keys move focus within the set. This prevents keyboard users from having to Tab through every item to reach the next element. Testing must verify: initial state (correct item has `tabindex="0"`), arrow key navigation (focus moves to correct item, tabindex updates), and Tab key behavior (exits the widget entirely, not steps through it).

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/roving-tabindex.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Roving tabindex pattern — composite widget keyboard navigation', () => {
  test('toolbar: only one item focusable via Tab (roving tabindex)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/toolbar');
    const toolbar = page.getByRole('toolbar');
    const toolbarButtons = toolbar.getByRole('button');

    // Tab into toolbar — first button should receive focus
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focused = page.locator(':focus');
    await expect(focused).toHaveRole('button');

    // Only the focused button has tabindex="0"; all others must be -1
    const buttonCount = await toolbarButtons.count();
    let zeroCount = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < buttonCount; i++) {
      const tabindex = await toolbarButtons.nth(i).getAttribute('tabindex');
      if (tabindex === '0' || tabindex === null) zeroCount++;
    }
    expect(zeroCount,
      'Exactly one toolbar button must be in the tab sequence (tabindex="0")'
    ).toBe(1);
  });

  test('toolbar: ArrowRight moves focus within toolbar without Tab', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/toolbar');
    // Tab into the toolbar
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');

    const firstButton = page.getByRole('toolbar').getByRole('button').first();
    await expect(firstButton).toBeFocused();

    // ArrowRight should move focus to second button, not exit the toolbar
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const secondButton = page.getByRole('toolbar').getByRole('button').nth(1);
    await expect(secondButton).toBeFocused();

    // First button now has tabindex="-1" (roving tabindex updated)
    await expect(firstButton).toHaveAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
    await expect(secondButton).toHaveAttribute('tabindex', '0');
  });

  test('toolbar: Tab exits the toolbar (does not step through items)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/toolbar');
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab'); // Tab into toolbar
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab'); // Tab out of toolbar

    // Focus must be outside the toolbar after second Tab
    const isInsideToolbar = await page.getByRole('toolbar').locator(':focus').count();
    expect(isInsideToolbar,
      'Tab key must exit the toolbar — not navigate within it'
    ).toBe(0);
  });

  test('radio group: arrow keys navigate, Tab exits', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/radio-group');
    const firstRadio = page.getByRole('radio').first();
    await firstRadio.focus();

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    const secondRadio = page.getByRole('radio').nth(1);
    await expect(secondRadio).toBeFocused();
    await expect(secondRadio).toBeChecked();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern for any composite widget: toolbar, menubar, listbox, radiogroup, grid, tablist, tree. Do NOT use roving tabindex for groups of independent controls (form fields, checkboxes without a group relationship) — those should all be individually Tab-focusable. Alternative: `aria-activedescendant` is the other valid keyboard pattern for composite widgets (focus stays on container, `aria-activedescendant` attribute changes), but it is harder to implement and test; roving tabindex is preferred by the ARIA APG for most patterns. [official]

---

### Pattern 6 (Cycle 28) — `prefers-reduced-motion` Emulation in Playwright Tests

WCAG 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions, Level AAA) and the broader principle of motion sensitivity requires that any animation triggered by user interaction can be disabled. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is the CSS media query that indicates user preference; Playwright can emulate it via `browser.newContext({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })`. Testing must verify: (a) the CSS `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` branch is present and removes transitions, and (b) animated components like carousels, loaders, and toast notifications still display their final state without motion when the preference is set.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/reduced-motion.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Create a test variant with reduced motion emulation
const reducedMotionTest = test.extend<{ page: typeof test['page'] extends infer P ? P : never }>({
  page: async ({ browser }, use) => {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await use(page);
    await context.close();
  },
});

reducedMotionTest.describe('prefers-reduced-motion emulation — WCAG 2.3.3', () => {
  reducedMotionTest('carousel: auto-advance disabled under reduced-motion', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/carousel');

    // Record initial slide
    const activeSlide = page.locator('[aria-current="true"], [aria-selected="true"]').first();
    const initialText = await activeSlide.textContent();

    // Wait 2s — if auto-advance is disabled, slide should not change
    await page.waitForTimeout(2000);
    await expect(activeSlide).toContainText(initialText ?? '');
  });

  reducedMotionTest('page transitions: transition property is 0s under reduced-motion', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const mainContent = page.locator('main, #main-content').first();

    // Computed transition-duration must be 0s when reduced-motion is active
    const transitionDuration = await mainContent.evaluate((el) =>
      getComputedStyle(el).transitionDuration
    );
    // 0s means CSS correctly responds to prefers-reduced-motion
    expect(
      transitionDuration === '0s' || transitionDuration === '',
      `Transition duration "${transitionDuration}" — expected 0s under reduced-motion`
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  reducedMotionTest('loading spinner: animation-duration is 0s under reduced-motion', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard?simulate-loading=true');
    const spinner = page.getByRole('progressbar', { name: /loading/i });

    if (await spinner.isVisible()) {
      const animationDuration = await spinner.evaluate((el) =>
        getComputedStyle(el).animationDuration
      );
      expect(animationDuration === '0s' || animationDuration === '',
        'Spinner animation must be paused under prefers-reduced-motion'
      ).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  reducedMotionTest('toast notification: no translateY transform under reduced-motion', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /save/i }).first().click();

    const toast = page.getByRole('status').first();
    if (await toast.isVisible()) {
      const transform = await toast.evaluate((el) => getComputedStyle(el).transform);
      // No translateY transform means the slide-in animation was skipped
      expect(transform === 'none' || transform === 'matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)').toBe(true);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` for every page that contains animations, transitions, carousels, or timed auto-advancing content. Do NOT test `animation-play-state: paused` instead of `animation-duration: 0s` — pausing retains the first keyframe and may cause layout issues; `0s` duration is the recommended CSS technique. Alternative: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` tests confirm motion works for users who want it — run both test contexts in CI. [official]

---

### Pattern 7 (Cycle 28) — Accessible Table Testing: `scope`, `headers`, and `aria-sort`

WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) requires that tabular data conveys its structure programmatically. HTML tables are accessible by default only when `<th>` elements use `scope="col"` or `scope="row"` correctly, or when complex tables use `headers` attributes on `<td>` cells. `aria-sort` on sortable column headers is required for WCAG 4.1.2. Testing must verify: all `<th>` elements have `scope`, complex tables link cells to headers via `id`/`headers`, sortable columns update `aria-sort` on activation, and the table has a caption or `aria-label`.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/data-table.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 1.3.1 — Accessible data table structure', () => {
  test('simple table: all th elements have scope attribute', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/reports/summary');

    const tableHeaders = page.locator('table th');
    const headerCount = await tableHeaders.count();
    expect(headerCount, 'Table must have at least one th element').toBeGreaterThan(0);

    for (let i = 0; i < headerCount; i++) {
      const scope = await tableHeaders.nth(i).getAttribute('scope');
      expect(scope,
        `th[${i}] must have scope="col" or scope="row"`
      ).toMatch(/^(col|row|colgroup|rowgroup)$/);
    }
  });

  test('table has accessible name (caption or aria-label)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/reports/summary');

    const table = page.getByRole('table').first();
    // Either <caption> or aria-label/aria-labelledby must be present
    const hasCaption = await table.locator('caption').count() > 0;
    const hasAriaLabel = await table.evaluate((el) =>
      el.hasAttribute('aria-label') || el.hasAttribute('aria-labelledby')
    );
    expect(hasCaption || hasAriaLabel,
      'Table must have an accessible name via <caption>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby'
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  test('sortable table: aria-sort updates on column header click', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/orders');
    const dateHeader = page.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /date/i });
    await expect(dateHeader).toBeVisible();

    // Initial state: unsorted or ascending
    const initialSort = await dateHeader.getAttribute('aria-sort');
    expect(['none', 'ascending', 'descending', null]).toContain(initialSort);

    // Click to sort — aria-sort must update
    await dateHeader.click();
    const afterSort = await dateHeader.getAttribute('aria-sort');
    expect(['ascending', 'descending']).toContain(afterSort);

    // Click again — sort direction must toggle
    await dateHeader.click();
    const afterToggle = await dateHeader.getAttribute('aria-sort');
    expect(afterToggle).not.toBe(afterSort);
  });

  test('axe scan detects table scope violations', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/reports/summary');
    const { default: AxeBuilder } = await import('@axe-core/playwright');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include('table')
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
      .analyze();

    const tableViolations = results.violations.filter((v) =>
      ['td-headers-attr', 'th-has-data-cells', 'scope-attr-valid'].includes(v.id)
    );
    expect(tableViolations,
      `Table structure violations: ${JSON.stringify(tableViolations.map(v => v.id))}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `scope="col"` for simple tables (one header row, no row headers). Use `id`/`headers` for complex tables with spanning headers — `scope` alone is insufficient for multi-level headers. Do NOT omit `<caption>` or `aria-label` just because the table's purpose is visually obvious — screen reader users navigate tables in isolation and need context. Alternative: if a table is purely decorative layout (not truly tabular data), use `role="presentation"` to strip its table semantics from the accessibility tree. [official]

---

### Pattern 8 (Cycle 28) — Skip Navigation Link Verification

WCAG 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks) requires a mechanism to skip repeated navigation blocks. The most common implementation is a skip-to-content link as the first focusable element on the page. Testing must verify three behaviors: (1) the link exists and is the first focusable element, (2) it becomes visible on keyboard focus (many implementations use CSS `opacity` or `transform` to visually hide it until focused), and (3) activating it moves focus to the main content area — not just scrolls to it. The third check is frequently missed: `href="#main"` scrolls the viewport but does not move keyboard focus unless the target has `tabindex="-1"` or is natively focusable.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/skip-navigation.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.1 — Skip navigation link', () => {
  test('first Tab keypress focuses the skip-to-content link', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Start from fresh (no element focused)
    await page.evaluate(() => (document.activeElement as HTMLElement)?.blur());

    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focused = page.locator(':focus');

    // The skip link must be the first focusable element
    await expect(focused).toHaveText(/skip to (main )?content|skip navigation/i);
  });

  test('skip link is visible when focused (not permanently hidden)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.evaluate(() => (document.activeElement as HTMLElement)?.blur());
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');

    const skipLink = page.locator(':focus');
    // Must be visible after focus — clip/transform-based hiding must reverse on focus
    await expect(skipLink).toBeVisible();

    // Verify it is not clipped off-screen
    const boundingBox = await skipLink.boundingBox();
    expect(boundingBox?.x ?? 0).toBeGreaterThan(-100);
    expect(boundingBox?.y ?? 0).toBeGreaterThan(-100);
  });

  test('activating skip link moves keyboard focus to main content', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.evaluate(() => (document.activeElement as HTMLElement)?.blur());
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

    // Focus must be on or inside the main content area
    const isFocusedInsideMain = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const focused = document.activeElement;
      const main = document.querySelector('main, #main-content, #content');
      return main ? main.contains(focused) || main === focused : false;
    });
    expect(isFocusedInsideMain,
      'Skip link must move keyboard focus into main content, not just scroll'
    ).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test on every page that has repeated navigation blocks (global header, sidebar). Do NOT accept "scroll into view" as passing — WCAG 2.4.1 requires moving keyboard focus, not visual position. The target element (`<main>`, `<div id="main">`) must have `tabindex="-1"` to receive programmatic focus via `focus()` or link activation if it is not natively focusable. Alternative: for SPAs with client-side routing, implement route change focus management instead of (or in addition to) skip links. [official]

---

### Pattern 9 (Cycle 28) — Accessible Modal Focus Trap: Enter, Tab Cycle, and Escape

WCAG 2.1.2 (No Keyboard Trap) specifically carves out dialogs: intentional focus trapping in modals is acceptable and required by the ARIA APG dialog pattern. However, the trap must be correct in three ways: (1) focus must move into the dialog on open (not stay on the trigger), (2) Tab and Shift+Tab must cycle within the dialog (first to last focusable element and back), and (3) Escape must close the dialog and return focus to the trigger. Failing any of these creates a severe accessibility barrier.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/modal-focus-trap.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA dialog pattern — focus trap and management (WCAG 2.1.2)', () => {
  test('opening dialog moves focus into dialog (not stays on trigger)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const openBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /open|settings|configure/i }).first();
    await openBtn.click();

    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();

    // Focus must be inside the dialog
    const focusedInsideDialog = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const focused = document.activeElement;
      const dialog = document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]');
      return dialog ? (dialog === focused || dialog.contains(focused)) : false;
    });
    expect(focusedInsideDialog, 'Focus must move inside dialog on open').toBe(true);
  });

  test('Tab cycles within dialog — does not escape to page background', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open|settings/i }).first().click();
    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();

    // Press Tab 20 times — focus must stay within the dialog
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
      const focusedInsideDialog = await page.evaluate(() => {
        const focused = document.activeElement;
        const dialog = document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]');
        return dialog ? (dialog === focused || dialog.contains(focused)) : false;
      });
      expect(focusedInsideDialog,
        `After ${i + 1} Tab presses, focus escaped the dialog`
      ).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test('Escape closes dialog and returns focus to trigger element', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const openBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /open|settings/i }).first();
    await openBtn.click();

    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(dialog).not.toBeVisible();

    // Focus must return to the button that opened the dialog
    await expect(openBtn).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('dialog has required ARIA attributes: role, aria-modal, aria-labelledby', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open|settings/i }).first().click();
    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');

    await expect(dialog).toHaveAttribute('aria-modal', 'true');
    // Must have accessible name via aria-labelledby or aria-label
    const hasLabel = await dialog.evaluate((el) =>
      el.hasAttribute('aria-labelledby') || el.hasAttribute('aria-label')
    );
    expect(hasLabel, 'Dialog must have accessible name').toBe(true);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern for every modal dialog, drawer, and popover that blocks interaction with the page behind it. Do NOT use `aria-modal="true"` as a substitute for actual focus trapping in JavaScript — `aria-modal` is a hint to screen readers to ignore background content, but it does not prevent keyboard users from tabbing to background elements. Real focus trapping via JavaScript is required. Alternative: libraries like `focus-trap` (npm) implement the ARIA APG focus trap pattern correctly; verify your chosen library passes these three tests. [official]

---

### Pattern 10 (Cycle 28) — Heading Hierarchy Audit via Playwright DOM Inspection

WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) and 2.4.6 (Headings and Labels) require that heading levels convey structure and are not skipped. A page jumping from `<h1>` to `<h3>` without an `<h2>` creates a structural gap that confuses screen reader users navigating by heading. Axe-core does not flag heading level skips by default (the `heading-order` rule exists but is tagged `best-practice`, not `wcag2a`). This pattern provides a direct DOM inspection test that enforces the heading hierarchy contract independently of axe.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/heading-hierarchy.spec.ts
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

/** Extracts heading levels in DOM order. Returns an array like [1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 3]. */
async function getHeadingLevels(page: Page): Promise<number[]> {
  return page.evaluate(() =>
    Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6,[role="heading"]'))
      .map((el) => {
        const level = el.getAttribute('aria-level');
        if (level) return parseInt(level, 10);
        const tag = el.tagName.toLowerCase();
        return parseInt(tag.replace('h', ''), 10);
      })
      .filter((l) => l >= 1 && l <= 6)
  );
}

test.describe('WCAG 1.3.1 / 2.4.6 — Heading hierarchy validation', () => {
  test('page has exactly one h1 (main page title)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const h1s = await page.locator('h1').count();
    expect(h1s,
      'Each page must have exactly one h1 element as the main title'
    ).toBe(1);
  });

  test('heading levels do not skip (no h1 to h3 without h2)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const levels = await getHeadingLevels(page);

    for (let i = 1; i < levels.length; i++) {
      const jump = levels[i] - levels[i - 1];
      expect(jump,
        `Heading level skip detected: h${levels[i - 1]} to h${levels[i]} at index ${i}`
      ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
    }
  });

  test('all key pages have a visible non-empty h1', async ({ page }) => {
    const pages = ['/', '/products', '/about', '/contact'];
    for (const path of pages) {
      await page.goto(path);
      const h1 = page.locator('h1').first();
      await expect(h1,
        `Page "${path}" must have a visible h1 element`
      ).toBeVisible();
      const text = await h1.textContent();
      expect(text?.trim().length,
        `Page "${path}" h1 must not be empty`
      ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });

  test('axe best-practice heading-order rule: explicitly enabled', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const { default: AxeBuilder } = await import('@axe-core/playwright');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .options({
        rules: { 'heading-order': { enabled: true } },
        resultTypes: ['violations'],
      })
      .analyze();

    const headingViolation = results.violations.find((v) => v.id === 'heading-order');
    expect(headingViolation,
      `Heading order violation: ${JSON.stringify(headingViolation?.nodes.map(n => n.html))}`
    ).toBeUndefined();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test on every page template. Do NOT apply the "no skip" rule to headings inside `<dialog>` elements — dialogs often restart at `h2` regardless of page hierarchy and that is acceptable. Alternative: the axe `heading-order` rule provides similar coverage but must be enabled explicitly since it is tagged `best-practice`, not `wcag2a`. [community]

---

### Pattern 11 (Cycle 28) — `getByRole` with `description` Parameter (Playwright v1.60+)

Playwright v1.60 added a `description` option to `getByRole()` allowing locators to match elements by their ARIA accessible description (computed from `aria-describedby` or `aria-description`). This is particularly useful for finding form inputs or action buttons that are identical in role and name but differ in context (e.g., two "Edit" buttons that have different descriptions). Previously, test code had to use `nth()` or `data-testid` to disambiguate — `description` enables semantic disambiguation without fragile index-based locators.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/getbyrole-description.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Playwright v1.60+ getByRole with description option', () => {
  test('disambiguate "Edit" buttons by their accessible description', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setContent(`
      <ul>
        <li>
          <span id="item1-name">Annual report 2025</span>
          <button aria-describedby="item1-name">Edit</button>
        </li>
        <li>
          <span id="item2-name">Q1 budget forecast</span>
          <button aria-describedby="item2-name">Edit</button>
        </li>
      </ul>
    `);

    // Without description: page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Edit' }) returns 2 elements
    // With description: precisely targets the correct button
    const editReport = page.getByRole('button', {
      name: 'Edit',
      description: 'Annual report 2025',
    });
    const editBudget = page.getByRole('button', {
      name: 'Edit',
      description: 'Q1 budget forecast',
    });

    await expect(editReport).toHaveCount(1);
    await expect(editBudget).toHaveCount(1);

    // Verify the descriptions are actually linked correctly
    await expect(editReport).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Annual report 2025');
    await expect(editBudget).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Q1 budget forecast');
  });

  test('icon buttons with aria-description are locatable by description', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setContent(`
      <nav aria-label="Pagination">
        <button aria-label="Previous" aria-description="Go to page 4 of 10">&#8592;</button>
        <button aria-label="Next" aria-description="Go to page 6 of 10">&#8594;</button>
      </nav>
    `);

    // Playwright v1.60: aria-description attribute supported in addition to aria-describedby
    const prevBtn = page.getByRole('button', {
      name: 'Previous',
      description: /page 4/,
    });
    await expect(prevBtn).toBeEnabled();
    await expect(prevBtn).toHaveAccessibleDescription(/page 4 of 10/i);
  });

  test('form fields: hint text accessible description is present', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');
    // Find password field specifically using its hint description
    const passwordField = page.getByRole('textbox', {
      name: /password/i,
      description: /at least 8 characters/i,
    });
    // If this locator fails, the hint text is not linked via aria-describedby
    await expect(passwordField).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `description` to disambiguate identical-name controls in table rows and lists — it is far more semantic than `nth()` or `data-testid`. Do NOT use it as a primary locator strategy when name-based locators are sufficient — `description` adds specificity only when disambiguation is genuinely needed. When NOT to use: `description` requires the element to have an `aria-describedby` or `aria-description` attribute — if neither is present, the locator will match zero elements even when the element exists. Check with `toHaveAccessibleDescription()` first to verify the description exists. [official]

---

### Pattern 12 (Cycle 28) — WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication: Paste and Autocomplete Testing

WCAG 3.3.8 (Accessible Authentication Minimum, Level AA, new in WCAG 2.2) prohibits authentication steps that require a cognitive function test without an alternative. Specifically: CAPTCHA is a cognitive function test; OTP entry via a code that the user must re-type is a cognitive function test unless copy-paste is enabled. Testing must verify: (a) password and OTP fields allow clipboard paste, (b) password managers can autofill the field (requires correct `autocomplete` attribute values), and (c) OTP fields do not block paste from the OS clipboard.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/accessible-authentication.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.8 — Accessible Authentication (Level AA)', () => {
  test('password field allows paste (not blocked by JS paste prevention)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    const passwordField = page.getByLabel(/password/i);
    await expect(passwordField).toBeVisible();

    // Write a test password to clipboard and paste it
    await page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.writeText('TestPass123!'));
    await passwordField.click();
    await page.keyboard.press('Control+V');

    // If paste is blocked, the field will remain empty
    const value = await passwordField.inputValue();
    expect(value.length,
      'Password field must allow clipboard paste — SC 3.3.8 requires paste not be blocked'
    ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('password field has correct autocomplete attribute for password managers', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    const passwordField = page.getByLabel(/password/i);
    const autocomplete = await passwordField.getAttribute('autocomplete');

    // Valid values: "current-password" (login) or "new-password" (registration)
    expect(['current-password', 'new-password']).toContain(autocomplete);
  });

  test('OTP / verification code input allows paste', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/verify');
    const otpField = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /code|otp|verification/i }).first();

    if (await otpField.isVisible()) {
      await page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.writeText('123456'));
      await otpField.click();
      await page.keyboard.press('Control+V');

      const value = await otpField.inputValue();
      expect(value.length,
        'OTP field must allow paste — manually typing codes is a cognitive function test (SC 3.3.8)'
      ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });

  test('login form has no JS-based paste event blocker on password field', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    const pasteBlocked = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const passwordField = document.querySelector('input[type="password"]');
      if (!passwordField) return false;

      const pasteEvent = new ClipboardEvent('paste', { cancelable: true, bubbles: true });
      passwordField.dispatchEvent(pasteEvent);
      return pasteEvent.defaultPrevented;
    });

    expect(pasteBlocked,
      'Password field must not call preventDefault() on paste events (SC 3.3.8)'
    ).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test for every authentication and verification flow. Do NOT rely solely on axe scanning for SC 3.3.8 — axe has no rule for paste blocking or missing authentication autocomplete values (axe `autocomplete-valid` only checks format, not the specific authentication semantics). The paste-blocked detection via `dispatchEvent` is fragile for React's synthetic event system — supplement with real paste testing via `page.keyboard.press('Control+V')` after writing to the clipboard. Alternative: manually test with a password manager (Bitwarden, 1Password) to verify autofill works end-to-end. [official]

### Pattern 13 (Cycle 28) — Color Contrast Testing Beyond axe: `oklch` and CSS Custom Property Chains

axe-core's `color-contrast` rule computes contrast from `getComputedStyle().color` and `getComputedStyle().backgroundColor`. This works correctly for most cases but fails silently when: (a) the background comes from a `background-image` (axe cannot evaluate gradient contrast), (b) colors are specified in modern CSS color spaces (`oklch`, `oklab`, `display-p3`) and the browser resolves them differently than sRGB, or (c) a color is inherited through a deeply nested custom property chain that JSDOM does not resolve. This pattern tests contrast using Playwright's real-browser computed values and a proper luminance calculation.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/color-contrast-advanced.spec.ts
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

/** sRGB relative luminance per WCAG 2.x */
function sRGBLuminance(r: number, g: number, b: number): number {
  const toLinear = (c: number): number => {
    const s = c / 255;
    return s <= 0.04045 ? s / 12.92 : ((s + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4;
  };
  return 0.2126 * toLinear(r) + 0.7152 * toLinear(g) + 0.0722 * toLinear(b);
}

function contrastRatio(l1: number, l2: number): number {
  const [lighter, darker] = l1 > l2 ? [l1, l2] : [l2, l1];
  return (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05);
}

function parseRgb(css: string): [number, number, number] | null {
  const m = css.match(/rgba?\((\d+),\s*(\d+),\s*(\d+)/);
  return m ? [parseInt(m[1]), parseInt(m[2]), parseInt(m[3])] : null;
}

async function measureContrast(page: Page, selector: string): Promise<number> {
  const colors = await page.evaluate((sel) => {
    const el = document.querySelector(sel) as HTMLElement | null;
    if (!el) return null;
    const style = window.getComputedStyle(el);
    return { fg: style.color, bg: style.backgroundColor };
  }, selector);
  if (!colors) return -1;
  const fgRgb = parseRgb(colors.fg);
  const bgRgb = parseRgb(colors.bg);
  if (!fgRgb || !bgRgb) return -1;
  return contrastRatio(sRGBLuminance(...fgRgb), sRGBLuminance(...bgRgb));
}

test.describe('Color contrast — beyond axe (WCAG 1.4.3 advanced)', () => {
  test('body text meets WCAG 1.4.3 minimum 4.5:1', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const ratio = await measureContrast(page, 'main p');
    expect(ratio,
      `Body text contrast ${ratio.toFixed(2)}:1 — minimum 4.5:1 (WCAG 1.4.3 AA)`
    ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4.5);
  });

  test('large heading text meets 3:1 minimum', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const ratio = await measureContrast(page, 'h1');
    expect(ratio,
      `h1 contrast ${ratio.toFixed(2)}:1 — minimum 3:1 for large text (WCAG 1.4.3 AA)`
    ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);
  });

  test('CSS custom property color resolves in real browser (oklch / display-p3)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // getComputedStyle always returns rgb() even for oklch/display-p3 in Chromium
    const resolvedColor = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const btn = document.querySelector('button');
      if (!btn) return null;
      return window.getComputedStyle(btn).color;
    });
    // Empty string or non-rgb means the CSS custom property chain is broken
    expect(resolvedColor).toMatch(/^rgb/i);
  });

  test('disabled button is programmatically disabled (exempt from contrast by WCAG 1.4.3)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout');
    // Disabled controls are explicitly exempt from WCAG 1.4.3 contrast requirements
    // But they must be TRULY disabled, not just visually styled to look disabled
    const disabledBtns = page.locator('button[disabled], button[aria-disabled="true"]');
    if (await disabledBtns.count() > 0) {
      const isDisabled = await disabledBtns.first().evaluate((el) =>
        (el as HTMLButtonElement).disabled || el.getAttribute('aria-disabled') === 'true'
      );
      expect(isDisabled,
        'Low-contrast "disabled" buttons must be programmatically disabled'
      ).toBe(true);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use Playwright-based contrast testing for design system tokens using `oklch` or deeply-nested CSS custom properties. Do NOT use this as a replacement for axe's `color-contrast` rule — axe handles the common cases; this supplements edge cases. Alternative: Browser DevTools' color picker reports computed contrast; Lighthouse accessibility audit also reports contrast failures. [community]

### Pattern 14 (Cycle 28) — SPA Route Change Focus Management Testing

In SPAs, client-side routing does not trigger a browser navigation — the page does not reload, the `<h1>` does not change with a browser announcement, and focus stays wherever it was. Screen reader users have no indication that the route changed. WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) applies; additionally, best practice requires moving focus to the page `<h1>` or a route announcement element after route changes. Testing must verify that focus moves to a meaningful target after navigation and that a screen reader announcement fires.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/spa-route-focus.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('SPA route changes — focus management and announcements', () => {
  test('navigating to a new page moves focus to h1 or page-announcement element', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const navLink = page.getByRole('navigation').getByRole('link').nth(1);
    const linkHref = await navLink.getAttribute('href');

    await navLink.click();
    await page.waitForURL(`**${linkHref ?? '/about'}**`, { timeout: 5000 }).catch(() => {});

    // After SPA navigation, focus must move to h1 or a designated announcement element
    const focusedTag = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.tagName?.toLowerCase());

    const isValidFocusTarget =
      focusedTag === 'h1' ||
      focusedTag === 'main' ||
      (await page.locator(':focus[aria-live]').count()) > 0;

    expect(isValidFocusTarget,
      `After SPA navigation, focus must move to h1 or page title — found: ${focusedTag}`
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  test('page title updates after route change', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const initialTitle = await page.title();

    const navLink = page.getByRole('navigation').getByRole('link').nth(1);
    await navLink.click();
    await page.waitForTimeout(500);

    const newTitle = await page.title();
    expect(newTitle, 'Page title must update after SPA navigation').not.toBe(initialTitle);
    expect(newTitle.trim().length, 'New page title must not be empty').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('aria-live route announcer exists and updates on navigation', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Look for a Next.js-style or framework-injected aria-live route announcement
    const routeAnnouncer = page.locator(
      '[aria-live="assertive"][aria-atomic="true"], [data-nextjs-route-announcer], [id*="route-announce"]'
    );

    if (await routeAnnouncer.count() > 0) {
      const navLink = page.getByRole('navigation').getByRole('link').nth(1);
      await navLink.click();
      await page.waitForTimeout(300);

      // Announcer must contain the new page title text
      const announcerText = await routeAnnouncer.first().textContent();
      expect(announcerText?.trim()).toBeTruthy();
    }
  });

  test('Back/Forward browser navigation restores correct focus and title', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('navigation').getByRole('link').nth(1).click();
    await page.waitForTimeout(300);

    await page.goBack();
    await page.waitForTimeout(300);

    const titleAfterBack = await page.title();
    expect(titleAfterBack.trim().length, 'Title must be set after browser back navigation').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use SPA route focus management tests for every React Router, Next.js, Remix, or Angular application. Do NOT rely on browser history API alone — history navigation does not announce page changes to screen readers. Next.js 13+ App Router has a built-in route announcer; verify it is present and functional. Alternative: `@reach/router` and React Router v6 both have built-in focus management hooks — test the specific library's implementation. [community]

### Pattern 15 (Cycle 28) — axe-core Tag Filtering: `wcag22aa` Phased Adoption Strategy

axe-core 4.10+ fully supports WCAG 2.2 AA with the `wcag22aa` tag, covering the 9 new WCAG 2.2 success criteria. Teams adopting WCAG 2.2 must add `wcag22aa` to their `withTags()` calls — existing tests using only `['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa']` silently skip the new SC checks. This pattern shows a phased CI adoption strategy: (1) run new SC checks in report-only mode for 1 sprint to baseline violations, (2) after baseline review, add `wcag22aa` to the gate, and (3) separately enable `best-practice` rules in a non-gating advisory report.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/wcag22-tag-strategy.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';
import type { AxeResults, Result } from 'axe-core';

const WCAG22_TAGS = ['wcag22aa', 'wcag22a'] as const;

test.describe('WCAG 2.2 adoption — tag filtering strategy', () => {
  test('WCAG 2.1 AA gate: existing CI baseline (must pass)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
      .analyze();

    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('WCAG 2.2 AA advisory: new SC audit (report-only — no fail)', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const results: AxeResults = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags([...WCAG22_TAGS])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'] })
      .analyze();

    // Attach full report for sprint review — do NOT fail the test yet
    await testInfo.attach('wcag22-violations-report', {
      body: JSON.stringify({
        pageUrl: page.url(),
        violationCount: results.violations.length,
        violations: results.violations.map((v: Result) => ({
          id: v.id,
          impact: v.impact,
          description: v.description,
          wcag: v.tags.filter((t) => t.startsWith('wcag')),
          affectedElements: v.nodes.length,
        })),
        incompleteCount: results.incomplete.length,
      }, null, 2),
      contentType: 'application/json',
    });

    if (results.violations.length > 0) {
      console.warn(`[WCAG 2.2 Advisory] ${results.violations.length} violation(s) — review before enabling gate`);
    }
    // Soft pass: WCAG 2.2 advisory does not block CI yet
  });

  test('WCAG 2.2 full gate: combined 2.1+2.2 AA (enable after baseline review)', async ({ page }) => {
    test.skip(
      process.env.WCAG22_GATE_ENABLED !== 'true',
      'WCAG 2.2 gate disabled — set WCAG22_GATE_ENABLED=true after baseline review'
    );

    await page.goto('/');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
      .analyze();

    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('best-practice advisory scan: non-gating quality signal', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['best-practice'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
      .analyze();

    await testInfo.attach('best-practice-report', {
      body: JSON.stringify(results.violations.map((v: Result) => ({
        id: v.id,
        impact: v.impact,
        nodes: v.nodes.length,
      })), null, 2),
      contentType: 'application/json',
    });

    if (results.violations.length > 0) {
      console.info(`[Best Practice] ${results.violations.length} advisory issue(s) — review in next sprint`);
    }
    // Non-gating: does not cause test failure
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use the phased `wcag22aa` adoption strategy for teams currently at WCAG 2.1 AA — immediate enforcement without a baseline review will fail every existing suite and erode trust in the CI gate. Do NOT include `wcag22aa` in the primary gate without confirming SC 2.4.13 (Focus Appearance) compliance first — it is the most commonly failing new criterion. Alternative: run `@axe-core/playwright` with all tags together (`['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa']`) from day one on greenfield projects. [official]

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 28)

136. **[community] `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` inline YAML uses subset matching — missing expected items fail, but additional elements do NOT; file-based snapshots use full equality and fail on any added element**: Playwright's `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` with inline YAML checks that the expected roles/names appear as a **subset** in the real aria tree, so added children do not cause failures — only missing expected items fail. However, `toMatchAriaSnapshot({ name: 'filename' })` (file-based snapshots) performs a full equality check, and any new correctly-labelled button still fails the snapshot. Teams mistake a legitimate feature addition for a broken a11y test. WHY: File-based and inline ARIA snapshot modes have different matching semantics — teams who read only one mode of the docs apply the wrong expectation model to the other and waste debugging cycles on false failures.

137. **[community] `aria-label` on a `<div>` with no ARIA role is silently ignored by screen readers — the label exists in the DOM but is never announced**: `aria-label` is only meaningful on elements whose ARIA role supports naming. A plain `<div aria-label="Product card">` has role `generic` which does not support `aria-label` naming — NVDA and VoiceOver ignore the attribute entirely. The fix is to add `role="region"` (for a landmark) or `role="group"` alongside the `aria-label`. WHY: Developers add `aria-label` to wrapper divs as "extra labelling insurance" without realizing the attribute is only effective when the element has a nameable role — the attribute is silently dropped, creating a false sense of accessibility coverage.

138. **[community] Autocomplete listboxes (`role="listbox"` + `role="option"`) trigger VoiceOver browse mode on macOS — arrow keys navigate by virtual cursor line instead of by option unless the combobox calls `preventDefault()` on arrow keydowns**: VoiceOver on macOS switches to browse (virtual cursor) mode when it encounters a `role="listbox"`. Arrow key presses in browse mode navigate by virtual cursor position, not by `aria-activedescendant`. The ARIA APG combobox pattern requires calling `event.preventDefault()` on `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` when the listbox is open to prevent VoiceOver from intercepting the keystrokes. WHY: Most combobox implementations are tested only on Windows (NVDA/JAWS) and miss this VoiceOver interaction model entirely, shipping broken autocompletes for macOS screen reader users.

139. **[community] `role="tooltip"` elements must NOT be focusable — making tooltips focusable causes screen readers to announce tooltip content twice (once via `aria-describedby`, once as focus moves into the tooltip element)**: WCAG 1.4.13 requires tooltip content to be available via keyboard (trigger focus reveals the tooltip), but the tooltip element itself should not receive focus. The trigger's `aria-describedby` pointing to the hidden tooltip element is the correct screen reader access pattern. Adding `tabindex="0"` to the tooltip for "keyboard accessibility" breaks the ARIA APG tooltip pattern and causes duplicate speech. WHY: Developers confuse "tooltip content must be accessible" (true — via the trigger's `aria-describedby`) with "tooltip element must be focusable" (false — it should never receive direct focus), leading to a double-announcement anti-pattern.

140. **[community] `axe-core`'s `autocomplete-valid` rule only checks that existing `autocomplete` attribute values are syntactically valid — it does NOT catch inputs missing `autocomplete` entirely (like a phone field with no `autocomplete="tel"`)**: The axe `autocomplete-valid` rule fires on inputs that have an `autocomplete` attribute with an invalid value. It does NOT fire on inputs missing a required `autocomplete` attribute. SC 1.3.5 (Identify Input Purpose) is partially automated by axe, but the "missing entirely" case requires manual review. Teams see `autocomplete-valid` passing and conclude their autocomplete implementation is complete, missing that the rule only validates format. WHY: The rule name implies comprehensive autocomplete coverage, but it only validates syntax — teams skip the manual check for presence, leaving password manager incompatibility and SC 1.3.5 failures unfound.

141. **[community] `display: contents` on a flex/grid container removes it from the accessibility tree in some browsers — child elements may lose their group context and be announced without structure**: `display: contents` makes an element "disappear" from the layout box model. In Chromium prior to 2024 fixes and Firefox prior to v121, elements with `display: contents` were also removed from the accessibility tree, losing their ARIA role and any `aria-label`. This was partially fixed but remains inconsistent across older browser versions still in production. Avoid `display: contents` on elements carrying accessibility semantics (`role`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`). WHY: Teams use `display: contents` to flatten CSS grid/flex structures for layout convenience, unaware that it historically broke the accessibility tree — and even in patched browsers, the behavior can vary between screen reader + browser pairings.
