## Cycle 29 — 2026-05-14

<!-- sources: official WCAG 2.2 W3C documentation + ARIA APG patterns + Playwright accessibility-testing docs + axe-core API docs + community knowledge (MDN, common practitioner failures, screen reader behaviour) -->

### Pattern 1 (Cycle 29) — WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: Sticky Header Scroll-Padding Verification

WCAG 2.4.11 (Level AA, new in 2.2) requires that when a component receives keyboard focus, it is **not entirely hidden** by author-created content such as sticky headers, sticky footers, or fixed cookie banners. Partial obscuration is acceptable at AA level; complete coverage is a failure. The most effective CSS remedy is `scroll-padding-top` set to the height of the sticky element. Testing must verify that after tab navigation to any focusable element, that element's bounding box overlaps visible viewport space and is not completely covered by a fixed-position ancestor.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/focus-not-obscured.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.11 — Focus Not Obscured (sticky header)', () => {
  test('tabbing through page: no focused element is fully hidden by sticky header', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Dismiss any overlays so header is the only sticky element
    await page.evaluate(() => (document.activeElement as HTMLElement)?.blur());

    const stickyHeaderHeight: number = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const header = document.querySelector(
        'header[style*="position: sticky"], header.sticky, [data-sticky]'
      ) as HTMLElement | null;
      return header ? header.getBoundingClientRect().bottom : 0;
    });

    // Tab through first 30 focusable elements and verify none are fully hidden
    for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
      const focusedBox = await page.evaluate(() => {
        const el = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;
        if (!el || el === document.body) return null;
        const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        return { top: r.top, bottom: r.bottom, left: r.left, right: r.right };
      });

      if (!focusedBox) break;

      // The element's bottom must be below the sticky header — i.e. not fully hidden behind it
      expect(
        focusedBox.bottom,
        `Focused element at Tab ${i + 1} is fully hidden behind sticky header (height: ${stickyHeaderHeight}px)`
      ).toBeGreaterThan(stickyHeaderHeight);
    }
  });

  test('scroll-padding-top CSS is set to at least sticky header height', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const scrollPaddingTop: string = await page.evaluate(() =>
      getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).scrollPaddingTop
    );
    const stickyHeaderHeight: number = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const header = document.querySelector('header') as HTMLElement | null;
      return header ? header.getBoundingClientRect().height : 0;
    });

    if (stickyHeaderHeight > 0) {
      const paddingPx = parseFloat(scrollPaddingTop);
      expect(
        paddingPx,
        `scroll-padding-top (${scrollPaddingTop}) must be >= sticky header height (${stickyHeaderHeight}px)`
      ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(stickyHeaderHeight);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test on every page layout that contains a sticky/fixed header or footer. Do NOT rely on `scroll-margin` on individual elements instead of `scroll-padding` on `:root` — `scroll-margin` works for scroll-into-view operations but does not help when the user navigates by Tab key, because Tab focus movement is not a scroll operation. Alternative: if the sticky element is a dismissible cookie banner or overlay, implement keyboard-accessible dismiss before testing focus obscuration — the WCAG 2.4.11 advisory permits dismissible overlays as long as the keyboard dismiss path is accessible. [official]

---

### Pattern 2 (Cycle 29) — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size Minimum: Interactive Control Geometry with Spacing Offset

WCAG 2.5.8 (Target Size Minimum, Level AA, new in 2.2) requires that interactive targets have a minimum size of 24×24 CSS pixels, OR that the spacing offset between adjacent targets compensates for smaller sizes (the "offset" algorithm: target size + spacing from nearest target edge ≥ 24px). This is more permissive than the AAA criterion 2.5.5 (44×44px). Testing must measure the bounding box of each interactive element and, for elements smaller than 24×24, verify that their closest-neighbor spacing brings the effective target area to 24px.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/target-size.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface TargetInfo {
  tag: string;
  text: string;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  top: number;
  left: number;
  bottom: number;
  right: number;
}

test.describe('WCAG 2.5.8 — Target Size Minimum (24×24 CSS px)', () => {
  test('all interactive controls meet 24×24 minimum or spacing offset', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    const targets: TargetInfo[] = await page.evaluate((): TargetInfo[] => {
      const selectors = 'a, button, [role="button"], input, select, textarea, [role="checkbox"], [role="radio"]';
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(selectors))
        .filter((el) => {
          const s = getComputedStyle(el);
          return s.display !== 'none' && s.visibility !== 'hidden' && (el as HTMLElement).offsetParent !== null;
        })
        .map((el) => {
          const r = (el as HTMLElement).getBoundingClientRect();
          return {
            tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
            text: ((el as HTMLElement).textContent ?? '').trim().slice(0, 40),
            width: r.width,
            height: r.height,
            top: r.top,
            left: r.left,
            bottom: r.bottom,
            right: r.right,
          };
        });
    });

    const MINIMUM = 24;
    const failures: string[] = [];

    for (let i = 0; i < targets.length; i++) {
      const t = targets[i];
      if (t.width >= MINIMUM && t.height >= MINIMUM) continue;

      // Find minimum spacing to any adjacent interactive element
      let minSpacing = Infinity;
      for (let j = 0; j < targets.length; j++) {
        if (i === j) continue;
        const other = targets[j];
        const hGap = Math.max(0, Math.max(t.left - other.right, other.left - t.right));
        const vGap = Math.max(0, Math.max(t.top - other.bottom, other.top - t.bottom));
        const gap = Math.sqrt(hGap ** 2 + vGap ** 2);
        if (gap < minSpacing) minSpacing = gap;
      }

      // Effective size: smaller dimension + spacing to nearest neighbour
      const effectiveWidth = t.width + minSpacing;
      const effectiveHeight = t.height + minSpacing;

      if (effectiveWidth < MINIMUM || effectiveHeight < MINIMUM) {
        failures.push(
          `<${t.tag}> "${t.text}" — size: ${t.width.toFixed(1)}×${t.height.toFixed(1)}px, spacing: ${minSpacing.toFixed(1)}px`
        );
      }
    }

    expect(failures, `Target size failures:\n${failures.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test on forms, toolbars, and icon-only button rows — these are the highest-risk areas for small targets. Do NOT apply to inline text links within a paragraph when the link text itself is the target and surrounding text provides implicit spacing — WCAG 2.5.8 explicitly exempts inline text links. Alternative: WCAG 2.5.5 (AAA, 44×44px) should be the target for critical CTAs and primary actions; 2.5.8 is the legal floor. [official]

---

### Pattern 3 (Cycle 29) — `aria-expanded` State Testing for Disclosure Widgets (Accordion, Collapsible)

WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) requires that all user interface components expose their current state programmatically. For disclosure widgets (accordions, collapsible sections, "show more" toggles), the trigger button must carry `aria-expanded="true"` when the panel is open and `aria-expanded="false"` when closed. Testing must verify: initial state matches DOM, state updates on interaction, panel visibility matches the `aria-expanded` value, and the trigger button's accessible name makes sense when expanded and collapsed.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/aria-expanded.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 4.1.2 — aria-expanded on disclosure widgets', () => {
  test('accordion trigger: initial aria-expanded reflects panel visibility', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');

    const triggers = page.locator('[aria-expanded]');
    const count = await triggers.count();
    expect(count, 'Page must have at least one aria-expanded trigger').toBeGreaterThan(0);

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const trigger = triggers.nth(i);
      const expanded = await trigger.getAttribute('aria-expanded');
      const controlsId = await trigger.getAttribute('aria-controls');

      if (controlsId) {
        const panel = page.locator(`#${CSS.escape(controlsId)}`);
        const panelVisible = await panel.isVisible();
        const expectedExpanded = panelVisible ? 'true' : 'false';
        expect(
          expanded,
          `Trigger ${i}: aria-expanded="${expanded}" but panel is ${panelVisible ? 'visible' : 'hidden'}`
        ).toBe(expectedExpanded);
      }
    }
  });

  test('clicking closed trigger opens panel and sets aria-expanded="true"', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');

    // Find a collapsed trigger
    const closedTrigger = page.locator('[aria-expanded="false"]').first();
    await expect(closedTrigger).toBeVisible();

    const controlsId = await closedTrigger.getAttribute('aria-controls');
    await closedTrigger.click();

    await expect(closedTrigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    if (controlsId) {
      await expect(page.locator(`#${CSS.escape(controlsId)}`)).toBeVisible();
    }
  });

  test('clicking open trigger closes panel and sets aria-expanded="false"', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');

    // Ensure at least one is open — click first closed one first
    const closedTrigger = page.locator('[aria-expanded="false"]').first();
    if (await closedTrigger.isVisible()) await closedTrigger.click();

    const openTrigger = page.locator('[aria-expanded="true"]').first();
    const controlsId = await openTrigger.getAttribute('aria-controls');
    await openTrigger.click();

    await expect(openTrigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    if (controlsId) {
      await expect(page.locator(`#${CSS.escape(controlsId)}`)).toBeHidden();
    }
  });

  test('Enter and Space keys also toggle aria-expanded on keyboard navigation', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const trigger = page.locator('[aria-expanded="false"]').first();
    await trigger.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
    await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
    await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test for every accordion, collapsible, "show more", and "details/summary"-based component. Do NOT test `aria-expanded` on `<details>`/`<summary>` — these elements expose open/closed state natively via the `open` attribute and screen readers read them correctly without `aria-expanded`. Applying `aria-expanded` to `<summary>` elements creates redundant state announcements. Alternative: for `<details>`/`<summary>`, use a dedicated native semantics test that verifies the `open` attribute toggles correctly. [official]

---

### Pattern 4 (Cycle 29) — `aria-live` Region Content Injection Timing: Polite vs Assertive

WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages, Level AA) requires that dynamically injected status messages are announced by screen readers without requiring focus to move to them. The correct mechanism is `aria-live="polite"` (waits for user pause before announcing) or `role="alert"` / `aria-live="assertive"` (interrupts immediately). A critical implementation gotcha is that the `aria-live` region must exist in the DOM **before** content is injected into it — dynamically creating the element with `aria-live` and immediately adding text is unreliable; screen readers may miss the initial injection. Testing must verify the live region is present on page load and that content changes are detected.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/aria-live-region.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 4.1.3 — aria-live status message regions', () => {
  test('page has pre-rendered aria-live regions before any dynamic content', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // The live region must be in the DOM before any JS runs content into it
    const liveRegions = page.locator('[aria-live], [role="status"], [role="alert"]');
    const count = await liveRegions.count();
    expect(count, 'At least one aria-live or role=status/alert region must exist on page load').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('form submission: success message appears in live region without focus move', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');

    // Record current focus target tag
    const focusBefore = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.tagName ?? 'BODY');

    await page.fill('[name="email"], input[type="email"]', 'test@example.com');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit|send/i }).click();

    const statusRegion = page.locator('[role="status"], [aria-live="polite"]').first();
    await expect(statusRegion).not.toBeEmpty({ timeout: 5000 });

    // Focus must NOT have moved to the status region
    const focusAfter = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.tagName ?? 'BODY');
    expect(focusAfter, 'Focus must not move to the status region on message injection').toBe(focusBefore);
  });

  test('error state: role="alert" region fires assertive announcement', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    // Trigger validation error by submitting empty form
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit|send/i }).click();

    const alertRegion = page.locator('[role="alert"]').first();
    // role=alert implies aria-live="assertive" + aria-atomic="true"
    await expect(alertRegion).toBeVisible({ timeout: 3000 });
    await expect(alertRegion).not.toBeEmpty();
  });

  test('axe scan validates aria-live region attributes', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const { default: AxeBuilder } = await import('@axe-core/playwright');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2aa'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
      .analyze();
    const liveViolations = results.violations.filter((v) =>
      ['aria-live-region-content', 'aria-required-attr'].includes(v.id)
    );
    expect(liveViolations, `Live region violations: ${JSON.stringify(liveViolations.map(v => v.id))}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `aria-live="polite"` for non-critical status messages (save confirmations, filter counts, loading completion). Use `role="alert"` (which implies `aria-live="assertive"`) only for errors and urgent warnings — overusing assertive announcements breaks the screen reader user's reading flow. Do NOT create live regions dynamically in JavaScript and immediately populate them; this is a well-documented screen reader timing bug. Regions must be in the DOM before content is injected. Alternative: for chat/log patterns that append multiple messages, use `aria-live="polite"` with `aria-atomic="false"` to announce only new additions, not the full accumulated content. [official]

---

### Pattern 5 (Cycle 29) — Keyboard Navigation: Roving Tabindex for Toolbar and RadioGroup Widgets

The ARIA APG roving tabindex pattern is required for composite widgets like toolbars, radio groups, tab lists, and menubars. In this pattern, only one element within the widget has `tabindex="0"` at any time (the "rover"); all others have `tabindex="-1"`. Arrow keys move focus within the widget and update which element is the rover. Tab moves focus out of the widget entirely. Testing must verify: Tab enters the widget at the current rover, Tab exits the widget in one keystroke, arrow keys move focus within the widget, and on re-entry Tab lands on the previously active rover.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/roving-tabindex-toolbar.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA roving tabindex — toolbar and radio group patterns', () => {
  test('toolbar: exactly one button has tabindex=0 at any time', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/editor');
    const toolbar = page.getByRole('toolbar').first();
    await expect(toolbar).toBeVisible();

    const tabindex0Count = await toolbar.locator('[tabindex="0"]').count();
    expect(tabindex0Count, 'Exactly one toolbar item must have tabindex=0 (the rover)').toBe(1);

    const tabindexNeg1Count = await toolbar.locator('[tabindex="-1"]').count();
    expect(tabindexNeg1Count, 'All non-rover toolbar items must have tabindex=-1').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('toolbar: Tab enters at the rover and exits in one keystroke', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/editor');
    await page.evaluate(() => (document.activeElement as HTMLElement)?.blur());

    // Tab into the toolbar area
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');

    // Arrow keys should now move within toolbar
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const firstArrowTarget = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? '');

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const secondArrowTarget = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? '');
    expect(firstArrowTarget).not.toBe(secondArrowTarget);

    // Confirm focus is still inside toolbar
    const focusBeforeTab = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;
      return el?.closest('[role="toolbar"]') !== null;
    });
    expect(focusBeforeTab).toBe(true);

    // One Tab from within the toolbar exits it
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focusAfterTab = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;
      return el?.closest('[role="toolbar"]') !== null;
    });
    expect(focusAfterTab, 'One Tab press must exit the toolbar entirely').toBe(false);
  });

  test('radiogroup: ArrowDown moves focus and checks the focused radio', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings');
    const radioGroup = page.getByRole('radiogroup').first();
    await expect(radioGroup).toBeVisible();

    const firstRadio = radioGroup.getByRole('radio').first();
    await firstRadio.focus();

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    const secondRadio = radioGroup.getByRole('radio').nth(1);
    await expect(secondRadio).toBeFocused();
    await expect(secondRadio).toBeChecked();
  });

  test('radiogroup: arrow key wraps from last to first option', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings');
    const radioGroup = page.getByRole('radiogroup').first();
    const radios = radioGroup.getByRole('radio');
    const count = await radios.count();

    await radios.nth(count - 1).focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    await expect(radios.first()).toBeFocused();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use roving tabindex for toolbars, menubars, radio groups, tab lists, and tree widgets — any composite widget where arrow keys provide the internal navigation. Do NOT use roving tabindex for simple lists of independent links or buttons — these should all have `tabindex="0"` (native tabbing is correct for non-composite widgets). Alternative: `aria-activedescendant` is an alternative to roving tabindex where the container receives focus and uses `aria-activedescendant` to point to the active child — recommended for large virtual lists where DOM focus management is expensive. [official]

---

### Pattern 6 (Cycle 29) — Image Alt Text Completeness: Decorative vs Informative vs Functional

WCAG 1.1.1 (Non-text Content, Level A) requires text alternatives for all non-text content. The correct alt value depends on image purpose: informative images need descriptive alt text, decorative images must have `alt=""` (empty string, not omitted), functional images (e.g., icon-only buttons) must describe the function rather than the appearance. Testing must distinguish all three categories and verify each pattern is implemented correctly. Axe-core's `image-alt` rule catches missing alt attributes but does NOT catch incorrect alt text or functional images with descriptive-only alt text.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/image-alt-text.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 1.1.1 — Image alt text completeness', () => {
  test('all <img> elements have an alt attribute (even empty)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const imagesWithoutAlt = await page.evaluate(() =>
      Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('img:not([alt])'))
        .map((img) => (img as HTMLImageElement).src.split('/').pop() ?? 'unknown')
    );
    expect(imagesWithoutAlt, `Images missing alt attribute: ${imagesWithoutAlt.join(', ')}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('decorative images have alt="" (empty string, not descriptive)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const decorativeImages = page.locator('img[role="presentation"], img[aria-hidden="true"]');
    const count = await decorativeImages.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const altText = await decorativeImages.nth(i).getAttribute('alt');
      expect(altText, `Decorative image ${i} should have alt="" not "${altText}"`).toBe('');
    }
  });

  test('icon-only buttons have accessible name from aria-label (not img alt)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Icon buttons: buttons containing only an img with no visible text
    const iconButtons = page.locator('button:has(img)');
    const count = await iconButtons.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const btn = iconButtons.nth(i);
      const visibleText = (await btn.textContent())?.trim() ?? '';
      if (visibleText.length > 0) continue; // Has text — not an icon-only button

      const hasAriaLabel = await btn.evaluate((el) =>
        el.hasAttribute('aria-label') || el.hasAttribute('aria-labelledby')
      );
      const imgAlt = await btn.locator('img').first().getAttribute('alt');
      expect(
        hasAriaLabel || (imgAlt !== null && imgAlt !== ''),
        `Icon button ${i} has no accessible name`
      ).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test('axe image-alt rule passes on all key pages', async ({ page }) => {
    for (const path of ['/', '/products', '/about']) {
      await page.goto(path);
      const { default: AxeBuilder } = await import('@axe-core/playwright');
      const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'], rules: { 'image-alt': { enabled: true } } })
        .analyze();
      const violations = results.violations.filter((v) => v.id === 'image-alt');
      expect(violations, `image-alt violations on ${path}: ${violations.length}`).toHaveLength(0);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test on every page that renders images. Do NOT rely solely on axe's `image-alt` rule — it only catches missing alt attributes, not wrong alt text. Functional images inside buttons need the button's accessible name to describe the action (e.g., `aria-label="Close dialog"` on the button), not the image appearance (e.g., `alt="X icon"` on the `<img>`). Alternative: for SVG icons used as button content, prefer `aria-label` on the button and `aria-hidden="true"` on the SVG — this is more robust than relying on SVG `<title>` elements for accessible naming. [official]

---

### Pattern 7 (Cycle 29) — Language-of-Parts Testing: `lang` Attribute on Embedded Foreign Text

WCAG 3.1.2 (Language of Parts, Level AA) requires that when passages of content are in a different language from the page's primary language, those passages carry a `lang` attribute identifying the language. Screen readers use this to switch to the correct pronunciation engine. Testing for this must identify multilingual pages and verify that embedded foreign-language passages are marked up. Automated detection uses the DOM to find text nodes whose content is not in the page's declared language — a heuristic approach since automated language identification is imperfect.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/language-of-parts.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.1.1 + 3.1.2 — Language attributes', () => {
  test('html element has a valid lang attribute', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const lang = await page.locator('html').getAttribute('lang');
    expect(lang, '<html> element must have a lang attribute').not.toBeNull();
    // BCP 47 language tag: at minimum a 2-letter code
    expect(lang).toMatch(/^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Z]{2,4})?$/);
  });

  test('multilingual content blocks have lang attributes', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/multilingual-demo');

    // Find elements with explicit lang attributes (should cover foreign passages)
    const langElements = page.locator('[lang]').filter({ hasNot: page.locator('html') });
    const count = await langElements.count();
    // If the page claims multilingual content, there must be at least one lang-annotated block
    if (await page.locator('[data-multilingual], .lang-block').count() > 0) {
      expect(count, 'Multilingual page must annotate foreign passages with lang attributes').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });

  test('lang attribute values are valid BCP 47 tags', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const langValues: string[] = await page.evaluate(() =>
      Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[lang]')).map((el) => el.getAttribute('lang') ?? '')
    );

    const BCP47_PATTERN = /^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*$/i;
    const invalid = langValues.filter((v) => v && !BCP47_PATTERN.test(v));
    expect(invalid, `Invalid BCP 47 lang values: ${invalid.join(', ')}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('page title is present (confirms page is fully loaded for screen reader)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const htmlLang = await page.locator('html').getAttribute('lang');
    const title = await page.title();
    expect(title.length, 'Page must have a non-empty title for screen readers').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(htmlLang).toBeTruthy();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test on internationalized applications, content management systems, and any page that mixes languages. Do NOT test for `lang` on every single word or phrase of foreign origin — only passages of sufficient length benefit from `lang` annotation; proper nouns and technical terms are typically exempt. Alternative: for SPAs with client-side i18n libraries, verify that the `lang` attribute on `<html>` is updated dynamically when the user switches locale, not just at initial load. [official]

---

### Pattern 8 (Cycle 29) — WCAG 3.2.6 Consistent Help: Help Mechanism DOM Position Testing

WCAG 3.2.6 (Consistent Help, Level A, new in 2.2) requires that if a web page provides any help mechanism (contact info, live chat, self-help link, or automated contact tool), that mechanism must appear in the same relative order in the page structure across a set of pages. This prevents cognitive load for users who have learned where to find help. Testing must verify that help-related links appear at a consistent DOM position across all pages within the same navigation set.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/consistent-help.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface HelpElementInfo {
  text: string;
  tagName: string;
  parentRole: string | null;
  indexInParent: number;
}

async function getHelpElementInfo(
  page: import('@playwright/test').Page
): Promise<HelpElementInfo | null> {
  return page.evaluate(() => {
    const candidates = Array.from(
      document.querySelectorAll('a[href*="help"], a[href*="support"], a[href*="contact"]')
    ) as HTMLElement[];
    const el = candidates[0] ?? null;
    if (!el) return null;

    const parent = el.parentElement;
    const siblings = parent ? Array.from(parent.children) : [];
    return {
      text: el.textContent?.trim() ?? '',
      tagName: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
      parentRole: parent?.getAttribute('role') ?? parent?.tagName.toLowerCase() ?? null,
      indexInParent: siblings.indexOf(el),
    };
  });
}

test.describe('WCAG 3.2.6 — Consistent Help mechanism position', () => {
  const pages = ['/', '/products', '/dashboard', '/profile'];

  test('help mechanism appears at consistent DOM context across pages', async ({ page }) => {
    const positions: Array<{ path: string; info: HelpElementInfo | null }> = [];

    for (const path of pages) {
      await page.goto(path);
      const info = await getHelpElementInfo(page);
      positions.push({ path, info });
    }

    const pagesWithHelp = positions.filter((p) => p.info !== null);
    if (pagesWithHelp.length < 2) return; // Not enough pages with help elements to compare

    // All help elements must live in the same parent container type across pages
    const parentRoles = new Set(pagesWithHelp.map((p) => p.info?.parentRole));
    expect(
      parentRoles.size,
      `Help mechanism appears in different parent containers across pages: ${[...parentRoles].join(', ')}`
    ).toBe(1);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test for multi-page applications with a global navigation or footer that repeats across pages. Do NOT enforce exact pixel-position consistency — WCAG 3.2.6 requires consistent DOM order (relative position), not visual position. Help mechanisms in footers that naturally appear last in DOM order across all pages satisfy the criterion. Alternative: if help is provided via a floating widget (e.g., an always-visible chat bubble), verify that the widget's position in the accessibility tree is consistent and not interspersed with main content on some pages but not others. [official]

---

### Pattern 9 (Cycle 29) — `toHaveAccessibleName` + `toHaveAccessibleDescription` Combined Assertion Pattern

Playwright v1.50+ provides `toHaveAccessibleName()` and `toHaveAccessibleDescription()` assertions that check the computed accessible name and description of elements via the accessibility tree. These assertions map directly to WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) and are more reliable than checking `aria-label` attributes directly — they exercise the full accname computation algorithm including `aria-labelledby`, `<label>` association, button text, and native HTML labeling. Testing with these assertions catches naming bugs that attribute checks miss.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/accessible-name-description.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 4.1.2 — Accessible Name and Description assertions', () => {
  test('form inputs have accessible names matching their visible labels', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');

    // These assertions use the full accname algorithm, not just aria-label
    await expect(page.getByLabel('Email address')).toHaveAccessibleName('Email address');
    await expect(page.getByLabel('Password')).toHaveAccessibleName('Password');
    await expect(page.getByLabel('Confirm password')).toHaveAccessibleName('Confirm password');
  });

  test('icon-only buttons have descriptive accessible names', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    const closeBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /close|dismiss/i }).first();
    await expect(closeBtn).toHaveAccessibleName(/close|dismiss/i);
  });

  test('inputs with helper text have matching accessible descriptions', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');
    const passwordInput = page.getByLabel('Password');
    // The description should mention password requirements
    await expect(passwordInput).toHaveAccessibleDescription(
      /at least|characters|uppercase|number/i
    );
  });

  test('error state: invalid input has accessible error message as description', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');
    // Trigger validation
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign up|register/i }).click();

    const emailInput = page.getByLabel('Email address');
    // After validation error, aria-describedby must point to the error message
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAccessibleDescription(/required|invalid|enter.*email/i);
  });

  test('multiple nav elements have distinct accessible names', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const navs = page.getByRole('navigation');
    const count = await navs.count();
    if (count > 1) {
      const names: string[] = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const name = await navs.nth(i).evaluate((el) =>
          el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? el.querySelector('h2')?.textContent ?? `nav-${i}`
        );
        names.push(name);
      }
      const unique = new Set(names);
      expect(unique.size, 'Multiple <nav> elements must have distinct accessible names').toBe(count);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `toHaveAccessibleName()` and `toHaveAccessibleDescription()` instead of `toHaveAttribute('aria-label', ...)` for all accessible naming assertions — attribute checks test only one possible naming source, while the assertion checks the computed name from all sources. Do NOT use `toHaveAccessibleName('')` to assert an element has no name — use `not.toHaveAccessibleName(/.+/)` or test that the element is correctly hidden with `aria-hidden="true"`. Alternative: for components tested in unit tests, `@testing-library/jest-dom`'s `toHaveAccessibleName()` provides equivalent coverage at the component level. [official]

---

### Pattern 10 (Cycle 29) — Colour Contrast for Placeholder Text and Disabled State

WCAG 1.4.3 (Contrast Minimum, Level AA) requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. A common implementation oversight is placeholder text and disabled form control text — both often render in a lighter colour than the regular input value. While WCAG 1.4.3 technically mentions "inactive UI components" as an exception, WCAG 2.2 guidance clarifies that placeholder text conveying information essential to understanding the input must meet contrast requirements. Testing must check placeholder and disabled state contrast programmatically using axe plus targeted DOM inspection.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/placeholder-disabled-contrast.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 1.4.3 — Placeholder and disabled state contrast', () => {
  test('placeholder text contrast is not the sole label mechanism (a11y anti-pattern)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');

    // Inputs relying ONLY on placeholder text with no visible <label> are a WCAG 1.3.1 + 1.4.3 risk
    const placeholderOnlyInputs = await page.evaluate(() => {
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('input[placeholder]'))
        .filter((el) => {
          const id = el.id;
          const hasLabel = id ? !!document.querySelector(`label[for="${id}"]`) : false;
          const hasAriaLabel = el.hasAttribute('aria-label');
          const hasAriaLabelledBy = el.hasAttribute('aria-labelledby');
          return !hasLabel && !hasAriaLabel && !hasAriaLabelledBy;
        })
        .map((el) => ({
          placeholder: el.getAttribute('placeholder'),
          name: el.getAttribute('name'),
        }));
    });

    expect(
      placeholderOnlyInputs,
      `Inputs using placeholder as the only label (fails when field is filled): ${JSON.stringify(placeholderOnlyInputs)}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('axe colour-contrast scan passes for visible form elements', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');
    const { default: AxeBuilder } = await import('@axe-core/playwright');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include('form, [role="form"]')
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'], rules: { 'color-contrast': { enabled: true } } })
      .analyze();
    const contrastViolations = results.violations.filter((v) => v.id === 'color-contrast');
    expect(
      contrastViolations,
      `Colour contrast violations in form: ${contrastViolations.flatMap(v => v.nodes.map(n => n.html)).join('\n')}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('disabled inputs do not use pointer cursor (visual distinction advisory)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings');
    const disabledInputs = page.locator('input[disabled], button[disabled]');
    const count = await disabledInputs.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const cursor = await disabledInputs.nth(i).evaluate((el) =>
        getComputedStyle(el).cursor
      );
      // Disabled elements should not show a pointer — that implies interactivity
      expect(cursor, `Disabled element ${i} should not have cursor: pointer`).not.toBe('pointer');
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern on forms with placeholders used as input labels (common anti-pattern) and disabled form elements. Do NOT skip contrast testing for disabled elements just because WCAG 1.4.3 mentions "inactive UI components" as an exception — this exception applies to elements that have no functionality, not to elements that carry information about the field's purpose. Alternative: use CSS `::placeholder` colour with a contrast-checked design token (e.g., `--color-text-muted` at a minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio). [community]

---

### Pattern 11 (Cycle 29) — WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry: Multi-Step Form Auto-Population Testing

WCAG 3.3.7 (Redundant Entry, Level A, new in 2.2) requires that information previously entered in a multi-step process is either auto-populated in later steps or available for the user to select without re-typing. This prevents cognitive burden for users with memory or motor impairments. Testing must verify that fields containing data entered in previous steps are pre-filled when that same data is required again, and that the user is never required to retype information they already provided in the same session.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/redundant-entry.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.7 — Redundant Entry: multi-step form pre-population', () => {
  test('billing address pre-populates from shipping address when "same as shipping" checked', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout/shipping');

    await page.fill('[name="shipping-first-name"], #shipping-first-name', 'Jane');
    await page.fill('[name="shipping-last-name"], #shipping-last-name', 'Smith');
    await page.fill('[name="shipping-street"], #shipping-street', '123 Main St');
    await page.fill('[name="shipping-city"], #shipping-city', 'Springfield');

    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /continue|next/i }).click();

    const sameAsShipping = page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: /same as shipping/i });
    if (await sameAsShipping.isVisible()) {
      await sameAsShipping.check();
      await expect(page.locator('[name="billing-first-name"], #billing-first-name'))
        .toHaveValue('Jane');
      await expect(page.locator('[name="billing-city"], #billing-city'))
        .toHaveValue('Springfield');
    }
  });

  test('previously entered email is visible on review step without re-entry', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup/step-1');
    const testEmail = 'test-redundant@example.com';
    await page.fill('[name="email"], input[type="email"]', testEmail);
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next|continue/i }).click();
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next|continue/i }).click();

    // Email must be displayed or pre-filled — not blank — on the review step
    const emailDisplay = await page.getByText(testEmail).count();
    const emailInput = page.locator(`input[value="${testEmail}"]`);
    const emailVisible = emailDisplay > 0 || await emailInput.count() > 0;
    expect(emailVisible,
      `Email "${testEmail}" entered in step 1 must be displayed or pre-filled in later steps`
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  test('two email input fields on same step must include a "confirm email" label', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');
    const emailInputs = page.locator('input[type="email"]');
    const count = await emailInputs.count();

    if (count > 1) {
      const labels: string[] = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const label = await emailInputs.nth(i).evaluate((el) => {
          const id = el.id;
          const labelEl = id ? document.querySelector(`label[for="${id}"]`) : null;
          return labelEl?.textContent?.trim() ?? el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? '';
        });
        labels.push(label);
      }
      const hasConfirmField = labels.some((l) => /confirm|verify|repeat/i.test(l));
      expect(hasConfirmField,
        `Two email fields found without a "confirm email" label — potential WCAG 3.3.7 redundant entry violation`
      ).toBe(true);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test for checkout flows, registration wizards, onboarding sequences, and any multi-step form where the same data category is requested more than once. Do NOT flag "Confirm password" and "Confirm email" fields as WCAG 3.3.7 failures — these verification fields are explicitly excluded from the criterion as security measures. Alternative: for server-side form frameworks, verify that session storage or query parameters carry forward previous field values between route transitions. [official]

---

### Pattern 12 (Cycle 29) — `aria-haspopup` and Popup Role Validation for Menus and Comboboxes

WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) requires that triggers for popup content communicate their relationship to the popup via `aria-haspopup`. The `aria-haspopup` attribute accepts specific values: `menu`, `listbox`, `tree`, `grid`, or `dialog`. Using `aria-haspopup="true"` (legacy boolean) implies `menu` but is less explicit — screen readers may handle it inconsistently. Testing must verify that popup triggers carry the correct `aria-haspopup` value, the popup element has the matching ARIA role, and `aria-expanded` is managed alongside `aria-haspopup`.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/aria-haspopup.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const VALID_HASPOPUP_VALUES = new Set(['menu', 'listbox', 'tree', 'grid', 'dialog', 'true', 'false']);

test.describe('WCAG 4.1.2 — aria-haspopup popup trigger validation', () => {
  test('all aria-haspopup triggers have valid attribute values', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const triggers = await page.evaluate(() =>
      Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[aria-haspopup]')).map((el) => ({
        tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
        haspopup: el.getAttribute('aria-haspopup'),
        text: (el as HTMLElement).textContent?.trim().slice(0, 30),
      }))
    );

    const invalid = triggers.filter((t) => !VALID_HASPOPUP_VALUES.has(t.haspopup ?? ''));
    expect(invalid, `Invalid aria-haspopup values: ${JSON.stringify(invalid)}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('navigation dropdown: aria-haspopup="menu" trigger opens role="menu" popup', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const menuTrigger = page.locator('[aria-haspopup="menu"]').first();

    if (await menuTrigger.count() === 0) {
      test.skip();
      return;
    }

    await menuTrigger.click();
    await expect(menuTrigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

    const popup = page.getByRole('menu').first();
    await expect(popup).toBeVisible();

    const menuItems = popup.getByRole('menuitem');
    const itemCount = await menuItems.count();
    expect(itemCount, 'Menu must contain at least one menuitem').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('combobox: aria-haspopup="listbox" and popup exposes role="listbox"', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    const combobox = page.getByRole('combobox').first();

    if (await combobox.count() === 0) {
      test.skip();
      return;
    }

    const haspopup = await combobox.getAttribute('aria-haspopup');
    expect(haspopup, 'Combobox must have aria-haspopup="listbox"').toBe('listbox');

    await combobox.fill('test');
    const listbox = page.getByRole('listbox').first();
    await expect(listbox).toBeVisible({ timeout: 3000 });
  });

  test('aria-haspopup trigger updates aria-expanded on open and Escape closes', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const trigger = page.locator('[aria-haspopup][aria-expanded]').first();

    if (await trigger.count() === 0) {
      test.skip();
      return;
    }

    await trigger.click();
    await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test on navigation menus, autocomplete inputs, multi-select dropdowns, and any trigger that opens a floating popup. Do NOT use `aria-haspopup="true"` on custom components unless you need legacy screen reader compatibility — use the explicit role string instead. The legacy `true` value implies `menu`, which is incorrect for `listbox` and `dialog` popups. Alternative: for tooltips, do NOT use `aria-haspopup` — tooltips are not popups in the ARIA sense and do not have a role matching the `aria-haspopup` value set. [official]

---

### Pattern 13 (Cycle 29) — `@axe-core/playwright` Scoped Component Scan with Violation Fingerprinting

When a codebase inherits third-party widgets or legacy sections that generate known axe violations, a fingerprinting mechanism allows the test suite to distinguish accepted baseline violations from newly introduced regressions. This pattern extends the violation fingerprinting approach by scoping scans to specific components and maintaining a typed exclusion list. New violations that do not match any fingerprint fail the test, while known fingerprinted violations are reported as warnings attached to the test report.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/component-scoped-axe.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import type { Result, NodeResult } from 'axe-core';

interface ViolationFingerprint {
  ruleId: string;
  selectorContains: string;
  reason: string;
  jiraTicket: string;
}

const ACCEPTED_VIOLATIONS: ViolationFingerprint[] = [
  {
    ruleId: 'color-contrast',
    selectorContains: '.legacy-datepicker',
    reason: 'Third-party datepicker v2.x — upgrade to v3 tracked in A11Y-204',
    jiraTicket: 'A11Y-204',
  },
  {
    ruleId: 'aria-required-attr',
    selectorContains: '#analytics-widget',
    reason: 'Analytics embed — vendor fix in progress, tracked in A11Y-211',
    jiraTicket: 'A11Y-211',
  },
];

function isAcceptedViolation(ruleId: string, node: NodeResult): boolean {
  return ACCEPTED_VIOLATIONS.some(
    (fp) => fp.ruleId === ruleId && node.target.some((sel) => sel.includes(fp.selectorContains))
  );
}

test.describe('Component scoped axe scan with fingerprinting', () => {
  test('main content area: no unaccepted violations', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    const { default: AxeBuilder } = await import('@axe-core/playwright');

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include('main, [role="main"], #main-content')
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
      .analyze();

    const unaccepted: Result[] = [];
    const accepted: Array<{ ruleId: string; selector: string; ticket: string }> = [];

    for (const violation of results.violations) {
      for (const node of violation.nodes) {
        if (isAcceptedViolation(violation.id, node)) {
          const fp = ACCEPTED_VIOLATIONS.find(
            (f) => f.ruleId === violation.id &&
              node.target.some((sel) => sel.includes(f.selectorContains))
          );
          accepted.push({ ruleId: violation.id, selector: node.target.join(', '), ticket: fp?.jiraTicket ?? '' });
        } else {
          unaccepted.push({ ...violation, nodes: [node] });
        }
      }
    }

    if (accepted.length > 0) {
      await testInfo.attach('accepted-violations-report', {
        body: JSON.stringify(accepted, null, 2),
        contentType: 'application/json',
      });
    }

    expect(
      unaccepted,
      `New unaccepted violations:\n${unaccepted.map((v) => `  ${v.id}: ${v.nodes[0]?.html ?? ''}`).join('\n')}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use violation fingerprinting when your project contains unmaintained third-party widgets, legacy sections under active migration, or analytics embeds you cannot modify. Do NOT add entries to `ACCEPTED_VIOLATIONS` without a Jira/GitHub issue ticket and a target resolution date — the list grows unbounded without a remediation process. Alternative: use `.exclude()` in AxeBuilder to skip scanned sections entirely, but only for sections completely outside the team's control; fingerprinting is preferable when the section is partially owned since it continues to catch regression in surrounding elements. [community]

---

### Pattern 14 (Cycle 29) — Voice Control Compatibility: `Label in Name` (WCAG 2.5.3) Testing

WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name, Level A) requires that for UI components with visible text labels, the accessible name contains the visible text. Voice control users (Dragon NaturallySpeaking, Windows Speech Recognition, iOS Voice Control) activate controls by saying the visible text label. If the accessible name differs from the visible text — for example, a button displaying "Search" but with `aria-label="Search the product catalog"` — voice control users must say the full aria-label phrase, not the visible word. Testing must verify that accessible names begin with or contain the visible text as a substring.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/label-in-name.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface LabeledControl {
  tag: string;
  visibleText: string;
  accessibleName: string;
  html: string;
}

test.describe('WCAG 2.5.3 — Label in Name for voice control compatibility', () => {
  test('interactive controls: accessible name contains visible text label', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    const controls: LabeledControl[] = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const selectors = 'a[aria-label], button[aria-label], [role="button"][aria-label]';
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(selectors))
        .map((el) => {
          const visibleText = (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.trim() ?? '';
          const ariaLabel = el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? '';
          return {
            tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
            visibleText,
            accessibleName: ariaLabel,
            html: el.outerHTML.slice(0, 120),
          };
        })
        .filter((c) => c.visibleText.length > 0 && c.accessibleName.length > 0);
    });

    const failures: string[] = [];
    for (const control of controls) {
      const visLower = control.visibleText.toLowerCase();
      const nameLower = control.accessibleName.toLowerCase();
      // WCAG 2.5.3: the accessible name must CONTAIN the visible text (case-insensitive)
      if (!nameLower.includes(visLower)) {
        failures.push(
          `<${control.tag}> visible: "${control.visibleText}" | accessible name: "${control.accessibleName}"`
        );
      }
    }

    expect(
      failures,
      `Label-in-Name violations (accessible name does not contain visible text):\n${failures.join('\n')}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('axe label-content-name-mismatch rule explicitly enabled and passing', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const { default: AxeBuilder } = await import('@axe-core/playwright');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .options({
        resultTypes: ['violations'],
        rules: { 'label-content-name-mismatch': { enabled: true } },
      })
      .analyze();
    const violations = results.violations.filter((v) => v.id === 'label-content-name-mismatch');
    expect(
      violations,
      `label-content-name-mismatch violations:\n${violations.flatMap(v => v.nodes.map(n => n.html)).join('\n')}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test for any interactive element that has both visible text content and an `aria-label`. Do NOT add `aria-label` to buttons or links just to provide extra context — if the visible text is sufficient, omit `aria-label` entirely; accessible name computation will use the visible text. If extra context is needed, use `aria-describedby` to add a description without replacing the name. Alternative: for icon buttons where there is no visible text, `aria-label` is the correct pattern and this criterion does not apply (there is no visible text to include in the name). [official]

---

### Pattern 15 (Cycle 29) — Playwright `ariaSnapshot` for Regression Testing After Content Changes

Playwright v1.49+ introduced `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` which serializes the accessibility tree into a YAML-like format and asserts it matches an expected baseline. When using inline YAML, the match is a subset — extra elements do not cause failures. When using file-based snapshots (`.aria.yaml`), the match is full equality. This pattern demonstrates the correct use of inline subset matching for regression testing of interactive components after content updates, including the `/children` skip pattern for ignoring dynamic child counts.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/aria-snapshot-regression.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Playwright ariaSnapshot — accessibility tree regression testing', () => {
  test('navigation menu: structure matches expected ARIA tree (subset match)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const nav = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /main/i }).first();

    // Inline YAML subset match — extra items in the real nav are OK, but these must exist
    await expect(nav).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - navigation "Main":
        - link "Home"
        - link "Products"
        - link "About"
    `);
  });

  test('modal dialog: ARIA structure correct when open', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /settings/i }).first().click();
    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();

    // The dialog must expose its title as a heading and have a close button
    await expect(dialog).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - dialog:
        - heading /settings/i
        - button "Close"
    `);
  });

  test('form fields: labels and roles visible in ARIA tree', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');

    const form = page.getByRole('form').first();
    await expect(form).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - form:
        - textbox "Email address"
        - textbox "Password"
        - button /sign up|register/i
    `);
  });

  test('search results: live region update reflected in aria snapshot', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    await page.fill('[role="searchbox"], input[type="search"]', 'laptop');
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

    const resultsRegion = page.getByRole('region', { name: /results/i }).first();
    await expect(resultsRegion).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5000 });

    // The results region must announce a count — subset match allows dynamic item count
    await expect(resultsRegion).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - region /results/i:
        - /\\d+ results? found/i
    `);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use inline `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` for component-level regression tests where child count may change; use file-based `.aria.yaml` snapshots only for stable, final-form components where any change (including correct additions) must be reviewed. Do NOT use `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` as a substitute for semantic assertions — if you need to verify that a specific button exists with a specific name, `getByRole` + `toHaveAccessibleName` is more readable and less brittle. Alternative: for teams running Playwright < 1.49, `page.accessibility.snapshot()` provided similar coverage, but was removed in Playwright 1.57 and must be replaced with `page.ariaSnapshot()` or `locator.ariaSnapshot()`. [official]

---

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 29)

142. **[community] `aria-label` on a `<section>` element does not create a landmark unless the browser's accessible name assignment triggers implicit landmark promotion**: In HTML, a `<section>` element only becomes a `region` landmark when it has an accessible name (via `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`). This is correct ARIA spec behaviour, but it means unnamed `<section>` elements are NOT exposed as landmarks — they are treated as `generic` role. The problem is subtle: teams add `<section>` elements expecting landmark navigation to work, but without an `aria-label`, screen reader users cannot jump to those sections via the landmark shortcuts (H or F6 in JAWS/NVDA). WHY: The spec's conditional landmark promotion behaviour (section becomes region only when named) is counterintuitive — developers assume the element alone creates a landmark, leading to navigation structures that look semantically correct in HTML but fail in screen reader landmark navigation entirely.

143. **[community] `axe-core` does not detect all WCAG 1.3.5 (Identify Input Purpose) failures — inputs like date-of-birth or phone number fields that lack `autocomplete` attributes pass axe silently**: The `autocomplete-valid` axe rule validates that existing `autocomplete` attribute values are syntactically correct, but it does NOT flag inputs that are missing `autocomplete` entirely. A date-of-birth field with `<input type="text" name="dob">` passes axe even though SC 1.3.5 requires `autocomplete="bday"`. WHY: The rule was designed to fix broken autocomplete values, not to enforce that all personal-data fields declare their purpose — teams mistake passing axe for full SC 1.3.5 compliance and skip the manual audit of form field autocomplete attributes, leaving password manager incompatibility and SC 1.3.5 failures unfound.

144. **[community] Playwright's `getByRole('button')` locates `<input type="submit">` elements — teams expecting only `<button>` elements are surprised when submit inputs are returned and `toHaveText()` fails**: The `getByRole` locator uses the ARIA role of elements, and `<input type="submit">` has an implicit role of `button`. Teams writing `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })` may intend to locate a `<button>Submit</button>` but instead get `<input type="submit" value="Submit">`. This is correct from an ARIA perspective, but `toHaveText()` fails because inputs have no text content — the name comes from the `value` attribute. WHY: The disconnect between HTML element type and ARIA role causes test authors to write name assertions using the wrong method (toHaveText vs toHaveAccessibleName vs toHaveValue), producing confusing failures on forms with submit inputs that work correctly for users.

145. **[community] `tabindex="0"` on a `<div>` makes it focusable but does NOT give it a role — screen readers announce it as text with no action verb, confusing keyboard users who expect to activate it**: Adding `tabindex="0"` to a `<div>` that functions as a button allows keyboard focus but does not add ARIA role semantics. Screen readers will announce the text content followed by nothing or "group", not "button". The user does not know they can press Enter or Space to activate it, because no role signals that it is interactive. The correct fix is `<div role="button" tabindex="0">` or better yet a real `<button>` element. WHY: Developers add `tabindex="0"` to pass "keyboard accessible" ticket acceptance criteria without understanding that keyboard focusability alone is not sufficient — WCAG 4.1.2 requires the role to be programmatically determinable, which `tabindex` alone does not provide.

146. **[community] iOS VoiceOver handles `aria-hidden="true"` on focusable elements inconsistently — swipe navigation may still land on aria-hidden focusable elements on older iOS versions even when correctly excluded from the virtual buffer on desktop screen readers**: On desktop (NVDA + Firefox/Chrome, JAWS + Chrome/Edge), `aria-hidden="true"` combined with `tabindex="-1"` reliably hides an element from both virtual cursor navigation and keyboard focus. On iOS VoiceOver, elements with `aria-hidden="true"` but without `tabindex="-1"` may still receive focus via swipe gesture in some browser + iOS version pairings. The safest combined approach is `aria-hidden="true"` + `tabindex="-1"` + the `inert` attribute (widely supported since 2023) on container elements. WHY: Teams test screen reader compatibility only on desktop and assume aria-hidden behaves identically on mobile — the iOS VoiceOver swipe model operates differently from the desktop virtual cursor model and older iOS versions do not fully honour aria-hidden on focusable elements.

| WCAG 2.2 Understanding — Accessible Authentication (3.3.8) | Official | https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/accessible-authentication-minimum.html | Paste/autocomplete; four compliant pathways |
| WCAG 2.2 Understanding — Consistent Help (3.2.6) | Official | https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-help.html | DOM order consistency; help mechanism types |
| WCAG 2.2 Understanding — Redundant Entry (3.3.7) | Official | https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/redundant-entry.html | Pre-population; confirm fields security exception |
| ARIA APG — Dialog Modal Pattern | Official | https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/ | Focus trap; required ARIA attributes; Escape behaviour |
| ARIA APG — Toolbar Pattern | Official | https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/ | Roving tabindex; arrow key navigation contract |
| Playwright toMatchAriaSnapshot API | Official | https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locatorassertions#locator-assertions-to-match-aria-snapshot | Inline vs file-based snapshot matching semantics |
| axe-core label-content-name-mismatch rule | Official | https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/label-content-name-mismatch | WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name automated detection |

## Cycle 30 — 2026-05-14

<!-- sources: Playwright accessibility-testing docs (WebFetch) + axe-core API docs (WebFetch) + WCAG 2.2 Understanding docs (WebFetch) + axe-core CHANGELOG 4.9–4.11 (WebFetch) + ARIA APG patterns (WebFetch) + WCAG 2.2 new criteria research + community knowledge base -->

### Pattern 1 (Cycle 30) — `axe.run()` Cross-Origin iframe Accessibility Scanning with `allowedOrigins`

By default axe-core only scans iframes that share the same origin as the parent page. When your application embeds third-party widgets (payment forms, maps, video players) in cross-origin iframes, axe silently skips them. For owned cross-origin iframes (e.g., a subdomain widget or a micro-frontend), you must explicitly list the frame origins in `axe.configure({ allowedOrigins: [...] })` called **inside each iframe document separately**. This is distinct from excluding iframes via `AxeBuilder.exclude()` — exclusion hides the gap, while `allowedOrigins` actually scans the content.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/cross-origin-iframe.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

/**
 * Pattern: axe cross-origin iframe scanning
 * Requirement: axe.configure({ allowedOrigins }) must be injected into each
 * iframe document individually — it does not propagate from the parent frame.
 */
test.describe('Cross-origin iframe accessibility', () => {
  test('owned subdomain iframe is included in axe scan', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout');

    // Wait for the payment iframe to load
    await page.frameLocator('iframe[title="Payment form"]')
      .locator('input[name="card-number"]').waitFor();

    // Inject axe into the iframe and configure allowedOrigins
    const iframeHandle = await page.$('iframe[title="Payment form"]');
    const frame = await iframeHandle!.contentFrame();
    expect(frame).not.toBeNull();

    // axe.configure must be called within the iframe's browsing context
    await frame!.evaluate(() => {
      // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
      (window as any).axe.configure({
        allowedOrigins: ['https://payments.example.com'],
      });
    });

    // Run axe inside the iframe directly
    const results = await frame!.evaluate(async () => {
      // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
      return (window as any).axe.run(document, {
        resultTypes: ['violations'],
        runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'] },
      });
    });

    const violations = (results as { violations: { id: string; impact: string }[] }).violations;
    if (violations.length > 0) {
      console.table(violations.map((v) => ({ id: v.id, impact: v.impact })));
    }
    expect(violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('third-party iframe excluded from scan (documented gap)', async ({ page }) => {
    const { default: AxeBuilder } = await import('@axe-core/playwright');
    await page.goto('/checkout');

    // Exclude unowned third-party iframes from the scan to avoid false positives
    // Document this as a known gap — manual review required
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .exclude('iframe[src*="third-party-analytics.com"]')
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
      .analyze();

    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `allowedOrigins` + in-iframe axe injection for iframes on subdomains your team owns. Do NOT attempt cross-origin injection on truly third-party iframes (Google Maps, Stripe embedded, social widgets) — you cannot inject scripts into them. Instead use `.exclude()` and log the exclusion as a documented gap in your ACR/VPAT. Alternative: WCAG 2.1 AA conformance claims can exclude third-party content that you do not control, but you must document the exclusion. [official]

### Pattern 2 (Cycle 30) — `axe-core` Shadow DOM Scanning with Open vs Closed Mode Detection

axe-core supports Shadow DOM via a flattened tree approach (v4.1+), but only for `mode: 'open'` shadow roots. Closed shadow roots are invisible to axe and must be excluded from conformance claims. For open shadow roots, axe automatically pierces into the shadow tree. This pattern tests: (1) shadow host accessible names, (2) that all custom elements use open mode, and (3) that slotted content labels are correctly exposed.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/shadow-dom.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('Shadow DOM component accessibility', () => {
  test('web component with open shadow root scanned by axe', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/design-system-showcase');

    // Ensure the custom element is upgraded before scanning
    await page.waitForFunction(() => customElements.get('my-button') !== undefined);

    // axe-core automatically pierces open shadow roots — no special config needed
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include('my-button')
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
      .analyze();

    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('shadow host exposes an accessible name to assistive technology', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/design-system-showcase');

    const hostName = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const host = document.querySelector('my-card[aria-label]');
      return host?.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? null;
    });

    expect(hostName).not.toBeNull();
    expect(hostName!.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('closed shadow roots documented as a scan gap', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/design-system-showcase');

    // Identify any elements marked as having closed shadow roots
    const closedHosts = await page.evaluate(() => {
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[data-shadow-mode="closed"]'))
        .map((el) => el.tagName.toLowerCase());
    });

    // Fail if undocumented closed shadow roots exist
    expect(
      closedHosts,
      `Closed shadow roots found — axe cannot scan them: ${closedHosts.join(', ')}. ` +
      'Add to a11y-exemptions.json or convert to open mode.'
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern for design system components built as web components. Do NOT assume axe fully covers Shadow DOM if the team uses `mode: 'closed'` — closed shadow roots require manual AT review on every release. Alternative: Storybook's `@storybook/addon-a11y` plugin also pierces open shadow roots, making it complementary for component-level testing during development. [official]

### Pattern 3 (Cycle 30) — WCAG 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced AA) — Sticky Header + Footer Guard

WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.12 (Level AA) requires that when a keyboard-focused element is scrolled into view, no part of it is fully hidden by sticky/fixed positioned content. The canonical CSS fix is `scroll-padding-top` / `scroll-padding-bottom` on the `<html>` element. This pattern tests both that the CSS fix is present and that focus remains geometrically visible during keyboard navigation.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/focus-not-obscured.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.12 — Focus Not Obscured Enhanced (AA)', () => {
  test('scroll-padding-top is at least as tall as the sticky header', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    const { headerHeight, scrollPaddingTop } = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const header = document.querySelector(
        'header[data-sticky], .sticky-header, [style*="position: sticky"]'
      );
      const hHeight = header ? (header as HTMLElement).offsetHeight : 0;
      const paddingStr = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).scrollPaddingTop;
      const paddingVal = parseInt(paddingStr, 10) || 0;
      return { headerHeight: hHeight, scrollPaddingTop: paddingVal };
    });

    expect(
      scrollPaddingTop,
      `scroll-padding-top (${scrollPaddingTop}px) must be >= sticky header height (${headerHeight}px)`
    ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(headerHeight);
  });

  test('last focusable element is not hidden under a sticky footer', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/long-content-page');

    // Tab to the last focusable element
    let prevFocused = '';
    for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
      const current = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.outerHTML ?? '');
      if (current === prevFocused) break;
      prevFocused = current;
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    }

    const visibility = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const focused = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;
      if (!focused) return { obscured: false, reason: 'no focused element' };
      const fRect = focused.getBoundingClientRect();
      const footer = document.querySelector('footer[data-sticky], .sticky-footer');
      if (!footer) return { obscured: false, reason: 'no sticky footer' };
      const fFooter = footer.getBoundingClientRect();
      const obscured = fRect.bottom > fFooter.top;
      return {
        obscured,
        reason: obscured
          ? `focused element bottom (${fRect.bottom}) overlaps sticky footer top (${fFooter.top})`
          : 'ok',
      };
    });

    expect(visibility.obscured, visibility.reason).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `scroll-padding` as a CSS-only fix — it is zero-overhead and requires no JavaScript. Do NOT add `scroll-padding` as an inline style via JavaScript on each focus event; the CSS approach is more reliable and performant. If the sticky element height changes responsively, set `scroll-padding-top` as a CSS variable updated by a ResizeObserver. Alternative: `scroll-margin-top` on individual focusable elements also works but requires adding it to every interactive element and breaks when new elements are added. [official]

### Pattern 4 (Cycle 30) — axe-core 4.10.0 `summary-name` Rule: `<details>/<summary>` Accessible Name

axe-core 4.10.0 added the `summary-name` rule, which flags `<summary>` elements without an accessible name. A `<details>/<summary>` widget is the native HTML accordion — it requires no ARIA, but the `<summary>` must have a non-empty accessible name. The rule catches summaries containing only unlabelled images. Importantly, `<details>` manages its own open/closed state natively — adding `aria-expanded` to `<summary>` creates conflicting signals.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/summary-name.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('axe-core summary-name rule — details/summary disclosure widgets', () => {
  test('all summary elements on the FAQ page have accessible names', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['summary-name'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
      .analyze();

    expect(
      results.violations,
      `summary-name violations:\n` +
      results.violations.flatMap((v) => v.nodes.map((n) => `  ${n.html}`)).join('\n')
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('icon SVGs inside summary elements are aria-hidden', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');

    const iconViolations = await page.evaluate(() => {
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('summary svg'))
        .filter((svg) => svg.getAttribute('aria-hidden') !== 'true')
        .map((svg) => svg.closest('summary')?.textContent?.trim() ?? 'unknown');
    });

    expect(
      iconViolations,
      `SVGs inside <summary> without aria-hidden="true": ${iconViolations.join(', ')}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('summary has no redundant aria-expanded — native details manages state', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');

    const hasRedundantExpanded = await page.evaluate(() =>
      document.querySelector('details summary[aria-expanded]') !== null
    );
    expect(
      hasRedundantExpanded,
      '<summary> must NOT have aria-expanded — <details> manages state natively'
    ).toBe(false);
  });

  test('details open/closed state is operable by keyboard', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const firstSummary = page.locator('details summary').first();
    await firstSummary.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

    const isOpen = await page.evaluate(() =>
      (document.querySelector('details') as HTMLDetailsElement | null)?.open ?? false
    );
    expect(isOpen).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use native `<details>/<summary>` for simple disclosure widgets — it requires no ARIA and no JavaScript for state management. Do NOT add `aria-expanded` to `<summary>` elements; native `<details>` communicates open/closed state automatically and `aria-expanded` creates conflicting signals. Use the ARIA accordion pattern (role="button", aria-expanded, aria-controls) only when you need animation control, multiple-panel open states, or custom keyboard interactions. [official]

### Pattern 5 (Cycle 30) — WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text and 1.4.10 Reflow: Viewport-Based Zoom Testing

WCAG 1.4.4 requires text to resize to 200% without loss of content or functionality. WCAG 1.4.10 (Reflow) requires content to reflow at 320 CSS px width (equivalent to 400% zoom on 1280px) without horizontal scrolling. Playwright tests both by setting viewport dimensions and checking for horizontal overflow.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/zoom-reflow.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const ZOOM_LEVELS = [
  { label: '100%', width: 1280, height: 720 },
  { label: '200%', width: 640, height: 360 },
  { label: '400%/320px reflow', width: 320, height: 256 },
];

test.describe('WCAG 1.4.4 + 1.4.10 — Text resize and reflow', () => {
  for (const zoom of ZOOM_LEVELS) {
    test(`no horizontal scroll at ${zoom.label} (${zoom.width}px width)`, async ({ page }) => {
      await page.setViewportSize({ width: zoom.width, height: zoom.height });
      await page.goto('/');
      await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

      const hasHorizontalOverflow = await page.evaluate(() =>
        document.documentElement.scrollWidth > document.documentElement.clientWidth
      );

      expect(
        hasHorizontalOverflow,
        `Horizontal overflow at ${zoom.label}: scrollWidth > clientWidth`
      ).toBe(false);
    });
  }

  test('form inputs remain operable at 320px width', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setViewportSize({ width: 320, height: 568 });
    await page.goto('/contact');

    const nameInput = page.getByLabel(/name/i).first();
    await nameInput.fill('Test User');
    await expect(nameInput).toHaveValue('Test User');

    const submitBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit|send/i });
    await expect(submitBtn).toBeVisible();
    await expect(submitBtn).toBeEnabled();
  });

  test('navigation links present (in hamburger or inline) at 320px', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setViewportSize({ width: 320, height: 568 });
    await page.goto('/');
    const navLinks = page.getByRole('navigation').getByRole('link');
    // Links may be in a collapsed menu — assert they exist in DOM
    expect(await navLinks.count()).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use viewport resizing to simulate zoom in CI where browser-level zoom APIs are unavailable. Do NOT treat passing viewport tests as full zoom compliance — CSS `zoom` and browser text-only zoom can produce different overflow patterns that viewport resizing does not replicate. For high-confidence results, supplement with manual tests in Chrome (Ctrl+Plus to 200%) and Firefox text-only zoom. Alternative: Playwright's `page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' })` does not affect zoom; these are separate test concerns. [official]
