### Pattern 6 (Cycle 30) — `@axe-core/react` Development-Time Violation Logging

`@axe-core/react` runs axe-core automatically after every React render in development mode. Unlike `jest-axe` (snapshot-based), it tests the live DOM in the browser during development, catching issues that only appear after interaction (state-driven ARIA changes, dynamically rendered tooltips, async-loaded content). It is a development ergonomic tool, not a CI gate.

```typescript
// src/index.tsx — development-only @axe-core/react setup
import React from 'react';
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client';
import App from './App';

async function setupA11yDevMode(): Promise<void> {
  if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') {
    // Dynamic import ensures zero production bundle impact
    const axe = await import('@axe-core/react');
    await axe.default(React, ReactDOM, 1000, {
      runOnly: {
        type: 'tag',
        values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'best-practice'],
      },
      rules: [
        // color-contrast works in real browser unlike jest-axe/JSDOM
        { id: 'color-contrast', enabled: true },
      ],
    });
    console.info('[a11y] @axe-core/react active — violations logged to DevTools console');
  }
}

// Initialize a11y dev mode before mounting the React root
setupA11yDevMode().then(() => {
  const root = ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root') as HTMLElement);
  root.render(
    <React.StrictMode>
      <App />
    </React.StrictMode>
  );
});

// Expected console output when a violation exists:
// [axe] button-name (critical): Buttons must have discernible text
//   node: <button><svg aria-hidden="true">...</svg></button>
//   helpUrl: https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.11/button-name
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `@axe-core/react` as a developer ergonomic tool to surface violations inline during feature development — it catches issues before code review without requiring a separate test run. Do NOT rely on it as a CI gate — it runs only in the browser during development and produces console output, not programmatic pass/fail. For CI, use `jest-axe` (component level) and `@axe-core/playwright` (E2E level). Note: v4.11+ supports React 18 with no additional configuration. [official]

### Pattern 7 (Cycle 30) — WCAG 3.2.6 Consistent Help: Cross-Page DOM Order Verification

WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6 (Level A, new in 2.2) requires that help mechanisms (human contact info, chat widget, self-help link, automated help tool) appear in the same relative DOM order on every page where they appear. This requires cross-page comparison, not single-page auditing — axe-core has no rule for it.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/consistent-help.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const PAGES_TO_CHECK = ['/', '/products', '/about', '/contact'];

interface HelpInfo {
  found: boolean;
  position: number;
  totalInteractive: number;
}

async function getHelpPosition(page: import('@playwright/test').Page): Promise<HelpInfo> {
  return page.evaluate(() => {
    const helpSelectors = [
      '[data-testid="help-widget"]',
      '[aria-label*="help" i]',
      '[aria-label*="support" i]',
      'a[href*="/help"]',
      'a[href*="/support"]',
      '#chat-widget',
    ];
    const allInteractive = Array.from(
      document.querySelectorAll('a[href], button:not([disabled]), [role="button"]')
    );
    for (const selector of helpSelectors) {
      const el = document.querySelector(selector) as HTMLElement | null;
      if (el) {
        return { found: true, position: allInteractive.indexOf(el), totalInteractive: allInteractive.length };
      }
    }
    return { found: false, position: -1, totalInteractive: allInteractive.length };
  });
}

test.describe('WCAG 3.2.6 — Consistent Help mechanism DOM order', () => {
  test('help mechanism appears at consistent relative DOM position across pages', async ({ page }) => {
    const positions: { url: string; position: number; total: number }[] = [];

    for (const url of PAGES_TO_CHECK) {
      await page.goto(url);
      await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
      const info = await getHelpPosition(page);
      if (info.found) {
        positions.push({ url, position: info.position, total: info.total });
      }
    }

    if (positions.length < 2) return; // Not enough data to compare

    const relatives = positions.map((p) => p.position / p.total);
    const maxDelta = Math.max(...relatives) - Math.min(...relatives);

    // Allow 10% tolerance for page-to-page variation in total element count
    expect(
      maxDelta,
      `Help mechanism relative position varies too much (delta: ${maxDelta.toFixed(2)}). ` +
      `Positions: ${JSON.stringify(positions)}`
    ).toBeLessThan(0.10);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test when your app has a chat widget, help button, or "Contact Support" link on multiple pages. Do NOT implement this test if help mechanisms only appear on specific pages — 3.2.6 only applies to mechanisms that recur across a set of pages. Alternative: manual review using browser DevTools to compare DOM order on two representative pages is faster for initial compliance checks; automate only after the pattern is confirmed. [official]

---

### Pattern 8 (Cycle 30) — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size Minimum (24×24 CSS px) Geometry Testing

WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (Target Size Minimum, Level AA) requires all interactive targets to be at least 24×24 CSS pixels, or that spacing around a smaller target brings the effective touch area to 24×24. This is the AA floor (not the AAA 44×44 target from 2.5.5). axe-core has no built-in rule for this — it must be implemented as a custom check.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/target-size.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface TargetInfo {
  tag: string;
  html: string;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  meetsMinimum: boolean;
}

test.describe('WCAG 2.5.8 — Target Size Minimum (24×24 CSS px)', () => {
  test('all interactive targets meet 24×24px minimum on homepage', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const targets: TargetInfo[] = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const MIN_SIZE = 24;
      const interactives = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(
        'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input[type="checkbox"], input[type="radio"], ' +
        '[role="button"], [role="link"], [role="checkbox"], [role="radio"], [role="switch"]'
      ));
      return interactives.map((el) => {
        const rect = (el as HTMLElement).getBoundingClientRect();
        return {
          tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
          html: el.outerHTML.slice(0, 100),
          width: Math.round(rect.width),
          height: Math.round(rect.height),
          meetsMinimum: rect.width >= MIN_SIZE && rect.height >= MIN_SIZE,
        };
      });
    });

    const failures = targets.filter((t) => !t.meetsMinimum);
    expect(
      failures,
      `Targets below 24×24px minimum:\n` +
      failures.map((f) => `  ${f.tag} ${f.width}×${f.height}px: ${f.html}`).join('\n')
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('inline text links in paragraphs are exempt from 2.5.8', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/article');

    // Inline links in body text are explicitly exempt from 2.5.8 (inline exception)
    // Flag only suspiciously tiny heights that suggest something else is wrong
    const suspiciousLinks = await page.evaluate(() => {
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('p a[href], li a[href]'))
        .filter((el) => (el as HTMLElement).getBoundingClientRect().height < 12)
        .map((el) => el.outerHTML.slice(0, 80));
    });

    expect(
      suspiciousLinks,
      `Inline links with height < 12px (non-exempt size issue):\n${suspiciousLinks.join('\n')}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use target size testing in CI for navigation, toolbar, and form controls. Do NOT enforce 24px on inline text links within prose — WCAG 2.5.8 includes an explicit inline exception where line height provides adequate spacing. The AAA criterion 2.5.5 (44×44px) is better for mobile-first touch targets. Alternative: axe-core does not have a built-in `target-size` rule at the 24px threshold — this test must be implemented as a custom check. [official]

---

### Pattern 9 (Cycle 30) — WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication: Paste and Autocomplete in Login Forms

WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.8 (Accessible Authentication Minimum, Level AA) prohibits cognitive function tests in authentication unless a compliant alternative is provided. Testing must verify that password managers work, paste is not blocked, and `autocomplete` attributes are correct. Blocking paste is both a WCAG 3.3.8 failure and a security anti-pattern.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/accessible-auth.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.8 — Accessible Authentication (AA)', () => {
  test('login form has correct autocomplete attributes', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');

    const usernameAC = await page
      .locator('input[name="username"], input[type="email"]').first()
      .getAttribute('autocomplete');
    const passwordAC = await page
      .locator('input[type="password"]').first()
      .getAttribute('autocomplete');

    // SC 1.3.5 + 3.3.8: credentials must have autocomplete to support password managers
    expect(
      ['username', 'email'],
      `Username/email autocomplete must be "username" or "email", got: "${usernameAC}"`
    ).toContain(usernameAC);

    expect(
      ['current-password', 'new-password'],
      `Password autocomplete must be "current-password" or "new-password", got: "${passwordAC}"`
    ).toContain(passwordAC);
  });

  test('password field allows programmatic fill (no paste block via readonly/maxlength=0)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');

    const passwordField = page.getByLabel(/password/i);
    // Playwright fill() would throw if the field is disabled or readonly
    await passwordField.fill('SecurePass123!');
    await expect(passwordField).toHaveValue('SecurePass123!');
  });

  test('CAPTCHA, if present, has an audio alternative (SC 3.3.8 compliant path)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');

    const hasCaptcha = await page.locator('iframe[title*="recaptcha" i]').count();
    if (hasCaptcha > 0) {
      // Verify audio challenge button exists as the accessible alternative
      await expect(
        page.locator('[id*="recaptcha-audio"]').first(),
        'CAPTCHA must provide an audio alternative for SC 3.3.8 compliance'
      ).toBeAttached();
    }
  });

  test('WebAuthn/passkey option available as cognitive-test-free auth path', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    // Passkeys are inherently SC 3.3.8 compliant — no cognitive test required
    const passkeyButton = page.locator('[data-testid="passkey-login"], button:has-text("passkey"), button:has-text("Sign in with passkey")');
    // This test is informational — presence of passkey option is a best practice indicator
    const hasPasskey = await passkeyButton.count();
    console.info(`Passkey login option present: ${hasPasskey > 0}`);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test for all authentication forms (login, MFA, password reset). Do NOT block paste in password fields — this violates SC 3.3.8 and encourages weaker passwords. Do NOT apply the security exception too broadly — it only covers cases where re-entry is genuinely required for security (confirm-password, CVV); it does not exempt CAPTCHA without an accessible alternative. Alternative: WebAuthn passkeys are inherently SC 3.3.8 compliant and eliminate the CAPTCHA compliance question entirely. [official]

### Pattern 10 (Cycle 30) — Playwright `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage` for `aria-errormessage` Validation

Playwright v1.50 introduced `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()`, which checks the value exposed by `aria-errormessage` on a form control. `aria-errormessage` requires the referenced element to be visible (not `display:none`) and the input to have `aria-invalid="true"`. This is semantically distinct from `aria-describedby` (general description) — `aria-errormessage` is for validation errors only.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/error-message.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Playwright toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage — form validation', () => {
  test('email field exposes accessible error message after invalid submit', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');

    await page.getByLabel(/email/i).fill('not-an-email');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit|sign up/i }).click();

    const emailInput = page.getByLabel(/email/i);

    // Assert aria-invalid is set on the field
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');

    // Assert the accessible error message resolves to expected text
    // toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage follows aria-errormessage → referenced element text
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(/valid email|invalid email/i);
  });

  test('correcting the field clears aria-invalid and removes the error message', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');
    await page.getByLabel(/email/i).fill('bad');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit|sign up/i }).click();

    const emailInput = page.getByLabel(/email/i);
    await emailInput.fill('user@example.com');
    await emailInput.blur();

    await expect(emailInput).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
  });

  test('aria-errormessage referenced element is visible (not display:none)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');
    await page.getByLabel(/email/i).fill('invalid');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit|sign up/i }).click();

    const errorMsgId = await page.getByLabel(/email/i).getAttribute('aria-errormessage');
    if (errorMsgId) {
      const errorEl = page.locator(`#${errorMsgId}`);
      // ARIA spec requires aria-errormessage referent to be visible
      await expect(errorEl).toBeVisible();
      await expect(errorEl).not.toHaveCSS('display', 'none');
      await expect(errorEl).not.toHaveCSS('visibility', 'hidden');
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `aria-errormessage` + `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` for form field validation errors when you need the semantically precise error-to-input binding. Do NOT use `aria-errormessage` if the referenced element can ever be `display:none` — the spec requires the error message container to be visible for the association to be valid. Prefer `aria-describedby` if the text also serves as general instruction (not purely an error). Alternative: `role="alert"` on the error element announces immediately but does not create a programmatic field-to-error association; for best AT support, combine `aria-errormessage` (for association) with `aria-live="polite"` on the container (for announcement). [official]

### Pattern 11 (Cycle 30) — Roving `tabindex` for Toolbar Arrow-Key Navigation (ARIA APG)

The roving `tabindex` pattern is the ARIA APG-recommended keyboard interaction model for composite widgets: toolbar, radiogroup, menu, listbox, and grid. One item has `tabindex="0"` (the roving active item); all others have `tabindex="-1"`. Arrow keys move focus within the group; Tab moves focus out entirely. This prevents keyboard users from Tabbing through every item individually.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/roving-tabindex.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Roving tabindex — toolbar arrow-key navigation (ARIA APG)', () => {
  test('Tab enters toolbar; arrows navigate within; Tab exits', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/editor');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="toolbar"]');

    // Tab until focus enters the toolbar
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
      const inToolbar = await page.evaluate(() => {
        const toolbar = document.querySelector('[role="toolbar"]');
        return toolbar?.contains(document.activeElement) ?? false;
      });
      if (inToolbar) break;
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    }

    // Exactly one item should have tabindex="0" at any time
    const tabZeroCount = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const toolbar = document.querySelector('[role="toolbar"]');
      return toolbar?.querySelectorAll('[tabindex="0"]').length ?? 0;
    });
    expect(tabZeroCount).toBe(1);

    // ArrowRight moves focus to the next item
    const firstFocused = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.textContent?.trim());
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const secondFocused = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.textContent?.trim());
    expect(secondFocused).not.toBe(firstFocused);

    // Tab exits the toolbar entirely
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const isStillInToolbar = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const toolbar = document.querySelector('[role="toolbar"]');
      return toolbar?.contains(document.activeElement) ?? false;
    });
    expect(isStillInToolbar).toBe(false);
  });

  test('exactly one tabindex="0" item throughout arrow-key navigation', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/editor');
    const toolbar = page.locator('[role="toolbar"]');
    await toolbar.waitFor();

    for (const key of ['ArrowRight', 'ArrowRight', 'ArrowLeft', 'Home', 'End']) {
      const zeroCount = await toolbar.locator('[tabindex="0"]').count();
      expect(zeroCount).toBe(1);
      await page.keyboard.press(key);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use roving tabindex for widgets where all items are conceptually a single selection unit: radio groups, toolbars, menu items, tab lists, and grids. Do NOT use roving tabindex for navigation menus where each item is a separate link — navigation links should each be Tab-reachable independently. Do NOT implement roving tabindex manually if a native HTML element handles it (`<select>`, `<input type="radio">`). Alternative: `aria-activedescendant` is an alternative pattern that keeps DOM focus on the container — preferred for virtualised trees where moving DOM focus on each arrow key is expensive. [official]

---

### Pattern 12 (Cycle 30) — Playwright Forced Colors / Windows High Contrast Emulation

Windows High Contrast Mode (WHCM) and the `forced-colors: active` media query cause browsers to override colours. Elements using background-color alone for state (e.g., a selected tab indicated only by blue background) lose that distinction. Playwright can emulate this with `page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' })` — no Windows machine required.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/forced-colors.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('Forced colors (Windows High Contrast) emulation', () => {
  test('selected tab uses border/outline indicator (not background-only)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' });
    await page.goto('/');

    const selectedTab = page.locator('[role="tab"][aria-selected="true"]').first();
    if (await selectedTab.count() === 0) return;

    const hasBorderIndicator = await selectedTab.evaluate((el) => {
      const styles = getComputedStyle(el);
      return (
        styles.borderBottomWidth !== '0px' ||
        styles.outlineWidth !== '0px' ||
        styles.borderTopWidth !== '0px'
      );
    });

    expect(
      hasBorderIndicator,
      'Selected tab must use a border/outline (not only background) for forced-colors compatibility'
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  test('axe scan passes in forced-colors mode', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' });
    await page.goto('/');

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();

    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('keyboard focus indicator remains visible in forced-colors mode', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' });
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');

    const focusVisible = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;
      if (!el) return false;
      const styles = getComputedStyle(el);
      return styles.outlineWidth !== '0px' || styles.borderWidth !== '0px';
    });

    expect(focusVisible, 'Focus indicator must be visible in forced-colors mode').toBe(true);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use forced-colors emulation in CI to catch colour-only state indicators. Do NOT suppress the `forced-colors` media query with `forced-color-adjust: none !important` — this overrides the user's OS accessibility settings. Ensure all interactive states use a shape, border, or outline — not just colour. Alternative: supplement Playwright emulation with manual review on Windows with High Contrast White and Black themes; Playwright emulates the CSS but cannot replicate all OS-level rendering overrides. [official]

### Pattern 13 (Cycle 30) — Pa11y CI Dual-Engine: axe + HTMLCS Complementary Scanning

Pa11y can run both axe-core and HTML_CodeSniffer (HTMLCS) as rule engines. The two engines have different rule sets: axe has lower false-positive rates (good for PR gates); HTMLCS has additional form labelling and table header rules (good for nightly deep scans). Pa11y CI v4.1.1 supports per-URL threshold overrides.

```typescript
// pa11y.config.ts — Pa11y CI dual-engine configuration
import type { Pa11yOptions } from 'pa11y';

const sharedOptions: Partial<Pa11yOptions> = {
  standard: 'WCAG2AA',
  timeout: 30000,
  wait: 2000,
  chromeLaunchConfig: {
    args: ['--no-sandbox', '--disable-setuid-sandbox'],
  },
};

export default {
  defaults: {
    ...sharedOptions,
    runners: ['axe'],         // Primary engine: axe (zero false positives)
    threshold: 0,             // PR gate: zero tolerance
    ignore: [
      // Documented third-party widget violations
      'WCAG2AA.Principle4.Guideline4_1.4_1_2.H91.A.NoContent',
    ],
  },
  urls: [
    {
      url: 'http://localhost:3000/',
      ...sharedOptions,
      runners: ['axe'],       // Homepage: axe only (fast PR gate)
    },
    {
      url: 'http://localhost:3000/forms',
      ...sharedOptions,
      // Forms: both engines — HTMLCS catches additional labelling issues
      runners: ['axe', 'htmlcs'],
      threshold: 2,           // Allow 2 known HTMLCS false-positives for date inputs
    },
    {
      url: 'http://localhost:3000/data-table',
      ...sharedOptions,
      // Tables: HTMLCS has stronger header-association rules than axe
      runners: ['axe', 'htmlcs'],
      threshold: 0,
    },
  ],
};

// package.json scripts:
// "test:a11y:pa11y": "pa11y-ci --config pa11y.config.ts"
// "test:a11y:pa11y:sitemap": "pa11y-ci --sitemap http://localhost:3000/sitemap.xml"
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use Pa11y dual-engine when your team has a mature a11y program and wants deeper coverage than axe alone, especially for forms and data tables. Do NOT use dual-engine as your primary PR gate — HTMLCS has higher false-positive rates that create noise in fast-feedback pipelines. Run the HTMLCS-inclusive scan in a separate nightly CI job. Alternative: IBM Equal Access Checker (`@ibm/equal-access-accessibility-checker`) is a third engine with strong WCAG 2.x and IBM product standard coverage. [community]

### Pattern 14 (Cycle 30) — WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry Testing in Multi-Step Forms

WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7 (Redundant Entry, Level A, new in 2.2) requires that information previously entered in the same process is either auto-populated or available for selection. axe-core has no rule for this — it is entirely a manual/custom-scripted test.

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/redundant-entry.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.7 — Redundant Entry in multi-step form', () => {
  test('step 2 pre-populates shipping address from billing address when opted in', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout/step-1');

    await page.getByLabel(/first name/i).fill('Jane');
    await page.getByLabel(/last name/i).fill('Doe');
    await page.getByLabel(/address line 1/i).first().fill('123 Main St');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next|continue/i }).click();

    await page.goto('/checkout/step-2');
    const sameAsBillingCheckbox = page.getByLabel(/same as billing/i);
    if (await sameAsBillingCheckbox.count() > 0) {
      await sameAsBillingCheckbox.check();
      // Field must be pre-populated — user should not re-type billing info
      await expect(page.getByLabel(/first name/i).first()).toHaveValue('Jane');
    }
  });

  test('review step shows previously entered data without re-entry', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout/review');

    const reviewSection = page.getByRole('region', { name: /review|summary/i }).first();
    if (await reviewSection.count() > 0) {
      // All previously entered information must appear in the review step
      await expect(reviewSection).toContainText(/jane/i);
    }
  });

  test('confirm-password is exempt from 3.3.7 (security exception)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');

    // Confirm-password is a legitimate re-entry (security exception)
    // It must start empty — it should NOT be pre-populated from the first field
    const confirmPassword = page
      .locator('input[name*="confirm"], input[autocomplete="new-password"]').last();
    if (await confirmPassword.count() > 0) {
      await expect(confirmPassword).toHaveValue('');
    }
  });

  test('form does not ask for the same information twice in a single step', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');

    // Check that no two visible inputs have the same accessible name (duplicate field pattern)
    const labelTexts = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const inputs = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('input:not([type="hidden"]), textarea'));
      return inputs.map((el) => {
        const id = el.getAttribute('id');
        const label = id ? document.querySelector(`label[for="${id}"]`) : null;
        return label?.textContent?.trim().toLowerCase() ?? '';
      }).filter(Boolean);
    });

    const seen = new Set<string>();
    const duplicates = labelTexts.filter((l) => {
      if (seen.has(l)) return true;
      seen.add(l);
      return false;
    });

    expect(duplicates, `Duplicate form field labels detected: ${duplicates.join(', ')}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use redundant entry tests for multi-step checkout, application, or registration flows with 3+ steps. Do NOT pre-populate sensitive fields like CVV, OTP codes, or security questions — the security exception in SC 3.3.7 explicitly allows re-entry for security purposes. Do NOT expect axe-core to catch this — SC 3.3.7 requires custom scripted testing. Alternative: for short 2-step forms, back-navigation with state preservation (React state or sessionStorage) is often simpler than explicit pre-population. [official]

---

### Pattern 15 (Cycle 30) — Playwright `locator.ariaSnapshot()` for Programmatic ARIA Tree State Diffing

`locator.ariaSnapshot()` (Playwright v1.49+) returns the ARIA tree of a locator as a YAML string without performing an assertion. This enables programmatic diffing: capture ARIA tree before and after a user action to verify that state changes are correctly reflected in the accessibility tree (e.g., `pressed: false` → `pressed: true`, `selected: false` → `selected: true`).

```typescript
// tests/accessibility/aria-tree-diff.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA tree diffing with locator.ariaSnapshot()', () => {
  test('toggle button: aria-pressed state changes correctly after click', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/editor');

    const boldButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: /bold/i });
    await boldButton.waitFor();

    // Capture ARIA snapshot before activation
    const beforeSnapshot = await boldButton.ariaSnapshot();
    expect(beforeSnapshot).toContain('pressed: false');

    await boldButton.click();

    // Capture ARIA snapshot after activation — state must have changed
    const afterSnapshot = await boldButton.ariaSnapshot();
    expect(afterSnapshot).toContain('pressed: true');
    expect(beforeSnapshot).not.toBe(afterSnapshot);
  });

  test('wizard stepper: exactly one step has aria-current="step"', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/onboarding');

    const steps = page.locator('[role="listitem"][aria-label*="step" i], [role="tab"]');
    const stepSnapshots: string[] = [];

    for (let i = 0; i < await steps.count(); i++) {
      stepSnapshots.push(await steps.nth(i).ariaSnapshot());
    }

    const currentSteps = stepSnapshots.filter((s) =>
      s.includes('current: true') || s.includes('selected: true')
    );
    expect(currentSteps).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  test('listbox: aria-selected updates in snapshot after option click', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    const listbox = page.getByRole('listbox').first();
    if (await listbox.count() === 0) return;

    const firstOption = listbox.getByRole('option').first();
    const beforeSnap = await firstOption.ariaSnapshot();

    await firstOption.click();

    const afterSnap = await firstOption.ariaSnapshot();
    expect(afterSnap).toContain('selected: true');
    expect(beforeSnap).not.toContain('selected: true');
  });

  test('page-level aria snapshot attached to test report as baseline', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    const snapshot = await page.ariaSnapshot();

    // Attach for CI report review and baseline tracking
    await testInfo.attach('aria-snapshot-dashboard', {
      body: snapshot,
      contentType: 'text/plain',
    });

    // Structural assertions: key landmarks must be present
    expect(snapshot).toContain('main');
    expect(snapshot).toContain('navigation');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `ariaSnapshot()` for diff-based state verification where the before/after ARIA change is the central assertion — ideal for toggle controls, wizard steps, and selection widgets. Do NOT use `ariaSnapshot()` as a replacement for specific attribute assertions like `toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true')` when the exact value is what matters — specific assertions are more readable and less fragile. Use file-based snapshot storage only for stable structures where any ARIA change should trigger a review. Alternative: `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` with inline YAML is better for regression testing of static structure. [official]

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 30)

147. **[community] `role="presentation"` and `role="none"` are synonyms but if either role is applied to an element that contains focusable descendants, both roles are silently ignored by the browser's accessibility tree — the element retains its native semantics**: Teams apply `role="none"` to layout tables expecting them to be completely invisible to AT, but any focusable cell (a linked table cell) causes the table structure to be re-exposed. WHY: Developers misunderstand the "ignored if contains focusable descendants" rule and apply `role="none"` expecting to suppress table semantics entirely, then discover that a linked cell causes the entire table to be announced as a data table again — the fix is to remove the link from the cell, not remove the `role="none"`.

148. **[community] `aria-describedby` pointing to an element with `display:none` silently fails — the description is not read by any screen reader, but axe-core produces no violation because it validates attribute syntax, not whether the referent is currently visible**: Teams build contextual help text that toggles with `display:none` while keeping the `aria-describedby` reference on the input, believing the description is always connected. When the help text is hidden, AT users receive no description. WHY: axe checks that `aria-describedby` references a valid ID, not that the referenced element is rendered — teams confuse "axe passes" with "description is accessible", and the fix is to use off-screen positioning (`position: absolute; left: -10000px`) rather than `display:none` to hide descriptive elements that are referenced by ARIA attributes.

149. **[community] Playwright's `page.fill()` on a `<textarea>` inside a rich text editor (CodeMirror, ProseMirror, Tiptap) sets the DOM `value` but bypasses the editor's keyboard event handlers — the editor's internal state and ARIA live regions do not update, making accessibility assertions incorrect**: Rich text editors intercept `keydown`/`input` events and manage their own content model. `fill()` writes to the DOM directly, so the editor's live region (which announces content to screen readers) remains stale. WHY: Teams write `await page.fill('.ProseMirror', 'hello')` expecting screen reader announcements to update, then wonder why the ARIA live region still shows the previous content — in production, AT users experience the same issue if they use an input method the editor does not handle; the fix is `page.locator('.ProseMirror').pressSequentially('hello')` which fires individual key events.

150. **[community] A blanket `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { * { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; } }` override silently removes functional transitions including focus indicator fade-ins that are designed to draw attention to the focused element**: WCAG does not mandate zero animation — it mandates that non-essential motion does not cause seizures and that essential motion can be disabled. Removing all transitions in reduced-motion mode trades one accessibility concern (vestibular sensitivity) for another (focus indicator conspicuousness). WHY: The blanket override is the simplest implementation but the wrong abstraction — the correct approach applies `animation: none` selectively to purely decorative animations while preserving functional transitions, which requires per-animation intentionality; teams that copy-paste the blanket rule from accessibility articles do not realise it applies to focus ring animations as well.

151. **[community] `aria-live="polite"` regions dynamically inserted into the DOM via React portals or JavaScript after the initial page load are not reliably announced by VoiceOver on macOS Safari — only live regions present in the DOM at page load time are consistently tracked by Safari's AT**: NVDA + Firefox and JAWS + Chrome handle dynamic live region insertion more reliably. VoiceOver scans the DOM at load time for live regions; a region mounted later (first-notification lazy mount pattern) is never registered. WHY: Teams implement notification systems where the live region container is appended to `document.body` on first toast, which works correctly in automated NVDA tests but silently fails for VoiceOver/Safari users — the fix is to render the live region container in the initial HTML (empty, positioned off-screen) and only update its text content, never inserting the container after load.

152. **[community] axe-core's `color-contrast` rule returns `incomplete` (not a violation) for text on background images, CSS gradients, or semi-transparent overlays — and most test configurations discard `incomplete` results, creating a silent gap where image-background contrast is never checked**: axe computes contrast using CSSOM `background-color` against `color`. When text sits on a photograph, a gradient, or a pattern, axe cannot compute effective contrast and marks it `incomplete`. Typical CI assertions (`expect(results.violations).toEqual([])`) never examine `incomplete`. WHY: Teams see "0 violations" and assume text-on-image contrast has been validated, unaware that the `incomplete` category contains the gap — the fix is to explicitly check `results.incomplete.filter(r => r.id === 'color-contrast')` and log those as manual review items in the ACR/VPAT, acknowledging the automated tool's limitation.

### Pattern 16 (Cycle 31) — WCAG 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced) Full Playwright Test Suite

WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.12 (Focus Not Obscured Enhanced, Level AAA) strengthens 2.4.11 (AA) by requiring that no part of the focused element is hidden by author-created content such as sticky headers, cookie banners, or overlapping drawers. While 2.4.11 allows partial obscuring, 2.4.12 requires full visibility of the focused element's bounding box.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/wcag22-focus-not-obscured-enhanced.spec.ts
// WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.12 (AAA): Focused element must be fully visible — no part hidden by sticky UI.
// Uses Playwright IntersectionObserver geometry to detect sticky-header overlap.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

async function getFocusObscurationReport(page: import('@playwright/test').Page): Promise<
  Array<{ tag: string; label: string; overlapPx: number }>
> {
  return page.evaluate(() => {
    const focused = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;
    if (!focused) return [];
    const focusRect = focused.getBoundingClientRect();
    const stickyEls = Array.from(
      document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[style*="position: sticky"], [style*="position:sticky"], header, [class*="sticky"], [class*="fixed"]')
    ).filter((el) => {
      const s = getComputedStyle(el);
      return s.position === 'sticky' || s.position === 'fixed';
    });
    const overlaps: Array<{ tag: string; label: string; overlapPx: number }> = [];
    for (const el of stickyEls) {
      const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      const overlapY = Math.max(0, r.bottom - focusRect.top);
      if (overlapY > 0) {
        overlaps.push({
          tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
          label: el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? el.className.slice(0, 40),
          overlapPx: Math.round(overlapY),
        });
      }
    }
    return overlaps;
  });
}

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced, AAA)', () => {
  test('tabbing through nav does not leave any focused element hidden by sticky header', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    const violations: unknown[] = [];

    for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
      const report = await getFocusObscurationReport(page);
      if (report.length > 0) violations.push(report);
    }
    expect(violations, `Focus obscured by sticky element: ${JSON.stringify(violations)}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('scroll-padding-top CSS mitigates sticky header focus obscurement on anchor links', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/docs#section-3');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const anchorTarget = page.locator('#section-3');
    if (await anchorTarget.count() === 0) return;

    // After anchor navigation the target must not be hidden under the sticky header
    const obscured = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const target = document.querySelector('#section-3') as HTMLElement | null;
      if (!target) return false;
      const targetRect = target.getBoundingClientRect();
      const header = document.querySelector('header') as HTMLElement | null;
      if (!header) return false;
      const headerRect = header.getBoundingClientRect();
      return targetRect.top < headerRect.bottom;
    });
    expect(obscured, 'Section 3 anchor target is hidden under sticky header').toBe(false);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use 2.4.12 tests when your product has sticky headers, persistent cookie banners, or in-page drawers that overlay content. Do NOT enable this test as a blocking PR gate for AAA criteria — mark it as an advisory/informational check that logs warnings rather than fails CI. Named alternative: `scroll-padding-top` CSS (C43 technique) applied to `<html>` is the cheapest fix when a sticky header is the obscurer; Playwright geometry tests verify the fix works. [official]

### Pattern 17 (Cycle 31) — ARIA `role="spinbutton"` Full Keyboard Contract and jest-axe Test

The ARIA `role="spinbutton"` exposes a numeric input widget to assistive technology. Native `<input type="number">` maps to this role automatically, but custom spinbutton widgets (e.g., styled quantity selectors) require explicit ARIA attributes and keyboard handling: `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuetext` (when numeric form is not meaningful), and arrow-key increment/decrement.

```typescript
// File: src/components/QuantityInput/__tests__/QuantityInput.a11y.spec.tsx
// Tests ARIA spinbutton keyboard contract per ARIA APG Spinbutton Pattern.
import React from 'react';
import { render, screen, fireEvent } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { axe, toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

interface QuantityInputProps {
  label: string;
  min: number;
  max: number;
  defaultValue?: number;
  onChange?: (v: number) => void;
}

function QuantityInput({ label, min, max, defaultValue = min, onChange }: QuantityInputProps) {
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState(defaultValue);
  const id = React.useId();
  const handleKey = (e: React.KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') {
      const next = Math.min(max, value + 1);
      setValue(next);
      onChange?.(next);
    } else if (e.key === 'ArrowDown') {
      const next = Math.max(min, value - 1);
      setValue(next);
      onChange?.(next);
    } else if (e.key === 'Home') {
      setValue(min);
      onChange?.(min);
    } else if (e.key === 'End') {
      setValue(max);
      onChange?.(max);
    }
  };
  return (
    <div>
      <label htmlFor={id}>{label}</label>
      <div
        id={id}
        role="spinbutton"
        aria-valuenow={value}
        aria-valuemin={min}
        aria-valuemax={max}
        aria-label={label}
        tabIndex={0}
        onKeyDown={handleKey}
        style={{ display: 'inline-block', padding: '4px 8px', border: '1px solid #ccc' }}
      >
        {value}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

describe('QuantityInput — ARIA spinbutton accessibility', () => {
  it('has no axe violations in default state', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<QuantityInput label="Quantity" min={1} max={10} />);
    expect(await axe(container)).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('exposes aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax', () => {
    render(<QuantityInput label="Quantity" min={1} max={10} defaultValue={3} />);
    const spinner = screen.getByRole('spinbutton', { name: 'Quantity' });
    expect(spinner).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '3');
    expect(spinner).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemin', '1');
    expect(spinner).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemax', '10');
  });

  it('ArrowUp increments value and updates aria-valuenow', async () => {
    render(<QuantityInput label="Quantity" min={1} max={10} defaultValue={5} />);
    const spinner = screen.getByRole('spinbutton', { name: 'Quantity' });
    await userEvent.type(spinner, '{ArrowUp}');
    expect(spinner).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '6');
  });

  it('ArrowDown decrements and clamps at min', async () => {
    render(<QuantityInput label="Quantity" min={1} max={10} defaultValue={1} />);
    const spinner = screen.getByRole('spinbutton', { name: 'Quantity' });
    await userEvent.type(spinner, '{ArrowDown}');
    expect(spinner).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '1');
  });

  it('Home sets value to min; End sets value to max', async () => {
    render(<QuantityInput label="Quantity" min={1} max={10} defaultValue={5} />);
    const spinner = screen.getByRole('spinbutton', { name: 'Quantity' });
    fireEvent.keyDown(spinner, { key: 'Home' });
    expect(spinner).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '1');
    fireEvent.keyDown(spinner, { key: 'End' });
    expect(spinner).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '10');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use custom `role="spinbutton"` when design requirements cannot be satisfied by `<input type="number">` (e.g., custom increment buttons, stepped sliders). Do NOT use `role="spinbutton"` for non-numeric values — use `role="listbox"` or `role="combobox"` instead. Named alternative: `<input type="number" min max step>` provides browser-native spinbutton behaviour including screen reader announcements without custom ARIA wiring. [official]

### Pattern 18 (Cycle 31) — Playwright `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` for Form Validation Accessibility (v1.50+)

Playwright v1.50 added `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()`, which asserts the accessible error message of an element as announced by screen readers — derived from `aria-errormessage` (pointing to a visible error element) or `aria-describedby` error text. This is more precise than checking `aria-invalid` or querying error text in the DOM.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/form-error-announcement.spec.ts
// Tests that form validation errors are correctly wired for screen reader announcement.
// Uses Playwright v1.50+ toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage() assertion.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('Form validation — accessible error announcement (WCAG 3.3.1, 4.1.3)', () => {
  test('email field surfaces accessible error message on invalid submission', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Submit without filling email
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit|send/i }).click();

    const emailField = page.getByLabel(/email/i);
    // WCAG 3.3.1: error must be described in text
    await expect(emailField).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
    // Playwright v1.50: asserts the text announced as error by screen readers
    await expect(emailField).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(/required|enter.*email/i);
  });

  test('password field announces specific constraint violation', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');

    await page.getByLabel(/^password$/i).fill('abc');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign up|create account/i }).click();

    const passwordField = page.getByLabel(/^password$/i);
    await expect(passwordField).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
    await expect(passwordField).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(/8 characters|too short/i);
  });

  test('error state has no new axe violations after submission', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit|send/i }).click();
    await page.waitForTimeout(300); // Allow error render

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('success state announces confirmation without moving focus', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    await page.getByLabel(/name/i).fill('Jane Doe');
    await page.getByLabel(/email/i).fill('jane@example.com');
    await page.getByLabel(/message/i).fill('Hello');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit|send/i }).click();

    // Success message must be in a live region — focus must not have moved to it
    const successMsg = page.getByRole('status');
    await expect(successMsg).toBeVisible();
    // Focus stays on the form area, not jumped to the status message
    const focused = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.tagName?.toLowerCase());
    expect(focused).not.toBe('div'); // status role is usually a div — focus should not be there
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` as the primary assertion for any form field that can be in an error state — it tests what AT actually announces, not just DOM attribute presence. Do NOT rely on `toHaveAttribute('aria-describedby', 'some-id')` alone — that verifies HTML wiring, not the actual error message text. Named alternative: `toHaveAccessibleDescription()` is broader and also picks up hint text from non-error `aria-describedby` references; use `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` specifically when the element uses `aria-errormessage`. [official]

### Pattern 19 (Cycle 31) — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size: Spacing-Offset Algorithm with Playwright

WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (Target Size Minimum, AA) allows a target smaller than 24×24 CSS px if it has at least 24px of spacing (offset) from all adjacent interactive targets. The spacing offset rule means that an icon button of 16×16px surrounded by 8px of non-interactive whitespace on all sides meets the criterion. Testing requires geometry analysis — axe-core has no rule for this.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/wcag22-target-size-spacing.spec.ts
// WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8: targets < 24×24px are exempt if they have ≥24px total spacing
// from adjacent interactive elements (the "spacing offset" exception).
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface TargetInfo {
  tag: string;
  text: string;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  top: number;
  left: number;
  right: number;
  bottom: number;
}

test.describe('WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 — Target Size with spacing offset', () => {
  test('all interactive targets on homepage either meet 24×24px or have ≥24px spacing', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const targets: TargetInfo[] = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const sel = 'button, a[href], input:not([type="hidden"]), select, [role="button"], [role="link"]';
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(sel))
        .filter((el) => el.getBoundingClientRect().width > 0)
        .map((el) => {
          const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
          return {
            tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
            text: (el.textContent ?? '').trim().slice(0, 30),
            width: Math.round(r.width),
            height: Math.round(r.height),
            top: Math.round(r.top),
            left: Math.round(r.left),
            right: Math.round(r.right),
            bottom: Math.round(r.bottom),
          };
        });
    });

    const violations: TargetInfo[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < targets.length; i++) {
      const t = targets[i];
      if (t.width >= 24 && t.height >= 24) continue; // Passes by size

      // Check spacing offset from every other target
      let minSpacing = Infinity;
      for (let j = 0; j < targets.length; j++) {
        if (i === j) continue;
        const o = targets[j];
        // Closest distance between bounding boxes
        const hGap = Math.max(0, Math.max(t.left - o.right, o.left - t.right));
        const vGap = Math.max(0, Math.max(t.top - o.bottom, o.top - t.bottom));
        const dist = Math.sqrt(hGap ** 2 + vGap ** 2);
        if (dist < minSpacing) minSpacing = dist;
      }
      // Spacing offset: diameter of a 24px circle (12px radius) around centre
      const needsSpacing = 24 - Math.min(t.width, t.height);
      if (minSpacing < needsSpacing / 2) violations.push(t);
    }

    if (violations.length > 0) console.table(violations);
    expect(violations, 'Targets below 24×24 without sufficient spacing').toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use the spacing-offset test for icon-dense toolbars and mobile navigation menus where increasing target size to 24×24px would break visual design. Do NOT skip the size gate entirely and rely solely on spacing offset — it is an exception pathway, not the default. Named alternative: CSS `min-width: 24px; min-height: 24px` on all interactive elements is simpler than maintaining spacing-offset logic; use the offset algorithm only when the design team explicitly needs smaller targets. [official]

### Pattern 20 (Cycle 31) — ARIA `role="tree"` / `role="treeitem"` Full Keyboard Contract

Tree views expose hierarchical navigation to screen reader users. The ARIA APG Tree Pattern mandates: single Tab stop for the tree, arrow key navigation within the tree, expand/collapse with Enter or ArrowRight/ArrowLeft, and `aria-expanded` state on parent nodes.

```typescript
// File: src/components/TreeView/__tests__/TreeView.a11y.spec.tsx
// ARIA APG Tree View keyboard contract: roving tabindex + arrow navigation + expand/collapse.
import React from 'react';
import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { axe, toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

interface TreeNode { id: string; label: string; children?: TreeNode[] }

function TreeView({ nodes }: { nodes: TreeNode[] }) {
  const [expanded, setExpanded] = React.useState<Set<string>>(new Set());
  const [focused, setFocused] = React.useState<string>(nodes[0]?.id ?? '');

  function toggle(id: string) {
    setExpanded((prev) => { const next = new Set(prev); next.has(id) ? next.delete(id) : next.add(id); return next; });
  }

  function renderNode(node: TreeNode, depth = 0) {
    const hasChildren = !!node.children?.length;
    const isExpanded = expanded.has(node.id);
    return (
      <li key={node.id} role="none">
        <span
          role="treeitem"
          tabIndex={focused === node.id ? 0 : -1}
          aria-expanded={hasChildren ? isExpanded : undefined}
          aria-level={depth + 1}
          onFocus={() => setFocused(node.id)}
          onClick={() => hasChildren && toggle(node.id)}
          onKeyDown={(e) => {
            if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') { if (hasChildren) toggle(node.id); }
            if (e.key === 'ArrowRight' && hasChildren && !isExpanded) toggle(node.id);
            if (e.key === 'ArrowLeft' && hasChildren && isExpanded) toggle(node.id);
          }}
        >
          {node.label}
        </span>
        {hasChildren && isExpanded && (
          <ul role="group">
            {node.children!.map((c) => renderNode(c, depth + 1))}
          </ul>
        )}
      </li>
    );
  }
  return <ul role="tree" aria-label="File explorer">{nodes.map((n) => renderNode(n))}</ul>;
}

const NODES: TreeNode[] = [
  { id: 'src', label: 'src', children: [{ id: 'comp', label: 'components' }, { id: 'utils', label: 'utils' }] },
  { id: 'tests', label: 'tests' },
];

describe('TreeView accessibility', () => {
  it('has no axe violations when collapsed', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<TreeView nodes={NODES} />);
    expect(await axe(container)).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('top-level tree has role="tree"', () => {
    render(<TreeView nodes={NODES} />);
    expect(screen.getByRole('tree', { name: 'File explorer' })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('parent nodes have aria-expanded="false" when collapsed', () => {
    render(<TreeView nodes={NODES} />);
    const srcNode = screen.getByRole('treeitem', { name: 'src' });
    expect(srcNode).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  });

  it('ArrowRight expands a collapsed parent node', async () => {
    render(<TreeView nodes={NODES} />);
    const srcNode = screen.getByRole('treeitem', { name: 'src' });
    srcNode.focus();
    await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowRight}');
    expect(srcNode).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
  });

  it('expanded tree has no axe violations', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<TreeView nodes={NODES} />);
    const srcNode = screen.getByRole('treeitem', { name: 'src' });
    await userEvent.click(srcNode);
    expect(await axe(container)).toHaveNoViolations();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `role="tree"` for file explorers, category hierarchies, and deeply nested navigation where sighted users see expand/collapse affordances. Do NOT use `role="tree"` for flat or 2-level navigation — `role="list"` with `role="listitem"` is simpler and more widely understood by AT. Named alternative: `<details>/<summary>` for a single level of disclosure avoids custom keyboard handling entirely; axe-core 4.10.0+ includes `summary-name` rule for these. [official]

### Pattern 21 (Cycle 31) — Playwright Forced Colors (High Contrast) Emulation Testing

Windows High Contrast Mode (WHCM) and the CSS `forced-colors: active` media query override author styles. Elements that rely on background colors, custom focus rings drawn with `box-shadow` only, or SVG fills without `currentColor` may become invisible in WHCM. Playwright can emulate forced colors without a physical Windows device.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/forced-colors.spec.ts
// Tests UI correctness under Windows Forced Colors / High Contrast emulation.
// Playwright uses Chromium's forced-colors emulation (--force-color-profile).
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.use({ colorScheme: 'no-preference' });

test.describe('Forced Colors (High Contrast) emulation', () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
    // Emulate forced-colors: active via Playwright CDP
    await page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' });
  });

  test('homepage has no axe violations under forced colors', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();
    // Under forced colors, color-contrast rules are less meaningful — focus on structure
    const structuralViolations = results.violations.filter(
      (v) => v.id !== 'color-contrast'
    );
    expect(structuralViolations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('focus indicators remain visible under forced colors (box-shadow only ring fails)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');

    const focusInfo = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;
      if (!el) return null;
      const s = getComputedStyle(el);
      return {
        outlineStyle: s.outlineStyle,
        outlineWidth: s.outlineWidth,
        boxShadow: s.boxShadow,
        tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
      };
    });

    // Under forced-colors, box-shadow is suppressed by the browser — only outline survives
    // A focus ring implemented purely with box-shadow will be invisible in WHCM
    expect(focusInfo?.outlineStyle).not.toBe('none');
    expect(parseFloat(focusInfo?.outlineWidth ?? '0')).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('icon buttons render text label or have visible outline under forced colors', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Capture screenshot under forced colors for manual review
    await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('homepage-forced-colors.png', {
      threshold: 0.1,
    });
  });

  test('SVG icons use currentColor fill to remain visible in forced-colors mode', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const svgFillViolations = await page.evaluate(() => {
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('svg path, svg circle, svg rect'))
        .filter((el) => {
          const fill = el.getAttribute('fill');
          // Hardcoded fills (hex/rgb) are overridden in forced-colors; currentColor or 'none' is safe
          return fill && fill !== 'currentColor' && fill !== 'none' && !fill.startsWith('url(');
        })
        .map((el) => ({ tag: el.tagName, fill: el.getAttribute('fill') }))
        .slice(0, 10);
    });
    if (svgFillViolations.length > 0) console.warn('SVG hardcoded fills:', svgFillViolations);
    expect(svgFillViolations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use forced-colors emulation for any product used on Windows (which includes virtually all enterprise desktop applications). Do NOT rely exclusively on screenshot diffing under forced-colors — combine with structural axe assertions and outline visibility checks. Named alternative: `@media (forced-colors: active) { * { forced-color-adjust: none; } }` CSS allows opting out of forced-colors for specific elements, but this disables WHCM for those elements entirely — use only for elements where WCAG 1.4.1/1.4.3 cannot be satisfied through forced-color-safe CSS. [official]
