### Pattern 22 (Cycle 31) — `@axe-core/react` DevTools Overlay Integration Test

`@axe-core/react` injects axe into React development builds and outputs violations to the browser console in real time. In a CI pipeline, you can run it headlessly via Playwright to capture console output and fail the build on violations. This bridges the gap between component-level jest-axe tests and full E2E axe scans.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/axe-react-devtools.spec.ts
// Captures @axe-core/react console output from a development build.
// @axe-core/react must be configured in the app's development entry point.
// Requires: npm install @axe-core/react --save-dev
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface AxeReactViolation {
  description: string;
  nodes: number;
  impact: string;
}

test.describe('@axe-core/react development overlay', () => {
  test('no critical or serious violations reported by @axe-core/react on app load', async ({ page }) => {
    const violations: AxeReactViolation[] = [];

    // Listen for console messages from @axe-core/react
    // @axe-core/react outputs structured console.error messages with [axe] prefix
    page.on('console', (msg) => {
      if (msg.type() === 'error' && msg.text().includes('[axe]')) {
        // Parse the violation count from @axe-core/react output
        violations.push({
          description: msg.text().slice(0, 120),
          nodes: 1,
          impact: msg.text().includes('critical') ? 'critical' : 'serious',
        });
      }
    });

    // Navigate to the development build (BASE_URL should point to dev server)
    await page.goto(process.env['BASE_URL'] ?? 'http://localhost:3000');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Give @axe-core/react time to run its debounced scan (default: 1000ms after React renders)
    await page.waitForTimeout(2000);

    const criticalOrSerious = violations.filter(
      (v) => v.impact === 'critical' || v.impact === 'serious'
    );

    if (criticalOrSerious.length > 0) {
      console.error('@axe-core/react violations:', criticalOrSerious);
    }
    expect(criticalOrSerious, `@axe-core/react found critical/serious violations`).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('product detail page has no @axe-core/react violations after dynamic content loads', async ({ page }) => {
    const axeErrors: string[] = [];
    page.on('console', (msg) => {
      if (msg.type() === 'error' && msg.text().includes('[axe]')) axeErrors.push(msg.text());
    });

    await page.goto('/product/123');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    await page.waitForTimeout(2000);

    expect(axeErrors, `@axe-core/react violations on product page`).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `@axe-core/react` when your team wants continuous accessibility feedback during development without adding tests — it catches violations at component render time in the browser. Do NOT use it in production builds — it adds significant bundle size and compute overhead. Named alternative: `@axe-core/playwright` in CI provides the same violation detection on production builds without requiring a development build; prefer it for CI gates. [official]

---

### Pattern 23 (Cycle 31) — WCAG 3.3.9 Accessible Authentication (Enhanced) — Passkey / WebAuthn Testing Pattern

WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.9 (Accessible Authentication Enhanced, Level AAA) removes all cognitive function tests from authentication — including the "object recognition" alternative allowed in SC 3.3.8. Passkeys (WebAuthn) satisfy both 3.3.8 and 3.3.9 because they require no cognitive function test and support `autocomplete="webauthn"`.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/wcag22-accessible-auth-enhanced.spec.ts
// WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.9 (AAA): No cognitive function test allowed, including image recognition.
// Tests that the login page provides a non-cognitive pathway (passkey / magic link / SSO).
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.9 — Accessible Authentication (Enhanced, AAA)', () => {
  test('login page has no axe violations with wcag22aa tags', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('password input has autocomplete="current-password" (WCAG 3.3.8 SC requirement)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    const passwordInput = page.locator('input[type="password"]').first();
    await expect(passwordInput).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', 'current-password');
  });

  test('passkey / WebAuthn button is present and keyboard accessible', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    // SC 3.3.9: at least one non-cognitive auth method must be available
    const passkeyButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: /passkey|sign in with passkey|use biometric|webauthn/i });
    const ssoButton = page.getByRole('link', { name: /sign in with google|sso|single sign.on/i });
    const magicLinkButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: /magic link|email link|passwordless/i });

    const atLeastOnePresent = (
      await passkeyButton.count() > 0 ||
      await ssoButton.count() > 0 ||
      await magicLinkButton.count() > 0
    );
    expect(atLeastOnePresent, 'SC 3.3.9: no non-cognitive auth method found on login page').toBe(true);
  });

  test('CAPTCHA on signup page has audio/text alternative (SC 3.3.8)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');
    const captchaFrame = page.frameLocator('[title*="recaptcha" i], [title*="captcha" i]');
    const captchaCount = await page.locator('iframe[title*="captcha" i]').count();

    if (captchaCount > 0) {
      // If CAPTCHA exists, audio alternative must be present (SC 3.3.8 exception pathway)
      const audioButton = captchaFrame.getByRole('button', { name: /audio|listen/i });
      await expect(audioButton).toBeVisible();
    }
    // Passing: no CAPTCHA on the page (preferred — fully satisfies 3.3.9)
  });

  test('new-password input has autocomplete="new-password" on signup', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/signup');
    const newPasswordInputs = page.locator('input[type="password"]');
    const count = await newPasswordInputs.count();
    expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    await expect(newPasswordInputs.first()).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', 'new-password');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use SC 3.3.9 tests when your product targets EU EAA compliance at AAA level or government procurement requiring AAA authentication criteria. Do NOT block CI on AAA criteria as PR gates — AAA compliance is aspirational, not legally required under current EAA/EN 301 549 mandates. Named alternative: for products targeting only WCAG 2.2 AA compliance, SC 3.3.8 (Minimum, AA) is sufficient — test only for paste support and autocomplete attributes. [official]

---

### Pattern 24 (Cycle 31) — `jest-axe` `impactLevels` Progressive CI Gate

jest-axe supports an `impactLevels` option to filter violations by severity before asserting. This enables a progressive rollout: gate CI on `critical` only at first, then expand to `serious`, then `moderate` over sprints — avoiding the "100 new violations broke the build" problem when first adding accessibility tests to a brownfield codebase.

```typescript
// File: src/setupTests.ts (or jest.config.ts axe configuration)
// Progressive a11y gate: start with critical-only, expand over sprints.
// This pattern avoids breaking CI when jest-axe is first added to a brownfield project.
import { configureAxe } from 'jest-axe';

// Sprint 1: gate on critical violations only (the ones that block AT users entirely)
export const axeCriticalOnly = configureAxe({
  rules: [{ id: 'color-contrast', enabled: false }], // JSDOM cannot compute contrast
  runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'] },
});

// Sprint 3+: add serious violations to the gate
export const axeCriticalAndSerious = configureAxe({
  rules: [{ id: 'color-contrast', enabled: false }],
  runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'] },
});

// Sprint 6+: full gate including moderate and best-practice
export const axeFull = configureAxe({
  rules: [{ id: 'color-contrast', enabled: false }],
  runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa', 'best-practice'] },
});

// In a test file — progressive gate example:
// import { axeCriticalOnly, toHaveNoViolationsAtLevel } from '../setupTests';
// expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);
//
// it('has no critical violations', async () => {
//   const { container } = render(<MyComponent />);
//   const results = await axeCriticalOnly(container);
//   // Filter to only the impact levels we are gating on this sprint
//   const gatedResults = {
//     ...results,
//     violations: results.violations.filter((v) => v.impact === 'critical'),
//   };
//   expect(gatedResults).toHaveNoViolations();
// });
```

```typescript
// File: src/components/Dashboard/__tests__/Dashboard.a11y.progressive.test.tsx
// Example of the progressive gate in a real test.
import React from 'react';
import { render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';
import { axeCriticalOnly, axeCriticalAndSerious } from '../../../setupTests';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

const SPRINT = parseInt(process.env['A11Y_SPRINT'] ?? '1', 10);

function gateResultsByImpact(results: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof axeCriticalOnly>>) {
  const impactsToGate = SPRINT >= 3
    ? ['critical', 'serious']
    : ['critical'];
  return { ...results, violations: results.violations.filter((v) => impactsToGate.includes(v.impact ?? '')) };
}

describe('Dashboard progressive a11y gate', () => {
  it(`gates on ${SPRINT >= 3 ? 'critical + serious' : 'critical'} violations (sprint ${SPRINT})`, async () => {
    const { container } = render(<div role="main" aria-label="Dashboard"><h1>Dashboard</h1></div>);
    const axe = SPRINT >= 3 ? axeCriticalAndSerious : axeCriticalOnly;
    const results = await axe(container);
    expect(gateResultsByImpact(results)).toHaveNoViolations();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `impactLevels` progressive gating when introducing accessibility testing to a brownfield project with many existing violations — a clean migration path prevents team resistance. Do NOT use progressive gating as a permanent state — establish a timeline (e.g., gate on all violations within 3 sprints) and stick to it; open-ended progressive gates become technical debt. Named alternative: axe violation baseline snapshot (suppress known violations by fingerprint) provides a different progressive strategy — new violations fail CI while existing ones are tracked separately. [community]

---

### Pattern 25 (Cycle 31) — ARIA `role="grid"` Data Table with Sortable Columns: Full a11y Test

The ARIA Grid pattern extends a data table with interactive cells supporting keyboard navigation (arrow keys within the grid) and `aria-sort` on column headers. `aria-sort` must change state on click and have its current value exposed correctly in the accessibility tree.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/data-grid-aria.spec.ts
// Tests ARIA grid pattern: role="grid", aria-sort lifecycle, cell keyboard navigation.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('ARIA grid — sortable data table accessibility', () => {
  test('data table has role="grid" and no axe violations', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/users');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const grid = page.getByRole('grid', { name: /users/i });
    await expect(grid).toBeVisible();

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include(grid)
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('column header has aria-sort="none" initially, updates to ascending on click', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/users');

    const nameHeader = page.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /name/i });
    await expect(nameHeader).toBeVisible();

    // Initial state: no sort applied
    const initialSort = await nameHeader.getAttribute('aria-sort');
    expect(['none', null]).toContain(initialSort);

    // Click to sort ascending
    await nameHeader.click();
    await expect(nameHeader).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'ascending');

    // Click again to sort descending
    await nameHeader.click();
    await expect(nameHeader).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'descending');
  });

  test('gridcell is reachable by arrow keys from focused column header', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/users');
    const firstCell = page.getByRole('gridcell').first();
    await firstCell.focus();

    // ArrowRight should move focus to the next cell in the same row
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const focusedTag = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role'));
    expect(focusedTag).toBe('gridcell');
  });

  test('aria snapshot reflects columnheader roles and aria-sort state', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/users');
    const grid = page.getByRole('grid', { name: /users/i });
    await expect(grid).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - grid "Users":
        - row:
          - columnheader /Name/
          - columnheader /Email/
          - columnheader /Role/
    `);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `role="grid"` for data tables where cells are interactive (clickable rows, editable cells, sortable columns). Do NOT apply `role="grid"` to presentational tables or simple read-only data tables — `role="table"` with `role="columnheader"` and `scope` attributes is correct and simpler. Named alternative: native `<table>` with `<th scope="col">` and JavaScript sort logic uses fewer ARIA attributes and has better AT support outside Chrome. [official]

---

### Pattern 26 (Cycle 31) — Playwright `page.locator().describe()` + Aria Snapshot Composition for Component Regression

Playwright v1.53 added `locator.describe()` which appends a human-readable description to any locator for improved test report readability. Combined with `toMatchAriaSnapshot()`, this creates self-documenting accessibility regression tests that surface component name in failure messages.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/component-aria-regression.spec.ts
// Uses Playwright v1.53 locator.describe() to add component names to aria snapshot assertions.
// Aria snapshot regressions now show component name in failure output.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Component ARIA snapshot regression suite', () => {
  test('navigation landmark matches expected ARIA snapshot', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const nav = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /main navigation/i })
      .describe('Main Navigation component');

    await expect(nav).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - navigation "Main Navigation":
        - list:
          - listitem:
            - link "Home"
          - listitem:
            - link "Products"
          - listitem:
            - link "About"
          - listitem:
            - link "Contact"
    `);
  });

  test('modal dialog matches expected ARIA snapshot when open', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /filter/i }).click();

    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog')
      .describe('Filter Modal dialog');

    await expect(dialog).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - dialog "Filter Products":
        - heading "Filter Products" [level=2]
        - group "Category":
          - checkbox "Electronics"
          - checkbox "Clothing"
        - button "Apply Filters"
        - button "Cancel"
    `);
  });

  test('breadcrumb navigation has correct aria structure', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products/electronics/laptops');

    const breadcrumb = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /breadcrumb/i })
      .describe('Breadcrumb navigation');

    await expect(breadcrumb).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - navigation "Breadcrumb":
        - list:
          - listitem:
            - link "Home"
          - listitem:
            - link "Products"
          - listitem:
            - link "Electronics"
          - listitem: "Laptops"
    `);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `locator.describe()` on all locators in snapshot tests and complex assertion chains — the description appears in failure output and makes triage faster in CI. Do NOT add `.describe()` to every single locator in simple tests — reserve it for complex chains where the component name would otherwise be lost in the failure message. Named alternative: naming test blocks precisely (`test('MainNav: ...')`) achieves similar readability without the API call overhead. [official]

---

### Pattern 27 (Cycle 31) — WCAG 3.2.6 Consistent Help — Cross-Page DOM Order Validation

WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6 (Consistent Help, Level A, new in 2.2) requires that help mechanisms (contact links, chat widgets, help phone numbers, self-service portals) appear in the same relative DOM order across pages where they appear. axe-core has no rule for this — it requires a custom Playwright multi-page test.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/wcag22-consistent-help.spec.ts
// WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6: help mechanisms must appear in consistent DOM order across pages.
// axe-core does not detect this — requires custom multi-page DOM order comparison.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const PAGES_TO_CHECK = ['/', '/products', '/about', '/contact'];

interface HelpElementInfo {
  tag: string;
  text: string;
  href: string | null;
  domIndex: number;
}

async function getHelpElements(page: import('@playwright/test').Page): Promise<HelpElementInfo[]> {
  return page.evaluate(() => {
    const helpSelectors = [
      'a[href*="support"], a[href*="help"], a[href*="contact"]',
      '[aria-label*="help" i], [aria-label*="support" i], [aria-label*="chat" i]',
      '[data-testid*="help"], [data-testid*="support"]',
    ].join(', ');

    const allEls = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('*'));
    return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(helpSelectors))
      .map((el) => ({
        tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
        text: (el.textContent ?? '').trim().slice(0, 40),
        href: el.getAttribute('href'),
        domIndex: allEls.indexOf(el),
      }));
  });
}

test.describe('WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6 — Consistent Help DOM order across pages', () => {
  test('help mechanisms appear in consistent relative DOM position across pages', async ({ page }) => {
    const helpOrderByPage: Record<string, HelpElementInfo[]> = {};

    for (const url of PAGES_TO_CHECK) {
      await page.goto(url);
      await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
      helpOrderByPage[url] = await getHelpElements(page);
    }

    // All pages that have help elements should have them in a consistent relative order
    const baselineTexts = helpOrderByPage[PAGES_TO_CHECK[0]]?.map((h) => h.text) ?? [];

    for (const [url, elements] of Object.entries(helpOrderByPage)) {
      if (elements.length === 0) continue;
      const texts = elements.map((h) => h.text);

      // The relative order of help texts must match the baseline page
      const intersection = texts.filter((t) => baselineTexts.includes(t));
      const baselineIntersection = baselineTexts.filter((t) => texts.includes(t));

      expect(
        intersection,
        `Help elements on ${url} are in different order than baseline (${PAGES_TO_CHECK[0]})`
      ).toEqual(baselineIntersection);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use the consistent help test for multi-page applications with global help widgets (sticky chat, footer support links). Do NOT test single-page applications where the entire page is a React component — the "DOM order" is effectively constant. Named alternative: visual regression testing (page screenshots + diff) can detect help element repositioning, but is less reliable for DOM-order-only changes that look identical. [official]

---

### Pattern 28 (Cycle 31) — `@axe-core/vitest` Component Unit Testing (Vitest-Native)

`@axe-core/vitest` (part of the axe-core-npm monorepo) provides axe integration for Vitest, the Jest-compatible test runner used with Vite-based React/Vue/Svelte projects. It avoids the `jest-axe` + Vitest compatibility caveats (especially around `configureAxe` and `toHaveNoViolations` global setup).

```typescript
// File: src/components/Card/__tests__/Card.a11y.spec.tsx
// @axe-core/vitest: native Vitest axe integration. No jest-axe compatibility shim needed.
// Requires: npm install @axe-core/vitest --save-dev
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { toHaveNoViolations, axe } from '@axe-core/vitest';
import React from 'react';

// Extend Vitest expect with toHaveNoViolations
expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

interface CardProps {
  title: string;
  description: string;
  href?: string;
  imageUrl?: string;
  imageAlt?: string;
}

function Card({ title, description, href, imageUrl, imageAlt }: CardProps) {
  return (
    <article aria-label={title}>
      {imageUrl && <img src={imageUrl} alt={imageAlt ?? ''} loading="lazy" />}
      <h3>{title}</h3>
      <p>{description}</p>
      {href && <a href={href} aria-label={`Read more about ${title}`}>Read more</a>}
    </article>
  );
}

describe('Card component — @axe-core/vitest', () => {
  it('card with all props has no axe violations', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <Card
        title="Accessible Card"
        description="A card with proper semantics"
        href="/details"
        imageUrl="/card.jpg"
        imageAlt="Descriptive image of card content"
      />
    );
    const results = await axe(container, {
      rules: [{ id: 'color-contrast', enabled: false }], // JSDOM limitation
    });
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('card without image has no axe violations (no missing alt)', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <Card title="Text-only Card" description="No image here" />
    );
    expect(await axe(container)).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('decorative image with empty alt has no axe violations', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <Card title="Card" description="Desc" imageUrl="/bg.jpg" imageAlt="" />
    );
    expect(await axe(container)).toHaveNoViolations();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `@axe-core/vitest` in Vite/Vitest projects instead of `jest-axe` — it avoids the Jest-v30/jest-axe-v10 incompatibility and is maintained in the same monorepo as axe-core, ensuring version alignment. Do NOT use `@axe-core/vitest` in Jest projects — the package is Vitest-specific; use `jest-axe` for Jest. Named alternative: `jest-axe` with `configureAxe` is the equivalent for Jest-based projects and has a larger community base of examples. [official]

---

### Pattern 29 (Cycle 31) — Playwright `prefers-reduced-motion` Emulation and Animation Accessibility Testing

WCAG 2.3.3 (AAA) and the operational principle 2.3.1 (A) address motion and animation. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is a CSS media query that users set at the OS level. Playwright can emulate it, enabling tests that verify motion is properly suppressed and that no essential information is conveyed only through animation.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/reduced-motion.spec.ts
// Tests that prefers-reduced-motion is respected and no essential motion is lost.
// Playwright emulates the media query via page.emulateMedia().
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('prefers-reduced-motion accessibility', () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
  });

  test('homepage has no axe violations under reduced-motion', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('hero carousel does not auto-play under reduced-motion', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const carousel = page.getByRole('region', { name: /carousel|hero/i });
    if (await carousel.count() === 0) return;

    // Record which slide is active before waiting
    const initialSlide = await carousel.getByRole('group', { name: /slide/i }).first().getAttribute('aria-hidden');
    await page.waitForTimeout(3000); // Long enough for auto-advance normally

    const slideAfterWait = await carousel.getByRole('group', { name: /slide/i }).first().getAttribute('aria-hidden');
    // Under reduced-motion the carousel must not auto-advance
    expect(initialSlide).toBe(slideAfterWait);
  });

  test('loading spinner transitions are suppressed under reduced-motion', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const spinnerAnimation = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const spinner = document.querySelector('[role="status"] svg, .spinner, [class*="spin"]') as HTMLElement | null;
      if (!spinner) return null;
      return getComputedStyle(spinner).animationDuration;
    });

    // Under reduced-motion, animation-duration should be 0s or 0.001s (near-zero)
    if (spinnerAnimation !== null) {
      const durationMs = parseFloat(spinnerAnimation) * 1000;
      expect(durationMs).toBeLessThan(100);
    }
  });

  test('page screenshot under reduced-motion matches baseline', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('homepage-reduced-motion.png', { threshold: 0.05 });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `prefers-reduced-motion` tests for any application with carousels, parallax scrolling, page transition animations, or loading spinners. Do NOT assert that all animations are completely absent — WCAG allows animations that communicate essential information (e.g., a progress bar that fills); only decorative or auto-playing animations must be suppressed. Named alternative: CSS `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` handled at the design system level (e.g., a global `transition: none` override) is simpler than per-component checks; test the CSS variable is respected globally rather than per element. [official]

---

### Pattern 30 (Cycle 31) — axe-core `resultTypes` Performance Optimization for Large SPAs

On large single-page applications with complex DOM structures, `axe.run()` can take 5–10 seconds per page. The `resultTypes` option limits which result categories are returned, dramatically reducing scan time — especially useful when only `violations` are needed for CI gates.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/axe-performance-optimized.spec.ts
// Uses axe resultTypes optimization to reduce scan time on large SPAs.
// Only requests 'violations' — skips 'passes', 'incomplete', and 'inapplicable' computation.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

// Shared helper: fast axe scan returning only violations
async function fastAxeScan(
  page: import('@playwright/test').Page,
  selector?: string
) {
  const builder = new AxeBuilder({ page }).withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa']);
  if (selector) builder.include(selector);
  // resultTypes: only compute violations — skip passes/incomplete for speed
  return builder.options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] }).analyze();
}

test.describe('Axe resultTypes performance optimization', () => {
  test('dashboard scan completes in < 3 seconds with resultTypes optimization', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const start = Date.now();
    const results = await fastAxeScan(page);
    const elapsed = Date.now() - start;

    console.log(`axe scan elapsed: ${elapsed}ms`);
    expect(elapsed, 'axe scan should complete in < 3s with resultTypes optimization').toBeLessThan(3000);
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('product listing page (500+ DOM nodes) scans quickly with resultTypes', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products?page=1&limit=50');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const start = Date.now();
    const results = await fastAxeScan(page);
    const elapsed = Date.now() - start;

    expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(4000);
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('scoped axe scan on main content is faster than full-page scan', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/reports');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const [scopedResults] = await Promise.all([
      fastAxeScan(page, 'main'), // Scoped to <main> — faster on pages with complex nav
    ]);

    expect(scopedResults.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `resultTypes: ['violations']` for CI PR gates where only violations matter and scan speed is important. Do NOT use this optimization when you need `incomplete` results — incomplete results reveal areas where axe could not determine compliance (e.g., contrast on background images) and are important for compliance reporting and ACR/VPAT documentation. Named alternative: scoping axe to `main` or a specific container achieves similar performance gains without sacrificing result completeness, and is preferable when `incomplete` results are used. [official]

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 31)

153. **[community] `aria-label` on a `<section>` element correctly creates a `region` landmark, but if the same label text is reused across multiple sections on the same page, screen reader users encounter a list of identically named "region" landmarks — making landmark navigation useless**: VoiceOver, NVDA, and JAWS all expose an "Accessible Landmarks" rotor or shortcut list. When every section is `aria-label="Section"` or uses a generic label like "Content", landmark navigation becomes equivalent to having no landmarks. WHY: Developers copy-paste `aria-label` from one section to the next without varying the value, unaware that landmark navigation is one of the primary speed-navigation techniques for screen reader users — the fix is to give each landmark a unique, descriptive label that describes its purpose (e.g., "Latest articles", "Promotional offers", "Newsletter signup").

154. **[community] `tabIndex={1}` (positive tabindex) on any element breaks the natural tab order for all users on the page — the element will receive focus before all tabIndex=0 and natural-order elements regardless of its DOM position, causing keyboard users to jump unexpectedly**: Positive tabindex values create a separate focus sequence that is serviced before the document's natural order. Even a single `tabIndex={1}` on a modal close button causes Tab to jump to the close button before any of the page's natural-order content on first Tab keypress. WHY: Developers use positive tabindex believing they are "making something more reachable", unaware that it disrupts the entire page's focus order — every keyboard user is affected, not just screen reader users; the ARIA APG and WCAG explicitly prohibit positive tabindex values outside of widgets that manage focus internally via roving tabindex.

155. **[community] `aria-hidden="true"` on a parent container does not prevent its focusable descendants from receiving keyboard focus — screen reader users can Tab into a visually hidden container and read content that was supposed to be invisible to AT, creating a ghost content experience**: `aria-hidden` removes elements from the accessibility tree (for screen reader browse mode) but has no effect on native tab order. A `<div aria-hidden="true">` containing a `<button>` — the button is still Tab-reachable, and when focused, some screen readers announce it because it receives keyboard focus outside of browse mode. WHY: Developers conflate "hidden from the accessibility tree" with "hidden from all AT interaction" — `aria-hidden` must be paired with `tabIndex={-1}` on all focusable descendants, or the container must use `inert` attribute (now Baseline across all major browsers as of 2023) to completely remove it from both the accessibility tree and focus order.

156. **[community] When testing accessible names with `getByRole({ name: /regex/ })` in Testing Library, regex matching is case-sensitive by default — `getByRole('button', { name: /Submit/ })` will not match a button whose accessible name is "submit" (lowercase), causing false test failures or missed elements**: The `name` option in Testing Library's `getByRole` performs a regular expression match against the computed accessible name. Without the `i` flag, case differences between the visible label text and the computed accessible name (which may be normalized by ARIA processing) produce mismatches. WHY: Teams write `getByRole('button', { name: /Submit Form/ })` expecting it to match any button labelled "Submit form" or "submit form", then the test breaks in an environment where the button text is lowercased by CSS `text-transform: lowercase` — the visible text is "SUBMIT FORM" but the accessible name is "submit form" (accessible name computation does not apply CSS transforms); always use the `i` flag for accessible name regex assertions.

157. **[community] Playwright `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` with inline YAML will silently pass if the actual ARIA tree contains extra roles or nodes that are not in the snapshot template — the assertion only checks that the snapshot template is a structural subset, not an exact match**: Teams write a minimal aria snapshot like `- button "Save"` expecting it to verify the full dialog structure, but a dialog with an extra unlabeled close button or a heading will still pass because the snapshot template is satisfied as a subset. WHY: Teams coming from Jest snapshot testing expect strict equality, but ARIA snapshot matching is designed for resilience — partial matching is intentional to avoid brittle tests, but it means you must include all critical structural elements explicitly in your snapshot template; for exact structure verification, assert the full aria tree including all roles, or use `expect(snapshot).toBe(fullExpectedYaml)` after `page.ariaSnapshot()`.

### Pattern 31 (Cycle 32) — WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: Sticky Footer / Cookie Banner Test

WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 (AA) requires that when a UI component receives keyboard focus it is not entirely hidden by author-created content such as sticky headers, cookie consent banners, or chat widgets. A focused element may be *partially* obscured and still pass 2.4.11; it must be *entirely* hidden to fail. SC 2.4.12 (AAA) requires it to be fully visible with no obscuring at all.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/focus-not-obscured.spec.ts
// Verifies WCAG 2.4.11: focused elements are not entirely hidden by sticky UI chrome.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.11 — Focus Not Obscured', () => {
  test('focused link in main content is not entirely covered by sticky cookie banner', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Ensure cookie banner is visible (not dismissed)
    const banner = page.locator('[data-testid="cookie-banner"]');
    await expect(banner).toBeVisible();

    // Tab to the first focusable element in main content area
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focusedEl = page.locator(':focus');
    await expect(focusedEl).toBeVisible();

    // Get bounding boxes
    const focusedBox = await focusedEl.boundingBox();
    const bannerBox = await banner.boundingBox();
    expect(focusedBox).not.toBeNull();
    expect(bannerBox).not.toBeNull();

    if (focusedBox && bannerBox) {
      // The focused element must not be entirely below the banner top edge
      const focusedBottom = focusedBox.y + focusedBox.height;
      const bannerTop = bannerBox.y;
      // If the entire focused element is within the banner bounding box, it is fully obscured
      const fullyObscured =
        focusedBox.y >= bannerTop &&
        focusedBottom <= bannerTop + bannerBox.height;
      expect(fullyObscured, 'Focused element must not be entirely hidden by sticky banner').toBe(false);
    }
  });

  test('Tab through all interactive elements: none fully obscured by sticky header', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const stickyHeader = page.locator('header[data-sticky]');
    const headerBox = await stickyHeader.boundingBox();

    // Tab through first 10 focusable items and assert none are fully behind the header
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
      const box = await page.locator(':focus').boundingBox();
      if (box && headerBox) {
        const entirelyBehindHeader = box.y + box.height <= headerBox.y + headerBox.height;
        expect(entirelyBehindHeader, `Focus stop ${i + 1} must not be entirely behind sticky header`).toBe(false);
      }
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern for any layout with `position: sticky` or `position: fixed` UI chrome (navbars, banners, footers, chat widgets). Do NOT write this test as a pixel-perfect overlap check — 2.4.11 only fails on *complete* obscuring; partial overlap is acceptable at AA level. Named alternative: the CSS fix (`scroll-padding-top` equal to the sticky header height) is more reliable than a test-only approach — pair the geometric Playwright assertion with a unit test that checks the computed `scroll-padding-top` value matches the sticky header height. [official]

### Pattern 32 (Cycle 32) — ARIA Spinbutton Keyboard Contract Test

WCAG SC 4.1.2 and the ARIA APG Spinbutton pattern require that `role="spinbutton"` widgets expose `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, and respond to Up/Down arrow and Home/End keys. This pattern validates the full keyboard contract and accessible value announcements.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/aria-spinbutton.spec.ts
// Tests ARIA spinbutton keyboard contract per WCAG 4.1.2 and ARIA APG.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Spinbutton — keyboard contract', () => {
  test('spinbutton exposes aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/quantity-selector');
    const spinbutton = page.getByRole('spinbutton', { name: 'Quantity' });

    await expect(spinbutton).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow');
    await expect(spinbutton).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemin');
    await expect(spinbutton).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemax');
  });

  test('ArrowUp increments aria-valuenow, ArrowDown decrements', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/quantity-selector');
    const spinbutton = page.getByRole('spinbutton', { name: 'Quantity' });
    await spinbutton.focus();

    const initialValue = parseInt(await spinbutton.getAttribute('aria-valuenow') ?? '0', 10);

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowUp');
    const afterUp = parseInt(await spinbutton.getAttribute('aria-valuenow') ?? '0', 10);
    expect(afterUp).toBe(initialValue + 1);

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    const afterDown = parseInt(await spinbutton.getAttribute('aria-valuenow') ?? '0', 10);
    expect(afterDown).toBe(initialValue);
  });

  test('Home sets aria-valuenow to aria-valuemin', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/quantity-selector');
    const spinbutton = page.getByRole('spinbutton', { name: 'Quantity' });
    await spinbutton.focus();

    const min = parseInt(await spinbutton.getAttribute('aria-valuemin') ?? '0', 10);
    await page.keyboard.press('Home');
    const afterHome = parseInt(await spinbutton.getAttribute('aria-valuenow') ?? '-1', 10);
    expect(afterHome).toBe(min);
  });

  test('End sets aria-valuenow to aria-valuemax', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/quantity-selector');
    const spinbutton = page.getByRole('spinbutton', { name: 'Quantity' });
    await spinbutton.focus();

    const max = parseInt(await spinbutton.getAttribute('aria-valuemax') ?? '0', 10);
    await page.keyboard.press('End');
    const afterEnd = parseInt(await spinbutton.getAttribute('aria-valuenow') ?? '-1', 10);
    expect(afterEnd).toBe(max);
  });

  test('aria-valuetext is set when numeric value needs textual context', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/font-size-selector');
    const spinbutton = page.getByRole('spinbutton', { name: 'Font size' });
    // When value has a unit (e.g. "16px") aria-valuetext should expose it
    await expect(spinbutton).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuetext');
    const valueText = await spinbutton.getAttribute('aria-valuetext');
    expect(valueText).toMatch(/\d+px/);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern for any custom numeric input widget built with `role="spinbutton"` (quantity selectors, rating inputs, font size pickers). Do NOT use `role="spinbutton"` for a native `<input type="number">` — native inputs already have the correct implicit role and keyboard behavior, and adding the explicit role is redundant and can confuse some assistive technologies. Named alternative: native `<input type="number">` gets the spinbutton role for free and handles ArrowUp/Down natively without custom JavaScript; prefer native elements over ARIA-augmented divs whenever possible. [official]

### Pattern 33 (Cycle 32) — Accessible Error Summary Pattern (WCAG 3.3.1 + 3.3.3)

When a form submission fails, WCAG 3.3.1 (Error Identification) requires that each error is described in text, and 3.3.3 (Error Suggestion, AA) requires that suggestions for fixing errors are provided where possible. An error summary injected at the top of the form — with focus moved to it — is the most reliable pattern for screen reader users.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/form-error-summary.spec.ts
// Verifies WCAG 3.3.1 + 3.3.3: error summary is rendered, focusable, and lists each field error.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Form error summary — WCAG 3.3.1 + 3.3.3', () => {
  test('submitting empty form renders error summary with role=alert', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/registration');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();

    // Error summary must appear at the top with role=alert (or aria-live="assertive")
    const errorSummary = page.getByRole('alert');
    await expect(errorSummary).toBeVisible();
    await expect(errorSummary).toContainText(/errors/i);
  });

  test('error summary receives focus on form submission failure', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/registration');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();

    const errorSummary = page.locator('[data-testid="error-summary"]');
    await expect(errorSummary).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('error summary links navigate to each invalid field', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/registration');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();

    const errorLinks = page.locator('[data-testid="error-summary"] a');
    const count = await errorLinks.count();
    expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    // Each error link should navigate to (focus) the corresponding field
    for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 3); i++) {
      const href = await errorLinks.nth(i).getAttribute('href');
      expect(href).toMatch(/^#/); // Must be an in-page anchor
      const fieldId = href?.replace('#', '') ?? '';
      const field = page.locator(`#${fieldId}`);
      await expect(field).toBeVisible();
    }
  });

  test('each field has aria-describedby referencing its inline error message', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/registration');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();

    const emailField = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i });
    await expect(emailField).toHaveAttribute('aria-describedby');
    await expect(emailField).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');

    const errorId = await emailField.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
    const errorEl = page.locator(`#${errorId}`);
    await expect(errorEl).toBeVisible();
    await expect(errorEl).not.toBeEmpty();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern for any multi-field form where invalid submission is possible. Do NOT rely on `aria-live="polite"` for form error summaries — polite regions may be interrupted or delayed, causing users to miss error announcements when focus movements also trigger announcements; `role="alert"` (equivalent to `aria-live="assertive"`) is the correct choice for form validation errors that require immediate attention. Named alternative: `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` in Playwright (v1.50+) checks the linked `aria-errormessage` element for individual field errors — use it to assert per-field error text in addition to the summary. [official]

---

### Pattern 34 (Cycle 32) — WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name: Voice Control Compatibility Test

WCAG 2.5.3 (A) requires that for interactive elements with visible text labels, the accessible name must *contain* the visible label text. Voice control software (Dragon NaturallySpeaking, Windows Voice Access) activates controls by their spoken visible label. If the accessible name does not contain the visible text, voice control users cannot activate the control by saying its label.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/label-in-name.spec.ts
// Verifies WCAG 2.5.3: accessible name of interactive elements contains visible text label.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('WCAG 2.5.3 — Label in Name', () => {
  test('axe detects label-in-name violations', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['label-content-name-mismatch'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('icon-only button with aria-label contains visible text when text is present', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products');
    // Check all buttons that have both visible text AND an aria-label
    const buttons = page.getByRole('button');
    const count = await buttons.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const btn = buttons.nth(i);
      const visibleText = (await btn.textContent())?.trim() ?? '';
      const ariaLabel = await btn.getAttribute('aria-label');

      if (visibleText && ariaLabel) {
        // WCAG 2.5.3: accessible name must CONTAIN the visible text (case-insensitive)
        expect(
          ariaLabel.toLowerCase().includes(visibleText.toLowerCase()),
          `Button "${visibleText}" has aria-label "${ariaLabel}" that does not contain visible text`
        ).toBe(true);
      }
    }
  });

  test('link accessible name contains visible link text', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/about');
    const links = page.getByRole('link');
    const count = await links.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 20); i++) {
      const link = links.nth(i);
      const visibleText = (await link.textContent())?.trim() ?? '';
      const ariaLabel = await link.getAttribute('aria-label');

      if (visibleText && ariaLabel && visibleText.length > 0) {
        expect(
          ariaLabel.toLowerCase().includes(visibleText.toLowerCase()),
          `Link "${visibleText}" has aria-label "${ariaLabel}" that omits visible text`
        ).toBe(true);
      }
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern whenever icon buttons have visible text labels alongside the icon, or when `aria-label` is used to augment visible text (e.g., "Delete" button with `aria-label="Delete item 42"`). Do NOT use a custom aria-label that *replaces* the visible text with completely different wording — for example, a "Search" button with `aria-label="Find content"` fails 2.5.3 because "Search" is not contained in "Find content". Named alternative: use `aria-describedby` to append context to the visible label (`aria-describedby="item-42-id"`) instead of replacing the accessible name via `aria-label` — the accessible name stays identical to the visible text, satisfying 2.5.3. [official]
