### Pattern 35 (Cycle 32) — `@axe-core/vitest` Component Accessibility Unit Tests

`@axe-core/vitest` provides a native Vitest integration for running axe-core against rendered components in jsdom or happy-dom environments. It replaces jest-axe in Vite/Vitest projects and provides the same `toHaveNoViolations()` matcher API.

```typescript
// File: src/components/__tests__/Badge.a11y.test.ts
// Component-level axe accessibility test using @axe-core/vitest.
import { render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { configureAxe, toHaveNoViolations } from '@axe-core/vitest';
import { expect, test, describe } from 'vitest';
import { Badge } from '../Badge';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

const axe = configureAxe({
  rules: {
    // Disable color-contrast in unit tests — jsdom has no layout engine
    'color-contrast': { enabled: false },
  },
});

describe('Badge component — accessibility', () => {
  test('status badge with role="status" has no axe violations', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <Badge variant="success" aria-label="Order confirmed">Confirmed</Badge>
    );
    const results = await axe(container);
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  test('badge without accessible name fails axe — regression guard', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<Badge variant="error" />);
    const results = await axe(container);
    // A badge with no text and no aria-label should have a violation
    expect(results.violations.some((v: { id: string }) => v.id === 'label')).toBe(true);
  });

  test('multiple badges on page share no duplicate IDs', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <div>
        <Badge variant="info" aria-label="1 notification">1</Badge>
        <Badge variant="warning" aria-label="3 warnings">3</Badge>
      </div>
    );
    const results = await axe(container);
    const duplicateIdViolation = results.violations.find((v: { id: string }) => v.id === 'duplicate-id');
    expect(duplicateIdViolation).toBeUndefined();
  });

  test('badge color variants all meet 1.4.3 contrast — documented for E2E', () => {
    // Contrast is not checked by jsdom axe; document for manual/E2E verification
    const variants = ['success', 'error', 'warning', 'info'] as const;
    // All variants should be tested in Playwright E2E with real browser layout
    expect(variants).toHaveLength(4);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `@axe-core/vitest` for component-level unit tests in Vite/Vitest projects — it runs fast in CI without a browser and catches structural ARIA issues early. Do NOT use it as a replacement for E2E axe scans — jsdom does not have a layout engine, so contrast violations, scroll behavior, and focus visibility cannot be tested; always pair with Playwright + `@axe-core/playwright` E2E scans. Named alternative: jest-axe is the equivalent for Jest projects, but is not compatible with Jest v30+ (due to ESM module resolution changes); prefer `@axe-core/vitest` in all new Vite/Vitest projects. [official]

---

### Pattern 36 (Cycle 32) — WCAG 3.1.2 Language of Parts: `lang` Attribute on Foreign-Language Content

WCAG 3.1.2 (AA) requires that the human language of each passage or phrase in the content is programmatically determinable. Screen readers switch pronunciation engines when they encounter a `lang` attribute, ensuring correct pronunciation of foreign text. This is commonly missed when applications embed foreign-language quotes, legal disclaimers, or i18n content.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/language-of-parts.spec.ts
// Verifies WCAG 3.1.2: foreign-language passages have correct lang attribute.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('WCAG 3.1.2 — Language of Parts', () => {
  test('html element has lang attribute matching BCP 47 format', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const htmlLang = await page.locator('html').getAttribute('lang');
    expect(htmlLang).toBeTruthy();
    expect(htmlLang).toMatch(/^[a-z]{2}(-[A-Z]{2})?$/); // e.g. "en", "en-US"
  });

  test('French disclaimer block has lang="fr"', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/legal');
    const frenchBlock = page.locator('[data-testid="french-disclaimer"]');
    await expect(frenchBlock).toHaveAttribute('lang', 'fr');
  });

  test('axe detects missing or invalid lang on html element', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['html-has-lang', 'html-lang-valid', 'valid-lang'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('i18n content block switches lang attribute when locale changes', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings?locale=de');
    const htmlLang = await page.locator('html').getAttribute('lang');
    expect(htmlLang).toBe('de');
  });

  test('code elements do not require lang override — WCAG 3.1.2 exemption documented', async ({ page }) => {
    // Technical terms like "npm install" do not require lang="en" on a non-English page.
    // WCAG 3.1.2 exempts proper names, technical terms, and indeterminate-language words.
    await page.goto('/docs/getting-started?locale=fr');
    const codeBlocks = page.locator('code');
    const count = await codeBlocks.count();
    // Code elements intentionally lack lang attributes — this is correct behavior
    expect(count).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern for multilingual applications, applications with legal disclaimers in multiple languages, and any page that embeds foreign-language quotes or UI strings. Do NOT add `lang` overrides to technical terms, proper nouns, or code snippets — WCAG 3.1.2 exempts these (they are language-neutral). Named alternative: server-side rendering with locale-aware `lang` attribute on `<html>` handles 3.1.1 (Language of Page) centrally; for 3.1.2 (Language of Parts), a component-level design system convention (e.g., a `<ForeignText lang="fr">` wrapper component) is more maintainable than ad-hoc `lang` attributes scattered through the markup. [official]

---

### Pattern 37 (Cycle 32) — WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text: 200% Zoom No Content Loss

WCAG 1.4.4 (AA) requires that text can be resized up to 200% without loss of content or functionality. This is commonly violated by fixed-height containers, `overflow: hidden` on text containers, or using `px` units instead of relative units for font sizes.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/resize-text.spec.ts
// Verifies WCAG 1.4.4: critical content remains accessible at 200% font scale.
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

async function set200PercentFontSize(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  // Simulate 200% text-only zoom by injecting a root font-size override
  await page.addStyleTag({
    content: 'html { font-size: 200% !important; }',
  });
  // Allow layout to reflow after font size change
  await page.waitForTimeout(200);
}

test.describe('WCAG 1.4.4 — Resize Text to 200%', () => {
  test('navigation links remain visible at 200% font size', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await set200PercentFontSize(page);

    const navLinks = page.getByRole('navigation').getByRole('link');
    const count = await navLinks.count();
    expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      await expect(navLinks.nth(i)).toBeVisible();
    }
  });

  test('form inputs remain visible at 200% font size', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    await set200PercentFontSize(page);

    const inputs = page.getByRole('textbox');
    const count = await inputs.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      await expect(inputs.nth(i)).toBeVisible();
    }
  });

  test('no horizontal scrollbar on main content at 200% font size (reflow check)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setViewportSize({ width: 1280, height: 800 });
    await page.goto('/');
    await set200PercentFontSize(page);

    const scrollWidth = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth);
    const clientWidth = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.clientWidth);
    expect(scrollWidth).toBeLessThanOrEqual(clientWidth + 5); // 5px tolerance
  });

  test('card component text does not overflow container at 200% zoom', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    await set200PercentFontSize(page);

    const card = page.locator('[data-testid="summary-card"]').first();
    const cardBox = await card.boundingBox();
    const cardText = card.locator('p').first();
    const textBox = await cardText.boundingBox();

    if (cardBox && textBox) {
      expect(textBox.x + textBox.width).toBeLessThanOrEqual(cardBox.x + cardBox.width + 2);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern to guard against `overflow: hidden` text clipping and fixed-height containers that hide content at large font sizes. Do NOT use browser zoom (which scales everything) to test 1.4.4 — the WCAG intent is specifically *text-only* resizing, which in modern browsers is controlled by the user's browser font size preference, not the zoom level; simulate it by overriding the root `font-size` as shown. Named alternative: Playwright's `page.setViewportSize()` combined with `--force-device-scale-factor` flag simulates full page zoom (1.4.10 Reflow) but not text-only zoom (1.4.4) — use both test approaches for full coverage. [official]

---

### Pattern 38 (Cycle 32) — ARIA `role=feed` Infinite Scroll Accessibility Pattern

The ARIA `role="feed"` pattern is the correct semantic structure for infinite-scroll or paginated article lists (news feeds, social timelines, search results). Each article in the feed must have `role="article"`, be focusable, and expose `aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset` if the total is known. Screen readers provide dedicated feed navigation shortcuts.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/aria-feed.spec.ts
// Tests ARIA feed pattern: role=feed, role=article, keyboard navigation per ARIA APG.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('ARIA feed pattern — role=feed + role=article', () => {
  test('feed container has role=feed and an accessible name', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/news-feed');
    const feed = page.getByRole('feed');
    await expect(feed).toBeVisible();
    // Feed must have an accessible name via aria-label or aria-labelledby
    const feedLabel = await feed.getAttribute('aria-label');
    const feedLabelledBy = await feed.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    expect(feedLabel || feedLabelledBy).toBeTruthy();
  });

  test('each article in feed has role=article and is focusable (tabindex=0)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/news-feed');
    const articles = page.getByRole('article');
    const count = await articles.count();
    expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 5); i++) {
      const tabIndex = await articles.nth(i).getAttribute('tabindex');
      expect(tabIndex, `Article ${i} must be focusable`).toBe('0');
    }
  });

  test('feed article exposes aria-posinset and aria-setsize when total count is known', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/news-feed?total=50');
    const firstArticle = page.getByRole('article').first();
    await expect(firstArticle).toHaveAttribute('aria-posinset', '1');
    await expect(firstArticle).toHaveAttribute('aria-setsize', '50');
  });

  test('Page Down key moves focus to next article', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/news-feed');
    const firstArticle = page.getByRole('article').first();
    await firstArticle.focus();

    await page.keyboard.press('PageDown');
    const focusedRole = await page.evaluate(
      () => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role')
    );
    expect(focusedRole).toBe('article');
  });

  test('axe scan of feed page finds no WCAG 2.2 AA violations', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/news-feed');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `role="feed"` for linear lists of articles that load dynamically (infinite scroll, load-more pagination). Do NOT use `role="feed"` for data grids, navigation menus, or static lists — the feed role implies keyboard navigation semantics (Page Down/Up, Escape to exit) that are unexpected on non-article content. Named alternative: a simple `<ul>` + `<li>` with `aria-live="polite"` on the container is sufficient for short, non-scrolling lists; `role="feed"` is specifically optimized for long, dynamically growing article collections. [official]

---

### Pattern 39 (Cycle 32) — Playwright Accessibility Snapshot Regression with `ariaSnapshot()`

Playwright v1.49+ introduced `page.ariaSnapshot()` and `expect(locator).toMatchAriaSnapshot()` for capturing and asserting the semantic structure of UI components. Pairing snapshot creation with structured inline YAML comments creates living documentation that catches ARIA regressions in CI.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/aria-snapshot-regression.spec.ts
// Uses Playwright ariaSnapshot for ARIA structure regression testing.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA snapshot regression tests', () => {
  test('navigation menu aria structure matches expected snapshot', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await expect(page.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Main' })).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - navigation "Main":
        - list:
          - listitem:
            - link "Home"
          - listitem:
            - link "Products"
          - listitem:
            - link "About"
          - listitem:
            - link "Contact"
    `);
  });

  test('dialog structure includes heading and close button', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).first().click();

    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - dialog:
        - heading /Add to cart/i
        - button /close/i
    `);
  });

  test('aria snapshot captures live region state after async update', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill('laptop');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Search' }).click();
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="status"]');

    const snapshot = await page.ariaSnapshot();
    expect(snapshot).toContain('status');
  });

  test('tab list structure matches expected ARIA tab pattern', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/account');
    await expect(page.getByRole('tablist')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - tablist:
        - tab "Profile" [selected]
        - tab "Security"
        - tab "Notifications"
    `);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` for structural regression testing of key interactive widgets (navigation, dialogs, tabs, forms). Do NOT treat ARIA snapshots as a substitute for functional axe scans — `toMatchAriaSnapshot` verifies structure (roles, names, hierarchy) but does not evaluate WCAG rule compliance (contrast, label association, focus management); use both. Named alternative: `page.ariaSnapshot()` returns a raw YAML string that can be logged and compared with custom logic — useful when you need to assert that a snapshot does NOT contain a specific pattern (e.g., checking that no `generic` roles appear where semantic roles are expected). [official]

---

### Pattern 40 (Cycle 32) — Keyboard Trap Detection in Modal Dialogs (WCAG 2.1.2)

WCAG 2.1.2 (A) allows keyboard traps in modal dialogs — but only when Escape (or a documented key sequence) releases the trap. Testing must verify both sides: (1) focus is correctly trapped inside the dialog while open, and (2) the trap is releasable via the correct key(s).

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/modal-focus-trap.spec.ts
// Tests WCAG 2.1.2: modal focus trap is correct — trapped while open, releasable via Escape.
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

async function openModal(page: Page, triggerLabel: string): Promise<void> {
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: triggerLabel }).click();
  await page.waitForSelector('[role="dialog"]', { state: 'visible' });
}

test.describe('Modal focus trap — WCAG 2.1.2', () => {
  test('focus moves into dialog on open', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products');
    await openModal(page, 'Add to cart');

    const isInsideDialog = await page.evaluate(
      () => document.activeElement?.closest('[role="dialog"]') !== null
    );
    expect(isInsideDialog).toBe(true);
  });

  test('Tab key cycles focus within modal — does not leave dialog', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await openModal(page, 'Open settings');

    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
    const focusableInDialog = dialog.locator('button, input, select, textarea, a[href], [tabindex="0"]');
    const count = await focusableInDialog.count();

    // Tab through all focusable elements + one more to wrap — should not leave dialog
    for (let i = 0; i <= count; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
      const isInsideDialog = await page.evaluate(
        () => document.activeElement?.closest('[role="dialog"]') !== null
      );
      expect(isInsideDialog).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test('Shift+Tab cycles backwards within modal — does not leave dialog', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await openModal(page, 'Open settings');

    await page.keyboard.press('Shift+Tab');
    const isInsideDialog = await page.evaluate(
      () => document.activeElement?.closest('[role="dialog"]') !== null
    );
    expect(isInsideDialog).toBe(true);
  });

  test('Escape key closes dialog and returns focus to trigger element', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products');
    const trigger = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).first();
    await trigger.click();
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="dialog"]', { state: 'visible' });

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="dialog"]', { state: 'hidden' });

    // Focus must return to the trigger element that opened the modal
    await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('close button in dialog closes it and returns focus to trigger', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products');
    const trigger = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).first();
    await trigger.click();
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="dialog"]', { state: 'visible' });

    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /close/i }).click();
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="dialog"]', { state: 'hidden' });
    await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern for any modal dialog (`role="dialog"`, `role="alertdialog"`) that traps focus. Do NOT use this test pattern for non-modal overlays (tooltips, popovers, dropdowns) — those must NOT trap focus (WCAG 2.1.2 only permits trapping in modals with an explicit close mechanism). Named alternative: the `inert` attribute (Baseline 2023) set on the background content is the most reliable focus-trap implementation alternative to manual JavaScript; test that `document.querySelector('main').inert === true` while the dialog is open. [official]

---

### Pattern 41 (Cycle 32) — `jest-axe` with `@testing-library` for React: Async State Testing

React components with async state (loading spinners, optimistic updates, data-fetched content) require `waitFor` + `act` patterns to ensure the component has finished rendering before axe scans it. Scanning too early catches violations in skeleton states that do not exist in the final rendered output.

```typescript
// File: src/components/__tests__/ProductList.a11y.test.tsx
// Tests axe accessibility after async data load using waitFor + act.
import { render, screen, waitFor, act } from '@testing-library/react';
import { axe, toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';
import { expect, test, describe } from '@jest/globals';
import { server } from '../../mocks/server';
import { rest } from 'msw';
import { ProductList } from '../ProductList';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

describe('ProductList — async accessibility', () => {
  test('has no violations after products load successfully', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<ProductList />);

    // Wait for loading state to resolve before running axe
    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(screen.queryByRole('progressbar')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    });

    const results = await axe(container);
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  test('loading state exposes an accessible progressbar', async () => {
    // Delay API response to isolate the loading state
    server.use(
      rest.get('/api/products', (_req, res, ctx) => res(ctx.delay(2000)))
    );
    const { container } = render(<ProductList />);

    const results = await axe(container);
    // Loading state must have a labelled progressbar and no other violations
    const violations = results.violations.filter((v: { id: string }) => v.id !== 'color-contrast');
    expect(violations).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(screen.getByRole('progressbar')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  test('error state renders an accessible alert message', async () => {
    server.use(
      rest.get('/api/products', (_req, res, ctx) => res(ctx.status(500)))
    );
    const { container } = render(<ProductList />);

    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(screen.getByRole('alert')).toBeInTheDocument();
    });

    await act(async () => {
      const results = await axe(container);
      expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
    });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern for components with loading, error, and success states to verify that all three states are accessible — many teams only test the success state. Do NOT run axe inside `waitFor` callbacks — `axe()` is async and returns a promise; awaiting it inside `waitFor` can produce misleading timeout errors; always `await axe(container)` after `waitFor` resolves. Named alternative: Playwright + `@axe-core/playwright` E2E tests can scan the same async states with real network conditions; use jest-axe for fast unit coverage and Playwright for integration-level validation. [community]

---

### Pattern 42 (Cycle 32) — Playwright `toHaveAccessibleName` and `toHaveAccessibleDescription` Combined Assertions

Playwright v1.44+ provides `toHaveAccessibleName()` and `toHaveAccessibleDescription()` matchers that verify the computed accessible name and description against what screen readers will announce. These replace fragile attribute-level assertions (`toHaveAttribute('aria-label', ...)`) with semantics-level assertions.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/accessible-name-description.spec.ts
// Uses Playwright toHaveAccessibleName + toHaveAccessibleDescription for AT-level assertions.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Accessible name and description assertions', () => {
  test('search input has correct accessible name from visible label element', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    // Accessible name should come from the <label> element, not aria-label
    await expect(page.getByRole('searchbox')).toHaveAccessibleName('Search products');
  });

  test('icon button with aria-label has correct accessible name', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const closeBtn = page.locator('[data-testid="close-notification"]');
    await expect(closeBtn).toHaveAccessibleName(/close/i);
  });

  test('form field with aria-describedby has correct accessible description', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/registration');
    const passwordField = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /password/i });
    // Description should come from the password hint paragraph via aria-describedby
    await expect(passwordField).toHaveAccessibleDescription(/at least 8 characters/i);
  });

  test('invalid field after submission has accessible error message', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/registration');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();
    const emailField = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i });
    await expect(emailField).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(/valid email/i);
  });

  test('hero image has non-empty accessible name from alt attribute', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/about');
    const heroImage = page.locator('img[data-testid="hero"]');
    const altText = await heroImage.getAttribute('alt');
    expect(altText?.trim()).toBeTruthy();
    await expect(heroImage).toHaveAccessibleName(/.+/);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `toHaveAccessibleName()` and `toHaveAccessibleDescription()` instead of `toHaveAttribute('aria-label', ...)` or `toHaveAttribute('aria-describedby', ...)` — attribute-level assertions check the markup attribute, not what the browser's accessibility API actually computes as the name (which may come from `<label>`, `aria-labelledby`, `title`, or element content). Do NOT use these matchers as a substitute for axe scans — they verify specific elements but do not catch missing labels, role violations, or ARIA misuse across the whole page. Named alternative: `getByRole('button', { name: /text/ })` in Playwright also matches by computed accessible name, so test selection and accessible name assertion can be combined into a single `getByRole` call. [official]

---

### Pattern 43 (Cycle 32) — WCAG 2.4.6 Headings and Labels: Heading Structure Audit

WCAG 2.4.6 (AA) requires that headings are descriptive. A deeper requirement (supported by best practice and screen reader user research) is that headings form a logical outline — no skipped levels, a single `<h1>` per page, and section headings that describe their content. Testing Library and axe do not fully verify heading logic; a custom Playwright audit is needed.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/heading-structure.spec.ts
// Audits WCAG 2.4.6: heading hierarchy is logical, single h1, no skipped levels.
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

interface HeadingInfo {
  level: number;
  text: string;
}

async function getHeadings(page: Page): Promise<HeadingInfo[]> {
  return page.evaluate(() => {
    const headings = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6'));
    return headings.map(h => ({
      level: parseInt(h.tagName.replace('H', ''), 10),
      text: (h.textContent ?? '').trim().slice(0, 80),
    }));
  });
}

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.6 — Heading Structure', () => {
  test('page has exactly one h1', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const headings = await getHeadings(page);
    const h1s = headings.filter(h => h.level === 1);
    expect(h1s).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  test('heading levels do not skip (no h2 directly followed by h4)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/docs/api');
    const headings = await getHeadings(page);

    for (let i = 1; i < headings.length; i++) {
      const prev = headings[i - 1];
      const curr = headings[i];
      // A heading level must not jump more than one level deeper
      const levelJump = curr.level - prev.level;
      expect(
        levelJump,
        `Heading "${curr.text}" (h${curr.level}) skips levels after "${prev.text}" (h${prev.level})`
      ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
    }
  });

  test('all headings have non-empty text content', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    const headings = await getHeadings(page);
    for (const h of headings) {
      expect(h.text, `h${h.level} must have non-empty text`).not.toBe('');
    }
  });

  test('axe detects empty-heading and heading-order violations', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['empty-heading', 'heading-order'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern during initial page audits and after major layout changes. Do NOT enforce `heading-order` as a hard CI gate for pages with complex multi-column layouts (e.g., a dashboard with independently-scrolling widgets) — in those cases, document the known heading order exceptions as accepted issues with business justification. Named alternative: axe's `heading-order` rule detects out-of-order headings automatically and is sufficient for most CI gate purposes; the custom Playwright audit above adds extra coverage for heading count and empty text that axe does not check. [official]

---

### Pattern 44 (Cycle 32) — `prefers-contrast: more` Emulation and Contrast Ratio Validation

WCAG 1.4.6 (AAA) requires a 7:1 contrast ratio for enhanced contrast. More importantly, Windows High Contrast Mode (WHCM) and macOS Increased Contrast users rely on the `prefers-contrast: more` media query to receive higher-contrast styles. Testing that this query is respected and that colors meet the enhanced ratio catches a class of issues invisible to standard contrast tests.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/enhanced-contrast.spec.ts
// Tests prefers-contrast: more media query and WCAG 1.4.6 enhanced contrast behavior.
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

async function setForcedColors(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark', forcedColors: 'active' });
}

/** Compute relative luminance per WCAG 2.x formula. */
function relativeLuminance(r: number, g: number, b: number): number {
  const toLinear = (c: number) => {
    const s = c / 255;
    return s <= 0.04045 ? s / 12.92 : Math.pow((s + 0.055) / 1.055, 2.4);
  };
  return 0.2126 * toLinear(r) + 0.7152 * toLinear(g) + 0.0722 * toLinear(b);
}

function contrastRatio(l1: number, l2: number): number {
  const lighter = Math.max(l1, l2);
  const darker = Math.min(l1, l2);
  return (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05);
}

function parseRgb(css: string): [number, number, number] {
  const m = css.match(/\d+/g)!;
  return [parseInt(m[0], 10), parseInt(m[1], 10), parseInt(m[2], 10)];
}

test.describe('Enhanced contrast — prefers-contrast: more + forced colors', () => {
  test('site renders without layout breakage under forced-colors: active', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await setForcedColors(page);
    const navLinks = page.getByRole('navigation').getByRole('link');
    const count = await navLinks.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      await expect(navLinks.nth(i)).toBeVisible();
    }
  });

  test('CTA button meets at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio in default mode', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const btn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /get started/i }).first();
    const color = await btn.evaluate(el => getComputedStyle(el).color);
    const bg = await btn.evaluate(el => getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor);

    const textLum = relativeLuminance(...parseRgb(color));
    const bgLum = relativeLuminance(...parseRgb(bg));
    const ratio = contrastRatio(textLum, bgLum);
    expect(ratio).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4.5); // WCAG AA minimum
  });

  test('focus indicator is visible under forced-colors mode', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await setForcedColors(page);
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focusedBox = await page.locator(':focus').boundingBox();
    expect(focusedBox).not.toBeNull();
    await expect(page.locator(':focus')).toBeVisible();
  });

  test('all interactive elements visible and non-empty under forced colors', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products');
    await setForcedColors(page);
    const buttons = page.getByRole('button');
    const count = await buttons.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 10); i++) {
      await expect(buttons.nth(i)).toBeVisible();
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern for applications used by enterprise/government users who commonly use Windows High Contrast Mode, or for applications targeting WCAG AAA conformance. Do NOT attempt to compute contrast ratios for CSS custom properties or variables at test time without resolving them — `getComputedStyle` returns resolved values in a real browser but may return unresolved variable names in environments with no layout engine. Named alternative: axe-core's `color-contrast` rule with `runOnly: ['wcag2aaa']` tag checks AAA contrast (7:1) automatically; the Playwright geometric test above adds WHCM-specific validation that axe does not perform. [official]

---

### Pattern 45 (Cycle 32) — Automated Accessibility CI Gate with Playwright + axe-core + Artifact Upload

A complete CI accessibility gate blocks PRs on WCAG 2.2 AA violations, uploads scan reports as test artifacts, and supports per-page violation summaries. This pattern integrates `@axe-core/playwright` with `testInfo.attach()` for rich CI output.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/ci-gate.spec.ts
// Full-page axe CI accessibility gate with artifact upload per page.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

const PAGES_TO_SCAN = [
  { name: 'Home', path: '/' },
  { name: 'Products', path: '/products' },
  { name: 'Checkout', path: '/checkout' },
  { name: 'Account', path: '/account' },
  { name: 'Registration', path: '/registration' },
] as const;

test.describe('Accessibility CI gate — critical pages', () => {
  for (const { name, path: pagePath } of PAGES_TO_SCAN) {
    test(`${name} page has no WCAG 2.2 AA violations`, async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
      await page.goto(pagePath);
      await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

      const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
        .options({ resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'] })
        .analyze();

      // Attach raw axe results as a JSON artifact for CI reporting
      await testInfo.attach(`axe-results-${name.toLowerCase()}`, {
        body: JSON.stringify(results, null, 2),
        contentType: 'application/json',
      });

      // Log violation summary to console for CI log readability
      if (results.violations.length > 0) {
        const summary = results.violations.map(v =>
          `  [${v.impact}] ${v.id}: ${v.description} (${v.nodes.length} node(s))`
        ).join('\n');
        console.error(`\n${name} page violations:\n${summary}`);
      }

      // Hard gate: zero violations required
      expect(
        results.violations,
        `${name} page has ${results.violations.length} WCAG 2.2 AA violations`
      ).toHaveLength(0);
    });
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this CI gate pattern for projects where a zero-violation policy is established. Do NOT run this pattern against all pages in a large application on every PR without scoping — scanning 50+ pages adds minutes to CI and noise to PR feedback; scope the gate to the 5–10 most critical user flows and run full-site scans on a nightly schedule. Named alternative: Pa11y CI with a JSON threshold file offers a simpler YAML-based configuration and built-in HTML reporting without TypeScript, suitable for teams with mixed JS/TS skill levels; use `@axe-core/playwright` when the project is already using Playwright for E2E tests. [official]

---

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 32)

158. **[community] `aria-live="polite"` regions that are rendered *after* page load with `display: none` initially and then shown via JavaScript will not announce their first content update in Firefox**: When a live region is created dynamically and content is inserted at the same time, Firefox does not announce the content because the live region was not in the DOM when the update was committed. Chrome and Safari handle this differently, creating a false sense that the pattern works cross-browser. WHY: Teams build toast notification systems where the toast container is conditionally rendered (e.g., `{isOpen && <div role="status">...</div>}` in React), test in Chrome where it works, then ship code that is completely silent in Firefox for all screen reader users — the fix is to always render the live region container in the DOM from initial page load with empty content (`<div role="status" aria-live="polite"></div>`) and only update its text content when an announcement is needed.

159. **[community] `<button>` elements inside a `<form>` without an explicit `type` attribute default to `type="submit"` per the HTML spec — screen reader users navigating by keyboard and pressing Space to activate what they believe is an action button may inadvertently submit the form**: The HTML specification defaults `<button>` elements inside a `<form>` to `type="submit"`. On pages where a `<form>` wraps a large section of the layout (common in CMS-generated pages or legacy codebases), any `<button>` without an explicit `type="button"` becomes a submit trigger. WHY: Developers add `type="button"` inconsistently, and linters/code review often miss it on buttons deep in nested component trees — the fix is to enforce an ESLint rule (such as `react/button-has-type`) that requires explicit `type` on all `<button>` elements, and to add a test that checks all non-submit buttons within forms have `type="button"`.

160. **[community] Using `display: contents` on a list item (`<li>`) removes its implicit `listitem` role from the accessibility tree in Chrome and Safari, causing axe to report the `<ul>` for missing list items even though the visual layout appears correct**: `display: contents` makes an element "disappear" from the box tree, which has an unintended side effect in Chrome and Safari: the element's ARIA role is also removed from the accessibility tree. A `<ul>` whose `<li>` children all have `display: contents` is announced as an empty list or not announced as a list at all. WHY: Teams use `display: contents` on `<li>` elements to achieve flex/grid layouts without wrapper divs, unaware that it breaks the semantic list structure for screen readers — the fix is to apply `display: contents` to a non-semantic inner `<div>` inside the `<li>` rather than to the `<li>` itself, preserving the listitem role.

161. **[community] Playwright's `getByRole('combobox')` matches both native `<select>` elements and ARIA combobox widgets simultaneously, so tests written for one silently pass against the other when a custom combobox replaces a native select**: `getByRole('combobox')` returns both native `<select>` and elements with `role="combobox"` because the browser maps `<select>` to the combobox role in the accessibility tree. A test asserting `getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Country' }).toBeVisible()` will pass whether the implementation is a native `<select name="country">` or a custom ARIA combobox widget, even if the custom widget has incorrect keyboard behavior. WHY: Teams migrate from native selects to custom comboboxes for design system consistency, but existing Playwright tests continue to pass against the new (potentially broken) widget — explicitly assert the element's tag name with `await expect(locator.evaluate(el => el.tagName)).toBe('SELECT')` when testing native selects, or assert `role="combobox"` attribute only for custom ARIA widgets, to distinguish them and prevent silent migration mismatches.

162. **[community] NVDA in browse mode (the default virtual cursor mode in Firefox) reads all text content in DOM order including visually-hidden elements like skip links styled with `.sr-only` — when both a visible element and a redundant `aria-label` are present, NVDA announces the content twice**: The standard `.sr-only` / `.visually-hidden` CSS class hides text visually while keeping it in the accessibility tree and DOM flow. NVDA in browse mode traverses the DOM and encounters visually-hidden instructional text, skip links, and shadow-content alongside the visible content. If an element has both visible text content and an `aria-label` that duplicates it, some AT combinations announce both. WHY: Developers add `aria-label` to already-labelled elements as a "belt and suspenders" approach, not realizing that both the element's text content and the `aria-label` can be exposed by specific AT/browser combinations — prefer `aria-labelledby` pointing to a visible label element over `aria-label` overrides, and always audit with NVDA in Firefox browse mode as well as Chrome to catch double-announcement issues before shipping.

## Cycle 33 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 46 (Cycle 33) — WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication: Password Manager and Paste Testing

Ensure login and registration forms do not block password managers or clipboard paste. WCAG 3.3.8 (Level AA, new in WCAG 2.2) prohibits requiring users to solve cognitive function tests — including manually transcribing passwords — without an accessible alternative. Password manager auto-fill and unrestricted paste are the primary alternative paths. Blocking `autocomplete` or preventing paste via `onpaste` event listeners is a direct violation. All authentication steps in a multi-factor flow must comply individually.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication', () => {
  test('login form permits password manager autocomplete', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');

    const usernameInput = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /username|email/i });
    const passwordInput = page.locator('input[type="password"]');

    // autocomplete must not be "off" — check the attribute
    const usernameAutocomplete = await usernameInput.getAttribute('autocomplete');
    const passwordAutocomplete = await passwordInput.getAttribute('autocomplete');

    expect(usernameAutocomplete).not.toBe('off');
    expect(passwordAutocomplete).not.toBe('off');

    // Recommended values: 'username' and 'current-password'
    expect(['username', 'email', null, '']).toContain(usernameAutocomplete);
    expect(['current-password', null, '']).toContain(passwordAutocomplete);
  });

  test('password field does not block clipboard paste', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');

    const passwordInput = page.locator('input[type="password"]');
    await passwordInput.focus();

    // Simulate paste via keyboard shortcut
    await page.keyboard.press('Control+v');

    // If paste is blocked, the input will remain empty after a paste attempt.
    // Fill via JS to simulate a clipboard write, then assert it is accepted.
    await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.querySelector('input[type="password"]') as HTMLInputElement;
      const nativeInputValueSetter = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(
        window.HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value'
      )!.set!;
      nativeInputValueSetter.call(el, 'PastedPassword123!');
      el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
    });

    await expect(passwordInput).toHaveValue('PastedPassword123!');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use when auditing login, registration, 2FA, and account recovery flows against WCAG 2.2 AA compliance. Do NOT apply the `autocomplete="off"` check to fields where `autocomplete="new-password"` is legitimately required (new password creation fields) — that value is valid and aids password managers. Alternative: Pa11y with a custom rule or a manual checklist review suffices for teams without a Playwright E2E suite, but the clipboard test genuinely requires a browser environment and cannot be replaced with static analysis. [official]

### Pattern 47 (Cycle 33) — WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry: Multi-Step Form Pre-Population Test

WCAG 3.3.7 (Level A, new in WCAG 2.2) requires that information the user has already entered in a multi-step process is either pre-populated in later steps or available for the user to select, unless re-entry is essential or security-mandated. Common violations include checkout flows that ask for a billing address after a shipping address has been entered, or registration flows that ask for the user's name on a confirmation screen after it was collected on step one. Testing this requires asserting value pre-population across form step navigation.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 3.3.7 — billing address pre-populated from shipping (Redundant Entry)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout/shipping');

  // Step 1: fill shipping address
  await page.getByLabel('First name').fill('Alex');
  await page.getByLabel('Last name').fill('Rivera');
  await page.getByLabel('Street address').fill('123 Main St');
  await page.getByLabel('City').fill('Springfield');
  await page.getByLabel('Postal code').fill('62701');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /continue|next/i }).click();

  // Step 2: assert billing address is either pre-filled or offers a copy option
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/billing/);

  const sameAsShippingCheckbox = page.getByRole('checkbox', {
    name: /same as shipping|billing same/i,
  });

  const isSameAddressAvailable = await sameAsShippingCheckbox.count() > 0;

  if (isSameAddressAvailable) {
    // Pattern A: "same as shipping" checkbox is the acceptable alternative
    await expect(sameAsShippingCheckbox).toBeVisible();
  } else {
    // Pattern B: fields must be pre-populated
    await expect(page.getByLabel('First name')).toHaveValue('Alex');
    await expect(page.getByLabel('Last name')).toHaveValue('Rivera');
    await expect(page.getByLabel('Street address')).toHaveValue('123 Main St');
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern for multi-step checkout flows, registration wizards, onboarding sequences, and any multi-page form that collects overlapping data. Do NOT apply it to authentication re-entry (entering a password a second time for confirmation is explicitly exempted as "essential"). Alternative: Manual walkthroughs by a QA engineer remain necessary for complex business logic that determines which fields are "the same" across steps; automation confirms the data is there, not that the mapping is semantically correct. [official]

---

### Pattern 48 (Cycle 33) — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum): Automated 24×24 CSS Pixel Audit

WCAG 2.5.8 (Level AA, new in WCAG 2.2) requires that interactive targets are at least 24×24 CSS pixels, or that undersized targets have sufficient spacing so that a 24px diameter circle centered on each target does not intersect another target's circle. Automated detection uses `getBoundingClientRect()` in the browser context to measure targets against the threshold. This pattern identifies interactive controls (buttons, links, inputs, checkboxes, radios) with bounding boxes smaller than 24×24 CSS pixels that are not inline text links (the inline exception applies).

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface SmallTarget {
  tag: string;
  role: string | null;
  text: string;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  isInlineText: boolean;
}

test('WCAG 2.5.8 — interactive targets meet 24×24 CSS pixel minimum', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const smallTargets: SmallTarget[] = await page.evaluate((): SmallTarget[] => {
    const selectors = 'a, button, input, select, textarea, [role="button"], [role="checkbox"], [role="radio"], [role="link"], [role="menuitem"], [role="tab"]';
    const elements = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(selectors));

    return elements
      .map((el) => {
        const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        const style = window.getComputedStyle(el);
        // Inline text links are exempt per WCAG 2.5.8 exception
        const isInlineText = el.tagName === 'A' && style.display === 'inline';
        return {
          tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
          role: el.getAttribute('role'),
          text: (el.textContent ?? '').trim().slice(0, 50),
          width: Math.round(rect.width),
          height: Math.round(rect.height),
          isInlineText,
        };
      })
      .filter(
        ({ width, height, isInlineText }) =>
          !isInlineText && (width < 24 || height < 24)
      );
  });

  if (smallTargets.length > 0) {
    const report = smallTargets
      .map(({ tag, text, width, height }) => `  <${tag}> "${text}" — ${width}×${height}px`)
      .join('\n');
    throw new Error(`WCAG 2.5.8: ${smallTargets.length} target(s) below 24×24 CSS px:\n${report}`);
  }

  expect(smallTargets).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this scan pattern on product pages, navigation menus, data tables with action icons, and mobile-targeted layouts where small icon-only buttons are common. Do NOT block PRs on this check without first reviewing spacing — a 20×20px icon button with 8px spacing on all sides satisfies the 24px circle spacing rule; the automated check above flags it as a violation when it may be compliant. Alternative: axe-core does not currently cover WCAG 2.5.8 natively; this custom Playwright evaluation is the best automated substitute until axe adds a dedicated rule. [official]

---

### Pattern 49 (Cycle 33) — WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging Movements: Drag-Alternative Keyboard Path Test

WCAG 2.5.7 (Level AA, new in WCAG 2.2) requires that all drag-dependent functionality has a pointer-only (single click or tap) alternative. This extends to sortable lists, kanban boards, sliders moved by dragging, range inputs, file upload drop zones, and reorderable table columns. Testing must verify that the non-drag path (click-to-select then click-to-place, keyboard arrow reorder, or explicit button-driven reorder) actually changes state correctly, not just that the alternative UI element exists.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 2.5.7 — sortable list supports keyboard/click reorder without drag', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings/notification-order');

  // Record the original order of items
  const getItemOrder = () =>
    page.locator('[data-testid="sortable-item"]').allTextContents();

  const originalOrder = await getItemOrder();
  expect(originalOrder.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);

  // Use the "move up" button alternative — must exist and be keyboard-accessible
  const firstItem = page.locator('[data-testid="sortable-item"]').first();
  const moveDownButton = firstItem.getByRole('button', { name: /move down|↓/i });

  await expect(moveDownButton).toBeVisible();
  await expect(moveDownButton).toBeEnabled();

  // Activate via keyboard (Tab + Enter)
  await moveDownButton.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

  const reorderedOrder = await getItemOrder();

  // The first item should now be second
  expect(reorderedOrder[0]).toBe(originalOrder[1]);
  expect(reorderedOrder[1]).toBe(originalOrder[0]);
});

test('WCAG 2.5.7 — range slider value can be set by clicking the track', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings/volume');

  const slider = page.getByRole('slider', { name: /volume/i });
  const sliderBox = await slider.boundingBox();
  expect(sliderBox).not.toBeNull();

  // Click at the 75% mark on the track — a pointer alternative to dragging
  const clickX = sliderBox!.x + sliderBox!.width * 0.75;
  const clickY = sliderBox!.y + sliderBox!.height / 2;
  await page.mouse.click(clickX, clickY);

  // Value must have changed from the initial state
  const newValue = await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow');
  expect(Number(newValue)).toBeGreaterThan(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use when the application contains drag-to-reorder lists, slider controls, drag-and-drop file uploaders, kanban columns, or resizable split panes. Do NOT focus drag-alternative tests on drawing canvas or map pan interactions where dragging is the only sensible interaction model and the "essential" exception legitimately applies. Alternative: Manual exploratory testing with keyboard-only navigation catches drag-only patterns that don't have visible UI alternatives; pair with an automated inventory of `draggable="true"` elements to scope the manual effort. [official]

---

### Pattern 50 (Cycle 33) — Playwright `toHaveRole()` Semantic Role Assertions (v1.44+)

Playwright's `toHaveRole()` assertion (introduced in v1.44) checks the computed ARIA role of an element as exposed to the accessibility tree, not merely the raw `role` HTML attribute. This is significant because computed roles account for the full ARIA role hierarchy, implicit roles from native HTML elements, and role presentation overrides. Unlike `expect(locator).toHaveAttribute('role', 'button')`, `toHaveRole('button')` also matches `<button>` elements without an explicit role attribute, and it does NOT match an element with `role="switch"` when asserting `toHaveRole('checkbox')` — roles are matched exactly, not hierarchically.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Playwright toHaveRole semantic assertions', () => {
  test('navigation landmark has correct computed role', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    // Native <nav> has implicit role="navigation" — no attribute needed
    const navLandmark = page.locator('nav').first();
    await expect(navLandmark).toHaveRole('navigation');
  });

  test('custom icon toggle has explicit switch role — not checkbox', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings');

    // role="switch" is NOT a subtype of checkbox for toHaveRole matching
    const darkModeToggle = page.getByLabel(/dark mode/i);
    await expect(darkModeToggle).toHaveRole('switch');

    // This assertion WOULD FAIL — switch !== checkbox in Playwright's exact matching:
    // await expect(darkModeToggle).toHaveRole('checkbox'); // ❌
  });

  test('presentation role removes element from accessibility tree', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    // Decorative images should have role="presentation" or aria-hidden="true"
    const decorativeImage = page.locator('img[alt=""]').first();
    // role="presentation" or role="none" are equivalent — both are valid
    const role = await decorativeImage.evaluate((el) =>
      el.getAttribute('role') ?? 'none'
    );
    expect(['presentation', 'none', '']).toContain(role);
  });

  test('dialog role is exposed during modal open state', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open dialog/i }).click();

    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();
    await expect(dialog).toHaveRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toHaveAccessibleName(/.+/); // must have a name
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `toHaveRole()` wherever the semantic role of a component is the critical quality gate (landmark regions, interactive widget types, decorative vs. meaningful images). Do NOT use `toHaveRole()` as a substitute for full keyboard interaction tests — confirming the role is correct does not confirm the keyboard contract (arrow keys, Home/End, Escape) is implemented correctly; pair with interaction tests from the ARIA APG. Alternative: `expect(locator).toHaveAttribute('role', 'dialog')` checks the HTML attribute but misses implicit roles from native elements; `toHaveRole` is strictly more accurate. [official]

---

### Pattern 51 (Cycle 33) — Playwright `getByRole()` with `description` Option (v1.60+)

Playwright v1.60 added a `description` option to `getByRole()` that matches elements by their accessible description, computed from `aria-describedby`, `aria-description`, or `title` attributes. This enables precise disambiguation when multiple elements share the same role and accessible name — a common scenario in data grids, icon button toolbars, and multi-section forms where several "Edit" or "Delete" buttons exist with the same name but different descriptions distinguishing the row or context.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('getByRole with description option — precision row actions', () => {
  test('table delete buttons are distinguishable by accessible description', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/users');

    // Each row has a "Delete" button but with a unique aria-describedby
    // pointing to the row's user name: "Delete Alex Rivera"
    const deleteAlexButton = page.getByRole('button', {
      name: 'Delete',
      description: 'Alex Rivera',
    });

    const deleteSamButton = page.getByRole('button', {
      name: 'Delete',
      description: 'Sam Chen',
    });

    await expect(deleteAlexButton).toBeVisible();
    await expect(deleteSamButton).toBeVisible();

    // Confirm they are different elements
    const alexHandle = await deleteAlexButton.elementHandle();
    const samHandle = await deleteSamButton.elementHandle();
    expect(alexHandle).not.toStrictEqual(samHandle);
  });

  test('icon buttons with identical names differ by description', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/documents');

    // Toolbar has three "Share" icon buttons — each described by the document title
    const shareReport = page.getByRole('button', {
      name: 'Share',
      description: 'Q4 Report',
    });

    await expect(shareReport).toBeEnabled();
    await shareReport.click();

    // Confirm the correct share dialog opened
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /share/i })).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.getByText('Q4 Report')).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use the `description` option when the page contains multiple elements with the same role and name that are differentiated only by their accessible description — data tables, image galleries with action buttons, and multi-panel dashboards. Do NOT rely on `description` matching as a substitute for improving accessible names: if buttons need descriptions to be distinguishable in tests, screen reader users also cannot distinguish them by name alone, which is an accessibility bug (WCAG 4.1.2); the test should also fail the name-uniqueness check. Alternative: `getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete Alex Rivera' })` — providing a full contextual name in the button itself is architecturally cleaner and avoids the need for `aria-describedby` disambiguation. [official]

---

### Pattern 52 (Cycle 33) — WCAG 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced / AAA): Full Visibility Assertion

WCAG 2.4.12 (Level AAA, new in WCAG 2.2) goes beyond the Level AA 2.4.11 requirement (at least partially visible) and requires that the focused component is not obscured by any author-created content. The entire focus indicator must be visible. This is commonly violated by chat widgets pinned to the bottom-right corner, cookie banners, sticky promotional headers, side navigation drawers that overlap content, and custom tooltips triggered by hover. Testing requires scripting focus to each interactive element and asserting the intersection of the element's bounding box with all overlapping elements.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

/**
 * WCAG 2.4.12 — Enhanced: focused element must be FULLY visible (no obscuration).
 * Tests the 10 most critical interactive elements on the page.
 */
test('WCAG 2.4.12 — focused elements are not fully obscured by overlapping content', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Collect interactive elements in tab order
  const focusableSelectors =
    'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), [tabindex="0"]';

  const results: { text: string; obscured: boolean; overlap: string }[] = await page.evaluate(
    (selectors: string) => {
      const elements = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(selectors)).slice(0, 10);
      return elements.map((el) => {
        (el as HTMLElement).focus();
        const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        const centerX = rect.left + rect.width / 2;
        const centerY = rect.top + rect.height / 2;

        // elementsFromPoint returns elements in paint order; first element is topmost
        const topElement = document.elementsFromPoint(centerX, centerY)[0];
        const isObscured = topElement !== el && !el.contains(topElement);

        return {
          text: (el.textContent ?? el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? '').trim().slice(0, 40),
          obscured: isObscured,
          overlap: isObscured ? topElement.tagName + (topElement.id ? '#' + topElement.id : '') : '',
        };
      });
    },
    focusableSelectors
  );

  const obscuredElements = results.filter((r) => r.obscured);
  if (obscuredElements.length > 0) {
    const details = obscuredElements
      .map((r) => `  "${r.text}" obscured by <${r.overlap}>`)
      .join('\n');
    throw new Error(`WCAG 2.4.12: ${obscuredElements.length} focused element(s) fully obscured:\n${details}`);
  }

  expect(obscuredElements).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use for AAA-targeted projects, public sector sites, or any product where sticky footers, banners, or chat widgets are deployed. Do NOT gate CI on this test without manual review — `elementsFromPoint` at the geometric center of a focused element may flag false positives when the element legitimately extends behind a transparent overlay. Alternative: The Level AA test (Pattern 31, Cycle 32) uses a `y + height > viewportHeight - stickyHeight` geometry check that is less brittle and appropriate for the majority of teams targeting AA compliance. [official]

---

### Pattern 53 (Cycle 33) — ARIA Tree View Keyboard Contract Test (APG Treeview Pattern)

The ARIA APG tree view pattern (`role="tree"`, `role="treeitem"`) has a strict keyboard contract that differs from standard list or menu navigation. Right Arrow expands a collapsed node or moves focus to the first child of an already-expanded node; Left Arrow collapses an expanded node or moves focus to the parent. Up/Down Arrow move linearly through visible nodes. Home/End jump to the first and last visible nodes. Type-ahead (pressing a printable character) should advance focus to the next treeitem whose label begins with that character. Automated testing must verify all six key bindings.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA APG Tree View keyboard contract', () => {
  test('tree navigation — Right Arrow expands collapsed node', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-explorer');

    // Focus the first treeitem
    const tree = page.getByRole('tree');
    await expect(tree).toBeVisible();

    const firstItem = tree.getByRole('treeitem').first();
    await firstItem.focus();
    await expect(firstItem).toBeFocused();

    // If the first item is collapsed, Right Arrow should expand it
    const expanded = await firstItem.getAttribute('aria-expanded');
    if (expanded === 'false') {
      await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
      await expect(firstItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    }

    // Second Right Arrow on an expanded node — focus moves to first child
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const focusedAfter = page.locator('[role="treeitem"]:focus');
    await expect(focusedAfter).toBeVisible();
    // Focused element should be a child of the first item
    const parentAriaLevel = await firstItem.getAttribute('aria-level') ?? '1';
    const childAriaLevel = await focusedAfter.getAttribute('aria-level');
    expect(Number(childAriaLevel)).toBeGreaterThan(Number(parentAriaLevel));
  });

  test('tree navigation — Left Arrow collapses expanded node', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-explorer');

    const tree = page.getByRole('tree');
    const expandedNode = tree.getByRole('treeitem', { expanded: true }).first();
    await expandedNode.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft');

    await expect(expandedNode).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  });

  test('tree navigation — Home moves focus to first treeitem', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-explorer');

    // Navigate to a middle item first
    const tree = page.getByRole('tree');
    await tree.getByRole('treeitem').nth(2).focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Home');

    const firstItem = tree.getByRole('treeitem').first();
    await expect(firstItem).toBeFocused();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern when implementing or auditing file explorers, navigation hierarchies, category trees, organization charts, and any component using the ARIA tree role. Do NOT apply it to accordion components (`role="button"` + collapsible regions) or menus (`role="menu"` + `role="menuitem"`) — those patterns have different keyboard contracts; mixing them is a common implementation error. Alternative: The APG tree view example at https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/examples/treeview-navigation/ provides a reference implementation whose keyboard behavior can be compared during manual testing when automated coverage is incomplete. [official]

### Pattern 54 (Cycle 33) — `jest-axe` with `jest.useFakeTimers()` Workaround

When a Jest test file uses `jest.useFakeTimers()` to control time (common in animation, debounce, or polling tests), axe-core hangs and the test suite times out. This is because axe-core internally relies on real `setTimeout` to queue work. The fix is to restore real timers for the duration of the axe assertion and then re-install fake timers. This pattern is also necessary when components under test use MUI or other UI libraries that use `setTimeout` internally for animations that trigger during rendering and interfere with the axe scan timing.

```typescript
import { render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { axe, toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';
import { MyAnimatedModal } from './MyAnimatedModal';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

// Test file uses fake timers for animation control
beforeAll(() => jest.useFakeTimers());
afterAll(() => jest.useRealTimers());

test('MyAnimatedModal has no axe violations when open', async () => {
  const { baseElement } = render(<MyAnimatedModal isOpen={true} onClose={() => {}} />);

  // axe-core uses real setTimeout internally — restore real timers for the scan
  jest.useRealTimers();

  let results;
  try {
    results = await axe(baseElement);
  } finally {
    // Re-install fake timers so subsequent test assertions are not affected
    jest.useFakeTimers();
  }

  expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this workaround whenever a test file mixes `jest.useFakeTimers()` with axe accessibility assertions. Do NOT forget the `finally` block — if axe throws before the `jest.useFakeTimers()` re-installation, subsequent tests in the same file will run with real timers, breaking animation tests. Alternative: Separate accessibility tests into their own test file that does not use fake timers; this is the cleaner architectural approach for large component suites where the interleaving of timer control and accessibility checks becomes complex. [community]

### Pattern 55 (Cycle 33) — `@axe-core/vitest` with Shadow DOM Component Testing

Axe-core does not fully traverse shadow DOM by default. Components built with Web Components, Lit, or Stencil that use shadow roots require axe to be run against the document body or the shadow host with `iframes` configuration enabled. The `@axe-core/vitest` package (Vite-native) provides `toHaveNoViolations()` compatible with Vitest's test runner. Testing Web Components with axe requires attaching the component to a real DOM environment (`happy-dom` or `jsdom`) and running axe against the shadow host element rather than the shadow root directly.

```typescript
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { axe, toHaveNoViolations } from '@axe-core/vitest';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

// Register the custom element before testing
import './my-button.js'; // defines <my-button> with shadow DOM

describe('@axe-core/vitest — Web Component shadow DOM accessibility', () => {
  it('my-button custom element has no axe violations', async () => {
    // Attach the custom element to the document so axe can traverse it
    const container = document.createElement('div');
    document.body.appendChild(container);
    container.innerHTML = '<my-button label="Save document">Save</my-button>';

    // axe must run on document.body (or the host element) — NOT the shadowRoot
    const results = await axe(document.body, {
      // Enable shadow DOM piercing rules (requires axe-core 4.6+)
      shadowDomSelector: 'my-button',
    });

    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();

    // Cleanup
    document.body.removeChild(container);
  });

  it('my-button in focused state announces label correctly', async () => {
    const btn = document.createElement('my-button') as HTMLElement & { label: string };
    btn.setAttribute('label', 'Delete item');
    document.body.appendChild(btn);

    const results = await axe(btn, {
      rules: { 'button-name': { enabled: true } },
    });

    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
    document.body.removeChild(btn);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `@axe-core/vitest` for component-level accessibility unit tests in Vite/Vitest projects that use Web Components or design systems built on Lit/Stencil. Do NOT assume shadow DOM piercing works out of the box for all axe rules — the `color-contrast` rule cannot reliably compute contrast within closed shadow roots because the computed styles are not accessible to the axe engine from the light DOM; test contrast separately with Playwright's `page.evaluate()` approach. Alternative: `jest-axe` with JSDOM is the equivalent for Jest/Webpack projects; the API is identical but the import path differs. [official]

### Pattern 56 (Cycle 33) — Playwright `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` for Form Validation (v1.50+)

Playwright v1.50 introduced `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()`, which asserts the content of an element's `aria-errormessage`. This is the correct way to test inline form validation errors because `aria-errormessage` is distinct from `aria-describedby`: `aria-errormessage` is only announced by AT when `aria-invalid="true"` is set on the input, and its value must be the ID of an in-DOM error element. Tests that only assert `toHaveText()` on an error element miss whether the association is correctly wired to the input via `aria-errormessage` and `aria-invalid`.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Form validation — aria-errormessage wiring (WCAG 3.3.1)', () => {
  test('email input shows accessible error message on invalid submission', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/register');

    // Submit the form without filling required fields
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /register|sign up/i }).click();

    const emailInput = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i });

    // 1. The input must be marked invalid
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');

    // 2. The accessible error message must be populated (Playwright v1.50+)
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(/required|valid email/i);
  });

  test('password input clears error message when valid value entered', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/register');

    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /register/i }).click();

    const passwordInput = page.locator('input[type="password"][name="password"]');

    // Initially invalid
    await expect(passwordInput).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
    await expect(passwordInput).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(/required/i);

    // Enter a valid password
    await passwordInput.fill('ValidPass1!');
    await passwordInput.blur();

    // Error must clear — aria-invalid removed and error message gone
    const isStillInvalid = await passwordInput.getAttribute('aria-invalid');
    expect(isStillInvalid).not.toBe('true');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` for all form validation tests in Playwright suites targeting WCAG 3.3.1 (Error Identification) and 3.3.3 (Error Suggestion). Do NOT use it as a substitute for `toHaveAccessibleDescription()` — `aria-errormessage` is only valid and announced by AT when `aria-invalid="true"` is simultaneously present; if the form uses `aria-describedby` for error messages instead (common legacy pattern), use `toHaveAccessibleDescription()` instead. Alternative: `axe-core`'s `aria-errormessage` rule checks that the referenced error element exists and is visible, but does not assert the content of the error message; use `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` for content correctness. [official]

### Pattern 57 (Cycle 33) — WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA): Automated Outline Geometry and Contrast Test

WCAG 2.4.13 (Level AAA, new in WCAG 2.2) requires that focus indicators meet a minimum area (perimeter of a 2px solid outline) and minimum contrast ratio (3:1 between focused and unfocused states). Automated testing can script Tab navigation, capture the CSS outline properties in focused state, and compute whether the outline meets the area threshold and color contrast requirement. This pattern targets the most impactful entry points: the primary CTA, form inputs, and navigation links.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface FocusStyleAudit {
  element: string;
  outlineWidth: number;
  outlineColor: string;
  outlineStyle: string;
  passesMinWidth: boolean;
}

test('WCAG 2.4.13 — focus indicator has >=2px outline on key interactive elements', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const selectors = [
    'a[href]:first-of-type',
    'button:first-of-type',
    'input[type="text"]:first-of-type',
    'input[type="email"]:first-of-type',
  ];

  const audits: FocusStyleAudit[] = [];

  for (const selector of selectors) {
    const locator = page.locator(selector).first();
    if (await locator.count() === 0) continue;

    await locator.focus();

    const style = await locator.evaluate((el): FocusStyleAudit => {
      const computed = window.getComputedStyle(el);
      const outlineWidth = parseFloat(computed.outlineWidth);
      return {
        element: el.tagName.toLowerCase() + (el.id ? '#' + el.id : ''),
        outlineWidth,
        outlineColor: computed.outlineColor,
        outlineStyle: computed.outlineStyle,
        passesMinWidth: outlineWidth >= 2,
      };
    });

    audits.push(style);
  }

  const failing = audits.filter((a) => !a.passesMinWidth || a.outlineStyle === 'none');

  if (failing.length > 0) {
    const report = failing
      .map((a) => `  <${a.element}>: outline ${a.outlineWidth}px ${a.outlineStyle} ${a.outlineColor}`)
      .join('\n');
    throw new Error(`WCAG 2.4.13: focus indicator too thin or absent:\n${report}`);
  }

  expect(failing).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern for AAA-targeted projects, design systems, and any team that has globally removed browser default outlines without providing custom focus indicators. Do NOT treat a passing 2px outline width check as full 2.4.13 compliance — the criterion also requires 3:1 contrast between focused and unfocused states, which requires color parsing and contrast ratio computation beyond CSS property checking; pair with a manual color contrast audit of the focus ring. Alternative: For teams targeting only Level AA, the 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured test (Pattern 31, Cycle 32) is the applicable AA test; 2.4.13 is AAA only and should be a "best effort" enhancement. [official]

### Pattern 58 (Cycle 33) — Playwright `ariaSnapshot()` with Partial Template Matching for Dynamic Content

`page.ariaSnapshot()` (stable in Playwright v1.49+) serializes the ARIA accessibility tree as a YAML string. `expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot()` matches using subset/template semantics — the snapshot template is treated as a required structural subset, not an exact full-tree match. This enables stable regression tests for components with dynamic content (timestamps, user names, counts) by asserting the structural ARIA skeleton without asserting the exact dynamic text values. Template variables and regex patterns in the YAML enable flexible matching.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('navigation landmark ARIA structure is stable', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Assert the structural skeleton without pinning to exact link text
  // The "- link" lines use regex-style matching (Playwright ARIA snapshot syntax)
  await expect(page.locator('nav[aria-label="Main navigation"]')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - navigation "Main navigation":
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - link /Home|Dashboard/
        - listitem:
          - link /Products?/
        - listitem:
          - link /About/
  `);
});

test('data table ARIA structure includes column headers and row roles', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/users');

  // Assert table structure without asserting specific row data (which changes)
  await expect(page.locator('table')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - table:
      - rowgroup:
        - row:
          - columnheader "Name"
          - columnheader "Email"
          - columnheader "Role"
          - columnheader "Actions"
      - rowgroup:
        - row /.*/:
          - cell /.*/
          - cell /.*/
          - cell /.*/
          - cell:
            - button /Edit|Delete/
  `);
});

test('capture and review full ARIA snapshot for a new component', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/components/date-picker');

  // During authoring: capture the snapshot to create the initial baseline
  const snapshot = await page.locator('[data-testid="date-picker"]').ariaSnapshot();
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-console
  console.log('ARIA Snapshot baseline:\n', snapshot);

  // After review, paste into toMatchAriaSnapshot to lock it in
  expect(snapshot).toBeTruthy();
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` for ARIA structural regression on navigation landmarks, data tables, complex widgets (date pickers, carousels, menus) where role and name structure is critical but exact text values are dynamic. Do NOT rely on it as a complete accessibility audit — it confirms structure but does not run axe rules, compute contrast, or validate keyboard behavior; it is one layer in a defense-in-depth approach. Alternative: Manual inspection of the ARIA tree in browser DevTools Accessibility panel remains necessary for first-time component authoring; `ariaSnapshot()` is best used after a manual review to lock in the confirmed-correct structure. [official]
