### Pattern 59 (Cycle 33) — WCAG 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose: `autocomplete` Token Audit

WCAG 1.3.5 (Level AA) requires that input fields collecting personal information have `autocomplete` attributes that match the WHATWG-defined autocomplete token taxonomy. This enables password managers, autofill tools, and AT to correctly identify the purpose of form fields regardless of visible label text. Common violations include `autocomplete="true"` (not a valid token), omitting `autocomplete` on personal data fields, using proprietary tokens like `autocomplete="fname"` instead of `"given-name"`, and setting `autocomplete="off"` on fields where user agents should be allowed to autofill.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// WHATWG-valid tokens for personal info fields per WCAG 1.3.5
const VALID_PERSONAL_AUTOCOMPLETE_TOKENS = new Set([
  'name', 'honorific-prefix', 'given-name', 'additional-name', 'family-name', 'honorific-suffix',
  'nickname', 'username', 'new-password', 'current-password', 'one-time-code',
  'organization-title', 'organization', 'street-address', 'address-line1', 'address-line2',
  'address-line3', 'address-level4', 'address-level3', 'address-level2', 'address-level1',
  'country', 'country-name', 'postal-code', 'cc-name', 'cc-given-name', 'cc-additional-name',
  'cc-family-name', 'cc-number', 'cc-exp', 'cc-exp-month', 'cc-exp-year', 'cc-csc', 'cc-type',
  'transaction-currency', 'transaction-amount', 'language', 'bday', 'bday-day', 'bday-month',
  'bday-year', 'sex', 'tel', 'tel-country-code', 'tel-national', 'tel-area-code', 'tel-local',
  'tel-extension', 'impp', 'url', 'photo', 'email',
]);

test('WCAG 1.3.5 — personal info inputs use valid autocomplete tokens', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/profile/edit');

  const violations: { label: string; autocomplete: string }[] = await page.evaluate(
    (validTokens: string[]) => {
      const inputs = Array.from(
        document.querySelectorAll<HTMLInputElement>('input[autocomplete]')
      );
      const validSet = new Set(validTokens);
      return inputs
        .map((el) => ({
          label: el.labels?.[0]?.textContent?.trim() ?? el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? el.name,
          autocomplete: el.autocomplete,
        }))
        .filter(({ autocomplete }) => {
          // Strip "section-*" and "shipping"/"billing" prefixes before token check
          const token = autocomplete.replace(/^(section-\w+ )?(shipping |billing )?/, '').trim();
          return token !== '' && token !== 'off' && !validSet.has(token);
        });
    },
    Array.from(VALID_PERSONAL_AUTOCOMPLETE_TOKENS)
  );

  if (violations.length > 0) {
    const report = violations
      .map(({ label, autocomplete }) => `  "${label}": autocomplete="${autocomplete}"`)
      .join('\n');
    throw new Error(`WCAG 1.3.5: Invalid autocomplete tokens found:\n${report}`);
  }

  expect(violations).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this audit on any form collecting personal, payment, or contact information — especially registration, checkout, profile editing, and account settings forms. Do NOT flag `autocomplete="off"` as a violation unconditionally — it is sometimes legitimately used for OTP fields, CVC fields, or fields where autofill would cause security issues; apply judgment and document exceptions. Alternative: axe-core's `autocomplete-valid` rule covers a subset of this check; use this custom pattern for complete WHATWG taxonomy validation beyond what axe currently checks. [official]

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 33)

163. **[community] `aria-expanded` on a `<button>` that controls a dropdown must be toggled synchronously on click — delaying the state update until after a CSS transition completes causes screen readers to announce the wrong state and users cannot trust the button's announced state**: Many UI libraries animate dropdowns with a CSS `max-height` or `opacity` transition before the menu is fully visible. If `aria-expanded` is only set to `"true"` after the transition ends (via `transitionend`), a screen reader that queries the button's state immediately after a click hears `aria-expanded="false"` while the menu is visually opening. WHY: Developers conflate the "animation complete" event with the semantic state change — the ARIA state must reflect the developer's intent (has the menu been opened?) not the visual state (is the animation done?); the fix is to set `aria-expanded="true"` synchronously on the click event before any animation begins, so AT immediately reflects the correct expanded state. [community]

164. **[community] React `StrictMode` causes axe-core component tests with `jest-axe` to double-invoke effects, which can result in race conditions where the axe scan runs against an intermediate DOM state during a second `useEffect` cleanup-and-rerun cycle, producing false positive violations for missing ARIA attributes**: In React 18 with `StrictMode`, effects are intentionally unmounted and re-mounted in development to surface side effects. If a component sets `aria-expanded`, `aria-selected`, or `aria-controls` in a `useEffect`, the ARIA attribute may be absent during the cleanup phase. Running `axe()` immediately after `render()` without awaiting effects can catch the component in this intermediate state. WHY: Teams scaffold new accessibility tests based on examples that do not account for React StrictMode's double-invocation, and the CI environment differs from local (StrictMode is often disabled in some configs); the fix is to always `await` React's async state flush using `await act(async () => { ... })` or `waitFor` from Testing Library before invoking `axe()`. [community]

165. **[community] `role="tooltip"` elements that are only shown on hover are invisible to touch screen users and mobile screen reader users on iOS who have no hover state — entire tooltip content (often critical instructions or error descriptions) is unreachable**: Tooltips implemented as `role="tooltip"` revealed by `:hover` pseudo-class CSS are fundamentally inaccessible on touch devices because touch interaction does not produce a hover event that persists long enough for the tooltip to be read. iOS VoiceOver and Android TalkBack navigate by swipe, bypassing the hover trigger entirely. WHY: Developers test tooltips on desktop with a mouse and declare them accessible because NVDA on Windows reads them — but the same component on an iPhone is completely silent for VoiceOver users; the fix is to also reveal tooltips on `:focus` and to ensure tooltip content that is essential (form field instructions, button context) is also available as `aria-describedby` content or persistent visible text rather than hidden in a tooltip. [community]

166. **[community] When Playwright's `getByRole()` queries are run against a page with a MutationObserver-driven accessibility tree updater (common in Angular CDK and some Vue accessibility plugins), role queries return stale results because Playwright snapshots the accessibility tree at query time, before the MutationObserver has fired**: Angular CDK's `LiveAnnouncer` and similar utilities use MutationObservers to dynamically update ARIA attributes. When a Playwright test triggers an action and immediately queries `getByRole()`, the ARIA role or name update from the MutationObserver microtask may not yet be reflected. WHY: Teams write `await page.click('#trigger'); const el = page.getByRole('alert')` expecting the alert to be present but the MutationObserver has not run yet — the fix is to add a `waitFor` step: `await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toBeVisible()` before making assertions, giving Playwright's auto-wait mechanism time to observe the DOM update. [community]

167. **[community] `axe-core`'s `color-contrast` rule is silently skipped for text nodes inside SVG elements, even when the SVG is used as an icon with visible text labels — teams using inline SVG charts or icon fonts with SVG fallback get false clean axe reports for contrast violations that are visible to low-vision users**: The axe-core `color-contrast` rule uses CSSOM `getComputedStyle()` to determine foreground and background colors, but SVG `fill` and `stroke` presentation attributes are not always reflected in `getComputedStyle()` in the same way as CSS properties, and axe skips nodes it cannot compute contrast for rather than reporting them as incomplete. A bar chart SVG with light gray axis labels against a white background may have a 1.8:1 contrast ratio that is invisible to axe but fails WCAG 1.4.3. WHY: Teams run axe on their dashboard page, see zero contrast violations, and ship charts with illegible labels — the fix is to also run a dedicated contrast audit on SVG text nodes using `page.evaluate()` to extract `fill` values and manually compute contrast ratios using a WCAG formula, and to use CSS class-based color declarations on SVG text instead of SVG presentation attributes so that axe can read them. [community]

168. **[community] Playwright's `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` assertion fails non-deterministically in CI when the page contains `aria-live` regions that update asynchronously during the snapshot capture — the ARIA tree captured mid-update differs from the expected template, producing intermittent test failures that are hard to reproduce locally**: Live region content (status messages, toasts, loading indicators) updates the accessibility tree dynamically. When `page.ariaSnapshot()` or `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` is called while a live region is mid-update, the captured YAML may include partial content or transient states. WHY: The test runs faster in CI (less DOM rendering overhead) and captures the snapshot before a pending `setTimeout` or `requestAnimationFrame` that populates the live region has fired, producing a tree that differs from the expected template — the fix is to call `await page.waitForFunction(() => document.querySelector('[aria-live]')?.textContent?.trim() !== '')` or use `expect(page.getByRole('status')).toHaveText(/.+/)` before calling `toMatchAriaSnapshot()`, ensuring the live region is settled before the structural snapshot is captured. [community]

| @axe-core/vitest npm package | Official | https://www.npmjs.com/package/@axe-core/vitest | Vitest-native toHaveNoViolations for Vite + Web Component projects |
| axe-core SVG color contrast limitation | Community | https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core/issues/2958 | Why SVG fill-based text evades axe contrast rules; manual audit needed |

## Cycle 34 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 60 (Cycle 34) — WCAG 3.2.6 Consistent Help: Cross-Page Help Mechanism Position Audit

**Description:** WCAG 3.2.6 (Level A, new in WCAG 2.2) requires that help mechanisms — human contact details, live chat, FAQs, chatbots — appear in the same relative order across all pages in a site set. The criterion is triggered only when help is present on multiple pages; if a site has no help mechanism it does not apply. Violations typically appear when a navigation header is implemented differently on marketing pages versus application pages, or when a help widget is injected by a third-party script that renders out-of-DOM-order. Automated testing can verify that a named help landmark (or its ARIA label) occupies a consistent serialized position in the accessibility tree across multiple routes.

```typescript
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

const HELP_ROUTES = ['/home', '/products', '/checkout', '/account/settings'];
const HELP_LANDMARK_LABEL = /help|support|contact us/i;

async function getHelpLandmarkIndex(page: Page): Promise<number> {
  const landmarks = page.getByRole('complementary').or(page.getByRole('navigation'));
  const allLandmarks = await landmarks.all();
  for (let i = 0; i < allLandmarks.length; i++) {
    const label = await allLandmarks[i].getAttribute('aria-label') ?? '';
    if (HELP_LANDMARK_LABEL.test(label)) return i;
  }
  return -1; // help mechanism not found on this page
}

test('WCAG 3.2.6 — help mechanism occupies consistent serialized landmark position', async ({ page }) => {
  const positions: Record<string, number> = {};
  for (const route of HELP_ROUTES) {
    await page.goto(route);
    await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');
    positions[route] = await getHelpLandmarkIndex(page);
  }

  const presentRoutes = Object.entries(positions).filter(([, idx]) => idx >= 0);
  if (presentRoutes.length < 2) return; // criterion only applies when help appears on multiple pages

  const [firstRoute, firstIndex] = presentRoutes[0];
  for (const [route, index] of presentRoutes.slice(1)) {
    expect(index, `Help landmark index on ${route} (${index}) differs from ${firstRoute} (${firstIndex})`).toBe(firstIndex);
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this audit on marketing sites and multi-page web applications that display a persistent help widget, chat launcher, or contact link in the header or footer across routes. Do NOT apply it to single-page apps that use a global layout shell where the help element is literally the same DOM node on every route — the criterion is met trivially in that case. Alternative: manually inspect the serialized DOM order by counting sibling elements before the help node using `page.evaluate()` if landmark-role-based position does not capture your specific help implementation. [official]

### Pattern 61 (Cycle 34) — ARIA Tabs Pattern: Arrow-Key Activation and `tabpanel` Focus Management Test

**Description:** The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide Tabs pattern mandates that Left/Right arrow keys move between tabs (without Tab key), that `Tab` skips the tab list and moves focus to the active `tabpanel`, and that inactive tabs are removed from the tab sequence via `tabindex="-1"`. Teams frequently implement a tab widget that works with Tab key but violates the roving-tabindex contract, causing screen reader users to encounter all tabs in the focus order and miss the required arrow key navigation model. Panels without focusable content must receive `tabindex="0"` so Tab moves focus into them. The test below drives a full keyboard sequence through a tabs widget and asserts each state.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('APG Tabs — roving tabindex and panel focus management', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/components/tabs-demo');
  const tabList = page.getByRole('tablist');
  const tabs = tabList.getByRole('tab');

  // Initially the first tab is selected and focused
  await tabs.first().focus();
  await expect(tabs.first()).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
  await expect(tabs.first()).toHaveAttribute('tabindex', '0');

  // Inactive tabs must not be in tab sequence
  const secondTab = tabs.nth(1);
  await expect(secondTab).toHaveAttribute('tabindex', '-1');

  // Right Arrow moves focus to next tab (roving tabindex model)
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
  await expect(secondTab).toBeFocused();
  await expect(secondTab).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
  await expect(tabs.first()).toHaveAttribute('tabindex', '-1');

  // Tab key moves focus OUT of tablist to the active panel
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  const activePanel = page.getByRole('tabpanel', { name: await secondTab.textContent() ?? '' });
  await expect(activePanel).toBeFocused();

  // End key jumps to last tab (optional but recommended)
  await secondTab.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('End');
  await expect(tabs.last()).toBeFocused();
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this when your tabs widget controls visible panels on the same page — the roving-tabindex + panel-focus model is mandatory per APG for standard tabs. Do NOT apply the Left/Right arrow expectation to a "fake tabs" implementation using `<a>` links with `role="tab"` but no accompanying `tablist` — those behave as links and Tab key navigation is expected; refactor to the correct ARIA roles first. Alternative: Playwright's `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` can capture the tablist/tab/tabpanel hierarchy in a YAML snapshot and catch regressions after refactors. [official]

### Pattern 62 (Cycle 34) — ARIA Combobox with `aria-activedescendant`: Scroll-Into-View and Screen Reader Name Test

**Description:** The ARIA combobox pattern uses `aria-activedescendant` to communicate the focused option to assistive technology while keeping DOM focus on the input. A critical requirement is that the visually "active" option scrolls into view as the user arrow-keys through a long list — browsers do not automatically scroll non-focused elements into view, so this must be done explicitly in the component's keyboard handler. The second common failure is that screen readers will not announce the option if the element referenced by `aria-activedescendant` does not have a computable accessible name (either text content or `aria-label`). This pattern tests both the scroll obligation and the name computation.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('ARIA combobox — activedescendant option is scrolled into view and has accessible name', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/components/combobox-demo');
  const input = page.getByRole('combobox');
  await input.focus();
  await input.fill('a'); // trigger autocomplete
  await expect(page.getByRole('listbox')).toBeVisible();

  // Press Down arrow 10 times to navigate deep into list
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  }

  // Get the currently active descendant ID
  const activeId = await input.getAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
  expect(activeId, 'aria-activedescendant must be set after ArrowDown').toBeTruthy();

  const activeOption = page.locator(`#${activeId}`);

  // Option must be visible in viewport (scrolled into view)
  await expect(activeOption).toBeInViewport();

  // Option must have a computable accessible name
  await expect(activeOption).toHaveRole('option');
  const name = await activeOption.evaluate((el) => el.textContent?.trim() ?? '');
  expect(name.length, 'Active option must have non-empty text content for AT to announce').toBeGreaterThan(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this on any custom combobox, autocomplete, or search-with-suggestions widget that uses `aria-activedescendant`. Do NOT use this test for combobox implementations that move DOM focus into the listbox options directly (some libraries prefer real focus over `aria-activedescendant`) — in that case use `toBeFocused()` on the option element instead. Alternative: Chrome DevTools `$0.computedRole` and `$0.computedName` in console can quickly spot missing names during exploratory testing before writing the automated assertion. [official]

### Pattern 63 (Cycle 34) — Playwright `ariaSnapshot()` `depth` and `mode` Options for Selective Tree Capture (v1.50+)

**Description:** Playwright v1.50 expanded `locator.ariaSnapshot()` with `depth` and `mode` options. The `depth` integer limits how many levels of the accessibility tree are captured, which is essential for testing widgets nested inside complex layouts where the full tree would be hundreds of lines. The `mode` option (`'raw'` vs `'default'`) controls whether hidden nodes are included in the snapshot — `'raw'` exposes the full unfiltered tree including `aria-hidden` content, useful for auditing elements that should be explicitly hidden from AT. Together these options enable surgical ARIA regression testing without brittle full-page snapshot files.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('ariaSnapshot depth option — captures navigation landmark without child noise', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  const nav = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Primary' });

  // Capture only the top 2 levels of the navigation landmark
  const shallowSnapshot = await nav.ariaSnapshot({ depth: 2 });

  // Shallow snapshot must list top-level links but not sub-menu items
  expect(shallowSnapshot).toContain('- link "Home"');
  expect(shallowSnapshot).toContain('- link "Products"');
  // Sub-menu items (depth 3+) should not appear in a depth-2 capture
  expect(shallowSnapshot).not.toContain('Sub-category');
});

test('ariaSnapshot mode raw — confirms aria-hidden elements are excluded from default tree', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/icon-buttons-demo');
  const toolbar = page.getByRole('toolbar');

  const rawSnapshot = await toolbar.ariaSnapshot({ mode: 'raw' });
  const defaultSnapshot = await toolbar.ariaSnapshot();

  // Decorative icon spans marked aria-hidden should appear in raw but not default
  expect(rawSnapshot).toContain('hidden: true');
  expect(defaultSnapshot).not.toContain('hidden: true');
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `depth` when the component under test has known depth boundaries and you want to isolate a specific layer of the ARIA tree. Use `mode: 'raw'` specifically to audit whether decorative or redundant elements are properly hidden from AT — do not use it as the default snapshot mode or your snapshots will contain hidden noise that makes maintenance painful. Do NOT rely on shallow snapshots for end-to-end navigation tests where you need to verify the entire landmark structure. Alternative: the `boxes` option (v1.50) adds `[box=x,y,width,height]` to each node for AI-assisted visual-accessibility correlation. [official]

### Pattern 64 (Cycle 34) — WCAG 3.3.9 Accessible Authentication (Enhanced / AAA): No Cognitive Function Test at Any Step

**Description:** WCAG 3.3.9 (Level AAA, new in WCAG 2.2) extends the Level AA criterion 3.3.8 by removing the "object recognition" and "personal content" exceptions — at AAA, no authentication step may require any cognitive function test whatsoever. This means CAPTCHA using image selection, audio challenges, or puzzle dragging must be removed entirely (not just supplemented). Teams pursuing AAA conformance must audit every authentication step including password reset, two-factor verification, email confirmation flows, and re-authentication prompts for session expiry. This pattern uses Playwright to assert that no CAPTCHA widgets are injected in the authentication flow.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const CAPTCHA_SELECTORS = [
  '[class*="captcha"]',
  '[id*="captcha"]',
  'iframe[src*="recaptcha"]',
  'iframe[src*="hcaptcha"]',
  'iframe[src*="turnstile"]',
  '[data-sitekey]',
];

async function detectCaptchaPresence(page: import('@playwright/test').Page): Promise<string[]> {
  const found: string[] = [];
  for (const selector of CAPTCHA_SELECTORS) {
    const count = await page.locator(selector).count();
    if (count > 0) found.push(selector);
  }
  return found;
}

test('WCAG 3.3.9 AAA — no CAPTCHA cognitive function test on login page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  const captchas = await detectCaptchaPresence(page);
  expect(captchas, `CAPTCHA detected (violates WCAG 3.3.9 AAA): ${captchas.join(', ')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});

test('WCAG 3.3.9 AAA — no CAPTCHA cognitive function test on password reset', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/forgot-password');
  const captchas = await detectCaptchaPresence(page);
  expect(captchas, `CAPTCHA detected on reset flow: ${captchas.join(', ')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this for AAA-targeted products (government, healthcare, enterprise accessibility compliance) where full removal of cognitive function tests is required. Do NOT use this to block Level AA compliance testing — 3.3.8 AA allows CAPTCHA if an alternative method without a cognitive test is also provided; this pattern is exclusively for verifying that the stricter AAA bar is met. Alternative: for Level AA verification, test that a non-CAPTCHA path (e.g., password manager autofill, passkey, email magic link) is present and operational alongside any CAPTCHA that exists. [official]

### Pattern 65 (Cycle 34) — Playwright `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` `/children: equal` for Strict List Ordering (v1.52+)

**Description:** Playwright v1.52 introduced the `/children: equal` YAML property for `toMatchAriaSnapshot()`, which switches the default partial-matching behaviour to an exact-children assertion — the element must have exactly those children, in that order, with no additional nodes. This is critical for testing ordered lists, navigation menus, and tab lists where an extra or missing item is a regression. Without `/children: equal`, the default snapshot matching is "subset" — extra children silently pass. Strict matching catches issues like a navigation item being conditionally rendered for wrong user roles, or a tab being added without updating test expectations.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('ariaSnapshot strict children — primary nav has exactly the expected links', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  const nav = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Primary' });

  await expect(nav).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - navigation "Primary":
      /children: equal
      - link "Home"
      - link "Products"
      - link "Solutions"
      - link "Pricing"
      - link "Contact"
  `);
});

test('ariaSnapshot strict children — tablist contains exactly four tabs after load', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  const tabList = page.getByRole('tablist');

  await expect(tabList).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - tablist:
      /children: equal
      - tab "Overview" [selected]
      - tab "Analytics"
      - tab "Reports"
      - tab "Settings"
  `);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `/children: equal` for stable, non-dynamic UI components where the complete child set is known and unexpected additions or removals are regressions. Do NOT use it on components that render differently for different user permissions or feature flags unless you have separate test fixtures per variant — strict matching will fail legitimately when conditional rendering is intentional. Alternative: use the default partial match (omit `/children: equal`) during early development and add strict matching once the component's content model is stabilised. [official]

### Pattern 66 (Cycle 34) — axe-core `wcag22aa` Tag: Running Full WCAG 2.2 AA Rule Set in Playwright Tests

**Description:** Many teams run axe-core with `withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])` but omit `'wcag22aa'`, leaving the new WCAG 2.2 AA rules (target-size, focus-not-obscured, dragging-movements, accessible-authentication, redundant-entry) unevaluated. The `wcag22aa` tag was added in axe-core 4.7 and is required to get automated coverage of 2.2 AA success criteria. Note that some WCAG 2.2 rules (like `target-size`) are off by default and must be enabled via `enableRules()`. This pattern shows the correct full-coverage tag set and demonstrates how to explicitly enable off-by-default WCAG 2.2 rules.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('axe-core full WCAG 2.2 AA coverage including off-by-default rules', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    // Include all WCAG 2.x AA tags — wcag22aa is required for 2.2 new criteria
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag22aa'])
    // target-size is off by default in axe-core; must be explicitly enabled
    .enableRules(['target-size'])
    .analyze();

  if (results.violations.length > 0) {
    await testInfo.attach('axe-violations', {
      body: JSON.stringify(results.violations, null, 2),
      contentType: 'application/json',
    });
  }

  expect(
    results.violations,
    `WCAG 2.2 AA violations:\n${results.violations.map((v) => `  [${v.id}] ${v.description}`).join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `wcag22aa` tag for any project that targets WCAG 2.2 AA conformance — this is the current baseline for most public-sector and enterprise accessibility requirements as of 2024. Do NOT assume that adding `wcag22aa` alone provides complete 2.2 coverage — some criteria (dragging movements, consistent help, redundant entry) require manual testing or custom Playwright scripts beyond what axe-core rules cover. Alternative: run the expanded tag set on a nightly schedule rather than every PR to balance CI speed with comprehensive rule coverage. [official]

### Pattern 67 (Cycle 34) — ARIA Menu Button Pattern: `aria-haspopup="menu"` and Focus-on-First-Item Test

**Description:** The APG Menu Button pattern specifies that the button must carry `aria-haspopup="menu"` (not `"true"` or `"listbox"`), must set `aria-expanded` to match the open/closed state, and that pressing Enter, Space, or Down Arrow must open the menu and move DOM focus to the first menu item. A common failure is opening the menu visually but leaving focus on the button, causing screen readers to announce a stale button state. A second common failure is using `aria-haspopup="listbox"` for a `role="menu"` — these are different ARIA roles with different keyboard contracts and screen reader announcements.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('APG Menu Button — aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, and focus-on-first-item', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/components/menu-button-demo');
  const menuButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: /actions|options|more/i });

  // Initial state: aria-haspopup must be "menu" and aria-expanded false
  await expect(menuButton).toHaveAttribute('aria-haspopup', 'menu');
  await expect(menuButton).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

  // Open menu via Enter key
  await menuButton.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

  // aria-expanded must switch to true synchronously
  await expect(menuButton).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

  // First menu item must receive DOM focus
  const menu = page.getByRole('menu');
  await expect(menu).toBeVisible();
  const firstItem = menu.getByRole('menuitem').first();
  await expect(firstItem).toBeFocused();

  // Escape must close menu and return focus to button
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(menuButton).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  await expect(menu).toBeHidden();
  await expect(menuButton).toBeFocused();
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this for any button that opens a `role="menu"` or `role="menubar"` — dropdown menus, context menus, action menus in data tables. Do NOT apply this pattern to a `<select>` replacement that uses `role="listbox"` — the `aria-haspopup` value for a listbox popup is `"listbox"` and the keyboard contract differs (Enter selects vs opens). Alternative: use `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` to capture the entire menu structure after open and catch regressions in menu item count or grouping. [official]

---

### Pattern 68 (Cycle 34) — `jest-axe` v10 with `axe-core` 4.10: Configuring `runOnly` for WCAG 2.2

**Description:** jest-axe v10 (released 2025) bundles axe-core 4.10, which includes updated WCAG 2.2 rule IDs. The API for configuring which rules run in jest-axe uses `configureAxe({ rules: [...] })` or the `options` parameter of `axe()`. Teams upgrading from jest-axe v8/v9 may have hardcoded old rule IDs or omitted the `wcag22aa` runOnly tags because their version of axe-core predated them. This pattern demonstrates the correct v10 configuration for component-level accessibility tests, including disabling inapplicable structural rules that produce noise when scanning isolated components outside a full-page context.

```typescript
import { render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { axe, toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';
import { configureAxe } from 'jest-axe';
import { act } from 'react';
import { SearchCombobox } from './SearchCombobox';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

const axeWithConfig = configureAxe({
  rules: {
    // Disable landmark rules — isolated component has no page-level landmark context
    region: { enabled: false },
    'landmark-one-main': { enabled: false },
    'page-has-heading-one': { enabled: false },
    // Enable WCAG 2.2 target-size rule (off by default in axe-core)
    'target-size': { enabled: true },
  },
  runOnly: {
    type: 'tag',
    values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'],
  },
});

test('SearchCombobox has no WCAG 2.2 AA violations', async () => {
  const { container } = render(<SearchCombobox placeholder="Search products" />);

  // Await React effects before running axe
  await act(async () => {
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0));
  });

  const results = await axeWithConfig(container);
  expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `configureAxe` for shared test setup when you have many component tests to avoid repeating configuration in every test file — put it in a `setupTests.ts` and export a pre-configured `axe` instance. Do NOT suppress the `landmark-one-main` rule globally without documenting why — it should only be disabled for unit/component tests, not integration or full-page tests. Alternative: use `@axe-core/vitest` for Vite-based projects where jest-axe does not integrate cleanly with Vitest's test runner. [official]

---

### Pattern 69 (Cycle 34) — Playwright `toHaveAccessibleName()` and `toHaveAccessibleDescription()` for Icon-Only Buttons (v1.51+)

**Description:** Icon buttons (buttons with only an SVG or icon font glyph, no visible text) are one of the most common accessibility failures — without an accessible name, screen readers announce "button" with no context. Playwright v1.51 introduced `toHaveAccessibleName()` and `toHaveAccessibleDescription()` as first-class assertions that check the computed name from the accessibility tree, accounting for `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `title`, and `alt` text resolution in the correct priority order. This replaces fragile attribute-level checks (`toHaveAttribute('aria-label', ...)`) which do not verify that the name is actually computable by AT.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('icon-only toolbar buttons all have computable accessible names', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/editor');
  const toolbar = page.getByRole('toolbar', { name: 'Text formatting' });
  const buttons = toolbar.getByRole('button');
  const count = await buttons.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const button = buttons.nth(i);
    // toHaveAccessibleName checks the full computed name from the AT perspective
    await expect(button).toHaveAccessibleName(/.+/);
  }
});

test('search input has accessible name AND description', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');
  const searchInput = page.getByRole('searchbox');

  // Name — must have a meaningful label
  await expect(searchInput).toHaveAccessibleName(/search/i);

  // Description — aria-describedby hint text must be non-empty
  await expect(searchInput).toHaveAccessibleDescription(/.+/);
});

test('close button in modal has specific accessible name including context', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/demo/modal');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open dialog' }).click();
  const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
  const closeButton = dialog.getByRole('button', { name: /close/i });

  // Verify the close button name includes the dialog title for context
  await expect(closeButton).toHaveAccessibleName(/close/i);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `toHaveAccessibleName()` over `toHaveAttribute('aria-label', ...)` for all accessible name assertions because it validates the computed result — a misspelled `aria-labelledby` reference returns an empty name even though the attribute exists. Do NOT use `/.+/` regex as the only assertion in production test suites — it only checks "non-empty" and will pass `aria-label=" "` (whitespace); use specific regex or string expectations where the expected name is known. Alternative: `page.accessibility.snapshot()` (deprecated) also captures computed names, but prefer the new assertions which are stable and semantically correct. [official]

---

### Pattern 70 (Cycle 34) — WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum / AA): Sticky Header Overlap Audit

**Description:** WCAG 2.4.11 (Level AA, new in WCAG 2.2) requires that a component receiving keyboard focus is not entirely hidden by author-created sticky or fixed content such as sticky headers, cookie banners, chat widgets, or bottom navigation bars. The criterion allows partial obscuring — the focused element must have at least some portion visible. Automated testing can detect full obscuration by comparing the focused element's bounding box against the union of all fixed/sticky elements' bounding boxes. This pattern is the AA-level complement to pattern 52 (WCAG 2.4.12 Full Visibility / AAA).

```typescript
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

async function getFocusedElementBoundingBox(page: Page) {
  return page.evaluate(() => {
    const el = document.activeElement;
    if (!el) return null;
    const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    return { top: rect.top, bottom: rect.bottom, left: rect.left, right: rect.right };
  });
}

async function getStickyObstructions(page: Page) {
  return page.evaluate(() => {
    const sticky = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('*')).filter((el) => {
      const s = getComputedStyle(el);
      return s.position === 'fixed' || s.position === 'sticky';
    });
    return sticky.map((el) => {
      const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      return { top: r.top, bottom: r.bottom, left: r.left, right: r.right };
    });
  });
}

function isCompletelyObscured(
  focused: { top: number; bottom: number; left: number; right: number },
  obstructions: Array<{ top: number; bottom: number; left: number; right: number }>
): boolean {
  return obstructions.some(
    (o) =>
      o.top <= focused.top &&
      o.bottom >= focused.bottom &&
      o.left <= focused.left &&
      o.right >= focused.right
  );
}

test('WCAG 2.4.11 — keyboard focus is not entirely obscured by sticky elements', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/long-form-page');
  const focusableSelectors = ['a[href]', 'button:not([disabled])', 'input:not([disabled])', 'select', '[tabindex="0"]'];
  const focusables = await page.locator(focusableSelectors.join(', ')).all();

  for (const el of focusables.slice(0, 20)) { // sample first 20
    await el.focus();
    const focused = await getFocusedElementBoundingBox(page);
    if (!focused) continue;
    const obstructions = await getStickyObstructions(page);
    const obscured = isCompletelyObscured(focused, obstructions);
    const label = await el.evaluate((e) => e.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? e.textContent?.trim() ?? e.tagName);
    expect(obscured, `WCAG 2.4.11: Element "${label}" is completely obscured by a sticky element`).toBe(false);
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this on pages with sticky headers, sticky footers, cookie consent banners, or chat widgets — these are the most common sources of 2.4.11 violations. Do NOT report partial obscuration as a WCAG 2.4.11 failure — the AA criterion only prohibits complete concealment; use the stricter WCAG 2.4.12 test (pattern 52) if your target is AAA conformance. Alternative: `page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getBoundingClientRect())` paired with a visual screenshot of the focused state gives strong evidence for a bug report when a violation is found. [official]

---

### Pattern 71 (Cycle 34) — Playwright `ariaSnapshot()` `boxes` Option for Visual-Accessibility Correlation (v1.50+)

**Description:** Playwright v1.50 added a `boxes` option to `locator.ariaSnapshot()` that appends each node's bounding box as `[box=x,y,width,height]` to the YAML output. This enables cross-referencing the accessibility tree with the visual layout — a node with `[box=0,0,0,0]` has zero dimensions and is likely invisible or off-screen, which can reveal ghost elements that appear in the AT tree but have no visual presence (confusing screen reader users who hear elements that do not visually exist). It also helps identify when an ARIA label is attached to the wrong element based on positional analysis.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('ariaSnapshot boxes — no interactive nodes with zero bounding box in main content', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  const main = page.getByRole('main');
  const snapshotWithBoxes = await main.ariaSnapshot({ boxes: true });

  // Parse any interactive nodes that have [box=0,0,0,0] (zero-size ghost elements)
  const zeroBoxPattern = /- (?:button|link|textbox|combobox|checkbox|radio)[^[\n]*\[box=0,0,0,0\]/g;
  const zeroBoxMatches = snapshotWithBoxes.match(zeroBoxPattern) ?? [];

  expect(
    zeroBoxMatches,
    `Zero-dimension interactive nodes found in AT tree (ghost elements):\n${zeroBoxMatches.join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});

test('ariaSnapshot boxes — decorative images have no AT presence (zero box or absent)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/marketing/hero');
  const hero = page.getByRole('banner');
  const snapshot = await hero.ariaSnapshot({ boxes: true });

  // Decorative images (role=img without label) should either not appear or have non-interactive zero box
  const unlabelledImages = snapshot.match(/- img\s*\[box=\d+,\d+,\d+,\d+\]/g) ?? [];
  expect(
    unlabelledImages,
    `Decorative images appear in AT tree without accessible name — add aria-hidden="true" or alt="":\n${unlabelledImages.join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use the `boxes` option during debugging sessions and audit runs where you need to correlate ARIA tree entries with visual layout — particularly useful for finding ghost elements, off-screen modals that are pre-rendered but should be `aria-hidden`, and misplaced labels. Do NOT include box coordinates in committed snapshot files used for regression testing — they will produce constant false failures as the page layout shifts with viewport changes; use `boxes` only for ad-hoc auditing, not persistent `.aria.yml` snapshot files. Alternative: Playwright's `screenshot()` combined with `page.accessibility.snapshot()` can provide similar correlation manually, but the `boxes` option integrates this directly into the ARIA output. [official]

---

### Pattern 72 (Cycle 34) — ARIA `role="status"` and `role="alert"` Live Region Assertion Test

**Description:** ARIA live regions are one of the most frequently misused ARIA features. `role="alert"` must be reserved for time-sensitive, disruptive messages (errors, warnings) because it announces with `aria-live="assertive"` and interrupts any currently-speaking content. `role="status"` is for polite status updates (save confirmations, search result counts) and uses `aria-live="polite"`. A common mistake is using `role="alert"` for every status message — this causes constant interruptions for screen reader users. Another failure is creating alert regions dynamically and then immediately injecting text, before AT has registered the live region; AT must observe the region in the DOM before content is added. This pattern tests both correct role usage and the injection timing contract.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('status messages use role="status" not role="alert" for non-critical feedback', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/todos');

  // Save action — should produce a polite status update, not an assertive alert
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }).click();

  const statusRegion = page.getByRole('status');
  const alertRegion = page.getByRole('alert');

  await expect(statusRegion).toBeVisible();
  await expect(statusRegion).toContainText(/saved|success/i);

  // Alert region must NOT fire for a non-critical save confirmation
  await expect(alertRegion).toBeHidden();
});

test('error messages use role="alert" for critical validation failures', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Submit with empty required fields — must produce an assertive alert
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place Order' }).click();

  const alertRegion = page.getByRole('alert');
  await expect(alertRegion).toBeVisible();
  await expect(alertRegion).toContainText(/error|required|invalid/i);
});

test('live region is present in DOM before content is injected', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');

  // The live region for search results count must exist before the search is performed
  const resultsStatus = page.getByRole('status', { name: /results/i });
  await expect(resultsStatus).toBeAttached(); // in DOM even when empty

  await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill('accessibility');
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

  await expect(resultsStatus).toContainText(/\d+ result/i);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `role="status"` for all non-critical asynchronous feedback (form saves, filter counts, loading completion) and reserve `role="alert"` for errors, warnings, and time-sensitive messages that demand immediate attention. Do NOT toggle a live region's `aria-live` attribute dynamically to switch between polite and assertive — AT may not re-register the changed property; use two separate pre-rendered live regions if you need both polite and assertive channels. Alternative: `aria-atomic="true"` on the region element ensures AT announces the entire region content on any change, not just the changed text node — use this when partial updates would confuse context. [official]

---

### Pattern 73 (Cycle 34) — axe-core Custom Rule: Verifying `aria-describedby` Reference Integrity

**Description:** The axe-core built-in rule `aria-valid-attr-value` checks that ARIA attributes have syntactically valid values but does not verify that `aria-describedby` references actually exist in the DOM as reachable elements. A component may set `aria-describedby="hint-text-123"` on an input but if `id="hint-text-123"` is inside a `display: none` container or is not in the same shadow root, the description is silently lost. This pattern implements a custom Playwright-based audit that verifies each `aria-describedby` reference resolves to a non-hidden, non-empty element.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface DescribedByViolation {
  inputLabel: string;
  describedById: string;
  reason: string;
}

async function auditAriaDescribedBy(page: import('@playwright/test').Page): Promise<DescribedByViolation[]> {
  return page.evaluate((): DescribedByViolation[] => {
    const violations: DescribedByViolation[] = [];
    const elements = document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[aria-describedby]');

    elements.forEach((el) => {
      const ids = (el.getAttribute('aria-describedby') ?? '').split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
      const label =
        el.getAttribute('aria-label') ??
        document.querySelector(`[for="${el.id}"]`)?.textContent?.trim() ??
        el.tagName;

      ids.forEach((id) => {
        const target = document.getElementById(id);
        if (!target) {
          violations.push({ inputLabel: label, describedById: id, reason: 'Element not found in DOM' });
          return;
        }
        const style = getComputedStyle(target);
        if (style.display === 'none' || style.visibility === 'hidden') {
          violations.push({ inputLabel: label, describedById: id, reason: 'Target element is hidden (display:none or visibility:hidden)' });
          return;
        }
        if ((target.textContent?.trim() ?? '').length === 0) {
          violations.push({ inputLabel: label, describedById: id, reason: 'Target element is empty — no description text' });
        }
      });
    });

    return violations;
  });
}

test('aria-describedby references resolve to visible, non-empty elements', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/registration');
  const violations = await auditAriaDescribedBy(page);

  expect(
    violations,
    `aria-describedby integrity failures:\n${violations.map((v) => `  "${v.inputLabel}" → #${v.describedById}: ${v.reason}`).join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this audit on forms with hint text, error messages, and instructional descriptions to catch broken `aria-describedby` wiring that axe-core's built-in rules miss. Do NOT flag `aria-describedby` targets that are `aria-hidden="true"` as violations automatically — some tooltip implementations intentionally hide the description from the accessibility tree and rely on the value being a static ID that browsers resolve; validate intent with the component owner. Alternative: axe-core's `aria-valid-attr-value` catches broken ID references in some cases, but it does not check for hidden or empty targets — this custom audit fills that gap. [community]

---

### Pattern 74 (Cycle 34) — ARIA `role="feed"` Keyboard Navigation Test for Infinite-Scroll Content

**Description:** The WAI-ARIA `role="feed"` is designed for infinite-scroll content regions (news feeds, social timelines, article lists) and gives screen reader users a dedicated keyboard interaction model. Each article inside the feed must have `role="article"`, and the feed keyboard contract requires that Page Down / Page Up move between articles while Tab exits the feed. Without `role="feed"`, screen reader users of infinite-scroll lists must Tab through every interactive element inside each article, making navigation impractical. A common failure is implementing a visual infinite-scroll with no ARIA feed semantics at all, or adding `role="feed"` without the corresponding `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset` attributes on articles when the total count is known.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('role="feed" — articles have correct structure and aria-setsize/posinset when count is known', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/timeline');

  const feed = page.getByRole('feed');
  await expect(feed).toBeVisible();

  // Feed must have an accessible label
  const feedLabel = await feed.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? await feed.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
  expect(feedLabel, 'role="feed" must have an accessible label via aria-label or aria-labelledby').toBeTruthy();

  const articles = feed.getByRole('article');
  const count = await articles.count();
  expect(count, 'Feed must contain at least one article').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Each article should have aria-posinset for position in feed
  const firstArticle = articles.first();
  const posinset = await firstArticle.getAttribute('aria-posinset');
  expect(posinset, 'Articles must have aria-posinset when position is known').toBe('1');

  // If total count is known, aria-setsize should be set (not -1)
  const setsize = await firstArticle.getAttribute('aria-setsize');
  if (setsize && setsize !== '-1') {
    expect(Number(setsize), 'aria-setsize must be a positive integer when total is known').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  }

  // Articles must have accessible names (for screen reader announcement context)
  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 5); i++) {
    await expect(articles.nth(i)).toHaveAccessibleName(/.+/);
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `role="feed"` for any infinite-scroll or lazy-loading content region where items are conceptually "articles" or discrete content units — social feeds, news streams, search results pages that load more on scroll. Do NOT use `role="feed"` for paginated lists with explicit page controls — use a `role="list"` with `role="listitem"` and a pagination landmark instead, as `role="feed"` semantics are specifically for append-only or infinite content. Alternative: if the total item count changes dynamically during the session, set `aria-setsize="-1"` to indicate an unknown size — do not try to keep it in sync with a changing count, as out-of-sync values are worse than `-1`. [official]

---

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 34)

169. **[community] React portals break `aria-controls` and `aria-owns` ID references when the controlled element is rendered into a portal outside the component tree — the IDs exist in the DOM but axe-core fails to resolve them as valid references, and screen readers on some browsers also fail to follow the reference across portal boundaries**: React portals render children into a different DOM node than the component tree, often `document.body`. When a component inside `div#app` sets `aria-controls="modal-content-123"` and the modal is rendered into `div#portal-root` (a sibling of `div#app`), the ARIA cross-reference spans DOM subtrees. Some AT implementations resolve ARIA IDREF attributes document-wide and handle this correctly, but axe-core's internal DOM traversal can flag these as broken references in certain configurations. WHY: Developers assume `id` uniqueness in the document is sufficient for ARIA IDREF resolution — which is true per spec — but the practical implementation varies; the fix is to ensure both elements are within the same shadow root (or both in the light DOM) and to write integration tests that assert the AT-visible relationship using Playwright's `getByRole` + `aria-controls` content check rather than relying on axe-core alone to validate portal-spanning references. [community]

170. **[community] `aria-live="polite"` regions in Next.js App Router pages fail to announce route change content to NVDA + Chrome because the region is unmounted and remounted during client-side navigation, causing AT to lose registration of the live region and miss the first update after navigation**: Next.js App Router performs partial page hydration where shared layout components are preserved across navigations, but page-specific components are unmounted and remounted. If a `role="status"` live region is placed inside the page component rather than the shared layout, it is unmounted and remounted on every navigation. AT (specifically NVDA and VoiceOver) must observe a live region in the DOM and then observe a text change — it cannot retroactively announce content that was injected at mount time. WHY: Developers test live regions by directly loading the target page and see announcements work, but during actual navigation the region is new and AT has not yet registered it; the fix is to hoist route-change announcement live regions into the root layout component so they persist across navigations, or use a route-change hook that delays the status message injection by one tick after the region is mounted. [community]

171. **[community] `focus-visible` CSS pseudo-class behaves differently than expected on iOS Safari 17+ — custom focus styles declared with `:focus-visible` are not applied when a user taps interactive elements on touch screen, causing keyboard-focused users who connected an external keyboard to see the custom focus style but touch users to see the browser's native focus ring or nothing**: iOS Safari 17 implemented `:focus-visible` with the "keyboard modality" heuristic, meaning elements only get the `:focus-visible` state when focus arrives via keyboard input, not pointer/touch. If a developer replaces `:focus` with `:focus-visible` and uses `outline: none` on `:focus`, touch users see no focus indicator at all, which violates WCAG 2.4.7 on touch devices with external keyboard support or switch access. WHY: Teams test `:focus-visible` on desktop Chrome (where it works correctly) and do not test on iPad with Magic Keyboard or iPhone with switch control — the discrepancy goes undetected; the fix is to add `:focus:not(:focus-visible)` styles as a fallback for touch/pointer focus contexts, or to keep a subtle `:focus` style as the base and enhance it with `:focus-visible`. [community]

172. **[community] When using `@testing-library/user-event` v14 with `jest-axe`, the axe scan runs synchronously after user interactions that trigger async state updates — the DOM may be in a transitional state when axe runs, producing both false positives and false negatives**: `userEvent.click()` in v14 fires all pointer events, synthesizes focus changes, and fires keyboard events in a microtask queue. If `axe()` is called immediately after `await userEvent.click()`, the React state updates triggered by those events may not yet be flushed to the DOM. An `aria-expanded` toggle on a dropdown or an error message added in a `useEffect` may not be visible to axe. WHY: v14 changed from v13's synchronous event model to an async queue, and many team test templates were written for v13 without updating the axe timing; the fix is to always await `waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible())` or similar DOM assertion before invoking axe, ensuring all pending state has been committed to the DOM. [community]

173. **[community] Playwright `getByRole('dialog')` returns zero matches for a modal that is visually open when the dialog element uses `visibility: hidden` on its backdrop and the content inside has `visibility: visible` — Playwright's accessibility tree computation treats the modal content as hidden because it inherits `visibility` from the backdrop ancestor**: Some modal implementations position a transparent overlay with `visibility: hidden` and then use `visibility: visible` on the inner dialog content to show it above the overlay. The CSS cascade means the dialog's `role="dialog"` element itself has `visibility: hidden` from an ancestor, and Playwright's AT-based locators (which respect the accessibility tree) will not find it by role even though it is visually rendered. WHY: Developers visually inspect the modal in DevTools and see it, then write `getByRole('dialog')` expecting it to work — but the test fails because AT locators are driven by the computed accessibility tree, not visual rendering; the fix is to apply `visibility: hidden` only to the backdrop element (a sibling of the dialog, not an ancestor) or to use `display: none` / `pointer-events: none` techniques instead of `visibility` toggling on ancestral elements. [community]
