### Pattern 75 (Cycle 35) — ARIA Tree View Full Keyboard Contract Test

**Description:** The ARIA tree view pattern (`role="tree"`) has a complex keyboard contract that differs from standard list navigation. Tree items use roving `tabindex` or `aria-activedescendant`, arrow keys navigate hierarchically (Right to expand or enter child, Left to collapse or move to parent), Home and End jump to first and last nodes, and type-ahead search moves focus to matching items. Many implementations only test Tab/Enter navigation and miss the arrow-key traversal contract entirely, leaving keyboard-only users unable to navigate the hierarchy efficiently. Parent nodes must carry `aria-expanded="true"/"false"` while leaf nodes must omit the attribute entirely. When `aria-multiselectable="true"` is set on the tree, Space toggles selection while arrow keys only move focus without changing selection.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('tree view — full keyboard navigation contract', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/file-explorer');

  const tree = page.getByRole('tree');
  await expect(tree).toBeVisible();
  await expect(tree).toHaveAttribute(
    /^aria-(label|labelledby)$/,
    /.+/
  );

  // Focus the tree and verify roving tabindex: only one treeitem is tabbable
  await tree.focus();
  const allTreeItems = tree.locator('[role="treeitem"]');
  const tabbableCount = await allTreeItems.evaluateAll(
    (items) => items.filter((el) => (el as HTMLElement).tabIndex === 0).length
  );
  expect(tabbableCount, 'Exactly one treeitem should have tabIndex=0 (roving tabindex)').toBe(1);

  // Arrow Down moves focus to next visible treeitem
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  const firstItem = allTreeItems.first();
  await expect(firstItem).toBeFocused();

  // Parent nodes must have aria-expanded; leaf nodes must NOT
  const parentNode = tree.locator('[role="treeitem"][aria-expanded]').first();
  const expandedVal = await parentNode.getAttribute('aria-expanded');
  expect(['true', 'false']).toContain(expandedVal);

  // Right arrow on a collapsed parent expands it
  await parentNode.focus();
  const wasExpanded = (await parentNode.getAttribute('aria-expanded')) === 'true';
  if (!wasExpanded) {
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    await expect(parentNode).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
  }

  // Left arrow on an expanded parent collapses it
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft');
  await expect(parentNode).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

  // End key moves to last visible treeitem
  await page.keyboard.press('End');
  const lastItem = allTreeItems.last();
  await expect(lastItem).toBeFocused();
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this full keyboard contract test for any file tree, navigation hierarchy, or structured menu rendered with `role="tree"`. Do NOT apply the tree keyboard contract to flat menus (`role="menu"`) or grouped lists (`role="listbox"`) — these have their own keyboard contracts (Up/Down only, no expand/collapse semantics). Alternative: if your tree uses `aria-activedescendant` instead of roving tabindex, the tree element itself stays focused and you must assert `aria-activedescendant` changes on `ArrowDown/Up` instead of asserting `toBeFocused()` on individual items. [official]

---

### Pattern 76 (Cycle 35) — ARIA Carousel Autoplay Pause and Slide Semantics Test

**Description:** The ARIA APG carousel pattern requires that auto-rotating carousels stop rotation whenever keyboard focus enters the carousel or when the mouse hovers over any carousel content. This is a WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide) compliance requirement — users with cognitive disabilities, motor disabilities, or those using screen magnifiers need the content to be stable while they interact. Each slide must carry `role="group"` and `aria-roledescription="slide"`, the carousel container must have `role="region"` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"` and an accessible label, and the rotation control button must update its accessible name dynamically to reflect its current state ("Stop slide rotation" vs "Start slide rotation"). Testing must verify both the semantic structure and the pause-on-focus behavior.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('carousel — semantic structure, autoplay pause, slide labeling', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/homepage');

  const carousel = page.locator('[aria-roledescription="carousel"]');
  await expect(carousel).toBeVisible();

  // Carousel must be a region with an accessible name
  await expect(carousel).toHaveAttribute('role', 'region');
  const carouselLabel =
    (await carousel.getAttribute('aria-label')) ??
    (await carousel.getAttribute('aria-labelledby'));
  expect(carouselLabel, 'Carousel region must have an accessible label').toBeTruthy();

  // Slides must have aria-roledescription="slide" and an accessible label
  const slides = carousel.locator('[aria-roledescription="slide"]');
  const slideCount = await slides.count();
  expect(slideCount, 'Carousel must contain at least one slide').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(slideCount, 3); i++) {
    const slideLabel =
      (await slides.nth(i).getAttribute('aria-label')) ??
      (await slides.nth(i).getAttribute('aria-labelledby'));
    expect(slideLabel, `Slide ${i + 1} must have an accessible label`).toBeTruthy();
  }

  // Rotation control must exist and have a descriptive accessible name
  const rotationBtn = carousel.getByRole('button', { name: /slide rotation/i });
  await expect(rotationBtn, 'Rotation control button must be present').toBeVisible();

  // Keyboard focus must pause auto-rotation
  await rotationBtn.focus();
  const initialSlide = await slides.first().getAttribute('aria-label');
  await page.waitForTimeout(2500); // Wait longer than typical rotation interval
  const slideAfterFocus = await slides.first().getAttribute('aria-label');
  expect(slideAfterFocus, 'Auto-rotation must pause when keyboard focus is in carousel').toBe(initialSlide);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test for any carousel with auto-play functionality — product image carousels, hero banners, testimonial sliders. Do NOT use `aria-roledescription` for non-carousel tab-panel widgets even if they visually resemble a carousel; use `role="tablist"` and `role="tabpanel"` with standard tab keyboard interactions for explicitly tab-based widgets. Alternative: if the carousel does not auto-rotate at all (user-controlled only), you can skip the pause-on-focus assertion but must still verify the slide/carousel semantic structure and that previous/next buttons have descriptive accessible names. [official]

---

### Pattern 77 (Cycle 35) — ARIA Grid Full Keyboard Navigation Test (Data Grid vs. Layout Grid)

**Description:** ARIA grids come in two forms with different keyboard expectations: data grids (tabular data with row/cell navigation) and layout grids (arrangement of interactive elements where cells can contain multiple focusable items). In a data grid, arrow keys move focus between cells one at a time, Ctrl+Home/End move to the first/last cell, and Enter activates the focused cell for editing while Escape exits edit mode. Layout grids allow Tab to cycle through focusable elements within a cell. When cells span multiple rows or columns, `aria-rowspan`/`aria-colspan` must be set; when the grid is virtualized, `aria-rowindex`/`aria-colindex` and `aria-rowcount`/`aria-colcount` must be set on the grid element with values matching the total row/column count. A common failure is setting `aria-rowcount` to match only the rendered rows rather than the total data rows.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('data grid — arrow key navigation, aria-rowindex and virtualization attributes', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/data-table');

  const grid = page.getByRole('grid');
  await expect(grid).toBeVisible();
  await expect(grid).toHaveAccessibleName(/.+/);

  // Check for virtualized grid attributes when rowcount is set
  const rowCount = await grid.getAttribute('aria-rowcount');
  if (rowCount && parseInt(rowCount) > 0) {
    const colCount = await grid.getAttribute('aria-colcount');
    expect(colCount, 'Virtualized grid must set aria-colcount alongside aria-rowcount').toBeTruthy();

    // First body row must have aria-rowindex (1-based, header is row 1)
    const firstDataRow = grid.locator('[role="row"]').nth(1);
    const rowIndex = await firstDataRow.getAttribute('aria-rowindex');
    expect(rowIndex, 'Data rows must have aria-rowindex in virtualized grids').toBeTruthy();
    expect(parseInt(rowIndex!), 'aria-rowindex must be >= 2 (row 1 is header)').toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
  }

  // Arrow key navigation: Down then Right
  const firstCell = grid.locator('[role="gridcell"], [role="columnheader"]').first();
  await firstCell.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  // Focus should have moved — the newly focused element should not be firstCell
  const focusedAfterDown = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role'));
  expect(['gridcell', 'rowheader', 'columnheader']).toContain(focusedAfterDown);

  // Ctrl+Home moves focus to first cell
  await page.keyboard.press('Control+Home');
  await expect(firstCell).toBeFocused();
});

test('grid cells with colspan/rowspan declare aria-colspan/aria-rowspan', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/merged-table');
  const grid = page.getByRole('grid');
  const spannedCells = grid.locator('[colspan], [rowspan]');
  const count = await spannedCells.count();
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const cell = spannedCells.nth(i);
    const colspan = await cell.getAttribute('colspan');
    const rowspan = await cell.getAttribute('rowspan');
    if (colspan && parseInt(colspan) > 1) {
      await expect(cell).toHaveAttribute('aria-colspan', colspan);
    }
    if (rowspan && parseInt(rowspan) > 1) {
      await expect(cell).toHaveAttribute('aria-rowspan', rowspan);
    }
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this pattern for data tables rendered as ARIA grids, virtual list tables, and spreadsheet-like UIs. Do NOT use `role="grid"` for static non-interactive tables — use `<table>` with `<th scope="col/row">` which gives AT all the navigation semantics natively without custom keyboard handling. Alternative: if you have a sortable data table, consider `role="table"` with `aria-sort` on column headers and standard link/button activations for column sorting rather than the full grid keyboard contract, reducing the implementation surface. [official]

---

### Pattern 78 (Cycle 35) — ARIA Slider Value Text and Range Boundary Test

**Description:** The ARIA slider pattern requires `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, and `aria-valuemax` on the focusable thumb element. When the numeric value is not user-friendly (a volume slider showing 0–100 where 72 is "medium-high"), `aria-valuetext` must override the announcement with a human-readable string. Without `aria-valuetext`, screen readers announce "72" which lacks context. For range sliders (dual-thumb), each thumb is a separate `role="slider"` element and must have its own `aria-labelledby` pointing to the thumb's label. The most common failure is updating `aria-valuenow` on slider drag without updating `aria-valuetext` when the text representation also changes, causing stale announcements. Vertical sliders must include `aria-orientation="vertical"` as horizontal is the ARIA default.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('slider — aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin/max, and arrow key interactions', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/audio-settings');

  const slider = page.getByRole('slider', { name: /volume/i });
  await expect(slider).toBeVisible();

  // Required range attributes
  const min = await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuemin');
  const max = await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuemax');
  const now = await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow');
  expect(min, 'aria-valuemin is required on role="slider"').not.toBeNull();
  expect(max, 'aria-valuemax is required on role="slider"').not.toBeNull();
  expect(now, 'aria-valuenow is required on role="slider"').not.toBeNull();
  expect(parseFloat(now!)).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(parseFloat(min!));
  expect(parseFloat(now!)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(parseFloat(max!));

  // Arrow Right should increment aria-valuenow
  await slider.focus();
  const initialValue = parseFloat((await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow'))!);
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
  const newValue = parseFloat((await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow'))!);
  expect(newValue, 'ArrowRight must increment slider value').toBeGreaterThan(initialValue);

  // Home key should set to minimum
  await page.keyboard.press('Home');
  const minValue = parseFloat((await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow'))!);
  expect(minValue).toBe(parseFloat(min!));

  // If aria-valuetext is set, it should be non-empty and consistent with valuenow
  const valueText = await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuetext');
  if (valueText !== null) {
    expect(valueText.trim().length, 'aria-valuetext must not be empty when present').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  }
});

test('vertical slider has aria-orientation="vertical"', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/equalizer');
  const verticalSliders = page.locator('[role="slider"][aria-orientation="vertical"]');
  const count = await verticalSliders.count();
  expect(count, 'Vertical sliders must declare aria-orientation="vertical"').toBeGreaterThan(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test for custom sliders — price range filters, media volume/seek controls, equalizer controls, date range pickers implemented as sliders. Do NOT use `role="slider"` for elements that are actually steppers or spinners (increment/decrement buttons on a numeric input) — use `role="spinbutton"` with `aria-valuenow/min/max` instead, as spinbutton has a different keyboard contract (allows direct text entry). Alternative: native `<input type="range">` provides slider semantics and keyboard interaction for free; prefer it over custom ARIA sliders unless design requirements mandate custom styling that cannot be achieved with CSS alone. [official]

---

### Pattern 79 (Cycle 35) — ARIA Spinbutton: Range Validation and `aria-invalid` State Test

**Description:** The ARIA spinbutton pattern (`role="spinbutton"`) is used for inputs where users select from a bounded discrete or continuous range, often featuring Up/Down arrow key increments alongside or instead of a text field. The critical testing gap is `aria-invalid="true"` — when a user types a value outside `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` or a non-numeric value, the spinbutton must surface `aria-invalid="true"` so screen reader users know their input was rejected. Without this, a blind user who types "999" into a 1–10 spinner sees no error feedback. Additionally, `aria-valuetext` should be used for non-numeric step units (e.g., "Large" instead of "3" for a font-size stepper with Small/Medium/Large steps). Focus must remain on the spinbutton text field throughout interactions, as per the APG guidance.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('spinbutton — range boundaries, arrow increments, and aria-invalid on bad input', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/ticket-quantity');

  const spinner = page.getByRole('spinbutton', { name: /quantity/i });
  await expect(spinner).toBeVisible();

  const min = parseInt((await spinner.getAttribute('aria-valuemin')) ?? '0');
  const max = parseInt((await spinner.getAttribute('aria-valuemax')) ?? '100');

  // Arrow Up increments within range
  await spinner.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowUp');
  const afterUp = parseInt((await spinner.getAttribute('aria-valuenow')) ?? '0');
  expect(afterUp, 'ArrowUp must increment aria-valuenow').toBeGreaterThan(min);

  // Arrow Down decrements
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  const afterDown = parseInt((await spinner.getAttribute('aria-valuenow')) ?? '0');
  expect(afterDown, 'ArrowDown must decrement aria-valuenow').toBeLessThan(afterUp);

  // Entering a value above max should trigger aria-invalid
  await spinner.fill(String(max + 100));
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab'); // Commit the value
  await spinner.focus();
  const invalid = await spinner.getAttribute('aria-invalid');
  expect(
    invalid,
    `Out-of-range value must set aria-invalid to "true" (got "${invalid}")`
  ).toBe('true');

  // Associated error message must also be announced
  const errorMsgId = await spinner.getAttribute('aria-errormessage');
  if (errorMsgId) {
    const errorMsg = page.locator(`#${errorMsgId}`);
    await expect(errorMsg).toBeVisible();
    await expect(errorMsg).not.toBeEmpty();
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this for quantity pickers, date/time part inputs (hour, minute, second), pagination jump-to inputs, and any bounded numeric text field. Do NOT use `role="spinbutton"` for a pure display counter (like a progress indicator showing step N of M) — that is `role="status"` or a progress element. Alternative: native `<input type="number" min max>` provides spinbutton semantics, built-in browser validation, and keyboard interaction for free; custom `role="spinbutton"` is warranted only when design requirements (custom styling, non-numeric step labels) cannot be met by native inputs. [official]

---

### Pattern 80 (Cycle 35) — ARIA Breadcrumb `aria-current="page"` and Navigation Landmark Test

**Description:** Breadcrumb navigation must be wrapped in a `<nav>` element (or `role="navigation"`) with an accessible label that distinguishes it from other navigation landmarks on the page — if a page has both a main navigation and a breadcrumb, both must have unique `aria-label` values. The current page link must carry `aria-current="page"` so screen reader users know where they are in the hierarchy. The breadcrumb list itself must be a `<ol>` or `<ul>` so screen readers announce the list count. A common failure is using a `<div>` container without semantics, which causes NVDA and JAWS to announce no list structure, leaving users without context about how many breadcrumb levels exist.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('breadcrumb — nav landmark, aria-label, aria-current="page", list structure', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products/shoes/running');

  // Breadcrumb must be a navigation landmark
  const breadcrumbNav = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /breadcrumb/i });
  await expect(breadcrumbNav).toBeVisible();

  // Must have a unique accessible label
  const navLabel = await breadcrumbNav.getAttribute('aria-label');
  expect(navLabel?.toLowerCase()).toContain('breadcrumb');

  // Must use an ordered or unordered list
  const list = breadcrumbNav.locator('ol, ul');
  await expect(list).toHaveCount(1);

  // Items must be links except possibly the current page
  const listItems = list.locator('li');
  const count = await listItems.count();
  expect(count, 'Breadcrumb must have at least one item').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Current page must have aria-current="page"
  const currentItem = breadcrumbNav.locator('[aria-current="page"]');
  await expect(currentItem).toHaveCount(1);

  // Current page item text should match the page title or H1
  const currentText = await currentItem.textContent();
  const pageTitle = await page.title();
  expect(
    pageTitle.toLowerCase().includes((currentText ?? '').toLowerCase().trim()),
    'aria-current="page" item text should match or be contained in the page title'
  ).toBe(true);

  // No other breadcrumb item should have aria-current
  const otherCurrentItems = breadcrumbNav.locator('[aria-current]:not([aria-current="page"])');
  await expect(otherCurrentItems).toHaveCount(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test for any page with hierarchical navigation paths — e-commerce category pages, documentation sites, admin dashboards with drill-down paths. Do NOT add `aria-current="page"` to navigation items outside of breadcrumbs unless they genuinely represent the current page; for indicating the current nav item in a sidebar, `aria-current="page"` is also appropriate but must be applied consistently. Alternative: if your breadcrumb is a single flat string rendered as text with `aria-label` providing the full path, ensure the path includes all ancestor context — but prefer structured `<ol><li>` markup as it allows AT users to query list item count. [official]

---

### Pattern 81 (Cycle 35) — ARIA Tooltip `role="tooltip"` + `aria-describedby` Escape Dismiss Test

**Description:** The ARIA APG tooltip pattern requires that the tooltip element has `role="tooltip"`, is connected to the triggering element via `aria-describedby`, and can be dismissed with the Escape key without moving focus. Tooltips must appear on both hover and keyboard focus, and must remain visible when the pointer moves from the trigger onto the tooltip content itself (hoverable requirement per WCAG 1.4.13). A critical testing failure is tooltips that appear on focus but dismiss immediately when the pointer moves within the tooltip boundary, or tooltips that cannot be dismissed with Escape. The tooltip element must not receive focus itself — it is purely supplemental description, never the primary label.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('tooltip — role="tooltip", aria-describedby, Escape dismiss, hover persistence', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/form-page');

  // Find a button/input with an associated tooltip
  const trigger = page.locator('[aria-describedby]').first();
  await expect(trigger).toBeVisible();

  const tooltipId = await trigger.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
  expect(tooltipId, 'Trigger must reference a tooltip via aria-describedby').toBeTruthy();

  const tooltip = page.locator(`#${tooltipId}`);
  await expect(tooltip).toHaveAttribute('role', 'tooltip');

  // Tooltip visible on focus
  await trigger.focus();
  await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible();

  // Escape dismisses the tooltip without moving focus
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(tooltip).toBeHidden();
  await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();

  // Tooltip visible on hover
  await trigger.hover();
  await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible();

  // Tooltip must remain visible when pointer enters tooltip (WCAG 1.4.13 hoverable)
  await tooltip.hover();
  await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible();

  // Tooltip must not be focusable
  const tooltipTabIndex = await tooltip.evaluate((el) => (el as HTMLElement).tabIndex);
  expect(
    tooltipTabIndex,
    'role="tooltip" must not be focusable (tabIndex should be -1 or absent)'
  ).toBe(-1);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this for icon-only buttons with tooltip labels, form field hints rendered as tooltips, and abbreviation/definition popups. Do NOT use `role="tooltip"` for interactive content (links, buttons, form elements) — interactive tooltips are actually `role="dialog"` or a non-modal popup and must be focusable with a proper close mechanism. Alternative: for form field hints that always appear below the input (not on hover/focus), use `aria-describedby` pointing to a visible hint paragraph with no `role="tooltip"` — always-visible description text doesn't need the tooltip role or the hover/focus show/hide behavior. [official]

---

### Pattern 82 (Cycle 35) — ARIA Radio Group Roving Tabindex and Selection State Test

**Description:** The ARIA radio group pattern requires roving tabindex — within a `role="radiogroup"`, only one `role="radio"` button has `tabIndex=0` at any time (the checked one, or the first if none are checked), and arrow keys move selection rather than Tab. The critical distinction from checkbox groups is that arrow key navigation in a radio group automatically checks the focused item (unless the group is inside a toolbar). An extremely common failure is implementing radio-like buttons as a set of individual `<button>` elements with `aria-pressed` — these behave as toggle buttons where Tab cycles through all of them, which makes the interaction model inconsistent with screen reader user expectations for mutually exclusive selection. The radiogroup must have an accessible label that describes the grouping purpose.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { checkA11y } from 'axe-playwright';

test('radiogroup — roving tabindex, arrow-key selection, aria-checked state', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/survey');

  const radioGroup = page.getByRole('radiogroup', { name: /preferred contact/i });
  await expect(radioGroup).toBeVisible();

  const radios = radioGroup.getByRole('radio');
  const radioCount = await radios.count();
  expect(radioCount, 'Radio group must have at least 2 options').toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);

  // Initially, exactly one radio has tabIndex=0 (either the checked one or the first)
  const tabbableRadios = await radios.evaluateAll(
    (els) => els.filter((el) => (el as HTMLElement).tabIndex === 0).length
  );
  expect(tabbableRadios, 'Exactly one radio must have tabIndex=0 in the group').toBe(1);

  // Focus first radio, press ArrowDown — focus and selection move to next radio
  await radios.first().focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  const secondCheckedAfter = await radios.nth(1).getAttribute('aria-checked');
  expect(secondCheckedAfter, 'ArrowDown in radiogroup must check the next radio').toBe('true');
  // First radio should now be unchecked
  const firstCheckedAfter = await radios.first().getAttribute('aria-checked');
  expect(firstCheckedAfter, 'Previous radio must be unchecked after ArrowDown').toBe('false');

  // axe scan on the radio group
  await checkA11y(page, radioGroup, { runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2aa', 'wcag22aa'] } });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test for shipping method selectors, survey answer grids, plan selectors, and any mutually-exclusive choice group. Do NOT implement radio groups as `<button aria-pressed>` elements — while this technically works as toggle buttons, it fails screen reader expectations for mutual exclusion and requires custom JS to enforce single selection; native `<input type="radio">` or `role="radio"` within `role="radiogroup"` is the correct pattern. Alternative: if the radio group is embedded in a `role="toolbar"`, change behavior to Space-to-select instead of arrow-key auto-select, and test both paths. [official]

---

### Pattern 83 (Cycle 35) — SVG Inline Accessibility: `role="img"` + `<title>` + `aria-hidden` Audit

**Description:** Inline SVG elements require explicit accessibility treatment that differs from `<img>` tags. Meaningful SVGs must receive `role="img"` on the `<svg>` element plus an accessible name provided via `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` pointing to a child `<title>` element, or both. The SVG `<title>` child element provides the default accessible name without `aria-label` but is not reliably announced by all screen reader + browser combinations without the corresponding `role="img"` — NVDA + Chrome notably ignores `<title>` without `role="img"`. Decorative SVGs (icons that are purely visual accompaniments to adjacent text) must have `aria-hidden="true"` to prevent screen readers from announcing empty text content or the SVG file path. A common failure is using an icon SVG inside a `<button>` without `aria-label` on the button and without `aria-hidden` on the SVG, causing the button to be announced with no accessible name.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('SVG accessibility audit — role="img", title, aria-hidden on decorative SVGs', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Meaningful SVGs should have role="img" and an accessible name
  const meaningfulSvgs = page.locator('svg[role="img"]');
  const meaningfulCount = await meaningfulSvgs.count();
  for (let i = 0; i < meaningfulCount; i++) {
    const svg = meaningfulSvgs.nth(i);
    const ariaLabel = await svg.getAttribute('aria-label');
    const ariaLabelledBy = await svg.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    expect(
      ariaLabel || ariaLabelledBy,
      `Meaningful SVG ${i + 1} must have aria-label or aria-labelledby`
    ).toBeTruthy();

    // If using aria-labelledby, the referenced element must exist and be non-empty
    if (ariaLabelledBy) {
      const titleEl = page.locator(`#${ariaLabelledBy}`);
      await expect(titleEl).toHaveCount(1);
      await expect(titleEl).not.toBeEmpty();
    }
  }

  // Icon SVGs inside buttons must either have aria-hidden (decorative) OR the button has aria-label
  const buttonSvgs = page.locator('button svg, [role="button"] svg');
  const buttonSvgCount = await buttonSvgs.count();
  const failures: string[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < buttonSvgCount; i++) {
    const svg = buttonSvgs.nth(i);
    const isHidden = await svg.getAttribute('aria-hidden');
    const parentBtn = svg.locator('xpath=ancestor::button[1] | xpath=ancestor::*[@role="button"][1]').first();
    const btnLabel = await parentBtn.getAttribute('aria-label');
    const btnLabelledBy = await parentBtn.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    const hasVisibleText = ((await parentBtn.textContent()) ?? '').replace(/\s/g, '').length > 0;
    if (isHidden !== 'true' && !btnLabel && !btnLabelledBy && !hasVisibleText) {
      failures.push(`Button SVG ${i + 1}: SVG not aria-hidden and button has no accessible name`);
    }
  }
  expect(failures, failures.join('\n')).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this audit on any page with inline SVG icons — navigation menus, action toolbars, status indicators, data visualization charts. Do NOT add `role="img"` to SVG elements that contain interactive children (links inside SVGs, clickable regions) — interactive SVGs need different treatment with individual roles on the interactive elements. Alternative: using `<img src="icon.svg" alt="description">` for non-interactive icons sidesteps the inline SVG complexity and has broader AT support, at the cost of losing CSS styling flexibility; inline SVG is warranted for icons that need to inherit color or be animated. [community]

---

### Pattern 84 (Cycle 35) — CSS `content` Property: Decorative vs. Meaningful Generated Content Audit

**Description:** CSS `content` property (used in `::before` and `::after` pseudo-elements) can inject text or Unicode characters into the visual presentation that some screen readers announce. In older screen reader versions (JAWS prior to 2022, NVDA prior to 2021), generated content was generally not announced. In modern versions, both NVDA and JAWS now announce `content` text in most contexts. This creates two failure modes: decorative generated content (chevrons, bullets, visual separators) being announced as noise, and meaningful generated content (step numbers, labels appended via `content: attr(data-label)`) lacking a programmatic text alternative. The correct fix for decorative content is `content: ""` or adding `aria-hidden` to the element; meaningful content should be moved to actual text in the DOM and hidden visually with `.sr-only` rather than relying on CSS generation.

```typescript
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

async function auditCSSGeneratedContent(page: Page): Promise<{ selector: string; content: string; risk: string }[]> {
  return page.evaluate(() => {
    const issues: { selector: string; content: string; risk: string }[] = [];
    const elements = document.querySelectorAll('*');
    elements.forEach((el) => {
      const before = getComputedStyle(el, '::before').content;
      const after = getComputedStyle(el, '::after').content;
      const ariaHidden = el.getAttribute('aria-hidden');

      [{ pseudo: '::before', val: before }, { pseudo: '::after', val: after }].forEach(({ pseudo, val }) => {
        if (!val || val === 'none' || val === '""' || val === "''") return;
        const text = val.replace(/^["']|["']$/g, '');
        if (text.trim().length === 0) return;
        if (ariaHidden !== 'true') {
          const tag = el.tagName.toLowerCase();
          const id = el.id ? `#${el.id}` : '';
          const cls = Array.from(el.classList).slice(0, 2).map((c) => `.${c}`).join('');
          issues.push({
            selector: `${tag}${id}${cls}${pseudo}`,
            content: text,
            risk: text.length > 2 ? 'meaningful-content-in-css' : 'decorative-symbol',
          });
        }
      });
    });
    return issues;
  });
}

test('CSS generated content audit — decorative vs meaningful', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/component-library');
  const issues = await auditCSSGeneratedContent(page);
  const meaningfulIssues = issues.filter((i) => i.risk === 'meaningful-content-in-css');

  expect(
    meaningfulIssues,
    `Meaningful text found in CSS content property — move to DOM:\n${meaningfulIssues.map((i) => `  ${i.selector}: "${i.content}"`).join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this audit during design system reviews and accessibility audits of component libraries where decorative icons and typographic enhancements are common. Do NOT block CI on every decorative-symbol finding (single Unicode chevrons, bullets) — add an allowlist for known-safe decorative patterns; focus CI blocking on meaningful text content injected via CSS. Alternative: using icon fonts (which also rely on `content` property Unicode characters) creates a similar problem — prefer inline SVG with `aria-hidden="true"` or `<img>` for icons rather than icon fonts, as icon font rendering varies across AT. [community]

---

### Pattern 85 (Cycle 35) — `prefers-reduced-motion` Emulation Test for Animation-Triggered Accessibility Issues

**Description:** WCAG 2.3.3 (AAA) recommends not causing motion sickness, and WCAG 2.2 guidance strongly endorses respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`. Beyond the WCAG AAA concern, motion that cannot be paused or reduced is increasingly considered a legal accessibility barrier under EAA for users with vestibular disorders. Playwright's `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` API enables automated testing of both the visual outcome (animations are removed/paused) and that all functionality remains available without animation. A critical failure is implementing `prefers-reduced-motion` only as a CSS media query that hides the visual animation but leaves JavaScript-driven animations (GSAP, Framer Motion, Web Animations API) running — screen readers are not affected, but users with vestibular sensitivity are still exposed to motion.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('prefers-reduced-motion — no JS animations play when preference is set', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
  await page.goto('/landing-page');

  // CSS transition durations should be 0 or near-0 in reduced motion mode
  const heroSection = page.locator('.hero-animation');
  if (await heroSection.count() > 0) {
    const transitionDuration = await heroSection.evaluate(
      (el) => getComputedStyle(el).transitionDuration
    );
    expect(
      transitionDuration,
      'Hero section transition must be 0s when prefers-reduced-motion is reduce'
    ).toBe('0s');
  }

  // Web Animations API: no running animations should have non-zero duration
  const runningAnimations = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return document.getAnimations().filter((a) => {
      return a.playState === 'running' && (a.effect as KeyframeEffect)?.getTiming().duration !== 0;
    }).length;
  });
  expect(
    runningAnimations,
    `${runningAnimations} JS animations still running with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
  ).toBe(0);

  // Carousel: should be paused or hidden
  const carousel = page.locator('[aria-roledescription="carousel"]');
  if (await carousel.count() > 0) {
    const rotationBtn = carousel.getByRole('button', { name: /start slide rotation/i });
    await expect(rotationBtn, 'Carousel rotation must start paused when reduced motion is preferred').toBeVisible();
  }
});

test('prefers-reduced-motion — all functionality remains accessible without animations', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
  await page.goto('/onboarding');

  // Multi-step wizard: next/back must work without animated transitions
  const nextBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /next/i });
  await nextBtn.click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /step 2/i })).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test for any page with CSS animations, GSAP/Framer Motion sequences, animated carousels, page transitions in SPAs, and scroll-triggered reveals. Do NOT skip this test assuming `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` CSS is sufficient — JavaScript animation libraries require separate opt-out logic that CSS media queries do not control. Alternative: use `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'no-preference' })` in a parallel test run to confirm animations do play in the normal mode, giving full before/after coverage. [official]

---

### Pattern 86 (Cycle 35) — WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry: Multi-Step Form Auto-Population Test

**Description:** WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7 (Redundant Entry, Level A) requires that information previously entered by the user within the same process is either auto-populated in subsequent steps or made available to select, unless re-entry is essential (security, validity). This criterion primarily protects users with cognitive disabilities and motor impairments for whom re-typing information is burdensome or error-prone. The most common failure is checkout flows that collect address on one step and require the user to re-enter the same address as billing information, without a "same as shipping" checkbox or auto-population. Testing requires simulating a complete multi-step flow and asserting that data entered in step N appears pre-filled in the relevant step N+2 field.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 3.3.7 — redundant entry: shipping address auto-populates billing', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Step 1: Fill shipping address
  const shippingData = {
    firstName: 'Jane',
    lastName: 'Doe',
    street: '123 Main St',
    city: 'Springfield',
    zip: '12345',
  };
  await page.getByLabel(/first name/i).fill(shippingData.firstName);
  await page.getByLabel(/last name/i).fill(shippingData.lastName);
  await page.getByLabel(/street address/i).fill(shippingData.street);
  await page.getByLabel(/city/i).fill(shippingData.city);
  await page.getByLabel(/zip/i).fill(shippingData.zip);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /continue/i }).click();

  // Step 2: Payment — billing address section
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /payment/i })).toBeVisible();

  // Option A: "same as shipping" checkbox exists and is checked by default
  const sameAsShipping = page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: /same as shipping/i });
  if (await sameAsShipping.count() > 0) {
    await expect(sameAsShipping).toBeChecked();
    return;
  }

  // Option B: billing fields are pre-populated with shipping data
  const billingCity = page.getByLabel(/billing city/i);
  if (await billingCity.count() > 0) {
    await expect(billingCity).toHaveValue(shippingData.city);
  }

  // Option C: previously-entered data is selectable from a dropdown
  const addressSelect = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: /billing address/i });
  if (await addressSelect.count() > 0) {
    const options = await addressSelect.locator('option').allTextContents();
    expect(
      options.some((opt) => opt.includes(shippingData.street)),
      'Previously entered address must be selectable in billing dropdown'
    ).toBe(true);
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this test for multi-step checkout flows, registration wizards, loan/insurance applications, and onboarding forms where users re-enter identical data across steps. Do NOT fail a form for requiring re-entry of passwords (the WCAG exception explicitly allows this for security) or one-time codes (short-lived, security-sensitive). Alternative: if your application stores user profiles, fulfilling SC 3.3.7 can be as simple as pre-populating from the saved profile rather than from earlier form steps — either approach satisfies the criterion. [official]

---

### Pattern 87 (Cycle 35) — WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication: Paste and Autocomplete Enablement Test

**Description:** WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.8 (Accessible Authentication — Minimum, Level AA) prohibits requiring cognitive function tests in authentication flows unless alternatives exist. The two most critical implementation requirements are: (1) password managers must be able to auto-fill credentials (fields must have correct `autocomplete` attributes and must not block paste), and (2) OTP/verification code fields must allow paste to avoid requiring users to manually transcribe codes. JavaScript `onpaste` event prevention is a frequent failure — blocking paste in password or OTP fields directly violates this criterion. The criterion also applies to CAPTCHA: if an image CAPTCHA is required, an audio alternative or alternative authentication method must be provided.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('SC 3.3.8 — login form allows paste in password field', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');

  const passwordField = page.getByLabel(/password/i);
  await expect(passwordField).toBeVisible();

  // Must have autocomplete attribute for password manager support
  await expect(passwordField).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', /current-password|new-password/);

  // Paste must not be blocked — set clipboard text and paste
  await passwordField.focus();
  await page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard?.writeText('TestPassword123!').catch(() => {}));
  await page.keyboard.press('Control+V');
  const pastedValue = await passwordField.inputValue();
  expect(
    pastedValue.length,
    'Password field must accept pasted content (paste should not be blocked)'
  ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
});

test('SC 3.3.8 — OTP verification field allows paste', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/verify-otp');

  const otpField = page.getByLabel(/verification code|one.time/i).first();
  if (await otpField.count() === 0) return;

  await otpField.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Control+V');
  const afterPaste = await otpField.inputValue();
  expect(afterPaste).toBeDefined();

  // No CAPTCHA without alternative: if a CAPTCHA exists, an audio alternative must exist
  const captchaImage = page.locator('[id*="captcha"] img, img[alt*="captcha"]');
  if (await captchaImage.count() > 0) {
    const audioCaptcha = page.getByRole('link', { name: /audio/i })
      .or(page.getByRole('button', { name: /audio captcha/i }));
    await expect(audioCaptcha, 'Image CAPTCHA must have an audio alternative (SC 3.3.8)').toBeVisible();
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use this for all authentication flows including login, registration, password reset, two-factor authentication, and account recovery. Do NOT configure Playwright's browser context with clipboard permissions that would falsely bypass paste-blocking — test in the same browser permission context that real users experience. Alternative: the best way to satisfy SC 3.3.8 is to adopt WebAuthn / passkeys which eliminate passwords entirely, removing the paste concern while also satisfying the "no cognitive function test" requirement. [official]

---

### Pattern 88 (Cycle 35) — axe-core `resultTypes` Performance Optimization for Large-Scale CI Scans

**Description:** By default, `axe.run()` computes and serializes the full DOM node list for violations, passes, incomplete items, and inapplicable rules. On large-page scans (dashboards, data tables, rich text editors), the serialization cost of the `passes` and `inapplicable` arrays can account for 60–80% of scan time with no actionable test output. Setting `resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete']` in the axe options reduces the data axe must serialize while still capturing all failures and manual-review items. In `@axe-core/playwright`, this option is passed via the `AxeBuilder.options()` method. This optimization is especially impactful in CI where scans run across 50+ pages. Benchmarks from axe-core team show 4–8x speedup on complex pages.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

async function fastAxeScan(page: import('@playwright/test').Page, tags = ['wcag2aa', 'wcag22aa']) {
  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(tags)
    .options({
      resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'],
    })
    .analyze();
  return results;
}

test('dashboard page axe scan — optimized for CI speed', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const results = await fastAxeScan(page);

  expect(
    results.violations,
    `axe violations:\n${results.violations.map((v) => `[${v.impact}] ${v.id}: ${v.description} (${v.nodes.length} nodes)`).join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);

  if (results.incomplete.length > 0) {
    console.warn(
      `axe incomplete (manual review needed):\n${results.incomplete.map((i) => `  ${i.id}: ${i.description}`).join('\n')}`
    );
  }
});

test('scan only main content region — targeted for component PR gating', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/product-detail');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .include('main')
    .withTags(['wcag2aa', 'wcag22aa'])
    .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] })
    .analyze();

  expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Use `resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete']` as the default configuration for all CI axe scans — the omitted `passes` and `inapplicable` arrays are only useful for generating conformance reports and auditing rule coverage, not for test gating. Do NOT use `resultTypes: ['violations']` alone — omitting `incomplete` hides issues axe flagged as needing manual review (color contrast on complex backgrounds, keyboard traps that require interaction to trigger). Alternative: for generating VPAT/ACR conformance reports, run a separate nightly scan without `resultTypes` restriction to capture the full rule coverage data, and keep the CI gate fast with the restricted configuration. [official]

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 35)

174. **[community] Framer Motion and GSAP animations bypass `prefers-reduced-motion` CSS media queries because they use the Web Animations API or direct style manipulation, not CSS transitions — setting `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { * { animation: none; transition: none } }` in your global stylesheet does not stop JavaScript-driven animations from playing**: When a design system standardizes on Framer Motion for page transitions and component animations, developers typically add the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` CSS reset as a blanket safeguard. However, Framer Motion computes animation values in JavaScript and applies them via the Web Animations API or inline styles, not through CSS `animation` or `transition` properties — the CSS reset has no effect on these animations. WHY: The mismatch is invisible during visual testing in a standard browser because the developer's own system preference is often set to "no preference"; it is only discovered when a QA tester or user with vestibular sensitivity reports that animations play despite their OS accessibility setting being on. The fix requires reading `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` in JavaScript and conditionally disabling animation variants, or using Framer Motion's built-in `useReducedMotion()` hook which handles this correctly. [community]

175. **[community] NVDA with Firefox announces `aria-live="polite"` region updates twice when the live region is inside a `<dialog>` element — the content is announced once as a live region update and once when NVDA reads the dialog region, causing confusing double-announcements for screen reader users submitting forms with inline validation**: Firefox and NVDA have a known interaction where ARIA live regions inside `role="dialog"` containers can trigger double-announcements. This occurs because NVDA monitors both live region mutations and dialog region content changes. When an error message appears in a live region inside a modal form, NVDA with Firefox announces the error immediately (live region) and then again when the user's virtual cursor reads the dialog. WHY: This is a browser/AT interaction bug rather than a developer error, but the practical fix is to move inline form validation announcements in modals from `aria-live` regions to `aria-describedby` on the input itself or `aria-errormessage` — these produce a single announcement when the user navigates to the input, which is less disruptive than a live region announcement in the middle of typing. [community]

176. **[community] `getByRole('combobox')` in Playwright returns the wrong element for native `<select>` elements when a custom dropdown component hides the native select and renders a `<div role="combobox">` — both elements match `getByRole('combobox')` causing tests to target the hidden native select instead of the visible custom component**: Custom select replacements are a very common UI pattern in design systems. The pattern hides the native `<select>` with `display: none` or moves it offscreen and renders a styled `<div role="combobox">`. Playwright's `getByRole('combobox')` matches both the native `<select>` (which may be aria-hidden or display:none) and the visible custom `<div role="combobox">`, leading to `expect(locator).toBeVisible()` failures or incorrect element targeting. WHY: Developers write `page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Country' })` expecting to get the visible custom combobox but sometimes get the hidden native select; the fix is to always add `.filter({ visible: true })` to `getByRole` queries for combobox elements, or to ensure the native select has `aria-hidden="true"` to remove it from the accessibility tree entirely. [community]

177. **[community] `jest-axe` v10 with Jest v30 throws a module resolution error because jest-axe v10 ships as ESM-only and Jest v30's default CommonJS module handling does not auto-transform node_modules — upgrading both simultaneously breaks the test suite with `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` or `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement in a CommonJS module`**: jest-axe v10 (released March 2025) was the first version to ship exclusively as ESM. Jest v30 changed its default module handling in ways that conflict with the ESM resolution when projects remain in CommonJS mode (no `"type": "module"` in package.json). WHY: Most Jest configurations still use CommonJS by default and Jest v30's auto-transform does not extend to node_modules by default; the fix is to add `jest-axe` to `transformIgnorePatterns` exclusions, or to migrate the test project to native ESM, or to pin jest-axe to v9 until the project is ready for full ESM migration. [community]

178. **[community] Playwright's `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` produces different YAML output on macOS vs. Linux CI because the accessibility tree computation differs between platforms — `<button>` and `<form>` elements receive subtly different implicit ARIA roles and computed names on macOS Chrome vs. Linux Chrome, causing snapshot mismatches in CI even though the page HTML is identical**: Chromium's accessibility tree implementation on macOS uses the macOS Accessibility API as a backend, while on Linux it uses AT-SPI2. Subtle differences in how implicit ARIA roles and computed names are resolved between these backends cause `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` to produce non-identical YAML for the same HTML. WHY: Teams generate aria snapshot baselines on developer machines (macOS) and then see CI (Linux) fail on first run with unexpected tree differences; the fix is to generate snapshot baselines on the same platform as CI (use Linux Docker container for baseline generation) or to use `{ mode: 'partial' }` in `toMatchAriaSnapshot` options to only assert on the stable subset of the tree. [community]

### Pattern 89 (Cycle 39) — axe-core 4.11.4 `aria-labelledby` Hidden Element Exclusion

**Description:** axe-core 4.11.4 (released 2026-04-23) changed how `aria-labelledby` references are resolved: elements that are natively hidden via CSS (`display:none`, `visibility:hidden`) or the `hidden` attribute are now excluded from the accessible name computation. Previously axe-core would include natively hidden elements referenced by `aria-labelledby` in the computed name, making a violation appear to pass when the referenced label element was invisible to screen readers. This fix aligns axe with the actual accname-1.1 algorithm: natively hidden elements are skipped in name computation. Teams relying on `aria-labelledby` pointing to a visually-hidden-but-not-CSS-hidden element (e.g., `clip` pattern) are unaffected; teams hiding label elements with `display:none` while using `aria-labelledby` will now see correct violations. This change may surface previously undetected `aria-label` violations in your codebase on upgrade.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/aria-labelledby-hidden.spec.ts
// Validates axe 4.11.4 behavior: aria-labelledby pointing to display:none element
// is flagged as a violation (label not in accessible name computation).
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('aria-labelledby hidden element exclusion (axe 4.11.4+)', () => {
  test('input with aria-labelledby pointing to display:none element triggers violation', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setContent(`
      <span id="hidden-label" style="display:none">Hidden label text</span>
      <input type="text" aria-labelledby="hidden-label" />
    `);

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();

    // axe 4.11.4+ should flag this as label or aria-required-attr violation
    const labelViolation = results.violations.find((v) =>
      v.id === 'label' || v.id === 'aria-required-attr' || v.id === 'aria-valid-attr-value'
    );
    expect(
      labelViolation,
      'Expected axe to flag aria-labelledby pointing to display:none element'
    ).toBeDefined();
  });

  test('input with aria-labelledby pointing to .sr-only element passes (clip pattern)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setContent(`
      <span id="sr-label" class="sr-only" style="
        position:absolute; width:1px; height:1px;
        padding:0; margin:-1px; overflow:hidden;
        clip:rect(0,0,0,0); white-space:nowrap; border:0;
      ">Visually hidden but accessible label</span>
      <input type="text" aria-labelledby="sr-label" />
    `);

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();

    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Upgrading to axe-core 4.11.4 may expose previously undetected violations in codebases that use `aria-labelledby` pointing to `display:none` elements (a common — but incorrect — pattern). Run a baseline scan before upgrading to identify regressions versus genuine newly-detected bugs. The `.sr-only` clip pattern is the correct alternative and continues to pass. [official]

---

### Pattern 90 (Cycle 39) — Playwright 1.60 `getByRole` `description` Parameter for Accessible Description Matching

**Description:** Playwright v1.60 added a `description` option to `getByRole()` that filters locators by accessible description (`aria-describedby` or `aria-description`). This closes a long-standing gap: previously, tests could only filter by accessible name, forcing developers to chain `.filter()` or use custom assertions to disambiguate two buttons with the same visible label but different descriptions. The `description` option accepts a string or regex and matches against the element's computed accessible description. This is particularly useful for icon-only buttons in toolbars (same role, potentially no name, differentiated by description) and for form fields where `aria-describedby` provides supplementary help text. Combining `getByRole('button', { name: 'Close', description: /modal/i })` makes test locators both robust and semantically precise.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/getbyrole-description.spec.ts
// Tests Playwright 1.60 getByRole description parameter for accessible description filtering.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('getByRole description parameter (Playwright 1.60+)', () => {
  test('locates button by accessible description to disambiguate toolbar actions', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setContent(`
      <div role="toolbar" aria-label="Text formatting">
        <button aria-label="Bold" aria-describedby="bold-desc">B</button>
        <span id="bold-desc" hidden>Toggle bold formatting</span>
        <button aria-label="Italic" aria-describedby="italic-desc">I</button>
        <span id="italic-desc" hidden>Toggle italic formatting</span>
      </div>
    `);

    // Locate by name + description combination — unambiguous even with terse labels
    const boldButton = page.getByRole('button', {
      name: 'Bold',
      description: 'Toggle bold formatting',
    });
    await expect(boldButton).toBeVisible();

    const italicButton = page.getByRole('button', {
      name: 'Italic',
      description: /italic formatting/i,
    });
    await expect(italicButton).toBeVisible();

    // Ensure we get exactly one match for each — no ambiguity
    await expect(boldButton).toHaveCount(1);
    await expect(italicButton).toHaveCount(1);
  });

  test('form field located by help text via aria-describedby', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setContent(`
      <label for="email">Email</label>
      <input id="email" type="email" aria-describedby="email-hint" />
      <span id="email-hint">We will never share your email address</span>
    `);

    const emailField = page.getByRole('textbox', {
      name: 'Email',
      description: /never share/i,
    });
    await expect(emailField).toBeVisible();
    await expect(emailField).toHaveAttribute('type', 'email');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** The `description` parameter requires Playwright ≥ 1.60. Teams on older Playwright versions must use `.filter()` or `locator.and()` compositions. The description filter also requires that `aria-describedby` IDs resolve to visible (or clip-hidden) elements — references to `display:none` elements may not be included in the computed description, mirroring the axe 4.11.4 behavior. [official]

---

### Pattern 91 (Cycle 39) — WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: Sticky Footer Overlap Test

**Description:** WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 (Focus Not Obscured, Minimum, AA) requires that when a keyboard-focusable component receives focus it is not entirely hidden by author-created content — sticky headers, cookie banners, or fixed footers are the most common offenders. This criterion was added because sticky UI elements frequently push the focused element completely off the visible viewport or behind the sticky layer without developers noticing (the tab key moves focus but nothing visually changes). The test strategy uses Playwright's `locator.boundingBox()` to measure the focused element's position and compare it against the sticky footer's top edge, asserting at least partial intersection with the viewport above the sticky element. This test is particularly important for "Accept all" cookie consent bars and persistent chat widgets.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/focus-not-obscured-footer.spec.ts
// Tests WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11: focused elements must not be entirely obscured by sticky footer.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured — sticky footer', () => {
  test('no focusable element is entirely hidden behind sticky footer', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const viewportHeight = page.viewportSize()!.height;

    // Find sticky/fixed footer element
    const stickyFooter = page.locator(
      'footer[style*="fixed"], [class*="sticky-footer"], [class*="cookie-banner"]'
    ).first();
    const footerBox = await stickyFooter.boundingBox();
    const footerTop = footerBox ? footerBox.y : viewportHeight;

    // Tab through all focusable elements and check none is fully behind the footer
    const focusableSelector =
      'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), ' +
      'textarea:not([disabled]), [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';
    const focusables = await page.locator(focusableSelector).all();

    const obscuredElements: string[] = [];

    for (const el of focusables) {
      await el.focus();
      const box = await el.boundingBox();
      if (!box) continue;

      const isCompletelyBelowFooter = box.y >= footerTop;

      if (isCompletelyBelowFooter) {
        const outerHTML = await el.evaluate(
          (node) => (node as HTMLElement).outerHTML.slice(0, 120)
        );
        obscuredElements.push(outerHTML);
      }
    }

    expect(
      obscuredElements,
      `These focusable elements are entirely obscured by the sticky footer (WCAG 2.4.11):\n` +
        obscuredElements.join('\n')
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** This test iterates over all focusable elements and calls `focus()` on each — it can be slow on pages with hundreds of interactive elements. Scope it to the page area near the footer, or run it as a dedicated audit test on a weekly cadence rather than on every PR. For SC 2.4.12 (Enhanced, AAA), assert that `box.y >= 0` (not partially hidden at the top either). [official]

---

### Pattern 92 (Cycle 39) — ARIA `role="feed"` with Dynamic Article Insertion Live Region Test

**Description:** The ARIA `role="feed"` pattern is designed for infinite-scroll content where articles are continuously added. A feed must: (1) have `role="feed"` on the container, (2) each child article must have `role="article"` with `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize`, and (3) a live region outside the feed must announce when new articles load so keyboard and screen reader users know content has been added without being interrupted. WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) and 4.1.3 (Status Messages) apply. The most common failure is missing live region announcements — new articles silently appear in the DOM and AT users have no way to discover them without manually scrolling. This test pattern validates the full contract: feed structure, article semantics, and live region announcement on load.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/aria-feed-live-region.spec.ts
// Tests ARIA feed pattern: role="feed", article semantics, live region on infinite scroll load.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('ARIA role="feed" accessibility contract', () => {
  test('feed container has role="feed" and articles have role="article"', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/news-feed');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const feed = page.locator('[role="feed"]');
    await expect(feed).toBeVisible();

    const articles = feed.locator('[role="article"]');
    const count = await articles.count();
    expect(count, 'Feed must contain at least one article').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('articles expose aria-posinset and aria-setsize', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/news-feed');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const firstArticle = page.locator('[role="feed"] [role="article"]').first();
    await expect(firstArticle).toHaveAttribute('aria-posinset', '1');
    const setsize = await firstArticle.getAttribute('aria-setsize');
    expect(Number(setsize)).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('live region announces new articles after infinite scroll load', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/news-feed');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const initialCount = await page.locator('[role="feed"] [role="article"]').count();

    // Trigger infinite scroll by scrolling to bottom
    await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight));
    await page.waitForFunction(
      (n) => document.querySelectorAll('[role="feed"] [role="article"]').length > n,
      initialCount,
      { timeout: 5000 }
    );

    const liveRegion = page.locator('[aria-live="polite"], [role="status"]').first();
    const announcement = await liveRegion.textContent();
    expect(
      announcement?.trim().length,
      'Live region must announce new content'
    ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('no axe violations on feed structure', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/news-feed');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include('[role="feed"]')
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'] })
      .analyze();

    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `role="feed"` is one of the lesser-known ARIA landmark roles and many component libraries omit it in favour of plain `<ul>` + virtual scroll. If the feed is implemented as a list, use `role="list"` with `aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset` on list items instead — the live region announcement pattern is the same. Do not use both `role="feed"` and `role="list"` on the same element — `feed` and `list` are conflicting roles. [official]

---

### Pattern 93 (Cycle 39) — `@axe-core/playwright` Single-Selector `include()` Limitation Workaround

**Description:** `@axe-core/playwright`'s `AxeBuilder.include()` method accepts only a single CSS selector string per call chain — multiple calls to `.include()` in the same builder are not additive (only the last call takes effect). This is a known limitation of the underlying axe-core context model. Teams building reusable scan fixtures that accept an array of selectors to scan (e.g., scanning multiple regions on a dashboard) must implement a workaround: either run a separate `AxeBuilder` instance per selector and merge violations, or pass a comma-separated compound selector string. This limitation is documented in the `@axe-core/playwright` GitHub README but is not surfaced as a TypeScript compile error, making it a silent test misconfiguration.

```typescript
// File: e2e/fixtures/multi-region-axe.ts
// Workaround for @axe-core/playwright single-selector include() limitation.
// Runs one AxeBuilder per selector and merges violations by rule ID + target.
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';
import type { Page } from '@playwright/test';
import type { Result } from 'axe-core';

interface MultiRegionScanOptions {
  selectors: string[];
  tags?: string[];
}

export async function scanMultipleRegions(
  page: Page,
  { selectors, tags = ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'] }: MultiRegionScanOptions
): Promise<Result[]> {
  const allViolations: Result[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();

  for (const selector of selectors) {
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include(selector)
      .withTags(tags)
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'] })
      .analyze();

    for (const violation of results.violations) {
      for (const node of violation.nodes) {
        const key = `${violation.id}::${node.target.join(',')}`;
        if (!seen.has(key)) {
          seen.add(key);
          const existing = allViolations.find((v) => v.id === violation.id);
          if (existing) {
            existing.nodes.push(node);
          } else {
            allViolations.push({ ...violation, nodes: [node] });
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }

  return allViolations;
}
```

**Tradeoff note:** The per-selector loop approach is slower than a single full-page scan because axe initialises and runs separately for each region. For scans with more than 5 selectors, prefer the comma-separated compound selector approach (`'.main-content, .sidebar, .nav'`) if the selectors are stable — this runs axe once. Use the per-selector loop only when each region needs different rule sets or exclusions. [official]
