### Pattern 94 (Cycle 39) — WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry: Shipping Address Pre-Population Test

**Description:** WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7 (Redundant Entry, Level A) requires that information previously entered by the user in the same session is either auto-populated or available for the user to select — they must not be asked to re-type it. The canonical use case is checkout flows where billing address is asked after shipping address: if the user entered a shipping address, the billing address form must either auto-populate from shipping or offer a "Same as shipping" checkbox. This SC targets cognitive-load reduction for users with memory or motor disabilities. The test validates that the billing form is pre-populated (or offers pre-population) after a shipping address is entered in the same session — a check that standard axe scans do not cover.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/redundant-entry-checkout.spec.ts
// Tests WCAG 3.3.7: billing address pre-populated from shipping in checkout flow.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry — checkout address pre-population', () => {
  test('billing address is pre-populated or offers same-as-shipping option', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout/shipping');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Fill in shipping address
    await page.getByLabel(/first name/i).fill('Alice');
    await page.getByLabel(/last name/i).fill('Smith');
    await page.getByLabel(/address/i).first().fill('123 Main St');
    await page.getByLabel(/city/i).fill('Springfield');
    await page.getByLabel(/postal|zip/i).fill('12345');

    // Proceed to billing step
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /continue|next|proceed/i }).click();
    await page.waitForURL(/billing|payment/);
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Check for either: pre-populated fields OR a "same as shipping" checkbox
    const sameAsShipping = page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: /same as shipping/i });
    const billingFirstName = page.getByLabel(/first name/i);

    const hasSameAsShipping = await sameAsShipping.isVisible().catch(() => false);
    const prepopulatedName = hasSameAsShipping
      ? null
      : await billingFirstName.inputValue().catch(() => '');

    const satisfiesRedundantEntry = hasSameAsShipping || prepopulatedName === 'Alice';

    expect(
      satisfiesRedundantEntry,
      'WCAG 3.3.7: billing form must either pre-populate from shipping or offer "Same as shipping" checkbox'
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  test('multi-step form does not re-ask for email entered on step 1', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout/contact');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const testEmail = 'qa-test@example.com';
    await page.getByLabel(/email/i).fill(testEmail);
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next|continue/i }).click();
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // On subsequent steps, email should not be re-requested empty
    const emailFields = page.getByLabel(/email/i);
    const count = await emailFields.count();
    if (count > 0) {
      const value = await emailFields.first().inputValue();
      expect(
        value,
        'WCAG 3.3.7: email must be pre-filled if shown again in the flow'
      ).toBe(testEmail);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** WCAG 3.3.7 has an exception for security-sensitive information (passwords, payment CVV) — these must NOT be pre-populated. Also excepted: information that has expired or is no longer valid. Tests for 3.3.7 are inherently application-specific and cannot be automated by axe; include them in your manual E2E accessibility checklist for multi-step forms. [official]

---

### Pattern 95 (Cycle 39) — `@axe-core/vitest` Component-Level Accessibility Testing

**Description:** `@axe-core/vitest` (part of the axe-core-npm monorepo) provides a Vitest-native matcher `toHaveNoViolations()` and the `checkA11y()` helper that integrates with Vitest's test runner without requiring Jest. As Vitest adoption grows (it has become the default in Vite-based projects including SvelteKit, Nuxt 3, and many React/Vue setups), teams should prefer `@axe-core/vitest` over `jest-axe` for component tests. Unlike `jest-axe`, `@axe-core/vitest` ships as a dual CJS/ESM package and works with Vitest's native ES module handling without `transformIgnorePatterns` workarounds. The API mirrors `jest-axe` closely, enabling straightforward migration. Pairing with `@testing-library/svelte`, `@testing-library/vue`, or `@testing-library/react` gives component-level axe scanning in the same test runtime as the component tests.

```typescript
// File: src/components/Alert/Alert.test.ts
// @axe-core/vitest component accessibility test — Vitest + @testing-library/react
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { axe, toHaveNoViolations } from '@axe-core/vitest';
import Alert from './Alert';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

describe('Alert component — accessibility', () => {
  it('renders with role="alert" and passes axe scan', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <Alert type="error" message="Something went wrong. Please try again." />
    );

    const results = await axe(container, {
      rules: {
        // Suppress region landmark rule — tested at page level, not component level
        region: { enabled: false },
      },
    });

    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('success alert has role="status" not role="alert"', async () => {
    const { getByRole } = render(
      <Alert type="success" message="Your changes were saved." />
    );

    // Success messages should use role="status" (polite) not role="alert" (assertive)
    expect(getByRole('status')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(() => getByRole('alert')).toThrow();
  });

  it('dismissible alert has accessible close button', async () => {
    const { getByRole, container } = render(
      <Alert type="info" message="New update available." dismissible />
    );

    const closeButton = getByRole('button', { name: /close|dismiss/i });
    expect(closeButton).toBeInTheDocument();

    const results = await axe(container);
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `@axe-core/vitest` requires Vitest ≥ 1.0 and is not compatible with Jest. If your project uses both Jest (for unit tests) and Vitest (for component tests), use `jest-axe` for Jest contexts and `@axe-core/vitest` for Vitest contexts — do not mix them. The `axe()` function in both packages accepts the same options object, so rule configuration is portable between them. [official]

---

### Pattern 96 (Cycle 39) — Playwright `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` for Form Validation Tests

**Description:** Playwright v1.50 added `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` which asserts that an element has a valid accessible error message exposed via `aria-errormessage`. This assertion validates two things: (1) the `aria-errormessage` attribute exists and points to a valid non-empty element in the DOM, and (2) the referenced element contains text matching the expected value. Previously, testing `aria-errormessage` required chaining `getAttribute('aria-errormessage')` + DOM lookup + text content assertion — three steps that could not be expressed as a single semantic assertion. The matcher is particularly important for WCAG 3.3.1 (Error Identification) compliance: it ensures the error is both programmatically associated (AT will announce it) and contains human-readable text. It also validates that the `aria-errormessage` ID reference is not broken (pointing to a non-existent element).

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/form-error-message.spec.ts
// Tests WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification via Playwright's toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage().
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification — aria-errormessage', () => {
  test('required field shows accessible error message after submit', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/registration');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Submit without filling required fields
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit|register/i }).click();
    await page.waitForTimeout(300); // Allow validation to run

    const emailInput = page.getByLabel(/email/i);

    // Assert: input has aria-invalid="true" and accessible error message
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(/required|enter.*email/i);
  });

  test('invalid email format shows format-specific error', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/registration');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const emailInput = page.getByLabel(/email/i);
    await emailInput.fill('not-an-email');
    await emailInput.blur();
    await page.waitForTimeout(200);

    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(/valid email|format/i);
  });

  test('error clears after valid input is entered', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/registration');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const emailInput = page.getByLabel(/email/i);
    await emailInput.fill('bad');
    await emailInput.blur();
    await page.waitForTimeout(200);

    // Error should be present
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');

    // Fix the value
    await emailInput.fill('good@example.com');
    await emailInput.blur();
    await page.waitForTimeout(200);

    // Error should clear — aria-invalid removed or set to "false"
    const ariaInvalid = await emailInput.getAttribute('aria-invalid');
    expect(ariaInvalid === null || ariaInvalid === 'false').toBe(true);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` requires Playwright ≥ 1.50 and will fail if the element uses `aria-describedby` for errors instead of `aria-errormessage` — these are different attributes with different AT behavior. `aria-errormessage` is only announced when `aria-invalid="true"` is also set; tests that assert `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage` without also asserting `aria-invalid="true"` miss half the contract. [official]

---

### Pattern 97 (Cycle 39) — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size: Minimum 24×24 CSS Pixel Touch Target Test

**Description:** WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (Target Size Minimum, AA) requires interactive targets to be at least 24×24 CSS pixels, or to have sufficient spacing such that a 24px diameter circle centred on the target does not intersect another target's circle. This criterion was introduced to reduce errors for users with motor disabilities, tremors, or who use touch screens. The spacing-offset exception means small targets (e.g., 16×16 icon buttons) are compliant if they have at least 4px spacing to the nearest target on all sides. axe-core includes a `target-size` rule tagged `wcag22aa` that fires on clear failures, but complex spacing calculations may be flagged as `incomplete` rather than violations. This test supplements axe by computing bounding boxes directly for all interactive elements and asserting the combined target+spacing criterion.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/target-size.spec.ts
// Tests WCAG 2.5.8: all interactive targets meet 24×24 CSS px minimum or spacing exception.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

const MIN_TARGET_PX = 24;

test.describe('WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size Minimum', () => {
  test('axe-core target-size rule passes on the page', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag22aa'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'] })
      .analyze();

    const targetSizeViolations = results.violations.filter((v) => v.id === 'target-size');
    expect(
      targetSizeViolations,
      `target-size axe violations:\n` +
        targetSizeViolations.map((v) => v.nodes.map((n) => n.html).join('\n')).join('\n')
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('all interactive elements are at least 24×24 CSS px', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const failingTargets = await page.evaluate((minPx: number) => {
      const selectors =
        'a[href], button:not([disabled]), [role="button"], ' +
        'input[type="checkbox"], input[type="radio"]';
      const elements = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(selectors));

      return elements
        .filter((el) => {
          const box = el.getBoundingClientRect();
          return box.width > 0 && box.height > 0 && (box.width < minPx || box.height < minPx);
        })
        .map((el) => ({
          tag: el.tagName,
          text: el.textContent?.trim().slice(0, 40) ?? '',
          width: Math.round(el.getBoundingClientRect().width),
          height: Math.round(el.getBoundingClientRect().height),
          selector: el.className ? `.${el.className.split(' ')[0]}` : el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
        }));
    }, MIN_TARGET_PX);

    expect(
      failingTargets,
      `These interactive elements are smaller than ${MIN_TARGET_PX}×${MIN_TARGET_PX}px (WCAG 2.5.8):\n` +
        failingTargets
          .map((t) => `  ${t.tag} "${t.text}" ${t.width}×${t.height}px (${t.selector})`)
          .join('\n')
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** The raw size check does not implement the full spacing-offset exception computation (which requires measuring the nearest neighbour's bounding box). A target that is 16×16 with 4px spacing all around passes WCAG 2.5.8 but will fail the raw size assertion. For precision, implement the full spacing algorithm or treat axe's `target-size` rule as the authoritative gate and use the raw size check only as an early warning. [official]

---

### Pattern 98 (Cycle 39) — High Contrast Mode (`forced-colors`) Testing with Playwright Media Emulation

**Description:** Windows High Contrast Mode (and the CSS `forced-colors: active` media feature) replaces the author's color scheme with a system-defined high-contrast palette. Elements that rely on `background-color` or `border-color` for visual differentiation (e.g., custom focus rings painted purely with `box-shadow`, SVG fills set via CSS variables) become invisible because the forced-colors engine replaces those CSS properties. WCAG 1.4.11 (Non-text Contrast) and 1.4.3 (Contrast Minimum) still apply but forced-colors compliance requires using `forced-color-adjust: none` selectively and CSS `ButtonText`, `Highlight`, `HighlightText` system colour keywords. This test emulates forced-colors in Playwright to verify focus indicators and interactive elements remain visible.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/forced-colors.spec.ts
// Tests accessibility in forced-colors (Windows High Contrast) mode via Playwright emulation.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Forced colors (High Contrast Mode) accessibility', () => {
  test('focus indicators are visible in forced-colors mode', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' });
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Tab to first interactive element and verify the focus indicator is non-zero
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focusedElement = page.locator(':focus');
    await expect(focusedElement).toBeFocused();

    const outline = await focusedElement.evaluate((el) => {
      const style = window.getComputedStyle(el);
      return {
        outlineStyle: style.outlineStyle,
        outlineWidth: style.outlineWidth,
        outlineColor: style.outlineColor,
      };
    });

    expect(
      outline.outlineStyle,
      'Focus indicator outline-style should not be "none" in forced-colors'
    ).not.toBe('none');
    expect(
      parseFloat(outline.outlineWidth),
      'Focus indicator outline-width should be > 0px in forced-colors'
    ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('custom buttons retain perceivable border in forced-colors mode', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' });
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const buttons = page.getByRole('button');
    const count = await buttons.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 5); i++) {
      const btn = buttons.nth(i);
      const borderWidth = await btn.evaluate(
        (el) => parseFloat(window.getComputedStyle(el).borderWidth)
      );
      // In forced-colors mode, buttons should have a non-zero border or outline
      // to remain distinguishable without relying on background-color
      expect(
        borderWidth,
        `Button "${await btn.textContent()}" has no border in forced-colors mode`
      ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0); // Advisory — adjust to > 0 if your design requires visible borders
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' })` is a Playwright emulation — it sets the CSS media feature but does not invoke the Windows OS High Contrast engine. Complex SVG and canvas elements may behave differently under actual OS High Contrast. Always supplement Playwright forced-colors emulation with a real Windows High Contrast Mode manual audit before major releases. [official]

---

### Pattern 99 (Cycle 39) — ARIA `aria-haspopup` and Submenu Keyboard Contract Test

**Description:** `aria-haspopup` communicates to AT users that activating a control will open a popup (menu, listbox, tree, grid, or dialog). The attribute has distinct valid values: `"menu"`, `"listbox"`, `"tree"`, `"grid"`, `"dialog"`, and `"true"` (synonym for `"menu"`). Using the wrong value (e.g., `aria-haspopup="true"` on a combobox that opens a `role="listbox"`) causes screen readers to announce incorrect popup semantics. The keyboard contract for `aria-haspopup="menu"` buttons requires: Enter/Space opens the menu, Escape closes it and returns focus to the button, arrow keys navigate menu items. This test validates the full contract including focus management on close.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/aria-haspopup-submenu.spec.ts
// Tests aria-haspopup attribute correctness and keyboard contract for nav menus.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('aria-haspopup keyboard contract', () => {
  test('navigation button with aria-haspopup="menu" opens menu on Enter', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const menuButton = page.locator('[aria-haspopup="menu"], [aria-haspopup="true"]').first();
    await menuButton.focus();
    await expect(menuButton).toBeFocused();

    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
    await page.waitForTimeout(200);

    // Popup should now be expanded
    await expect(menuButton).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

    const menuItems = page.locator('[role="menuitem"], [role="option"]');
    const itemCount = await menuItems.count();
    expect(itemCount, 'Menu must contain at least one item after opening').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('Escape closes menu and returns focus to trigger button', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const menuButton = page.locator('[aria-haspopup="menu"], [aria-haspopup="true"]').first();
    await menuButton.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
    await page.waitForTimeout(200);

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await page.waitForTimeout(200);

    // Focus returns to the trigger button and menu is collapsed
    await expect(menuButton).toBeFocused();
    await expect(menuButton).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  });

  test('aria-haspopup value matches the actual popup role', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const haspopupElements = page.locator('[aria-haspopup]');
    const count = await haspopupElements.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const el = haspopupElements.nth(i);
      const haspopupValue = await el.getAttribute('aria-haspopup');
      const ariaControls = await el.getAttribute('aria-controls');

      if (ariaControls) {
        const popup = page.locator(`#${ariaControls}`);
        const popupRole = await popup.getAttribute('role');
        if (popupRole && haspopupValue && haspopupValue !== 'true') {
          expect(
            haspopupValue,
            `aria-haspopup="${haspopupValue}" should match popup role="${popupRole}"`
          ).toBe(popupRole);
        }
      }
    }
  });

  test('no axe violations on navigation menus', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include('nav')
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'] })
      .analyze();

    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `aria-haspopup="true"` is a legacy value that maps to `"menu"` — it is still valid per ARIA 1.2 but less explicit. Prefer specific values (`"menu"`, `"listbox"`, `"dialog"`) to enable accurate AT announcements. `aria-haspopup` without `aria-expanded` is incomplete — AT users cannot know the current state; always pair them. [official]

### Pattern 100 (Cycle 39) — axe-core RGAA Tag Compliance Scan (French Accessibility Framework)

**Description:** axe-core 4.11.0 (October 2025) added RGAA (Référentiel Général d'Amélioration de l'Accessibilité) tags to rules, enabling French public-sector organizations and EU companies targeting French markets to run targeted RGAA compliance scans. RGAA 4.1 is the French national standard derived from WCAG 2.1; it maps to specific criteria numbers (e.g., `rgaa42`) that differ from WCAG SC numbering. Using `.withTags(['rgaa42'])` in `AxeBuilder` runs only the rules mapped to RGAA 4.2 criteria. This is distinct from WCAG tags — some WCAG rules are not mapped to RGAA and vice versa. Teams building for French government clients or EU digital services must run both `wcag21aa` and `rgaa42` tag sets to achieve full bi-standard compliance.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/rgaa-compliance.spec.ts
// Tests RGAA 4.2 compliance using axe-core 4.11.0+ RGAA tags.
// Use for French public sector / EU digital services accessibility compliance.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

const CRITICAL_PAGES = [
  { url: '/', name: 'Homepage' },
  { url: '/services', name: 'Services' },
  { url: '/contact', name: 'Contact' },
];

for (const { url, name } of CRITICAL_PAGES) {
  test(`${name} — RGAA 4.2 compliance scan`, async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto(url);
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Run RGAA-specific rules alongside WCAG 2.1 AA
    const [rgaaResults, wcagResults] = await Promise.all([
      new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .withTags(['rgaa42'])
        .options({ resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'] })
        .analyze(),
      new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
        .options({ resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'] })
        .analyze(),
    ]);

    // Combine unique violation IDs from both scans
    const allViolationIds = new Set([
      ...rgaaResults.violations.map((v) => v.id),
      ...wcagResults.violations.map((v) => v.id),
    ]);

    expect(
      [...allViolationIds],
      `${name}: accessibility violations found in RGAA+WCAG scan:\n` +
        [...allViolationIds].join(', ')
    ).toHaveLength(0);

    if (rgaaResults.incomplete.length > 0) {
      console.warn(
        `${name}: ${rgaaResults.incomplete.length} RGAA criteria require manual review:\n` +
          rgaaResults.incomplete.map((i) => `  ${i.id}: ${i.description}`).join('\n')
      );
    }
  });
}
```

**Tradeoff note:** RGAA tags were added in axe-core 4.11.0 — earlier versions will silently return zero results for `withTags(['rgaa42'])` rather than throwing an error. Always verify the axe-core version installed in your project before relying on RGAA scan results. The RGAA criterion-to-axe-rule mapping is not 1:1 with WCAG — consult the official RGAA 4.2 technical mapping document to identify criteria that require manual testing (complex images, captcha, complex tables). [official]

### Pattern 101 (Cycle 39) — Playwright ARIA Snapshot `mode: 'partial'` for Cross-Platform CI Stability

**Description:** `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` (Playwright ≥ 1.49) can generate fragile baselines when running on different OS/browser combinations because the accessibility tree computation differs between macOS (Accessibility API) and Linux (AT-SPI2). Playwright 1.59+ added a `mode` option to `ariaSnapshot()` and `toMatchAriaSnapshot()`: `mode: 'partial'` asserts that the expected YAML structure is a subset of the actual tree rather than an exact match. This is the recommended approach for CI environments running on a different OS than developer machines. Using partial mode also makes snapshots more maintainable — minor structural changes (e.g., a new ARIA landmark added to the page) do not invalidate snapshot tests that are only concerned with a specific component's tree.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/aria-snapshot-partial.spec.ts
// Uses toMatchAriaSnapshot with mode:'partial' for cross-platform CI stability (Playwright 1.59+).
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA snapshot — partial mode for cross-platform CI', () => {
  test('navigation menu ARIA structure — partial snapshot', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const nav = page.locator('nav[aria-label]').first();

    // mode: 'partial' — only assert the parts we care about
    // Safe to run on macOS dev boxes AND Linux CI without OS-specific baseline generation
    await expect(nav).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - navigation:
        - list:
          - listitem:
            - link
    `, { mode: 'partial' });
  });

  test('dialog ARIA structure includes heading and close button', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open.*settings|preferences/i }).click();
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="dialog"]');

    const dialog = page.locator('[role="dialog"]');

    await expect(dialog).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - dialog:
        - heading
        - button /close|dismiss/i
    `, { mode: 'partial' });
  });

  test('generate baseline snapshot scoped to depth 3', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const mainContent = page.locator('main');

    // depth option (Playwright 1.59+) limits snapshot verbosity for large pages
    const snapshot = await mainContent.ariaSnapshot({ depth: 3 });

    // Partial assertion — stable across OS environments
    await expect(mainContent).toMatchAriaSnapshot(snapshot, { mode: 'partial' });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `mode: 'partial'` reduces test specificity — a page with a severely degraded accessibility tree may still pass if the asserted subset happens to remain intact. Use partial mode for cross-platform structural smoke tests and supplement with full-mode snapshots generated on a locked CI platform (e.g., a Docker Linux container) for authoritative regression detection. The `depth` option limits snapshot verbosity for large pages — use `depth: 3` or `depth: 4` for component-level snapshots. [official]

---

### Pattern 102 (Cycle 39) — `aria-busy` State Test for Asynchronous Content Loading

**Description:** `aria-busy="true"` signals to AT that a region is being updated and they should wait before reading its content. Without `aria-busy`, screen readers may announce the intermediate loading state ("Loading…" placeholder text) as if it were the final content, causing confusion. The pattern is: set `aria-busy="true"` on the container before the async operation starts, update the content, then set `aria-busy="false"` (or remove the attribute) when the update is complete. This is particularly important for data tables, dashboards, and search results panels. `aria-busy` is complementary to `aria-live` — `aria-busy` suppresses announcements during the update while `aria-live` announces the update when it completes. axe-core does not currently check `aria-busy` usage, making this a manual/semi-automated test pattern.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/aria-busy-loading.spec.ts
// Tests aria-busy lifecycle: must be true during async update, false/absent after completion.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('aria-busy state management for async content', () => {
  test('search results region clears aria-busy after results load', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const searchInput = page
      .getByRole('searchbox')
      .or(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /search/i }));
    const resultsRegion = page
      .locator('[role="region"][aria-label*="result"], [aria-live], [role="status"]')
      .first();

    await searchInput.fill('accessibility testing');
    await searchInput.press('Enter');

    // Capture transient aria-busy=true if present (advisory check)
    let observedBusy = false;
    try {
      await page.waitForFunction(
        () =>
          Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[role="region"], [aria-live], main')).some(
            (el) => el.getAttribute('aria-busy') === 'true'
          ),
        { timeout: 2000 }
      );
      observedBusy = true;
    } catch {
      console.warn(
        'aria-busy="true" was not observed during search loading — ' +
          'consider implementing for better AT UX (WCAG advisory)'
      );
    }

    // After loading, aria-busy must be cleared
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    const finalBusyState = await resultsRegion.getAttribute('aria-busy').catch(() => null);
    expect(
      finalBusyState === null || finalBusyState === 'false',
      'aria-busy must be removed or set to "false" after content loads'
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  test('data table clears aria-busy after sort completes', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/data-table');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const table = page.locator('table, [role="grid"], [role="table"]').first();
    const sortableHeader = page
      .locator('th[aria-sort], [role="columnheader"][aria-sort]')
      .first();

    if (await sortableHeader.isVisible()) {
      await sortableHeader.click();
      await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

      const finalBusy = await table.getAttribute('aria-busy');
      expect(
        finalBusy === null || finalBusy === 'false',
        'table aria-busy must clear after sort completes'
      ).toBe(true);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `aria-busy` is not validated by axe-core — it is a progressive enhancement that improves the AT experience but does not surface as an automated violation when absent. Prioritize implementing `aria-busy` for regions with slow async operations (>500ms). For regions using skeleton loaders, the skeleton content itself should be hidden from AT with `aria-hidden="true"` rather than using `aria-busy`. [community]

### Pattern 103 (Cycle 39) — `@axe-core/playwright` Deferred Iframe Accessibility Scan

**Description:** `@axe-core/playwright` by default skips cross-origin iframes because the browser's same-origin policy prevents axe from injecting into them. Same-origin iframes are scanned by default. For applications that embed same-origin iframes (e.g., a payment form in a sandboxed iframe, a rich text editor in an iframe), axe's default behavior scans the iframe content automatically. However, iframes that are loaded lazily (via IntersectionObserver or explicit `src` injection) may not have loaded when the first `analyze()` call is made, resulting in the iframe content being silently skipped. The test pattern waits for iframe content to be ready before scanning and explicitly verifies the iframe was included in the scan.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/iframe-scan.spec.ts
// Tests that same-origin iframes are included in axe scans after lazy load.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('iframe accessibility scanning', () => {
  test('same-origin iframe is included in axe scan', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/page-with-iframe');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Wait for lazy iframe src to be set before scanning
    await page.waitForSelector('iframe[src]:not([src=""])', { timeout: 5000 });

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'] })
      .analyze();

    // Iframe violations are surfaced with nested target arrays: [['iframe', '#el-inside']]
    const hasIframeContent = results.violations.some((v) =>
      v.nodes.some((n) => Array.isArray(n.target[0]))
    );
    console.log(
      hasIframeContent
        ? 'Iframe content was scanned — violations found inside it'
        : 'Iframe content was scanned — no violations inside'
    );

    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('iframe form fields have accessible labels', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/page-with-iframe');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const frame = page.frameLocator('iframe').first();
    const inputs = frame.locator('input:not([type="hidden"])');
    const inputCount = await inputs.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < inputCount; i++) {
      const input = inputs.nth(i);
      const ariaLabel = await input.getAttribute('aria-label');
      const ariaLabelledby = await input.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
      const id = await input.getAttribute('id');

      let hasLabel = !!(ariaLabel || ariaLabelledby);
      if (!hasLabel && id) {
        const label = frame.locator(`label[for="${id}"]`);
        hasLabel = (await label.count()) > 0;
      }

      expect(hasLabel, `Input at index ${i} inside iframe has no accessible label`).toBe(true);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Cross-origin iframes (e.g., Stripe payment iframes, third-party embeds) cannot be scanned by axe due to browser same-origin policy. Document these as known scan exclusions and rely on the third-party vendor's own accessibility conformance statements. For same-origin iframes, ensure the page has reached `networkidle` before scanning — lazy-loaded iframes will be silently skipped if their `src` is not yet set at scan time. [official]

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 39)

179. **[community] Playwright `page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')` does not guarantee that React `useEffect` hooks triggered by route changes have completed — axe scans run immediately after `networkidle` can miss dynamically rendered ARIA roles injected by effects that fire after the initial hydration**: In React applications using Next.js or Remix, `networkidle` signals that no network requests are in flight, but React's `useEffect` hooks (which run after the render is committed to the DOM) may fire after the last network request completes. If an effect injects `role="status"`, `aria-live`, or `aria-expanded` attributes, the axe scan may run before these attributes are in the DOM. WHY: Teams observe intermittent axe failures in CI that cannot be reproduced locally — the race window is smaller on developer machines due to faster CPU. The fix is to use `page.waitForSelector('[aria-live]')` or `page.waitForFunction(() => document.querySelectorAll('[role="dialog"]').length > 0)` after `networkidle` to ensure effect-injected ARIA attributes are present before scanning. [community]

180. **[community] `aria-describedby` and `aria-errormessage` are not interchangeable — using `aria-describedby` to announce form errors works in most screen readers but fails WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages because `aria-describedby` is only announced when the user navigates to the element, not when the error is dynamically injected**: Many form validation implementations use `aria-describedby` to associate an error message with an input field. While AT will announce the error when the user tabs to the input, `aria-describedby` does not trigger a live announcement when the error appears dynamically after a failed submit. `aria-errormessage` (combined with `aria-invalid="true"`) is the correct attribute for inline form errors; additionally a live region or `role="alert"` on the error container announces the error to users who are not currently focused on the input. WHY: Developers copy accessible form patterns from older tutorials that predate `aria-errormessage` (introduced in ARIA 1.1) and use `aria-describedby` throughout, missing the live announcement requirement that `aria-errormessage` combined with `aria-invalid` is designed to satisfy. [community]

181. **[community] Custom `<select>`-replacement dropdowns built with `role="listbox"` + `role="option"` do not support the AT type-ahead navigation contract on Android TalkBack — TalkBack does not implement the `listbox` keyboard contract and instead treats the widget as a flat list of clickable elements, making letter-by-letter type-ahead selection non-functional**: The ARIA `listbox` pattern specifies that AT should support type-ahead navigation (pressing "C" moves to the first option starting with "C"). This works correctly in NVDA, JAWS, and VoiceOver on macOS/iOS. However, TalkBack on Android does not implement listbox type-ahead — it instead reads each item sequentially. WHY: Teams test custom dropdowns with NVDA on Windows and pass accessibility review, then field complaints from Android users who cannot efficiently navigate long option lists. The practical fix for Android is to include a search/filter input above the listbox for lists with more than 10 items, so TalkBack users can filter rather than navigate item-by-item. [community]

182. **[community] `axe.run()` called inside a Jest `fake timers` context silently hangs and never resolves — `jest.useFakeTimers()` replaces `setTimeout`/`setInterval` globally, and axe-core's internal timeout mechanism (which uses `setTimeout` to break long scans into chunks) waits indefinitely for a fake timer that is never advanced**: This is a common source of test suite hangs in component tests that use jest-axe alongside Jest's fake timer API. The hang has no error message — the test simply times out after Jest's default timeout. WHY: axe-core's chunked processing uses real timers for cooperative multitasking; under fake timers these never fire. The fix is to call `jest.useRealTimers()` before running `axe()` and restore fakes afterward with `jest.useFakeTimers()` after the axe call completes. Alternatively, structure the test file to not mix fake timers and axe scans. [community]

183. **[community] React Strict Mode double-invocation of effects causes ARIA live regions to announce content twice in development builds — `useEffect` runs twice in React 18+ Strict Mode, which fires the `aria-live` region text setter twice, resulting in screen readers announcing messages double in the development environment but only once in production**: React 18 Strict Mode deliberately invokes effects twice (mount → unmount → mount) in development to surface side-effect bugs. If a live region announcement is implemented by setting state in a `useEffect`, the double invocation writes to the live region twice. In development, this causes double announcements in NVDA or VoiceOver. WHY: Developers who test with a screen reader in development mode hear doubled announcements and mistakenly conclude their live region implementation is broken — they then introduce de-duplication logic that breaks the production announcement (which runs only once). The diagnosis: always disable Strict Mode or test AT behavior in production builds, not development builds. [community]

184. **[community] Icon fonts (Font Awesome, Material Icons) using pseudo-element `::before` content with a Unicode glyph value have no accessible alternative by default — axe-core flags the parent element as needing an accessible name only if the element has an interactive role; purely decorative glyphs inside non-interactive elements pass axe but are still read aloud as Unicode code point characters by JAWS and NVDA**: Font icon glyphs rendered via CSS `content: "\f015"` in a `::before` pseudo-element are in the accessibility tree by default in some browsers. NVDA + Chrome reads the glyph as the Unicode character name (e.g., "house" for U+F015), which is tolerable for branded icons but nonsensical for private-use area glyphs. axe-core only flags this pattern when the icon is the sole content of an interactive element. WHY: Teams rely on axe to catch icon accessibility issues but axe only catches the most critical case (interactive element with no accessible name); purely decorative icons in non-interactive contexts pass axe even when they produce confusing announcements. The fix is to add `aria-hidden="true"` on all icon font elements — both interactive (where a real label must be provided separately) and non-interactive (to suppress the glyph reading). [community]
