## Cycle 40 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 104 (Cycle 40) — WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6 Consistent Help: Help Mechanism Position Regression Test

**Description:** WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6 (Level A) requires that any help mechanism present across multiple pages — human contact details, live chat, a FAQ link, or a chatbot trigger — must appear in the same relative serialization order on every page. The criterion measures DOM order, not visual position, so a sticky widget that appears visually in the bottom-right corner on all pages could still fail if its DOM position differs between pages. Regression risk is high after CMS template changes or navigation refactors that reorder landmark regions. The test pattern navigates to a set of representative pages, captures the DOM order of the help element relative to its parent container, and asserts consistency across pages.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/consistent-help.spec.ts
// Verifies WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6 — help mechanism serialization order is consistent.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const PAGES_UNDER_TEST = ['/', '/products', '/about', '/contact'];
const HELP_SELECTOR = '[data-testid="help-widget"], a[href*="support"], [aria-label*="chat"]';

async function getHelpSiblingIndex(page: import('@playwright/test').Page): Promise<number> {
  return page.evaluate((sel: string) => {
    const helpEl = document.querySelector(sel);
    if (!helpEl) return -1;
    const siblings = Array.from(helpEl.parentElement?.children ?? []);
    return siblings.indexOf(helpEl as Element);
  }, HELP_SELECTOR);
}

test.describe('WCAG 3.2.6 Consistent Help position', () => {
  test('help widget appears at the same sibling index on every page', async ({ page }) => {
    const indices: number[] = [];

    for (const path of PAGES_UNDER_TEST) {
      await page.goto(path);
      await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');
      const idx = await getHelpSiblingIndex(page);
      expect(idx, `Help element not found on ${path}`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
      indices.push(idx);
    }

    const firstIndex = indices[0];
    for (let i = 1; i < indices.length; i++) {
      expect(
        indices[i],
        `Help element sibling index differs on ${PAGES_UNDER_TEST[i]}: expected ${firstIndex}, got ${indices[i]}`
      ).toBe(firstIndex);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** This test requires a curated list of pages; it cannot automatically discover all pages in a site. Single-page applications with client-side routing can produce false negatives if the help widget is rendered by a shared layout component that is never re-mounted — in that case the DOM node persists across routes and the position cannot regress. Verify with a real multi-page or SSR application where templates can diverge. [official]

---

### Pattern 105 (Cycle 40) — WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 Dragging Movements: Alternative Controls Presence Test

**Description:** WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7 (Level AA) mandates that every function performed by a drag operation must also be achievable by a single pointer action without dragging. Common drag interactions include sortable lists, range sliders with thumb dragging, kanban card reordering, resizable panels, and map interactions. Playwright can detect elements with `draggable="true"` or elements that register `dragstart` event listeners, and then assert that sibling or parent containers provide a non-drag mechanism (buttons, context menus, or numeric inputs for sliders). The test is semi-automated — it flags widgets with no detectable alternative for manual follow-up rather than producing a definitive pass/fail.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/dragging-movements.spec.ts
// Detects draggable elements and checks for non-drag alternatives (WCAG 2.5.7).
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging Movements', () => {
  test('all draggable elements have a non-drag alternative', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const draggableInfo = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const draggables = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[draggable="true"]'));
      return draggables.map((el) => {
        const parent = el.closest('[data-sortable], [data-kanban], [role="list"]') ?? el.parentElement;
        const hasButtonAlternative = (parent?.querySelectorAll('button').length ?? 0) > 0;
        const hasMenuAlternative = (parent?.querySelectorAll('[role="menu"], [role="menuitem"]').length ?? 0) > 0;
        const hasInputAlternative = (parent?.querySelectorAll('input[type="number"]').length ?? 0) > 0;
        return {
          tagName: el.tagName,
          ariaLabel: (el as HTMLElement).getAttribute('aria-label') ?? '',
          hasAlternative: hasButtonAlternative || hasMenuAlternative || hasInputAlternative,
        };
      });
    });

    const missingAlternatives = draggableInfo.filter((d) => !d.hasAlternative);
    expect(
      missingAlternatives,
      `Draggable elements without non-drag alternatives: ${JSON.stringify(missingAlternatives)}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** JavaScript event listener detection (whether an element handles `dragstart`) is not possible from the Playwright page context without injecting a monkey-patch before page load — the approach of targeting `[draggable="true"]` only catches elements using the HTML drag-and-drop API, not pointer-event-based drag implementations (e.g., custom sortable libraries using `pointermove`). For pointer-event-based drag widgets, supplement with a manual review checklist. [official]

---

### Pattern 106 (Cycle 40) — WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance: Minimum Focus Indicator Area and Contrast Check

**Description:** WCAG 2.4.13 (Level AAA) specifies that keyboard focus indicators must meet two measurable criteria: the indicator area must be at least as large as a 2 CSS pixel perimeter around the unfocused component, and the contrast ratio between focused and unfocused states must be at least 3:1. Unlike other contrast criteria that measure foreground-to-background ratios, SC 2.4.13 measures the ratio between the same pixels in the two states — making it untestable by standard color contrast tools. The pattern uses Playwright to compare screenshots of an element in focused and unfocused states and then uses the axe best-practice rule `focus-visible` as an automated proxy, supplemented by screenshot attachment for manual measurement.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/focus-appearance.spec.ts
// Tests focus indicator visibility using axe best-practice rules and manual screenshot comparison.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance', () => {
  test('interactive elements have a visible focus indicator (axe best-practice)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['best-practice'])
      .options({ runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['best-practice'] } })
      .analyze();

    const focusViolations = results.violations.filter(
      (v) => v.id === 'focus-visible' || v.id === 'scrollable-region-focusable'
    );
    expect(focusViolations, JSON.stringify(focusViolations, null, 2)).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('primary call-to-action button has visually distinct focus style', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const button = page.locator('button[data-testid="primary-cta"]').first();

    // Capture unfocused screenshot
    const unfocused = await button.screenshot();

    // Tab to focus the button
    await button.focus();
    await page.waitForTimeout(50); // allow CSS transition to settle

    // Capture focused screenshot
    const focused = await button.screenshot();

    // Screenshots must differ (focus style changes at least one pixel)
    expect(Buffer.compare(unfocused, focused)).not.toBe(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** axe-core's `focus-visible` best-practice rule only checks that `outline: none` or `outline: 0` is not applied without a replacement — it does not measure indicator size or the 3:1 contrast-change requirement from SC 2.4.13. The screenshot comparison asserts visual difference exists but cannot compute the exact contrast-change ratio without a pixel-level image diffing library (e.g., `pixelmatch`). For AAA compliance sign-off, manual measurement with a browser devtools color picker remains necessary. [official]

---

### Pattern 107 (Cycle 40) — ARIA Carousel Pattern: `aria-roledescription` and `aria-live` State Verification

**Description:** The ARIA Authoring Practices Guide carousel pattern requires the carousel container to have `aria-roledescription="carousel"` and each slide to have `aria-roledescription="slide"` with an accessible name indicating its position (e.g., "3 of 10"). Auto-rotating carousels must set `aria-live="off"` on the slide container to suppress continuous announcements; paused carousels use `aria-live="polite"`. The rotation control button label must change dynamically between "Stop slide rotation" and "Start slide rotation". The pattern verifies each of these requirements programmatically and also confirms that auto-rotation stops when keyboard focus enters the carousel.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/carousel.spec.ts
// Verifies ARIA carousel pattern compliance per APG requirements.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Carousel pattern compliance', () => {
  test('carousel container has correct roledescription and label', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/homepage');
    await page.waitForSelector('[aria-roledescription="carousel"]');

    const carousel = page.locator('[aria-roledescription="carousel"]').first();
    await expect(carousel).toHaveAttribute('aria-roledescription', 'carousel');

    // Must have an accessible name
    const label = await carousel.getAttribute('aria-label')
      ?? await carousel.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    expect(label, 'Carousel must have aria-label or aria-labelledby').toBeTruthy();
  });

  test('slides have roledescription and position name', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/homepage');
    const slides = page.locator('[aria-roledescription="slide"]');
    const count = await slides.count();
    expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const label = await slides.nth(i).getAttribute('aria-label');
      expect(label, `Slide ${i + 1} must have aria-label with position`).toMatch(/\d+ of \d+/);
    }
  });

  test('auto-rotation stops when keyboard focus enters carousel', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/homepage');
    const firstSlide = page.locator('[aria-roledescription="slide"]').first();
    const initialLabel = await firstSlide.getAttribute('aria-label');

    // Move focus into carousel
    await page.locator('[aria-roledescription="carousel"] button').first().focus();
    await page.waitForTimeout(2000); // wait longer than typical auto-rotate interval

    const afterFocusLabel = await firstSlide.getAttribute('aria-label');
    expect(afterFocusLabel).toBe(initialLabel); // slide did not advance
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** The auto-rotation stop test requires knowledge of the carousel's rotation interval; the 2-second wait is a heuristic that may be too short for slow-rotating carousels or produce false failures if the carousel has no auto-rotation. Parameterize the wait based on the component's known rotation interval, or read it from a data attribute. `aria-roledescription` values are not validated by axe-core — this manual assertion is the only automated check for the carousel naming contract. [official]

---

### Pattern 108 (Cycle 40) — ARIA Accordion: `aria-expanded` and Heading Level Regression Test

**Description:** ARIA accordion headers must be buttons wrapped in heading elements at the appropriate level (`<h2>`, `<h3>`, etc.) with `aria-expanded` set to `"true"` when open and `"false"` when closed. The region container (when used) must reference its controlling button via `aria-labelledby`. A common regression is resetting `aria-expanded` to `undefined` rather than `"false"` when a panel closes, which causes screen readers to announce no expanded state at all. The test pattern opens and closes each accordion panel and asserts that `aria-expanded` is explicitly `"false"` on closed panels.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/accordion.spec.ts
// Validates ARIA accordion pattern: heading roles, aria-expanded lifecycle, and region labeling.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Accordion pattern', () => {
  test('all accordion buttons have aria-expanded and are in a heading', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

    const buttons = page.locator('[role="button"][aria-expanded], button[aria-expanded]');
    const count = await buttons.count();
    expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const btn = buttons.nth(i);
      const expanded = await btn.getAttribute('aria-expanded');
      expect(['true', 'false'], `aria-expanded must be "true" or "false", not "${expanded}"`).toContain(expanded);

      // Button must be inside a heading element
      const inHeading = await btn.evaluate((el) => {
        const headings = ['H1','H2','H3','H4','H5','H6'];
        return headings.includes((el.parentElement?.tagName ?? ''));
      });
      expect(inHeading, `Accordion button at index ${i} is not inside a heading element`).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test('aria-expanded transitions correctly on open/close', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const firstButton = page.locator('button[aria-expanded]').first();

    // Ensure it starts closed
    if (await firstButton.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true') {
      await firstButton.click();
    }
    await expect(firstButton).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

    // Open
    await firstButton.click();
    await expect(firstButton).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

    // Close again
    await firstButton.click();
    await expect(firstButton).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false'); // must be "false", not undefined
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** This test assumes accordions use the `aria-expanded` attribute directly on the button; some implementations use a wrapper element with `aria-expanded` and a child `<button>`. The locator strategy may need adjustment for non-standard implementations. Setting `aria-expanded` is not sufficient if CSS uses `[aria-expanded="false"] + .panel { display: none }` — both the ARIA state and the visual state must be in sync; test that the panel is actually hidden when `aria-expanded="false"`. [official]

---

### Pattern 109 (Cycle 40) — ARIA Tree Widget: `aria-expanded`, `aria-level`, and Roving Tabindex Validation

**Description:** ARIA tree widgets require `role="tree"` on the container, `role="treeitem"` on each node, and `role="group"` on subtree containers. Parent nodes must have `aria-expanded` (`"true"`/`"false"`); leaf nodes must not have `aria-expanded` at all. `aria-level`, `aria-setsize`, and `aria-posinset` are required on dynamically loaded trees to provide positional context. The roving tabindex pattern — where only the currently focused treeitem has `tabindex="0"` and all others have `tabindex="-1"` — enables arrow key navigation without AT remapping. The test validates these structural requirements and confirms the roving tabindex state after arrow key navigation.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/tree-widget.spec.ts
// Validates ARIA tree widget structural compliance and roving tabindex behavior.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Tree widget compliance', () => {
  test('tree structure has correct roles and aria-expanded only on parents', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-explorer');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="tree"]');

    const allItems = page.locator('[role="treeitem"]');
    const itemCount = await allItems.count();
    expect(itemCount).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(itemCount, 20); i++) {
      const item = allItems.nth(i);
      const hasChildren = (await item.locator('[role="group"]').count()) > 0
        || (await item.locator('[role="treeitem"]').count()) > 0;
      const ariaExpanded = await item.getAttribute('aria-expanded');

      if (hasChildren) {
        expect(['true', 'false']).toContain(ariaExpanded);
      } else {
        // Leaf nodes must NOT have aria-expanded
        expect(ariaExpanded, `Leaf treeitem at index ${i} must not have aria-expanded`).toBeNull();
      }
    }
  });

  test('roving tabindex: only one treeitem has tabindex="0" at a time', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-explorer');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="tree"]');

    // Initially exactly one item should be tab-reachable
    const focusableItems = page.locator('[role="treeitem"][tabindex="0"]');
    await expect(focusableItems).toHaveCount(1);

    // After ArrowDown, the next item becomes the only tabindex="0" item
    await focusableItems.first().focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    await expect(page.locator('[role="treeitem"][tabindex="0"]')).toHaveCount(1);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset` are only required when the full list of tree items is not present in the DOM (e.g., on-demand loading). If the tree is fully rendered at page load, browser accessibility implementations can compute these values automatically, making explicit attributes redundant but not harmful. Omitting `aria-level` on a dynamically loaded tree is the most common cause of NVDA announcing "treeitem" without a level number, which is disorienting in deep hierarchies. [official]

---

### Pattern 110 (Cycle 40) — Playwright `toMatchAriaSnapshot` with `.aria.yml` External Fixtures for Stable CI

**Description:** Playwright 1.49+ supports storing aria snapshot baselines in separate `.aria.yml` fixture files rather than inline template literals, enabling version-controlled semantic structure tests that are updated via `--update-snapshots` in CI. The `.aria.yml` approach is more maintainable for large component trees and integrates with diff-based code review. Combined with `mode: 'partial'` (Playwright 1.50+), only the specified subset of the tree is asserted, making snapshots resilient to unrelated DOM additions. The pattern demonstrates the file-based fixture workflow with partial mode for a navigation landmark.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/nav-snapshot.spec.ts
// Uses aria snapshot fixtures (.aria.yml) with partial mode for stable navigation assertions.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Navigation aria snapshots', () => {
  test('main navigation landmark matches aria snapshot', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const nav = page.locator('nav[aria-label="Main navigation"]');
    await expect(nav).toMatchAriaSnapshot({
      name: 'main-navigation',
      // Partial mode ignores extra items added to nav without breaking the test
      mode: 'partial',
    });
  });

  test('primary heading hierarchy is stable', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const headings = page.locator('h1, h2[data-testid]');

    await expect(headings).toMatchAriaSnapshot({
      name: 'heading-hierarchy',
      mode: 'partial',
    });
  });

  test('footer help links are present in correct order', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const footer = page.locator('footer');

    await expect(footer).toMatchAriaSnapshot({
      name: 'footer-help-links',
      mode: 'partial',
    });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** External `.aria.yml` fixture files must be committed to the repository and regenerated whenever the component's semantic structure intentionally changes — this requires a deliberate `--update-snapshots` run followed by a PR review of the diff. On first run in a clean repository (no baseline files), tests will fail or generate new files depending on CI configuration; ensure your CI pipeline runs `--update-snapshots` once to generate baselines on a dedicated baseline branch before enforcing the check. [official]

---

### Pattern 111 (Cycle 40) — axe-core Shadow DOM Traversal: Web Component Accessibility Scanning

**Description:** axe-core 4.x automatically traverses open shadow roots when scanning — it injects into each open shadow root it finds during the tree walk. Closed shadow roots (created with `{ mode: 'closed' }`) are inaccessible to axe and will be silently skipped. Many UI component libraries (Shoelace, Spectrum Web Components, Material Web) use open shadow DOM, meaning violations inside custom elements are surfaced in axe results with the shadow host selector as the first element in the `target` array and the inner element as the second (e.g., `['my-input', '#internal-input']`). The test pattern verifies that a web component library page produces no axe violations and includes an assertion that shadow DOM content was actually scanned.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/shadow-dom-scan.spec.ts
// Verifies axe-core traverses open shadow roots and detects violations inside web components.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('Web component shadow DOM accessibility scan', () => {
  test('open shadow roots are scanned by axe', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/design-system-demo');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
      .analyze();

    // Shadow DOM violations have nested target arrays
    const shadowViolations = results.violations.filter((v) =>
      v.nodes.some((n) => n.target.some((t) => Array.isArray(t)))
    );

    if (shadowViolations.length > 0) {
      console.warn('Shadow DOM violations found:', JSON.stringify(shadowViolations, null, 2));
    }

    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('custom element form inputs have accessible labels (shadow DOM check)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/design-system-demo');
    // Verify shadow DOM is traversed by checking for open shadow roots
    const hasWebComponents = await page.evaluate(() =>
      Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('*')).some(
        (el) => el.shadowRoot !== null && el.shadowRoot.mode === 'open'
      )
    );

    if (!hasWebComponents) {
      test.skip('No open shadow roots found on this page');
    }

    const shadowInputs = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const hosts = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('*')).filter(
        (el) => el.shadowRoot?.mode === 'open'
      );
      return hosts.flatMap((host) =>
        Array.from(host.shadowRoot!.querySelectorAll('input:not([type="hidden"])'))
          .map((inp) => ({
            host: host.tagName,
            hasLabel: !!(
              (inp as HTMLElement).getAttribute('aria-label') ||
              (inp as HTMLElement).getAttribute('aria-labelledby') ||
              host.shadowRoot!.querySelector(`label[for="${inp.id}"]`)
            ),
          }))
      );
    });

    const unlabeled = shadowInputs.filter((i) => !i.hasLabel);
    expect(unlabeled, `Shadow DOM inputs without labels: ${JSON.stringify(unlabeled)}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Closed shadow roots cannot be scanned by axe or inspected by Playwright's `evaluate` — components using closed mode are effectively black boxes for automated accessibility testing. If your design system ships closed shadow components, you must test those components in isolation using the component library's own test harness (e.g., Web Test Runner + @web/test-runner-playwright) before publishing, as integration-level axe scans will miss their internals. [official]

---

### Pattern 112 (Cycle 40) — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size: Computed Bounding Box Audit for All Interactive Elements

**Description:** WCAG 2.5.8 (Level AA) requires that interactive targets be at least 24×24 CSS pixels, with an exception for targets whose bounding box plus an offset area totaling 24px still does not overlap any adjacent target. The criterion applies to links, buttons, and other interactive elements but excludes inline text links within a sentence, browser-controlled elements, and elements where spacing to the nearest neighbor provides the equivalent of the 24px minimum via offset. The automated test retrieves the bounding box of all interactive elements and flags any whose width or height is below 24px for manual offset verification.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/target-size.spec.ts
// Audits interactive element bounding boxes for WCAG 2.5.8 target size compliance.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const MINIMUM_TARGET_SIZE_PX = 24;

test.describe('WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)', () => {
  test('all interactive elements meet 24x24 CSS pixel minimum (with exceptions noted)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const smallTargets = await page.evaluate((minSize: number) => {
      const interactiveSelectors = 'button, a[href], input, select, textarea, [role="button"], [role="link"], [role="checkbox"], [role="radio"], [role="switch"]';
      const elements = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(interactiveSelectors));
      return elements
        .filter((el) => {
          const style = window.getComputedStyle(el);
          if (style.display === 'none' || style.visibility === 'hidden') return false;
          // Exclude inline text links (inside <p>, <li>, <td>)
          const inlineParent = el.closest('p, li, td, th, span');
          if (inlineParent && el.tagName === 'A') return false;
          return true;
        })
        .map((el) => {
          const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
          return {
            tag: el.tagName,
            label: (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.trim().slice(0, 30) ?? '',
            width: Math.round(rect.width),
            height: Math.round(rect.height),
          };
        })
        .filter((info) => info.width < minSize || info.height < minSize);
    }, MINIMUM_TARGET_SIZE_PX);

    if (smallTargets.length > 0) {
      console.warn('Targets below 24px (manual offset verification required):', smallTargets);
    }

    // Fail only on targets that are also zero-size (completely untappable)
    const zeroTargets = smallTargets.filter((t) => t.width === 0 || t.height === 0);
    expect(zeroTargets, `Zero-size interactive targets found: ${JSON.stringify(zeroTargets)}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Automated bounding box measurement cannot apply the spacing offset exception: a 16×16px icon button with 8px margin on all sides technically satisfies SC 2.5.8 because the offset pushes the effective target boundary to 24px. The test therefore logs small-but-not-zero targets as warnings for manual offset review rather than automatic failures, avoiding false positives for legitimately spaced targets. axe-core does not currently have a rule for SC 2.5.8 — this custom evaluation is the primary automated signal. [official]

---

### Pattern 113 (Cycle 40) — Playwright `toHaveRole` Assertion for ARIA Role Contract Testing

**Description:** Playwright's `toHaveRole()` assertion (available since Playwright 1.44) verifies that an element exposes the expected computed ARIA role to the accessibility tree. Unlike checking the `role` attribute directly, `toHaveRole()` resolves the implicit role of native HTML elements (a `<button>` has an implicit role of `"button"`) and validates that custom elements with explicit roles match the expected value. This is particularly useful for verifying that design-system components expose the correct semantic role after rendering and that custom elements with `role` attributes haven't been overridden by nested ARIA. The pattern tests a component library's button, checkbox, and dialog roles.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/role-assertions.spec.ts
// Uses Playwright toHaveRole() to verify computed ARIA roles for design system components.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA role assertions with toHaveRole()', () => {
  test('design system components expose correct computed roles', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/design-system-demo');
    await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

    // Primary button — implicit role from <button> element
    const primaryBtn = page.locator('[data-testid="primary-button"]');
    await expect(primaryBtn).toHaveRole('button');

    // Custom toggle — uses <div role="checkbox">
    const toggle = page.locator('[data-testid="toggle-switch"]');
    await expect(toggle).toHaveRole('checkbox');

    // Navigation landmark
    const mainNav = page.locator('[data-testid="main-nav"]');
    await expect(mainNav).toHaveRole('navigation');

    // Alert banner rendered by JS after form submit
    await page.locator('[data-testid="submit-form"]').click();
    const alert = page.locator('[data-testid="success-alert"]');
    await expect(alert).toBeVisible();
    await expect(alert).toHaveRole('alert');
  });

  test('modal dialog has correct role and is in the accessibility tree when open', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.locator('[data-testid="open-modal-btn"]').click();
    const modal = page.locator('[data-testid="modal"]');
    await expect(modal).toBeVisible();
    await expect(modal).toHaveRole('dialog');

    // aria-modal suppresses background content in modern AT
    await expect(modal).toHaveAttribute('aria-modal', 'true');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `toHaveRole()` checks the element's ARIA role as reported by the accessibility tree — it does not verify keyboard interaction contracts or that the role's required owned elements are present. A `<div role="listbox">` will pass `toHaveRole('listbox')` even if it contains no `<div role="option">` children, which violates the required ownership contract for `listbox`. Combine `toHaveRole()` with axe-core scans (which check required ownership) for complete role validation. [official]

---

### Pattern 114 (Cycle 40) — Focus Management After Modal Close: Return-Focus Regression Test

**Description:** WCAG SC 2.4.3 Focus Order and SC 3.2.2 On Input both require that focus is managed predictably when interactive components are opened and closed. When a modal dialog closes, focus must return to the element that triggered it — if focus instead lands on the document body or is lost entirely, keyboard and AT users must re-navigate from the top of the page to find their previous location. This regression is extremely common after refactoring that replaces a modal with a new component: the new component may not implement the return-focus behavior. The test pattern captures the triggering element before opening, then asserts it regains focus after close.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/focus-return.spec.ts
// Tests that focus returns to the trigger element after closing a modal dialog.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Focus management after modal close', () => {
  test('focus returns to trigger button after modal is dismissed', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const trigger = page.locator('[data-testid="open-settings-modal"]');
    await trigger.focus();

    // Confirm trigger has focus before opening
    await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();

    // Open modal
    await trigger.click();
    const modal = page.locator('[role="dialog"]');
    await expect(modal).toBeVisible();

    // Focus should have moved into the dialog
    const closeBtn = modal.locator('[aria-label="Close"], [data-testid="modal-close"]').first();
    await expect(closeBtn).toBeFocused();

    // Close the modal via button
    await closeBtn.click();
    await expect(modal).not.toBeVisible();

    // Focus must return to the original trigger
    await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('focus returns after modal dismissed by Escape key', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const trigger = page.locator('[data-testid="open-settings-modal"]');
    await trigger.click();
    await expect(page.locator('[role="dialog"]')).toBeVisible();

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(page.locator('[role="dialog"]')).not.toBeVisible();
    await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Return-focus behavior requires the application to store a reference to `document.activeElement` at the time the modal opens. If modals can be opened programmatically (not triggered by a user interaction), there may be no meaningful element to return focus to — in that case, focus should move to the first logical content heading (`<h1>`) rather than the body. Test both user-initiated and programmatic open scenarios if both are possible in your application. [official]

---

### Pattern 115 (Cycle 40) — Virtual Scrolling Accessibility: Off-Screen Content and AT Navigation

**Description:** Virtual list implementations (TanStack Virtual, React Window, AG Grid virtual rows) render only the visible rows to the DOM, removing off-screen rows to improve performance. This breaks AT navigation: screen reader users using the virtual cursor or JAWS arrow keys navigate the actual DOM, not a conceptual list, so they reach the last rendered row and cannot continue — the list appears to end at the visible window boundary. The ARIA-compliant approach uses `role="feed"` for infinite lists or explicitly maintains `aria-rowcount` / `aria-rowindex` on `role="row"` elements within a `role="grid"` so AT announces the true total. The test pattern detects virtual list containers and asserts that size-hint ARIA attributes are present.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/virtual-scroll.spec.ts
// Detects virtual scrolling containers and asserts ARIA size-hint attributes are present.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Virtual scroll ARIA compliance', () => {
  test('virtual list grid exposes aria-rowcount and aria-rowindex', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/data-table');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const grid = page.locator('[role="grid"]').first();
    const rowCount = await grid.getAttribute('aria-rowcount');
    expect(
      rowCount,
      'Virtual grid must have aria-rowcount declaring total rows (even if not all are rendered)'
    ).not.toBeNull();
    expect(parseInt(rowCount!, 10)).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    // First visible data row should have aria-rowindex
    const firstRow = grid.locator('[role="row"]').first();
    const rowIndex = await firstRow.getAttribute('aria-rowindex');
    expect(rowIndex, 'First visible row must have aria-rowindex').not.toBeNull();
  });

  test('infinite scroll feed has role="feed" and aria-label', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/activity-feed');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="feed"]');
    const feed = page.locator('[role="feed"]').first();
    const label = await feed.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? await feed.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    expect(label, 'role="feed" container must have an accessible name').toBeTruthy();

    // Articles within feed must have role="article" and be labeled
    const articles = feed.locator('[role="article"]');
    const count = await articles.count();
    expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `aria-rowcount` with a value of `-1` is a valid signal that the total count is unknown (e.g., infinite scroll with no known end), and AT will announce "unknown number of rows." This is acceptable for truly unbounded data sources but should not be used as a shortcut when the total count is known but inconvenient to compute. For keyboard users, virtual scroll implementations should also respond to `End` key with a deliberate scroll-to-end action, or provide a "Jump to end" button, because the virtual cursor cannot navigate past the rendered window. [community]

---

### Pattern 116 (Cycle 40) — Skip Link Functionality in Single-Page Applications

**Description:** Skip links (`<a href="#main-content">Skip to main content</a>`) are a foundational keyboard accessibility mechanism. In traditional multi-page applications they work reliably, but in single-page applications with client-side routing, the `<main id="main-content">` element persists across route changes while the skip link URL fragment is only applied once on the initial page load. Subsequent route changes leave focus at the top of the page with the skip link unfocused — the user must tab past the entire navigation on every navigation event. The correct SPA fix is to programmatically move focus to the main heading or main element on each route change, not to rely solely on the skip link. The test verifies skip link click focus placement and SPA route-change focus behavior.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/skip-link.spec.ts
// Tests skip link focus placement and SPA route-change focus management.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Skip link and SPA focus management', () => {
  test('skip link moves focus to main content on activation', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const skipLink = page.locator('a[href="#main-content"], a[href*="skip"]').first();
    await skipLink.focus();
    await expect(skipLink).toBeVisible(); // skip links must become visible on focus

    await skipLink.press('Enter');

    const main = page.locator('#main-content, main').first();
    await expect(main).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('SPA route change moves focus to main heading', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Simulate navigation by clicking an internal link
    await page.locator('nav a[href="/about"]').first().click();
    await page.waitForURL('/about');

    // After SPA navigation, focus should land on the main heading or main element
    const mainHeading = page.locator('main h1, #main-content').first();
    await expect(mainHeading).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('skip link is visible on focus (not hidden when blurred)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const skipLink = page.locator('a[href="#main-content"]').first();
    await skipLink.focus();
    // Must be visible when focused
    await expect(skipLink).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** SPA frameworks handle route-change focus differently: Next.js App Router does not automatically move focus on navigation (as of Next.js 14), requiring manual implementation via `router.events` or a `<RouteAnnouncer>` component. React Router also provides no built-in focus management. The safest implementation is a `<RouteChangeAnnouncer>` component that sets `tabindex="-1"` on the `<main>` element, calls `main.focus()` on each route change, and announces the new page title to a live region. Test the SPA navigation scenario explicitly — skip link tests on the initial page load may pass while route-change focus is completely broken. [community]

---

### Pattern 117 (Cycle 40) — Accessible Name Computation for SVG Icons in Buttons

**Description:** SVG icons are commonly used inside buttons and links, and their accessible name computation requires special attention. An `<svg>` element with no accessible text and a `<button>` that contains only the SVG will produce an empty accessible name, making the button unparsable by AT. The correct approach is either `aria-label` on the button, a visually hidden `<span>` sibling inside the button, or a `<title>` element as the first child of the SVG combined with `role="img"` and `aria-labelledby` pointing to the title. The test uses Playwright's `toHaveAccessibleName()` to assert every icon-only button has a non-empty computed accessible name.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/svg-icon-buttons.spec.ts
// Tests that icon-only buttons backed by SVGs have non-empty accessible names.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('SVG icon button accessible names', () => {
  test('all icon-only buttons have a non-empty accessible name', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

    const iconButtonData = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const buttons = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('button, a[href]'));
      return buttons
        .filter((btn) => {
          const hasSvg = btn.querySelector('svg') !== null;
          const hasImg = btn.querySelector('img') !== null;
          const visibleText = Array.from(btn.childNodes)
            .filter((n) => n.nodeType === Node.TEXT_NODE)
            .map((n) => n.textContent?.trim())
            .join('');
          const hasHiddenSpan = btn.querySelector('.sr-only, .visually-hidden') !== null;
          // Icon-only: has SVG/img and no visible text outside hidden spans
          return (hasSvg || hasImg) && (visibleText.length === 0 || hasHiddenSpan);
        })
        .map((btn, i) => ({ index: i, tag: btn.tagName, id: btn.id, testId: (btn as HTMLElement).dataset['testid'] ?? '' }));
    });

    for (const info of iconButtonData) {
      const selector = info.testId
        ? `[data-testid="${info.testId}"]`
        : info.id
        ? `#${info.id}`
        : `${info.tag.toLowerCase()}:has(svg)`;
      const locator = page.locator(selector).first();
      await expect(locator).not.toHaveAccessibleName('');
    }
  });

  test('decorative SVGs inside text buttons have aria-hidden="true"', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const decorativeIssues = await page.evaluate(() => {
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('button svg, a svg'))
        .filter((svg) => {
          const btn = svg.closest('button, a');
          const btnText = (btn?.textContent ?? '').replace(svg.textContent ?? '', '').trim();
          // SVG is decorative if the button has other text content
          return btnText.length > 0 && svg.getAttribute('aria-hidden') !== 'true';
        })
        .map((svg) => svg.closest('button, a')?.outerHTML?.slice(0, 100) ?? '');
    });

    expect(
      decorativeIssues,
      `Decorative SVGs in text buttons without aria-hidden="true": ${JSON.stringify(decorativeIssues)}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** The `<title>` element inside SVG is announced inconsistently across browser and AT combinations: VoiceOver on Safari reads it, but NVDA + Chrome previously ignored SVG `<title>` unless the SVG had `role="img"` and `aria-labelledby` pointing to the `<title>` element's id. As of 2025, Chrome's accessibility tree includes SVG `<title>` content for `role="img"` SVGs but not for SVGs with no role. The safest cross-AT approach is `aria-label` on the containing button rather than relying on SVG-internal labeling. [community]

---

### Pattern 118 (Cycle 40) — Color Contrast for Text over Gradient and Image Backgrounds

**Description:** axe-core's `color-contrast` rule computes contrast by sampling the background color of the bounding box's corners and center, which works well for solid backgrounds but produces inaccurate results for text over gradients, background images, or video. On a gradient that transitions from light to dark, axe may sample a region where contrast passes while the actual text rendering spans a region where it fails. The test pattern combines an axe scan (excluding known gradient containers) with screenshot attachments for those containers, delegating the gradient regions to a manual review queue in the CI artifact viewer.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/gradient-contrast.spec.ts
// Combines axe scan with manual exclusion list for gradient/image backgrounds.
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

const GRADIENT_CONTAINERS = [
  '[data-testid="hero-banner"]',
  '[data-testid="promo-card"]',
  '.gradient-header',
];

test.describe('Color contrast including gradient backgrounds', () => {
  test('axe color-contrast scan excluding known gradient containers', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    let builder = new AxeBuilder({ page }).withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa']);
    for (const selector of GRADIENT_CONTAINERS) {
      builder = builder.exclude(selector);
    }

    const results = await builder.analyze();
    const contrastViolations = results.violations.filter((v) => v.id === 'color-contrast');
    expect(contrastViolations, JSON.stringify(contrastViolations, null, 2)).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('hero banner text is legible: screenshot saved for manual review', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const hero = page.locator('[data-testid="hero-banner"]');
    await expect(hero).toBeVisible();

    const screenshot = await hero.screenshot();
    await testInfo.attach('hero-banner-contrast-review', {
      body: screenshot,
      contentType: 'image/png',
    });

    // Structural assertion: the hero must contain at least one heading
    const heading = hero.locator('h1, h2').first();
    await expect(heading).toBeVisible();
    await expect(heading).not.toHaveCSS('color', 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Automated per-pixel color contrast analysis is computationally expensive and requires a browser-side image processing step or external tooling (e.g., `sharp`, `jimp`, or `@deque/color-contrast-checker`). The screenshot attachment approach delegates visual judgment to a human reviewer in the CI artifact viewer — it is not a pass/fail gate. For production sign-off, verify each text color variant against the lightest and darkest points of the gradient to confirm 4.5:1 (AA normal text) or 3:1 (AA large text / UI components) is maintained throughout the full gradient range. [community]

---

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 40)

185. **[community] Playwright's `toBeFocused()` assertion passes for elements with `tabindex="-1"` that have received programmatic focus via `.focus()` — but AT users cannot reach `tabindex="-1"` elements through standard Tab key navigation, so a test confirming an element is focused does not confirm it is keyboard-reachable**: `tabindex="-1"` elements are excluded from the tab sequence but can still receive focus programmatically. A common pattern is for modal dialogs to call `modal.focus()` on open and for the test to assert `toBeFocused()` on the modal container — this passes even if the modal has `tabindex="-1"`, which means keyboard users can navigate into the modal but the modal container itself is never reached via Tab key. WHY: Developers write focus tests that call `.focus()` directly on the element under test and then assert `toBeFocused()`, bypassing the Tab sequence entirely; the correct test approach for Tab navigation is `await page.keyboard.press('Tab')` in a loop until the expected element receives focus, which validates actual keyboard reachability rather than just programmatic focusability. [community]

186. **[community] axe-core's `landmark-one-main` rule passes when a `<main>` element is present anywhere in the document — even inside a `role="none"` or `display:none` ancestor — because axe checks for the existence of the landmark element but not whether it is exposed in the accessibility tree**: Some application shells conditionally render a hidden `<main>` element for SEO purposes while the visible content is inside a `<div role="main">`. In this configuration, axe passes `landmark-one-main` (because `<main>` exists) but AT users navigate to the hidden `<main>` rather than the visible `role="main"` container, confusing navigation. WHY: Developers trust the axe `landmark-one-main` pass as proof that their main landmark is accessible when in fact having both a `<main>` and a `role="main"` in the same document creates two competing main landmarks — NVDA announces "main landmark" twice, disorienting users who rely on the F6 landmarks shortcut. The fix is to use exactly one `<main>` element and never mix `<main>` with `role="main"` on separate elements. [community]

187. **[community] VoiceOver on iOS Safari does not announce `aria-live="assertive"` updates that occur during a scroll-to-reveal animation — the live region update fires while the element is in the process of being scrolled into the viewport, and iOS VoiceOver's focus management during scroll suppresses the live announcement**: This affects infinite scroll feeds that append a "Loading more items…" live region update while simultaneously scrolling to reveal a newly loaded batch. On desktop screen readers this works correctly, but on iOS VoiceOver the announcement is dropped silently. WHY: iOS VoiceOver suspends live region processing while an animated scroll is in progress to prevent announcement interruptions during content motion; the practical fix is to delay the `aria-live` update by one animation frame using `requestAnimationFrame(() => setLiveText('Loaded 10 more items'))` so the announcement fires after the scroll animation completes rather than during it. [community]

188. **[community] The `color-contrast` rule in axe-core does not account for CSS `opacity` on text elements — text with `opacity: 0.85` may visually fail 4.5:1 contrast but axe reports a pass because it computes contrast using the element's declared `color` value without factoring in opacity compositing against the background**: CSS `opacity` on a text element multiplicatively reduces the effective contrast by blending the text color toward the background color. An `opacity: 0.85` on `color: #767676` (which barely passes 4.5:1 on white) will drop below 4.5:1 visually, but axe-core reads the raw CSS `color` value and background color without compositing the opacity. WHY: Design systems use `opacity` variants for disabled, placeholder, or secondary text styles and add them to the token library after a single pass/fail check with the base color — the opacity-adjusted variants are never re-checked, producing axe passes that mask real contrast failures visible to users. The fix is to always compute effective contrast at the composited color value: for `opacity: α` on a white background, effective RGB = `α × text_color + (1 − α) × 255`. [community]

189. **[community] `aria-label` on a form input does not override a `<label>` element's text in NVDA's forms mode — NVDA in forms mode reads the `<label>` element text rather than `aria-label` when both are present, causing a discrepancy between what `toHaveAccessibleName()` asserts (which follows the ARIA name computation algorithm and resolves `aria-label` first) and what NVDA actually announces to users**: The ARIA accessible name computation spec resolves `aria-label` before checking the associated `<label>` element, so the accessibility API returns the `aria-label` value. Playwright's `toHaveAccessibleName()` uses this API. However, NVDA's forms mode in some versions reads the visual `<label>` text in preference to `aria-label`. WHY: Teams write accessible name tests that pass CI, ship the component, then receive bug reports from users with NVDA saying the screen reader announces the wrong label; the fix is to ensure the `<label>` text and `aria-label` value are identical when both are present, or to remove `aria-label` entirely and rely solely on `<label>` — never place conflicting text in both attributes on the same input. [community]

190. **[community] When using `role="status"` for polite form success messages, some AT + browser combinations double-announce the content when the status region is populated immediately after a button click on the same event loop tick — the accessibility tree change event fires before the button's click acknowledgement is complete, causing AT to announce the status change and then re-read it when it re-polls the live region**: This is observed in NVDA + Firefox where synchronous DOM updates in a click handler populate the live region before the AT finishes processing the click event, leading to a double-announcement. The issue is not reproducible in NVDA + Chrome because Chrome's accessibility tree notifies AT asynchronously. WHY: Teams test exclusively with NVDA + Chrome (the most common AT + browser combination in accessibility audits) and never encounter the double-announcement that Firefox users experience; the fix is to defer live region population by one microtask: `queueMicrotask(() => setStatusText('Form submitted successfully'))` decouples the status update from the synchronous click handler, producing a single announcement in both Chrome and Firefox. [community]
