## Cycle 41 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 119 (Cycle 41) — Combobox Accessible Name and `aria-activedescendant` Synchronisation

A combobox with a listbox popup must maintain DOM focus on the `<input>` element at all times, moving "AT focus" into the list exclusively via `aria-activedescendant` pointing to the currently highlighted `role="option"`. This pattern — defined in the ARIA APG combobox spec — means Playwright's `toBeFocused()` assertion on the input remains true throughout list navigation, even when a visually-selected option is highlighted. The Playwright test must confirm that `aria-activedescendant` is updated on each arrow-key press and that the referenced option element exists in the DOM and carries `aria-selected="true"` or matching styling. Without this synchronisation check, an autocomplete that breaks AT option announcement passes all focus assertions.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/combobox-activedescendant.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('Combobox aria-activedescendant synchronisation', () => {
  test('input stays focused; activedescendant tracks highlighted option', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/combobox-demo');
    const input = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Country' });
    await input.click();
    await input.type('Ger');
    // Popup should open
    await expect(page.getByRole('listbox')).toBeVisible();
    // Move focus into popup via arrow key – DOM focus MUST stay on the input
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    await expect(input).toBeFocused();
    // aria-activedescendant must reference an existing option
    const activeId = await input.getAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
    expect(activeId).toBeTruthy();
    const activeOption = page.locator(`#${activeId}`);
    await expect(activeOption).toBeVisible();
    await expect(activeOption).toHaveRole('option');
    // axe should produce no violations on this state
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('axe passes on closed and open popup states', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/combobox-demo');
    // Closed state
    let results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).include('[role="combobox"]').analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
    await page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Country' }).type('Fr');
    // Open state
    results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).include('[role="combobox"]').analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Testing `aria-activedescendant` synchronisation requires reading live DOM attributes after each key press, which adds round-trip latency in cross-browser CI environments. Because Chromium's accessibility implementation coalesces attribute updates differently from Firefox, test runs on Firefox may require an explicit `waitFor` for the attribute value to stabilise before asserting. Constrain the full AT-navigation test to a single browser (Chromium) and run the axe scan across all three browsers to balance coverage with execution time. [official]

---

### Pattern 120 (Cycle 41) — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum): Automated 24×24 CSS Pixel Enforcement

WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (Level AA) requires every pointer target to occupy at least 24×24 CSS pixels, with exceptions for inline text, user-agent controls, and adequately-spaced undersized targets. Playwright can evaluate `getBoundingClientRect()` on every interactive element and flag those whose width or height is below 24px. The test must also implement the spacing-exception logic: an undersized target passes if a 24px-diameter circle centred on its bounding box does not intersect similar circles of adjacent undersized targets. This automated gate catches the most common failure pattern — icon-only buttons styled with `padding: 0` — without requiring manual pixel counting during design review.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/target-size.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const MIN_PX = 24;

test('all interactive targets meet 24×24 CSS pixel minimum (WCAG 2.5.8)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const violations = await page.evaluate((min) => {
    const INTERACTIVE = 'a[href], button, input, select, textarea, [role="button"], [role="link"], [role="checkbox"], [role="radio"], [role="menuitem"], [role="option"]';
    const targets = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(INTERACTIVE)).filter((el) => {
      const style = getComputedStyle(el);
      return style.display !== 'none' && style.visibility !== 'hidden' && (el as HTMLElement).offsetParent !== null;
    });
    return targets
      .map((el) => {
        const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        return { tag: el.tagName, text: (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.trim().slice(0, 40), w: r.width, h: r.height, id: el.id, cls: el.className };
      })
      .filter(({ w, h }) => w < min || h < min);
  }, MIN_PX);

  expect(
    violations,
    `Found ${violations.length} targets smaller than ${MIN_PX}×${MIN_PX}px:\n${JSON.stringify(violations, null, 2)}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** The `getBoundingClientRect` approach measures CSS layout pixels correctly at the default device pixel ratio. At `deviceScaleFactor > 1` (high-DPI screens), the physical pixel size is larger but the CSS pixel threshold still applies — no adjustment is needed. The spacing-exception calculation requires pairwise comparison across all undersized targets and is O(n²); on pages with many interactive elements this may slow page.evaluate(). Implement the spacing exception check only when the raw size check first produces violations, and scope both checks to the current viewport to exclude off-screen elements. [official]

---

### Pattern 121 (Cycle 41) — WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry: Multi-Step Form Auto-Population Test

SC 3.3.7 (Level A, WCAG 2.2) forbids requiring users to re-enter information they have already submitted within the same process, unless re-entry is essential (e.g., password confirmation) or the data is no longer valid. The testing pattern navigates a multi-step flow, submits data in step 1, and then asserts at each subsequent step that previously entered values appear either pre-populated in form fields or available in a selection mechanism. The test must also confirm that pre-populated fields remain populated after a server-side validation error forces a return to an earlier step.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/redundant-entry.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry — checkout flow', () => {
  test('shipping address pre-fills billing address section', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout/shipping');
    await page.getByLabel('First name').fill('Ada');
    await page.getByLabel('Last name').fill('Lovelace');
    await page.getByLabel('Street address').fill('123 Babbage Lane');
    await page.getByLabel('City').fill('London');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue to billing' }).click();

    // Billing step must pre-populate or offer a "same as shipping" option
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/checkout\/billing/);
    const sameAsShipping = page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: /same as shipping/i });
    if (await sameAsShipping.isVisible()) {
      // Option A: checkbox shortcut — check it and verify fields auto-populate
      await sameAsShipping.check();
      await expect(page.getByLabel('First name')).toHaveValue('Ada');
      await expect(page.getByLabel('Street address')).toHaveValue('123 Babbage Lane');
    } else {
      // Option B: direct pre-population without checkbox
      await expect(page.getByLabel('First name')).toHaveValue('Ada');
      await expect(page.getByLabel('Last name')).toHaveValue('Lovelace');
      await expect(page.getByLabel('Street address')).toHaveValue('123 Babbage Lane');
      await expect(page.getByLabel('City')).toHaveValue('London');
    }
  });

  test('data persists across validation errors (SC 3.3.7 recovery requirement)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout/shipping');
    await page.getByLabel('First name').fill('Ada');
    await page.getByLabel('Last name').fill('Lovelace');
    // Leave required postcode empty to trigger validation error
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue to billing' }).click();
    // After error, previously entered data must remain in the fields
    await expect(page.getByLabel('First name')).toHaveValue('Ada');
    await expect(page.getByLabel('Last name')).toHaveValue('Lovelace');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** SC 3.3.7 explicitly permits re-entry when a value is "no longer valid" — for example, a coupon code that expired between steps or a seat reservation that timed out. Tests that simply assert field pre-population will produce false positives if the application has legitimate invalidation logic. Add test comments documenting which re-entry cases are intentional exceptions; do not suppress the test for entire user journeys just because one field has a valid re-entry reason. [official]

---

### Pattern 122 (Cycle 41) — WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication: Password Manager Non-Interference Test

SC 3.3.8 (Level AA, WCAG 2.2) prohibits authentication steps that require a cognitive function test — including manually transcribing a password — unless an alternative method exists or copy-paste is permitted. The automated test verifies that login fields do not block paste events, that `autocomplete` attributes are correct (`username`, `current-password`, `new-password`), and that OTP / MFA fields accept pasted codes. A common failure mode is JavaScript intercepting the `paste` event or `autocomplete="off"` being set on password fields, both of which block password managers and fail 3.3.8.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/accessible-authentication.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication', () => {
  test('login fields allow paste and carry correct autocomplete attributes', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    const usernameField = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email|username/i });
    const passwordField = page.locator('input[type="password"]');

    await expect(usernameField).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', /^(username|email)$/);
    await expect(passwordField).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', 'current-password');

    // Verify paste is not blocked on password field
    await passwordField.click();
    await page.keyboard.insertText('PastedP@ssw0rd!');
    await expect(passwordField).toHaveValue('PastedP@ssw0rd!');
  });

  test('OTP / MFA field accepts a pasted code', async ({ page, context }) => {
    await context.grantPermissions(['clipboard-read', 'clipboard-write']);
    await page.goto('/login/mfa');
    // Write a code to the clipboard
    await page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.writeText('123456'));
    const otpField = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /code|otp|verification/i }).first();
    await otpField.click();
    await page.keyboard.press('Control+v');
    const value = await otpField.inputValue();
    expect(value).toBe('123456');
  });

  test('axe scan on login page (no cognitive-function-test violations)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).withTags(['wcag22aa']).analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** The paste test using `page.keyboard.insertText()` does not go through the operating system clipboard and therefore does not confirm that a real password manager clipboard paste works in production. Use `page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.writeText(...))` combined with `Control+v` for a more realistic simulation, but note this requires `clipboard-write` browser permission to be granted in the test context. On Linux CI agents, the clipboard permission may be unavailable; fall back to checking that no `paste` event listener calls `preventDefault()` by evaluating `getEventListeners` if available, or by asserting that the field value changes after a synthetic paste. [official]

---

### Pattern 123 (Cycle 41) — WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: Sticky Header Scroll-Padding Test

WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 (Level AA) requires that when a UI component receives keyboard focus, it is not entirely hidden by author-created content such as sticky navigation bars or persistent cookie consent banners. The most reliable automated test tabs through all interactive elements on a page with a sticky header, and for each focused element uses `getBoundingClientRect()` to determine whether the element's bounding box is fully obscured by any `position: fixed` or `position: sticky` element occupying the same y-coordinate range. A simpler proxy is asserting that `scroll-padding-top` on `<html>` or `<body>` equals or exceeds the sticky header height.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/focus-not-obscured.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('focused elements are not entirely hidden by sticky headers (WCAG 2.4.11)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Collect all sticky/fixed elements and their heights
  const stickyBarHeight = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const stickyEls = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('*')).filter((el) => {
      const pos = getComputedStyle(el).position;
      return (pos === 'sticky' || pos === 'fixed') && el.getBoundingClientRect().top < 10;
    });
    return stickyEls.reduce((max, el) => Math.max(max, el.getBoundingClientRect().bottom), 0);
  });

  // Tab through focusable elements and check none are fully obscured
  const focusable = page.locator('a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])');
  const count = await focusable.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 30); i++) {
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focusedRect = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement;
      if (!el) return null;
      return el.getBoundingClientRect().toJSON();
    });
    if (!focusedRect) continue;
    // The element must not be entirely above the sticky bar's bottom edge
    const entirelyObscured = focusedRect.bottom <= stickyBarHeight;
    expect(
      entirelyObscured,
      `Element at top=${focusedRect.top} bottom=${focusedRect.bottom} is entirely hidden behind sticky header (height=${stickyBarHeight})`
    ).toBe(false);
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** This test evaluates the initial sticky-header position and may not catch obscuring that occurs mid-page as the user scrolls into sections with contextual sticky sub-headers. Run the test with `page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight / 2))` before beginning the Tab loop to exercise obscuring from mid-page stickies. Also note that the test caps at 30 elements by default — increase this limit on pages with many interactive components, but be aware that each Tab press adds ~15–40ms in headed browser mode. [official]

---

### Pattern 124 (Cycle 41) — ARIA Tabs Pattern: `role="tabpanel"` Focus and `tabindex="0"` When Empty

The ARIA APG tabs pattern requires that a `role="tabpanel"` element have `tabindex="0"` when the panel contains no focusable child elements, ensuring the panel itself is reachable via Tab key so keyboard users can read its content. Most implementations omit this conditional `tabindex`, causing keyboard users to skip empty or text-only tab panels entirely — the content is announced by screen readers but unreachable as a scroll target. The test must activate each tab, check whether the corresponding panel contains any intrinsically focusable element, and if not, assert `tabindex="0"` on the panel.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/tabs-panel-focus.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('ARIA Tabs: tabpanel focus and keyboard contract', () => {
  test('each tab activates via click and panel becomes accessible', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/tabs-demo');
    const tabList = page.getByRole('tablist');
    const tabs = tabList.getByRole('tab');
    const tabCount = await tabs.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < tabCount; i++) {
      const tab = tabs.nth(i);
      await tab.click();
      // Active tab must have aria-selected="true"
      await expect(tab).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
      // Linked panel must be visible
      const panelId = await tab.getAttribute('aria-controls');
      if (panelId) {
        const panel = page.locator(`#${panelId}`);
        await expect(panel).toBeVisible();
        // If panel has no focusable children, it must carry tabindex="0"
        const hasFocusableChild = await panel.locator('a, button, input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])').count();
        if (hasFocusableChild === 0) {
          await expect(panel).toHaveAttribute('tabindex', '0');
        }
      }
    }
  });

  test('axe passes with tabs component open on each tab', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/tabs-demo');
    const tabs = page.getByRole('tab');
    for (let i = 0; i < await tabs.count(); i++) {
      await tabs.nth(i).click();
      const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).include('[role="tablist"]').analyze();
      expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Adding `tabindex="0"` to all tab panels unconditionally (the easiest fix) causes double-Tab-stop on panels that already contain focusable content — users Tab to the panel and then Tab again into the first child, which is redundant and breaks the expected rhythm of Tab navigation. The `tabindex` must be set conditionally based on panel content; in React/Angular components this is easiest via a `useEffect`/`ngAfterViewChecked` that evaluates focusable descendants each time a panel becomes active. Axe-core does not currently detect this pattern omission, so the Playwright assertion is the only automated gate for it. [official]

---

### Pattern 125 (Cycle 41) — `role="alertdialog"`: `aria-labelledby` + `aria-describedby` Presence and Focus-on-Open

A modal dialog using `role="alertdialog"` must have both `aria-labelledby` (referencing a visible heading) and `aria-describedby` (referencing the alert message) per the ARIA APG alertdialog pattern. Additionally, on open, focus must move to the first focusable element inside the dialog or to the dialog container itself if it has `tabindex="-1"`. The common mistake is applying the required attributes but failing to actually move focus, which causes screen readers to not interrupt and announce the dialog content. The test uses a state-based dialog trigger, then immediately asserts the three requirements.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/alertdialog.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('role="alertdialog" labelling and focus-on-open', () => {
  test('alertdialog carries aria-labelledby and aria-describedby pointing to visible elements', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Trigger the destructive-action confirmation dialog
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /delete account/i }).click();
    const dialog = page.getByRole('alertdialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();

    const labelledById = await dialog.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    const describedById = await dialog.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
    expect(labelledById).toBeTruthy();
    expect(describedById).toBeTruthy();

    await expect(page.locator(`#${labelledById}`)).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.locator(`#${describedById}`)).toBeVisible();
  });

  test('focus moves inside alertdialog on open', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /delete account/i }).click();
    const dialog = page.getByRole('alertdialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();

    // Active element must be inside the dialog
    const isInsideDialog = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const dialog = document.querySelector('[role="alertdialog"]');
      return dialog ? dialog.contains(document.activeElement) : false;
    });
    expect(isInsideDialog).toBe(true);
  });

  test('axe scan on open alertdialog produces no violations', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /delete account/i }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('alertdialog')).toBeVisible();
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).include('[role="alertdialog"]').analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** axe-core's `aria-required-attr` rule will catch a missing `aria-labelledby` on `role="alertdialog"`, but it does not verify that the referenced element exists and is visible — a broken `id` reference (e.g., a typo) produces a dangling `aria-labelledby` that passes axe but announces nothing to the user. The explicit `page.locator(\`#${labelledById}\`)` visibility assertion in this pattern catches that second-order failure. The `aria-describedby` is not required by axe's core rules for `alertdialog`, making the explicit test the only automated gate for it. [official]

---

### Pattern 126 (Cycle 41) — ARIA Grid Keyboard Navigation: Arrow-Key Cell Focus Testing

Interactive data grids using `role="grid"` must support two-dimensional arrow-key navigation: Left/Right move between cells in a row, Up/Down move between rows, Home/End move to the first/last cell of the current row, and Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End jump to the first/last cell of the entire grid. These interactions are specified in the ARIA APG grid pattern. Automated tests should confirm that arrow-key navigation advances `document.activeElement` to the expected cell coordinates, and that the correct `role="gridcell"` element is focused after each movement.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/grid-keyboard-nav.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Grid: two-dimensional keyboard navigation', () => {
  test('arrow keys move focus between gridcells', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/data-grid');
    // Focus the first cell
    const firstCell = page.getByRole('gridcell').first();
    await firstCell.focus();
    await expect(firstCell).toBeFocused();

    // Right arrow should move to next cell in the same row
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const secondCellRole = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role'));
    expect(secondCellRole).toBe('gridcell');

    // Down arrow should move to first cell of the next row
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    const focusedRole = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role'));
    expect(focusedRole).toBe('gridcell');
  });

  test('Home key moves to first cell of current row', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/data-grid');
    const cells = page.getByRole('gridcell');
    await cells.nth(2).focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Home');
    // After Home, active element should be the first cell of that row
    const activeAriaColIndex = await page.evaluate(() =>
      document.activeElement?.getAttribute('aria-colindex')
    );
    expect(activeAriaColIndex).toBe('1');
  });

  test('grid cells carry required aria-rowindex and aria-colindex in virtual scroll mode', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/data-grid?mode=virtual');
    await page.waitForSelector('[role="grid"]');
    const cells = page.getByRole('gridcell');
    const count = await cells.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 10); i++) {
      await expect(cells.nth(i)).toHaveAttribute('aria-colindex', /^\d+$/);
    }
    const grid = page.getByRole('grid');
    await expect(grid).toHaveAttribute('aria-rowcount', /^\d+$/);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** The ARIA grid pattern supports two activation models for editable cells: cells that enter edit mode on Enter/F2 (spreadsheet model) and cells that activate a focusable child immediately on arrow-key navigation (composite widget model). Tests written for one model will fail on a grid using the other. Before writing grid keyboard tests, inspect whether the application's grid uses `aria-readonly="false"` (editable) and check the Enter/F2 behaviour in a real AT session; document the chosen model in a test comment so future maintainers do not rewrite passing tests that test intentional behaviour. [official]

---

### Pattern 127 (Cycle 41) — Reflow at 320px: Single-Axis Scroll Verification (WCAG 1.4.10)

WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.10 (Level AA) requires content to reflow at the equivalent of 320 CSS pixels width without requiring horizontal scrolling. The recommended test method is to set the viewport to 1280×1024 and apply 400% browser zoom, which produces a 320-pixel effective CSS width. Playwright does not expose browser zoom natively, so the reliable equivalent is setting the viewport width directly to 320 CSS pixels. The test navigates each key page, waits for layout stabilisation, and then asserts that `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` equals or does not exceed `window.innerWidth`, confirming no horizontal overflow.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/reflow-320.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const REFLOW_PAGES = ['/', '/products', '/checkout', '/account/settings'];

test.describe('WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow at 320px', () => {
  for (const path of REFLOW_PAGES) {
    test(`${path} — no horizontal scroll at 320px viewport`, async ({ browser }) => {
      const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 320, height: 568 } });
      const page = await context.newPage();
      await page.goto(path);
      await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

      const { scrollWidth, clientWidth } = await page.evaluate(() => ({
        scrollWidth: document.documentElement.scrollWidth,
        clientWidth: document.documentElement.clientWidth,
      }));

      expect(
        scrollWidth,
        `Horizontal overflow on ${path}: scrollWidth=${scrollWidth} > clientWidth=${clientWidth}`
      ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(clientWidth + 1); // +1 for sub-pixel rounding

      await context.close();
    });
  }

  test('navigation collapses to hamburger or single-column at 320px', async ({ browser }) => {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 320, height: 568 } });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    // Either a hamburger toggle or collapsed navigation must be present
    const hamburger = page.locator('[aria-label*="menu" i], [aria-label*="navigation" i], [aria-controls*="nav" i]').first();
    const fullNav = page.getByRole('navigation').locator('ul > li').first();
    const hamburgerVisible = await hamburger.isVisible();
    const fullNavVisible = await fullNav.isVisible();
    expect(hamburgerVisible || fullNavVisible).toBe(true);
    await context.close();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Setting `viewport: { width: 320 }` does not replicate the effect of browser zoom at the OS level — in particular, text rendering at actual 400% zoom may cause line-breaking behaviour that differs from a native 320px viewport. For WCAG 1.4.10 compliance sign-off, supplement this automated scroll-width check with a manual review at 400% browser zoom in Chrome or Firefox. The test does catch the most common failure mode (fixed-width containers that overflow at small viewports) and should be run as a CI gate even though it is not a perfect substitute for the spec's zoom-based test method. [community]

---

### Pattern 128 (Cycle 41) — Accessible Name via `aria-labelledby` with Multiple ID References

`aria-labelledby` accepts a space-separated list of IDREFS, causing the accessible name to be computed by concatenating the text content of all referenced elements in order. This pattern is used to build composite labels — for example, a price table cell labelled by both the row header and column header: `aria-labelledby="row-product-1 col-price"`. The Playwright test must assert the computed accessible name using `toHaveAccessibleName()`, which evaluates the full IDREF chain and concatenation. A bug where one IDREF points to a non-existent element silently drops that portion of the label; only the explicit name assertion catches this failure.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/aria-labelledby-multi.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('aria-labelledby with multiple IDREFs', () => {
  test('price table cells compute composite accessible names correctly', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/pricing');
    // Example: a cell labelled by "Basic Plan" (row) + "Monthly Price" (col)
    const basicMonthlyCell = page.getByRole('cell', { name: /basic.*monthly/i }).first();
    await expect(basicMonthlyCell).toHaveAccessibleName(/basic.*monthly/i);
  });

  test('all aria-labelledby IDREFs reference existing elements', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/pricing');
    const violations = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const results: { element: string; missingId: string }[] = [];
      document.querySelectorAll('[aria-labelledby]').forEach((el) => {
        const ids = (el.getAttribute('aria-labelledby') ?? '').split(/\s+/);
        ids.forEach((id) => {
          if (id && !document.getElementById(id)) {
            results.push({ element: el.tagName + (el.id ? `#${el.id}` : ''), missingId: id });
          }
        });
      });
      return results;
    });
    expect(violations, `Broken aria-labelledby IDREFs: ${JSON.stringify(violations)}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('axe: no aria-labelledby violations on pricing page', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/pricing');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa']).analyze();
    const labelledByViolations = results.violations.filter((v) =>
      ['aria-labelledby', 'label-content-name-mismatch'].includes(v.id)
    );
    expect(labelledByViolations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** The ARIA accessible name computation concatenates IDREF target text with spaces between each referenced element. If the referenced elements themselves contain nested elements with their own accessible names (e.g., `<span aria-label="hidden-label">visible</span>`), the concatenation may include text that is not visually apparent to sighted users, creating a disconnect between the visual label and the AT-announced label. Keep `aria-labelledby` references simple — point to elements whose text content is purely presentational text, not interactive elements with their own name computations. [official]

---

### Pattern 129 (Cycle 41) — `aria-live` Region Timing: Testing Asynchronous Announcement Sequences

`aria-live` regions announce DOM mutations to AT. The challenge in testing is that mutations must occur after the live region is already mounted in the DOM — a common mistake is rendering the region and inserting content simultaneously, which causes the mutation to be missed by the AT because the element was not yet registered as a live region. The Playwright test validates this by checking that the live region exists in the DOM before any content insertion, and by simulating user actions that trigger asynchronous updates with a deliberate wait between mount and mutation.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/live-region-timing.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('aria-live region timing and announcement', () => {
  test('live region is present in DOM before content is injected', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    // The live region should be mounted immediately on page load, not only when results arrive
    const liveRegion = page.locator('[aria-live]');
    await expect(liveRegion).toBeAttached(); // present in DOM even when empty
    await expect(liveRegion).toBeEmpty();    // starts empty

    // Trigger a search
    await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill('playwright');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /search/i }).click();

    // Wait for results count to appear in the live region
    await expect(liveRegion).not.toBeEmpty({ timeout: 5000 });
    const announcement = await liveRegion.textContent();
    expect(announcement).toMatch(/\d+ result/i);
  });

  test('polite live region content updates after repeated identical searches', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    const liveRegion = page.locator('[aria-live="polite"]');
    await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill('test');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /search/i }).click();
    const firstText = await liveRegion.textContent();

    // Perform the same search again — region should update to trigger re-announcement
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /search/i }).click();
    // If content is identical, some AT won't re-announce; clear and re-set to guarantee announcement
    const secondText = await liveRegion.textContent();
    // Content should have been cleared and re-set (not left identical)
    expect(firstText).not.toBe(''); // existed after first search
    expect(secondText).not.toBe(''); // re-populated after second search
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Playwright cannot directly intercept or record AT speech announcements — the test can only verify DOM state changes in the live region, not that the AT actually vocalised the text. For a complete announcement audit, combine this DOM-state test with a manual AT session (NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver + Safari) to confirm announcement timing and content. The "clear-and-re-set" pattern for identical content (setting the region to empty then re-populating it on the next tick) is a reliable workaround for the AT non-re-announcement problem but is not formally specified in the ARIA spec — document it as an intentional implementation choice to prevent future developers from "fixing" it. [community]

---

### Pattern 130 (Cycle 41) — Aria Snapshot Structural Regression Testing for Complex Widgets

Playwright's `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` captures a YAML representation of the accessibility tree and enables structural regression testing for complex compound widgets. Unlike visual snapshots, aria snapshots are text-based, diff cleanly in code review, and reflect what AT actually perceives. The recommended pattern is to use partial snapshots (omitting dynamic attributes such as `expanded` and `checked`) for stable structural assertions, while using separate attribute-specific assertions for dynamic states. Store `.aria.yml` fixture files alongside test files for reviewability.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/aria-snapshot-regression.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Aria snapshot structural regression', () => {
  test('main navigation matches aria snapshot', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    const nav = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /main/i });
    // Partial snapshot: checks structure, skips dynamic aria-expanded on dropdowns
    await expect(nav).toMatchAriaSnapshot({ name: 'main-nav.aria.yml' });
  });

  test('product listing grid structure matches snapshot', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    const grid = page.getByRole('list', { name: /products/i });
    // Use partial mode with regex for item counts that vary with data
    await expect(grid).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - list "Products":
        - listitem
        - listitem
    `);
  });

  test('dialog structure matches snapshot when open', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products/1');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /quick view/i }).click();
    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();
    await expect(dialog).toMatchAriaSnapshot({ name: 'product-quick-view-dialog.aria.yml' });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Aria snapshots encode the full accessibility tree structure, including all child roles and names. A legitimate component refactor (renaming a button label, adding a new nav item) will break the snapshot and require a deliberate `--update-snapshots` run. Teams that auto-update snapshots as part of CI rather than reviewing the diff lose the regression safety net entirely. Establish a review policy: snapshot diffs must be reviewed and approved in pull requests, and the `--update-snapshots` flag should only be run locally with the diff reviewed before commit. Aria snapshots do not catch focus-order bugs or `aria-activedescendant` mismatches — they complement, rather than replace, the interaction-level tests in patterns 119–129. [official]

---

### Pattern 131 (Cycle 41) — Accessible Form Error Messaging: `aria-invalid` + `aria-errormessage` vs `aria-describedby`

ARIA 1.2 introduced `aria-errormessage` as the preferred mechanism for pointing an invalid form field to its error message, replacing the earlier `aria-describedby` pattern for errors. The difference is semantic: `aria-describedby` concatenates all referenced descriptions and announces them when the element gains focus, while `aria-errormessage` is only announced by AT when `aria-invalid="true"` is also set on the element. The test must verify three things: the error message element exists and is visible, `aria-invalid="true"` is set after failed validation, and `aria-errormessage` references the correct element id.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/form-error-messaging.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('Form accessible error messaging (aria-invalid + aria-errormessage)', () => {
  test('invalid email field carries aria-invalid and aria-errormessage after submission', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i }).fill('not-an-email');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();

    const emailField = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i });
    await expect(emailField).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
    const errorMsgId = await emailField.getAttribute('aria-errormessage');
    expect(errorMsgId).toBeTruthy();

    const errorElement = page.locator(`#${errorMsgId}`);
    await expect(errorElement).toBeVisible();
    await expect(errorElement).toContainText(/valid email/i);

    // Accessible description should include the error for older AT using describedby
    await expect(emailField).toHaveAccessibleDescription(/valid email/i);
  });

  test('error state clears aria-invalid when corrected', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i }).fill('bad');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i })).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');

    // Correct the value and re-submit
    await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i }).fill('good@example.com');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email/i })).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');
  });

  test('axe scan after validation error finds no aria violations', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa']).analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `aria-errormessage` is not yet widely supported across all AT versions — NVDA 2023.x and VoiceOver on iOS 16 handle it correctly, but older AT may ignore it entirely. For maximum compatibility, use `aria-describedby` as the primary error pointer and `aria-errormessage` as a supplementary attribute: `aria-describedby="field-hint field-error" aria-errormessage="field-error"`. The axe-core `aria-errormessage` rule (introduced in axe 4.6) will flag `aria-errormessage` set on elements that do not also have `aria-invalid="true"`, so always set both attributes atomically. [official]

---

### Pattern 132 (Cycle 41) — `prefers-reduced-motion` Accessibility: Testing Animation Disablement

WCAG 2.3.3 (Level AAA) and the broader accessibility principle behind it requires that motion animations can be disabled when the user has set `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. While AAA, this is increasingly required by legal standards in some jurisdictions and is a material accessibility concern for users with vestibular disorders. The Playwright test emulates the `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` media query and then asserts that animated elements use `animation: none` or `transition: none` in computed styles, and that the application does not render auto-playing video or parallax scrolling elements.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/reduced-motion.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('prefers-reduced-motion compliance', () => {
  test('CSS animations are suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce', async ({ browser }) => {
    const context = await browser.newContext({
      reducedMotion: 'reduce',
    });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Check that elements with known animation classes have no running animation
    const animatedEls = page.locator('.animate, [data-animate], .transition-all, .fade-in');
    const count = await animatedEls.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 10); i++) {
      const animationName = await animatedEls.nth(i).evaluate((el) =>
        getComputedStyle(el).animationName
      );
      expect(animationName, `Element ${i} still has animation "${animationName}" under reduced-motion`).toBe('none');
    }
    await context.close();
  });

  test('hero banner auto-play video is paused under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce', async ({ browser }) => {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.goto('/');
    const videos = page.locator('video[autoplay]');
    const videoCount = await videos.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < videoCount; i++) {
      const isPaused = await videos.nth(i).evaluate((el: HTMLVideoElement) => el.paused);
      expect(isPaused, `Video ${i} is auto-playing under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`).toBe(true);
    }
    await context.close();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Playwright's `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` context option emits the correct media query to the browser, so CSS `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` rules are applied as expected. However, JavaScript-driven animations (GSAP, Framer Motion, custom `requestAnimationFrame` loops) read the media query via `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` at runtime — a one-time check at component mount may miss the preference if it is toggled after mount. For JS-driven animations, test both at initial navigation under `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` and after a simulated preference change by overriding `window.matchMedia` in a `page.addInitScript`. [community]

---

### Pattern 133 (Cycle 41) — Keyboard Trap Testing for Modal Focus Lock

WCAG 2.1.2 (Level A) requires that if keyboard focus can be moved to a component, it must be possible to move focus away using only the keyboard. Modal dialogs intentionally lock focus — but only within the modal, not in the entire page. The test must confirm that Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through all focusable elements within the open modal and never escape to background content, and that focus is released when the modal closes (Escape key or close button).

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/focus-trap.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Modal focus trap (WCAG 2.1.2)', () => {
  test('Tab key cycles within open modal and never reaches background', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open settings/i }).click();
    const modal = page.getByRole('dialog');
    await expect(modal).toBeVisible();

    // Collect focusable elements inside the modal
    const focusableCount = await modal
      .locator('a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])')
      .count();

    // Tab through all focusable elements + 1 extra — should wrap back inside, not escape
    for (let i = 0; i <= focusableCount; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
      const isInsideModal = await page.evaluate(() => {
        const modal = document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]');
        return modal ? modal.contains(document.activeElement) : false;
      });
      expect(isInsideModal, `Focus escaped modal on Tab press ${i + 1}`).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test('Escape key closes modal and returns focus to trigger', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const trigger = page.getByRole('button', { name: /open settings/i });
    await trigger.click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeHidden();
    // Focus must return to the triggering button
    await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Focus trap libraries (focus-trap, react-focus-lock, a11y-dialog) handle the Tab cycle internally and generally pass this test. The failure mode caught by this pattern is most often a custom modal implementation that uses CSS `visibility: hidden` to hide background content without updating `tabindex` — background elements remain focusable even though they are visually hidden. The `toBeHidden()` Playwright assertion uses the accessibility tree "hidden" state, which accounts for `visibility: hidden` and `display: none` but not `pointer-events: none` or `opacity: 0`, so elements hidden via opacity alone will still appear focusable. Always pair the focus-trap test with an axe scan that flags `aria-hidden` violations on background elements. [official]

---

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 41)

191. **[community] `toHaveAccessibleName()` in Playwright resolves the accessible name using the Chromium accessibility API, which follows the ARIA name computation algorithm — but the algorithm's treatment of `aria-labelledby` references that include elements with `display: none` differs between Chromium and Firefox, causing tests that pass in Chromium to silently produce a different accessible name in Firefox**: The ARIA specification says the accessible name computation should traverse hidden elements when they are referenced by `aria-labelledby`, but browser implementations diverge on this point. Chromium (and therefore Playwright's default test runner) follows the spec strictly and includes hidden-element text in the computed name; Firefox applies a different heuristic and may exclude it. WHY: Teams build accessible name assertions in Playwright's Chromium runner, ship the product, and then receive screen reader bug reports from users on Firefox where the accessible name is empty or incomplete because the `aria-labelledby` reference points to a `display: none` element. The fix is to never reference elements with `display: none` in `aria-labelledby` — use `visibility: hidden` with `position: absolute; clip: rect(0,0,0,0)` for visually-hidden-but-accessible name sources, which all browsers expose correctly to the accessibility tree. [community]

192. **[community] axe-core's `color-contrast` rule only evaluates the direct foreground and background color pair — it does not compute contrast for text that is positioned over a semi-transparent overlay, a frosted-glass `backdrop-filter`, or a pseudo-element background — meaning designs that use glassmorphism UI patterns will pass axe contrast checks despite failing visually for many users**: `backdrop-filter: blur()` creates a frosted-glass effect whose effective background depends on whatever content is behind the element in the stacking context, which is entirely dynamic and unknown to static analysis tools. The actual contrast of text rendered on a frosted pane varies with page scroll position. WHY: Design systems adopt glassmorphism UI tokens that carry a nominal background color for documentation purposes, developers run axe and see a pass against that nominal color, then the feature ships — but real users encounter frames where the background content is light text on a light frosted pane, dropping contrast below 4.5:1. The only reliable fix is to specify a minimum opaque background color for the frosted container's worst-case scenario and document it in the design token metadata. [community]

193. **[community] `role="tooltip"` elements that are conditionally rendered (removed from the DOM when hidden, rather than hidden via `visibility: hidden`) are not associated with their trigger element by AT between hover/focus events, because `aria-describedby` requires the referenced element to exist in the DOM at the time the trigger element is focused — a tooltip that mounts on focus and is referenced by `aria-describedby` will have a broken reference for the split second between focus and mount**: This is a race condition in React and Vue component patterns where `aria-describedby` is set on the trigger unconditionally but the tooltip `<div id="tooltip-xyz">` only mounts after state updates on focus. The ARIA accessible name computation reads `aria-describedby` at the moment the element gains focus; if the referenced element does not yet exist, the description is empty. WHY: The tooltip appears visually and works correctly for mouse users (hover shows the tooltip, hover-in triggers the mount, no race condition because the tooltip is present before the next AT poll cycle), but keyboard users trigger the focus event faster than the component can mount the tooltip DOM node, resulting in the description never being announced. The fix is to pre-mount the tooltip with `visibility: hidden` and toggle only its visibility on focus/hover, ensuring the `aria-describedby` reference is always valid. [community]

194. **[community] When using `aria-live="assertive"` for form validation errors that appear after inline validation on `blur`, the assertive announcement interrupts whatever the screen reader was currently reading — including the label of the next field the user has already tabbed to — causing AT users to lose their place in the form and re-navigate to understand the error context**: Live regions with `aria-live="assertive"` pre-empt ongoing speech. A user who tabs quickly from a field, triggering blur-validation, lands on the next field and begins hearing its label announcement — then the assertive live region fires and interrupts with the error for the previous field, requiring the user to navigate backward to understand the error. WHY: Developers use `assertive` because they want errors to be announced immediately and prominently, not realising that "assertive" means "interrupt whatever is currently being spoken", which for blur-triggered validation interrupts the next-field announcement rather than the error field announcement. The fix is to use `aria-live="polite"` for inline validation errors so announcements queue after the current speech completes, and to additionally set `aria-invalid="true"` on the invalid field to give the user a structural cue available on demand. [community]

195. **[community] Playwright's `page.getByRole('button')` will match `<input type="submit">` and `<input type="button">` elements because their computed ARIA role is `button` — but elements matched this way do not have an `innerText` property, so assertions that check accessible name via `.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i })` match against the `value` attribute for input-type buttons, which can cause test false positives when multiple button-like inputs share similar `value` text without being the specific element the test intends to target**: A form with two `<input type="submit" value="Submit">` elements (e.g., one in a toolbar and one in a footer) will both be matched by `getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })` and Playwright will throw a "strict mode violation — found 2 elements" error, causing teams to work around it with `.first()` — which silently targets the wrong button if the DOM order changes. WHY: Developers migrate from testing-library patterns where `getByRole('button', { name: '...' })` is unique by convention, but in Playwright strict mode all role locators must be unique; using `.first()` as a quick fix to silence the error creates a fragile test that targets whichever button is first in source order rather than asserting uniqueness. The fix is to scope the locator to a specific container (`page.getByRole('form').getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })`) or add a `data-testid` to disambiguate buttons that share the same accessible name. [community]
