## Cycle 42 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 134 (Cycle 42) — WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging Movements: Single-Pointer Alternative Coverage

WCAG 2.5.7 (Level AA, new in 2.2) requires that every UI feature relying on a dragging movement also exposes an equivalent single-pointer (click/tap) path. The three most common drag surfaces that violate this criterion are: sortable lists with no up/down buttons, range sliders with no text-input fallback, and canvas-based drawing tools with no keyboard-invokable endpoint selector. A Playwright test must enumerate each drag target, attempt to complete the same action through click-only interaction, and assert an equivalent outcome — it must not simulate a drag.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/dragging-movements-2_5_7.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging Movements — single-pointer alternatives', () => {
  test('range slider exposes a text input or click-on-track alternative', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings/audio');
    const slider = page.getByRole('slider', { name: /volume/i });
    await expect(slider).toBeVisible();

    // Verify a non-drag alternative exists: either a sibling <input type="number"> or
    // clicking the track at a specific X offset advances the value
    const inputFallback = page.getByRole('spinbutton', { name: /volume/i });
    const hasFallback = await inputFallback.count() > 0;

    if (hasFallback) {
      await inputFallback.fill('75');
      await inputFallback.press('Enter');
      await expect(slider).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '75');
    } else {
      // Click on the track at 75% of its width
      const box = await page.locator('[data-volume-track]').boundingBox();
      expect(box).not.toBeNull();
      await page.mouse.click(box!.x + box!.width * 0.75, box!.y + box!.height / 2);
      const valueNow = Number(await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow'));
      expect(valueNow).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(70);
    }
  });

  test('sortable list has up/down button controls as drag alternative', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard/widgets');
    const listItems = page.getByRole('listitem');
    const firstItemText = await listItems.first().innerText();

    // Each item must have a "Move up" or "Move down" control
    const moveDownBtn = listItems.first().getByRole('button', { name: /move down/i });
    await expect(moveDownBtn).toBeVisible();
    await moveDownBtn.click();

    const newFirstItemText = await listItems.first().innerText();
    expect(newFirstItemText).not.toBe(firstItemText);
  });

  test('axe scan confirms no drag-only patterns flagged', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard/widgets');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag22aa'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** WCAG 2.5.7 does not prohibit dragging — it requires an *alternative*, not a replacement. Tests that only verify drag interaction do not surface violations; the test must positively confirm the non-drag path completes the same task. axe-core does not yet have a dedicated `dragging-movements` automated rule (the criterion requires semantic understanding of intent), so all coverage for this SC is manual or interaction-level. Do not rely on axe tags alone to catch 2.5.7 violations — treat this pattern as an exclusively manual-or-e2e concern. [official]

---

### Pattern 135 (Cycle 42) — WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance: Area and Contrast Formula Testing

WCAG 2.4.13 (Level AAA, new in 2.2) requires that the focus indicator: (a) encloses the perimeter of the focused component by at least a 2 CSS-pixel-thick area, and (b) achieves at least a 3:1 contrast ratio between the focused and unfocused state pixels. Playwright can evaluate both requirements by reading computed styles (`outline-width`, `outline-color`, `outline-offset`) and computing the perimeter area formula client-side. The area formula is: `area ≥ 2 × perimeter` where perimeter is the CSS outline of the unfocused bounding rectangle.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/focus-appearance-2_4_13.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Minimal luminance-to-contrast helper (W3C formula)
function relativeLuminance(r: number, g: number, b: number): number {
  const toLinear = (c: number) => {
    const s = c / 255;
    return s <= 0.04045 ? s / 12.92 : Math.pow((s + 0.055) / 1.055, 2.4);
  };
  return 0.2126 * toLinear(r) + 0.7152 * toLinear(g) + 0.0722 * toLinear(b);
}
function contrastRatio(l1: number, l2: number): number {
  const [lo, hi] = l1 < l2 ? [l1, l2] : [l2, l1];
  return (hi + 0.05) / (lo + 0.05);
}

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance', () => {
  const interactiveSelectors = ['a[href]', 'button:not([disabled])', 'input:not([type="hidden"])'];

  test('primary CTA button focus indicator meets 2px area and 3:1 contrast', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const btn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /get started/i }).first();
    await btn.focus();

    const styles = await btn.evaluate((el) => {
      const cs = getComputedStyle(el);
      return {
        outlineWidth: parseFloat(cs.outlineWidth),
        outlineOffset: parseFloat(cs.outlineOffset),
        outlineColor: cs.outlineColor,           // rgb(r,g,b)
        backgroundColor: cs.backgroundColor,
      };
    });

    // Area requirement: outline-width must be >= 2px
    expect(styles.outlineWidth, 'outline-width must be at least 2px').toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);

    // Contrast requirement: parse outline color and background
    const parseRgb = (s: string) => {
      const m = s.match(/\d+/g)!.map(Number);
      return { r: m[0], g: m[1], b: m[2] };
    };
    const fg = parseRgb(styles.outlineColor);
    const bg = parseRgb(styles.backgroundColor);
    const ratio = contrastRatio(
      relativeLuminance(fg.r, fg.g, fg.b),
      relativeLuminance(bg.r, bg.g, bg.b),
    );
    expect(ratio, `Focus indicator contrast ${ratio.toFixed(2)} does not meet 3:1`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** WCAG 2.4.13 is Level AAA and not legally required in most jurisdictions, but it is the formalization of a practice already required by WCAG 1.4.11 (non-text contrast) for UI components. Computing the exact perimeter area in Playwright requires knowing the element's border-radius — a pill button's perimeter is longer than a rectangle's perimeter, so a 2px outline on a pill-shaped button covers more area than required. The test above approximates by checking `outline-width >= 2` which is sufficient for rectangular elements; for rounded elements with `border-radius > 0`, compute `2 × (2 × (W + H) + 2π × r)` client-side for an accurate floor. The contrast formula measures focused-vs-unfocused state delta, not foreground-vs-background, so a dark outline on a white background that disappears on a dark mode background would fail. [official]

---

### Pattern 136 (Cycle 42) — ARIA Treeview Keyboard Contract: `role=tree`, `role=treeitem`, Arrow Navigation

WCAG 4.1.2 (Level A) and the ARIA Authoring Practices Guide define a strict keyboard contract for tree widgets: Right Arrow opens a collapsed node or moves focus to its first child; Left Arrow closes an open node or moves focus to the parent; Up/Down Arrow moves focus between visible nodes without changing expansion state; Home/End move to the first/last visible node. Playwright tests must exercise all four arrow keys plus Home/End and assert the correct `aria-expanded` state transitions and `document.activeElement` positions after each.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/treeview-keyboard.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Treeview keyboard contract (APG)', () => {
  test('Right Arrow expands collapsed parent treeitem', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-browser');
    const tree = page.getByRole('tree');
    await expect(tree).toBeVisible();

    const firstParent = tree.getByRole('treeitem', { name: /src/i }).first();
    await expect(firstParent).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    await firstParent.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    await expect(firstParent).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
  });

  test('Right Arrow on open parent moves focus to first child', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-browser');
    const tree = page.getByRole('tree');
    const parent = tree.getByRole('treeitem', { name: /src/i }).first();
    await parent.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight'); // expand
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight'); // move to first child
    const focused = await page.evaluate(() =>
      document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role') + ':' +
      document.activeElement?.textContent?.trim()
    );
    expect(focused).toMatch(/^treeitem:/);
  });

  test('Left Arrow on open parent collapses it', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-browser');
    const parent = page.getByRole('tree').getByRole('treeitem', { name: /src/i }).first();
    await parent.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight'); // expand
    await expect(parent).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft'); // collapse
    await expect(parent).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  });

  test('Down/Up Arrow navigates visible nodes sequentially', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-browser');
    const tree = page.getByRole('tree');
    const items = tree.getByRole('treeitem');
    await items.first().focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    const secondText = await items.nth(1).textContent();
    const focusedText = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.textContent?.trim());
    expect(focusedText).toBe(secondText?.trim());
  });

  test('Home/End navigate to first/last visible treeitem', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/file-browser');
    const tree = page.getByRole('tree');
    const items = tree.getByRole('treeitem');
    const firstText = (await items.first().textContent())?.trim();
    const lastText = (await items.last().textContent())?.trim();

    await items.first().focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('End');
    const afterEnd = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.textContent?.trim());
    expect(afterEnd).toBe(lastText);

    await page.keyboard.press('Home');
    const afterHome = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.textContent?.trim());
    expect(afterHome).toBe(firstText);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Tree widgets are one of the most complex ARIA patterns to implement correctly. The most common failure is using `tabindex` on every `treeitem` rather than the roving `tabindex` pattern (only the currently active node should have `tabindex="0"`; all others should have `tabindex="-1"`). Playwright's `focus()` call bypasses the roving tabindex contract — always verify keyboard navigation using actual key presses, not `locator.focus()`. For virtualized trees that only render visible nodes in the DOM, `Home`/`End` assertions must account for the fact that the last visible DOM node may not be the last logical tree node; assert `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset` instead. [official]

---

### Pattern 137 (Cycle 42) — ARIA Disclosure Widget: `aria-expanded` Toggle + Keyboard Contract

The ARIA APG Disclosure pattern covers `<button aria-expanded="true|false" aria-controls="content-id">` — a simpler pattern than accordion but often confused with it. The disclosure button uses Enter and Space to toggle; there is no arrow-key navigation between sibling disclosures (that is the accordion variant). Tests must verify the `aria-expanded` attribute matches the visual state, that `aria-controls` references the correct container id, and that a keyboard-only user can reach and activate the button.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/disclosure-widget.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('ARIA Disclosure widget (APG)', () => {
  test('disclosure button is reachable by Tab and toggles with Enter', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const disclosure = page.getByRole('button', { name: /what is your return policy/i });
    await expect(disclosure).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

    await disclosure.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
    await expect(disclosure).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

    // Controlled region must be visible
    const controlledId = await disclosure.getAttribute('aria-controls');
    expect(controlledId).toBeTruthy();
    await expect(page.locator(`#${controlledId}`)).toBeVisible();
  });

  test('Space key also toggles disclosure', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const disclosure = page.getByRole('button', { name: /what is your return policy/i });
    await disclosure.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
    await expect(disclosure).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
    await expect(disclosure).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  });

  test('aria-controls id references an existing element', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const buttons = page.getByRole('button').filter({ has: page.locator('[aria-expanded]') });
    const count = await buttons.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const controlledId = await buttons.nth(i).getAttribute('aria-controls');
      if (controlledId) {
        const target = page.locator(`#${controlledId}`);
        await expect(target).toHaveCount(1);
      }
    }
  });

  test('axe scan finds no ARIA attribute violations on faq page', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page }).withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa']).analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `aria-controls` has historically had poor AT support (JAWS did not follow `aria-controls` for disclosure buttons until JAWS 2022). The APG still recommends including it because screen readers that do support it can announce the controlled element's role, and the attribute is required for the pattern to be formally correct. However, when `aria-controls` references an id that does not exist in the DOM — a common mistake in React where ids are generated dynamically — AT will silently ignore the reference rather than surfacing an error. axe-core's `aria-valid-attr-value` rule does catch dangling `aria-controls` references, so include the axe scan step in this test. [official]

---

### Pattern 138 (Cycle 42) — Virtual Scroll Accessibility: `aria-rowcount`, `aria-rowindex`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-posinset`

Virtual/windowed lists and grids only render the visible rows in the DOM, breaking AT assumptions about total item counts. ARIA provides four attributes to communicate the logical (not DOM) size: `aria-rowcount`/`aria-colcount` on `role=grid` or `role=table`, `aria-rowindex` on each `role=row`, and `aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset` on flat `role=listbox` or `role=list` patterns. The test must scroll the virtual container and assert that `aria-rowindex` increments correctly and that `aria-rowcount` matches the data source count rather than the DOM node count.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/virtual-scroll-aria.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Virtual scroll ARIA position attributes', () => {
  test('grid aria-rowcount equals total data rows, not DOM rows', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/reports/transactions');
    const grid = page.getByRole('grid');
    await expect(grid).toBeVisible();

    const domRowCount = await grid.getByRole('row').count();
    const ariaRowCount = Number(await grid.getAttribute('aria-rowcount'));
    // Virtual scroll renders only ~20 rows; total data set is much larger
    expect(ariaRowCount).toBeGreaterThan(domRowCount);
  });

  test('aria-rowindex values are sequential and start at 1', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/reports/transactions');
    const grid = page.getByRole('grid');
    const rows = grid.getByRole('row').filter({ hasNot: page.getByRole('columnheader') });
    const count = await rows.count();

    let expectedIndex = 1;
    for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 10); i++) {
      const idx = Number(await rows.nth(i).getAttribute('aria-rowindex'));
      expect(idx, `Row ${i} aria-rowindex mismatch`).toBe(expectedIndex++);
    }
  });

  test('after scrolling, aria-rowindex continues sequentially from scroll offset', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/reports/transactions');
    const container = page.locator('[data-virtual-scroller]');
    await container.evaluate((el) => { el.scrollTop = 2000; });
    await page.waitForTimeout(300); // allow virtualized re-render

    const grid = page.getByRole('grid');
    const firstVisibleRow = grid.getByRole('row')
      .filter({ hasNot: page.getByRole('columnheader') })
      .first();
    const rowIndex = Number(await firstVisibleRow.getAttribute('aria-rowindex'));
    expect(rowIndex).toBeGreaterThan(10); // must reflect scroll offset, not reset to 1
  });

  test('listbox uses aria-setsize and aria-posinset for flat virtual list', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill('report');
    const listbox = page.getByRole('listbox');
    await expect(listbox).toBeVisible();

    const firstOption = listbox.getByRole('option').first();
    await expect(firstOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-posinset', '1');
    const setSize = Number(await firstOption.getAttribute('aria-setsize'));
    expect(setSize).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `aria-rowcount=-1` is the ARIA-defined sentinel value meaning "total count is unknown" — this is valid for infinite scroll that has no predetermined end. However, AT support for `-1` varies: JAWS and NVDA announce it as "unknown number of rows", which is acceptable, but some AT incorrectly announce it as "-1 rows". Prefer setting the real count when known and use `-1` only for genuinely unbounded streams. Also note: `aria-rowindex` is 1-based in the ARIA spec — a common implementation error is 0-based `aria-rowindex` which causes JAWS to announce "row 0 of N" rather than "row 1 of N". [official]

---

### Pattern 139 (Cycle 42) — `toHaveRole` and `toHaveAccessibleName` Combined Assertion Pattern

Playwright 1.44+ exposes `toHaveRole(role)` as a dedicated assertion that checks the *computed* ARIA role (not the `role` attribute value). Combining `toHaveRole` with `toHaveAccessibleName` provides a two-axis check: semantic role is correct AND the name computation resolves to the expected string. This pattern replaces fragile `getAttribute('role')` assertions and avoids the `getByRole` locator ambiguity when an element's role is being explicitly verified rather than used for selection.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/role-name-assertions.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('toHaveRole + toHaveAccessibleName combined assertions', () => {
  test('navigation landmark has correct role and label', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const mainNav = page.locator('nav').first();
    await expect(mainNav).toHaveRole('navigation');
    await expect(mainNav).toHaveAccessibleName(/main navigation/i);
  });

  test('icon-only button resolves accessible name from aria-label', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const closeBtn = page.locator('[data-testid="close-banner"]');
    await expect(closeBtn).toHaveRole('button');
    // Accessible name must not be empty — icon-only button requires aria-label
    await expect(closeBtn).toHaveAccessibleName(/close/i);
  });

  test('custom div-based toggle has computed role=switch', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings/notifications');
    const toggle = page.locator('[data-testid="email-toggle"]');
    await expect(toggle).toHaveRole('switch');
    await expect(toggle).toHaveAccessibleName(/email notifications/i);
    // Verify checked state attribute is present
    const checked = await toggle.getAttribute('aria-checked');
    expect(['true', 'false']).toContain(checked);
  });

  test('image with decorative empty alt has role=none/presentation', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/about');
    // Decorative images must have role=none or empty alt that removes them from the tree
    const decorativeImg = page.locator('img[alt=""]').first();
    // An img with alt="" is implicitly presentation — accessible name should be absent
    const name = await decorativeImg.evaluate((el) =>
      el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? el.getAttribute('alt') ?? ''
    );
    expect(name).toBe('');
  });

  test('article landmark resolves accessible name from aria-labelledby', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/blog');
    const article = page.getByRole('article').first();
    await expect(article).toHaveRole('article');
    // Article accessible name derived from heading inside via aria-labelledby
    const name = await article.evaluate((el) => {
      const id = el.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
      if (!id) return null;
      return document.getElementById(id)?.textContent?.trim() ?? null;
    });
    expect(name).toBeTruthy();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `toHaveRole` checks the computed ARIA role, which means it respects role inheritance and role overrides — an `<input type="checkbox">` has computed role `checkbox` even without an explicit `role` attribute, and a `<button role="link">` has computed role `link`. This is correct behavior and should not be worked around. The edge case to watch is `role="none"` vs `role="presentation"` — they are synonyms in ARIA 1.2, but Playwright's `toHaveRole` normalizes to the canonical role name. Ensure assertions use `'none'` or `'presentation'` consistently with whatever the implementation uses to avoid false failures. [official]

---

### Pattern 140 (Cycle 42) — Accessible Authentication Testing: WCAG 3.3.8 Paste Non-Interference + Autocomplete

WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum, Level AA, new in 2.2) prohibits requiring users to solve cognitive function tests — including transcribing characters from a CAPTCHA or solving a puzzle — to authenticate. It also implicitly requires that login fields do not block paste (clipboard injection) or password manager autofill. The Playwright test must verify: (1) `autocomplete` attributes are correctly set, (2) paste into the password field is not blocked by a `paste` event listener, and (3) any CAPTCHA has an accessible alternative.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/accessible-auth-3_3_8.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication', () => {
  test('username field has autocomplete="username"', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    const username = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /email|username/i });
    await expect(username).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', 'username');
  });

  test('password field has autocomplete="current-password"', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    const pwd = page.locator('input[type="password"]');
    await expect(pwd).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', 'current-password');
  });

  test('paste into password field is not blocked', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    const pwd = page.locator('input[type="password"]');
    await pwd.focus();

    // Use clipboard API to paste a value
    await page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.writeText('PasteTestPwd1!'));
    await page.keyboard.press('Control+v');
    // Allow async paste handler to complete
    await page.waitForTimeout(100);

    const value = await pwd.inputValue();
    expect(value.length, 'Password field appears to block paste — value is empty after Ctrl+V').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('new-password autocomplete is set on registration form', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/register');
    const newPwd = page.locator('input[type="password"]').first();
    await expect(newPwd).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', 'new-password');
  });

  test('axe scan includes best-practice rules for autocomplete', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'best-practice'])
      .analyze();
    const autocompleteViolations = results.violations.filter(v =>
      v.id === 'autocomplete-valid' || v.id === 'input-button-name'
    );
    expect(autocompleteViolations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Some SPAs use controlled inputs and `onPaste` handlers that call `event.preventDefault()` to enforce password complexity rules client-side before storing the value — this directly violates WCAG 3.3.8. The Playwright paste test above catches this pattern reliably when the clipboard API is available. In CI environments where the clipboard API requires permissions, use `page.evaluate(() => { ... })` to inject the paste via `document.execCommand('insertText', false, value)` as a fallback. Note that `autocomplete="new-password"` on the confirm-password field may cause some password managers to offer to save two separate passwords — the correct approach is `autocomplete="new-password"` on both the password and confirm-password fields. [official]

---

### Pattern 141 (Cycle 42) — `aria-live` Region Debounce and Pre-render Pattern Testing

AT reads `aria-live` regions by polling for DOM mutations. Two well-known failure modes exist: (1) injecting content into a live region before the region is mounted causes AT to miss the announcement because the initial population is not a "change" (the region must exist empty before content is inserted), and (2) rapid successive updates cause AT to skip intermediate announcements — only the last update within the debounce window is announced. Tests must assert both the pre-mount empty state and the post-update non-empty state, and must not collapse multiple updates into a single assertion.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/aria-live-regions.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('aria-live region correctness patterns', () => {
  test('status live region is in DOM and empty before search is triggered', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    const status = page.getByRole('status');
    // Region must exist before user interaction (pre-render pattern)
    await expect(status).toBeAttached();
    await expect(status).toBeEmpty();
  });

  test('status region announces result count after search', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill('accessibility');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /search/i }).click();
    const status = page.getByRole('status');
    await expect(status).toContainText(/\d+ result/i);
  });

  test('alert region is empty until error condition and pre-exists in DOM', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout');
    const alert = page.getByRole('alert');
    await expect(alert).toBeAttached();
    // No error yet — content must be empty or hidden
    const initialText = (await alert.textContent())?.trim() ?? '';
    expect(initialText).toBe('');

    // Trigger an error
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /place order/i }).click();
    await expect(alert).not.toBeEmpty();
  });

  test('rapid successive updates — last update is persisted in live region', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/live-updates');
    const log = page.getByRole('log');
    await expect(log).toBeAttached();

    // Trigger rapid updates
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /start feed/i }).click();
    await page.waitForTimeout(500);

    // Log must have at least one entry — content not be cleared by rapid mutation
    await expect(log).not.toBeEmpty();
    const text = await log.textContent();
    expect(text!.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Playwright cannot actually assert that AT *announced* a live region update — it can only assert that the DOM content changed. Playwright has no screen reader integration layer by default (Guidepup provides that). These tests verify the structural prerequisites for correct AT behavior (region exists before content, content is non-empty after trigger) but cannot confirm the announcement was made. AT behavior also differs by `aria-live` type: `polite` queues after the current utterance, `assertive` interrupts immediately, and `role=log` implies `aria-live="polite"` with `aria-atomic="false"` (individual additions are announced, not the whole log). Never set `aria-atomic="true"` on a log — it would announce the entire log history each time a new line is added. [community]

---

### Pattern 142 (Cycle 42) — Guidepup Screen Reader Automation: VoiceOver and NVDA Real AT Testing

Guidepup (`@guidepup/playwright`) provides real screen reader automation for VoiceOver on macOS/iOS and NVDA on Windows, running as Playwright fixtures. Unlike axe-core or Playwright accessibility assertions (which test the accessibility tree), Guidepup drives actual AT software and captures what was *spoken*, enabling tests that verify the full announcement chain. The primary use case is testing complex patterns — comboboxes, live regions, modal dialogs — where the accessibility tree may be correct but the AT announcement order is wrong.

```typescript
// File: e2e/screen-reader/voiceover-modal.spec.ts
// Requires: @guidepup/playwright installed; voiceoverTest fixture available
// Run only on macOS CI runners with VoiceOver enabled
import { voiceoverTest as test, expect } from '@guidepup/playwright';

test.describe('VoiceOver modal dialog announcement (Guidepup)', () => {
  test('modal open announcement includes role and name', async ({ page, voiceOver }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await voiceOver.interact();
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open settings/i }).click();

    // Give VoiceOver time to announce the dialog
    await page.waitForTimeout(300);
    const spokenPhrases = await voiceOver.spokenPhraseLog();

    // VoiceOver should announce "Settings, web dialog"
    const dialogAnnounced = spokenPhrases.some(p =>
      /settings/i.test(p) && /dialog/i.test(p)
    );
    expect(dialogAnnounced, `VoiceOver did not announce dialog — log: ${spokenPhrases.join(' | ')}`).toBe(true);
  });

  test('first focusable element in modal receives focus and is announced', async ({ page, voiceOver }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await voiceOver.interact();
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open settings/i }).click();
    await page.waitForTimeout(200);

    const spokenPhrases = await voiceOver.spokenPhraseLog();
    // First interactive control in the dialog should be announced
    const hasFirstControl = spokenPhrases.some(p => /button|text field|checkbox/i.test(p));
    expect(hasFirstControl).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Guidepup tests are expensive: they require a specific OS (macOS for VoiceOver, Windows for NVDA), real AT installed and enabled, and run significantly slower than headless Playwright tests (5–20 seconds per test vs 0.5–2 seconds). Reserve Guidepup tests for the highest-risk interactive patterns — modal dialogs, complex forms, comboboxes — and run them in a separate CI job gated only on merge to main rather than on every PR. Guidepup VoiceOver tests require `voiceOver.interact()` to start AT interaction mode; forgetting this call means VoiceOver is running but not focused on the browser, and all `spokenPhraseLog()` calls will return an empty array without error. [community]

---

### Pattern 143 (Cycle 42) — Skip Link Existence, Visibility on Focus, and Target Focusability

WCAG 2.4.1 (Level A) requires a mechanism to skip blocks of repeated content. The canonical implementation is a visually-hidden "Skip to main content" link that becomes visible on focus and whose `href="#main"` target is either a `<main>` landmark or an element with `id="main"` that has `tabindex="-1"` (so it is programmatically focusable). Three tests are needed: (1) the link exists in the DOM, (2) it becomes visible when focused, and (3) activating it moves focus to the correct target and the target is reachable.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/skip-link.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Skip link (WCAG 2.4.1)', () => {
  test('skip link is the first focusable element on the page', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Tab once from the top of the page
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focused = page.locator(':focus');
    await expect(focused).toHaveRole('link');
    await expect(focused).toHaveAccessibleName(/skip to main content/i);
  });

  test('skip link becomes visible on focus (not hidden when focused)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const skipLink = page.locator(':focus');
    // Must be visible (not clipped, not zero-size) when focused
    await expect(skipLink).toBeVisible();
    const box = await skipLink.boundingBox();
    expect(box).not.toBeNull();
    expect(box!.width).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(box!.height).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('activating skip link moves focus to main content area', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

    // Focus should now be on the main landmark or its tabindex="-1" container
    const focusedRole = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement;
      return el?.getAttribute('role') ?? el?.tagName?.toLowerCase();
    });
    expect(['main', 'div', 'section']).toContain(focusedRole);

    // Verify the focused element is inside or is the main landmark
    const isInsideMain = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const main = document.querySelector('main, [role="main"]');
      return main ? (main.contains(document.activeElement) || main === document.activeElement) : false;
    });
    expect(isInsideMain).toBe(true);
  });

  test('skip link target has tabindex="-1" if it is not natively focusable', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const skipLink = page.locator('a[href^="#"]').filter({ hasText: /skip/i }).first();
    const href = await skipLink.getAttribute('href');
    expect(href).toBeTruthy();
    const targetId = href!.replace('#', '');
    const target = page.locator(`#${targetId}`);
    const tagName = await target.evaluate(el => el.tagName.toLowerCase());
    if (!['a', 'button', 'input', 'select', 'textarea'].includes(tagName)) {
      await expect(target).toHaveAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** A common implementation error is setting the skip link target to `<main>` without `tabindex="-1"` — `<main>` is not natively focusable, so `focus()` called on it does nothing and the focused element remains on the skip link itself. The page appears to work visually (the viewport scrolls to main) but AT users remain at the link position in reading order. Playwright's `page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement)` check catches this. Another gotcha: skip links hidden via `transform: translateY(-100%)` may not become visible on focus if the `transition` duration is longer than Playwright's default assertion timeout — add `{ timeout: 500 }` to `toBeVisible()` to account for the animation. [official]

---

### Pattern 144 (Cycle 42) — Non-Text Contrast Testing (WCAG 1.4.11) for UI Component Boundaries

WCAG 1.4.11 (Level AA) requires that UI components — buttons, form inputs, focus indicators, custom checkboxes — have at least a 3:1 contrast ratio against adjacent colors for the visual boundary that defines the component. axe-core's `button-name` and `label` rules do not cover non-text contrast; `non-text-contrast` is a separate axe rule. However, axe-core only catches a subset of non-text contrast failures (primarily form inputs without sufficient border contrast). Playwright tests using `evaluate()` to compute contrast from computed styles are needed for icon boundaries, custom checkbox frames, and slider tracks.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/non-text-contrast.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

function luminance(r: number, g: number, b: number): number {
  const f = (c: number) => { const s = c/255; return s <= 0.04045 ? s/12.92 : ((s+0.055)/1.055)**2.4; };
  return 0.2126*f(r) + 0.7152*f(g) + 0.0722*f(b);
}
function contrast(c1: [number,number,number], c2: [number,number,number]): number {
  const [l1, l2] = [luminance(...c1), luminance(...c2)];
  return (Math.max(l1,l2)+0.05) / (Math.min(l1,l2)+0.05);
}

test.describe('Non-text contrast (WCAG 1.4.11)', () => {
  test('axe non-text-contrast rule finds no violations on forms page', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();
    const nonTextViolations = results.violations.filter(v => v.id === 'non-text-contrast');
    expect(nonTextViolations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('text input border has at least 3:1 contrast against white background', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    const input = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /name/i }).first();
    const colors = await input.evaluate((el) => {
      const cs = getComputedStyle(el);
      return { border: cs.borderColor, bg: cs.backgroundColor };
    });
    const parseRgb = (s: string): [number,number,number] => {
      const m = s.match(/\d+/g)!.map(Number);
      return [m[0], m[1], m[2]];
    };
    const ratio = contrast(parseRgb(colors.border), parseRgb(colors.bg));
    expect(ratio, `Input border contrast ${ratio.toFixed(2)} is below 3:1`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);
  });

  test('custom checkbox frame has 3:1 contrast against page background', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    const checkbox = page.getByRole('checkbox').first();
    const colors = await checkbox.evaluate((el) => {
      const cs = getComputedStyle(el);
      const body = getComputedStyle(document.body);
      return { border: cs.borderColor || cs.outlineColor, bg: body.backgroundColor };
    });
    const parseRgb = (s: string): [number,number,number] => {
      const m = s.match(/\d+/g)!.map(Number) as [number,number,number];
      return m;
    };
    const ratio = contrast(parseRgb(colors.border), parseRgb(colors.bg));
    expect(ratio).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** axe-core's `non-text-contrast` rule only evaluates elements it can structurally identify as UI components — it will miss non-text contrast failures on components built with CSS background images, SVG icons, or pseudo-elements (`::before`/`::after`) used as visual boundaries. The computed-style approach in the test above also misses pseudo-element borders because `getComputedStyle(el)` does not return pseudo-element styles. For comprehensive non-text contrast testing of icon-based UI, use a visual regression tool (Percy, Chromatic) configured with a contrast overlay plugin, or conduct manual evaluation with the browser's DevTools color picker. [community]

---

### Pattern 145 (Cycle 42) — `prefers-contrast: more` / `forced-colors` High Contrast Mode Testing

Windows High Contrast Mode (`forced-colors: active`) and the `prefers-contrast: more` media query serve different user populations. `forced-colors` overrides all colors with a small OS-defined palette (ButtonText, Canvas, Highlight, etc.) and makes CSS-injected colors invisible unless the author uses the `forced-color-adjust` property. `prefers-contrast: more` targets users who want higher contrast without a full color override. Playwright supports both via browser context options: `forcedColors: 'active'` and `media: { 'prefers-contrast': 'more' }`.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/high-contrast-forced-colors.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('Forced Colors / High Contrast Mode', () => {
  test('page renders without layout collapse in forced-colors mode', async ({ browser }) => {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ forcedColors: 'active' });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Critical landmark regions must still be present
    await expect(page.getByRole('banner')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toBeVisible();

    // No JavaScript errors due to missing color values
    const errors: string[] = [];
    page.on('pageerror', (e) => errors.push(e.message));
    await page.reload();
    expect(errors).toHaveLength(0);
    await context.close();
  });

  test('focus indicators remain visible in forced-colors mode', async ({ browser }) => {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ forcedColors: 'active' });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focused = page.locator(':focus');
    await expect(focused).toBeVisible();
    const box = await focused.boundingBox();
    expect(box).not.toBeNull();
    expect(box!.width).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    await context.close();
  });

  test('axe scan in prefers-contrast: more finds no contrast violations', async ({ browser }) => {
    const context = await browser.newContext({
      colorScheme: 'light',
    });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.emulateMedia({ media: 'screen', forcedColors: 'none' });
    // emulate prefers-contrast via CSS override
    await page.addStyleTag({ content: '@media (prefers-contrast: more) { :root { --contrast-override: high; } }' });
    await page.goto('/');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();
    const contrastViolations = results.violations.filter(v => v.id === 'color-contrast');
    expect(contrastViolations).toHaveLength(0);
    await context.close();
  });

  test('custom focus outline uses Highlight system color in forced-colors mode', async ({ browser }) => {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ forcedColors: 'active' });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const outlineColor = await page.locator(':focus').evaluate((el) =>
      getComputedStyle(el).outlineColor
    );
    // In forced-colors mode, outline should be a system color keyword or its resolved value
    // Highlight is typically a bright accent color — ensure it's not transparent/none
    expect(outlineColor).not.toBe('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)');
    expect(outlineColor).not.toBe('transparent');
    await context.close();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Playwright's `forcedColors: 'active'` context option uses Chromium's DevTools forced-colors emulation, which approximates Windows High Contrast Mode but does not replicate the exact OS palette — the system color keywords (`ButtonText`, `Highlight`) resolve to Chromium's internal defaults rather than the user's chosen Windows theme colors. This means tests pass even if the application's CSS does not honor `forced-color-adjust: none` correctly, because Chromium's emulated colors may differ from the actual OS values. For genuine Windows High Contrast compliance, supplement Playwright emulation tests with manual verification in Windows 11 High Contrast Black and White themes. [community]

---

### Pattern 146 (Cycle 42) — `aria-roledescription` Misuse Detection

`aria-roledescription` overrides the AT announcement of an element's role with a custom string. It is intended for cases where no existing ARIA role accurately describes a widget (e.g., `role="group" aria-roledescription="slide"` for a carousel slide). Misuse occurs when `aria-roledescription` is placed on elements with interactive roles like `button`, `link`, or `textbox` — this causes AT to announce the custom description *instead of* the native role, removing the semantic meaning the user relies on for interaction. The test must flag any interactive element that carries `aria-roledescription`.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/aria-roledescription-misuse.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const INTERACTIVE_ROLES = ['button', 'link', 'textbox', 'checkbox', 'radio', 'listbox', 'combobox', 'menuitem', 'tab'];

test.describe('aria-roledescription misuse detection', () => {
  const pages = ['/', '/products', '/contact', '/settings'];

  for (const path of pages) {
    test(`no interactive elements carry aria-roledescription on ${path}`, async ({ page }) => {
      await page.goto(path);
      const violations = await page.evaluate((interactiveRoles) => {
        const results: string[] = [];
        const withRoleDesc = document.querySelectorAll('[aria-roledescription]');
        withRoleDesc.forEach((el) => {
          const role = el.getAttribute('role') ?? el.tagName.toLowerCase();
          const isInteractive = interactiveRoles.some(r =>
            role === r ||
            el.tagName.toLowerCase() === 'button' ||
            el.tagName.toLowerCase() === 'a' ||
            (el.tagName.toLowerCase() === 'input' && !['hidden', 'submit', 'reset'].includes((el as HTMLInputElement).type))
          );
          if (isInteractive) {
            results.push(`<${el.tagName.toLowerCase()} role="${role}" aria-roledescription="${el.getAttribute('aria-roledescription')}">`);
          }
        });
        return results;
      }, INTERACTIVE_ROLES);

      expect(violations, `aria-roledescription misuse found: ${violations.join(', ')}`).toHaveLength(0);
    });
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `aria-roledescription` has legitimate uses: carousel slide containers (`role="group" aria-roledescription="slide"`), custom time-picker cells (`role="gridcell" aria-roledescription="hour selector"`). The test above correctly excludes non-interactive roles from the check. The ARIA specification explicitly states that `aria-roledescription` must not be used to override the role announcement of interactive elements that have keyboard semantics — doing so prevents users from understanding how to interact with the element (they no longer hear "button" or "link" and may not know to press Enter or Space). If a design genuinely needs a custom label for an interactive element, use `aria-label` to change the name, not `aria-roledescription` to change the role description. [official]

---

### Pattern 147 (Cycle 42) — Tab Order Snapshot with `tabindex` Positive Value Anti-Pattern Detection

WCAG 2.4.3 (Level A) requires that if a page can be navigated sequentially, the navigation order must be logical and intuitive. Positive `tabindex` values (`tabindex="1"`, `tabindex="2"`, ...) are an anti-pattern because they move those elements to the front of the tab order, ahead of all `tabindex="0"` elements, breaking the expected DOM-order tab sequence. The Playwright test must collect the full tab order by iterating Tab presses and flag any element with a positive `tabindex` value.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/tab-order-positive-tabindex.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Tab order: positive tabindex anti-pattern detection', () => {
  test('no elements use positive tabindex values', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const positiveTabindex = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const all = document.querySelectorAll('[tabindex]');
      const violations: string[] = [];
      all.forEach((el) => {
        const idx = Number(el.getAttribute('tabindex'));
        if (idx > 0) {
          violations.push(`${el.tagName.toLowerCase()}[tabindex="${idx}"] — text: "${el.textContent?.trim().slice(0, 40)}"`);
        }
      });
      return violations;
    });
    expect(
      positiveTabindex,
      `Positive tabindex values found (break tab order): ${positiveTabindex.join('; ')}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('tab order matches DOM source order for main navigation', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const navLinks = page.getByRole('navigation').getByRole('link');
    const count = await navLinks.count();
    const expectedOrder = await Promise.all(
      Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => navLinks.nth(i).textContent())
    );

    // Collect tab order by pressing Tab from start of page
    await page.evaluate(() => { (document.body as HTMLElement).focus(); });
    const tabOrder: string[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < count + 5; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
      const text = await page.evaluate(() =>
        document.activeElement?.closest('nav a')?.textContent?.trim() ?? null
      );
      if (text !== null) tabOrder.push(text);
      if (tabOrder.length === count) break;
    }

    // Navigation links in tab order must match DOM source order
    expect(tabOrder).toEqual(expectedOrder.map(t => t?.trim()).filter(Boolean));
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Positive `tabindex` values are not caught by axe-core's standard `wcag2a` tag — axe has a `tabindex` best-practice rule that flags positive values, but it must be explicitly enabled with `.withTags(['best-practice'])`. The test above provides deterministic DOM-crawl coverage without relying on axe. Note that `tabindex="0"` is correct and necessary for custom interactive widgets (`role="slider"`, `role="switch"`) that need to be in the tab order — only values greater than 0 are problematic. `tabindex="-1"` is also correct for elements that should be programmatically focusable but excluded from the tab sequence (modal close buttons reached by focus trap, skip link targets). [official]

---

### Pattern 148 (Cycle 42) — `aria-required` vs HTML `required` Attribute Interaction Testing

WCAG 3.3.2 (Level A) requires labels that identify required fields. There are two mechanisms: the native HTML `required` attribute (which sets the ARIA `aria-required` property automatically) and the explicit `aria-required="true"` attribute. Both cause AT to announce the field as required, but they behave differently for HTML5 form validation — `required` triggers browser-native validation, while `aria-required` does not. Tests must verify: (1) required fields are announced as required by AT (via `aria-required` or `required`), (2) they are not using `aria-required="false"` when `required` is also present (conflicting signals), and (3) the validation error announcement is accessible.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/aria-required-fields.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('Required field accessibility (WCAG 3.3.2)', () => {
  test('required fields carry required or aria-required="true"', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    const requiredFields = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const inputs = document.querySelectorAll('input, select, textarea');
      const missing: string[] = [];
      inputs.forEach((el) => {
        const label = document.querySelector(`label[for="${el.id}"]`);
        const labelText = label?.textContent ?? '';
        const isVisuallyRequired = labelText.includes('*') || labelText.toLowerCase().includes('required');
        const hasAttr = el.hasAttribute('required') || el.getAttribute('aria-required') === 'true';
        if (isVisuallyRequired && !hasAttr) {
          missing.push(`${el.tagName.toLowerCase()}#${el.id} — label says required but lacks attribute`);
        }
      });
      return missing;
    });
    expect(requiredFields, `Fields marked required visually but missing attribute: ${requiredFields.join('; ')}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('no field has both required and aria-required="false" (conflicting signals)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    const conflicts = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const inputs = document.querySelectorAll('input[required][aria-required="false"], select[required][aria-required="false"], textarea[required][aria-required="false"]');
      return Array.from(inputs).map(el => `${el.tagName.toLowerCase()}#${(el as HTMLElement).id}`);
    });
    expect(conflicts, `Fields with conflicting required + aria-required="false": ${conflicts.join('; ')}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('axe scan flags missing required-field labeling', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();
    const requiredViolations = results.violations.filter(v =>
      ['label', 'label-content-name-mismatch', 'label-title-only'].includes(v.id)
    );
    expect(requiredViolations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `aria-required="true"` is redundant when `required` is already present — the `required` attribute implicitly sets `aria-required` to `true` in the accessibility tree. However, redundancy here is harmless and acceptable for codebases that use `aria-required` for consistency across native and custom form controls. The dangerous conflict is `aria-required="false"` on a native `required` field — this explicitly overrides the implicit `aria-required: true` and causes AT to announce the field as not required, misleading users about mandatory fields. axe-core's `aria-required-attr` and `aria-required-children` rules address structural validity but do not catch the `required + aria-required="false"` conflict; the DOM-crawl check above is the only reliable way to detect it. [official]

---

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 42)

196. **[community] `toHaveAccessibleName()` can pass even when the accessible name source is deprecated — specifically, the `title` attribute is a valid accessible name source for images and form inputs, but AT handling of `title`-derived names is inconsistent: NVDA reads it only on hover, not on keyboard focus, meaning an image or input with only a `title` attribute appears to pass automated tests but is announced incorrectly (or silently) during keyboard navigation**: The accessible name computation algorithm (ACCNAME-1.2) places `title` as the last-resort fallback source for most elements, meaning an `<img title="Company logo">` with no `alt` attribute will have a computed accessible name of "Company logo" — axe and Playwright assertions will pass — but most screen readers present the `title` as a tooltip on hover rather than reading it on element focus or during virtual cursor navigation. WHY: Teams audit images using `toHaveAccessibleName()` and see green, conclude all images are accessible, and ship — but NVDA users hear nothing when navigating images by keyboard because NVDA only reads `title` on pointer hover, not keyboard focus. The fix is to always use `alt` for images and `aria-label` for inputs rather than relying on `title` as the sole name source, and to add a dedicated test that asserts the image has a non-empty `alt` attribute. [community]

197. **[community] Playwright's `getByRole('heading', { level: 2 })` matches elements that have `role="heading" aria-level="2"` as well as `<h2>` elements — but it does NOT match `<div role="heading">` without an `aria-level`, even though the ARIA specification says `role="heading"` without `aria-level` defaults to level 2, because Chromium's accessibility API treats `aria-level` as absent rather than defaulting it**: Developers implement heading hierarchies using `<div role="heading">` (without `aria-level`) expecting it to behave as an `<h2>` at level 2, test with `getByRole('heading', { level: 2 })` in Playwright, see a "not found" failure, and conclude there is a locator bug — but the real issue is the missing `aria-level` attribute. WHY: The ARIA spec states that the default value of `aria-level` on `role="heading"` is 2, but browser implementations are inconsistent about whether to expose this default in the accessibility tree API. Always set `aria-level` explicitly on `role="heading"` elements, and prefer native `<h1>`–`<h6>` elements which never require `aria-level`. [community]

198. **[community] When a Playwright test calls `locator.focus()` on a custom widget that uses `tabindex="-1"` (intended to be programmatically focusable but not tab-reachable), the widget receives focus correctly — but this bypasses the keyboard navigation contract entirely, so tests using `locator.focus()` as a shortcut to simulate user navigation will pass even if the widget is completely unreachable by Tab key for AT users**: `tabindex="-1"` elements are focusable via `focus()` in JavaScript (and therefore in Playwright) but are invisible to the sequential Tab navigation that AT users rely on. A test that calls `await customWidget.focus()` then checks `toHaveAccessibleName()` is testing programmatic focusability, not keyboard reachability. WHY: Teams write accessibility tests that use `locator.focus()` as a convenience and then conclude the widget is keyboard accessible — but Tab-key users (including JAWS, NVDA, and VoiceOver users in forms mode) can never reach those elements. Always test keyboard reachability by using actual `page.keyboard.press('Tab')` sequences rather than `locator.focus()` for elements that should be in the tab sequence. [community]

199. **[community] `AxeBuilder.include()` and `AxeBuilder.exclude()` both accept a single CSS selector string, not an array of selectors, in `@axe-core/playwright` — attempting to pass an array to either method causes the method to silently ignore the additional selectors (not throw), meaning scoped scans that developers believe cover multiple sections are actually only scanning the first selector provided**: The `@axe-core/playwright` TypeScript types accept `string | string[]` for these parameters, which correctly mirrors axe-core's underlying API, but an observed regression in some versions collapses the array to its first element during serialization. Teams write `new AxeBuilder({ page }).include(['.component-a', '.component-b'])` expecting both components to be scanned, but only `.component-a` is analyzed and violations in `.component-b` are missed. WHY: The test passes (no violations found in the scanned scope) and CI gates go green, but the intended coverage was never achieved. The safest mitigation is to run separate `AxeBuilder` instances per selector rather than relying on multi-selector `include()` until the monorepo version behavior is confirmed against your pinned package version. [community]

200. **[community] When testing pages that use CSS Grid or Flexbox with `order` property to visually reorder content, the visual reading order can diverge significantly from the DOM order — Playwright's `getByRole` locators follow DOM order, so tests that navigate by role and collect text content will reflect DOM order, but AT users and keyboard users experience the DOM order while sighted users see the visual order, creating a WCAG 1.3.2 (Meaningful Sequence) violation that tests never flag**: A design pattern common in card layouts uses CSS `order: -1` to promote a CTA card to the visual top, but it remains last in the DOM for source order reasons. Playwright tests navigate to the CTA by `getByRole('button', { name: /get started/i })` successfully (the element is present in the DOM), but a keyboard user Tab-bing through the page reaches the CTA last because Tab follows DOM order, not visual order. WHY: Automated tests do not simulate the experience of sequential keyboard navigation — they find elements by role anywhere in the DOM regardless of sequence. Detect this pattern by comparing visual bounding box Y coordinates against DOM index order: elements whose bounding box Y position is less than a preceding DOM-order element have been visually promoted via CSS, and should be flagged for manual WCAG 1.3.2 review. [community]
