## Cycle 43 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 149 (Cycle 43) — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) Automated Measurement

WCAG 2.5.8 (Level AA, WCAG 2.2) requires that pointer targets measure at least 24×24 CSS pixels, or that any undersized target has at least 24px of spacing clearance around it such that a 24px-diameter circle centered on the target does not intersect any adjacent target's bounding box. The five exception categories are: spacing (clearance rule), equivalent (alternative control exists), inline (links embedded in text), user-agent control (native browser widgets), and essential (information-dense visualizations). Testing must measure each interactive element's bounding box dimensions, identify targets below 24×24px, and then verify whether those targets satisfy the spacing exception by ensuring a centered 24px circle does not overlap any neighbor's bounding box.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/target-size-minimum.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface TargetInfo {
  tag: string;
  text: string;
  x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number;
  ariaRole: string | null;
}

test.describe('WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) — 24×24 CSS px', () => {
  test('all interactive targets meet 24×24 px or satisfy spacing exception', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const targets: TargetInfo[] = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const interactiveTags = ['button', 'a', 'input', 'select', 'textarea', '[role="button"]', '[role="link"]', '[role="checkbox"]', '[role="radio"]'];
      const selector = interactiveTags.join(', ');
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(selector)).map((el) => {
        const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        return {
          tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
          text: (el.textContent ?? '').trim().slice(0, 40),
          x: rect.x, y: rect.y,
          width: rect.width, height: rect.height,
          ariaRole: el.getAttribute('role'),
        };
      });
    });

    const MINIMUM = 24;
    const undersized = targets.filter(t => t.width > 0 && t.height > 0 && (t.width < MINIMUM || t.height < MINIMUM));

    // For each undersized target, check the spacing exception:
    // a 24px-diameter circle (radius 12) centered on the target must not intersect any sibling target
    const violations: string[] = [];
    for (const t of undersized) {
      const cx = t.x + t.width / 2;
      const cy = t.y + t.height / 2;
      const RADIUS = 12;
      const spacingFails = targets.filter((other) => {
        if (other === t) return false;
        const closestX = Math.max(other.x, Math.min(cx, other.x + other.width));
        const closestY = Math.max(other.y, Math.min(cy, other.y + other.height));
        const dist = Math.sqrt((cx - closestX) ** 2 + (cy - closestY) ** 2);
        return dist < RADIUS;
      });
      if (spacingFails.length > 0) {
        violations.push(`<${t.tag}> "${t.text}" ${t.width.toFixed(0)}×${t.height.toFixed(0)}px — spacing exception fails (${spacingFails.length} neighbors within 24px circle)`);
      }
    }
    expect(violations, `WCAG 2.5.8 violations:\n${violations.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** This test only evaluates visible targets with non-zero dimensions at page load in a 1280×720 viewport. Inline links (inside `<p>` text) are explicitly exempt from WCAG 2.5.8, and the test does not filter them out automatically — teams should add a tag or data attribute (`data-inline="true"`) to inline links to suppress false positives, or extend the test to check whether the element's offsetParent is a block-level text container. Additionally, CSS `transform: scale()` and SVG `viewBox` scaling can cause getBoundingClientRect to return a CSS pixel size that does not reflect the actual rendered touch target on high-DPI devices. [official]

---

### Pattern 150 (Cycle 43) — WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured by Sticky Headers

WCAG 2.4.11 (Level AA, WCAG 2.2) requires that when a component receives keyboard focus, it is not entirely hidden behind author-created content such as sticky navigation bars, cookie banners, or fixed sidebars. The criterion allows partial obscuring (a focused element may be partially covered) but not complete hiding. The most reliable CSS fix is `scroll-padding-top` on the `<html>` element set to at least the sticky header height — this causes the browser to reserve scroll space when an element receives focus, bringing it below the fixed overlay. Testing must verify that after each Tab press the focused element's bounding box is visible within the viewport (not fully behind a fixed element).

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/focus-not-obscured.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)', () => {
  test('focused elements are not entirely hidden behind sticky headers', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    // Collect bounding boxes of all position:fixed or position:sticky elements
    const fixedRects = await page.evaluate(() => {
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('*')).flatMap((el) => {
        const style = getComputedStyle(el);
        if (style.position === 'fixed' || style.position === 'sticky') {
          const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
          if (rect.width > 0 && rect.height > 0) {
            return [{ top: rect.top, left: rect.left, bottom: rect.bottom, right: rect.right }];
          }
        }
        return [];
      });
    });

    // Tab through the first 20 focusable elements and check for complete obscuring
    const violations: string[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
      const focusedInfo = await page.evaluate(() => {
        const el = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;
        if (!el || el === document.body) return null;
        const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        return { tag: el.tagName, text: (el.textContent ?? '').trim().slice(0, 40), top: rect.top, left: rect.left, bottom: rect.bottom, right: rect.right };
      });
      if (!focusedInfo) continue;

      // Check if the focused element is completely covered by any fixed element
      for (const fixed of fixedRects) {
        const completelyObscured =
          focusedInfo.top >= fixed.top &&
          focusedInfo.left >= fixed.left &&
          focusedInfo.bottom <= fixed.bottom &&
          focusedInfo.right <= fixed.right;
        if (completelyObscured) {
          violations.push(`<${focusedInfo.tag}> "${focusedInfo.text}" is entirely behind a fixed/sticky element`);
        }
      }
    }
    expect(violations, `WCAG 2.4.11 violations:\n${violations.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** This test only catches complete obscuring. WCAG 2.4.12 (AAA) requires that no part of the focused element is hidden — this test does not assert that. Also, `getBoundingClientRect` in Playwright reflects layout at that instant; if a sticky header uses `position: sticky` with a `top` threshold (visible only when scrolled), it may not be in the fixed region at page load but activates mid-scroll. Supplement this automated check with manual keyboard navigation through long pages to verify focus visibility at various scroll depths. The CSS `scroll-padding-top` fix must match the header height at all responsive breakpoints. [official]

---

### Pattern 151 (Cycle 43) — Accordion Widget Keyboard Contract Verification

The ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG) accordion pattern requires that: each panel's header is a `<button>` (or `role="button"`) within a heading element (`<h2>`–`<h6>` or `role="heading" aria-level`), the button carries `aria-expanded` (true/false), the button carries `aria-controls` pointing to the panel ID, and the panel carries the panel ID. Optional: Down/Up Arrow keys navigate between accordion headers; Home/End jump to first/last. The Playwright test must verify the full keyboard contract: Tab focuses the first header button, Enter/Space toggles expansion, `aria-expanded` reflects state, and panel content becomes visible.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/accordion-keyboard-contract.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Accordion ARIA keyboard contract (ARIA APG)', () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
  });

  test('accordion header buttons carry aria-expanded and aria-controls', async ({ page }) => {
    const buttons = page.locator('[aria-expanded]').filter({ has: page.locator(':scope') });
    const count = await buttons.count();
    expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const btn = buttons.nth(i);
      await expect(btn).toHaveAttribute('aria-controls');
      const expanded = await btn.getAttribute('aria-expanded');
      expect(['true', 'false']).toContain(expanded);
    }
  });

  test('Enter key on collapsed accordion header expands the panel', async ({ page }) => {
    const firstCollapsed = page.locator('[aria-expanded="false"]').first();
    const panelId = await firstCollapsed.getAttribute('aria-controls');
    expect(panelId).toBeTruthy();
    await firstCollapsed.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
    await expect(firstCollapsed).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    await expect(page.locator(`#${panelId}`)).toBeVisible();
  });

  test('Space key on expanded accordion header collapses the panel', async ({ page }) => {
    // First expand a panel
    const firstBtn = page.locator('[aria-expanded]').first();
    await firstBtn.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
    await expect(firstBtn).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    // Now collapse with Space
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
    await expect(firstBtn).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  });

  test('accordion header buttons are contained within heading elements', async ({ page }) => {
    const violations = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const buttons = document.querySelectorAll('[aria-expanded]');
      const results: string[] = [];
      buttons.forEach((btn) => {
        const heading = btn.closest('h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6,[role="heading"]');
        if (!heading) {
          results.push(`Button "${btn.textContent?.trim().slice(0, 40)}" is not inside a heading element`);
        }
      });
      return results;
    });
    expect(violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** The APG marks Down/Up Arrow key navigation between accordion headers as "optional recommended" — not all implementations include it, and axe-core does not flag its absence. If your design system requires Arrow key navigation (common in enterprise component libraries), add a dedicated test for it. The test above uses `[aria-expanded]` as the accordion button selector — if your implementation uses a different attribute pattern (some use `data-state="open"`), update the selector. Always check that `aria-controls` resolves to an actual DOM ID; a broken reference causes AT to not announce the panel relationship. [official]

---

### Pattern 152 (Cycle 43) — Modal Dialog Focus Trap and `aria-modal` Verification

The ARIA APG dialog pattern requires: `role="dialog"` on the container, `aria-modal="true"` on the container, `aria-labelledby` referencing a visible heading or `aria-label`, focus moved to the first focusable element (or least-destructive button) on open, Tab/Shift+Tab cycling within the dialog without escaping, Escape closing the dialog, and focus returning to the trigger element on close. Additionally, background content must be made inert (via the `inert` attribute or `aria-hidden="true"`) because `aria-modal` alone is not honored by all AT (notably VoiceOver on Safari ignores `aria-modal` and requires `inert` on background content).

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/modal-dialog-focus-trap.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Modal dialog focus trap and ARIA contract', () => {
  test('dialog has role=dialog, aria-modal=true, and accessible name', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open|show|details/i }).first().click();
    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();
    await expect(dialog).toHaveAttribute('aria-modal', 'true');
    const labelledBy = await dialog.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    const label = await dialog.getAttribute('aria-label');
    expect(labelledBy || label).toBeTruthy();
  });

  test('Tab key cycles within the dialog and does not escape', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open|show|details/i }).first().click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();

    // Collect tabbable elements inside the dialog
    const tabbableCount = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const dialog = document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]');
      if (!dialog) return 0;
      const sel = 'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), [tabindex="0"]';
      return dialog.querySelectorAll(sel).length;
    });
    expect(tabbableCount).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    // Tab through all elements + 2 more to verify wrap
    for (let i = 0; i < tabbableCount + 2; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
      const focusInDialog = await page.evaluate(() => {
        const dialog = document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]');
        return dialog ? dialog.contains(document.activeElement) : false;
      });
      expect(focusInDialog).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test('Escape key closes the dialog and returns focus to trigger', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const trigger = page.getByRole('button', { name: /open|show|details/i }).first();
    await trigger.focus();
    await trigger.click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).not.toBeVisible();
    // Focus should return to the trigger
    await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `aria-modal="true"` tells AT to treat the dialog as a modal and restrict virtual cursor browsing to the dialog contents — but VoiceOver on macOS/iOS does not honor `aria-modal`. The only cross-AT solution for preventing VoiceOver's swipe navigation from reaching background content is to apply the `inert` attribute to all background content siblings of the dialog. Test with both `aria-modal` assertion and a runtime check for `inert` on background elements. The `inert` attribute is fully supported in all modern browsers as of 2023, making it the preferred implementation going forward. [official]

---

### Pattern 153 (Cycle 43) — Combobox `aria-activedescendant` vs Roving Tabindex Correctness

The ARIA APG combobox pattern specifies that when a combobox has a listbox popup, DOM focus stays on the `<input>` element and AT focus is moved through the options using `aria-activedescendant` on the input, pointing to the currently "active" option's ID. Using roving tabindex (moving actual DOM focus into the listbox options) is incorrect for combobox — it causes AT to exit the input context and lose the typed text announcement. The test must verify that while a listbox popup is open and Arrow keys are pressed, DOM focus remains on the input element, and `aria-activedescendant` on the input updates to point to the highlighted option's ID.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/combobox-activedescendant.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Combobox aria-activedescendant contract (ARIA APG)', () => {
  test('DOM focus stays on input while navigating listbox with arrow keys', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    const input = page.getByRole('combobox');
    await input.fill('a');
    await expect(page.getByRole('listbox')).toBeVisible();

    // Press Down Arrow — focus must remain on input
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    const focusedTag = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.tagName.toLowerCase());
    expect(focusedTag).toBe('input');
  });

  test('aria-activedescendant on input points to the highlighted option ID', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    const input = page.getByRole('combobox');
    await input.fill('a');
    await expect(page.getByRole('listbox')).toBeVisible();

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    const activeDescId = await input.getAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
    expect(activeDescId).toBeTruthy();

    // The element pointed to must exist in the DOM and be inside the listbox
    const targetEl = page.locator(`#${activeDescId}`);
    await expect(targetEl).toBeVisible();
    const isInListbox = await page.evaluate((id) => {
      const el = document.getElementById(id ?? '');
      const listbox = document.querySelector('[role="listbox"]');
      return listbox?.contains(el) ?? false;
    }, activeDescId);
    expect(isInListbox).toBe(true);
  });

  test('pressing ArrowDown advances aria-activedescendant to the next option', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/search');
    const input = page.getByRole('combobox');
    await input.fill('a');
    await expect(page.getByRole('listbox')).toBeVisible();

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    const firstId = await input.getAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    const secondId = await input.getAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
    expect(firstId).not.toBe(secondId);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Some combobox implementations set `aria-activedescendant` only when the listbox is open, and clear it when the input is typed into again — this is correct behavior. A common bug is implementations that set `aria-activedescendant` to a non-existent or empty string ID, which causes AT to announce nothing. Always verify that the ID referenced by `aria-activedescendant` resolves to a DOM element that has `role="option"` and is currently visible. Some AT (older NVDA versions) require `aria-selected="true"` on the active option in addition to `aria-activedescendant` to announce it — the APG pattern notes this as a compatibility measure. [official]

---

### Pattern 154 (Cycle 43) — `aria-live` Region Population Timing Test

ARIA live regions only announce mutations that happen after the region is registered with AT. A common bug is creating the live region element dynamically (via JavaScript) and immediately populating it — AT may not have registered the new element as a live region before the text is set, causing the announcement to be silently dropped. The live region element must exist in the DOM (even if empty) before any content is injected into it. The Playwright test verifies that live regions are present in the initial HTML (not injected after user action) and that announcements are fired after dynamic interactions.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/live-region-timing.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('aria-live region population timing', () => {
  test('live regions exist in the initial DOM before dynamic content loads', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const liveRegions = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const nodes = document.querySelectorAll('[aria-live], [role="status"], [role="alert"], [role="log"]');
      return Array.from(nodes).map((el) => ({
        tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
        ariaLive: el.getAttribute('aria-live'),
        role: el.getAttribute('role'),
        id: el.id,
        isEmpty: el.textContent?.trim() === '',
      }));
    });
    // At minimum, a status region for form feedback should be present
    expect(liveRegions.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    // All live regions should be empty initially (content injected later triggers announcement)
    const prePopulated = liveRegions.filter(r => !r.isEmpty);
    expect(prePopulated, `Live regions pre-populated with content on load (announce on load is an anti-pattern): ${JSON.stringify(prePopulated)}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('form submission error appears in a live region and is not just visually shown', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();

    // The error must appear inside a live region, not just a static div
    const errorInLiveRegion = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const liveRegions = document.querySelectorAll('[aria-live], [role="alert"], [role="status"]');
      return Array.from(liveRegions).some(r => (r.textContent?.trim().length ?? 0) > 0);
    });
    expect(errorInLiveRegion, 'Form errors must be announced via a live region for AT users').toBe(true);
  });

  test('aria-atomic="true" is set on status regions that give context-dependent messages', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const atomicViolations = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const statusRegions = document.querySelectorAll('[role="status"], [role="timer"]');
      const results: string[] = [];
      statusRegions.forEach((el) => {
        if (el.getAttribute('aria-atomic') !== 'true') {
          results.push(`<${el.tagName.toLowerCase()} role="${el.getAttribute('role')}"> missing aria-atomic="true"`);
        }
      });
      return results;
    });
    expect(atomicViolations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `role="alert"` implicitly sets `aria-live="assertive"` and `aria-atomic="true"` — adding `aria-live="assertive"` redundantly on a `role="alert"` element is harmless in modern browsers but causes double announcements in older VoiceOver versions on iOS. Prefer `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"` for non-urgent messages. Also, populating a live region by clearing it first (setting `textContent = ''`) and then setting new text is a reliable cross-AT technique to guarantee re-announcement of the same message — some AT ignore identical string mutations but announce after a clear-then-set cycle. [official]

---

### Pattern 155 (Cycle 43) — SVG Accessible Name Verification (`role="img"` + `<title>` + `aria-labelledby`)

Inline SVGs used as meaningful images require `role="img"` on the `<svg>` element and an accessible name provided via either: a `<title>` element as the first child of `<svg>` with `aria-labelledby` on `<svg>` pointing to the `<title>`'s ID (most reliable across AT), or `aria-label` directly on `<svg>`. Decorative SVGs must have `aria-hidden="true"` to be excluded from the accessibility tree. The `<title>` element alone without `aria-labelledby` is insufficient — NVDA and JAWS do not expose it consistently. The test must identify inline SVGs, classify them as meaningful or decorative, and assert the correct accessible name mechanism.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/svg-accessible-names.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('SVG accessible name patterns', () => {
  test('meaningful inline SVGs have role=img and aria-labelledby or aria-label', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const violations = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const results: string[] = [];
      document.querySelectorAll('svg').forEach((svg) => {
        const isDecorative = svg.getAttribute('aria-hidden') === 'true' || svg.getAttribute('role') === 'presentation' || svg.getAttribute('role') === 'none';
        if (isDecorative) return;
        const role = svg.getAttribute('role');
        const ariaLabel = svg.getAttribute('aria-label');
        const ariaLabelledBy = svg.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
        const hasTitle = svg.querySelector('title') !== null;
        if (role !== 'img') {
          results.push(`SVG missing role="img": "${svg.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? svg.querySelector('title')?.textContent ?? '[unnamed]'}"`);
        }
        if (!ariaLabel && !ariaLabelledBy) {
          results.push(`SVG role="img" missing aria-label or aria-labelledby`);
        }
        if (ariaLabelledBy && !hasTitle) {
          results.push(`SVG uses aria-labelledby but has no <title> child element`);
        }
      });
      return results;
    });
    expect(violations, `SVG accessible name violations:\n${violations.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('decorative SVGs carry aria-hidden="true"', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const decorativeWithoutHidden = await page.evaluate(() => {
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('svg[role="presentation"], svg[role="none"]'))
        .filter(svg => svg.getAttribute('aria-hidden') !== 'true')
        .map(svg => svg.outerHTML.slice(0, 80));
    });
    // role="presentation" or role="none" without aria-hidden is unreliable in older AT
    expect(decorativeWithoutHidden, `Decorative SVGs should use aria-hidden="true" for broad AT compatibility: ${decorativeWithoutHidden.join('; ')}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('axe scan catches missing SVG names', async ({ page }) => {
    const AxeBuilder = (await import('@axe-core/playwright')).default;
    await page.goto('/');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();
    const svgViolations = results.violations.filter(v => v.id === 'image-alt' || v.id === 'role-img-alt');
    expect(svgViolations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** The `<title>` element alone (without `aria-labelledby`) works in VoiceOver on Safari but is unreliable in NVDA+Firefox and JAWS+Chrome. The most robust pattern is `<svg role="img" aria-labelledby="svgTitle"><title id="svgTitle">Description</title></svg>`. For icon buttons that contain an SVG (e.g., a trash icon button), the accessible name should come from the button's `aria-label`, not from the SVG's `<title>` — the SVG should be `aria-hidden="true"` in this case. Never use `title` attribute on `<svg>` (distinct from the `<title>` child element) — it shows a browser tooltip but is not exposed in the accessibility tree. [community]

---

### Pattern 156 (Cycle 43) — Sortable Table Column `aria-sort` Correctness

WCAG 1.3.1 (Level A) requires that information, structure, and relationships conveyed visually are also programmatically determinable. For sortable data tables, the column that is currently sorted must carry `aria-sort` on the `<th>` element: `ascending`, `descending`, or `none`. After a user clicks a column header to sort, the `aria-sort` value must update to reflect the new sort state, and previous column headers must be set back to `none` (not omitted — omitting `aria-sort` is valid for columns that are not sortable, but a previously-sorted column returning to unsorted should use `none`). Playwright must verify the full sort cycle: initial state, first sort, second sort (toggle), and state on a different column.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/table-aria-sort.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Sortable table aria-sort contract (WCAG 1.3.1)', () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/data-table');
  });

  test('sortable column headers carry aria-sort attribute', async ({ page }) => {
    const sortableHeaders = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const ths = document.querySelectorAll('th[aria-sort]');
      return Array.from(ths).map(th => ({ text: th.textContent?.trim(), sort: th.getAttribute('aria-sort') }));
    });
    expect(sortableHeaders.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('clicking a column header sets aria-sort to ascending or descending on first click', async ({ page }) => {
    const firstSortableHeader = page.locator('th[aria-sort]').first();
    await firstSortableHeader.click();
    const sortValue = await firstSortableHeader.getAttribute('aria-sort');
    expect(['ascending', 'descending']).toContain(sortValue);
  });

  test('second click on same header toggles aria-sort between ascending and descending', async ({ page }) => {
    const header = page.locator('th[aria-sort]').first();
    await header.click();
    const firstSort = await header.getAttribute('aria-sort');
    await header.click();
    const secondSort = await header.getAttribute('aria-sort');
    const expected = firstSort === 'ascending' ? 'descending' : 'ascending';
    expect(secondSort).toBe(expected);
  });

  test('sorting one column sets other previously-sorted columns to aria-sort="none"', async ({ page }) => {
    const headers = page.locator('th[aria-sort]');
    const count = await headers.count();
    if (count < 2) test.skip();
    await headers.first().click();
    await headers.nth(1).click();
    // First header should now be none (no longer the sort column)
    const firstSort = await headers.first().getAttribute('aria-sort');
    expect(firstSort).toBe('none');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** Omitting `aria-sort` entirely on unsortable columns is correct — `aria-sort` should only be present on columns that participate in the sort feature. However, an `aria-sort` value of `none` is required (not just omission) on sortable columns that are not currently sorted, to signal to AT users that the column is sortable but not active. Some AT (NVDA) only announce sortability when `aria-sort` is explicitly present; they do not infer sortability from visual indicators alone. axe-core's `aria-allowed-attr` rule will flag invalid `aria-sort` values but does not check that the sort cycle is implemented correctly. [official]

---

### Pattern 157 (Cycle 43) — `prefers-reduced-motion` Animation Suppression Testing

WCAG 2.3.3 (Level AAA) and the broadly applicable best practice require that animations and transitions are suppressed or significantly reduced when the user has enabled "reduce motion" in their OS accessibility settings. The CSS media query `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` should disable or replace decorative animations. Playwright can emulate this preference and then verify that computed animation and transition durations are zero (or near-zero) for animated elements. This pattern also covers testing that auto-playing videos and animated GIFs have accessible pause controls.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/prefers-reduced-motion.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('prefers-reduced-motion animation suppression', () => {
  test('CSS animations and transitions are disabled under reduced-motion preference', async ({ browser }) => {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.goto('/');

    const animatedElements = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const results: { tag: string; className: string; animDuration: string; transDuration: string }[] = [];
      const all = document.querySelectorAll('*');
      all.forEach((el) => {
        const style = getComputedStyle(el);
        const animDuration = style.animationDuration;
        const transDuration = style.transitionDuration;
        const animMs = parseFloat(animDuration) * (animDuration.includes('ms') ? 1 : 1000);
        const transMs = parseFloat(transDuration) * (transDuration.includes('ms') ? 1 : 1000);
        if (animMs > 100 || transMs > 100) {
          results.push({ tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(), className: (el as HTMLElement).className.slice(0, 40), animDuration, transDuration });
        }
      });
      return results;
    });

    expect(
      animatedElements,
      `Elements with >100ms animation/transition in reduced-motion mode:\n${animatedElements.map(e => `${e.tag}.${e.className}: anim=${e.animDuration} trans=${e.transDuration}`).join('\n')}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
    await context.close();
  });

  test('auto-playing video has accessible pause control', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const autoPlayVideos = page.locator('video[autoplay]');
    const count = await autoPlayVideos.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      // Each auto-playing video must have a pause button reachable by keyboard
      const videoContainer = autoPlayVideos.nth(i).locator('..');
      const pauseBtn = videoContainer.getByRole('button', { name: /pause|stop/i });
      await expect(pauseBtn, `Auto-playing video ${i} missing accessible pause control`).toBeAttached();
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` in Playwright sets `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` in the browser context. The 100ms threshold in the test above is a pragmatic choice: very short transitions (< 100ms) for hover state changes are generally acceptable even in reduced-motion mode. The WCAG 2.3.3 criterion is Level AAA, meaning it is aspirational rather than required for conformance — however, the WCAG 2.2 Level AA baseline still requires that users can pause, stop, or hide any moving content that lasts more than 3 seconds (WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide). The `prefers-reduced-motion` test verifies the developer-controlled CSS path; supplement with manual verification for third-party embeds (maps, marketing widgets) that do not respect the media query. [official]

---

### Pattern 158 (Cycle 43) — `axe-core` `resultTypes` Performance Optimization for Large Pages

On pages with more than 50,000 DOM nodes, running `axe.run()` or `AxeBuilder.analyze()` without constraints can take 30+ seconds and time out CI jobs. axe-core provides the `resultTypes` option, which limits the selectors computed for non-violation results — setting `resultTypes: ['violations']` tells axe to only compute full CSS selector paths for rules that fire violations, while passes, incomplete, and inapplicable results return empty selector arrays. This dramatically reduces the serialization payload sent from the browser context back to Node, and halves analysis time on large pages. The test must still report all violations but is dramatically faster to execute.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/axe-large-page-optimized.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

const PAGES_TO_SCAN = ['/', '/dashboard', '/reports', '/admin'];

test.describe('Optimized axe scan for large/complex pages', () => {
  for (const path of PAGES_TO_SCAN) {
    test(`WCAG 2.1 AA — ${path}`, async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
      await page.goto(path);
      await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

      // Performance optimization: only compute full selectors for violations
      const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa'])
        .options({
          resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'],
          frameWaitTime: 2000,
        } as Parameters<AxeBuilder['options']>[0])
        .analyze();

      // Attach full results for debugging
      await testInfo.attach('axe-results.json', {
        body: JSON.stringify(results, null, 2),
        contentType: 'application/json',
      });

      expect(
        results.violations,
        `Violations on ${path}:\n${results.violations.map(v => `${v.id}: ${v.description} (${v.nodes.length} nodes)`).join('\n')}`
      ).toHaveLength(0);

      if (results.incomplete.length > 0) {
        console.warn(`[axe incomplete — manual review needed on ${path}]:`, results.incomplete.map(r => r.id).join(', '));
      }
    });
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `resultTypes: ['violations']` causes axe to return empty `nodes` arrays for `passes`, `incomplete`, and `inapplicable` — this means you cannot use the results to report "which rules passed" in your test report. If your pipeline uses the `passes` array to generate a compliance report, remove `resultTypes` from those runs and accept the performance cost. The `frameWaitTime` option is relevant for pages with `<iframe>` content — axe-core tries to inject into child frames and a short `frameWaitTime` on slow frames causes the frame scan to be skipped silently. Set it to at least 2000ms in CI environments where frame load times are variable. [official]

### Pattern 159 (Cycle 43) — Color Contrast for Non-Text UI Components (WCAG 1.4.11)

WCAG 1.4.11 (Level AA) requires a minimum 3:1 contrast ratio between the visual presentation of UI components (buttons, input borders, focus indicators, progress bars, sliders) and their adjacent color. Unlike WCAG 1.4.3 (text contrast, 4.5:1 for normal text), 1.4.11 covers the boundary or visual affordance that identifies the component — not the component's text label (which is covered by 1.4.3). axe-core's `non-text-contrast` rule checks this. The test must verify that common UI components in both enabled and disabled states have sufficient boundary contrast, noting that disabled components are exempt from 1.4.11.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/non-text-contrast.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('Non-text contrast — WCAG 1.4.11', () => {
  const routes = ['/', '/contact', '/settings'];

  for (const route of routes) {
    test(`non-text-contrast violations on ${route}`, async ({ page }) => {
      await page.goto(route);
      const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .withRules(['non-text-contrast'])
        .analyze();
      expect(
        results.violations,
        `WCAG 1.4.11 violations on ${route}:\n${results.violations.flatMap(v => v.nodes.map(n => n.html)).join('\n')}`
      ).toHaveLength(0);
    });
  }

  test('focus indicator has 3:1 contrast against adjacent background', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focusedEl = page.locator(':focus');
    await expect(focusedEl).toBeVisible();

    const contrastData = await focusedEl.evaluate((el) => {
      const style = getComputedStyle(el);
      return {
        outlineColor: style.outlineColor,
        outlineWidth: style.outlineWidth,
        backgroundColor: style.backgroundColor,
      };
    });
    // Outline must have a non-transparent, non-zero width
    expect(contrastData.outlineWidth).not.toBe('0px');
    expect(contrastData.outlineColor).not.toBe('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)');
    expect(contrastData.outlineColor).not.toBe('transparent');
  });

  test('input borders have sufficient contrast (manual axe incomplete review)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['non-text-contrast'])
      .analyze();
    const incompleteForInputs = results.incomplete.filter(r => r.id === 'non-text-contrast');
    if (incompleteForInputs.length > 0) {
      console.warn('non-text-contrast incomplete for manual review:', incompleteForInputs.flatMap(r => r.nodes.map(n => n.html)).join('; '));
    }
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** axe-core's `non-text-contrast` rule returns `incomplete` for many cases where the visual boundary color cannot be computed from CSS alone — specifically, when border colors are defined via CSS custom properties whose values are not resolvable in the static DOM (e.g., `border-color: var(--color-input-border)`), axe cannot determine the resolved color and marks the check as incomplete instead of a violation. This means `non-text-contrast` passing in automated tests does not guarantee compliance; always manually verify input borders, focus rings, toggle switch tracks, checkbox borders, and radio button outlines in the browser with the DevTools color picker or the Colour Contrast Analyser tool. [official]

---

### Pattern 160 (Cycle 43) — `lang` Attribute Completeness for Multi-Language Pages

WCAG 3.1.1 (Level A) requires that the default human language of each web page is programmatically determinable via the `lang` attribute on the `<html>` element. WCAG 3.1.2 (Level AA) further requires that each passage of text in a different language is identified with a `lang` attribute on the containing element. Common failures: missing `lang` on `<html>`, using wrong BCP 47 language tag (e.g., `lang="en_US"` uses underscore rather than hyphen, which is invalid), having inline content in a foreign language without a `lang` attribute on its container, and using `lang` on an element that is fully in the page's primary language (redundant but harmless). Testing must verify the `<html lang>` attribute syntax and flag inline content that appears to be in a different language.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/lang-attributes.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

// BCP 47 basic validation: language[-region] e.g. en, en-US, fr-CA, zh-Hans
const BCP47_PATTERN = /^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z]{2,4}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8})*)?$/;

test.describe('Language attribute completeness (WCAG 3.1.1 / 3.1.2)', () => {
  test('<html> element has a valid BCP 47 lang attribute', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const lang = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.lang);
    expect(lang, '<html> element is missing lang attribute').toBeTruthy();
    expect(BCP47_PATTERN.test(lang), `lang="${lang}" is not a valid BCP 47 language tag (use hyphens, not underscores; e.g. en-US not en_US)`).toBe(true);
  });

  test('all pages in the sitemap carry a matching <html lang>', async ({ page }) => {
    const routes = ['/', '/about', '/contact', '/products'];
    for (const route of routes) {
      await page.goto(route);
      const lang = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.lang);
      expect(lang, `Page ${route} has no lang attribute on <html>`).toBeTruthy();
      expect(BCP47_PATTERN.test(lang), `Page ${route}: lang="${lang}" is invalid BCP 47`).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test('axe html-has-lang and html-lang-valid rules pass', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['html-has-lang', 'html-lang-valid', 'valid-lang'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('inline elements with explicit lang attributes use valid BCP 47 tags', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const invalidLangs = await page.evaluate((pattern) => {
      const withLang = document.querySelectorAll('[lang]:not(html)');
      const regex = new RegExp(pattern);
      return Array.from(withLang)
        .filter(el => !regex.test(el.getAttribute('lang') ?? ''))
        .map(el => `${el.tagName.toLowerCase()}[lang="${el.getAttribute('lang')}"]`);
    }, BCP47_PATTERN.source);
    expect(invalidLangs, `Invalid BCP 47 lang tags on inline elements: ${invalidLangs.join(', ')}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** axe-core's `html-lang-valid` rule checks that the `lang` value is a valid IETF language tag, but it does not verify that the stated language matches the actual page content — a page written entirely in French with `lang="en"` will pass axe validation. WCAG 3.1.1 conformance requires the tag to be accurate, not just syntactically valid. Also, Chinese requires explicit script subtags for correct AT behavior: `zh-Hans` (Simplified Chinese) and `zh-Hant` (Traditional Chinese) — `lang="zh"` alone causes some AT to default to Mandarin with incorrect character pronunciation rules for Traditional Chinese content. [official]

---

### Pattern 161 (Cycle 43) — `inert` Attribute as Focus Trap Mechanism Verification

The HTML `inert` attribute (now supported in all modern browsers) makes an element and all its descendants non-interactive: they cannot receive focus, pointer events, or be found by AT virtual cursor navigation. It is the correct modern replacement for `aria-hidden="true"` + `tabindex="-1"` on all children for the background content behind a modal. Unlike `aria-hidden="true"` (which hides from the accessibility tree but still allows keyboard focus), `inert` removes both keyboard focus and AT discoverability. Testing must verify that modal dialogs apply `inert` to background content and that `inert` is removed when the modal closes.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/inert-attribute-modal.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('inert attribute for modal background content', () => {
  test('opening a modal applies inert to background content', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const trigger = page.getByRole('button', { name: /open|show|modal/i }).first();
    await trigger.click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();

    // Background content siblings of the dialog should carry inert
    const inertApplied = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const dialog = document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]');
      if (!dialog) return false;
      const parent = dialog.parentElement;
      if (!parent) return false;
      const siblings = Array.from(parent.children).filter(el => el !== dialog);
      return siblings.some(sibling => sibling.hasAttribute('inert') || sibling.getAttribute('aria-hidden') === 'true');
    });
    expect(inertApplied, 'Background content is not made inert or aria-hidden when modal is open').toBe(true);
  });

  test('Tab key cannot reach background content while modal is open', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open|show|modal/i }).first().click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();

    // Press Tab 30 times — focus must never leave the dialog
    for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
      const inDialog = await page.evaluate(() => {
        const dialog = document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]');
        return dialog ? dialog.contains(document.activeElement) : false;
      });
      expect(inDialog).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test('inert is removed from background content after modal closes', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open|show|modal/i }).first().click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).not.toBeVisible();

    // Background content should be interactive again
    const inertRemaining = await page.evaluate(() => {
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[inert]')).length;
    });
    expect(inertRemaining).toBe(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** `inert` is fully supported in Chrome 102+, Firefox 112+, Safari 15.5+ — applications targeting older browsers require a polyfill (`wicg-inert`). Some React modal libraries (Headless UI, Radix UI) use `aria-hidden="true"` instead of `inert` — this correctly hides the accessibility tree but does NOT prevent keyboard focus from reaching background elements on all browsers. A user pressing Tab while a modal with only `aria-hidden` on the background can focus a hidden background button in some configurations. Always prefer `inert` for new implementations; it is the only attribute that covers all three dimensions: AT discoverability, keyboard focus, and pointer events. [community]

---

### Pattern 162 (Cycle 43) — Scoped `AxeBuilder` Fixture Pattern for Reusable Configuration

When a test suite has multiple spec files all running axe scans, repeating the `AxeBuilder` configuration (tags, disabled rules, custom rules) in every test leads to divergence — one file disables a rule that all others enforce, or different files use different tag sets. The Playwright fixture pattern allows a single shared `axeBuilder` fixture that pre-configures all `AxeBuilder` instances consistently. The fixture can also automatically attach results as test artifacts, enabling the Playwright HTML report to include accessibility scan details for every failing test without boilerplate.

```typescript
// File: e2e/fixtures/axe-fixture.ts
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

type AxeFixtures = {
  makeAxeBuilder: () => AxeBuilder;
};

export const test = base.extend<AxeFixtures>({
  makeAxeBuilder: async ({ page }, use) => {
    const makeAxeBuilder = () =>
      new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa'])
        .disableRules([
          // Document why each rule is disabled here, e.g.:
          // 'color-contrast' -- CSS custom properties unresolvable by axe; manually verified
        ]);
    await use(makeAxeBuilder);
  },
});

export { expect };

// File: e2e/accessibility/home-page.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/axe-fixture';

test('home page passes WCAG 2.1 AA', async ({ page, makeAxeBuilder }, testInfo) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  const results = await makeAxeBuilder().analyze();

  await testInfo.attach('axe-results', {
    body: JSON.stringify(results, null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  expect(
    results.violations,
    results.violations.map(v =>
      `[${v.impact}] ${v.id}: ${v.description}\n  Nodes: ${v.nodes.map(n => n.html).join('\n  ')}`
    ).join('\n\n')
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** The fixture pattern forces all axe scans through a single configuration, which makes global rule changes easy but can hide legitimate per-test configuration needs (e.g., a specific test page that intentionally tests accessible error states needs different rules). Use `makeAxeBuilder().disableRules(['specific-rule'])` in individual tests to override while still inheriting the base configuration. Storing disabled rules in the fixture with comments explaining WHY they are disabled (e.g., `// CSS custom properties make color-contrast unresolvable by axe; manual verified`) creates a maintainable exclusion audit trail. Never disable rules without a comment — undocumented suppressions accumulate into a false-confidence situation. [community]

---

### Pattern 163 (Cycle 43) — WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry — Prefill Verification for Multi-Step Forms

WCAG 3.3.7 (Level A, WCAG 2.2) requires that information previously entered by the user is either auto-populated in subsequent steps of the same process, or made available for the user to select (e.g., "same as above" checkbox). This prevents users with motor or cognitive disabilities from having to re-type the same information multiple times in a checkout flow, registration wizard, or multi-step form. The test must navigate a multi-step form, enter data in step 1, advance to step 2, and verify that the same fields in step 2 are either pre-populated or have a mechanism to carry over the step-1 data.

```typescript
// File: e2e/accessibility/redundant-entry.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry — multi-step form prefill', () => {
  test('billing address prefills from shipping address on checkout step 2', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout');

    // Step 1: Enter shipping address
    await page.getByLabel(/first name/i).fill('Jane');
    await page.getByLabel(/last name/i).fill('Smith');
    await page.getByLabel(/address/i).first().fill('123 Main St');
    await page.getByLabel(/city/i).fill('Springfield');
    await page.getByLabel(/zip|postal/i).fill('12345');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next|continue/i }).click();

    // Step 2: billing address — check for prefill or "same as shipping" option
    const sameAsShipping = page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: /same as shipping/i });
    const billingFirstName = page.getByLabel(/billing.*first name|first name.*billing/i);

    const hasSameAsOption = await sameAsShipping.isVisible().catch(() => false);
    const hasPrefill = await billingFirstName.inputValue().catch(() => '');

    expect(
      hasSameAsOption || hasPrefill === 'Jane',
      'WCAG 3.3.7: Billing step should either prefill from shipping or provide "same as shipping" option'
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  test('"same as shipping" checkbox populates billing fields when checked', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout');
    await page.getByLabel(/first name/i).fill('Jane');
    await page.getByLabel(/address/i).first().fill('123 Main St');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next|continue/i }).click();

    const sameAsShipping = page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: /same as shipping/i });
    if (!(await sameAsShipping.isVisible().catch(() => false))) {
      test.skip();
      return;
    }
    await sameAsShipping.check();
    // After checking, billing address fields should be populated
    const billingAddress = await page.getByLabel(/billing.*address|address.*billing/i).inputValue();
    expect(billingAddress).toBe('123 Main St');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff note:** WCAG 3.3.7 is Level A in WCAG 2.2 — it is not aspirational; non-conformance is a real accessibility barrier. Three exceptions exist: (1) re-entry for security reasons (password confirmation fields), (2) the previously entered information is no longer valid (session-expired data), and (3) re-entering is essential to the purpose (a quiz where retaining prior answers would compromise integrity). The test above is application-specific — the selectors must match your actual checkout flow labels. In teams using design systems, add this test to the design system's multi-step form component story so it is verified at the component level before integration. [official]

---

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 43)

201. **[community] `AxeBuilder.withTags(['wcag22aa'])` requires axe-core 4.7+ — using it with an older pinned axe-core version causes the tag to be silently ignored and the WCAG 2.2 rules (2.5.8, 2.4.11, 3.3.7, 3.3.8) are never evaluated, while the scan still returns zero violations and CI passes**: The `wcag22a` and `wcag22aa` tag strings were added to axe-core in version 4.7.0. Codebases that pin `@axe-core/playwright` at `^4.6` or lower will accept the tag without error but skip all rules tagged `wcag22aa`, giving a false sense of WCAG 2.2 coverage. WHY: Teams that upgrade their WCAG conformance claim from 2.1 to 2.2 and add `wcag22aa` to their `withTags()` call see no new failures and conclude their application is already WCAG 2.2 conformant — but they have actually tested nothing new because the axe-core version predates those rules. Always check `require('@axe-core/playwright/package.json').dependencies['axe-core']` against the axe-core 4.7 release notes when adding WCAG 2.2 tags. [community]

202. **[community] Playwright's `getByRole('combobox')` matches both native `<select>` elements and custom `role="combobox"` widgets — submitting the same `fill()` call to both causes the native `<select>` to receive text input (which is ignored) while the custom combobox is correctly populated, leading to test false-passes when a native select is unintentionally matched by the locator and the test proceeds without asserting that the value was actually set**: The ARIA role `combobox` is implicitly assigned to `<select>` elements in the accessibility tree, so `getByRole('combobox')` matches both native selects and custom ARIA comboboxes on the same page. A test that calls `page.getByRole('combobox').fill('Canada')` intending to test a custom search-combobox can accidentally match a native `<select>` that happens to be the first combobox in DOM order. WHY: `fill()` on a `<select>` does not throw — it silently does nothing — and subsequent assertions like `expect(result).toContain('Canada')` may pass for unrelated reasons, giving false confidence in the custom widget's accessible behavior. Always scope combobox locators with a label: `getByRole('combobox', { name: /country/i })`. [community]

203. **[community] When a Playwright test uses `page.waitForSelector('[role="dialog"]')` to await a modal before running an axe scan, the axe scan may still miss violations in the modal if the modal's inner content is loaded asynchronously after the `role="dialog"` container appears — because axe scans the DOM at the instant `analyze()` is called, not when the visual content finishes loading**: Large modals that fetch and render content asynchronously (e.g., a product detail modal that fetches images and descriptions) will show the modal container immediately but populate it 200–800ms later. An axe scan that runs right after `waitForSelector('[role="dialog"]')` sees an empty or partially populated modal and reports no violations — because there is no content to scan yet. WHY: Missing alt text, empty heading violations, and missing form labels inside the modal are all invisible to the scan. The fix is to await a visible element inside the modal that confirms full content load: `await page.waitForSelector('[role="dialog"] h2')` or `await expect(page.getByRole('dialog').getByRole('heading')).toBeVisible()` before calling `analyze()`. [community]

204. **[community] `aria-describedby` pointing to a hidden element (`display: none` or `visibility: hidden`) is not exposed in the accessibility tree by any browser — but the axe-core `aria-valid-attr-value` rule does not check whether the referenced element is visible, only that the ID exists in the DOM, so axe passes while AT users receive no description**: Teams add `aria-describedby="error-hint"` on form inputs and conditionally hide the hint element with `display: none` when there is no error, expecting AT to remain silent when the hint is hidden and announce it when shown. However, some implementations apply `display: none` to the hint container and then update its `textContent` while it is hidden, forgetting to also remove `display: none` — axe finds the element with the matching ID and passes `aria-valid-attr-value`, but the description is never exposed to AT because the referenced element is hidden. WHY: axe does not resolve the computed visibility of `aria-describedby` targets. Use `aria-live` regions for dynamic error hints rather than toggling `aria-describedby` targets in and out of visibility; or, use `aria-describedby` only when the target is reliably visible and non-empty. [community]

205. **[community] Testing with `@axe-core/playwright` in a Playwright project that uses `page.route()` to intercept API calls can cause axe scan timeouts if `page.route()` handlers block stylesheet or resource requests — because axe-core's preloading step fetches stylesheets to compute accurate color contrast ratios, and when the interceptor blocks those requests, axe either skips the contrast checks silently or hangs waiting for the resource**: axe-core's `preload` step fetches resources (like stylesheets) to compute contrast ratios accurately. In test setups that mock all network traffic after navigation, the axe preload fetch hits the interceptor and is blocked or returns an empty response — causing axe to either skip those checks (no violation reported) or hang indefinitely. WHY: Tests run successfully with the mock network in place but silently miss color-contrast violations that only appear when stylesheets are fully loaded. The fix is to either disable axe preloading via `options({ preload: false })` (this makes contrast results less accurate but avoids the hang), or exempt stylesheet requests from the route interceptor by checking `request.resourceType() === 'stylesheet'` in the handler and calling `route.continue()` for those. [community]
