## Cycle 45 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 164 — WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication — Paste and Autofill Verification [official]

WCAG 3.3.8 (Accessible Authentication Minimum, Level AA) prohibits cognitive function tests at any authentication step unless an alternative exists. Concretely, this means password fields must not block clipboard paste, and input fields must expose their `autocomplete` purpose so browsers and password managers can autofill. A Playwright test can verify both: it writes a credential to the clipboard via `page.evaluate`, attempts to paste it, and confirms the field is populated; it also checks that `autocomplete` is set to a recognized value (`username`, `current-password`, `new-password`, `one-time-code`). Blocking paste is a WCAG 3.3.8 failure without exception; blocking `autocomplete` is a failure of WCAG 1.3.5 (Identify Input Purpose, Level AA), which is a prerequisite for password-manager autofill. Both must pass before a login page can claim WCAG 2.2 AA conformance.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.8 — Accessible Authentication', () => {
  test('password field allows clipboard paste', async ({ page, context }) => {
    await context.grantPermissions(['clipboard-read', 'clipboard-write']);
    await page.goto('/login');

    // Write a credential to the clipboard
    await page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.writeText('P@ssw0rd!Secure'));

    const passwordField = page.getByLabel(/password/i);
    await passwordField.click();
    await page.keyboard.press('Control+v');

    const value = await passwordField.inputValue();
    expect(value, 'WCAG 3.3.8: paste into password field must not be blocked').toBe('P@ssw0rd!Secure');
  });

  test('login inputs expose correct autocomplete purpose', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');

    const usernameAC = await page.getByLabel(/username|email/i).getAttribute('autocomplete');
    const passwordAC = await page.getByLabel(/^password$/i).getAttribute('autocomplete');

    expect(
      ['username', 'email', 'tel', 'nickname'].includes(usernameAC ?? ''),
      `WCAG 1.3.5 + 3.3.8: username field autocomplete="${usernameAC}" is not a recognized identity value`
    ).toBe(true);

    expect(
      ['current-password', 'new-password'].includes(passwordAC ?? ''),
      `WCAG 1.3.5 + 3.3.8: password field autocomplete="${passwordAC}" is not recognized`
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  test('OTP / MFA code field allows paste', async ({ page, context }) => {
    await context.grantPermissions(['clipboard-read', 'clipboard-write']);
    await page.goto('/mfa');

    const otpField = page.getByLabel(/code|otp|one.time/i).first();
    if (!(await otpField.isVisible().catch(() => false))) { test.skip(); return; }

    await page.evaluate(() => navigator.clipboard.writeText('123456'));
    await otpField.click();
    await page.keyboard.press('Control+v');

    const value = await otpField.inputValue();
    expect(value, 'WCAG 3.3.8: OTP field must not block paste of verification code').toBe('123456');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `context.grantPermissions(['clipboard-read', 'clipboard-write'])` is Chromium-only; on Firefox and WebKit, `navigator.clipboard.writeText` requires the `clipboard-write` permission which Playwright does not expose for those engines. As a fallback, use `page.keyboard.type` after `execCommand('paste')` via `page.evaluate`, or simulate the paste event directly with `InputEvent` — but note that `execCommand('paste')` is deprecated and unreliable. The most robust cross-browser approach is to check only that the field's `oncopy`/`onpaste` event handlers do not call `e.preventDefault()`, which you can assert by adding a listener before the test action. [official]

---

### Pattern 165 — WCAG 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced) — Full Visibility Check [official]

WCAG 2.4.12 (Level AAA) strengthens 2.4.11 by requiring that *no part* of the focused component is hidden — not merely that *some* part remains visible. Sticky headers, cookie banners, chat widgets, and bottom navigation bars all create obscuring zones. The Playwright approach is to iterate every focusable element via `Tab` keypress, retrieve the bounding box of the focused element via `page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement.getBoundingClientRect())`, and compare it against the viewport dimensions minus any known fixed-position overlay heights. A focused element whose `top` is less than the header height, or whose `bottom` exceeds `viewportHeight − footer height`, is partially or fully obscured. This test is particularly valuable on mobile-viewport emulations where sticky UI is proportionally larger relative to the visible area.

```typescript
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

async function getFixedOverlayZones(page: Page) {
  return page.evaluate(() => {
    const zones = { top: 0, bottom: 0 };
    document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('*').forEach(el => {
      const style = getComputedStyle(el);
      if (style.position !== 'fixed' && style.position !== 'sticky') return;
      const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      if (rect.top === 0) zones.top = Math.max(zones.top, rect.height);
      if (rect.bottom === window.innerHeight) zones.bottom = Math.max(zones.bottom, rect.height);
    });
    return zones;
  });
}

test('WCAG 2.4.12 — focused elements are not obscured by sticky overlays', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  const viewport = page.viewportSize()!;
  const zones = await getFixedOverlayZones(page);

  const violations: string[] = [];
  // Tab through up to 60 focusable elements
  for (let i = 0; i < 60; i++) {
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const rect = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement;
      if (!el || el === document.body) return null;
      const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      return { top: r.top, bottom: r.bottom, label: (el as HTMLElement).textContent?.slice(0, 40) ?? el.tagName };
    });
    if (!rect) continue;
    if (rect.top < zones.top)
      violations.push(`"${rect.label}" top=${rect.top} obscured by header (height=${zones.top})`);
    if (rect.bottom > viewport.height - zones.bottom)
      violations.push(`"${rect.label}" bottom=${rect.bottom} obscured by footer zone`);
  }
  expect(violations, 'WCAG 2.4.12: focused elements must be fully visible').toEqual([]);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The fixed-overlay detection heuristic identifies elements positioned at exactly `top: 0` or `bottom: viewportHeight`. Overlays with small offsets (e.g., a cookie banner that is 2px from the bottom) are missed. For more robustness, cross-reference against a known list of your sticky element selectors (e.g., `['[data-testid="site-header"]', '#cookie-banner']`) and compute their heights explicitly. The tab-loop limit of 60 may not cover deep forms — increase it for pages with large numbers of inputs. [official]

---

### Pattern 166 — Carousel Auto-Rotation Stops on Focus and Hover [official]

WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide, Level A) requires that any moving, blinking, or scrolling content that starts automatically and lasts more than five seconds must be pauseable, stoppable, or hideable by the user. Auto-rotating carousels are the most common failure. The ARIA APG Carousel pattern further specifies that auto-rotation must pause when any carousel element receives keyboard focus, and when the pointer hovers over the carousel. Playwright can verify both behaviors: record the active slide index before and after focusing a carousel control, and assert the index has not advanced; then simulate hover and assert the same. The pause/play button state should also be verified — its accessible name must reflect the current state (e.g., "Stop slide rotation" when rotating, "Start slide rotation" when paused).

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.2.2 — Carousel auto-rotation behavior', () => {
  test('auto-rotation pauses when a carousel control receives focus', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const carousel = page.getByRole('region', { name: /carousel|featured/i }).first();
    if (!(await carousel.isVisible().catch(() => false))) { test.skip(); return; }

    const getActiveSlide = () =>
      carousel.evaluate(el => {
        const active = el.querySelector('[aria-hidden="false"], [aria-current="true"], .active');
        return active?.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? active?.textContent?.slice(0, 40) ?? null;
      });

    const slideBefore = await getActiveSlide();
    // Focus the next-slide button (or any interactive control inside the carousel)
    await carousel.getByRole('button', { name: /next|previous|pause|stop/i }).first().focus();
    // Wait longer than a typical auto-rotation interval
    await page.waitForTimeout(3500);
    const slideAfter = await getActiveSlide();

    expect(slideAfter, 'WCAG 2.2.2: carousel must not advance while a control has keyboard focus')
      .toBe(slideBefore);
  });

  test('auto-rotation pauses on mouse hover over the carousel', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const carousel = page.getByRole('region', { name: /carousel|featured/i }).first();
    if (!(await carousel.isVisible().catch(() => false))) { test.skip(); return; }

    const getActiveSlide = () =>
      carousel.evaluate(el => el.querySelector('[aria-hidden="false"], .active')?.textContent?.slice(0, 40) ?? null);

    await carousel.hover();
    const slideBefore = await getActiveSlide();
    await page.waitForTimeout(3500);
    const slideAfter = await getActiveSlide();

    expect(slideAfter, 'WCAG 2.2.2: carousel must not advance while mouse hovers over it')
      .toBe(slideBefore);
  });

  test('carousel play/pause button accessible name reflects current state', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const carousel = page.getByRole('region', { name: /carousel|featured/i }).first();
    if (!(await carousel.isVisible().catch(() => false))) { test.skip(); return; }

    const pauseBtn = carousel.getByRole('button', { name: /stop.*rotation|pause.*rotation|pause/i }).first();
    if (!(await pauseBtn.isVisible().catch(() => false))) { test.skip(); return; }

    await pauseBtn.click();
    await expect(
      carousel.getByRole('button', { name: /start.*rotation|resume|play/i }).first()
    ).toBeVisible({ timeout: 2000 });
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** A `waitForTimeout(3500)` creates a real 3.5-second delay per test — this is unavoidable when validating time-based behavior. To limit test-suite slowdown, run carousel tests in their own file with a separate `--project` in `playwright.config.ts` and exclude them from fast smoke runs. Alternatively, expose a `data-auto-interval` attribute from your carousel component and read it in the test to use the actual interval plus 500ms of buffer instead of a hardcoded value. [official]

---

### Pattern 167 — ARIA Grid `aria-rowcount` / `aria-colcount` for Virtualized Tables [official]

When a data table uses virtual scrolling (only rendering visible rows in the DOM), the accessibility tree exposes only the rendered rows — screen reader users hear "row 1 of 20" even when the actual dataset has 10,000 rows. The ARIA spec addresses this with `aria-rowcount` on the `grid`/`table` element (set to the total row count, or `-1` if unknown) and `aria-rowindex` on each rendered row (set to its position in the full dataset, 1-based). Similarly, `aria-colcount` and `aria-colindex` handle partially-rendered column sets. Playwright can verify that these attributes exist and are consistent: `aria-rowindex` must be >= 1, must increase monotonically across rendered rows, and must be <= `aria-rowcount` (unless `aria-rowcount` is -1).

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('virtualized table exposes aria-rowcount and correct aria-rowindex values', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/data-table');
  const table = page.getByRole('grid').first();
  await expect(table).toBeVisible();

  const rowcount = await table.getAttribute('aria-rowcount');
  expect(
    rowcount !== null,
    'ARIA grid with virtual scroll must have aria-rowcount on the grid element'
  ).toBe(true);

  const rows = table.getByRole('row');
  const rowCount = await rows.count();
  expect(rowCount).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  let lastIndex = 0;
  for (let i = 1; i < rowCount; i++) { // skip header row at i=0
    const indexStr = await rows.nth(i).getAttribute('aria-rowindex');
    if (!indexStr) continue; // header row may not have aria-rowindex
    const index = parseInt(indexStr, 10);
    expect(index, `Row ${i} aria-rowindex must be >= 1`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
    expect(index, `Row ${i} aria-rowindex must be > previous row's aria-rowindex (${lastIndex})`).toBeGreaterThan(lastIndex);
    if (rowcount !== '-1') {
      expect(index, `Row ${i} aria-rowindex must be <= aria-rowcount (${rowcount})`).toBeLessThanOrEqual(Number(rowcount));
    }
    lastIndex = index;
  }

  // After scrolling, rowindex values should advance
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    const grid = document.querySelector('[role="grid"]');
    if (grid) grid.scrollTop = 1000;
  });
  await page.waitForTimeout(300);
  const firstRenderedIndex = await rows.nth(1).getAttribute('aria-rowindex');
  expect(
    Number(firstRenderedIndex ?? 0),
    'After scroll, first rendered row aria-rowindex must reflect its true dataset position'
  ).toBeGreaterThan(1);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `aria-rowcount` set to `-1` is valid and means the total count is unknown (e.g., infinite scroll). When it is `-1`, you can only assert that `aria-rowindex` values are monotonically increasing across rendered rows — you cannot assert an upper bound. For tables that load data incrementally, assert that `aria-rowcount` is updated after each data-fetch batch, because leaving it at `-1` permanently degrades the AT experience even when the total eventually becomes known. [official]

---

### Pattern 168 — Accessible Name Computation for Icon-Only Buttons [community]

Icon-only buttons — rendered with an SVG icon and no visible text — are one of the most frequent axe-core `button-name` violations. The accessible name computation algorithm (accname-1.1) tries five sources in order: `aria-labelledby`, `aria-label`, the element's subtree text content, `title`, and finally `placeholder`. An SVG child element provides no text content unless it contains a `<title>` element that is then exposed via `aria-labelledby`. Three patterns are common: (1) `aria-label` on the `<button>`, (2) visually hidden `<span>` inside the button, and (3) `<title>` inside the SVG with `aria-labelledby` on the button pointing to the title's `id`. The axe rule `button-name` fires when none of these are present or when they produce an empty string after trimming whitespace.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { AxeBuilder } from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('Icon-only button accessible names', () => {
  test('all icon-only buttons have non-empty accessible names', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Axe-core button-name rule catches missing names
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['button-name'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations, 'button-name violations found').toEqual([]);
  });

  test('icon buttons in the toolbar have meaningful names (not just "button")', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/editor');
    const buttons = page.getByRole('toolbar').getByRole('button');
    const count = await buttons.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const btn = buttons.nth(i);
      const name = await btn.evaluate(el =>
        (el as HTMLElement).getAttribute('aria-label') ??
        (el as HTMLElement).getAttribute('title') ??
        el.textContent?.trim() ?? ''
      );
      expect(
        name.length,
        `Toolbar button at index ${i} has empty accessible name`
      ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      expect(
        name.toLowerCase(),
        `Toolbar button at index ${i} name "${name}" is too generic`
      ).not.toMatch(/^(button|icon|image|svg)$/i);
    }
  });

  test('SVG icons used as button content expose title via aria-labelledby', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const svgButtons = page.locator('button svg[aria-labelledby]');
    const count = await svgButtons.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const svgEl = svgButtons.nth(i);
      const labelledById = await svgEl.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
      if (!labelledById) continue;
      const titleEl = page.locator(`#${CSS.escape(labelledById)}`);
      await expect(titleEl, `SVG title element #${labelledById} must exist in DOM`).toBeAttached();
      const titleText = await titleEl.textContent();
      expect(
        (titleText ?? '').trim().length,
        `SVG title #${labelledById} must have non-empty text content`
      ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `aria-label` on the `<button>` is the simplest pattern and has the best AT support, but it creates a maintenance burden because the label lives in HTML/JSX rather than with the icon definition. Visually hidden `<span>` text (using a `.sr-only` CSS class) is often preferred in design systems because the label is co-located with the component and can be translated by standard i18n pipelines. The `<title>` + `aria-labelledby` SVG approach is the most semantically pure but has inconsistent AT support on older Safari + VoiceOver combinations — test with real AT before deploying. [community]

---

### Pattern 169 — Breadcrumb Navigation Landmark and `aria-current="page"` Verification [official]

The ARIA APG Breadcrumb pattern requires: (1) the breadcrumb is wrapped in a `<nav>` element (or element with `role="navigation"`) labeled with `aria-label="Breadcrumb"` or equivalent; (2) all links except the last are standard anchor elements; (3) the last item — representing the current page — carries `aria-current="page"`. Assistive technologies use `aria-current="page"` to announce the current page link differently, so AT users know where they are in the hierarchy. A common error is setting `aria-current` on the `<li>` container rather than the `<a>` element — this passes visual inspection but is not exposed correctly in the accessibility tree.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Breadcrumb navigation accessibility', () => {
  test('breadcrumb is wrapped in a labeled nav landmark', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products/shoes/running');
    const breadcrumb = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /breadcrumb/i });
    await expect(breadcrumb, 'Breadcrumb must be inside a <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">').toBeVisible();
  });

  test('last breadcrumb item has aria-current="page" on the anchor', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products/shoes/running');
    const breadcrumb = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /breadcrumb/i });
    const links = breadcrumb.getByRole('link');
    const count = await links.count();
    expect(count, 'Breadcrumb must have at least one link').toBeGreaterThan(0);

    const lastLink = links.last();
    const ariaCurrent = await lastLink.getAttribute('aria-current');
    expect(
      ariaCurrent,
      'Last breadcrumb link must have aria-current="page"'
    ).toBe('page');
  });

  test('non-final breadcrumb items do not have aria-current', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products/shoes/running');
    const breadcrumb = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /breadcrumb/i });
    const links = breadcrumb.getByRole('link');
    const count = await links.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count - 1; i++) {
      const ariaCurrent = await links.nth(i).getAttribute('aria-current');
      expect(
        ariaCurrent,
        `Breadcrumb link at index ${i} must not have aria-current (only the last item should)`
      ).toBeNull();
    }
  });

  test('aria-current is on the <a> element, not the <li> container', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/products/shoes/running');
    // Check that no <li> in the breadcrumb has aria-current
    const liWithCurrent = page.locator('nav[aria-label*="breadcrumb" i] li[aria-current]');
    await expect(
      liWithCurrent,
      'aria-current must be on the <a> element, not the <li> container'
    ).toHaveCount(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Some design systems render the current breadcrumb as a `<span>` rather than an `<a>` (since linking to the current page is redundant). This is acceptable per ARIA APG — the `aria-current="page"` attribute is valid on non-link elements — but axe-core's `aria-allowed-attr` rule may flag `aria-current` on a `<span>` in older rule sets. If your design system uses `<span aria-current="page">`, pin your axe-core version and verify the rule is not incorrectly failing. The `getByRole('link')` locator above will miss this pattern; adapt the test to also check `breadcrumb.locator('[aria-current="page"]')`. [official]

---

### Pattern 170 — Tab Widget Keyboard Contract: Arrow Key Navigation and `aria-selected` [official]

The ARIA APG Tabs pattern defines a strict keyboard contract: Arrow Left/Right move focus between tabs (with optional wrap-around), Tab moves focus to the active `tabpanel`, and Shift+Tab returns focus from the panel back to the active tab. When `activateTabOnFocus` is true (automatic activation), the panel content must update immediately on arrow-key focus — there must be no noticeable rendering delay. When `activateTabOnFocus` is false (manual activation), Space or Enter activates the focused-but-not-selected tab. The `aria-selected="true"` attribute must match the currently active tab, and the corresponding `tabpanel` must either be rendered (not `hidden`) or connected via `aria-controls` pointing to the active panel.

```typescript
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

async function getTabState(page: Page, tabList: ReturnType<Page['getByRole']>) {
  return tabList.evaluate(el => {
    const tabs = [...el.querySelectorAll('[role="tab"]')];
    return tabs.map(tab => ({
      name: (tab as HTMLElement).textContent?.trim() ?? '',
      selected: tab.getAttribute('aria-selected') === 'true',
      controls: tab.getAttribute('aria-controls') ?? null,
    }));
  });
}

test.describe('ARIA Tab keyboard contract', () => {
  test('arrow keys move focus between tabs; only the active tab is aria-selected', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/tabs-demo');
    const tabList = page.getByRole('tablist').first();
    await expect(tabList).toBeVisible();

    const firstTab = tabList.getByRole('tab').first();
    await firstTab.focus();

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const focusedName = await page.evaluate(() =>
      (document.activeElement as HTMLElement)?.textContent?.trim() ?? ''
    );
    expect(focusedName, 'ArrowRight must move focus to the next tab').not.toBe('');

    const state = await getTabState(page, tabList);
    const selectedTabs = state.filter(t => t.selected);
    expect(selectedTabs.length, 'Exactly one tab must be aria-selected at a time').toBe(1);
  });

  test('Tab key from tablist moves focus into the active tabpanel', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/tabs-demo');
    const tabList = page.getByRole('tablist').first();
    const firstTab = tabList.getByRole('tab').first();
    await firstTab.focus();

    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const activeRole = await page.evaluate(() =>
      document.activeElement?.closest('[role="tabpanel"]')?.getAttribute('role') ?? null
    );
    expect(
      activeRole,
      'Tab from a tab must land inside the active tabpanel'
    ).toBe('tabpanel');
  });

  test('active tabpanel is visible and not hidden', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/tabs-demo');
    const tabList = page.getByRole('tablist').first();
    const state = await getTabState(page, tabList);
    const activeTab = state.find(t => t.selected);
    expect(activeTab, 'One tab must be selected by default').toBeTruthy();

    if (activeTab?.controls) {
      const panel = page.locator(`#${CSS.escape(activeTab.controls)}`);
      await expect(panel, 'Active tabpanel must be visible').toBeVisible();
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Some tab implementations use `role="tabpanel"` with `tabindex="0"` to make the panel itself focusable, while others place focusable elements inside the panel. Both are valid per APG, but a panel with `tabindex="0"` means that after pressing Tab from the tablist, focus lands on the panel container rather than the first interactive element inside it — which can feel awkward for keyboard users with complex panel content. If your panels contain interactive widgets, prefer placing focusable elements directly inside the panel and do not set `tabindex="0"` on the panel itself. [official]

---

### Pattern 171 — `role="status"` and `role="alert"` for Toast Notifications [official]

Toast notifications that appear after user actions (form submit, save, delete) must be announced to AT users even though they do not receive focus. The ARIA spec provides `role="status"` (polite, equivalent to `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"`) for non-critical confirmations and `role="alert"` (assertive, equivalent to `aria-live="assertive" aria-atomic="true"`) for errors and critical warnings. A common implementation error is injecting toast content into a pre-existing `role="status"` container using innerHTML — this works on most platforms but silently fails on VoiceOver/Safari because WebKit requires a brief DOM mutation pause between clearing old text and inserting new text; injecting both in the same synchronous operation means only the final state is announced. The Playwright test can verify that the container exists before the action and that it has the correct role.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Toast notifications — ARIA live region contract', () => {
  test('success toast uses role="status" and is announced politely', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings');

    // Verify the live region container exists before the action (required for reliable AT announcement)
    const statusRegion = page.locator('[role="status"]').first();
    await expect(
      statusRegion,
      'role="status" container must exist in DOM before any action (not injected dynamically)'
    ).toBeAttached();

    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /save|update/i }).click();

    await expect(statusRegion).not.toBeEmpty({ timeout: 5000 });
    const text = await statusRegion.textContent();
    expect((text ?? '').trim().length, 'Success status region must have non-empty text after save').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('error toast uses role="alert" for assertive announcement', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings');

    // Trigger a validation error (submit empty required field)
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /save/i }).click();

    const alertRegion = page.locator('[role="alert"]').first();
    const toastWithAlert = page.getByRole('alert');

    // Either a dedicated alert region or the toast itself carries role="alert"
    const alertCount = await toastWithAlert.count();
    if (alertCount > 0) {
      await expect(toastWithAlert.first()).not.toBeEmpty({ timeout: 4000 });
    }
  });

  test('live region container is pre-rendered, not dynamically injected on trigger', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Inject a mutation observer before any action to detect dynamic live-region injection
    const dynamicallyInjected = await page.evaluate(() => {
      return new Promise<boolean>(resolve => {
        const observer = new MutationObserver(mutations => {
          for (const m of mutations) {
            m.addedNodes.forEach(node => {
              if (node instanceof Element) {
                const role = node.getAttribute('role');
                if (role === 'status' || role === 'alert') resolve(true);
              }
            });
          }
        });
        observer.observe(document.body, { childList: true, subtree: true });
        setTimeout(() => { observer.disconnect(); resolve(false); }, 4000);
      });
    });
    // Trigger a toast during the observation window
    const saveBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /save/i }).first();
    if (await saveBtn.isVisible().catch(() => false)) await saveBtn.click();

    expect(
      dynamicallyInjected,
      'Live region must be pre-rendered in the DOM, not injected at trigger time (causes silent AT failures on VoiceOver/Safari)'
    ).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The mutation observer test is inherently racy — if the toast appears after the 4-second timeout it produces a false-pass. Calibrate the timeout to be at least 2× your application's typical server response time. Alternatively, check for the live region container synchronously on page load before any user action, which is a simpler and more reliable proxy for "was it pre-rendered". The mutation observer approach is only necessary if you want to detect injection patterns specifically. [official]

---

### Pattern 172 — AxeBuilder Fixture with Per-Suite WCAG Tag Scoping [community]

Large test suites that run `new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze()` on every page without scoping accumulate false positives from known third-party widgets and create long lists of violations that mask new regressions. The recommended pattern is a shared Playwright fixture that creates a pre-configured `AxeBuilder` instance: it pins the WCAG version tags relevant to your conformance claim (e.g., `wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa`, `wcag22a`, `wcag22aa`), excludes a allowlisted set of third-party selectors that are out of your team's control, and optionally accepts a `scope` parameter for targeting specific page regions. This ensures all teams in a monorepo scan for the same compliance level without copy-pasting tag lists.

```typescript
// fixtures/axe-fixture.ts
import { test as base, Page } from '@playwright/test';
import { AxeBuilder } from '@axe-core/playwright';

type AxeFixture = {
  makeAxeBuilder: (scope?: string) => AxeBuilder;
};

// Third-party selectors excluded from all scans — add only what your team cannot fix
const THIRD_PARTY_EXCLUSIONS = [
  '[data-cookiebanner]',      // Cookie consent widget (vendor-provided)
  '#livechat-container',      // Live chat widget (vendor-provided)
  '[data-recaptcha]',         // reCAPTCHA (Google-managed)
];

export const test = base.extend<AxeFixture>({
  makeAxeBuilder: async ({ page }, use) => {
    const makeAxeBuilder = (scope?: string): AxeBuilder => {
      let builder = new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22a', 'wcag22aa'])
        .exclude(THIRD_PARTY_EXCLUSIONS);

      if (scope) {
        builder = builder.include(scope);
      }
      return builder;
    };
    await use(makeAxeBuilder);
  },
});

export { expect } from '@playwright/test';

// In your test files:
// import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/axe-fixture';
//
// test('home page has no WCAG 2.2 AA violations', async ({ page, makeAxeBuilder }) => {
//   await page.goto('/');
//   const results = await makeAxeBuilder().analyze();
//   expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
// });
//
// test('checkout form region is WCAG compliant', async ({ page, makeAxeBuilder }) => {
//   await page.goto('/checkout');
//   const results = await makeAxeBuilder('#checkout-form').analyze();
//   expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
// });
```

**Tradeoff.** The `THIRD_PARTY_EXCLUSIONS` list must be actively maintained — as third-party widgets get updated or replaced, previously excluded selectors may match unrelated elements or no longer match the widget, creating coverage gaps. Schedule a quarterly review of the exclusion list in your team's sprint rituals. Additionally, `withTags(['wcag22aa'])` is only meaningful on axe-core 4.7+; add a version assertion in your CI setup script (`node -e "const v=require('@axe-core/playwright/node_modules/axe-core/package.json').version; if(parseInt(v)<'4.7')process.exit(1)"`) to catch accidental downgrades. [community]

---

### Pattern 173 — Cross-Frame Axe Scan with `allowedOrigins` for Embedded Content [official]

Applications that embed same-origin iframes (e.g., a payment widget, an embedded chat form, or a micro-frontend) will have those frames scanned automatically by axe-core only if they share the same origin. For same-origin iframes, axe propagates results automatically. For cross-origin iframes, axe cannot access the frame DOM due to browser security restrictions and will either skip the frame silently or return a `frame-tested` incomplete result. When the embedded content is hosted on a different origin that your team controls, you can inject axe-core into that frame separately and collect results, then merge them into your main-page report. Understanding which scan pattern applies prevents silently missing accessibility violations inside embedded content.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { AxeBuilder } from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('same-origin iframes are included in the axe scan', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/embed-demo');

  // Verify that iframes are present
  const frames = page.frames();
  expect(frames.length, 'Page should have at least one iframe to test this pattern').toBeGreaterThan(1);

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
    .analyze();

  // The "frame-tested" incomplete result indicates a frame was skipped
  const skippedFrames = results.incomplete.filter(r => r.id === 'frame-tested');
  expect(
    skippedFrames,
    'All same-origin iframes must be scanned — cross-origin frames cannot be scanned automatically'
  ).toEqual([]);

  expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
});

test('cross-origin iframe is scanned separately and has no violations', async ({ browser }) => {
  // Create a new browser context and navigate to the embedded content's origin directly
  const embeddedContext = await browser.newContext();
  const embeddedPage = await embeddedContext.newPage();
  await embeddedPage.goto('https://payment.example.com/card-form');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page: embeddedPage })
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
    .analyze();

  await embeddedContext.close();
  expect(results.violations, 'Payment form (cross-origin iframe content) must have no violations').toEqual([]);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Scanning the cross-origin content as a standalone page (second test above) does not replicate the exact embedding context — styles, fonts, or content injected by the parent frame may differ. For the most accurate scan of embedded content, host the embedded page on the same origin in your test environment (via a proxy or test server that rewrites the origin) so that axe can scan it in-frame. If the embedded content is a third-party widget you cannot control, document the frame as an explicit exclusion in your accessibility conformance statement rather than silently missing it. [official]

---

### Pattern 174 — `prefers-color-scheme: dark` Contrast Verification [community]

Many applications support a dark mode that is activated by the OS-level `prefers-color-scheme: dark` media query. WCAG contrast requirements (1.4.3 and 1.4.11) apply equally to dark mode — but automated contrast scanning is typically only run against the light-mode theme. Playwright can emulate `prefers-color-scheme: dark` via the browser context option `colorScheme: 'dark'`, enabling a full axe-core contrast scan of the dark theme. Teams that skip this step frequently ship dark modes with insufficient contrast ratios, particularly for placeholder text, disabled state indicators, and icon-only UI components on dark backgrounds.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { AxeBuilder } from '@axe-core/playwright';

// Create a browser context that emulates dark mode
const darkModeTest = test.extend({
  page: async ({ browser }, use) => {
    const ctx = await browser.newContext({ colorScheme: 'dark' });
    const darkPage = await ctx.newPage();
    await use(darkPage);
    await ctx.close();
  },
});

darkModeTest.describe('Dark mode contrast — WCAG 1.4.3 + 1.4.11', () => {
  darkModeTest('home page has no contrast violations in dark mode', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Confirm dark mode is actually active
    const isDark = await page.evaluate(() =>
      window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches
    );
    expect(isDark, 'Dark mode emulation must be active for this test').toBe(true);

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['color-contrast', 'color-contrast-enhanced'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations, 'Dark mode must pass WCAG contrast rules').toEqual([]);
  });

  darkModeTest('form inputs maintain contrast in dark mode', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include('form')
      .withRules(['color-contrast'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** axe-core's color contrast rule relies on computed CSS `color` and `background-color` values. When a dark theme is implemented using CSS custom properties (variables) that override values under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`, Chromium correctly exposes the computed dark values when the `colorScheme` context option is set. However, dark mode implemented via a JavaScript class toggle (e.g., `.dark` on `<body>`) is not automatically activated by the Playwright `colorScheme` option — those tests require manually toggling the class before scanning. Always verify with `window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches` and a visual check before trusting contrast scan results. [community]

---

### Pattern 175 — Accessible Name for `<figure>` and `<figcaption>` [official]

The `<figure>` element with a `<figcaption>` creates an implicit grouping: the figcaption provides the accessible name for the figure. When used for images (instead of or alongside `alt`), the accessible name computation resolves to the figcaption text rather than the `img`'s `alt` attribute, which can cause redundant announcements: AT may announce the `alt` text, pause, then announce "group" with the figcaption label. The ARIA spec recommends that when a `<figure>` contains a single image and a `<figcaption>`, the `<img>` should have `alt=""` (empty alt, marked as decorative) to prevent double-announcement, while the figcaption provides the sole accessible description. axe-core's `image-alt` rule does not flag `alt=""` inside `<figure>` as a violation — it only flags missing `alt` attributes.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { AxeBuilder } from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('<figure> + <figcaption> accessible name pattern', () => {
  test('images inside <figure> with <figcaption> use alt="" to avoid double announcement', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/blog');

    const figures = page.locator('figure:has(figcaption) img');
    const count = await figures.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const img = figures.nth(i);
      const alt = await img.getAttribute('alt');
      expect(
        alt,
        `Image at index ${i} inside <figure> with <figcaption> must have alt="" (empty, not missing)`
      ).toBe('');
    }
  });

  test('figcaption provides non-empty visible description', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/blog');
    const captions = page.locator('figure figcaption');
    const count = await captions.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const text = await captions.nth(i).textContent();
      expect(
        (text ?? '').trim().length,
        `figcaption at index ${i} must have non-empty visible text`
      ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });

  test('axe-core reports no image-alt violations for figure+figcaption pattern', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/blog');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['image-alt'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** This pattern only applies when the figcaption is a true substitute for the image's informational alt text. If the figcaption provides only supplementary context (e.g., a copyright notice or styling credit), the image still needs a meaningful `alt` attribute — in that case, do not use `alt=""`. Additionally, SVG images inside `<figure>` should use `role="img"` with `aria-labelledby` pointing to the figcaption's `id` rather than relying on the implicit figure semantics, because SVG's accessible name computation is less consistently implemented across AT. [official]

---

### Pattern 176 — Keyboard Trap Detection in Non-Modal Interactive Regions [community]

WCAG 2.1.2 (No Keyboard Trap, Level A) requires that if focus can be moved into a component via keyboard, the user must be able to move focus out using standard key sequences (Tab, Shift+Tab, Escape, or documented alternative). Keyboard traps are most commonly introduced by: custom `focusin` event handlers that call `e.preventDefault()`, infinite tab-cycle implementations in non-modal contexts (date pickers, time pickers, color pickers that are always expanded inline), and third-party widgets that implement their own focus management without a documented exit key. Playwright can detect keyboard traps by recording focus positions over a sequence of Tab presses and asserting that focus eventually escapes the component's DOM subtree.

```typescript
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

async function detectKeyboardTrap(page: Page, enterSelector: string, maxTabs = 30): Promise<boolean> {
  const component = page.locator(enterSelector).first();
  await component.focus();

  const componentHandle = await component.elementHandle();
  const visited = new Set<string>();
  let escapedComponent = false;

  for (let i = 0; i < maxTabs; i++) {
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const result = await page.evaluate((comp) => {
      const active = document.activeElement;
      if (!active || active === document.body) return { inside: false, id: 'body' };
      const inside = comp?.contains(active) ?? false;
      const id = active.getAttribute('id') ?? active.tagName + '_' + active.textContent?.slice(0, 20);
      return { inside, id };
    }, componentHandle);

    if (!result.inside) { escapedComponent = true; break; }
    if (visited.has(result.id)) {
      // Focus is cycling within the same set of elements — likely a trap
      return true;
    }
    visited.add(result.id);
  }
  return !escapedComponent;
}

test.describe('WCAG 2.1.2 — No Keyboard Trap', () => {
  test('inline date picker does not trap keyboard focus', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/booking');
    const trapped = await detectKeyboardTrap(page, '[data-testid="date-picker"]');
    expect(trapped, 'WCAG 2.1.2: Inline date picker must not trap keyboard focus').toBe(false);
  });

  test('navigation mega-menu does not trap keyboard focus', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const navMenu = page.getByRole('navigation').getByRole('button').first();
    await navMenu.click();
    const trapped = await detectKeyboardTrap(page, '[role="menu"]');
    expect(trapped, 'WCAG 2.1.2: Navigation mega-menu must not trap keyboard focus').toBe(false);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The cycle-detection heuristic (revisiting the same focus target ID within `maxTabs` iterations) can produce false positives for small widgets with only 2-3 focusable elements — two traversals of a 3-element widget look identical to a trap. Increase the trap threshold: instead of flagging on first revisit, flag only when the same `id` is visited 3+ times without escaping. Modal dialogs and `<dialog>` elements are intentional focus traps and should be excluded from this test; scope `detectKeyboardTrap` to non-modal interactive regions only. [community]

---

### Pattern 177 — `aria-expanded` State Synchronization for Disclosure Widgets [official]

The ARIA Disclosure pattern requires that the triggering button carries `aria-expanded="false"` when the controlled content is hidden and `aria-expanded="true"` when it is visible. The most common failure mode is stale `aria-expanded` state: the button's attribute is set on initial render but never updated when the controlled section's visibility changes via CSS class toggle or `display`/`visibility` manipulation. AT users hear the button announced as "collapsed" even when the content is visible — or vice versa. Playwright can verify synchronization by checking the visible state of the controlled content against the button's `aria-expanded` value after both expand and collapse actions.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Disclosure — aria-expanded synchronization', () => {
  test('expanding a disclosure updates aria-expanded and reveals content', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const toggles = page.getByRole('button', { name: /\?|faq|expand|show/i }).or(
      page.locator('button[aria-expanded]').first().locator('..')
    );
    const toggle = page.locator('button[aria-expanded="false"]').first();
    if (!(await toggle.isVisible().catch(() => false))) { test.skip(); return; }

    const controlledId = await toggle.getAttribute('aria-controls');
    await toggle.click();

    expect(await toggle.getAttribute('aria-expanded'), 'aria-expanded must be "true" after click').toBe('true');
    if (controlledId) {
      await expect(page.locator(`#${CSS.escape(controlledId)}`), 'Controlled content must be visible').toBeVisible();
    }
  });

  test('collapsing a disclosure updates aria-expanded and hides content', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const toggle = page.locator('button[aria-expanded="false"]').first();
    if (!(await toggle.isVisible().catch(() => false))) { test.skip(); return; }

    const controlledId = await toggle.getAttribute('aria-controls');
    await toggle.click(); // expand
    await expect(toggle).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

    await toggle.click(); // collapse
    expect(await toggle.getAttribute('aria-expanded'), 'aria-expanded must return to "false" after collapse').toBe('false');
    if (controlledId) {
      await expect(page.locator(`#${CSS.escape(controlledId)}`), 'Controlled content must be hidden after collapse').toBeHidden();
    }
  });

  test('all disclosure buttons have initial aria-expanded attribute', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/faq');
    const buttonsWithoutExpanded = page.locator('button:not([aria-expanded])').filter({
      has: page.locator('[id]'), // heuristic: buttons that control something
    });
    // More precise: look for buttons that visually collapse/expand content
    const disclosureButtons = page.locator('[data-disclosure] button, .accordion button, .faq button');
    const count = await disclosureButtons.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const expanded = await disclosureButtons.nth(i).getAttribute('aria-expanded');
      expect(
        expanded !== null,
        `Disclosure button at index ${i} must have aria-expanded attribute (found null)`
      ).toBe(true);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Checking `aria-expanded` synchronization via DOM attribute inspection does not verify AT announcement timing — a stale `aria-expanded` that is corrected 50ms after the content renders will pass this test but may still cause an incorrect announcement in VoiceOver. For AT-level fidelity, supplement DOM tests with manual VoiceOver/NVDA testing during sprint reviews. The `aria-controls` attribute pointing to the controlled element is recommended by ARIA APG but not required — some implementations omit it (using proximity or `aria-owns` instead); guard your `controlledId` assertions with a null check as shown above. [official]

---

### Pattern 178 — Skip Navigation Link Visibility and Target Verification [official]

WCAG 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks, Level A) requires a mechanism to skip repeated navigation blocks. The standard implementation is a visually hidden "Skip to main content" link that becomes visible on focus. Three failure modes are common: (1) the link exists but its `href` points to an `id` that does not exist in the DOM, so activating it does nothing; (2) the link is visually hidden with `visibility: hidden` or `display: none` rather than a clip/translate technique, making it unfocusable (and therefore unavailable to keyboard users); (3) the link receives focus but its target `<main>` or `id="main-content"` does not have `tabindex="-1"`, so keyboard focus does not actually move to the target on older browsers. Playwright can verify all three failure modes.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.1 — Skip Navigation', () => {
  test('skip link is the first focusable element and becomes visible on focus', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    // First Tab press should land on the skip link
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focusedHref = await page.evaluate(() =>
      (document.activeElement as HTMLAnchorElement)?.href ?? null
    );
    expect(focusedHref, 'First Tab focus must land on a skip link (href contains #main or #content)').toMatch(/#(main|content|skip)/i);

    // The skip link should be visible when focused
    const skipLink = page.locator('a[href*="#main"], a[href*="#content"], a[href*="#skip"]').first();
    await expect(skipLink, 'Skip link must be visible when focused').toBeVisible();
  });

  test('skip link target element exists in the DOM', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const skipLink = page.locator('a[href^="#"]').first();
    const href = await skipLink.getAttribute('href');
    if (!href) { test.skip(); return; }

    const targetId = href.replace('#', '');
    const target = page.locator(`#${CSS.escape(targetId)}`);
    await expect(
      target,
      `Skip link target #${targetId} must exist in the DOM`
    ).toBeAttached();
  });

  test('activating skip link moves focus to the target', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab'); // focus skip link
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter'); // activate

    const focusedId = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.id ?? null);
    const isMain = await page.evaluate(() =>
      document.activeElement?.tagName === 'MAIN' ||
      document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role') === 'main'
    );
    expect(
      focusedId || isMain,
      'Activating skip link must move keyboard focus to the main content area'
    ).toBeTruthy();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Some implementations render the skip link as `position: absolute; transform: translateY(-100%)` and use `focus:translate-y-0` to bring it on-screen — this works with keyboard but may not work with switch access devices that do not trigger CSS `:focus` states the same way. The most robust pattern is to use a visually hidden class (clip-path or clip-rect with `position: absolute`) combined with `:focus-within` or `:focus-visible` to reveal it. Additionally, the target element (`<main>` or `#main-content`) should have `tabindex="-1"` explicitly to ensure programmatic focus works reliably across all browsers — without it, `focus()` calls from browsers' skip-link activation mechanism work inconsistently on Safari. [official]

---

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 45)

206. **[community] When `aria-expanded` is set to the string `"false"` rather than the boolean `false` in a React/JSX component (e.g., `aria-expanded={isOpen}` where `isOpen` is initialized as `undefined`), the attribute is omitted from the DOM entirely during the initial render — AT announces no state at all — and axe-core's `aria-required-attr` rule does not flag the missing attribute because the rule only checks required ARIA attributes when the role is present, not when an expected optional attribute is simply absent**: In React, JSX attributes with `undefined` values are silently omitted from the rendered HTML. A button that starts with `isOpen = undefined` will render as `<button>` with no `aria-expanded`, rather than `<button aria-expanded="false">`. Screen reader users receive no indication that the button controls an expandable region until after the first interaction. WHY: Teams that test `aria-expanded` only after clicking the button (when `isOpen` becomes `true`) never observe the initial omission. Always initialize disclosure state with an explicit boolean: `const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false)` (not `undefined` or `null`), and add a test that checks the `aria-expanded` attribute on first page load before any interaction. [community]

207. **[community] Playwright's `toBeVisible()` returns `true` for elements that are within the viewport but have `opacity: 0` — meaning a skip-to-main link or a visually hidden disclosure button that uses `opacity: 0` as its hide mechanism passes a `toBeVisible()` assertion even though a sighted keyboard user cannot see it**: Playwright's visibility check does not consider `opacity: 0` as hidden because the element still occupies space in the layout and is technically interactive. A skip link implemented with `opacity: 0; transition: opacity 0.2s` and `:focus { opacity: 1 }` is testable — but a bug that removes the `:focus` rule (while keeping `opacity: 0` on the default state) will still cause `toBeVisible()` to pass. WHY: CI accessibility tests pass, but sighted keyboard users navigating the live site see no skip link because it remains transparent. Use `page.evaluate(() => parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).opacity) > 0)` as an additional assertion whenever your skip link or focus-visible implementation relies on opacity transitions. [community]

208. **[community] The axe-core rule `landmark-one-main` fails when a page has zero `<main>` elements OR when it has more than one — but single-page applications that lazy-load route components often momentarily render with zero `<main>` elements during a route transition, causing axe scans run during navigation to report a violation that disappears 100–300ms later, creating intermittent CI failures that are hard to reproduce locally**: In SPAs using React Router, Next.js app router, or Vue Router, the incoming route's `<main>` element is mounted asynchronously after the old page's `<main>` is unmounted. An axe scan that fires immediately after a `page.goto()` or `page.click()` that triggers a navigation may catch the page mid-transition with no `<main>` in the DOM. WHY: Developers dismiss the CI failure as "flaky" without investigating. The fix is to always await a landmark-level element before scanning: `await page.getByRole('main').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })` before calling `analyze()`. [community]

209. **[community] `AxeBuilder.include('#my-dialog')` scans only the dialog element and its descendants — but the axe-core `aria-allowed-attr`, `aria-required-children`, and `scrollable-region-focusable` rules consider ancestor context when evaluating some role constraints, and scoping to the dialog can suppress violations that would fire during a full-page scan because the rule engine lacks the parent DOM context needed to detect the conflict**: The axe-core documentation states that `include()` constrains which elements' violations are reported, not which elements are loaded into the analysis context. However, certain rules internally reference ancestor roles (e.g., whether a `listitem` is inside a `list`) to determine validity, and when the ancestor is outside the scoped region, axe uses a partial context that may not trigger the rule. WHY: A dialog containing a `<li>` without a parent `<ul>` will cause the `listitem` rule to fire in a full-page scan but not in a dialog-scoped scan, because the rule checks for a `list` ancestor and finds none outside the included scope. Use scoped scanning for performance, but run a full-page scan at least once per page in your CI pipeline to catch cross-context rule violations. [community]

210. **[community] When `color-contrast-enhanced` (WCAG 1.4.6, Level AAA) is included in an `AxeBuilder.withRules()` call alongside `color-contrast` (WCAG 1.4.3, Level AA), axe-core reports violations for both rules independently for the same element — causing the violations array to contain duplicate elements with different rule IDs — and teams that iterate the violations array and auto-generate tickets create duplicate remediation tickets for what is a single visual design decision**: The `color-contrast-enhanced` rule enforces a 7:1 ratio for normal text and 4.5:1 for large text, while `color-contrast` enforces 4.5:1 and 3:1 respectively. An element failing both means it fails the lower threshold too, and one remediation fixes both. WHY: CI pipelines that convert axe violations to Jira/GitHub issues using `violations.length` as the ticket-creation count will create two tickets for the same `<p>` element — one for "contrast 1.4.3" and one for "contrast 1.4.6" — causing confusion about whether a single fix resolves both. Deduplicate by grouping violations by CSS selector before ticket creation, and only claim Level AAA conformance for enhanced contrast if your conformance statement specifically targets AAA. [community]

### Key Resources — Cycle 45

| Name | Type | URL | Why useful |
|------|------|-----|------------|
