## Cycle 47 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 179 — WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging Movements: Single-Pointer Alternative Verification [official]

WCAG 2.5.7 (Level AA, added in WCAG 2.2) requires that every function requiring a dragging movement — reorder lists, range sliders, resizable panels, canvas draw tools — must also be operable via a single pointer action that involves no drag path. The criterion covers author-implemented drag operations only; browser-native scroll or OS-level drag-to-refresh is excluded. A "single pointer alternative" can be a separate control (e.g., up/down buttons for a sort list) or an equivalent interaction (e.g., click-on-track to set a slider thumb position), but the alternative must be discoverable and must produce the same result. Testing strategy is two-pronged: enumerate all drag surfaces in the page and verify that each has a pointer-only path that does not require holding a button while moving the pointer.

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 2.5.7 single-pointer alternative verification
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.5.7 – Dragging Movements', () => {
  test('reorder list item via non-drag alternative (up/down buttons)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/tasks');

    // Capture initial order
    const items = page.getByRole('listitem');
    const firstText = await items.nth(0).textContent();
    const secondText = await items.nth(1).textContent();

    // Activate the "Move down" button on the first item — no drag needed
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /move down/i }).first().click();

    // Verify order flipped
    await expect(items.nth(0)).toHaveText(secondText!.trim());
    await expect(items.nth(1)).toHaveText(firstText!.trim());
  });

  test('range slider can be set via click-on-track without drag', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings/volume');
    const track = page.getByRole('slider').locator('..'); // slider parent = track
    const trackBox = await track.boundingBox();
    if (!trackBox) { test.fail(); return; }

    // Click at 75% of the track width — pointer-only, no dragTo
    const clickX = trackBox.x + trackBox.width * 0.75;
    const clickY = trackBox.y + trackBox.height / 2;
    await page.mouse.click(clickX, clickY);

    const value = await page.getByRole('slider').getAttribute('aria-valuenow');
    expect(Number(value), 'Slider value must change from click-on-track (non-drag path)').toBeGreaterThan(50);
  });

  test('sortable list announces new position after keyboard-equivalent move', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/tasks');
    // Keyboard is the ultimate drag alternative — verify it also works
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /move down/i }).first().focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
    // Check aria-live region or visual confirmation
    const announcement = page.getByRole('status');
    await expect(announcement).toContainText(/moved/i);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Providing both a drag path and a separate button pair (move-up/move-down) is the most robust approach but doubles the UI chrome for reorder interactions. An alternative that keeps the drag interaction as the primary UX while allowing click-to-set (e.g., clicking a slider track) is leaner but requires careful implementation: click-to-set must position the thumb at the click target, not just increment by one step. Teams building canvas-based draw tools often overlook that an "undo" alternative is not sufficient — the criterion requires a non-drag path to perform the same draw operation, which may mean adding a coordinate-input field. [official]

---

### Pattern 180 — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum): 24×24 CSS Pixel Measurement and Spacing Offset Check [official]

WCAG 2.5.8 (Level AA, WCAG 2.2) requires all pointer targets to be at least 24×24 CSS pixels, or — if the target itself is smaller — that its offset (spacing to the nearest adjacent target) brings the combined 24px diameter circle around the target's center to intersect with no other target. Icon-only toolbar buttons, close buttons in chip/tag components, pagination dots, and inline link icons are the most common failure points. The inline text exception exempts links embedded in body prose (because reflow makes consistent sizing impossible), but standalone icon links in navigation or UI chrome are not exempt. Testing uses `getBoundingClientRect()` to measure each interactive element. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 2.5.8 target size audit
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const MIN_TARGET_PX = 24;

test('all interactive controls meet 24×24 CSS pixel minimum target size', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const violations = await page.evaluate((min) => {
    const interactiveSelectors = [
      'a[href]', 'button', 'input', 'select', 'textarea',
      '[role="button"]', '[role="link"]', '[role="menuitem"]',
      '[role="checkbox"]', '[role="radio"]', '[role="switch"]',
    ];
    const candidates = Array.from(
      document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(interactiveSelectors.join(','))
    );

    return candidates
      .filter(el => {
        // Exempt inline text links per WCAG 2.5.8 Exception
        if (el.tagName === 'A' && el.closest('p, li, td, dd')) return false;
        // Skip hidden or zero-size elements
        const box = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        if (box.width === 0 || box.height === 0) return false;
        return box.width < min || box.height < min;
      })
      .map(el => ({
        tag: el.tagName,
        role: el.getAttribute('role') ?? '',
        label: el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? el.textContent?.trim().slice(0, 40),
        width: Math.round(el.getBoundingClientRect().width),
        height: Math.round(el.getBoundingClientRect().height),
      }));
  }, MIN_TARGET_PX);

  expect(
    violations,
    `Found ${violations.length} interactive element(s) below 24×24 CSS px:\n` +
    violations.map(v => `  <${v.tag} role="${v.role}"> "${v.label}" — ${v.width}×${v.height}px`).join('\n')
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The `getBoundingClientRect()` approach measures rendered size, which accounts for CSS transforms and zoom, but it cannot verify the offset/spacing exception without also computing the distance to adjacent targets — that requires iterating all pairs of small targets and checking whether their 24px circles overlap. For most CI pipelines, catching elements that are outright smaller than 24px in both dimensions is the highest-value first pass. A second, more expensive check can compute inter-target distances for elements in the 16–23px range. Note that this test will produce false positives on toggle-switch thumb elements (the track is larger than 24px even if the thumb isn't), so adding allowlist patterns for known correct components is common. [official]

---

### Pattern 181 — WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name: `aria-label` Must Contain the Visible Text String [official]

WCAG 2.5.3 (Level A) requires that when a UI component has a visible text label, the component's accessible name must contain that visible text — so voice control users can say the label they see to activate the control. The most common failure is using `aria-label` to replace rather than augment the visible text: `<button aria-label="Delete item">✕</button>` is fine because there is no visible text; but `<button aria-label="Remove from cart">Delete</button>` is a violation because the accessible name "Remove from cart" does not contain the visible text "Delete". The accessible name must contain the visible text verbatim (case-insensitively) as a substring. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 2.5.3 label-in-name audit
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 2.5.3 — accessible names contain their visible text labels', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const violations = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const interactives = Array.from(
      document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('button, a, [role="button"], [role="link"]')
    );

    return interactives.flatMap(el => {
      const visibleText = (el.innerText ?? '').trim().toLowerCase();
      // Only check elements that have visible text content
      if (!visibleText || visibleText.length === 0) return [];

      const ariaLabel = (el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? '').toLowerCase();
      const ariaLabelledBy = el.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');

      let accessibleName = ariaLabel;
      if (ariaLabelledBy) {
        const labeller = document.getElementById(ariaLabelledBy);
        accessibleName = (labeller?.innerText ?? '').toLowerCase();
      }

      // If there is an explicit accessible name and it does NOT contain the visible text
      if (accessibleName && !accessibleName.includes(visibleText)) {
        return [{
          tag: el.tagName,
          visibleText,
          accessibleName,
          outerHTML: el.outerHTML.slice(0, 120),
        }];
      }
      return [];
    });
  });

  expect(
    violations,
    `WCAG 2.5.3 violations (accessible name does not contain visible text):\n` +
    violations.map(v => `  "${v.visibleText}" vs name="${v.accessibleName}"  —  ${v.outerHTML}`).join('\n')
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** This test fires a false positive when an element's visible text is a single punctuation character (e.g., `×` or `>`) that is intentionally overridden by a more descriptive `aria-label`. Filter out visible text that matches `\p{P}` (punctuation) or is a single non-word character before evaluating. Also, `aria-labelledby` that composes text from multiple elements requires more complex resolution than a single `getElementById` lookup — for full correctness, use the accname algorithm rather than a DIY implementation. The test as written is a high-signal approximation suitable for CI, not a formally correct accname computation. [official]

---

### Pattern 182 — ARIA Modal Dialog: `aria-modal`, Focus Trap, and Restore-Focus Verification [official]

A dialog with `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"` requires three runtime behaviours: (1) focus is moved inside the dialog when it opens, ideally to the first focusable descendant or the dialog's heading; (2) Tab and Shift+Tab cycle within the dialog and never escape to background content; (3) when the dialog is dismissed (Escape key or explicit close button), focus returns to the element that triggered it. Playwright can verify all three behaviours in a single test suite. `aria-modal="true"` alone does not create a focus trap — it is the JavaScript's `keydown` listener and `inert` attribute (or equivalent) on background content that produce the trap; axe-core's `aria-allowed-attr` rule only checks the attribute value, not the runtime focus behaviour. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — dialog focus management: open, trap, restore
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG — Modal Dialog Focus Management', () => {
  test('focus moves inside dialog when opened', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const trigger = page.getByRole('button', { name: /open settings/i });
    await trigger.click();

    const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();

    // Focus must be inside the dialog
    const focusedInsideDialog = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const dialog = document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]');
      return dialog?.contains(document.activeElement) ?? false;
    });
    expect(focusedInsideDialog, 'Focus must move inside the dialog on open').toBe(true);
  });

  test('Tab key cannot escape the dialog (focus trap)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open settings/i }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();

    // Tab through all focusable elements more times than a dialog could contain
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
      const focusedInsideDialog = await page.evaluate(() => {
        const dialog = document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]');
        return dialog?.contains(document.activeElement) ?? false;
      });
      expect(focusedInsideDialog, `Focus escaped dialog on Tab press ${i + 1}`).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test('Escape closes dialog and restores focus to trigger', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const trigger = page.getByRole('button', { name: /open settings/i });
    await trigger.click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).not.toBeVisible();

    // Focus must return to the trigger
    const triggerFocused = await page.evaluate(() =>
      document.activeElement?.getAttribute('aria-label')?.toLowerCase().includes('open settings') ||
      (document.activeElement as HTMLElement)?.innerText?.toLowerCase().includes('open settings')
    );
    expect(triggerFocused, 'Focus must return to the dialog trigger on Escape').toBe(true);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The 20-Tab-press loop for the focus trap test is a pragmatic upper bound — no real dialog should have 20 focusable children, so if focus has not escaped after 20 presses it has not escaped. However, this approach is slow (20 keyboard events × network round-trip). An alternative is to find all focusable descendants with `querySelectorAll`, press Tab exactly `n+1` times (where n is the count), and assert focus wrapped back to the first focusable child. The Escape-key / restore-focus test will fail if the triggering element is removed from the DOM while the dialog is open (e.g., a button that opens a multi-step flow where the trigger page is unmounted). In that case, focus should move to a logical substitute — document this as a known exception rather than suppressing the test. [official]

---

### Pattern 183 — ARIA Listbox Keyboard Contract: Arrow Navigation, `aria-selected`, and Multi-Select with `aria-multiselectable` [official]

The `role="listbox"` widget requires Down/Up arrows to move focus between options, with options carrying `aria-selected="true"` or `aria-selected="false"` on every option (never omitted). Single-select listboxes follow selection-follows-focus: pressing Down automatically deselects the previously selected option and selects the new focused one. Multi-select listboxes (marked with `aria-multiselectable="true"`) decouple focus from selection — the user presses Space to toggle selection without losing previously selected items. Home/End must move to the first/last option. The listbox container needs an accessible name via `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Type-ahead (pressing a letter to jump to the first option beginning with that character) is strongly recommended. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — listbox keyboard interaction contract
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Listbox keyboard contract', () => {
  test('Down/Up arrow keys navigate options and update aria-selected (single-select)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/select-country');
    const listbox = page.getByRole('listbox', { name: /country/i });
    await listbox.focus();

    // Initial state: first option should be selected or focused
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    const options = listbox.getByRole('option');
    const secondSelected = await options.nth(1).getAttribute('aria-selected');
    expect(secondSelected, 'ArrowDown must select the second option in a single-select listbox').toBe('true');

    // All other options must be deselected
    const firstSelected = await options.nth(0).getAttribute('aria-selected');
    expect(firstSelected, 'Previously selected option must be deselected after ArrowDown').toBe('false');
  });

  test('Space toggles selection without moving focus in multi-select listbox', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/select-skills');
    const listbox = page.getByRole('listbox', { name: /skills/i });
    await expect(listbox).toHaveAttribute('aria-multiselectable', 'true');

    await listbox.focus();
    // Select first option
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
    const opt0 = listbox.getByRole('option').nth(0);
    await expect(opt0).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');

    // Move to second option and select it — first must stay selected
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
    const opt1 = listbox.getByRole('option').nth(1);
    await expect(opt1).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
    await expect(opt0, 'First option must remain selected in multi-select after selecting second').toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
  });

  test('Home/End keys jump to first and last options', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/select-country');
    const listbox = page.getByRole('listbox', { name: /country/i });
    const options = listbox.getByRole('option');
    const count = await options.count();

    await listbox.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('End');
    const lastFocused = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.textContent?.trim());
    const lastText = await options.nth(count - 1).textContent();
    expect(lastFocused).toBe(lastText?.trim());

    await page.keyboard.press('Home');
    const firstFocused = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.textContent?.trim());
    const firstText = await options.nth(0).textContent();
    expect(firstFocused).toBe(firstText?.trim());
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Selection-follows-focus in single-select listboxes is the ARIA APG default but can conflict with server-round-trip patterns: if each option selection triggers an async fetch, moving with arrow keys hammers the API. Teams often compromise by using a "commit on Enter" pattern — focus moves with arrows, but selection (and the fetch) is deferred to Enter. This is a known deviation from the APG default; document it explicitly in the accessibility conformance statement and ensure the AT announcement still reflects the "pending" vs "committed" state difference. [official]

---

### Pattern 184 — ARIA Tree View: `aria-expanded` Only on Parent Nodes, `aria-selected` vs `aria-checked` Consistency [official]

The `role="tree"` pattern uses `role="treeitem"` for every node. Parent nodes (those that have child nodes) must carry `aria-expanded="false"` (collapsed) or `aria-expanded="true"` (expanded). Leaf nodes — nodes with no children — must NOT carry `aria-expanded` at all; its presence on a leaf causes screen readers to announce the node as a parent that can be collapsed, misleading users about tree structure. Right arrow expands a collapsed parent (or moves focus to the first child if already expanded); Left arrow collapses an expanded parent (or moves to its parent if already collapsed). `aria-selected` is correct for selection-state tracking; `aria-checked` may be used as an alternative in multi-select trees but should not be mixed with `aria-selected` in the same tree. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — tree view: leaf nodes must not have aria-expanded
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('ARIA tree — leaf nodes must not carry aria-expanded', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/file-browser');
  const tree = page.getByRole('tree');

  const leafViolations = await tree.evaluate((treeEl) => {
    const allItems = Array.from(treeEl.querySelectorAll('[role="treeitem"]'));
    return allItems
      .filter(item => {
        const hasChildren = item.querySelector('[role="treeitem"]') !== null ||
          item.getAttribute('aria-owns') !== null;
        const hasExpanded = item.hasAttribute('aria-expanded');
        return !hasChildren && hasExpanded; // leaf with aria-expanded = violation
      })
      .map(item => item.textContent?.trim().slice(0, 60));
  });

  expect(
    leafViolations,
    `Leaf treeitem(s) incorrectly carry aria-expanded: ${leafViolations.join(', ')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});

test('ARIA tree — Right arrow expands collapsed parent, Left arrow collapses expanded parent', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/file-browser');
  const tree = page.getByRole('tree');

  // Find a collapsed parent node
  const collapsedParent = tree.locator('[role="treeitem"][aria-expanded="false"]').first();
  await collapsedParent.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
  await expect(collapsedParent).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

  // Collapse it again
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft');
  await expect(collapsedParent).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
});

test('ARIA tree — aria-selected and aria-checked are not mixed on the same tree', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/file-browser');
  const tree = page.getByRole('tree');

  const hasSelected = await tree.locator('[role="treeitem"][aria-selected]').count();
  const hasChecked  = await tree.locator('[role="treeitem"][aria-checked]').count();

  const mixedUsage = hasSelected > 0 && hasChecked > 0;
  expect(mixedUsage, 'Tree must not mix aria-selected and aria-checked on treeitems').toBe(false);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Lazy-loaded trees (where child nodes are fetched when the parent is expanded) often render the parent node without children in the initial DOM. This means the `aria-expanded` detection logic above (checking for `[role="treeitem"]` descendants) will incorrectly classify an un-loaded parent as a leaf. The recommended fix is to always render parent nodes with a `data-has-children="true"` attribute or to include a zero-opacity placeholder child so the structural test can distinguish them from genuine leaves. Alternatively, drive the test from the data: if your tree data layer knows node X has children, assert that node X's treeitem has `aria-expanded` after render. [official]

---

### Pattern 185 — ARIA Menubar: Horizontal Arrow Key Navigation, Submenu Open/Close, and Tab-Key Exit Contract [official]

A `role="menubar"` widget uses Left/Right arrow keys to move between top-level items and Down arrow (or Enter on an item with `aria-haspopup="menu"`) to open a submenu. Within an open submenu (`role="menu"`), Up/Down arrows navigate options, Escape closes the submenu and returns focus to the parent menubar item, and Left/Right arrows should close the submenu and move to the adjacent menubar item. Pressing Tab while the menubar is focused must move focus entirely out of the menubar to the next focusable element in the page (Tab is not for navigating within a composite widget). All menubar items except the first should have `tabindex="-1"` with the first carrying `tabindex="0"` (roving tabindex pattern). [official]

```typescript
// playwright — menubar keyboard contract
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Menubar keyboard contract', () => {
  test('Right/Left arrow keys move between top-level menu items', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const menubar = page.getByRole('menubar');
    const items = menubar.getByRole('menuitem');

    await items.nth(0).focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const secondFocused = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.textContent?.trim());
    const secondText = await items.nth(1).textContent();
    expect(secondFocused).toBe(secondText?.trim());
  });

  test('Down arrow opens submenu from menubar item with aria-haspopup', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const menubar = page.getByRole('menubar');
    const parentItem = menubar.getByRole('menuitem', { name: /products/i });
    await parentItem.focus();

    await expect(parentItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-haspopup', 'menu');
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');

    const submenu = page.getByRole('menu');
    await expect(submenu).toBeVisible();
    await expect(parentItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
  });

  test('Escape closes submenu and returns focus to parent menubar item', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('menuitem', { name: /products/i }).focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown'); // open submenu
    await expect(page.getByRole('menu')).toBeVisible();

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(page.getByRole('menu')).not.toBeVisible();

    const focusedText = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.textContent?.trim());
    expect(focusedText?.toLowerCase()).toContain('products');
  });

  test('Tab key moves focus out of menubar to next page element', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByRole('menubar').getByRole('menuitem').first().focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');

    const focusInsideMenubar = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const menubar = document.querySelector('[role="menubar"]');
      return menubar?.contains(document.activeElement) ?? false;
    });
    expect(focusInsideMenubar, 'Tab must move focus OUT of the menubar').toBe(false);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The Escape-to-parent behavior interacts badly with SPAs that unmount the submenu component entirely on close: if the `role="menu"` element is removed from the DOM, `toBeVisible()` will throw a "target closed" error. Use `await page.getByRole('menu').waitFor({ state: 'detached' })` for unmounting implementations, and `await expect(menu).not.toBeVisible()` for implementations that hide in-place with CSS. These require different test code for the same conceptual assertion, so parameterize by implementation type in your test helper. [official]

---

### Pattern 186 — WCAG 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose: `autocomplete` Token Validation for User-Data Forms [official]

WCAG 1.3.5 (Level AA) requires that input fields collecting information about the user must carry an `autocomplete` attribute with a valid HTML 5.3 token that matches the field's semantic purpose (e.g., `autocomplete="email"` on an email field, not `autocomplete="off"` or a custom string). This enables browsers to autofill with saved credentials and allows assistive technologies to render purpose icons, reducing cognitive load for users with memory or attention disabilities. The `autocomplete="off"` value explicitly disables autofill and is a WCAG 1.3.5 failure when the field collects personal user data. Testing validates both the presence and semantic correctness of the token. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 1.3.5 autocomplete token audit
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Valid tokens from HTML 5.3 § 4.10.18.7
const VALID_AUTOCOMPLETE_TOKENS = new Set([
  'name', 'honorific-prefix', 'given-name', 'additional-name', 'family-name',
  'honorific-suffix', 'nickname', 'username', 'new-password', 'current-password',
  'one-time-code', 'organization-title', 'organization', 'street-address',
  'address-line1', 'address-line2', 'address-line3', 'address-level4',
  'address-level3', 'address-level2', 'address-level1', 'country',
  'country-name', 'postal-code', 'cc-name', 'cc-given-name', 'cc-additional-name',
  'cc-family-name', 'cc-number', 'cc-exp', 'cc-exp-month', 'cc-exp-year',
  'cc-csc', 'cc-type', 'transaction-currency', 'transaction-amount',
  'language', 'bday', 'bday-day', 'bday-month', 'bday-year', 'sex',
  'url', 'photo', 'tel', 'tel-country-code', 'tel-national',
  'tel-area-code', 'tel-local', 'tel-extension', 'impp', 'email',
]);

test('WCAG 1.3.5 — user-data inputs carry valid autocomplete tokens', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/register');

  const violations = await page.evaluate((validTokens) => {
    const inputs = Array.from(
      document.querySelectorAll<HTMLInputElement>(
        'input[type="text"], input[type="email"], input[type="tel"], ' +
        'input[type="password"], input[type="date"], input[name*="name"], ' +
        'input[name*="email"], input[name*="phone"], input[name*="address"]'
      )
    );
    return inputs.flatMap(input => {
      const ac = (input.getAttribute('autocomplete') ?? '').toLowerCase().trim();
      // Split compound tokens like "shipping street-address"
      const tokens = ac.split(/\s+/).filter(t => t.length > 0 && t !== 'on');
      const semanticToken = tokens[tokens.length - 1]; // last token is the field type
      if (ac === 'off') {
        return [{ name: input.name, type: input.type, autocomplete: ac, issue: 'autocomplete=off disables autofill (WCAG 1.3.5 failure)' }];
      }
      if (!semanticToken || !validTokens.includes(semanticToken)) {
        return [{ name: input.name, type: input.type, autocomplete: ac, issue: 'missing or invalid token' }];
      }
      return [];
    });
  }, [...VALID_AUTOCOMPLETE_TOKENS]);

  expect(
    violations,
    `WCAG 1.3.5 autocomplete violations:\n` +
    violations.map(v => `  input[name="${v.name}"] type="${v.type}" autocomplete="${v.autocomplete}" — ${v.issue}`).join('\n')
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The `autocomplete="new-password"` token is a deliberate exception: it prevents password managers from autofilling a "create new password" field with the user's current password. This is intentional and WCAG-conformant; add `new-password` to a test allowlist when checking password fields. Also, React form libraries (Formik, react-hook-form) and UI kits sometimes set `autocomplete="off"` on their internal composite components (date pickers, phone-number inputs with prefix selectors) to prevent double-autofill — audit these case by case rather than blanket-failing them. [official]

### Pattern 187 — WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text: 200% Browser Zoom — No Loss of Content or Clipping [official]

WCAG 1.4.4 (Level AA) requires that all text remains readable and functional when the user's browser zoom is at 200% — no text clipping, no overflow-hidden containers that truncate text, no broken form controls, and no buttons that shrink to zero size. Fixed-pixel heights (`height: 48px`) on containers that hold text are the primary failure vector: the text grows with zoom but the container does not, causing either overflow-hidden clipping or text escape. Viewport-unit font sizes (`font-size: 2vw`) are another common failure because they scale with viewport width, not zoom level. Testing sets the browser viewport to simulate 200% zoom and verifies no scrollbars or clipping appear. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 1.4.4 text resize at 200% zoom
import { test, expect, Browser } from '@playwright/test';

// Simulating 200% zoom: set viewport to half its normal size so the page
// renders as if the user has zoomed in to 200%.
// Normal desktop viewport: 1280×720. At 200% zoom: 640×360.
const ZOOM_200_VIEWPORT = { width: 640, height: 360 };

test('WCAG 1.4.4 — no text clipping or horizontal scroll at 200% zoom', async ({ browser }: { browser: Browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: ZOOM_200_VIEWPORT });
  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto('/');

  // Check for horizontal scrollbar (indicates content escaped its container)
  const hasHorizontalScroll = await page.evaluate(() =>
    document.documentElement.scrollWidth > document.documentElement.clientWidth
  );
  expect(hasHorizontalScroll, 'No horizontal scrollbar should appear at 200% zoom equivalent').toBe(false);

  // Check for overflow-hidden containers that clip visible text
  const clippedTextContainers = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const all = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('*'));
    return all
      .filter(el => {
        const style = getComputedStyle(el);
        const isClipped = style.overflow === 'hidden' || style.overflowY === 'hidden';
        if (!isClipped) return false;
        return el.scrollHeight > el.clientHeight + 4; // +4px tolerance
      })
      .map(el => ({
        tag: el.tagName,
        class: el.className.toString().slice(0, 60),
        scrollHeight: el.scrollHeight,
        clientHeight: el.clientHeight,
      }))
      .slice(0, 10); // cap at 10 for readability
  });

  expect(
    clippedTextContainers,
    `Found overflow-hidden containers that clip content at 200% zoom:\n` +
    clippedTextContainers.map(c => `  <${c.tag} class="${c.class}"> scrollH=${c.scrollHeight} clientH=${c.clientHeight}`).join('\n')
  ).toHaveLength(0);

  await context.close();
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The half-viewport simulation is the standard approach for emulating 200% zoom in Playwright (which does not support `page.setZoomLevel()`). However, some responsive frameworks shift to a mobile layout at 640px width, which may actually reflow content better than the desktop layout would at 200% zoom — producing a false-pass. For thoroughness, also test at 1280px viewport with CSS `zoom: 2` injected via `page.addStyleTag({ content: 'html { zoom: 2; }' })` and verify scrollWidth is still within bounds. The `scrollHeight > clientHeight` overflow check generates many false positives on intentionally scrollable regions (code blocks, data tables) — add a selector exclusion list for `pre`, `code`, and `[role="grid"]` containers. [official]

---

### Pattern 188 — WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow: 320 CSS Pixel Width — No Two-Dimensional Scrolling [official]

WCAG 1.4.10 (Level AA) requires that content can be presented without loss of information or functionality and without requiring scrolling in two dimensions at a width of 320 CSS pixels (equivalent to 400% zoom on a 1280px-wide viewport). Tables, code blocks, and complex data visualizations are explicitly excepted when two-dimensional layout is essential to their meaning. All other content — navigation, forms, article text, card grids — must reflow into a single-column layout without horizontal scroll. The test viewport is `320×256px` (matching the WCAG technical note for 320 CSS pixel width at standard aspect ratio). [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 1.4.10 reflow at 320px width
import { test, expect, Browser } from '@playwright/test';

const REFLOW_VIEWPORT = { width: 320, height: 256 };

test.describe('WCAG 1.4.10 — Reflow at 320px width', () => {
  let context: import('@playwright/test').BrowserContext;

  test.beforeAll(async ({ browser }: { browser: Browser }) => {
    context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: REFLOW_VIEWPORT });
  });
  test.afterAll(() => context.close());

  for (const route of ['/', '/contact', '/products', '/checkout']) {
    test(`no horizontal scroll on ${route}`, async () => {
      const page = await context.newPage();
      await page.goto(route);

      const overflows = await page.evaluate(() => {
        // Check every block-level element for horizontal overflow
        const blocks = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(
          'main, section, article, nav, header, footer, form, div, ul, ol'
        ));
        const viewportWidth = window.innerWidth;
        return blocks
          .filter(el => {
            const box = el.getBoundingClientRect();
            // Element extends beyond viewport right edge
            return box.right > viewportWidth + 1;
          })
          .map(el => ({
            tag: el.tagName,
            id: el.id,
            class: el.className.toString().slice(0, 50),
            right: Math.round(el.getBoundingClientRect().right),
          }))
          .slice(0, 5);
      });

      expect(
        overflows,
        `Horizontal overflow at 320px on ${route}:\n` +
        overflows.map(o => `  <${o.tag} id="${o.id}" class="${o.class}"> right=${o.right}px`).join('\n')
      ).toHaveLength(0);

      await page.close();
    });
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Data tables, code samples, and multi-column spreadsheets are the official WCAG 1.4.10 exceptions — but CSS frameworks that use `<table>` for layout or responsive grids that degrade to tables at breakpoints will generate false positives. Add an exclusion for `table`, `pre`, and `canvas` elements in the overflow check. Also, Playwright's `getBoundingClientRect()` returns `right` relative to the current scroll position in some browsers — always call `page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0,0))` before measuring to ensure all measurements are taken from the same scroll origin. [official]

---

### Pattern 189 — WCAG 3.2.6 Consistent Help: Help Mechanism Position Constancy Across Pages [official]

WCAG 3.2.6 (Level A, WCAG 2.2) requires that when a set of pages includes a help mechanism — a human contact link, a chatbot trigger, a FAQs link, an inline "?" tooltip trigger — that mechanism appears in the same relative order in the page's DOM and visual layout on every page where it appears. The criterion is about serial order in the content, not pixel position; responsive layout changes are permitted if the user's action (zoom, orientation change) caused the shift. The practical test is: scrape the DOM order of the help element relative to a stable landmark (e.g., the primary navigation), and assert that this relative position is the same on all pages that carry the help element. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 3.2.6 consistent help position
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const PAGES_WITH_HELP = ['/', '/products', '/checkout', '/account'];

async function getHelpRelativePosition(page: import('@playwright/test').Page): Promise<number | null> {
  return page.evaluate(() => {
    // Find the help trigger — adjust selector to match your implementation
    const help = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(
      '[data-help-trigger], [aria-label*="help" i], a[href*="help"], a[href*="faq" i], button[aria-label*="support" i]'
    );
    if (!help) return null;

    // Count its DOM position relative to the body's flat children order
    const allInteractives = Array.from(
      document.querySelectorAll('a[href], button, [role="button"]')
    );
    return allInteractives.indexOf(help);
  });
}

test('WCAG 3.2.6 — help mechanism appears in consistent DOM position across pages', async ({ page }) => {
  const positions: Record<string, number | null> = {};

  for (const route of PAGES_WITH_HELP) {
    await page.goto(route);
    positions[route] = await getHelpRelativePosition(page);
  }

  // Filter to pages where help exists
  const presentPages = Object.entries(positions).filter(([, pos]) => pos !== null);
  if (presentPages.length < 2) { test.skip(); return; }

  const firstPos = presentPages[0][1]!;
  for (const [route, pos] of presentPages) {
    expect(
      pos,
      `Help mechanism is at DOM position ${pos} on ${route} but ${firstPos} on ${presentPages[0][0]} — position must be consistent (WCAG 3.2.6)`
    ).toBe(firstPos);
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Counting absolute DOM index is fragile — a page with one extra navigation link before the help button will shift the index even if the visual/relative position is unchanged. A more robust measure is the count of interactive elements in the same section (e.g., only within `<footer>`) before the help element, or asserting that the help element appears after the `<main>` landmark and before a specific footer copyright text on every page. The test above is a starting-point approximation; tune the anchor selector and measurement scope to your specific layout. [official]

---

### Pattern 190 — `scrollable-region-focusable`: Keyboard Access to Overflow-Scroll Containers [official]

The axe-core rule `scrollable-region-focusable` fires when an element has `overflow: scroll` or `overflow: auto` with content that overflows, but neither the element nor any of its descendants are keyboard-reachable — meaning keyboard users cannot scroll that region. The fix is to add `tabindex="0"` to the scrollable container so keyboard users can focus it and then use arrow keys to scroll. The rule fires even if the container has focusable children (e.g., links inside a scrollable `<div>`) because the children's focus does not itself scroll the container in all browsers. The rule does not fire on `<body>` (always scrollable by keyboard) or on elements with `overflow: hidden`. [official]

```typescript
// playwright + axe — scrollable-region-focusable
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('axe scrollable-region-focusable — all scrollable containers are keyboard-reachable', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  // Ensure any lazy-loaded panels are visible before scanning
  await page.getByRole('main').waitFor({ state: 'visible' });

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withRules(['scrollable-region-focusable'])
    .analyze();

  expect(
    results.violations,
    `scrollable-region-focusable violations:\n` +
    results.violations.flatMap(v =>
      v.nodes.map(n => `  ${n.target.join(' ')} — ${n.failureSummary}`)
    ).join('\n')
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});

test('manual: custom scrollable panels accept keyboard focus and scroll', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  // Locate all containers with explicit tabindex=0 indicating scrollable regions
  const scrollPanels = page.locator('[tabindex="0"][style*="overflow"], [tabindex="0"].scroll-region');
  const count = await scrollPanels.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const panel = scrollPanels.nth(i);
    await panel.focus();
    const isFocused = await page.evaluate((el) => document.activeElement === el, await panel.elementHandle());
    expect(isFocused, `Scrollable panel ${i} must accept keyboard focus`).toBe(true);
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Adding `tabindex="0"` to every scrollable container adds stop points in the Tab order that may frustrate users who are navigating past a long code block or a data table — they must Tab through the container focus stop to reach the next interactive element. The WCAG-conformant mitigation is to ensure the container is only in the Tab order when it actually overflows (i.e., when there is content beyond the visible area), toggling `tabindex` dynamically with a ResizeObserver. Additionally, the axe rule has a documented false positive on `overflow: auto` containers where `scrollHeight === clientHeight` — content fits and no scrollbar appears — yet the rule still fires in some versions because it checks the CSS property rather than the computed scroll state. Pin `@axe-core/playwright` to a version where this is fixed, or suppress the rule on elements where `scrollHeight <= clientHeight`. [official]

---

### Pattern 191 — Focus Obscured by Sticky Header: Geometry Check with `getBoundingClientRect` [official]

WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum, Level AA, WCAG 2.2) requires that a focused component is not entirely hidden by author-created content (sticky headers, cookie banners, chat widgets). WCAG 2.4.12 (Level AAA) tightens this to "no part" of the focus indicator is hidden. The practical test is: after Tab-focusing each interactive element, compare the element's `getBoundingClientRect().top` against the `getBoundingClientRect().bottom` of any `position: fixed` or `position: sticky` overlay at the top of the viewport. If the overlay's bottom is greater than the focused element's bottom (the element is entirely below the overlay), the criterion is failed. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 2.4.11 focus not fully obscured by sticky header
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 2.4.11 — focused elements are not fully obscured by sticky header', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Find the sticky/fixed header bottom edge
  const headerBottom = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const sticky = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(
      'header[style*="sticky"], header[style*="fixed"], ' +
      '[style*="position: fixed"], [style*="position:fixed"], ' +
      '[style*="position: sticky"], [style*="position:sticky"]'
    ) ?? document.querySelector('header');
    if (!sticky) return 0;
    const computed = getComputedStyle(sticky);
    if (computed.position !== 'fixed' && computed.position !== 'sticky') return 0;
    return sticky.getBoundingClientRect().bottom;
  });

  // Tab through visible interactive elements
  const interactives = await page.locator(
    'a[href]:visible, button:visible, input:visible, select:visible, textarea:visible'
  ).all();

  const obscured: string[] = [];
  for (const el of interactives.slice(0, 30)) { // cap at 30 for performance
    await el.focus();
    const box = await el.boundingBox();
    if (!box) continue;

    // Element is fully obscured if its bottom edge is at or above the header's bottom edge
    if (box.y + box.height <= headerBottom) {
      const label = await el.getAttribute('aria-label') ??
        await el.textContent().then(t => t?.trim().slice(0, 40)) ?? '?';
      obscured.push(`"${label}" (bottom=${Math.round(box.y + box.height)}px, headerBottom=${Math.round(headerBottom)}px)`);
    }
  }

  expect(
    obscured,
    `WCAG 2.4.11 — focused element(s) fully hidden behind sticky header:\n${obscured.map(s => '  ' + s).join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The `position: sticky` offset changes as the user scrolls — an element that is obscured at the top of the page may be fully visible when scrolled to a point where the element is near the centre of the viewport. This test only checks the element's initial rendered position; for a thorough assessment, scroll to each element first (`await el.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()`) and then re-measure. There is a known interaction with smooth-scroll behaviour: if the browser's `scroll-behavior: smooth` is active, `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()` returns before scrolling completes and the bounding-box snapshot is stale. Inject `document.documentElement.style.scrollBehavior = 'auto'` at the start of the test to disable smooth scroll. [official]

---

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 47)

211. **[community] When a custom `role="listbox"` renders its options as `<div>` elements without `role="option"`, axe-core's `aria-required-children` rule correctly reports a violation — but if the team adds `role="option"` to the divs without also adding `aria-selected` (or sets `aria-selected` only on the selected option and omits it on unselected ones), axe passes while screen readers announce every unselected option as "not selectable" rather than "not selected" because the `aria-selected` attribute is entirely missing**: The ARIA spec requires all options in a listbox to have `aria-selected` with an explicit value (`"true"` or `"false"`). When the attribute is absent, the option's selection state is indeterminate — NVDA and JAWS both announce "not selectable" (implying the option cannot be selected) rather than "not selected" (implying it is currently unselected but could be). WHY: Developers add `aria-selected="true"` to the active item and nothing to the others, thinking the default absence of the attribute means "not selected". axe-core does not enforce `aria-selected` presence on all children when at least one child has it, so CI stays green. Always set `aria-selected="false"` explicitly on every unselected option. [community]

212. **[community] Playwright's `page.getByRole('option')` only matches elements inside a `select`, `listbox`, or `combobox` context — using it on a custom `role="option"` element that is a child of a `role="combobox"` wrapper rather than a `role="listbox"` child will often return zero matches, causing the test to skip without failure, and the underlying keyboard contract is never verified**: The `getByRole('option')` locator uses the accessibility tree, which only exposes `option` roles when they are owned by a widget that can have options (like `listbox`). A combobox popup that uses `role="listbox"` to wrap its options will expose them correctly; one that incorrectly uses `role="group"` or no role on the popup container will cause the options to be invisible to `getByRole('option')`. WHY: Tests written as `page.getByRole('option').first()` silently find zero elements if the ARIA ownership is broken, `first()` returns an empty locator, and subsequent assertions on that locator pass vacuously with zero elements evaluated. Use `locator.count()` assertions before chaining `.first()` to guard against empty sets. [community]

213. **[community] The WCAG 2.5.8 target-size spacing exception is commonly misapplied to densely packed icon toolbars — teams measure the 24px spacing circle around each icon button and conclude each circle fits within its allocated grid cell, but they fail to account for the fact that the grid cell padding is part of the button's clickable area only if the `padding` is applied to the `<button>` element itself rather than to a wrapping container**: If a toolbar renders `<div class="icon-cell"><button><svg/></button></div>` and applies `padding: 4px` to `.icon-cell` rather than to `button`, the button's `getBoundingClientRect()` returns only the SVG's 16×16px dimensions — not the padded 24×24px cell. The offset/spacing exception requires that the clickable target itself plus its spacing to the nearest neighbouring target sums to 24px; spacing on a parent wrapper does not count. WHY: Visual inspection shows 4px gaps between icons and developers conclude the 24px rule is met, but the button's hit area is actually 16×16px with no spacing from the button's own boundaries. Move padding inside the `<button>` element, or use `min-width/min-height: 24px` on the button itself. [community]

214. **[community] When axe-core scans a page that uses `<details>/<summary>` for disclosure without JavaScript (relying on native browser behaviour), it sometimes reports a false `aria-required-attr` violation claiming `aria-expanded` is missing on the `<summary>` element — because axe treats `<summary>` as a button with implicit ARIA disclosure semantics and expects `aria-expanded`, even though the native `<details>` element exposes open/closed state via the `open` IDL attribute and browsers map it to the accessibility tree without an explicit `aria-expanded`**: Native `<details>`/`<summary>` elements have built-in accessibility semantics in modern browsers (Chrome 89+, Firefox 49+, Safari 6+). The `<summary>` element maps to a disclosure button with the open/closed state taken from the parent `<details>` `open` attribute — no `aria-expanded` is needed or appropriate. Adding `aria-expanded` to `<summary>` to satisfy axe creates a second, independent state representation that can desync from the native `open` attribute. WHY: Teams suppress the rule site-wide with `disableRules(['aria-required-attr'])` rather than fixing only the false-positive selector, inadvertently hiding genuine `aria-required-attr` violations elsewhere. Use `AxeBuilder.exclude('details summary')` instead of globally disabling the rule. [community]

215. **[community] Playwright's `locator.focus()` does not scroll the element into the viewport before attempting to focus it — and if the element is outside the visible viewport (e.g., in a collapsed accordion section or below the fold in a long page), `focus()` silently succeeds in the DOM (the element gets `document.activeElement` assignment) but the element is not visually focused from the user's perspective, causing visual focus-indicator tests to report "no focus indicator visible" even though one is technically present**: `locator.focus()` is a programmatic DOM `focus()` call, not a keyboard Tab press. It does not trigger scroll-into-view the way keyboard navigation does. A test that calls `await el.focus()` and then `await page.screenshot()` to verify the focus ring is visible may capture a screenshot where the focused element is off-screen, reporting no visible focus ring even though the CSS `:focus-visible` styles are correctly applied. WHY: The test produces false failures on correctly-implemented focus styles, eroding trust in the test suite. Use `await el.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()` followed by `await el.focus()` (or use Playwright's Tab key navigation for the most realistic simulation) before any focus-indicator screenshot assertion. [community]

| ARIA APG Menubar Pattern | Official | https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/ | Left/Right between top-level items; Down to open submenu; Escape to close and return focus; Tab exits menubar entirely; roving tabindex |
| ARIA APG Dialog Pattern | Official | https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/ | aria-modal="true"; focus-on-open to first element; Tab trap; Escape + restore focus; aria-labelledby on dialog container |
| HTML 5.3 § 4.10.18.7 — Autofill field names | Official | https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#autofill-field-names | Canonical token list for autocomplete; compound token ordering (shipping/billing prefix); new-password semantics |
| Playwright — `locator.dragTo()` | Official | https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-drag-to | sourcePosition/targetPosition options; steps for interpolated moves; force flag for bypass; trial mode for actionability checks only |
| Playwright — `browser.newContext({ viewport })` | Official | https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browser#browser-new-context | Viewport sizing for zoom simulation; 320×256 reflow viewport; 640×360 for 200% zoom; context isolation between viewport tests |

## Cycle 48 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 192 — Pointer Cancellation: Up-Event Activation with Click vs. Mousedown [official]

WCAG 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation (Level A) requires that any functionality triggered by a single-pointer action must meet at least one of four conditions: no down-event trigger, abort/undo available, up-reversal possible, or the down-event is essential. The simplest conformant approach is to bind all destructive or irreversible actions to the `click` event (which fires on the up-event when the pointer releases inside the target) rather than to `mousedown` or `pointerdown`. When the user presses the pointer button, moves out of the target area while still holding, and then releases, a `click` event is not fired — meaning the action is automatically cancelled. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 2.5.2 pointer cancellation: verify down-event abort works
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 2.5.2 — pointer cancellation: dragging off a button prevents activation', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  const deleteBtn = page.locator('[data-testid="delete-item-btn"]').first();
  await deleteBtn.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();

  // Get button bounding box so we can drag away
  const box = await deleteBtn.boundingBox();
  expect(box).not.toBeNull();

  const startX = box!.x + box!.width / 2;
  const startY = box!.y + box!.height / 2;

  // Simulate press-and-drag-off: mousedown on the button, move 200px away, mouseup off-target
  await page.mouse.move(startX, startY);
  await page.mouse.down();
  await page.mouse.move(startX + 200, startY + 50, { steps: 10 });
  await page.mouse.up();

  // The delete action must NOT have fired — item should still be present
  const itemCount = await page.locator('[data-testid="cart-item"]').count();
  expect(itemCount, 'Dragging off the delete button must not trigger deletion (WCAG 2.5.2)').toBeGreaterThan(0);
});

test('WCAG 2.5.2 — confirm dialog provides undo path for destructive pointer actions', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  const deleteBtn = page.locator('[data-testid="delete-item-btn"]').first();

  // Click normally — check that either a confirm dialog or undo toast appears
  await deleteBtn.click();

  const confirmDialog = page.locator('[role="alertdialog"], [role="dialog"]');
  const undoToast = page.locator('[data-testid="undo-toast"], .undo-notification');

  const hasConfirm = await confirmDialog.isVisible().catch(() => false);
  const hasUndo = await undoToast.isVisible().catch(() => false);

  expect(
    hasConfirm || hasUndo,
    'Destructive actions must provide a confirm dialog or undo mechanism (WCAG 2.5.2 abort/undo condition)'
  ).toBe(true);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Binding all actions to `click` rather than `mousedown` adds a small perceptible latency for power users who expect instant response — for example, drawing applications or piano-keyboard instruments where the down-event is essential. The "essential" exception in WCAG 2.5.2 covers these cases, but the team must document the exception explicitly. For non-essential actions (form submission, deletion, navigation), defaulting to `click` is always correct. Be aware that `touchstart` is the touch equivalent of `mousedown` — the same pattern applies: bind touch-triggered actions to `touchend` (or use `click` which fires consistently after the touch sequence) rather than `touchstart`. [official]

### Pattern 193 — Motion Actuation: `DeviceMotionEvent` Alternative UI and Disable Mechanism [official]

WCAG 2.5.4 Motion Actuation (Level A) requires that any function triggered by device motion (accelerometer, gyroscope) or user motion (camera gestures) must also be operable via standard UI controls, and users must be able to disable motion sensing to prevent accidental triggering caused by tremors or involuntary movements. Failure F106 covers systems that provide no mechanism to disable motion actuation. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 2.5.4 motion actuation: verify UI alternative and disable option exist
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 2.5.4 — shake-to-undo has a button alternative', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/editor');

  // If the app registers DeviceMotionEvent or DeviceOrientationEvent,
  // an equivalent UI control (e.g. undo button) must exist
  const undoBtn = page.locator('[aria-label*="Undo" i], [data-testid="undo-btn"], button:has-text("Undo")');
  await expect(
    undoBtn.first(),
    'A UI-based undo control must exist alongside any shake-to-undo motion gesture (WCAG 2.5.4)'
  ).toBeVisible();
});

test('WCAG 2.5.4 — motion actuation can be disabled in application settings', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings');

  // Look for a motion/gesture disable toggle — required by WCAG 2.5.4 failure F106
  const motionToggle = page.locator(
    '[data-testid="disable-motion"], ' +
    '[aria-label*="motion" i], ' +
    'label:has-text("motion"), ' +
    'label:has-text("shake"), ' +
    'label:has-text("gesture")'
  );

  const hasMotionSetting = await motionToggle.count();

  // If the app uses motion events (checked via script injection), a disable option must exist
  const usesMotionEvents = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return typeof (window as any).__motionEnabled !== 'undefined' ||
      document.documentElement.dataset.motionEnabled === 'true';
  });

  if (usesMotionEvents) {
    expect(
      hasMotionSetting,
      'App using DeviceMotionEvent must provide a user-accessible toggle to disable it (WCAG 2.5.4 / F106)'
    ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  }
});

test('WCAG 2.5.4 — prefers-reduced-motion media query is respected', async ({ page }) => {
  // Emulate reduced-motion OS preference — apps must also honour this for motion actuation
  await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
  await page.goto('/editor');

  const hasAutoDisabledMotion = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const mq = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)');
    return mq.matches;
  });

  expect(hasAutoDisabledMotion, 'prefers-reduced-motion should be honoured in motion-actuation context').toBe(true);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` addresses animation and transition motion but is not technically the same as disabling sensor-based motion actuation — a user may want animations but still have a tremor that causes accidental shake-to-undo triggering. The in-app disable toggle serves a different population from the OS-level preference, so both must be provided independently. Additionally, the `DeviceMotionEvent` permission prompt (required by browsers following the Generic Sensor API permissions model) can itself be a barrier — users who dismiss the permission prompt may inadvertently disable motion features entirely with no UI fallback visible. [official]
