### Pattern 194 — ARIA Combobox: `aria-activedescendant` vs. DOM Focus Management [official]

ARIA combobox implementations must choose between two focus management strategies: moving DOM focus into the listbox popup (true DOM focus), or keeping DOM focus on the input while using `aria-activedescendant` to point to the currently highlighted option. The `aria-activedescendant` pattern is preferred because it allows the screen reader to announce option labels while the user continues typing in the input — moving DOM focus to the listbox breaks typing. The `aria-controls` attribute (not deprecated `aria-owns`) must reference the popup container element. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — ARIA combobox: aria-activedescendant and aria-expanded keyboard contract
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('combobox aria-expanded toggles correctly and popup appears', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');

  const combobox = page.locator('[role="combobox"]');
  await combobox.focus();

  // Initially collapsed
  await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

  // Type to trigger suggestions
  await combobox.type('app');
  await page.waitForTimeout(300); // debounce

  await expect(combobox, 'aria-expanded must be true when popup is visible').toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

  const listboxId = await combobox.getAttribute('aria-controls');
  expect(listboxId, 'aria-controls must reference the popup element').toBeTruthy();

  const listbox = page.locator(`#${listboxId}`);
  await expect(listbox, 'popup referenced by aria-controls must be visible').toBeVisible();
});

test('combobox arrow keys update aria-activedescendant without moving DOM focus', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');

  const combobox = page.locator('[role="combobox"]');
  await combobox.focus();
  await combobox.type('app');
  await page.waitForTimeout(300);

  // Press ArrowDown to highlight first option
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');

  const activeDescendant = await combobox.getAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
  expect(activeDescendant, 'aria-activedescendant must be set after ArrowDown').toBeTruthy();

  // DOM focus must remain on the combobox input, not move to the option
  const focusedRole = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role'));
  expect(focusedRole, 'DOM focus must stay on combobox input, not move to option').toBe('combobox');

  // The referenced option must have aria-selected="true"
  const activeOption = page.locator(`#${activeDescendant}`);
  await expect(activeOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
});

test('combobox Escape dismisses popup and clears aria-activedescendant', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');
  const combobox = page.locator('[role="combobox"]');
  await combobox.focus();
  await combobox.type('app');
  await page.waitForTimeout(300);
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');

  await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  const activeDescendant = await combobox.getAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
  expect(activeDescendant ?? '', 'aria-activedescendant must be cleared after Escape').toBe('');
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `aria-activedescendant` requires that the referenced element exists in the DOM at the time the attribute is set — virtual scrolling that removes off-screen option elements from the DOM will break screen reader announcement because the referenced ID no longer resolves to a real element. Teams using virtual lists inside combobox popups must either pre-render all options (expensive for large datasets), use a windowed DOM with the currently-active option always present, or switch to true DOM focus management into the visible portion of the virtual list. [official]

---

### Pattern 195 — WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance: 2 CSS Pixel Perimeter Area Calculation [official]

WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (Level AAA, WCAG 2.2) requires that the focus indicator area is at least as large as the area of a 2 CSS pixel thick perimeter of the unfocused component, AND that the indicator has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 between focused and unfocused states. The perimeter area equals 2 × (width + height) × 2px thickness = 4 × (width + height) square CSS pixels. A single 2px solid outline satisfies this requirement for any rectangular component because `outline` draws outside the border-box. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 2.4.13 focus appearance: geometry and contrast check
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 2.4.13 — focus indicator area meets 2px perimeter minimum', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const buttons = page.locator('button:visible, a[href]:visible').first();
  await buttons.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();

  // Focus the element
  await buttons.focus();

  // Get focus indicator geometry via computed styles
  const focusStyles = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const el = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('button:focus-visible, a:focus-visible');
    if (!el) return null;
    const styles = getComputedStyle(el);
    return {
      outlineWidth: parseFloat(styles.outlineWidth),
      outlineOffset: parseFloat(styles.outlineOffset),
      outlineStyle: styles.outlineStyle,
      outlineColor: styles.outlineColor,
      borderWidth: parseFloat(styles.borderWidth),
    };
  });

  if (focusStyles) {
    // Minimum: outline-width >= 2px, or equivalent border change
    const totalIndicatorWidth = (focusStyles.outlineStyle !== 'none')
      ? focusStyles.outlineWidth
      : focusStyles.borderWidth;

    expect(
      totalIndicatorWidth,
      `WCAG 2.4.13: focus indicator must be at least 2 CSS pixels wide (got ${totalIndicatorWidth}px)`
    ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
  }
});

test('WCAG 2.4.13 — focus indicator has visible contrast change', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  const btn = page.locator('button:visible').first();
  await btn.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();

  // Capture unfocused state
  const unfocusedScreenshot = await btn.screenshot();

  await btn.focus();

  // Capture focused state
  const focusedScreenshot = await btn.screenshot();

  // Screenshots must differ — pixel-identical result means no focus indicator
  expect(
    Buffer.compare(unfocusedScreenshot, focusedScreenshot),
    'WCAG 2.4.13: focused state screenshot must differ from unfocused (focus indicator must be visible)'
  ).not.toBe(0);
});

test('WCAG 2.4.13 — outline is not removed via CSS reset', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const outlineReset = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const styleSheets = Array.from(document.styleSheets);
    const violations: string[] = [];
    for (const sheet of styleSheets) {
      try {
        const rules = Array.from(sheet.cssRules ?? []);
        for (const rule of rules) {
          if (rule instanceof CSSStyleRule) {
            if (rule.style.outline === 'none' || rule.style.outline === '0') {
              violations.push(`${rule.selectorText}: outline: ${rule.style.outline}`);
            }
          }
        }
      } catch { /* cross-origin stylesheet */ }
    }
    return violations.slice(0, 5);
  });

  if (outlineReset.length > 0) {
    console.warn(`WCAG 2.4.13 warning — outline reset rules found (verify custom focus styles compensate):\n${outlineReset.join('\n')}`);
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The 2px perimeter area calculation can be satisfied by outlines, box shadows, background-color changes, or border changes — as long as the area of changed pixels covers the minimum and the contrast change is at least 3:1. A common false pass: using `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #005fcc` achieves the geometry requirement but if the background under the shadow is close in luminance to `#005fcc`, the contrast ratio may be below 3:1. Always measure the contrast ratio between the shadow colour and the colour directly adjacent to the shadow (which is the element's own background, not the page background). [official]

---

### Pattern 196 — WCAG 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus: Tooltip Dismissal and Hover Persistence [official]

WCAG 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (Level AA) requires that additional content appearing on hover or focus meets three conditions: dismissible (can be dismissed without moving hover or focus, typically via Escape), hoverable (pointer can move onto the appeared content without it disappearing), and persistent (content stays until the user removes hover/focus or dismisses it). The most common failure is a tooltip that vanishes when the pointer moves slightly away from the trigger element before reaching the tooltip. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 1.4.13 tooltip: hoverable, dismissible, persistent
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 1.4.13 — tooltip remains visible when pointer moves onto it', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/help');

  const trigger = page.locator('[data-tooltip], [aria-describedby], [title]').first();
  await trigger.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
  await trigger.hover();

  // Tooltip should appear
  const tooltip = page.locator('[role="tooltip"]').first();
  await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible({ timeout: 2000 });

  const tooltipBox = await tooltip.boundingBox();
  expect(tooltipBox).not.toBeNull();

  // Move pointer onto the tooltip content — it must remain visible (hoverable condition)
  await page.mouse.move(tooltipBox!.x + tooltipBox!.width / 2, tooltipBox!.y + tooltipBox!.height / 2);
  await page.waitForTimeout(500);

  await expect(
    tooltip,
    'WCAG 1.4.13 hoverable: tooltip must remain visible when pointer moves onto it'
  ).toBeVisible();
});

test('WCAG 1.4.13 — tooltip can be dismissed with Escape without moving focus', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/help');

  const trigger = page.locator('[data-tooltip], [aria-describedby]').first();
  await trigger.focus();

  const tooltip = page.locator('[role="tooltip"]').first();
  await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible({ timeout: 2000 });

  // Dismiss with Escape — focus must remain on the trigger element
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');

  await expect(
    tooltip,
    'WCAG 1.4.13 dismissible: Escape key must dismiss tooltip without moving focus'
  ).toBeHidden();

  expect(
    await trigger.evaluate(el => el === document.activeElement),
    'Focus must remain on trigger element after Escape dismisses tooltip'
  ).toBe(true);
});

test('WCAG 1.4.13 — tooltip content persists without time limit', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/help');

  const trigger = page.locator('[data-tooltip]').first();
  await trigger.hover();

  const tooltip = page.locator('[role="tooltip"]').first();
  await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible({ timeout: 2000 });

  // Wait 3 seconds — tooltip must not auto-dismiss
  await page.waitForTimeout(3000);

  await expect(
    tooltip,
    'WCAG 1.4.13 persistent: tooltip must not auto-dismiss while hover is maintained'
  ).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The `title` HTML attribute creates browser-native tooltips that are exempt from WCAG 1.4.13 because they are user-agent controlled — but native `title` tooltips are notoriously inaccessible: they do not appear on keyboard focus in most browsers, do not work on touch devices, and cannot be styled for low-vision users. Teams that replace `title` with a custom `[role="tooltip"]` gain control but take on the obligation to implement all three WCAG 1.4.13 conditions themselves. A common shortcut that fails: using CSS-only tooltips (`:hover::before` pseudo-elements) — these cannot be reached by pointer hover (the pseudo-element does not itself trigger pointer events), so the "hoverable" condition fails. [official]

---

### Pattern 197 — ARIA Live Regions: `aria-live="polite"` Announcement Timing and `aria-atomic` [official]

ARIA live regions (`aria-live="polite"` or `role="status"`) must be present in the DOM before content is injected into them — screen readers register the live region on page load and then monitor it for changes. Injecting the live region element and simultaneously setting its text content in the same JavaScript tick produces no announcement because the browser/AT has not yet registered the live region. The `aria-atomic="true"` attribute instructs the screen reader to announce the entire region's content whenever any part changes, preventing partial announcements when multiple child nodes are updated. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — ARIA live region announcement timing
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('live region is present in DOM before content changes', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/form');

  // Live region must already exist in DOM (empty) before any interaction
  const liveRegion = page.locator('[aria-live="polite"], [role="status"]').first();
  await expect(
    liveRegion,
    'ARIA live region must be present in DOM on page load, before any dynamic updates'
  ).toBeAttached();
});

test('live region content updates after form submission', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/form');

  const liveRegion = page.locator('[aria-live="polite"], [role="status"]').first();

  // Submit form to trigger a status update
  await page.locator('form').locator('button[type="submit"]').click();

  // Live region content should change
  await expect(liveRegion).not.toBeEmpty({ timeout: 3000 });
});

test('assertive live region is empty on normal page load', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/form');

  // aria-live="assertive" should not be used for routine status updates
  const assertiveRegions = page.locator('[aria-live="assertive"]:not([role="alert"])');
  const count = await assertiveRegions.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const region = assertiveRegions.nth(i);
    const content = await region.textContent();
    expect(
      content?.trim() ?? '',
      `Assertive live region must be empty on initial load — not for routine messages`
    ).toBe('');
  }
});

test('multi-child live regions declare aria-atomic="true"', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/cart');

  const statusRegions = page.locator('[role="status"], [aria-live="polite"]');
  const regionCount = await statusRegions.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < regionCount; i++) {
    const region = statusRegions.nth(i);
    const childCount = await region.locator('*').count();

    if (childCount > 1) {
      const atomic = await region.getAttribute('aria-atomic');
      expect(
        atomic,
        `Live region with ${childCount} children should have aria-atomic="true" for complete announcements`
      ).toBe('true');
    }
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `aria-atomic="true"` causes the entire region to be re-read on any change, including trivial updates. For a region that shows a character count ("120 characters remaining") updated on every keystroke, `aria-atomic="true"` combined with `aria-live="polite"` means the screen reader queues an announcement after each keystroke — resulting in a backlog of queued announcements that fire after the user stops typing. For frequently-updated regions, use `aria-live="off"` with a debounced manual announcement injected into a separate, initially-empty announcement container, or use a `role="status"` region with a 500ms debounce on the update. [official]

---

### Pattern 198 — WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: UI Component Border and Icon Contrast Testing [official]

WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (Level AA) requires a minimum 3:1 contrast ratio for the visual presentation of UI components (button borders, input field borders, checkbox/radio visual indicators) and graphical objects (icons required for understanding). Unlike WCAG 1.4.3 (text contrast, 4.5:1 AA), the threshold for UI components is 3:1 and the measurement is made against the adjacent colour, not the overall background. Inactive/disabled components are exempt. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast: form control and icon checks
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('WCAG 1.4.11 — axe-core catches non-text contrast failures', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/form');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
    .include('form')
    .analyze();

  const contrastViolations = results.violations.filter(v =>
    v.id === 'color-contrast' || v.id === 'color-contrast-enhanced'
  );

  expect(
    contrastViolations,
    `WCAG 1.4.11 contrast violations:\n` +
    contrastViolations.flatMap(v =>
      v.nodes.map(n => `  ${n.target.join(' ')} — ${n.failureSummary}`)
    ).join('\n')
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});

test('WCAG 1.4.11 — checkbox contrast values are logged for manual review', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/form');

  const contrastInfo = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const el = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input[type="checkbox"]');
    if (!el) return null;
    const styles = getComputedStyle(el);
    const parentStyles = getComputedStyle(el.parentElement!);
    return {
      borderColor: styles.borderColor,
      backgroundColor: styles.backgroundColor,
      parentBackground: parentStyles.backgroundColor,
      accentColor: styles.accentColor,
    };
  });

  // Log for manual contrast ratio verification (3:1 required against adjacent colour)
  if (contrastInfo) {
    console.log('Checkbox colours for WCAG 1.4.11 manual check:', contrastInfo);
  }
  expect(contrastInfo, 'Checkbox element must be present for contrast check').not.toBeNull();
});

test('WCAG 1.4.11 — SVG icons are either decorative or have accessible names', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const svgIcons = page.locator('svg');
  const count = await svgIcons.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 20); i++) {
    const icon = svgIcons.nth(i);
    const ariaHidden = await icon.getAttribute('aria-hidden');
    const ariaLabel = await icon.getAttribute('aria-label');
    const titleCount = await icon.locator('title').count();

    const isDecorative = ariaHidden === 'true';
    const isNamed = !!(ariaLabel || titleCount > 0);

    expect(
      isDecorative || isNamed,
      `SVG icon ${i} must be decorative (aria-hidden="true") or have an accessible name (WCAG 1.4.11 / 4.1.2)`
    ).toBe(true);
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The 3:1 threshold for UI component borders is measured specifically between the border colour and the colour immediately adjacent to it — a text-input with a light grey border (`#767676`) against a white background satisfies 3:1 (4.6:1), but the same border against a light cream background (`#f5f5f5`) drops to roughly 2.5:1, failing the criterion. axe-core's `color-contrast` rule covers text contrast but has limited detection for UI component border contrast (it does not inspect `border-color` against adjacent page colours). Manual inspection or a dedicated contrast analysis tool (e.g. Colour Contrast Analyser desktop application) is required for thorough WCAG 1.4.11 coverage beyond what axe-core provides. [official]

---

### Pattern 199 — WCAG 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced): Zero-Pixel Overlap Check [official]

WCAG 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured Enhanced (Level AAA, WCAG 2.2) tightens the Level AA criterion 2.4.11: no part (rather than not entirely) of the focused component may be hidden by author-created content. In practice this means sticky elements must not overlap the focused element at all — even one pixel of overlap is a failure. The test strategy is the same as Pattern 191 (getBoundingClientRect comparison) but the threshold changes from "entirely hidden" to "any overlap". [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 2.4.12 (AAA) focus not obscured enhanced: zero overlap check
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 2.4.12 — no part of focused element is hidden by sticky overlays', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Collect all sticky/fixed overlays
  const stickyOverlays = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const overlays: Array<{ top: number; bottom: number; left: number; right: number; selector: string }> = [];
    document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('*').forEach(el => {
      const computed = getComputedStyle(el);
      if (computed.position === 'fixed' || computed.position === 'sticky') {
        const box = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        if (box.width > 0 && box.height > 0) {
          overlays.push({
            top: box.top, bottom: box.bottom,
            left: box.left, right: box.right,
            selector: el.tagName + (el.id ? `#${el.id}` : '')
          });
        }
      }
    });
    return overlays;
  });

  const interactives = await page.locator(
    'a[href]:visible, button:visible, input:visible, select:visible, textarea:visible, [tabindex="0"]:visible'
  ).all();

  const partiallyObscured: string[] = [];

  for (const el of interactives.slice(0, 25)) {
    await el.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
    await el.focus();
    const box = await el.boundingBox();
    if (!box) continue;

    for (const overlay of stickyOverlays) {
      // Any overlap is a WCAG 2.4.12 failure
      const overlapX = box.x < overlay.right && (box.x + box.width) > overlay.left;
      const overlapY = box.y < overlay.bottom && (box.y + box.height) > overlay.top;

      if (overlapX && overlapY) {
        const label = await el.getAttribute('aria-label') ??
          await el.textContent().then(t => t?.trim().slice(0, 30)) ?? '?';
        partiallyObscured.push(`"${label}" overlaps with ${overlay.selector}`);
      }
    }
  }

  expect(
    partiallyObscured,
    `WCAG 2.4.12 (AAA) — focused element(s) partially hidden by sticky overlay:\n${partiallyObscured.map(s => '  ' + s).join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** WCAG 2.4.12 is Level AAA and not required for AA conformance claims — but testing against it is valuable because it catches partially-obscured focus states invisible to keyboard users relying on visible focus indicators. The most common false positives arise from zero-height fixed elements (e.g. `position: fixed; height: 0` notification bars that grow dynamically) — their `getBoundingClientRect()` returns `height: 0` and the overlap check never triggers. Test after overlays have rendered at full height by scrolling to a mid-page position before running the focus loop. [official]

---

### Pattern 200 — WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name: Accessible Name Must Contain the Visible Label Text [official]

WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name (Level A) requires that for UI components with visible text labels, the accessible name contains the visible label text as a substring. This is essential for speech-control users (Dragon NaturallySpeaking) who speak the visible label to activate a control — if the accessible name does not contain the visible text, the voice command fails silently. The most common violation: `<button aria-label="Close dialog"><span>X</span></button>` where speech users say "click X" but the accessible name is "Close dialog". The fix is to ensure `aria-label` starts with or contains the visible text. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 2.5.3 label in name: accessible name contains visible text
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('WCAG 2.5.3 — axe-core label-content-name-mismatch rule passes', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag21a'])
    .analyze();

  const labelInNameViolations = results.violations.filter(v => v.id === 'label-content-name-mismatch');

  expect(
    labelInNameViolations,
    `WCAG 2.5.3 label-in-name violations:\n` +
    labelInNameViolations.flatMap(v =>
      v.nodes.map(n => `  ${n.target.join(' ')} — ${n.failureSummary}`)
    ).join('\n')
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});

test('WCAG 2.5.3 — icon buttons with visible text have matching accessible names', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const buttons = page.locator('button:visible');
  const count = await buttons.count();
  const violations: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 30); i++) {
    const btn = buttons.nth(i);
    const visibleText = (await btn.textContent())?.trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ') ?? '';
    const ariaLabel = await btn.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? '';

    if (visibleText && ariaLabel) {
      // WCAG 2.5.3: aria-label must contain the visible text (case-insensitive)
      if (!ariaLabel.toLowerCase().includes(visibleText.toLowerCase())) {
        violations.push(`Button "${visibleText.slice(0, 30)}" has aria-label "${ariaLabel}" — does not contain visible text`);
      }
    }
  }

  expect(
    violations,
    `WCAG 2.5.3 label-in-name failures:\n${violations.map(v => '  ' + v).join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The WCAG 2.5.3 specification allows the accessible name to be a superset of the visible label (e.g., `aria-label="Delete item: Shopping cart"` for a button with visible text "Delete item" is conformant), but many implementations get the order wrong: `aria-label="Shopping cart: Delete item"` fails because speech users say "click Delete item" and the voice control engine searches for an exact match at the start of the accessible name. The safest pattern is to start the `aria-label` with the visible text verbatim, then add context after a separator: `aria-label="Delete item — Shopping cart"`. [official]

---

### Pattern 201 — `AxeBuilder.withTags`: Scoping Automated Scans to Specific WCAG Levels [official]

`@axe-core/playwright`'s `withTags()` method accepts WCAG level tags (`wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21aa`, `wcag22aa`, `best-practice`) to scope a scan to only rules applicable to a specific conformance claim. Running `withTags(['wcag22aa'])` enables all WCAG 2.2 Level AA rules. Combining tags runs the union of rules: `withTags(['wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])` runs all AA rules across WCAG versions 2.0, 2.1, and 2.2. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — @axe-core/playwright tag-scoped scans with structured violation output
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

function formatViolations(violations: Awaited<ReturnType<AxeBuilder['analyze']>>['violations']) {
  return violations.map(v =>
    `[${v.id}] ${v.description} (impact: ${v.impact})\n` +
    v.nodes.slice(0, 3).map(n =>
      `    target: ${n.target.join(' ')}\n    fix: ${n.failureSummary?.slice(0, 120) ?? 'N/A'}`
    ).join('\n')
  ).join('\n\n');
}

test('WCAG 2.2 AA full-page scan with structured violation output', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
    .analyze();

  expect(
    results.violations,
    `WCAG 2.2 AA violations found:\n\n${formatViolations(results.violations)}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});

test('best-practice rules audit alongside WCAG AA', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2aa', 'best-practice'])
    .analyze();

  const wcagViolations = results.violations.filter(v => !v.tags.includes('best-practice'));
  const bpViolations = results.violations.filter(v => v.tags.includes('best-practice'));

  expect(
    wcagViolations,
    `WCAG AA required violations:\n${formatViolations(wcagViolations)}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);

  if (bpViolations.length > 0) {
    console.warn(`[Accessibility best-practice warnings]:\n${formatViolations(bpViolations)}`);
  }
});

test('critical-flow WCAG 2.2 AA scan: checkout funnel', async ({ page }) => {
  const checkoutSteps = ['/cart', '/checkout/address', '/checkout/payment', '/checkout/confirm'];

  for (const url of checkoutSteps) {
    await page.goto(url);
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
      .exclude('[data-testid="third-party-widget"]')
      .analyze();

    expect(
      results.violations,
      `WCAG 2.2 AA violations on ${url}:\n${formatViolations(results.violations)}`
    ).toHaveLength(0);
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The `wcag22aa` tag only enables axe-core rules that have been implemented for 2.2 criteria — as of axe-core 4.9, not all WCAG 2.2 success criteria have automated rules (e.g. 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size have limited automated coverage). Passing all `wcag22aa` axe rules does not constitute a full WCAG 2.2 AA conformance claim — it is a necessary but not sufficient condition. Always accompany automated scanning with a manual review checklist covering criteria without automated coverage. [official]

---

### Pattern 202 — Keyboard Trap Detection: Tab Cycle Completeness Test [official]

WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap (Level A) requires that if keyboard focus can be moved to a component using a keyboard, focus can also be moved away using only the keyboard. Keyboard traps most commonly occur in: modal dialogs that do not release focus on Escape, third-party embedded widgets (chat, maps), and custom rich-text editors. The Playwright test strategy is to Tab through a fixed number of focusable elements and verify that focus eventually leaves the widget and cycles through distinct elements. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — WCAG 2.1.2 keyboard trap detection
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 2.1.2 — keyboard focus cycles through page without trapping', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const interactiveCount = await page.locator(
    'a[href]:visible, button:visible, input:visible, select:visible, textarea:visible, [tabindex="0"]:visible'
  ).count();

  // Tab through 2x the number of interactive elements to detect traps
  const maxTabs = Math.min(interactiveCount * 2, 100);
  const focusedElements: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < maxTabs; i++) {
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focused = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement;
      if (!el || el === document.body) return 'body';
      return el.tagName + (el.id ? `#${el.id}` : '') +
        (el.className ? `.${String(el.className).split(' ')[0]}` : '');
    });
    focusedElements.push(focused);
  }

  // Trap detection: if focus visits only 1 unique element in the last 10 Tab presses
  const lastTen = focusedElements.slice(-10);
  const uniqueInLastTen = new Set(lastTen).size;

  expect(
    uniqueInLastTen,
    `WCAG 2.1.2: possible keyboard trap — focus repeating same ${uniqueInLastTen} element(s):\n  ${lastTen.join(' → ')}`
  ).toBeGreaterThan(1);
});

test('WCAG 2.1.2 — modal dialog closes on Escape and returns focus to trigger', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const modalTrigger = page.locator('[data-opens-modal], button:has-text("Open"), button:has-text("Dialog")').first();
  if (!(await modalTrigger.isVisible().catch(() => false))) return;

  await modalTrigger.click();
  const modal = page.locator('[role="dialog"]').first();
  await expect(modal).toBeVisible({ timeout: 2000 });

  // Press Escape — modal must close
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(modal).toBeHidden({ timeout: 2000 });

  // Focus must return to the trigger, not be lost to body
  const isTriggerFocused = await modalTrigger.evaluate(el => el === document.activeElement);
  expect(
    isTriggerFocused,
    'WCAG 2.1.2: after Escape closes a dialog, focus must return to the trigger element'
  ).toBe(true);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The tab-cycle completeness test has high false-positive risk on single-page applications that lazy-load content — by the time the loop reaches Tab press 80, new content may have rendered, changing the count of focusable elements and causing the heuristic to fire spuriously. Scope the test to a specific region with `include()` or fix the viewport to prevent lazy loading during the test. For modal dialog trap testing, be aware that the intentional Tab containment inside an open dialog (required by WCAG 2.4 for modal dialogs) is different from a keyboard trap — the dialog Tab containment must release on Escape or explicit close. [official]

---

### Pattern 203 — `page.getByRole` Accessibility Tree Queries in Playwright [official]

Playwright's `page.getByRole()` queries the computed accessibility tree (roles, accessible names, and states) rather than the DOM. This makes role-based locators robust against implementation changes and serves as an accessibility test in itself — if `getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })` matches zero elements, the button is not properly exposed to assistive technologies. Common issues: computed roles differing from explicit roles due to forbidden role/element combinations, and accessible names not being computed as expected. [official]

```typescript
// playwright — getByRole as accessibility tree probe
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('primary action button is exposed with correct role and accessible name', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // getByRole queries the computed accessibility tree — fails if role or name is wrong
  const submitBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit order/i });
  await expect(submitBtn, 'Submit button must have role=button and accessible name containing "Submit order"').toBeVisible();
});

test('main navigation landmark is exposed with accessible name', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // WCAG 2.4.1: bypass blocks — navigation landmark must exist
  const nav = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /main/i });
  await expect(nav, 'Main navigation must have role=navigation and an accessible name').toBeVisible();
});

test('icon buttons without accessible names are detected', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  const unnamedButtons = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const buttons = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('button, [role="button"]'));
    return buttons
      .filter(el => {
        const name = el.getAttribute('aria-label') ??
          el.getAttribute('aria-labelledby') ??
          el.textContent?.trim();
        return !name;
      })
      .map(el => el.outerHTML.slice(0, 80));
  });

  expect(
    unnamedButtons,
    `Buttons without accessible names (violates WCAG 4.1.2):\n${unnamedButtons.map(s => '  ' + s).join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});

test('heading hierarchy is correct and exposed in accessibility tree', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Verify h1 exists (exactly one per page for accessibility)
  const h1s = page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 });
  await expect(h1s, 'Page must have exactly one h1 for screen reader navigation').toHaveCount(1);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `getByRole` uses Playwright's internal accessibility tree snapshot, which may differ from what NVDA or JAWS report because different screen readers use different accessibility APIs (IA2, UIA, ATK/AT-SPI). A `getByRole('button')` match confirms the element is exposed as a button in Chromium's accessibility tree — not necessarily in all screen reader / browser combinations. For comprehensive testing, supplement `getByRole` assertions with screen reader testing on the target browser/AT combinations defined in your test plan. [official]

---

### Pattern 204 — `prefers-reduced-motion`: Respecting OS Animation Preferences [community]

The `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` media query is an OS-level signal that the user has requested reduced motion — typically set by users with vestibular disorders, epilepsy, or motion sensitivity. CSS animations and transitions must either be disabled or significantly reduced when this preference is active. JavaScript-driven animations (GSAP, anime.js, canvas) must also check `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` and skip or substitute safe alternatives. [community]

```typescript
// playwright — prefers-reduced-motion emulation and CSS animation check
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('CSS animations are disabled when prefers-reduced-motion is active', async ({ page }) => {
  // Emulate OS-level reduced motion preference — must be called before page.goto
  await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
  await page.goto('/');

  const animatedElements = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const elements = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('*'));
    const violators: string[] = [];

    for (const el of elements) {
      const styles = getComputedStyle(el);
      const duration = parseFloat(styles.animationDuration);
      const transition = parseFloat(styles.transitionDuration);

      // Animation duration > 10ms or transition > 200ms indicates reduced-motion not honoured
      if (duration > 0.01 || transition > 0.2) {
        const selector = el.tagName + (el.id ? `#${el.id}` : '') +
          (el.className ? `.${String(el.className).split(' ')[0]}` : '');
        violators.push(`${selector}: animation=${duration}s, transition=${transition}s`);
      }
    }
    return violators.slice(0, 10);
  });

  expect(
    animatedElements,
    `prefers-reduced-motion not honoured — elements still animate:\n${animatedElements.map(s => '  ' + s).join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});

test('JS animation frameworks respect reduced-motion preference', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
  await page.goto('/landing');

  const prefersReduced = await page.evaluate(() =>
    window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches
  );
  expect(prefersReduced, 'prefers-reduced-motion emulation must be active').toBe(true);

  const cta = page.locator('[data-testid="hero-cta"]');
  if (await cta.isVisible()) {
    await cta.click();
    await page.waitForTimeout(400);
    const hasAnimationClass = await page.locator('.animating, .is-animated, [data-gsap]').count();
    expect(
      hasAnimationClass,
      'JS animation library must not apply animation classes when reduced-motion is preferred'
    ).toBe(0);
  }
});

test('prefers-reduced-motion CSS custom property is set for component use', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
  await page.goto('/');

  // Some design systems expose a CSS variable for reduced motion
  const motionVar = await page.evaluate(() =>
    getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--motion-duration').trim()
  );

  if (motionVar) {
    const durationMs = parseFloat(motionVar);
    expect(
      durationMs,
      `CSS --motion-duration variable must be 0 or near-0 when reduced-motion is active (got ${motionVar})`
    ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(10);
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Playwright's `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` injects a media query override at the browser level but does not affect JavaScript that reads `prefers-reduced-motion` before the emulation is set — if the page checks the media query at module load time (before Playwright's emulation takes effect), the check will return the default OS value. Always call `emulateMedia` before `page.goto()` to ensure the preference is active at initial script execution. Additionally, `transition-duration: 0.01s` technically meets the CSS reduced-motion pattern but may still cause perceptible flicker for highly sensitive users — aim for `0ms` or `none` when honouring the preference. [community]

---

### Pattern 205 — Table Accessibility: `scope`, `headers`, and Complex Table ARIA [community]

HTML tables used for tabular data require proper header association for screen readers to announce context with each data cell. Simple tables use `<th scope="col">` and `<th scope="row">`. Complex tables with multi-level headers require `scope="colgroup"` / `scope="rowgroup"` or explicit `id`/`headers` attribute pairing. Using `role="grid"` instead of a plain `<table>` invokes the full ARIA grid keyboard contract (arrow key navigation between cells) which must be completely implemented or the widget is broken for keyboard users. [community]

```typescript
// playwright — table accessibility: scope, headers, and layout table detection
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('data tables have proper th[scope] or headers/id association', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2a'])
    .include('table')
    .analyze();

  const tableViolations = results.violations.filter(v =>
    ['td-headers-attr', 'th-has-data-cells', 'scope-attr-valid', 'table-duplicate-name'].includes(v.id)
  );

  expect(
    tableViolations,
    `Table accessibility violations:\n` +
    tableViolations.flatMap(v =>
      v.nodes.map(n => `  [${v.id}] ${n.target.join(' ')} — ${n.failureSummary}`)
    ).join('\n')
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});

test('every th element has scope or id attribute', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports');

  const tableHeaders = page.locator('table th');
  const headerCount = await tableHeaders.count();

  const headersWithoutScope: string[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < headerCount; i++) {
    const th = tableHeaders.nth(i);
    const scope = await th.getAttribute('scope');
    const id = await th.getAttribute('id');
    if (!scope && !id) {
      const text = await th.textContent();
      headersWithoutScope.push(text?.trim().slice(0, 30) ?? `th[${i}]`);
    }
  }

  expect(
    headersWithoutScope,
    `Table headers missing scope or id:\n${headersWithoutScope.map(s => '  ' + s).join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});

test('tables without headers have role="presentation" (layout tables)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const regularTables = page.locator('table:not([role])');
  const count = await regularTables.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const table = regularTables.nth(i);
    const thCount = await table.locator('th').count();
    const captionCount = await table.locator('caption').count();

    if (thCount === 0 && captionCount === 0) {
      const html = await table.evaluate(el => el.outerHTML.slice(0, 100));
      console.warn(`Possible layout table missing role="presentation" — verify intent: ${html}`);
    }
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Adding `role="grid"` to a data table to enable `aria-sort` on column headers brings in the full ARIA grid keyboard contract — Arrow keys navigate between cells, Tab moves to the next widget outside the grid. This is a significant implementation burden. If the team only wants sortable column headers without full keyboard cell navigation, the correct approach is to leave the element as a plain `<table>` and add `aria-sort="ascending"` on `<th>` elements with click/keyboard handlers on the header buttons. Adding `role="grid"` without implementing Arrow key navigation creates a broken ARIA pattern that is worse for screen reader users than the unmodified table. [community]

---

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 48)

216. **[community] When a React or Vue component re-renders and replaces the DOM node containing an `aria-live` region rather than updating its text content in place, screen readers do not announce the new content because the live region registration is lost — the newly-inserted DOM node is treated as a freshly loaded element, not an update to a monitored region**: React's reconciliation algorithm re-uses a DOM node when the component type and key are stable, but if the component unmounts and remounts (e.g., conditional rendering with `{show && <StatusRegion />}`), the live region node is destroyed and recreated. The screen reader's AT bridge de-registers the old node and registers the new one, but since the new node was inserted with content already present (not as a change to an existing node), no announcement fires. WHY: Developers assume mounting `<div aria-live="polite">File uploaded successfully</div>` will trigger an announcement — it does not, because announcements only fire when text changes within an already-registered live region. The fix is to keep the live region in the DOM at all times (even when empty) and update its `textContent` via JavaScript, never by swapping the node. [community]

217. **[community] Playwright's `page.getByRole('combobox')` matches both native `<select>` elements and custom `role="combobox"` elements — when a page has both, `.first()` may resolve to the native `<select>` rather than the custom combobox widget, causing keyboard interaction tests to pass (because native `<select>` has correct keyboard behaviour) while the custom widget's broken keyboard contract goes untested**: Native `<select>` elements have implicit `role="combobox"` (or `role="listbox"` depending on browser/AT) and satisfy `getByRole('combobox')` queries. If the `<select>` appears earlier in the DOM than the custom combobox widget, `.first()` always resolves to the native element. WHY: Test authors write `page.getByRole('combobox').first().press('ArrowDown')` believing they are testing the custom widget; the native select handles ArrowDown correctly, the test passes, and the custom widget's missing ArrowDown handler is never discovered. Always target custom widgets with a more specific locator such as `page.locator('[role="combobox"]')` to match only elements with an explicit role attribute, or use `[data-testid]` selectors for custom components. [community]

218. **[community] Adding `aria-required="true"` to a `<fieldset>` element to mark an entire radio group as required does not expose the required state to screen readers — `aria-required` is only reliably honoured on individual form widgets (`input`, `select`, `textarea`) and `role="group"` required-state support is inconsistent across NVDA+Firefox, JAWS+Chrome, and VoiceOver+Safari, so axe-core passes while screen readers announce no required state**: The ARIA spec lists `aria-required` as applicable to `role="group"` in some versions but cross-browser AT support for this combination varies significantly. The reliable pattern is to include the word "required" in the `<legend>` text (e.g., `<legend>Payment method (required)</legend>`) and mark each `<input type="radio">` inside with the `required` HTML attribute, which browsers interpret as a group-level requirement. WHY: Teams instrument fieldsets with `aria-required` because it mirrors the pattern for individual inputs — the attribute is syntactically valid, axe-core does not flag it, and the implementation appears correct until screen-reader testing reveals the state is never announced. [community]

219. **[community] Using `AxeBuilder.disableRules(['color-contrast'])` to suppress false positives from third-party content disables the rule site-wide for that scan — including genuine colour contrast failures in first-party content elsewhere on the same page — silently removing contrast violations from the CI report**: `disableRules()` applies globally to the entire scan scope, not just to excluded elements. The correct tool for suppressing known issues in specific elements is `AxeBuilder.exclude('[data-testid="third-party-widget"]')`, which removes those elements from the scan entirely while keeping the colour-contrast rule active for all other elements. WHY: When a developer adds `disableRules(['color-contrast'])` as a quick fix for a third-party widget false positive, all subsequent PRs introducing first-party contrast failures pass CI undetected. The CI report shows zero colour-contrast violations — technically accurate but dangerously misleading. Always use `exclude()` for element-scoped suppression and reserve `disableRules()` only for rules that produce global false positives with no element-level workaround. [community]

220. **[community] Playwright's `locator.fill()` bypasses keyboard event simulation by setting the value property directly — input components that derive their accessible name or ARIA state from the `value` attribute and only update those attributes in response to individual `keydown`/`keypress`/`keyup` events will not update their accessible name after `fill()`, causing `getByRole` queries matching on the accessible name to fail even though the value is visually correct**: `locator.fill()` sets the `value` IDL property programmatically and dispatches `input` and `change` events but does not simulate individual key events. Some custom components (particularly React-controlled inputs with character-by-character state updates) do not update ARIA attributes until they receive key events. For these components, use `locator.pressSequentially()` (Playwright 1.38+) which simulates each keystroke individually, triggering the full keyboard event chain and allowing the component to update all ARIA state in response. WHY: Tests using `fill()` pass visually but `getByRole` assertions on the resulting accessible name fail intermittently, leading to flaky-test investigations that focus on timing when the real cause is the event simulation method. [community]

### Pattern 206 — ARIA Listbox: Keyboard Contract and `aria-selected` Testing [official]

A `listbox` widget presents a list of options for user selection. The correct keyboard contract requires Arrow keys to move focus between options, with `aria-selected` reflecting the current selection state. Testing must verify that DOM focus movement and selection state remain in sync, and that multi-select variants expose `aria-multiselectable="true"`.

```typescript
// playwright + jest-axe listbox keyboard contract test
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Listbox keyboard contract', () => {
  test('arrow keys move focus and update aria-selected', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/listbox-demo');

    const listbox = page.getByRole('listbox', { name: 'Choose a fruit' });
    await listbox.focus();

    // initial: first option should be focused/selected
    const firstOption = listbox.getByRole('option').first();
    await expect(firstOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');

    // Down Arrow moves to next option
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    const secondOption = listbox.getByRole('option').nth(1);
    await expect(secondOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
    // first option no longer selected in single-select mode
    await expect(firstOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'false');

    // Home goes back to first option
    await page.keyboard.press('Home');
    await expect(firstOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');

    // End goes to last option
    const options = listbox.getByRole('option');
    const lastIndex = (await options.count()) - 1;
    await page.keyboard.press('End');
    await expect(options.nth(lastIndex)).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
  });

  test('multi-select listbox exposes aria-multiselectable and uses Space to toggle', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/multiselect-listbox');

    const listbox = page.getByRole('listbox', { name: 'Select toppings' });
    await expect(listbox).toHaveAttribute('aria-multiselectable', 'true');

    await listbox.focus();
    // Space toggles selection without moving focus
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
    const firstOpt = listbox.getByRole('option').first();
    await expect(firstOpt).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
    const secondOpt = listbox.getByRole('option').nth(1);
    await expect(secondOpt).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');

    // first option remains selected in multi-select mode
    await expect(firstOpt).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** A listbox where every option contains nested HTML (badge icons, description sub-text) loses those inner semantics in screen reader output — the entire option text is announced as a single string without heading, list, or landmark context. Keep option content to plain or lightly formatted text. If rich content is required, consider a `grid` role instead, which supports cell-level focus and sub-element semantics but brings a significantly heavier keyboard contract (Arrow key cell navigation). [official]

### Pattern 207 — ARIA Slider: `aria-valuenow` Live Update Testing [official]

An ARIA slider (`role="slider"`) must expose its current value via `aria-valuenow` and keep it updated as the user presses Arrow keys. When numeric values are not meaningful to screen reader users (e.g., representing a day-of-week as 0–6), `aria-valuetext` must also be updated. Tests must assert both the functional range boundaries (`aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`) and real-time value changes.

```typescript
// playwright slider value tracking test
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Slider', () => {
  test('Arrow keys update aria-valuenow within valid range', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/price-slider');

    const slider = page.getByRole('slider', { name: 'Max price' });

    // assert static range attributes on mount
    await expect(slider).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemin', '0');
    await expect(slider).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemax', '1000');

    const initialValue = parseInt(
      await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow') ?? '500'
    );

    await slider.focus();

    // right arrow increases by one step
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const afterIncrease = parseInt(await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow') ?? '0');
    expect(afterIncrease).toBeGreaterThan(initialValue);

    // left arrow decreases by one step
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft');
    const afterDecrease = parseInt(await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow') ?? '0');
    expect(afterDecrease).toBeLessThan(afterIncrease);

    // Home sets to minimum
    await page.keyboard.press('Home');
    await expect(slider).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '0');

    // End sets to maximum
    await page.keyboard.press('End');
    await expect(slider).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '1000');
  });

  test('aria-valuetext is present and meaningful for non-numeric scales', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/day-slider');
    const slider = page.getByRole('slider', { name: 'Day of week' });
    // numeric 0–6 needs human-readable text
    const valueText = await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuetext');
    expect(valueText).toBeTruthy();
    expect(valueText).not.toMatch(/^\d+$/); // must not be a bare number
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Implementing `Page Up`/`Page Down` for larger step increments is listed as optional in the APG spec but is expected by power users and JAWS users who rely on it for fast navigation of wide ranges. Omitting it is technically conformant but degrades usability for sliders with large ranges (e.g., 0–10 000). Adding the handler is low-effort; skipping it is a UX debt that accumulates in support tickets. [official]

### Pattern 208 — ARIA Switch: Toggle State and Label Stability Testing [official]

A `switch` role (`role="switch"`) represents a binary on/off control. Unlike a checkbox, a switch must not have an indeterminate state. The APG keyboard contract requires Space (and optionally Enter) to toggle `aria-checked` between `"true"` and `"false"`. A critical correctness requirement is that the visible label must not change when the state changes — only the `aria-checked` value changes.

```typescript
// playwright switch toggle contract test
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Switch', () => {
  test('Space toggles aria-checked and label stays constant', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings/notifications');

    const emailSwitch = page.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Email notifications' });

    // record initial state
    const initialChecked = await emailSwitch.getAttribute('aria-checked');
    const labelBefore = await emailSwitch.accessibleName();

    await emailSwitch.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');

    const afterChecked = await emailSwitch.getAttribute('aria-checked');
    expect(afterChecked).not.toEqual(initialChecked);

    // label must be identical after toggle
    const labelAfter = await emailSwitch.accessibleName();
    expect(labelAfter).toEqual(labelBefore);

    // toggle back to original state
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
    await expect(emailSwitch).toHaveAttribute('aria-checked', initialChecked!);
  });

  test('switch is not in indeterminate state', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings/notifications');
    const switches = page.getByRole('switch');
    const count = await switches.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const sw = switches.nth(i);
      const checked = await sw.getAttribute('aria-checked');
      expect(['true', 'false']).toContain(checked);
    }
  });

  test('grouped switches have group label via role=group', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/settings/notifications');
    const group = page.getByRole('group', { name: /notification/i });
    await expect(group).toBeVisible();
    await expect(group.getByRole('switch').first()).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Using a native `<input type="checkbox">` styled visually as a switch is simpler to implement and passes axe-core scans because the `checked` attribute maps cleanly to the binary boolean. However, native checkboxes are announced as "checkbox" by screen readers, while `role="switch"` is announced as "switch" — a meaningful semantic distinction for AT users who rely on role names to understand UI controls. Teams must decide whether screen-reader-correct semantics are worth the added ARIA and keyboard handler complexity. [official]

### Pattern 209 — ARIA Menu/Menubar: Arrow Key Navigation and `aria-expanded` State Testing [official]

A `menubar` containing `menu` widgets requires a specific two-dimensional keyboard model: horizontal Arrow keys navigate between top-level `menuitem` elements, while vertical Arrow keys navigate within open submenus. `aria-expanded` must reflect open/closed state on parent items. Tests must cover the full open/navigate/close cycle including focus restoration on close.

```typescript
// playwright menubar keyboard contract test
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Menubar', () => {
  test('right/left arrow moves between top-level items', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const menubar = page.getByRole('menubar');
    const firstItem = menubar.getByRole('menuitem').first();
    await firstItem.focus();

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const secondItem = menubar.getByRole('menuitem').nth(1);
    await expect(secondItem).toBeFocused();

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft');
    await expect(firstItem).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('Enter/Down Arrow opens submenu and focuses first item', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const fileMenu = page.getByRole('menuitem', { name: 'File' });
    await expect(fileMenu).toHaveAttribute('aria-haspopup', /menu|true/);
    await expect(fileMenu).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

    await fileMenu.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

    await expect(fileMenu).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    const submenu = page.getByRole('menu', { name: 'File' });
    await expect(submenu).toBeVisible();
    await expect(submenu.getByRole('menuitem').first()).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('Escape closes menu and returns focus to parent menuitem', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const fileMenu = page.getByRole('menuitem', { name: 'File' });
    await fileMenu.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');

    await expect(fileMenu).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    await expect(fileMenu).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('typeahead moves focus to item beginning with typed character', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const editMenu = page.getByRole('menuitem', { name: 'Edit' });
    await editMenu.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
    // type 'c' should focus Copy, Cut, etc.
    await page.keyboard.press('c');
    const focused = page.locator('[role="menuitem"]:focus');
    const name = await focused.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? await focused.textContent();
    expect(name?.toLowerCase()).toMatch(/^c/);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** A common shortcut is to implement the menubar using `<nav>` with `<ul>`/`<li>` links and only adding `role="menubar"` and ARIA attributes without rewriting keyboard handlers. This produces a widget that looks correct in axe-core scans but fails AT usability testing because arrow key navigation is not implemented — screen reader users pressing ArrowRight expect to move to the next top-level item and instead nothing happens. The APG keyboard contract for `menubar` is substantial; teams that are not committed to the full implementation should use a navigation landmark with visible `<a>` links, which requires no custom keyboard handling. [official]

---

### Pattern 210 — ARIA Tree View: Expand/Collapse and `aria-expanded` Contract Testing [official]

A `tree` widget provides hierarchical navigation where Right Arrow expands closed nodes and Left Arrow collapses open nodes. `aria-expanded` must be present on parent nodes (`treeitem` with children) and absent from leaf nodes. Tests must verify that leaf nodes do not carry `aria-expanded` (which would mislead AT into announcing them as expandable parent nodes).

```typescript
// playwright tree view keyboard contract test
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Tree View', () => {
  test('Right Arrow expands closed node without moving focus', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/file-tree');
    const tree = page.getByRole('tree');
    const parentNode = tree.getByRole('treeitem', { name: 'src' });

    await expect(parentNode).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    await parentNode.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    await expect(parentNode).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
    // focus remains on the parent
    await expect(parentNode).toBeFocused();

    // press Right again: moves focus to first child
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const firstChild = tree.getByRole('treeitem').nth(1);
    await expect(firstChild).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('Left Arrow on open node collapses it; Left Arrow on child moves to parent', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/file-tree');
    const tree = page.getByRole('tree');
    const parentNode = tree.getByRole('treeitem', { name: 'src' });
    await parentNode.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight'); // expand
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight'); // move into child
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft'); // should move back to parent
    await expect(parentNode).toBeFocused();

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft'); // should collapse
    await expect(parentNode).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  });

  test('leaf nodes do not have aria-expanded attribute', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/file-tree');
    const tree = page.getByRole('tree');

    // expand all nodes to expose leaves
    const parentNodes = tree.locator('[aria-expanded]');
    const count = await parentNodes.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const node = parentNodes.nth(i);
      if (await node.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'false') {
        await node.focus();
        await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
      }
    }

    // check for treeitem nodes without aria-expanded (leaves)
    const allItems = tree.getByRole('treeitem');
    const total = await allItems.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < total; i++) {
      const item = allItems.nth(i);
      const hasChildren = await item.locator('[role="treeitem"]').count() > 0;
      if (!hasChildren) {
        await expect(item).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded');
      }
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Some teams implement tree view expand/collapse by toggling CSS `display:none` on the child group without updating `aria-expanded`. The visual behaviour is correct, but AT users hear "collapsed" or "expanded" based on `aria-expanded`, not the visibility of child nodes. When `aria-expanded` is out of sync with actual visibility, JAWS announces a node as "collapsed" while its children are visible — producing a confusing and broken experience. Always update `aria-expanded` in the same synchronous operation that toggles child visibility. [official]

---

### Pattern 211 — `aria-describedby` vs `aria-details`: Choosing the Right Description Mechanism [official]

`aria-describedby` links an element to plain-text description nodes and announces the referenced text as a description after the element name and role. `aria-details` (ARIA 1.3, broadly supported since 2024) links to rich structured content (tables, lists, paragraphs) but most ATs announce only that additional information is available, not the full content inline. Use `aria-describedby` for concise supplementary text; use `aria-details` for complex referenced content the user may choose to explore.

```typescript
// jest-axe + Playwright aria-describedby / aria-details association tests
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('aria-describedby and aria-details', () => {
  test('aria-describedby references exist and are visible to AT', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/form/password-field');

    const passwordInput = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Password' });
    const describedById = await passwordInput.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
    expect(describedById).toBeTruthy();

    // referenced element must exist in DOM
    const descEl = page.locator(`#${describedById}`);
    await expect(descEl).toBeAttached();

    // referenced element must not be aria-hidden
    const ariaHidden = await descEl.getAttribute('aria-hidden');
    expect(ariaHidden).not.toBe('true');
  });

  test('aria-details references a non-empty rich content node', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/chart/bar-chart');

    const chart = page.getByRole('img', { name: /quarterly revenue/i });
    const detailsId = await chart.getAttribute('aria-details');
    expect(detailsId).toBeTruthy();

    const detailsEl = page.locator(`#${detailsId}`);
    await expect(detailsEl).toBeAttached();
    // details node must contain meaningful structure
    const hasTable = await detailsEl.locator('table').count() > 0;
    const hasList = await detailsEl.locator('ul, ol').count() > 0;
    const hasParagraph = await detailsEl.locator('p').count() > 0;
    expect(hasTable || hasList || hasParagraph).toBe(true);
  });

  test('no aria-describedby references non-existent IDs (axe aria-valid-attr-value)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/form/password-field');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations.filter(v => v.id === 'aria-valid-attr-value')).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Using `aria-describedby` to reference a large block of text (e.g., a paragraph with 300 words of instructions) causes screen readers to read the full text every time the element receives focus — with no mechanism for the user to stop or skip the description. This severely degrades the experience for AT users who re-visit the element frequently. For long instructional content, use `aria-details` to point to the content or provide a link to a details section, giving users opt-in access to the information. [official]

---

### Pattern 212 — WCAG 3.3.9 Accessible Authentication (Enhanced): No Cognitive Function Test at All [official]

WCAG 3.3.9 (AAA, WCAG 2.2) prohibits all cognitive function tests in authentication, with no exceptions for alternative methods. This extends 3.3.8 (AA) which allows a second factor. Tests must verify that no authentication step requires transcribing characters, solving puzzles, or recognising objects — even when an alternative method is offered elsewhere in the flow.

```typescript
// Playwright WCAG 3.3.9 authentication scan: no CAPTCHA or cognitive puzzle allowed
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.9 Accessible Authentication Enhanced', () => {
  const authPages = ['/login', '/2fa', '/signup', '/reset-password'];

  for (const path of authPages) {
    test(`${path} — no CAPTCHA or image-recognition elements`, async ({ page }) => {
      await page.goto(path);

      // block any CAPTCHA iframe or script domains
      const captchaFrames = page.frameLocator('iframe[src*="recaptcha"], iframe[src*="hcaptcha"]');
      const captchaCount = await captchaFrames.locator('*').count().catch(() => 0);
      expect(captchaCount, `CAPTCHA iframe found on ${path}`).toBe(0);

      // no "identify all images" or "type the text" challenges
      const challengeTexts = page.locator('text=/identify all (images|squares|traffic)/i');
      await expect(challengeTexts).toHaveCount(0);
    });

    test(`${path} — autocomplete attributes present on credential fields`, async ({ page }) => {
      await page.goto(path);

      const usernameInput = page.locator('input[type="email"], input[name*="user"], input[autocomplete*="user"]').first();
      const passwordInput = page.locator('input[type="password"]').first();

      if (await usernameInput.count() > 0) {
        const ac = await usernameInput.getAttribute('autocomplete');
        expect(['username', 'email'], `Username field missing autocomplete on ${path}`).toContain(ac);
      }
      if (await passwordInput.count() > 0) {
        const ac = await passwordInput.getAttribute('autocomplete');
        expect(['current-password', 'new-password'], `Password field missing autocomplete on ${path}`).toContain(ac);
      }
    });
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Removing all CAPTCHAs satisfies WCAG 3.3.9 but opens forms to bot abuse. The recommended replacement is server-side bot detection (honeypot fields, rate limiting, IP analysis, device fingerprinting) combined with passkeys or magic-link authentication that requires no cognitive test. Passkeys (FIDO2/WebAuthn) are inherently accessible: they rely on biometrics or device PIN, which qualifies as a non-cognitive-function alternative under 3.3.8 and also satisfies 3.3.9. The tradeoff is development investment in passkey infrastructure versus ongoing CAPTCHA maintenance. [official]

---

### Pattern 213 — `aria-roledescription`: Custom Widget Labelling and Misuse Prevention [official]

`aria-roledescription` overrides the human-readable role name announced by screen readers. It is appropriate only when the ARIA role is correct but the default role label is insufficient to describe the widget to users (e.g., a `group` of slides called "Slide Show" rather than "group"). Tests must verify that `aria-roledescription` is not applied to native interactive elements (`button`, `a`, `input`) where it strips expected role semantics, and that any custom description is meaningful and not redundant.

```typescript
// Playwright aria-roledescription misuse detection test
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('aria-roledescription usage', () => {
  test('aria-roledescription is not applied to native interactive elements', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    const nativeInteractives = [
      'button[aria-roledescription]',
      'a[aria-roledescription]',
      'input[aria-roledescription]',
      'select[aria-roledescription]',
      'textarea[aria-roledescription]',
    ];

    for (const selector of nativeInteractives) {
      const count = await page.locator(selector).count();
      expect(count, `Unexpected aria-roledescription on native element: ${selector}`).toBe(0);
    }
  });

  test('aria-roledescription is not empty or whitespace-only', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/carousel');

    const roledescElements = page.locator('[aria-roledescription]');
    const total = await roledescElements.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < total; i++) {
      const val = await roledescElements.nth(i).getAttribute('aria-roledescription');
      expect(val?.trim().length ?? 0).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });

  test('carousel slides expose aria-roledescription="slide" and position labels', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/carousel');

    const carousel = page.getByRole('group', { name: /carousel|slide show/i });
    await expect(carousel).toHaveAttribute('aria-roledescription', 'carousel');

    const slides = carousel.locator('[aria-roledescription="slide"]');
    const slideCount = await slides.count();
    expect(slideCount).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    for (let i = 0; i < slideCount; i++) {
      const label = await slides.nth(i).getAttribute('aria-label');
      // Each slide should announce its position e.g. "1 of 5"
      expect(label).toMatch(/\d+\s+of\s+\d+/i);
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Applying `aria-roledescription="button"` to a `<div role="button">` effectively replaces the AT-announced role name with a custom string that looks identical. This is a no-op at best and actively misleading at worst — it teaches AT users a non-standard role name that will not match their mental model of a button. The correct approach is to use a real `<button>` element and avoid `aria-roledescription` entirely unless overriding an ARIA role that genuinely has no standard human-readable description matching the widget's purpose in context. [official]

---

### Pattern 214 — `prefers-contrast: more` Emulation and High-Contrast Mode Testing [community]

Operating systems expose a `prefers-contrast: more` media query for users who enable high-contrast or increased-contrast system settings. CSS must not reduce contrast below readable levels when this query is active. In Playwright, `page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' })` simulates Windows High Contrast mode, which replaces CSS colours with system colours. Tests should verify that content remains readable and interactive elements remain distinguishable under both emulation modes.

```typescript
// Playwright forced-colors and prefers-contrast emulation tests
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('High contrast and forced-colours emulation', () => {
  test('critical text is visible under prefers-contrast: more', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'light' });
    await page.goto('/');

    // inject forced contrast stylesheet check
    const lowContrastElements = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const els = document.querySelectorAll('p, h1, h2, h3, label, button');
      const flagged: string[] = [];
      for (const el of els) {
        const style = window.getComputedStyle(el);
        const color = style.color;
        const bg = style.backgroundColor;
        // simplified: flag elements with identical foreground and background
        if (color === bg) flagged.push(el.tagName + ':' + el.textContent?.slice(0, 20));
      }
      return flagged;
    });
    expect(lowContrastElements).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('page renders without missing content under forced-colors: active', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' });
    await page.goto('/');

    // critical nav links, headings, and form labels must still exist
    await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 })).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.locator('label').first()).toBeVisible();
  });

  test('SVG icons are visible under forced-colors via currentColor', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' });
    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    // SVG fill should be currentColor, not a hardcoded hex
    const hardcodedFills = await page.locator('svg [fill]:not([fill="currentColor"]):not([fill="none"])').count();
    expect(hardcodedFills, 'SVG elements with hardcoded fill colours fail forced-colors mode').toBe(0);
  });

  test('focus indicators remain visible under forced-colors mode', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' });
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focusedEl = page.locator(':focus');
    // In forced-colors, outline should use Highlight or ButtonText system colour
    const outlineStyle = await focusedEl.evaluate(el => window.getComputedStyle(el).outline);
    expect(outlineStyle).not.toBe('0px none rgb(0, 0, 0)');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Designing focus indicators using `outline: 2px solid var(--brand-blue)` satisfies WCAG 2.4.7 and 2.4.13 in normal mode but fails under Windows High Contrast mode because forced-colours replaces CSS custom-property colours with system colours, potentially making the outline invisible if it was relying on a specific hex value to contrast against the background. The correct pattern is to always include a `forced-colors: active` media query that explicitly sets `outline-color: Highlight` or `outline-color: ButtonText`, which are system-colour tokens that remain visible in all high-contrast themes. [community]
