### Pattern 215 — `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage`: Testing Form Error Announcements [official]

Playwright 1.50 introduced `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()`, which asserts that an input element has a non-empty accessible error message linked via `aria-errormessage` or `aria-describedby` pointing to an element with `role="alert"`. This replaces fragile `aria-errormessage` attribute string matching with a semantic-aware assertion that resolves the actual announced error text.

```typescript
// Playwright toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage form error test
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Form accessible error messages', () => {
  test('required field shows accessible error on submit', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');

    // submit without filling required fields
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Send message' }).click();

    const emailInput = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Email' });
    // Playwright 1.50+ semantic error message assertion
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(/required|valid email/i);
  });

  test('error message element has role="alert" or aria-live', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Send message' }).click();

    const emailInput = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Email' });
    const errId = await emailInput.getAttribute('aria-errormessage')
      ?? await emailInput.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
    expect(errId).toBeTruthy();

    const errEl = page.locator(`#${errId}`);
    await expect(errEl).toBeAttached();

    const role = await errEl.getAttribute('role');
    const live = await errEl.getAttribute('aria-live');
    const isAnnounceable = role === 'alert' || live === 'assertive' || live === 'polite';
    expect(isAnnounceable, 'Error message not in a live region').toBe(true);
  });

  test('error clears when field is corrected', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Send message' }).click();

    const emailInput = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Email' });
    await expect(emailInput).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(/required|valid/i);

    await emailInput.fill('user@example.com');
    await emailInput.blur();

    // error should clear after valid input
    await expect(emailInput).not.toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `aria-errormessage` requires the referenced element to have `role="alert"` or be in an `aria-live` region — otherwise, JAWS and NVDA may not announce the error text on input blur. Some teams use `aria-describedby` pointing to a static `<span>` for error text, which announces on focus but not when the error appears dynamically after blur. For dynamically injected error messages, `aria-errormessage` pointing to `role="alert"` provides the most consistent cross-AT announcement. The tradeoff: `role="alert"` causes assertive interruption of any ongoing AT speech, which can be disruptive if multiple fields fail simultaneously. Consider `aria-live="polite"` for multi-field validation batches, accepting a slight announcement delay. [official]

### Pattern 216 — `axe.run()` `reporter` Option: Generating EARL Reports for Compliance Audits [community]

Axe-core supports multiple result reporters. The `earl` reporter formats violations as EARL (Evaluation and Report Language) JSON-LD, which is the output format required for WCAG-EM 2.0 accessibility evaluations and EU public sector conformance reporting. When generating audit evidence for the EU Web Accessibility Directive or EAA, configuring axe to emit EARL output avoids post-processing and keeps the CI artefact directly consumable by conformance tools.

```typescript
// axe EARL report generation for compliance audits
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';
import { test } from '@playwright/test';
import fs from 'fs';
import path from 'path';

const AUDIT_PAGES = ['/', '/about', '/contact', '/products'];

test.describe('EARL compliance report generation', () => {
  test('generate EARL report for all audit pages', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
    const earlResults: object[] = [];

    for (const pagePath of AUDIT_PAGES) {
      await page.goto(pagePath);

      const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
        .analyze();

      // attach axe JSON for each page
      await testInfo.attach(`axe-${pagePath.replace('/', 'root')}.json`, {
        contentType: 'application/json',
        body: JSON.stringify(results, null, 2),
      });

      earlResults.push({
        '@type': 'earl:TestSubject',
        '@id': pagePath,
        violations: results.violations.map(v => ({
          id: v.id,
          wcag: v.tags.filter(t => t.startsWith('wcag')),
          impact: v.impact,
          nodes: v.nodes.length,
        })),
        passes: results.passes.length,
        incomplete: results.incomplete.length,
      });
    }

    const reportDir = path.join(process.cwd(), 'test-results', 'earl');
    fs.mkdirSync(reportDir, { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(
      path.join(reportDir, `accessibility-audit-${Date.now()}.json`),
      JSON.stringify({ '@context': 'http://www.w3.org/ns/earl#', pages: earlResults }, null, 2)
    );

    // CI gate: zero critical violations across all pages
    const criticalViolations = earlResults.flatMap((r: any) =>
      r.violations.filter((v: any) => v.impact === 'critical')
    );
    expect(criticalViolations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The built-in axe EARL reporter is not natively supported in `@axe-core/playwright` — the raw `results` object from `analyze()` uses axe's internal schema, not EARL JSON-LD. Generating a true EARL report requires either post-processing the results (as shown above) or using the standalone `axe-reporter-earl` package. For true WCAG-EM conformance evidence, a human auditor must supplement automated results; axe EARL output covers only the ~30–40% of WCAG SC that are automatable. Teams relying solely on the EARL output for EU directive compliance will underreport manual-only failures. [community]

---

### Pattern 217 — `page.getByRole` with `description` Option: Playwright 1.60 Accessible Description Matching [official]

Playwright 1.60 added a `description` option to `getByRole()` that filters elements by their computed accessible description (from `aria-describedby` or `aria-details`). This enables precise targeting of elements that share the same role and accessible name but differ in their description — a common pattern in data tables where multiple sort buttons share the label "Sort" but differ in their description ("Sort by Name ascending", "Sort by Date descending").

```typescript
// Playwright 1.60 getByRole description option test
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('getByRole with description option (Playwright 1.60)', () => {
  test('targets sort button by accessible description', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard/table');

    // Without description, multiple "Sort" buttons are ambiguous
    const allSortButtons = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sort' });
    const count = await allSortButtons.count();
    expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(1);

    // With description, target the exact column sort button
    const sortByName = page.getByRole('button', {
      name: 'Sort',
      description: /sort by name/i,
    });
    await expect(sortByName).toHaveCount(1);
    await sortByName.click();

    // verify the aria-sort state updated on the column header
    const nameHeader = page.getByRole('columnheader', { name: 'Name' });
    await expect(nameHeader).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'ascending');
  });

  test('form inputs with shared labels are distinguishable by description', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/address-form');

    // Two "Phone" inputs (home and work) with distinct descriptions
    const homePhone = page.getByRole('textbox', {
      name: 'Phone',
      description: /home phone/i,
    });
    const workPhone = page.getByRole('textbox', {
      name: 'Phone',
      description: /work phone/i,
    });

    await expect(homePhone).toBeVisible();
    await expect(workPhone).toBeVisible();
    await homePhone.fill('555-0100');
    await workPhone.fill('555-0200');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The `description` option in `getByRole` is powerful but fragile if `aria-describedby` content changes frequently (e.g., description text is generated from dynamic sort state). Hardcoding a description regex in the test creates a coupling between test and implementation that breaks when the description format changes. For stable targeting, prefer `data-testid` attributes on interactive elements when the accessible description is dynamic. Reserve the `description` option for tests that explicitly assert correct `aria-describedby` wiring as part of an accessibility contract test, not just as a locator convenience. [official]

---

### Pattern 218 — `jest-axe` `impactLevels` Option: Progressive Rollout for Legacy Codebases [community]

`jest-axe` exposes an `impactLevels` option that restricts which axe violation impact levels are treated as test failures. This allows teams to adopt automated accessibility testing in a legacy codebase by first gating only on `['critical']`, then progressively tightening to `['critical', 'serious']`, then `['critical', 'serious', 'moderate']`, without requiring a full remediation sprint before CI goes green.

```typescript
// jest-axe impactLevels progressive rollout pattern
import { render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { axe, toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';
import { PaymentForm } from '../PaymentForm';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

// PHASE 1: gate on critical only — allows landing CI without full remediation
describe('PaymentForm - Phase 1 accessibility gate (critical only)', () => {
  it('has no critical axe violations', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<PaymentForm />);
    const results = await axe(container, {
      impactLevels: ['critical'],
    });
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });
});

// PHASE 2: extend gate to critical + serious — after critical issues resolved
describe('PaymentForm - Phase 2 accessibility gate (critical + serious)', () => {
  it('has no critical or serious axe violations', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<PaymentForm />);
    const results = await axe(container, {
      impactLevels: ['critical', 'serious'],
    });
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });
});

// PHASE 3: full gate — all violations fail CI
describe('PaymentForm - Phase 3 full accessibility gate', () => {
  it('has no axe violations at any impact level', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<PaymentForm />);
    const results = await axe(container);
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });
});

// Helper: log remaining violations for triage without failing the test
describe('PaymentForm - violation triage report', () => {
  it('logs non-critical violations for backlog', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<PaymentForm />);
    const results = await axe(container, {
      impactLevels: ['moderate', 'minor'],
    });
    if (results.violations.length > 0) {
      console.table(results.violations.map(v => ({
        id: v.id,
        impact: v.impact,
        nodes: v.nodes.length,
        wcag: v.tags.filter(t => t.startsWith('wcag')).join(', '),
      })));
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The progressive rollout approach delays full accessibility compliance and risks "phase-gate freeze" — the team ships Phase 1 (critical only), resolves critical issues, and then never progresses to Phase 2 because the CI is green and product pressure moves on. To prevent this, codify the target phase and timeline in the project's accessibility policy document and add a CI check that fails if the impact gate has not advanced to `['critical', 'serious', 'moderate']` by a defined sprint milestone. The `impactLevels` mechanism is a technical debt management tool, not a permanent exemption strategy. [community]

---

### Pattern 219 — WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured: `scroll-padding` Geometry Test [official]

WCAG 2.4.11 (AA, WCAG 2.2) requires that when a UI component receives keyboard focus, it is not entirely hidden by author-created content. Sticky headers and fixed footers are the primary failure pattern. The CSS fix is `scroll-padding-top` equal to the sticky header height. Tests should verify that a focused element's `getBoundingClientRect().top` is not fully overlapped by a sticky toolbar.

```typescript
// Playwright WCAG 2.4.11 focus-not-obscured geometry test
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured', () => {
  test('focused elements are not completely hidden by sticky header', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/long-page');

    // get sticky header height
    const stickyHeader = page.locator('header[style*="position: sticky"], header.sticky');
    const headerBox = await stickyHeader.boundingBox();
    const headerBottom = headerBox ? headerBox.y + headerBox.height : 0;

    // tab through focusable elements and verify each is not obscured
    const focusableLinks = page.locator('a[href], button, input, select, textarea, [tabindex="0"]');
    const count = await focusableLinks.count();

    // check a representative sample of mid-page elements
    for (let i = Math.floor(count / 3); i < Math.min(Math.floor(count / 3) + 10, count); i++) {
      await focusableLinks.nth(i).focus();
      const box = await focusableLinks.nth(i).boundingBox();
      if (box) {
        // WCAG 2.4.11: element must not be ENTIRELY obscured — top of element must be below header bottom
        // full overlap = box.y + box.height <= headerBottom
        const isCompletelyHidden = box.y + box.height <= headerBottom;
        expect(isCompletelyHidden, `Element ${i} is completely obscured by sticky header`).toBe(false);
      }
    }
  });

  test('scroll-padding-top is set on html/body when sticky header exists', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/long-page');

    const hasSticky = await page.locator('[style*="position: sticky"], .sticky, .fixed-header').count() > 0;
    if (hasSticky) {
      const scrollPaddingTop = await page.evaluate(() =>
        window.getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).scrollPaddingTop
      );
      expect(
        scrollPaddingTop,
        'scroll-padding-top must be set on <html> when a sticky header is present (WCAG 2.4.11)'
      ).not.toBe('0px');
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Setting `scroll-padding-top` equal to the sticky header height fixes the WCAG 2.4.11 scroll-into-view case (when Tab scrolls a focused element into view, it clears the header). However, it does not fix the case where the user has manually scrolled so that a partially visible element receives focus — the browser does not re-scroll on `focus()` when the element is already partially in view. For complete WCAG 2.4.11 compliance, combine `scroll-padding-top` with `Element.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })` called in the focus event handler, or accept the residual manual-scroll case as a known partial failure. [official]

---

### Pattern 220 — `testInfo.attach()` Axe Scan Evidence Pattern for CI Audit Trails [community]

Playwright's `testInfo.attach()` API allows arbitrary binary or text artefacts to be embedded into the HTML report. Using it to attach the full axe-core JSON scan output creates a self-contained audit trail: each test run in CI contains the exact violation evidence without requiring a separate artefact upload step. This pattern is particularly useful for WCAG conformance audits where stakeholders need to review the raw scan data.

```typescript
// Playwright testInfo.attach() axe scan evidence pattern
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('Accessibility scan with artefact attachment', () => {
  // run this fixture for all pages that need CI evidence
  async function runAccessibilityScan(
    page: import('@playwright/test').Page,
    testInfo: import('@playwright/test').TestInfo,
    url: string,
    label: string,
  ) {
    await page.goto(url);

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
      .analyze();

    // attach full axe JSON for audit trail
    await testInfo.attach(`axe-scan-${label}.json`, {
      contentType: 'application/json',
      body: JSON.stringify(results, null, 2),
    });

    // attach human-readable violation summary
    if (results.violations.length > 0) {
      const summary = results.violations.map(v =>
        `[${v.impact}] ${v.id}: ${v.description} (${v.nodes.length} node(s))\n` +
        `  WCAG: ${v.tags.filter(t => t.startsWith('wcag')).join(', ')}\n` +
        v.nodes.slice(0, 3).map(n => `  - ${n.html.slice(0, 80)}`).join('\n')
      ).join('\n\n');

      await testInfo.attach(`axe-violations-${label}.txt`, {
        contentType: 'text/plain',
        body: summary,
      });
    }

    return results;
  }

  test('homepage has no WCAG 2.2 AA violations', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
    const results = await runAccessibilityScan(page, testInfo, '/', 'homepage');
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('checkout flow has no WCAG 2.2 AA violations', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
    const results = await runAccessibilityScan(page, testInfo, '/checkout', 'checkout');
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Attaching the full axe JSON output to every test run significantly increases Playwright HTML report size — a scan of a complex page can produce 200–500 KB of JSON per page. For large test suites scanning dozens of pages, this can make the HTML report unwieldy. The mitigation is to attach the full JSON only on failure (check `results.violations.length > 0` before attaching) and always attach the compact summary. For passing scans, attach only the `passes.length` and `incomplete.length` counts as metadata, not the full pass list which can run into thousands of items. [community]

---

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 49)

221. **[community] Using `role="presentation"` on a `<table>` element removes the table semantics for screen readers but does not remove the semantics from child `<th>` elements — NVDA and JAWS continue to announce "column header" for `<th>` cells inside a `role="presentation"` table, creating a confusing mixture of "presentation" container with "header" children**: `role="presentation"` on a `<table>` suppresses the table, row-group, and row roles, but child elements with implicit or explicit roles maintain their own computed role. A `<th>` inside the presentation table is still announced as a column header with no table context, which is semantically incoherent. WHY: Developers add `role="presentation"` to the `<table>` wrapper believing this removes all table semantics from the subtree — it does not. The correct fix for layout tables is `role="presentation"` on `<table>` **and** converting all `<th>` to `<td>` (or `<div>`/`<span>`) so that no header role is inherited. [community]

222. **[community] `aria-label` values that exactly duplicate the element's visible text content are redundant but harmless — however, `aria-label` values that contradict the visible text (e.g., `<button aria-label="Close menu">Save</button>`) cause WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name failures because voice control users say "Save" to activate the button but the accessible name is "Close menu" so voice control ignores the command**: WCAG 2.5.3 requires the accessible name to *contain* the visible text label. An `aria-label` that wholly replaces the visible text with a different string breaks voice control activation for the millions of users who rely on Dragon NaturallySpeaking and similar tools. WHY: Developers add `aria-label` to provide longer context for screen reader users (e.g., "Close menu" instead of just "Save") without realising that this overwrites the accessible name computed from the button's text content, breaking the voice-control activation contract. If extra context is needed, use `aria-describedby` for supplementary description while keeping `aria-label` either absent or beginning with the visible text. [community]

223. **[community] Playwright's `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` assertion performs a deep-equal check on the ARIA snapshot by default, meaning any change to the DOM structure — including adding a new non-interactive element or reordering children — causes the snapshot to fail even if the accessibility tree semantics are unchanged**: The ARIA snapshot format captures the computed accessibility tree as YAML; `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` in its default mode treats the snapshot as an exact structural template. Adding a decorative `<span>` inside a `<button>` does not change the button's accessible name but changes the snapshot structure, breaking tests. WHY: Teams treating ARIA snapshots as black-box regression tests find that routine DOM refactoring generates snapshot failures with no accessibility regression, eroding trust in the test suite and leading developers to blindly update snapshots. Use `toMatchAriaSnapshot({ mode: 'partial' })` (Playwright 1.60+) to assert only the semantically meaningful parts of the accessibility tree, or scope snapshots to specific components rather than full-page trees. [community]

224. **[community] The `autocomplete` attribute on `<input>` fields is required by WCAG 1.3.5 (Identify Input Purpose) for personal data fields, but using incorrect `autocomplete` values (e.g., `autocomplete="name"` on a last-name-only field, or `autocomplete="off"` on a username field) is technically valid HTML, passes all axe-core checks, and passes Lighthouse — but breaks browser auto-fill for users who rely on it for motor or cognitive accessibility reasons**: WCAG 1.3.5 requires that the `autocomplete` attribute value correctly identifies the input's purpose using the official token list. `autocomplete="name"` on a field that accepts only a last name will cause password managers and browser auto-fill to populate the full name instead of just the last name. For users with motor disabilities who rely on one-click auto-fill to avoid repetitive typing, an incorrect token is as bad as `autocomplete="off"`. WHY: Axe-core rule `autocomplete-valid` checks that the attribute value is a valid token from the HTML spec list — it does not check semantic correctness (whether the token matches the field's actual purpose). Teams pass axe-core checks while shipping the wrong autocomplete tokens because no automated tool verifies semantic intent. [community]

225. **[community] When `aria-live="assertive"` is used on a notification container, the screen reader interrupts the user's current activity to announce the message — if multiple assertive announcements fire in rapid succession (e.g., form validation running on every keystroke), the AT announcement queue floods and users lose the current field context**: `aria-live="assertive"` is designed for time-sensitive information where the user must be interrupted (e.g., a session timeout warning). Using it for routine form validation, search suggestions, or general status messages causes screen reader users to experience constant interruptions while typing. WHY: Developers choose `assertive` over `polite` because they want to ensure the message is announced "immediately", not realising that `polite` announcements are delivered as soon as the user pauses — which is the correct behaviour for non-urgent notifications. The fix is to use `aria-live="polite"` for validation messages and reserve `assertive` only for critical, session-ending, or error-severity alerts. Additionally, debounce assertive announcements with a minimum 1-second guard window to prevent queue flooding when multiple events fire in sequence. [community]

### Pattern 221 — ARIA Grid Keyboard Contract: Navigation, Selection, and Focus Management [official]

The ARIA `role="grid"` pattern covers two distinct use cases: data grids (spreadsheet-like tables with editable or interactive cells) and layout grids (groups of widgets reduced to a single tab stop). Both share a two-dimensional Arrow Key navigation model but differ in cell roles and selection semantics. Only one focusable element inside the grid is included in the page tab sequence at any time — the roving `tabindex` pattern manages which cell holds `tabindex="0"` while all others hold `tabindex="-1"`. `aria-colcount` and `aria-rowcount` must be set on the `<div role="grid">` when not all rows/columns are rendered in the DOM (virtual scrolling), so assistive technologies can announce "row 12 of 500" rather than "row 12 of 20".

```typescript
// grid-keyboard.spec.ts — ARIA APG Grid keyboard contract
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Grid keyboard contract', () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/data-grid');
  });

  test('arrow keys navigate between cells', async ({ page }) => {
    // focus the first cell
    await page.locator('[role="gridcell"]').first().focus();
    // ArrowRight moves to next cell in row
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const focused = page.locator('[role="gridcell"]:focus');
    await expect(focused).toBeVisible();
    // ArrowDown moves to same column, next row
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    // Home moves to first cell in current row
    await page.keyboard.press('Home');
    const firstInRow = page.locator('[role="row"]:focus-within [role="gridcell"]').first();
    await expect(firstInRow).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End navigate to grid extremes', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.locator('[role="gridcell"]').nth(5).focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Control+Home');
    await expect(page.locator('[role="gridcell"]').first()).toBeFocused();
    await page.keyboard.press('Control+End');
    await expect(page.locator('[role="gridcell"]').last()).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('virtual grid reports aria-rowcount and aria-colcount', async ({ page }) => {
    const grid = page.locator('[role="grid"]');
    await expect(grid).toHaveAttribute('aria-rowcount');
    await expect(grid).toHaveAttribute('aria-colcount');
    const rowCount = await grid.getAttribute('aria-rowcount');
    expect(parseInt(rowCount ?? '0', 10)).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('selected cell has aria-selected="true"', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.locator('[role="gridcell"]').first().click();
    await expect(page.locator('[role="gridcell"]').first()).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The roving `tabindex` pattern for grids requires JavaScript to update `tabindex` on every Arrow Key press. If the grid re-renders cells (virtual scrolling, React reconciliation), the `tabindex="0"` attribute can be lost and focus returns to the grid container rather than the expected cell. Teams should store the focused cell coordinates in state and restore `tabindex="0"` after render. Layout grids used purely for grouping widgets (e.g., a toolbar of icon buttons) often use `role="toolbar"` instead of `role="grid"`, which has a simpler one-dimensional Arrow Key model. [official]

---

### Pattern 222 — ARIA Toolbar Keyboard Contract: Arrow Key Navigation Inside Grouped Controls [official]

A toolbar (`role="toolbar"`) is a container for grouping a set of controls, typically action buttons. It uses the roving `tabindex` pattern: Tab enters the toolbar and lands on one control; Arrow Left/Right move between controls inside the toolbar; Tab exits the toolbar entirely to the next focusable element in the page. The toolbar must have an accessible name (via `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`) to distinguish it from other toolbars on the page. If a toolbar contains only one item, it should not be implemented as a toolbar — use a plain button instead.

```typescript
// toolbar-keyboard.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Toolbar keyboard contract', () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/editor');
  });

  test('toolbar has accessible name', async ({ page }) => {
    const toolbar = page.locator('[role="toolbar"]');
    await expect(toolbar).toBeVisible();
    // Must have aria-label or aria-labelledby
    const label = await toolbar.getAttribute('aria-label');
    const labelledBy = await toolbar.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    expect(label || labelledBy).toBeTruthy();
  });

  test('Tab enters toolbar and lands on first active control', async ({ page }) => {
    // Tab from outside the toolbar
    await page.locator('body').focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    // First enabled control inside toolbar should receive focus
    const firstControl = page.locator('[role="toolbar"] [tabindex="0"]').first();
    await expect(firstControl).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('ArrowRight and ArrowLeft navigate between controls', async ({ page }) => {
    const controls = page.locator('[role="toolbar"] button, [role="toolbar"] [role="button"]');
    await controls.first().focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    await expect(controls.nth(1)).toBeFocused();
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft');
    await expect(controls.first()).toBeFocused();
  });

  test('Tab from within toolbar exits to next page focusable element', async ({ page }) => {
    const controls = page.locator('[role="toolbar"] button');
    await controls.first().focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    // Focus must be outside the toolbar
    const activeRole = await page.evaluate(() =>
      document.activeElement?.closest('[role="toolbar"]') ? 'inside' : 'outside'
    );
    expect(activeRole).toBe('outside');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The one-dimensional Arrow Key model of `role="toolbar"` conflicts with users' expectation of Tab navigation between buttons. Sighted keyboard users who have not read AT documentation often press Tab expecting to move between toolbar buttons and are confused when Tab exits the toolbar. The UX tension is real: ARIA APG specifies Arrow Keys for intra-toolbar navigation precisely to reduce Tab stops in complex editing UIs. Provide a visible tooltip or onboarding hint that explains toolbar keyboard navigation for new users. [official]

### Pattern 223 — ARIA Feed Pattern: Infinite Scroll Accessibility [official]

The `role="feed"` pattern is designed for infinite-scroll content streams (news feeds, social timelines). Each article inside the feed has `role="article"`. Screen reader users navigate the feed with Page Down / Page Up to move between articles. `aria-busy="true"` is set on the feed container while new content loads and cleared to `aria-busy="false"` (or removed) once loading completes, which signals to screen readers that they can continue announcing new content. The feed container must have an accessible name. Each article should carry a unique `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` pointing to its headline so users can navigate by article title.

```typescript
// feed-a11y.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('ARIA Feed accessibility', () => {
  test('feed container has role=feed and accessible name', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/timeline');
    const feed = page.locator('[role="feed"]');
    await expect(feed).toBeVisible();
    const label = await feed.getAttribute('aria-label');
    const labelledBy = await feed.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    expect(label || labelledBy).toBeTruthy();
  });

  test('each article has role=article with unique label', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/timeline');
    const articles = page.locator('[role="feed"] [role="article"]');
    const count = await articles.count();
    expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 5); i++) {
      const article = articles.nth(i);
      const label = await article.getAttribute('aria-label');
      const labelledBy = await article.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
      expect(label || labelledBy).toBeTruthy();
    }
  });

  test('aria-busy is set during load and cleared after', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/timeline');
    // Trigger load more
    await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight));
    const feed = page.locator('[role="feed"]');
    // At some point during loading, aria-busy should be "true"
    // After loading completes it should be absent or "false"
    await expect(feed).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-busy', 'true');
  });

  test('feed has no axe violations', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/timeline');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include('[role="feed"]')
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The `role="feed"` pattern is under-supported in older screen reader versions — JAWS 2022 and earlier require the user to enter "reading mode" to use Page Down/Up feed navigation, while modern NVDA and VoiceOver handle it natively. For broad AT compatibility, supplement feed navigation with a "Load more" button that keyboard and screen reader users can activate explicitly, rather than relying solely on scroll-triggered loading. The button provides a fallback activation method when AT-managed navigation fails. [official]

### Pattern 224 — WCAG 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced): Full Visibility Guarantee [official]

WCAG 2.4.12 (AA, introduced in WCAG 2.2) requires that no part of the focused element is hidden by author-created content — it is a stricter extension of 2.4.11 (Focus Not Obscured Minimum, which only requires *some* part of the component to be visible). Sticky headers, cookie banners, and chat widgets are the primary failure vectors. The CSS fix is `scroll-padding-top` on the `<html>` element matching the sticky header height. For dynamic banners that resize, use a CSS custom property `--sticky-offset` updated by JavaScript and referenced in `scroll-padding-top: var(--sticky-offset)`.

```typescript
// focus-not-obscured-enhanced.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)', () => {
  test('no focused element is fully or partially obscured by sticky header', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Collect all focusable elements
    const focusables = await page.$$('a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), [tabindex="0"]');

    for (const el of focusables.slice(0, 30)) {
      await el.focus();
      // Get bounding boxes
      const elBox = await el.boundingBox();
      if (!elBox) continue;

      // Get sticky header height
      const stickyHeight = await page.evaluate(() => {
        const header = document.querySelector('header[class*="sticky"], [style*="position: sticky"]') as HTMLElement | null;
        return header ? header.getBoundingClientRect().bottom : 0;
      });

      // The top of the focused element must be below the sticky header bottom
      // (2.4.12 requires no part is hidden, so full visibility needed)
      if (stickyHeight > 0) {
        expect(elBox.y).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(stickyHeight - 1); // 1px tolerance
      }
    }
  });

  test('scroll-padding-top accounts for sticky header height', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const scrollPadding = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const computed = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
      return parseInt(computed.scrollPaddingTop || '0', 10);
    });
    const stickyHeight = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const header = document.querySelector('header') as HTMLElement | null;
      return header ? header.getBoundingClientRect().height : 0;
    });
    // scroll-padding must be at least as tall as sticky header
    expect(scrollPadding).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(stickyHeight - 2);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** WCAG 2.4.12 is AA level (required for full WCAG 2.2 AA conformance) while 2.4.11 is also AA. Many teams discover they pass 2.4.11 (something visible) but fail 2.4.12 (fully visible) when the focused element scrolls to a position where the top half is under the sticky header. Dynamic sticky elements (collapsing headers on scroll, toast notifications) make this test context-dependent — write the test with the page in its "header visible" state and its "header collapsed" state separately. [official]

---

### Pattern 225 — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size Minimum: 24×24 px with Spacing Offset [official]

WCAG 2.5.8 (AA, WCAG 2.2) requires that interactive targets be at least 24×24 CSS pixels, or that there is at least 24px of spacing between the target's centre and the nearest adjacent target's boundary. This replaces the older recommendation of 44×44 px (which was AAA under 2.5.5). The spacing offset algorithm: for a target smaller than 24px, calculate whether a 24px circle centred on the target fits in the bounding space without overlapping adjacent targets. Playwright's `boundingBox()` provides the geometry needed to automate this check.

```typescript
// target-size.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface TargetBox { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }

function checkSpacingOffset(a: TargetBox, b: TargetBox): boolean {
  // Centre points
  const ax = a.x + a.width / 2;
  const ay = a.y + a.height / 2;
  const bx = b.x + b.width / 2;
  const by = b.y + b.height / 2;
  const distance = Math.sqrt((ax - bx) ** 2 + (ay - by) ** 2);
  return distance >= 24;
}

test.describe('WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size Minimum', () => {
  test('all interactive targets are at least 24×24 px or meet spacing offset', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const targets = page.locator('a, button:not([disabled]), [role="button"], input[type="checkbox"], input[type="radio"]');
    const count = await targets.count();
    const boxes: TargetBox[] = [];

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const box = await targets.nth(i).boundingBox();
      if (box) boxes.push(box);
    }

    const failures: string[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < boxes.length; i++) {
      const b = boxes[i];
      if (b.width >= 24 && b.height >= 24) continue; // passes by size
      // Check spacing offset against all other targets
      const tooClose = boxes.some((other, j) => j !== i && !checkSpacingOffset(b, other));
      if (tooClose) {
        failures.push(`Target at (${Math.round(b.x)},${Math.round(b.y)}) is ${Math.round(b.width)}×${Math.round(b.height)}px and has a neighbour within 24px centre distance`);
      }
    }
    expect(failures, failures.join('\n')).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The spacing offset algorithm in 2.5.8 is significantly more permissive than the old 44×44 AAA guidance — it allows small targets as long as adjacent targets are not too close, which is common in many icon toolbars and navigation menus. The challenge is that the spec's "offset" calculation involves circular bounding geometry, not rectangular bounding boxes, so simple box overlap checks undercount failures. The test above uses centre-to-centre distance as a conservative proxy. For full spec accuracy, implement the exact offset circle algorithm from the Understanding document. [official]

---

### Pattern 226 — ARIA Window Splitter: Resizable Pane Keyboard Contract [official]

The `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation` and `aria-valuenow/min/max` implements a resizable splitter between two panes (e.g., a code editor with a sidebar). Arrow Keys change the split position, Home/End jump to extremes, and F6 cycles focus between the panes. The separator must announce its current position as a percentage via `aria-valuenow` so screen reader users know the pane proportions.

```typescript
// window-splitter.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Window Splitter', () => {
  test('separator has correct ARIA attributes', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/editor-layout');
    const splitter = page.locator('[role="separator"][aria-valuenow]');
    await expect(splitter).toBeVisible();
    await expect(splitter).toHaveAttribute('aria-orientation');
    await expect(splitter).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemin');
    await expect(splitter).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemax');
    await expect(splitter).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow');
    await expect(splitter).toHaveAttribute('aria-controls');
  });

  test('ArrowRight increases pane size and updates aria-valuenow', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/editor-layout');
    const splitter = page.locator('[role="separator"][aria-valuenow]');
    await splitter.focus();
    const before = parseInt((await splitter.getAttribute('aria-valuenow')) ?? '50', 10);
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const after = parseInt((await splitter.getAttribute('aria-valuenow')) ?? '50', 10);
    expect(after).toBeGreaterThan(before);
  });

  test('Home sets splitter to minimum value', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/editor-layout');
    const splitter = page.locator('[role="separator"][aria-valuenow]');
    await splitter.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Home');
    const valueMin = await splitter.getAttribute('aria-valuemin');
    const valueNow = await splitter.getAttribute('aria-valuenow');
    expect(valueNow).toBe(valueMin);
  });

  test('End sets splitter to maximum value', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/editor-layout');
    const splitter = page.locator('[role="separator"][aria-valuenow]');
    await splitter.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('End');
    const valueMax = await splitter.getAttribute('aria-valuemax');
    const valueNow = await splitter.getAttribute('aria-valuenow');
    expect(valueNow).toBe(valueMax);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Window splitters implemented with mouse-only drag handles are one of the most commonly missed keyboard interaction patterns in complex UIs. The `role="separator"` with value attributes is the correct semantic, but many component libraries (including several popular React UI kits) implement splitters as plain `<div>` elements with only mouse event listeners. When auditing, check that the splitter element is focusable (`tabindex="0"`), has `role="separator"`, and that all four required ARIA value attributes are present and updated on keypress. [official]

---

### Pattern 227 — `@axe-core/react` v4.11.x: Component-Level Unit Testing with React 18 `act()` [community]

`@axe-core/react` provides accessibility scanning integrated into the React render cycle. After upgrading to React 18, violations can fire before the component has finished rendering because React 18's concurrent renderer may defer state updates. Wrapping the axe scan call in `act()` and awaiting it ensures all state updates flush before the scan runs. Without this, false positives appear for dynamic content that updates its ARIA attributes after the initial render.

```typescript
// Button.a11y.test.tsx — @axe-core/react with React 18 act() pattern
import React from 'react';
import { render, act } from '@testing-library/react';
import axe from 'axe-core';
import { toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

async function runAxeOnComponent(ui: React.ReactElement) {
  let container!: HTMLElement;
  await act(async () => {
    const result = render(ui);
    container = result.container;
    // Allow concurrent renderer to flush deferred updates
    await Promise.resolve();
  });

  const results = await axe.run(container, {
    runOnly: {
      type: 'tag',
      values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'],
    },
    resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'],
  });

  return results;
}

describe('LoadingButton accessibility', () => {
  it('idle state has no violations', async () => {
    const results = await runAxeOnComponent(
      <button type="button" aria-label="Save document">Save</button>
    );
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('loading state with aria-busy is announced correctly', async () => {
    const results = await runAxeOnComponent(
      <button type="button" aria-busy="true" aria-label="Saving document">
        <span aria-hidden="true">⏳</span> Saving…
      </button>
    );
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('disabled state exposes aria-disabled not disabled attribute for AT', async () => {
    const results = await runAxeOnComponent(
      <button type="button" aria-disabled="true" tabIndex={0}>Submit</button>
    );
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Using `act()` from `@testing-library/react` resolves React 18 concurrent mode false positives, but `act()` suppresses React's own "not wrapped in act()" warnings in tests — teams may find these warnings masked. The deeper issue is that `@axe-core/react` was designed for the synchronous React 16/17 render model. For React 18 with Suspense boundaries and server components, component-level axe testing is most reliable in `@testing-library/react` tests that render the component in a jsdom environment, not in the React DevTools injection mode (which `@axe-core/react` uses in development mode). [community]

---

### Pattern 228 — `axe-core` `resultTypes` Performance Optimisation: Fastest Scan Configuration [community]

By default, `axe.run()` collects four result buckets: `violations`, `passes`, `incomplete`, and `inapplicable`. The `passes` and `inapplicable` arrays can each contain thousands of items on a complex page, increasing scan time by 3–8× over a violations-only scan. Setting `resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete']` reduces the data collected without skipping any rule execution — rules still run in full; only which result bucket is populated changes. This pattern is critical in CI where multiple pages are scanned per test run.

```typescript
// fast-axe-scan.ts — resultTypes performance optimisation
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';
import type { Page } from '@playwright/test';
import type { AxeResults } from 'axe-core';

/**
 * Run axe with resultTypes optimisation.
 * Violations and incomplete are collected; passes/inapplicable are omitted.
 * Rule execution is unchanged — only result collection is limited.
 */
export async function fastAxeScan(
  page: Page,
  tags = ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'],
): Promise<AxeResults> {
  return new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(tags)
    .options({
      // Omit passes and inapplicable to reduce serialisation cost
      resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'],
    })
    .analyze();
}

// Usage in test
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const PAGES = ['/', '/products', '/cart', '/checkout', '/account'];

for (const path of PAGES) {
  test(`${path} has no WCAG 2.2 AA violations (fast scan)`, async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto(path);
    const results = await fastAxeScan(page);
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Omitting `passes` means you lose the ability to report on which rules are confirmed passing — useful for compliance audits that require both a violation list and a conformance evidence list. For audit trail purposes (producing a VPAT or ACR), run a full scan with all result types on a scheduled nightly job, and use the `resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete']` fast scan in pre-commit and PR CI gates where speed matters. Never omit `incomplete` — it surfaces needs-review items that automated tools cannot definitively classify as pass or fail. [community]

---

### Pattern 229 — WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry: Multi-Step Form Pre-Population Test [official]

WCAG 3.3.7 (A, WCAG 2.2) requires that information previously entered by the user in the same session is either auto-populated or available for the user to select when the same information is requested again. This prevents users with cognitive disabilities and motor impairments from having to re-type information they have already provided. The canonical example is a checkout flow that asks for shipping address on step 2 and billing address on step 3 — if billing address defaults to the shipping address (or provides a "Same as shipping" checkbox), 3.3.7 is met.

```typescript
// redundant-entry.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry', () => {
  test('checkout billing address is pre-populated from shipping or provides same-as option', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout/shipping');

    // Fill in shipping address
    await page.getByLabel('First name').fill('Alex');
    await page.getByLabel('Last name').fill('Taylor');
    await page.getByLabel('Street address').fill('123 Main St');
    await page.getByLabel('City').fill('Springfield');
    await page.getByLabel('ZIP code').fill('12345');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue to billing' }).click();

    // On billing step: either fields are pre-populated OR a "same as shipping" control exists
    const sameAsShipping = page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: /same as shipping/i });
    const firstNameField = page.getByLabel('First name');

    const hasSameAsOption = await sameAsShipping.isVisible().catch(() => false);
    const isPrePopulated = await firstNameField.inputValue().then(v => v === 'Alex').catch(() => false);

    expect(
      hasSameAsOption || isPrePopulated,
      'Billing form must either pre-populate from shipping data or provide a "Same as shipping" option'
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  test('multi-step form does not re-ask for email entered on step 1', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/register/step-1');
    await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('user@example.com');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next/i }).click();

    // On step 2 there must be no email input, OR the email input must be pre-filled
    const emailOnStep2 = page.getByLabel('Email');
    const exists = await emailOnStep2.isVisible().catch(() => false);
    if (exists) {
      const value = await emailOnStep2.inputValue();
      expect(value).toBe('user@example.com');
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** WCAG 3.3.7 has an important exception: re-entry is allowed when it is essential for security (e.g., a "confirm password" field), or when the previously entered information is no longer valid. Automated tests cannot determine whether a re-entry requirement is "essential" — they can only verify that pre-population or a "same as" option exists where it is expected. Flag all re-entry instances in a manual review checklist so a human determines whether the exception applies. [official]

---

### Pattern 230 — WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication: CAPTCHA Alternatives and `autocomplete` CI Tests [official]

WCAG 3.3.8 (AA, WCAG 2.2) prohibits requiring the user to solve a cognitive function test (e.g., transcribing distorted text CAPTCHA, solving a puzzle) to authenticate, unless an alternative method is also provided. Acceptable alternatives include: a second authentication method that does not require a cognitive function test (e.g., email link, passkey), an object recognition test (identifying a picture of a cat), or a personal content test (identifying a photo the user uploaded). The `autocomplete="current-password"` and `autocomplete="username"` attributes on login fields are required so that password managers can fill credentials without requiring users to type them.

```typescript
// accessible-auth.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication', () => {
  test('login form has autocomplete attributes for password manager support', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    await expect(page.getByLabel(/username|email/i)).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', /username|email/);
    await expect(page.getByLabel(/password/i)).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', /current-password/);
  });

  test('no CAPTCHA-only gate without alternative method', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    // If a CAPTCHA widget is present, an alternative must also be visible
    const captcha = page.locator('[class*="captcha"], [id*="captcha"], iframe[src*="recaptcha"]');
    const captchaCount = await captcha.count();
    if (captchaCount > 0) {
      // Alternative: email link, passkey, or magic link button
      const alternative = page.locator(
        'a[href*="magic"], button:has-text("Send login link"), button:has-text("Use passkey")'
      );
      await expect(alternative.first()).toBeVisible();
    }
  });

  test('login form has no axe violations', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include('form')
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag22aa'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('forgot password flow does not require typing verification code without paste', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/forgot-password');
    await page.getByLabel(/email/i).fill('user@example.com');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /send|submit/i }).click();
    // If a verification code field appears, it must allow paste
    const codeField = page.getByLabel(/verification code|one-time code/i);
    if (await codeField.isVisible().catch(() => false)) {
      // Paste must not be blocked
      await codeField.focus();
      await page.keyboard.press('Control+v');
      // No error should appear after paste attempt
      await expect(page.locator('[role="alert"]')).not.toBeVisible();
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** WCAG 3.3.8 AA requires an *alternative* to cognitive function tests — it does not ban CAPTCHAs entirely. However, 3.3.9 (AAA) removes all exceptions and bans cognitive function tests entirely. Teams targeting WCAG 2.2 AA only need to ensure an alternative exists; teams targeting AAA must remove all CAPTCHAs. The paste-blocking test is critical because some CAPTCHA and OTP implementations block clipboard paste via JavaScript event listener cancellation, which forces motor-impaired users to type codes manually and fails 3.3.8. [official]

### Pattern 231 — `Pa11y CI` v4.1.1: Per-URL Configuration and Dual-Engine Sitemaps [community]

Pa11y CI v4.1.1 supports per-URL overrides within a single `.pa11yci.json` config file, allowing different WCAG levels or ignore lists for specific pages without creating multiple config files. Combined with a sitemap URL as the target, Pa11y CI can crawl and test an entire site with one command. Pairing Pa11y (HTMLCodeSniffer engine) with `@axe-core/playwright` in CI provides complementary coverage — Pa11y catches HTML structure violations that axe-core's DOM-based checks sometimes miss, and axe-core catches dynamic ARIA and keyboard contract issues that Pa11y's static HTML analysis cannot detect.

```typescript
// .pa11yci.json — per-URL configuration with dual-engine approach
```
```json
{
  "defaults": {
    "standard": "WCAG2AA",
    "runners": ["axe", "htmlcs"],
    "threshold": 0,
    "wait": 1000,
    "chromeLaunchConfig": {
      "args": ["--no-sandbox", "--disable-setuid-sandbox"]
    }
  },
  "urls": [
    "https://example.com/",
    "https://example.com/products",
    {
      "url": "https://example.com/login",
      "standard": "WCAG2AA",
      "ignore": ["WCAG2AA.Principle1.Guideline1_4.1_4_3.G18.BgImage"]
    },
    {
      "url": "https://example.com/admin",
      "standard": "WCAG2AAA",
      "threshold": 3
    }
  ]
}
```

```typescript
// pa11y-ci-runner.ts — programmatic dual-engine execution
import { execSync } from 'child_process';

const result = execSync('npx pa11y-ci --config .pa11yci.json --reporter json', {
  encoding: 'utf8',
  stdio: 'pipe',
});

const report = JSON.parse(result);
const failures = Object.entries(report.results as Record<string, { issues: unknown[] }>)
  .filter(([, r]) => r.issues.length > 0)
  .map(([url, r]) => `${url}: ${r.issues.length} issues`);

if (failures.length > 0) {
  console.error('Pa11y CI failures:\n' + failures.join('\n'));
  process.exit(1);
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Running both the `axe` and `htmlcs` runners in Pa11y doubles scan time per page and can produce duplicate violations for the same underlying issue reported from two different rule perspectives. Teams should de-duplicate results by impact and WCAG criterion before reporting, or run the two engines on different CI job stages (fast axe-only gate on every PR, full dual-engine scan on nightly builds). The `threshold` field allows a per-URL violation budget — use it only as a temporary measure while fixing known issues, not as a permanent baseline. [community]

---

### Pattern 232 — ARIA Spinbutton: Numeric Input with Keyboard Increment/Decrement [official]

`role="spinbutton"` is the ARIA equivalent of `<input type="number">`. It requires `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, and `aria-valuemax`. Arrow Up/Down increment and decrement by one step; Page Up/Down by a larger step; Home/End jump to min/max. When `aria-valuenow` would not be meaningful to a screen reader user (e.g., a date picker month spinbutton showing "1" instead of "January"), `aria-valuetext` overrides the announced value. Custom spinbuttons built from `<div>` elements must manage keyboard events and update all four ARIA attributes.

```typescript
// spinbutton.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('ARIA Spinbutton keyboard contract', () => {
  test('spinbutton has required ARIA value attributes', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/quantity-selector');
    const spin = page.locator('[role="spinbutton"]');
    await expect(spin).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow');
    await expect(spin).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemin');
    await expect(spin).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemax');
  });

  test('ArrowUp increments aria-valuenow', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/quantity-selector');
    const spin = page.locator('[role="spinbutton"]');
    await spin.focus();
    const before = parseInt((await spin.getAttribute('aria-valuenow')) ?? '0', 10);
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowUp');
    const after = parseInt((await spin.getAttribute('aria-valuenow')) ?? '0', 10);
    expect(after).toBe(before + 1);
  });

  test('ArrowDown decrements aria-valuenow and stops at aria-valuemin', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/quantity-selector');
    const spin = page.locator('[role="spinbutton"]');
    await spin.focus();
    // Press Home to jump to minimum
    await page.keyboard.press('Home');
    const min = parseInt((await spin.getAttribute('aria-valuemin')) ?? '0', 10);
    // Another ArrowDown should not go below minimum
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
    const val = parseInt((await spin.getAttribute('aria-valuenow')) ?? '0', 10);
    expect(val).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(min);
  });

  test('aria-valuetext is present for non-numeric display values', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/month-picker');
    const spin = page.locator('[role="spinbutton"]');
    // Month spinbutton should expose text like "January" not "1"
    const valueText = await spin.getAttribute('aria-valuetext');
    if (valueText) {
      expect(valueText).toMatch(/^[A-Z]/); // starts with capital letter — a month name
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `<input type="number">` provides native spinbutton semantics, automatic ARIA attributes, and cross-browser keyboard support without any JavaScript. Custom `role="spinbutton"` widgets are only necessary when `<input type="number">` cannot meet visual design requirements (e.g., custom spinner arrows, unit labels inline with the field). The most common failure in custom spinbuttons is not clamping `aria-valuenow` at the min/max boundary on keyboard navigation — the DOM value updates correctly but the ARIA attribute continues past the valid range, causing screen readers to announce impossible values. [official]

### Pattern 233 — WCAG 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus: Tooltip Dismiss, Hover, and Persist Tests [official]

WCAG 1.4.13 requires that tooltip/popover content triggered by hover or focus meets three conditions: (1) Dismissible — the user can dismiss it without moving focus (typically Escape key); (2) Hoverable — the pointer can move onto the triggered content without it disappearing (so the user can interact with a tooltip that contains a link); (3) Persistent — the content stays visible until the trigger loses hover/focus, the user dismisses it, or it becomes invalid. CSS-only tooltips using `:hover` pseudo-class fail condition 1 (no Escape dismiss) and sometimes condition 2 (tooltip disappears when pointer moves off trigger).

```typescript
// tooltip-hover-focus.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('WCAG 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus', () => {
  test('tooltip appears on focus', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const trigger = page.locator('[data-tooltip], [aria-describedby]').first();
    await trigger.focus();
    const tooltipId = await trigger.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
    if (tooltipId) {
      await expect(page.locator(`#${tooltipId}`)).toBeVisible();
    }
  });

  test('tooltip is dismissible with Escape without moving focus', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const trigger = page.locator('[data-tooltip]').first();
    await trigger.focus();
    // Tooltip should be visible
    const tooltipText = await trigger.getAttribute('data-tooltip');
    // Press Escape — tooltip must disappear, focus must remain on trigger
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();
    // Tooltip should be hidden
    const tooltip = page.locator(`[role="tooltip"]:visible`);
    await expect(tooltip).toHaveCount(0);
  });

  test('tooltip content remains visible when pointer moves from trigger to tooltip', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const trigger = page.locator('[data-tooltip]').first();
    const triggerBox = await trigger.boundingBox();
    if (!triggerBox) return;
    // Hover trigger
    await page.mouse.move(triggerBox.x + triggerBox.width / 2, triggerBox.y + triggerBox.height / 2);
    // Tooltip should be visible
    const tooltip = page.locator('[role="tooltip"]:visible').first();
    await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible();
    // Move pointer to tooltip
    const tooltipBox = await tooltip.boundingBox();
    if (tooltipBox) {
      await page.mouse.move(tooltipBox.x + 5, tooltipBox.y + 5);
      // Tooltip must still be visible (hoverable condition)
      await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible();
    }
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Testing the "hoverable" condition requires mouse movement simulation with `page.mouse.move()`, which is straightforward in Playwright but can be flaky in headless environments where hover state tracking differs from headed mode. The "persistent" condition (tooltip stays until dismissed) is hardest to automate because it requires confirming that a timeout-based auto-dismiss is not shorter than 5 seconds. The WCAG understanding document does not mandate a minimum persistence duration — it requires only that the content is not dismissed by a timer that the user cannot control. Manual review is recommended for timer-based tooltips alongside the automated hover and dismiss tests. [official]

---

### Pattern 234 — `locator.normalize()`: Whitespace-Normalised Text Matching for Accessible Name Assertions [community]

Playwright 1.50+ added `locator.normalize()` as a string normalisation helper for accessible name assertions. When accessible names are computed from text content that contains irregular whitespace (multiple spaces, ` ` non-breaking spaces, newlines from inline elements), `toHaveAccessibleName()` can fail with whitespace mismatch errors even though the screen reader announces the correct name. `locator.normalize()` normalises the accessible name string before comparison.

```typescript
// accessible-name-normalize.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Accessible name whitespace normalisation (Playwright 1.50+)', () => {
  test('button accessible name matches despite whitespace in DOM', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // The button's DOM structure: <button><span>Save  </span><span> document</span></button>
    // Computed accessible name has irregular whitespace from span concatenation
    const btn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /save/i });
    // Normalize trims and collapses whitespace before assertion
    await expect(btn).toHaveAccessibleName('Save document');
  });

  test('link text with non-breaking spaces is correctly compared', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/nav');
    // Some CMS systems inject &nbsp; between words — e.g., "Home Page"
    const link = page.getByRole('link').first();
    const rawName = await link.evaluate(el => el.textContent ?? '');
    // Normalise: replace nbsp and collapse spaces
    const normalised = rawName.replace(/ /g, ' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
    await expect(link).toHaveAccessibleName(normalised);
  });

  test('icon button accessible name is sourced from aria-label not icon glyph', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/toolbar');
    // Icon buttons should have aria-label — icon text (e.g., "✕") should not be the accessible name
    const closeBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /close|dismiss/i });
    await expect(closeBtn).toBeVisible();
    // Verify aria-label is the source, not the raw icon character
    const ariaLabel = await closeBtn.getAttribute('aria-label');
    expect(ariaLabel).toBeTruthy();
    expect(ariaLabel).not.toMatch(/^[^\w\s]/); // must not start with a symbol/emoji
  });

  test('form field accessible name from label element is correctly resolved', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    const emailField = page.getByLabel('Email address');
    await expect(emailField).toHaveAccessibleName('Email address');
    await expect(emailField).toHaveAttribute('type', 'email');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `locator.normalize()` is a convenience method but it can mask genuine whitespace bugs in accessible names. A button with an accessible name of `"Save   document"` (three spaces) would pass a normalised assertion but would cause screen readers to announce unusual pauses. Use normalised assertions for regression tests where you control the expected text, but also run a raw whitespace audit as a separate test to catch CMS-injected or dynamically generated accessible names that contain unexpected characters. [community]

---

### Pattern 235 — Guidepup: Automated VoiceOver/NVDA Screen Reader Testing in CI [community]

Guidepup is a Node.js library that drives macOS VoiceOver and Windows NVDA screen readers programmatically, enabling automated tests that verify what a real screen reader actually announces — not what ARIA attributes *should* announce. This closes the gap between ARIA compliance (which axe-core verifies) and actual AT output (which Guidepup verifies). Guidepup integrates with Playwright via `@guidepup/playwright` and supports TypeScript.

```typescript
// voiceover-nav.spec.ts — Guidepup VoiceOver automated test
// Requires: macOS with VoiceOver, @guidepup/playwright installed
// Run with: GUIDEPUP_VOICEOVER=true npx playwright test voiceover-nav.spec.ts

import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { voiceOverTest } from '@guidepup/playwright';

voiceOverTest.describe('Homepage VoiceOver navigation', () => {
  voiceOverTest('announces page title on load', async ({ page, voiceOver }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    // Start VoiceOver and navigate to the page
    await voiceOver.navigate();

    // Read the first item announced
    const firstAnnouncement = await voiceOver.lastSpokenPhrase();
    expect(firstAnnouncement).toMatch(/home|welcome/i);
  });

  voiceOverTest('main navigation links are announced with correct roles', async ({ page, voiceOver }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    // Move to landmark navigation
    await voiceOver.perform(voiceOver.keyboardCommands.moveToNextLandmark);
    const navAnnouncement = await voiceOver.lastSpokenPhrase();
    expect(navAnnouncement).toMatch(/navigation/i);

    // Tab through links — each must be announced as "link"
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      await voiceOver.perform(voiceOver.keyboardCommands.moveToNextItem);
      const phrase = await voiceOver.lastSpokenPhrase();
      if (phrase.toLowerCase().includes('link')) {
        expect(phrase).toMatch(/link/i);
      }
    }
  });

  voiceOverTest('form error is announced after failed submission', async ({ page, voiceOver }) => {
    await page.goto('/contact');
    // Submit empty form
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();
    // VoiceOver should announce the error message
    await voiceOver.perform(voiceOver.keyboardCommands.moveToNextItem);
    const errorAnnouncement = await voiceOver.lastSpokenPhrase();
    expect(errorAnnouncement).toMatch(/error|required|invalid/i);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Guidepup tests require the actual operating system screen reader to be installed and enabled — VoiceOver tests can only run on macOS, NVDA tests only on Windows. This makes Guidepup tests unsuitable for standard Linux CI agents (GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest, etc.). Teams must maintain separate CI jobs on macOS or Windows runners, which cost significantly more than Linux runners. For most teams, Guidepup is most practical as a periodic manual-automation tool (run weekly on a dedicated macOS machine) rather than a per-PR gate. The axe-core + ARIA snapshot combination covers automated per-PR accessibility regression; Guidepup validates actual AT output on a longer cadence. [community]

---

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 50)

226. **[community] `aria-hidden="true"` on a parent element hides all descendants from the accessibility tree — but if a descendant element has `tabindex="0"` or is a natively focusable element (`<a href>`, `<button>`, `<input>`), keyboard users can still Tab to it even though screen readers cannot perceive it, creating a "ghost focus" that traps keyboard users inside invisible content**: When a keyboard user Tabs into an `aria-hidden="true"` subtree, their focus position becomes invisible to them (no visual feedback other than the browser's own focus ring, no screen reader announcement), and they cannot tell where they are in the document. WHY: Developers use `aria-hidden="true"` to hide decorative overlays or collapsed panels from screen readers while forgetting that `aria-hidden` does not affect focusability — it only affects the accessibility tree. The correct pattern is to combine `aria-hidden="true"` with `inert` (the HTML `inert` attribute, now broadly supported since 2023) or to programmatically set `tabindex="-1"` on all focusable descendants when the container is hidden from the AT. [community]

227. **[community] The `role="button"` ARIA attribute on a `<div>` or `<span>` makes the element announced as a button by screen readers but does not give it native button behaviour — it does not respond to Enter or Space keypresses, does not participate in form submission, and does not fire a `click` event on Space bar without an explicit `keydown` event listener, causing keyboard users to experience broken activation**: Native `<button>` elements fire `click` on both Enter and Space by default. A `<div role="button">` requires explicit JavaScript `keydown` event listeners for both `Enter` and `Space` to replicate this behaviour. WHY: Developers prototype with `<div role="button">` for styling flexibility and then forget to add the keyboard event handlers, or they add only the `click` listener (which responds to Enter in some browsers but not Space). The axe-core rule `keyboard` catches elements with interactive roles that are not focusable (missing `tabindex`), but it does not detect the missing Space-key handler — this requires manual or Playwright keyboard contract testing. Always prefer `<button>` and style it with CSS; use `role="button"` only when the element's tag truly cannot be changed. [community]

228. **[community] CSS `pointer-events: none` on an element removes it from mouse interaction but does not remove it from the accessibility tree or keyboard tab order — screen reader users and keyboard users can still reach and "activate" elements styled with `pointer-events: none`, which often produces JavaScript errors or no-op activations because the element's click handlers assume pointer-events are enabled**: Teams use `pointer-events: none` to disable visual interaction (e.g., a "disabled" state for a custom component) without updating the element's ARIA state (`aria-disabled="true"`) or removing its focusability. Screen readers announce these elements as interactive and fully operable. WHY: CSS visual states and accessibility states are entirely separate layers. A visually "disabled" element that still has `tabindex="0"` and `role="button"` without `aria-disabled="true"` is announced as an enabled button. The fix is three-part: set `aria-disabled="true"`, set `tabindex="-1"` (or leave natively disabled via `disabled` attribute on `<button>`), and set `pointer-events: none`. All three must be coordinated or partial fixes create new accessibility bugs. [community]

229. **[community] When using `React.StrictMode`, React renders components twice in development mode (since React 18, only in development), which causes `@axe-core/react` to fire the accessibility scan twice — the second scan runs against the double-render DOM, which may contain duplicate IDs from the double-invocation of `useId()` in older React 17 code, generating false-positive `duplicate-id` violations in development that do not appear in production**: `@axe-core/react` attaches a `setTimeout`-based callback after each React render. In StrictMode, the component mounts, unmounts, and remounts, triggering multiple axe scans. If IDs are generated non-idempotently (e.g., a global counter), the double render produces duplicate IDs that axe flags. WHY: Developers see `duplicate-id` violations in their development console (where StrictMode is active) and add suppressions to their axe configuration, masking real duplicate-ID bugs that appear in other parts of the application. The correct fix is to use React 18's `useId()` hook (which generates stable IDs across double renders in StrictMode) rather than manual counters or `Math.random()`-based ID generation. [community]

230. **[community] Playwright's `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` fails when the component under test contains dynamically generated IDs in ARIA attribute values (e.g., `aria-describedby="tooltip-1729384756"`) because the snapshot records the exact ID string, and the ID changes on every test run — teams add the snapshot to version control and find it fails in CI because the timestamp-based ID is different from the one captured during snapshot generation**: ARIA snapshot YAML captures the resolved accessible name and description text (dereferencing `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` to their text content), not the raw attribute values — but if the referenced element is not in the scoped snapshot, the ID reference is captured as a raw string. WHY: Developers scope aria snapshots to a component subtree that contains the trigger but not the tooltip/description element it references. The snapshot records `describedby: "tooltip-1729384756"` as a literal string. The fix is either to scope the snapshot to include both the trigger and the referenced element, or to use `page.locator().ariaSnapshot({ refs: false })` (if available) to exclude reference resolution, or to use stable ID generation (CSS Modules, design system tokens) so IDs are deterministic across runs. [community]

---

### Key Resources — Cycle 50

| Name | Type | URL | Why useful |
|------|------|-----|------------|
| ARIA APG Grid Pattern | Official | https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/ | Two-dimensional arrow key model; roving tabindex; aria-rowcount/aria-colcount for virtual scroll; data grid vs layout grid distinction |
| ARIA APG Toolbar Pattern | Official | https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/ | Arrow key intra-toolbar navigation; single tab stop; aria-label required; F6 pane cycling |
| ARIA APG Feed Pattern | Official | https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/feed/ | role=feed + role=article structure; Page Down/Up navigation; aria-busy loading state; unique article labels |
| ARIA APG Window Splitter Pattern | Official | https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/ | role=separator with valuenow/min/max; Arrow key resize; Home/End extremes; F6 pane focus cycling |
| ARIA APG Spinbutton Pattern | Official | https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/spinbutton/ | ArrowUp/Down increment; Page Up/Down large step; Home/End min/max; aria-valuetext for non-numeric display |
