## Cycle 52 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 251 — ARIA Menubar: Full Keyboard Contract Testing with Sub-menus [official]

The ARIA APG menubar pattern requires a specific keyboard contract that differs from most other composite widgets: Arrow-key navigation is used within the menubar and its sub-menus (not Tab), while Tab and Shift+Tab exit the menubar entirely. Parent menuitems must carry `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded` to communicate sub-menu state to screen readers.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('menubar: full keyboard navigation contract', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/navigation');

  const menubar = page.getByRole('menubar');
  await expect(menubar).toBeVisible();

  // Focus the first menuitem with keyboard
  const firstItem = menubar.getByRole('menuitem').first();
  await firstItem.focus();
  await expect(firstItem).toBeFocused();

  // Right Arrow moves to the next menuitem in the menubar
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
  const secondItem = menubar.getByRole('menuitem').nth(1);
  await expect(secondItem).toBeFocused();

  // Enter or ArrowDown opens a sub-menu
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  const submenu = page.getByRole('menu').first();
  await expect(submenu).toBeVisible();
  await expect(secondItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

  // Escape closes the sub-menu and returns focus to the parent menuitem
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(submenu).toBeHidden();
  await expect(secondItem).toBeFocused();
  await expect(secondItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

  // Tab moves focus completely out of the menubar
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  await expect(firstItem).not.toBeFocused();
  await expect(secondItem).not.toBeFocused();
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The menubar Arrow-key-only model is correct per the ARIA APG but is unfamiliar to many developers who default to Tab-navigation. Testing only `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded` presence is insufficient — the keyboard contract (ArrowRight/Down opens, Escape closes, Tab exits) must be verified end-to-end. Automated axe scans do not test keyboard event flows, so this pattern must be a manual-or-Playwright test. [official]

---

### Pattern 252 — ARIA Listbox: Single-Select and Multi-Select Keyboard Contract [official]

A `role="listbox"` widget requires Arrow-key navigation between options, Home/End jumps to first/last, and typeahead character search. Single-select listboxes move focus-and-selection together; multi-select listboxes require Space to toggle selection independently of focus movement. The `aria-multiselectable` attribute on the container distinguishes the two modes.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('listbox: single-select keyboard navigation and selection', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/components/country-selector');

  const listbox = page.getByRole('listbox', { name: /country/i });
  await listbox.focus();

  // First option is focused/selected by default
  const firstOption = listbox.getByRole('option').first();
  await expect(firstOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');

  // Arrow Down moves focus to second option and selects it
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  const secondOption = listbox.getByRole('option').nth(1);
  await expect(secondOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
  await expect(firstOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'false');

  // End jumps to last option
  await page.keyboard.press('End');
  const lastOption = listbox.getByRole('option').last();
  await expect(lastOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');

  // Home jumps back to first
  await page.keyboard.press('Home');
  await expect(firstOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');

  // Verify aria-multiselectable is absent or false for single-select
  const isMulti = await listbox.getAttribute('aria-multiselectable');
  expect(isMulti).not.toBe('true');
});

test('listbox: multi-select Space toggles without moving selection', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/components/permissions-selector');
  const listbox = page.getByRole('listbox', { name: /permissions/i });
  await expect(listbox).toHaveAttribute('aria-multiselectable', 'true');

  await listbox.focus();
  const firstOption = listbox.getByRole('option').first();

  // Space selects without deselecting others
  await page.keyboard.press('Space');
  await expect(firstOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');

  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  await page.keyboard.press('Space');
  const secondOption = listbox.getByRole('option').nth(1);
  await expect(secondOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
  // First option remains selected in multi-select
  await expect(firstOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Multi-select listboxes are tricky: the recommended APG pattern uses Space to toggle without a modifier key, but an alternative pattern uses Shift+Arrow for range selection. Teams must choose one model and test it consistently. The simpler Space-toggle model has better AT compatibility; the Shift+Arrow model feels more natural for power users but is more complex to implement correctly. axe-core checks that `role="option"` elements are children of a listbox and have `aria-selected`, but does not test keyboard behavior. [official]

---

### Pattern 253 — ARIA Tree View: Expand/Collapse and Keyboard Navigation Testing [official]

The ARIA tree view pattern uses `role="tree"` as a container, `role="treeitem"` for each node, and `role="group"` to wrap child nodes. Nodes with children must carry `aria-expanded`. The Asterisk key is a required shortcut that expands all sibling nodes at the current level — a frequently omitted implementation detail. Arrow-key navigation follows: Right expands or moves into first child, Left collapses or moves to parent, Up/Down move between visible nodes.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('tree view: expand/collapse keyboard contract', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/file-explorer');

  const tree = page.getByRole('tree', { name: /file explorer/i });
  await expect(tree).toBeVisible();

  const rootItem = tree.getByRole('treeitem').first();
  await rootItem.focus();

  // Initially collapsed — aria-expanded="false"
  await expect(rootItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

  // Right Arrow expands the node
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
  await expect(rootItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

  // The child group is now visible
  const childGroup = rootItem.getByRole('group');
  await expect(childGroup).toBeVisible();

  // Right Arrow again moves focus to first child
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
  const firstChild = childGroup.getByRole('treeitem').first();
  await expect(firstChild).toBeFocused();

  // Left Arrow on a child moves focus to parent
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft');
  await expect(rootItem).toBeFocused();

  // Left Arrow on expanded parent collapses it
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft');
  await expect(rootItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

  // Home/End navigate to first/last visible treeitem
  await page.keyboard.press('End');
  const lastItem = tree.getByRole('treeitem').last();
  await expect(lastItem).toBeFocused();
});

test('tree view: aria-level, aria-setsize, aria-posinset on dynamic nodes', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/file-explorer');
  const treeitems = page.getByRole('treeitem');

  // Each treeitem must report its level
  const firstItem = treeitems.first();
  await expect(firstItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-level');
  const level = await firstItem.getAttribute('aria-level');
  expect(Number(level)).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The Asterisk (*) key to expand all siblings is part of the APG specification but is rarely tested and commonly omitted. When building automated tests, expanding all siblings requires knowing which `treeitem` elements share a parent — this is difficult to query programmatically and is best tested as a dedicated test case rather than incorporated into a broad keyboard sweep. For lazy-loaded trees, `aria-level`/`aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset` are essential because screen readers cannot infer hierarchy from unloaded children. [official]

---

### Pattern 254 — ARIA Grid: `aria-rowcount`/`aria-colcount` for Virtualised Grids [official]

When a data grid virtualises its DOM (rendering only visible rows), `aria-rowcount` and `aria-colcount` on the `role="grid"` element communicate the true total dimensions to screen readers. Without these attributes, a screen reader reports the grid as having only as many rows/columns as are currently rendered, misleading users about the amount of data available. Each rendered row and cell must carry `aria-rowindex` and `aria-colindex` (1-based) to communicate their position in the full dataset.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('virtual grid: aria-rowcount and aria-colcount reflect full dataset', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/data-table?rows=10000');

  const grid = page.getByRole('grid', { name: /transactions/i });
  await expect(grid).toBeVisible();

  // aria-rowcount must reflect the full dataset, not just rendered rows
  const rowCount = await grid.getAttribute('aria-rowcount');
  expect(Number(rowCount)).toBeGreaterThan(100); // much more than the DOM rows

  // Spot-check that aria-colcount is present
  const colCount = await grid.getAttribute('aria-colcount');
  expect(colCount).not.toBeNull();

  // Every rendered row must have a unique aria-rowindex
  const rows = await grid.getByRole('row').all();
  const rowIndices = new Set<string>();
  for (const row of rows) {
    const idx = await row.getAttribute('aria-rowindex');
    expect(idx).not.toBeNull();
    if (idx) rowIndices.add(idx);
  }
  expect(rowIndices.size).toBe(rows.length); // all unique

  // columnheader cells must have aria-colindex
  const headers = await grid.getByRole('columnheader').all();
  for (const header of headers) {
    await expect(header).toHaveAttribute('aria-colindex');
  }
});

test('grid: Enter/Escape cell edit mode contract', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/editable-grid');
  const grid = page.getByRole('grid');
  const editableCell = grid.getByRole('gridcell', { name: /edit/i }).first();

  await editableCell.focus();
  // Enter should activate edit mode
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  const cellInput = editableCell.getByRole('textbox');
  await expect(cellInput).toBeFocused();

  // Escape should exit edit mode and return focus to the cell
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(editableCell).toBeFocused();
  await expect(cellInput).not.toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `aria-rowcount=-1` is a valid value telling screen readers the total is unknown (for infinite-scroll grids without a known total). Use `-1` deliberately and document it — do not use it as a shortcut to avoid implementing the count, because `-1` versus an incorrect positive count produce different AT announcement behaviours. Virtual lists that use `role="list"` rather than `role="grid"` should use `aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset` on `role="listitem"` elements instead. [official]

---

### Pattern 255 — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size Minimum: CSS Geometry Measurement and Spacing Offset Algorithm [official]

WCAG 2.5.8 (AA, new in WCAG 2.2) requires that interactive targets are at least 24×24 CSS pixels. Targets smaller than 24×24 are permitted if a 24 CSS-pixel-diameter circle centered on each target's bounding box does not intersect another target or the circle of another undersized target. Playwright can measure `getBoundingClientRect()` and calculate the spacing offset to verify compliance programmatically.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface TargetMetrics {
  width: number;
  height: number;
  cx: number; // bounding box center X
  cy: number; // bounding box center Y
}

test('WCAG 2.5.8: icon buttons meet 24×24 minimum or have sufficient spacing', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/toolbar');

  const iconButtons = page.locator('button[aria-label], [role="button"][aria-label]');
  const count = await iconButtons.count();

  const metrics: TargetMetrics[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const btn = iconButtons.nth(i);
    const rect = await btn.evaluate((el) => {
      const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      return { width: r.width, height: r.height, left: r.left, top: r.top, right: r.right, bottom: r.bottom };
    });

    const cx = (rect.left + rect.right) / 2;
    const cy = (rect.top + rect.bottom) / 2;
    metrics.push({ width: rect.width, height: rect.height, cx, cy });

    const meets24x24 = rect.width >= 24 && rect.height >= 24;
    if (!meets24x24) {
      // Check spacing offset: 24px-diameter circles must not intersect
      // For simplicity, verify no other target centre is within 24px
      const label = await btn.getAttribute('aria-label');
      console.warn(`Target "${label}" is ${rect.width}×${rect.height}px — checking spacing offset`);
    }
  }

  // Spacing check: for undersized targets, centres must be ≥ 24px apart
  const undersized = metrics.filter(m => m.width < 24 || m.height < 24);
  for (let i = 0; i < undersized.length; i++) {
    for (let j = i + 1; j < undersized.length; j++) {
      const dx = undersized[i].cx - undersized[j].cx;
      const dy = undersized[i].cy - undersized[j].cy;
      const distance = Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
      expect(distance).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(24); // circles must not intersect
    }
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The spacing offset algorithm applies only between undersized targets — a 20×20 button next to a 30×30 button only needs to verify that the 20×20 button's spacing circle does not intersect the adjacent target, not the larger button's circle. Testing this exhaustively in Playwright is feasible for toolbars and action rows with known layouts but becomes complex in dynamic or responsive layouts where positions change. The CSS technique `min-width: 24px; min-height: 24px` (C42) is simpler and should be the implementation preference; the Playwright test serves as a regression guard for designers who reduce button sizes. [official]

---

### Pattern 256 — `jest-axe` with `configureAxe` for Component-Scoped Rules and `impactLevels` Progressive Rollout [community]

`jest-axe` wraps axe-core for unit tests in JSDOM. The `configureAxe` factory creates a reusable axe instance with team-specific defaults: disabling rules that generate false positives in isolated component tests (e.g., `region`, `landmark-one-main`) and enabling `impactLevels` to gate CI on `critical` and `serious` violations only while continuing to surface lower-severity issues for review. This enables a staged rollout without blocking CI on every legacy component.

```typescript
import { render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { configureAxe, toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'; // or Jest

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

// Shared axe instance: disables context-only rules for unit tests,
// scoped to critical/serious violations for CI gate
const axe = configureAxe({
  rules: {
    // Disable landmark rules — unit tests render single components, not full pages
    region: { enabled: false },
    'landmark-one-main': { enabled: false },
    'page-has-heading-one': { enabled: false },
  },
  // Stage 1: block only critical + serious; moderate/minor are warnings
  impactLevels: ['critical', 'serious'],
});

describe('Button component', () => {
  it('has no critical or serious axe violations', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <button type="button" aria-label="Close dialog">
        ✕
      </button>
    );
    const results = await axe(container);
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('has no violations with disabled state', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <button type="button" disabled aria-disabled="true">
        Save
      </button>
    );
    const results = await axe(container);
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });
});

// React portal pattern: use baseElement for portals (modals, tooltips)
it('modal portal has no critical axe violations', async () => {
  const { baseElement } = render(<Modal isOpen={true} title="Confirm" />);
  const results = await axe(baseElement);
  expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
});
```

**Tradeoff.** `configureAxe` with `impactLevels: ['critical', 'serious']` only fails the test for those impact levels; `moderate` and `minor` violations are still reported in the results object but do not cause the assertion to fail. Teams must consciously schedule reviews of the lower-severity violations — they will not self-surface as CI failures. Color contrast violations also do not work in JSDOM (they require a real browser rendering engine), so `jest-axe` should be paired with Playwright/AxeBuilder for contrast testing. [community]

---

### Pattern 257 — `@axe-core/playwright` AxeBuilder: Tagging WCAG 2.2 AA Scans and Attaching Reports to CI Artefacts [official]

`@axe-core/playwright` integrates axe-core into Playwright tests via the `AxeBuilder` class. Using `.withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])` explicitly targets WCAG 2.2 AA rules. Attaching the full axe scan JSON to the Playwright test report via `testInfo.attach()` provides auditable evidence for WCAG conformance reporting and VPAT generation.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('WCAG 2.2 AA: full-page axe scan with CI artefact attachment', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
    .exclude('.third-party-widget') // known third-party, tracked separately
    .analyze();

  // Attach full scan results as a CI artefact (visible in Playwright HTML report)
  await testInfo.attach('axe-scan-dashboard.json', {
    body: JSON.stringify(results, null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  // Build a concise violation summary for readable assertion failure messages
  const violationSummary = results.violations.map((v) => ({
    id: v.id,
    impact: v.impact,
    description: v.description,
    nodes: v.nodes.length,
    helpUrl: v.helpUrl,
  }));

  expect(
    violationSummary,
    `Found ${violationSummary.length} WCAG 2.2 AA violations:\n` +
      JSON.stringify(violationSummary, null, 2)
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});

test('WCAG 2.2 AA: scoped scan on checkout form only', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .include('#checkout-form')
    .withTags(['wcag22aa', 'best-practice'])
    .analyze();

  await testInfo.attach('axe-checkout-form.json', {
    body: JSON.stringify(results.violations, null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Adding `wcag22aa` to `.withTags()` enables the WCAG 2.2-specific axe rules (e.g., target-size, ARIA 1.2 updates), but axe-core's automated coverage of WCAG 2.2 new criteria is partial — particularly 2.5.8 Target Size, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry, and 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication require supplementary manual or Playwright geometry tests. The `testInfo.attach()` pattern is essential for VPAT workflows: the JSON artefact can be post-processed by EARL report tools to generate machine-readable conformance evidence. [official]

---

### Pattern 258 — WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication: `autocomplete` Attribute and Paste-Blocking Detection [official]

WCAG 3.3.8 (AA) prohibits authentication flows that require users to solve cognitive function tests (recognise characters, solve puzzles) without providing an alternative mechanism, an object recognition alternative, or personal content recognition. The most common technical failure is disabling clipboard paste on password fields (`onpaste="return false"`) and failing to expose `autocomplete="current-password"` — both of which prevent password manager auto-fill and penalise users with cognitive or motor disabilities.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 3.3.8: password fields allow paste and have autocomplete', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');

  const passwordField = page.getByLabel(/password/i);
  await expect(passwordField).toBeVisible();

  // Must expose autocomplete="current-password" for password managers
  await expect(passwordField).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', 'current-password');

  // Paste must not be blocked — programmatically simulate a paste event
  await passwordField.focus();
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    const field = document.querySelector('input[type="password"]') as HTMLInputElement;
    if (!field) return;
    const pasteEvent = new ClipboardEvent('paste', {
      bubbles: true,
      cancelable: true,
      clipboardData: new DataTransfer(),
    });
    pasteEvent.clipboardData!.setData('text/plain', 'TestPassword123!');
    const wasCancelled = !field.dispatchEvent(pasteEvent);
    (window as Window & { __pasteWasCancelled?: boolean }).__pasteWasCancelled = wasCancelled;
  });
  const pasteBlocked = await page.evaluate(
    () => (window as Window & { __pasteWasCancelled?: boolean }).__pasteWasCancelled
  );
  expect(pasteBlocked).toBe(false); // paste must NOT be blocked

  // Verify no cognitive CAPTCHA is required without alternative
  const captchaPresent = await page.locator('[class*="captcha"], [id*="captcha"]').count();
  if (captchaPresent > 0) {
    // Must have an alternative — e.g., audio CAPTCHA or email OTP
    const captchaAlternative = page.getByText(/audio|email.*code|sms|one-time/i);
    await expect(captchaAlternative).toBeVisible();
  }
});

test('WCAG 3.3.8: new account registration exposes autocomplete on all fields', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/register');

  // Email/username field
  const emailField = page.getByLabel(/email/i);
  await expect(emailField).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', /email|username/);

  // New password field
  const newPasswordField = page.getByLabel(/^password$/i);
  await expect(newPasswordField).toHaveAttribute('autocomplete', 'new-password');
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Paste detection via `dispatchEvent` tests whether the application cancels the paste event via JavaScript (`event.preventDefault()`), which is the most common anti-paste implementation. However, paste can also be blocked via `oncopy`, `oncut`, and `onpaste` HTML attributes in addition to `addEventListener` — the `dispatchEvent` approach catches inline handlers (because `returnValue = false` also cancels) but may miss edge cases in older frameworks that intercept at a higher level. Supplement programmatic tests with a manual checklist step: physically paste a value from the OS clipboard in the test environment. [official]

---

### Pattern 259 — `prefers-reduced-motion`: Asserting Animation Suppression and CSS Media Query Emulation [official]

`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is a CSS media query that users enable in their OS accessibility settings to request minimal motion. Playwright can emulate this preference to verify that animations, transitions, and auto-playing content are suppressed. The Web Animations API and CSS `transition`/`animation` properties must both be checked, as they are controlled independently.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Reduced-motion context: emulate OS setting
const reducedMotionTest = test.extend<{}>({});

test('prefers-reduced-motion: page animations are suppressed', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext({
    reducedMotion: 'reduce',
  });
  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto('/landing');

  // Hero section animation should be suppressed
  const heroSection = page.locator('[data-animate="hero"]');
  const animationDuration = await heroSection.evaluate((el) => {
    return parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).animationDuration || '0');
  });
  // With prefers-reduced-motion, animations should be 0s or near-0s
  expect(animationDuration).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0.01);

  // Auto-playing carousel must be paused
  const carousel = page.locator('[data-component="carousel"]');
  if (await carousel.count() > 0) {
    const isPaused = await carousel.evaluate((el) =>
      el.getAttribute('data-playing') === 'false' ||
      el.classList.contains('paused')
    );
    expect(isPaused).toBe(true);
  }

  // CSS transitions must also be suppressed
  const transitionBtn = page.getByRole('button').first();
  const transitionDuration = await transitionBtn.evaluate((el) => {
    return parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).transitionDuration || '0');
  });
  expect(transitionDuration).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0.01);

  await context.close();
});

// Playwright config-level emulation (playwright.config.ts)
// use: { reducedMotion: 'reduce' }
// Applies to ALL tests in the project when set globally
```

**Tradeoff.** Playwright's `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` only emulates the CSS media query — it does not pause the Web Animations API's `Animation.playState`. Applications that animate via `element.animate()` or a JavaScript animation library (GSAP, Framer Motion) must listen to the media query in JavaScript (`window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')`) and pause/skip animations programmatically. A Playwright test that only checks CSS properties will pass even if JavaScript animations continue. For complete coverage, test both the CSS computed values and a JavaScript `Animation` object's `playState` property on known animated elements. [official]

---

### Pattern 260 — ARIA `role="tooltip"` and `aria-describedby`: Accessible Tooltip Implementation and Testing [official]

The ARIA `tooltip` role conveys supplementary contextual information that appears on hover or focus. The owning element must reference the tooltip via `aria-describedby`, not `aria-labelledby` — the tooltip supplements the accessible name, it does not replace it. WCAG 1.4.13 additionally requires tooltip content to be dismissible (Escape), hoverable (pointer can enter the tooltip without it disappearing), and persistent (tooltip stays until dismissed).

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('tooltip: aria-describedby connects trigger to tooltip', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/components/tooltip-demo');

  const trigger = page.getByRole('button', { name: /info/i });
  const tooltipId = await trigger.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
  expect(tooltipId).toBeTruthy();

  // Tooltip element must exist in the DOM with the matching id and role
  const tooltip = page.locator(`#${tooltipId}`);
  await expect(tooltip).toBeAttached();
  await expect(tooltip).toHaveAttribute('role', 'tooltip');

  // Before hover: tooltip should be hidden (not visible)
  await expect(tooltip).not.toBeVisible();

  // Hover trigger: tooltip becomes visible
  await trigger.hover();
  await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible();

  // WCAG 1.4.13: tooltip must be hoverable (pointer can move into it)
  const triggerBox = await trigger.boundingBox();
  const tooltipBox = await tooltip.boundingBox();
  expect(tooltipBox).not.toBeNull();
  // Move pointer from trigger to tooltip — tooltip must remain visible
  if (triggerBox && tooltipBox) {
    await page.mouse.move(
      tooltipBox.x + tooltipBox.width / 2,
      tooltipBox.y + tooltipBox.height / 2,
      { steps: 5 }
    );
  }
  await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible(); // persists while hovering the tooltip

  // WCAG 1.4.13: tooltip must be dismissible via Escape
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(tooltip).not.toBeVisible();
});

test('tooltip: focus also triggers tooltip (keyboard accessibility)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/components/tooltip-demo');
  const trigger = page.getByRole('button', { name: /info/i });
  const tooltipId = await trigger.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
  const tooltip = page.locator(`#${tooltipId}`);

  await trigger.focus();
  await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible();

  // Blur removes tooltip
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  await expect(tooltip).not.toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff.** A tooltip's `aria-describedby` reference must point to an element that is present in the DOM even when hidden (just not visible). Implementations that inject and remove the tooltip DOM node on hover/focus break the `aria-describedby` reference when the element is not shown — screen readers will silently ignore the description. The safer implementation keeps the tooltip in the DOM at all times with `visibility: hidden` or `display: none`, toggling only visibility. Playwright's `toBeAttached()` assertion verifies DOM presence regardless of visibility, while `toBeVisible()` verifies visual display. [official]

---

### Pattern 261 — axe-core `allowlist`: Accepting Third-Party Violations Without Disabling Entire Rules [official]

Production pages often embed third-party widgets (chat bubbles, payment iframes, analytics badges) that have known accessibility violations that the team cannot fix. Disabling the entire axe rule (e.g., disabling `color-contrast` globally) to suppress third-party noise creates blind spots in first-party code. The correct pattern is to use axe-core's `rules` option to disable a rule only within a specific CSS selector scope, or to post-filter results by node's CSS selector to programmatically suppress known third-party violations while leaving the rule active everywhere else.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

// Known third-party violations: map violation ID to the CSS selector of the containing element
const ACCEPTED_THIRD_PARTY_VIOLATIONS: Record<string, string> = {
  'color-contrast': '[data-widget="live-chat"]',
  'image-alt': 'iframe#payment-frame',
};

function filterAcceptedViolations(
  violations: Array<{ id: string; nodes: Array<{ target: string[][] }> }>
) {
  return violations.filter((violation) => {
    const acceptedSelector = ACCEPTED_THIRD_PARTY_VIOLATIONS[violation.id];
    if (!acceptedSelector) return true; // not accepted — include in results

    // Remove only nodes whose target matches the accepted selector
    const firstPartyNodes = violation.nodes.filter(
      (node) => !node.target.some((t) => t.some((s) => s.includes(acceptedSelector)))
    );
    return firstPartyNodes.length > 0; // keep violation if first-party nodes remain
  });
}

test('axe allowlist: first-party violations detected, third-party suppressed', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa'])
    .analyze();

  const firstPartyViolations = filterAcceptedViolations(
    results.violations as Array<{ id: string; nodes: Array<{ target: string[][] }> }>
  );

  expect(
    firstPartyViolations,
    `First-party WCAG violations found:\n${JSON.stringify(firstPartyViolations, null, 2)}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The `filterAcceptedViolations` post-filter approach is explicit about what is being accepted and why; it can be committed to the repository and reviewed in PRs. The alternative — using `.exclude('[data-widget="live-chat"]')` in `AxeBuilder` — is simpler but silently excludes the entire node from all axe rules, not just the accepted violation. This can mask genuine first-party violations that happen to occur within or adjacent to the third-party widget's DOM subtree. The post-filter approach is more surgical and auditable. [official]

---

### Pattern 262 — ARIA `role="status"` Pre-Render Container: Preventing Lost Announcements on Page Load [official]

Screen readers only announce `aria-live` region updates that occur **after** the region is present in the DOM. Content that is rendered into a live region during the initial page load (before the AT has finished reading the page) is frequently silently ignored. The robust pattern is to include an empty `role="status"` or `role="alert"` container in the initial HTML and update its text content dynamically, rather than injecting the container and its content simultaneously.

```typescript
// React pattern: pre-rendered empty status container
// In your HTML template or root component:
// <div role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" id="app-status" />

import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('live region: pre-render container is empty, then updated dynamically', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  const statusContainer = page.locator('[role="status"]#app-status');

  // Container must be present in the initial DOM (pre-rendered)
  await expect(statusContainer).toBeAttached();

  // Container must be empty on page load (announcements come later)
  const initialText = await statusContainer.innerText();
  expect(initialText.trim()).toBe('');

  // Trigger an action that should produce an announcement
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /save/i }).click();

  // Status container must be updated (not a new element injected)
  await expect(statusContainer).not.toBeEmpty();
  const announcement = await statusContainer.innerText();
  expect(announcement).toMatch(/saved|success|updated/i);
});

test('live region: role="alert" for errors uses assertive politeness', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Submit incomplete form
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();

  // Error region must use role="alert" (assertive) for immediate announcement
  const errorRegion = page.locator('[role="alert"]');
  await expect(errorRegion).toBeVisible();
  await expect(errorRegion).not.toBeEmpty();

  // Alert must NOT also have aria-live="polite" — that contradicts assertive semantics
  const ariaLive = await errorRegion.getAttribute('aria-live');
  expect(ariaLive).not.toBe('polite'); // must be "assertive" or absent (alert implies assertive)
});
```

**Tradeoff.** Using `aria-atomic="true"` on a live region causes the entire region's content to be announced whenever any part of it changes. This is correct for short, single-message status regions (e.g., "3 items selected") but wrong for chat message feeds where individual messages should be announced as they arrive. For message feeds, omit `aria-atomic` (default `false`) and update only the new message element. For status summaries, use `aria-atomic="true"` to ensure the full updated summary is read rather than just the changed character substring. [official]

---

### Pattern 263 — `jest-axe` with `jest.useFakeTimers()`: Re-enabling Real Timers for Axe Execution [community]

`jest-axe` internally uses `setTimeout` to debounce its JSDOM scan. When tests use `jest.useFakeTimers()` for debounced component behavior or animation frame testing, the fake timers prevent axe from completing its scan, causing the `await axe()` promise to hang indefinitely or time out. The fix is to temporarily restore real timers before running axe and re-apply fake timers afterward.

```typescript
import { render } from '@testing-library/react';
import { axe, toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach, vi } from 'vitest';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

describe('AutoSave component (uses debounce)', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.useFakeTimers(); // tests need fake timers for debounce assertions
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    vi.useRealTimers();
  });

  it('renders accessible markup despite using fake timers', async () => {
    const { container } = render(<AutoSave delay={500} onSave={vi.fn()} />);

    // Temporarily restore real timers for axe scan
    vi.useRealTimers();
    const results = await axe(container);
    vi.useFakeTimers(); // restore fake timers for remaining test body

    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('debounce fires after delay (fake timers test)', async () => {
    const onSave = vi.fn();
    const { getByRole } = render(<AutoSave delay={500} onSave={onSave} />);

    const input = getByRole('textbox');
    await userEvent.type(input, 'hello');

    expect(onSave).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(500);
    expect(onSave).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff.** The `vi.useRealTimers()` / `vi.useFakeTimers()` sandwich is necessary because axe-core's JSDOM runner uses real `setTimeout` internally and the scan cannot complete with fake timers in place. This is a JSDOM-only limitation; `@axe-core/playwright` runs in a real browser and is not affected. The pattern works with both Jest and Vitest. An alternative for Jest is to call `jest.runAllTimers()` before `axe()`, but this can produce side effects if the component has pending timers that should not have fired yet. The real-timers sandwich is safer. [community]

---

### Pattern 264 — WCAG 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured Enhanced (AAA): Sticky Header Viewport Overlap Detection [official]

WCAG 2.4.11 (AA) requires that focused components are at least partially visible; WCAG 2.4.12 (AAA) requires that no part of a focused component is hidden by author-created content. Sticky headers and footers are the primary failure vector. Playwright can check whether the focused element's bounding box is fully within the viewport minus the sticky element's height, using `scroll-padding-top` as the CSS fix mechanism.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 2.4.12: focused element is not obscured by sticky header (AAA)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/docs/long-page');

  // Get sticky header height
  const stickyHeader = page.locator('header[data-sticky], .sticky-header');
  const headerBox = await stickyHeader.boundingBox();
  const headerHeight = headerBox?.height ?? 0;

  // Tab through all interactive elements and check none are obscured
  const focusableCount = await page.evaluate(() =>
    document.querySelectorAll('a, button, input, select, textarea, [tabindex="0"]').length
  );

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(focusableCount, 20); i++) {
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');

    const focused = page.locator(':focus');
    const focusedBox = await focused.boundingBox();

    if (focusedBox) {
      // WCAG 2.4.12 (AAA): entire focused element must be below the sticky header
      const topEdge = focusedBox.y;
      expect(topEdge).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(headerHeight);
    }
  }
});

test('CSS scroll-padding-top matches sticky header height', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/docs/long-page');

  const stickyHeader = page.locator('header[data-sticky]');
  const headerBox = await stickyHeader.boundingBox();
  const headerHeight = Math.round(headerBox?.height ?? 0);

  // scroll-padding-top must be at least the header height
  const scrollPaddingTop = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).scrollPaddingTop) || 0;
  });

  expect(scrollPaddingTop).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(headerHeight);
});
```

**Tradeoff.** WCAG 2.4.12 is AAA, meaning most teams target 2.4.11 (AA). However, for applications with tall sticky navigation, failing even 2.4.11 (focus partially visible) is a genuine usability failure. The `scroll-padding-top` CSS fix is the simplest mechanism: it instructs the browser's native scroll-to-focused-element behavior to leave space at the top equal to the sticky header height. Without it, the browser scrolls the focused element to the top edge of the viewport, which is covered by the header. The Playwright test is most valuable run after layout changes that alter the sticky header height. [official]

---

### Pattern 265 — ARIA Annotation Roles (`role="insertion"`, `role="deletion"`, `role="mark"`): Accessible Track-Changes [official]

ARIA 1.3 introduced annotation roles for document editing contexts: `role="insertion"` (equivalent to `<ins>`), `role="deletion"` (equivalent to `<del>`), `role="mark"` (equivalent to `<mark>`), `role="suggestion"` (wraps a paired insertion+deletion), and `role="comment"`. These roles allow custom rich text editors that do not use semantic HTML elements to convey tracked-change semantics to screen readers. The `aria-description` attribute (ARIA 1.2+) provides the annotation detail text.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('track-changes editor: insertion/deletion annotations are accessible', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/document-editor?mode=review');

  // All insertions must use role="insertion" or <ins> element
  const insertions = page.locator('[role="insertion"], ins');
  const insertionCount = await insertions.count();
  expect(insertionCount).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // All deletions must use role="deletion" or <del> element
  const deletions = page.locator('[role="deletion"], del');
  const deletionCount = await deletions.count();
  expect(deletionCount).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Suggestions should wrap a paired insertion+deletion
  const suggestions = page.locator('[role="suggestion"]');
  for (const suggestion of await suggestions.all()) {
    const hasInsertion = await suggestion.locator('[role="insertion"], ins').count();
    const hasDeletion = await suggestion.locator('[role="deletion"], del').count();
    expect(hasInsertion + hasDeletion).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  }

  // aria-description provides author/timestamp context on suggestion/comment
  const comments = page.locator('[role="comment"]');
  for (const comment of await comments.all()) {
    const description = await comment.getAttribute('aria-description');
    expect(description).toBeTruthy(); // must describe who added the comment and when
  }
});

test('mark role: highlighted search terms are accessible', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search-results');

  // Search result highlights must use <mark> or role="mark"
  const highlights = page.locator('mark, [role="mark"]');
  const count = await highlights.count();
  expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Highlighted text must be non-empty
  for (const highlight of await highlights.all()) {
    const text = await highlight.innerText();
    expect(text.trim().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  }
});
```

**Tradeoff.** ARIA 1.3 annotation roles have limited AT support as of 2026 — NVDA, JAWS, and VoiceOver have partial support for `role="insertion"` and `role="deletion"` (since they map to the well-established `<ins>` / `<del>` elements), but `role="suggestion"` and `role="comment"` are newer and may be silently ignored by older AT versions. Teams should test with actual screen readers after adopting annotation roles and provide visible author/timestamp text as a fallback, rather than relying solely on `aria-description` for the annotation metadata. [official]

### New Community Gotchas (Cycle 52)

236. **[community] Using `aria-label` on a `<button>` that also contains visible text replaces the visible text as the accessible name — if the `aria-label` wording differs from the visible text, voice control users who say the visible text cannot activate the button (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name failure)**: A common pattern is `<button aria-label="Remove item from cart">Remove</button>` — developers intend the full phrase to be read by screen readers, but voice control users see "Remove" on screen and say "click Remove", which fails because the accessible name is "Remove item from cart". WHY: Voice control software activates elements by matching the spoken phrase against the accessible name, not the visible text. The WCAG 2.5.3 rule requires the accessible name to **contain** the visible text. The fix is either to make `aria-label` start with the visible text (`aria-label="Remove item — Hat size M"`) or to use `aria-describedby` for supplemental context and keep `aria-label` absent so the accessible name is derived from button content. [community]

237. **[community] `aria-hidden="true"` on a focused element does not prevent the element from receiving keyboard focus — the element is removed from the accessibility tree (screen readers skip it) but still participates in the tab order, creating a "ghost focus" where focus moves to an element that screen readers cannot see or describe**: This typically occurs when a modal's trigger button is hidden with `aria-hidden` while the modal is open, but the button retains `tabindex="0"`. A keyboard user pressing Tab can land on the hidden trigger, see no focus indicator (because the button's visible state is gone), and be confused about their position. WHY: `aria-hidden` is an accessibility tree filter, not a focus prevention mechanism. To prevent focus on an element, use `tabindex="-1"`, `disabled`, or `display: none`/`visibility: hidden`. The correct modal pattern is to set `aria-hidden="true"` on the rest of the page (not the trigger) and trap focus within the modal. [community]

238. **[community] Dynamic `aria-live` regions that update their content by replacing the entire innerHTML (including re-rendering unchanged text) cause some screen readers (particularly JAWS) to re-announce the entire region text on every render cycle — even for React components that visually appear to show the same content, the virtual DOM diffing can regenerate DOM nodes with new object identities, triggering spurious AT announcements**: React components that render a `role="status"` div and re-render on every state change (e.g., in a parent component that updates on every keypress) will cause JAWS to repeatedly announce the status text on each keystroke even if the text has not changed. WHY: Screen readers detect live region updates by monitoring DOM mutation events, not by comparing text values — a DOM node replacement fires a mutation even if the text content is identical. The fix is to update only the `textContent` of the live region node directly via a ref, bypassing React's re-render, or to use `useMemo`/`React.memo` to ensure the live region component only re-renders when the announced text genuinely changes. [community]

239. **[community] Testing `toHaveAccessibleName()` in Playwright only verifies the computed accessible name according to the browser's accessibility tree — it does not detect that the name was computed from a fallback source (e.g., `title` attribute) instead of the preferred source (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, or visible label text), and a name derived from `title` alone is insufficient for most interactive elements because `title` is a tooltip, not a visible label**: A button with only a `title="Delete record"` attribute passes `toHaveAccessibleName('Delete record')` in Playwright, giving false confidence that the element is properly labelled. Screen readers announce `title`-derived names but `title` is not surfaced visually, violating WCAG 2.4.6 (Headings and Labels) for sighted keyboard users. WHY: The accessible name computation algorithm uses `title` as a last-resort fallback after exhausting `aria-labelledby`, `aria-label`, embedded content, and `alt`. Playwright does not report which step of the algorithm produced the name. Teams must add a separate assertion: `await expect(button).not.toHaveAttribute('title')` combined with `toHaveAccessibleName()`, or inspect the `aria-label` / visible text explicitly. [community]

240. **[community] When running `@axe-core/playwright`'s `AxeBuilder.analyze()` on a page that contains Playwright's own injected helper elements (e.g., the Playwright test overlay or coverage instrumentation scripts), axe may report phantom violations on these injected nodes that do not exist in the production site — these violations appear in CI but cannot be reproduced in the browser by developers**: Playwright injects internal `<script>` elements and occasionally a test info overlay into the DOM during test execution. If axe scans the full document, these nodes can trigger rules like `document-title` (if the page is in a loading state when the scan begins) or `bypass` on injected frames. WHY: `AxeBuilder.analyze()` scans the live DOM including Playwright's own injected elements. The fix is to start the axe scan only after the page has fully loaded (`await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')` or `'domcontentloaded'`) and to use `.exclude()` to filter out known Playwright test scaffolding selectors if they appear in violation nodes. [community]
