**Pattern 299: WCAG 2.4.7 — Focus Visible: Ensure No `outline: none` Regression** [official]
Guard against CSS resets or component library updates that globally suppress focus rings. Axe-core's `focus-visible` rule partially covers this, but this pattern uses Playwright to walk every interactive element and programmatically verify outline is not zeroed out.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('no interactive element has suppressed focus outline globally', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Axe scan for focus-visible violations
  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
    .include('main')
    .analyze();

  const focusViolations = results.violations.filter(
    (v) => v.id === 'focus-visible' || v.id === 'focus-order-semantics'
  );

  if (focusViolations.length > 0) {
    const summary = focusViolations
      .flatMap((v) => v.nodes.map((n) => `${v.id}: ${n.html.slice(0, 80)}`))
      .join('\n');
    expect.soft(focusViolations, `Focus violations:\n${summary}`).toHaveLength(0);
  }

  // Additionally verify no global CSS override exists
  const globalOutlineZeroed = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const sheet = Array.from(document.styleSheets).find((s) => {
      try { return s.cssRules.length > 0; } catch { return false; }
    });
    if (!sheet) return false;
    return Array.from(sheet.cssRules).some((r) => {
      const text = r.cssText;
      return text.includes('outline: 0') || text.includes('outline: none');
    });
  });

  expect(globalOutlineZeroed, 'Global outline suppression detected in stylesheet').toBe(false);
});
```
Tradeoff: The CSS rule scan only inspects the first accessible stylesheet. Inline styles and Shadow DOM stylesheets are not covered. Use `expect.soft` for violations to capture all issues before failing, avoiding early bail-out that hides multiple regressions.

**Pattern 300: WCAG 4.1.2 — ARIA Role + Name + State Completeness via axe-core Scoped Scan** [official]
Run a scoped axe scan on interactive widget subtrees immediately after mount to verify that every interactive role has a computable accessible name and correct required properties, catching missing `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, or required ARIA state attributes at the component level.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

const INTERACTIVE_ROLES = ['button', 'link', 'checkbox', 'radio', 'combobox', 'slider', 'textbox'];

test('all interactive controls have accessible name and required ARIA state', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Wait for dynamic content to settle
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'best-practice'])
    .analyze();

  const nameAndStateViolations = results.violations.filter((v) =>
    ['label', 'aria-required-attr', 'aria-required-children', 'aria-valid-attr-value'].includes(v.id)
  );

  expect(
    nameAndStateViolations,
    nameAndStateViolations.map((v) => `${v.id}: ${v.description}`).join('\n')
  ).toHaveLength(0);

  // Verify each interactive role has non-empty accessible name
  for (const role of INTERACTIVE_ROLES) {
    const elements = await page.getByRole(role as any).all();
    for (const el of elements) {
      const name = await el.getAttribute('aria-label') ??
        await el.evaluate((e) => e.getAttribute('aria-labelledby')) ??
        await el.textContent();
      expect(name?.trim(), `${role} element missing accessible name`).toBeTruthy();
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `getByRole` traversal iterates all matching elements, which can be slow on pages with hundreds of form controls. Cache `all()` results and bail on first failure using `expect.soft` chains for faster CI feedback on large forms.

**Pattern 301: WCAG 2.4.1 — Skip Navigation Link Is First Focusable and Leads to Main Content** [official]
Verify that the skip-to-content link is the first element in the tab order, is visible on focus, and correctly moves focus to the `<main>` landmark so keyboard users can bypass navigation.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('skip navigation link is first focusable and functional', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // First tab should reach the skip link
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  const activeTag = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.tagName.toLowerCase());
  expect(activeTag).toBe('a');

  const skipHref = await page.evaluate(() => (document.activeElement as HTMLAnchorElement)?.href);
  expect(skipHref).toMatch(/#main/i);

  // Skip link must be visible when focused (not off-screen via clip)
  const visibility = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const el = document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
    const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    return rect.top >= 0 && rect.left >= 0 && rect.width > 0 && rect.height > 0;
  });
  expect(visibility, 'Skip link must be visible when focused').toBe(true);

  // Activate the skip link and verify focus moves to main
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  const mainFocused = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const el = document.activeElement;
    return el?.tagName.toLowerCase() === 'main' || el?.id === 'main-content';
  });
  expect(mainFocused, 'Focus must move to main content after skip link activation').toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: Some implementations place the skip link inside a visually hidden container revealed only on focus — both off-screen (clip) and opacity-0 patterns exist. This test's visibility check catches the clip-at-negative-position anti-pattern but may need adjustment for opacity-based implementations.

**Pattern 302: WCAG 1.4.10 — Content Reflow at 320px Without Horizontal Scroll** [official]
Emulate a 320 CSS pixel viewport (equivalent to 400% zoom on a 1280px screen) and assert that no horizontal scrollbar appears and all content is still accessible — covering the WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow success criterion.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('content reflows at 320px viewport with no horizontal overflow', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext({
    viewport: { width: 320, height: 568 },
  });
  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto('/pricing');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Assert no horizontal scrollbar (scrollWidth <= clientWidth)
  const hasHorizontalScroll = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return document.documentElement.scrollWidth > document.documentElement.clientWidth;
  });
  expect(hasHorizontalScroll, 'Horizontal scroll present at 320px viewport').toBe(false);

  // Run axe scan at narrow viewport for any new violations
  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2aa'])
    .analyze();

  // Filter for scroll/overflow-related violations
  const criticalViolations = results.violations.filter(
    (v) => v.impact === 'critical' || v.impact === 'serious'
  );
  expect(
    criticalViolations,
    criticalViolations.map((v) => v.id).join(', ')
  ).toHaveLength(0);

  await context.close();
});
```
Tradeoff: The 320px test must be a separate browser context — resizing within an existing test page may not re-trigger CSS media queries for all layout frameworks. Data tables and complex data grids legitimately require horizontal scroll per WCAG exception SC 1.4.10 Note 1; exclude those containers with `.exclude('[role="grid"]')`.

**Pattern 303: ARIA Live Region — Dynamic Content Announcement Verification** [official]
Verify that status messages, form validation feedback, and loading state changes are wrapped in appropriate `aria-live` regions and that the regions are pre-rendered in the DOM (not dynamically injected) to ensure screen readers register the live region before content changes.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('form submission error is announced via aria-live region', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/contact');

  // Verify the live region exists before interaction (must be pre-rendered)
  const liveRegion = page.locator('[aria-live]').first();
  await expect(liveRegion).toBeAttached();
  const liveValue = await liveRegion.getAttribute('aria-live');
  expect(['polite', 'assertive']).toContain(liveValue);

  // Trigger a validation error
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /send message/i }).click();

  // Error content must appear in the live region (not just anywhere on page)
  await expect(liveRegion).not.toBeEmpty();
  const regionText = await liveRegion.textContent();
  expect(regionText?.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Verify role=alert shorthand is not combined with aria-live=polite (contradictory)
  const alertWithPolite = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[role="alert"][aria-live="polite"]')).length;
  });
  expect(alertWithPolite, 'role=alert implicitly sets aria-live=assertive; polite override is contradictory').toBe(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Playwright cannot directly intercept screen reader announcements — this test validates DOM structure correctness, not actual AT announcement. True announcement verification requires a real screen reader driver (e.g., screen-reader-testing-library) or manual testing. The pre-render check is critical: live regions injected after page load are not registered by JAWS and NVDA.

**Pattern 304: WCAG 2.5.3 — Label in Name: Visible Label Text is Contained in Accessible Name** [official]
For controls with visible text labels, verify that the accessible name contains the visible label text (per WCAG 2.5.3). Controls where the accessible name overrides the visual label with different text break voice control software like Dragon NaturallySpeaking.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('accessible names contain visible label text for all form controls', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings');

  const inputs = await page.getByRole('textbox').all();

  for (const input of inputs) {
    // Get the visible label via aria-labelledby or associated <label>
    const visibleLabelText = await input.evaluate((el) => {
      const id = el.id;
      if (id) {
        const label = document.querySelector(`label[for="${id}"]`);
        if (label) return label.textContent?.trim() ?? '';
      }
      const labelledById = el.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
      if (labelledById) {
        return document.getElementById(labelledById)?.textContent?.trim() ?? '';
      }
      return '';
    });

    const ariaLabel = await input.getAttribute('aria-label');
    const accessibleName = ariaLabel ?? visibleLabelText;

    if (visibleLabelText && accessibleName) {
      // Accessible name must include visible label (case-insensitive)
      expect(
        accessibleName.toLowerCase(),
        `Accessible name "${accessibleName}" must contain visible label "${visibleLabelText}"`
      ).toContain(visibleLabelText.toLowerCase());
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Only checks `textbox` roles and `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` patterns — does not cover `title` attribute as accessible name fallback (which is deprecated per ARIA 1.2). Extend to include `getByRole('button')` for icon buttons with `aria-label` that replaces visible text, as these are common 2.5.3 violations.

---

**Pattern 305: WCAG 2.2 — Focus Not Obscured (AA) — Sticky Header Overlap Detection** [official]
WCAG 2.4.11 (AA, new in 2.2) requires that focused elements are not entirely hidden by author-created sticky content. Detect whether sticky headers or cookie banners fully obscure focused elements by comparing bounding rectangles.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('sticky header does not fully obscure focused elements', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/docs/installation');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Get sticky element bottom edge
  const stickyBottom = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const sticky = document.querySelector('[style*="position: sticky"], header[class*="sticky"]') as HTMLElement;
    if (!sticky) return 0;
    return sticky.getBoundingClientRect().bottom;
  });

  if (stickyBottom === 0) return; // No sticky element, test not applicable

  // Tab through 20 elements and check none are fully obscured
  for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focusedRect = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement;
      if (!el) return null;
      const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      return { top: rect.top, bottom: rect.bottom, height: rect.height };
    });

    if (focusedRect && focusedRect.height > 0) {
      const fullyObscured = focusedRect.bottom <= stickyBottom;
      expect(
        fullyObscured,
        `Focused element at top=${focusedRect.top} is fully obscured by sticky header bottom=${stickyBottom}`
      ).toBe(false);
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Only detects full obscurement (WCAG 2.4.11 AA). Partial obscurement (element partially hidden) is covered by 2.4.12 AAA and is not tested here. Sticky footers and side-navigation panels also require testing — extend the sticky element query to include `[style*="fixed"]` and `footer[class*="sticky"]`.

**Pattern 306: WCAG 3.3.2 — Labels or Instructions: All Required Fields Are Marked Programmatically** [official]
Verify that every required form field has both a visual indicator and a programmatic `required` attribute or `aria-required="true"`, and that the accessible name includes the word "required" or the field's label is linked to an explicit required indicator.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('all required fields are programmatically marked', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/register');

  // Axe scan for label violations
  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2a'])
    .analyze();

  const labelViolations = results.violations.filter((v) =>
    ['label', 'label-title-only', 'label-content-name-mismatch'].includes(v.id)
  );
  expect(labelViolations, labelViolations.map((v) => v.description).join('\n')).toHaveLength(0);

  // Check all required inputs have aria-required or HTML required
  const requiredInputs = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('input, select, textarea'))
      .filter((el) => {
        const label = document.querySelector(`label[for="${el.id}"]`);
        return label?.textContent?.includes('*') || label?.textContent?.toLowerCase().includes('required');
      })
      .map((el) => ({
        id: el.id,
        hasRequired: el.hasAttribute('required'),
        hasAriaRequired: el.getAttribute('aria-required') === 'true',
      }));
  });

  for (const field of requiredInputs) {
    expect(
      field.hasRequired || field.hasAriaRequired,
      `Field #${field.id} visually marked required but missing required/aria-required attribute`
    ).toBe(true);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: The visual required indicator detection relies on asterisk (`*`) or the word "required" in label text — custom icons (e.g., red dots via `::after` pseudo-elements) are not detectable via text inspection. For custom indicators, audit via manual testing or screenshot comparison against the design spec.

**Pattern 307: ARIA Combobox Pattern — Full Keyboard Contract Verification** [official]
Test the complete keyboard interaction contract for ARIA combobox widgets per the ARIA APG: Alt+Down to open, typing to filter, arrow keys to navigate options, Enter to select, Escape to close and return focus to input.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('combobox keyboard contract: open, navigate, select, dismiss', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');

  const combobox = page.getByRole('combobox', { name: /search/i });
  await combobox.focus();

  // Alt+Down should open the popup (ARIA APG pattern)
  await page.keyboard.press('Alt+ArrowDown');
  const listbox = page.getByRole('listbox');
  await expect(listbox).toBeVisible();
  await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

  // Type to filter
  await combobox.type('appl');
  const options = await page.getByRole('option').all();
  expect(options.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Arrow Down navigates to first option
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  const activeOption = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.textContent?.trim());
  expect(activeOption).toBeTruthy();

  // Enter selects focused option
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(listbox).not.toBeVisible();
  await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

  // Re-open and press Escape to dismiss
  await page.keyboard.press('Alt+ArrowDown');
  await expect(listbox).toBeVisible();
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(listbox).not.toBeVisible();

  // Focus must return to the combobox input after Escape
  const focusedRole = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role'));
  expect(focusedRole).toBe('combobox');
});
```
Tradeoff: The Alt+Down open gesture is for editable comboboxes (pattern 1 in APG). Pattern 2 (select-only combobox) uses Alt+Down/Up exclusively for navigation. Always check which APG combobox pattern the implementation follows before writing the test — the keyboard contracts are different.

---

**Pattern 308: `axe-core` Tagged Scan Baseline — Establish and Diff Violation Counts** [community]
Establish a violation-count baseline at project start and fail CI when the count increases — preventing accessibility debt accumulation without requiring a zero-violation policy that can block feature work.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

const BASELINE_FILE = path.join(__dirname, 'axe-baseline.json');

test('axe violation count does not regress from baseline', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
    .analyze();

  const currentCount = results.violations.length;

  if (!fs.existsSync(BASELINE_FILE)) {
    // First run: write baseline
    fs.writeFileSync(BASELINE_FILE, JSON.stringify({ count: currentCount }, null, 2));
    console.log(`Baseline established: ${currentCount} violations`);
    return;
  }

  const baseline = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(BASELINE_FILE, 'utf-8'));
  const regression = currentCount - baseline.count;

  expect(
    regression,
    `Accessibility regression: ${regression} new violation(s). Current: ${currentCount}, Baseline: ${baseline.count}`
  ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Baseline files checked into git create merge conflicts when multiple branches introduce violations simultaneously. Use a monotonically non-increasing count rather than exact equality. For monorepos, scope baselines per-route (store as a map of URL→count). Baseline-based approaches can mask equal-trade regressions where new violations appear and old ones are fixed.

---

**Pattern 309: WCAG 2.5.8 / Touch Target — Mobile Viewport Touch Target Size Assertion** [official]
On a mobile viewport, verify that interactive elements meet the WCAG 2.2 minimum touch target size of 24×24 CSS pixels (AA) and ideally 44×44px (Apple/Google guidelines) by inspecting computed bounding boxes.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('touch targets meet 24x24px minimum on mobile viewport', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext({
    viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 }, // iPhone 14 Pro
    isMobile: true,
    hasTouch: true,
  });
  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto('/mobile-nav');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const smallTargets = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const interactive = document.querySelectorAll('button, a, [role="button"], input[type="checkbox"], input[type="radio"]');
    const failures: { tag: string; text: string; width: number; height: number }[] = [];
    for (const el of interactive) {
      const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      if (rect.width < 24 || rect.height < 24) {
        failures.push({
          tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
          text: (el.textContent ?? '').trim().slice(0, 40),
          width: Math.round(rect.width),
          height: Math.round(rect.height),
        });
      }
    }
    return failures;
  });

  expect(
    smallTargets,
    `Touch targets below 24×24px:\n${smallTargets.map((t) => `  <${t.tag}> "${t.text}" — ${t.width}×${t.height}px`).join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);

  await context.close();
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.5.8 allows exceptions for inline links in running text and native browser controls. Filter those out before asserting. The 24px minimum applies to the target's CSS size, not its rendered tap area; padding-based hit-area expansion (touch-action area via pseudo-element) is invisible to `getBoundingClientRect()` and requires separate verification.

---

**Pattern 310: WCAG 1.2.2 / 1.2.4 — Caption Track Presence and Non-Empty Content Verification** [official]
Assert that `<video>` elements with audio have a `<track kind="captions">` element with a valid `src` attribute, and that the `.vtt` file is non-empty and reachable.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('all videos with audio have non-empty caption tracks', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/tutorials');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const videoData = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('video')).map((video) => {
      const tracks = Array.from(video.querySelectorAll('track[kind="captions"], track[kind="subtitles"]'));
      const muted = video.muted;
      return {
        src: video.src || video.currentSrc,
        muted,
        captionTracks: tracks.map((t) => ({
          src: t.getAttribute('src'),
          label: t.getAttribute('label'),
          srclang: t.getAttribute('srclang'),
        })),
      };
    });
  });

  for (const video of videoData) {
    if (video.muted) continue; // Muted video exempt from caption requirement

    expect(
      video.captionTracks.length,
      `Video "${video.src}" has no caption or subtitle track`
    ).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    // Verify each track file is reachable and non-empty
    for (const track of video.captionTracks) {
      if (track.src) {
        const response = await page.request.get(track.src);
        expect(response.status(), `Caption track ${track.src} returned non-200`).toBe(200);
        const body = await response.text();
        expect(body.trim().length, `Caption track ${track.src} is empty`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      }
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Playwright's `page.request.get()` sends an unauthenticated request — authenticated `.vtt` files behind CDN tokens will return 403. Handle that case by checking `response.status() !== 404` (file exists) rather than 200 (accessible). Also: `<track>` presence does not validate caption accuracy or synchronisation — manual QA is still required for caption quality.

### Community Gotchas

**Gotcha G251: `role="tooltip"` elements must be referenced by `aria-describedby` on their trigger — adding `role="tooltip"` alone provides no accessible description to users who cannot hover**
Tooltip components often add `role="tooltip"` to the tooltip container for visual purposes, but unless the triggering element carries `aria-describedby` pointing to the tooltip's `id`, screen readers never surface the tooltip content. Users navigating by keyboard who cannot trigger hover events receive no hint the tooltip exists. WHY: The ARIA specification defines `role="tooltip"` as a "description" role — it is only exposed to assistive technology via the accessible description mechanism, which requires an explicit `aria-describedby` reference from the triggering element. The tooltip's `id` must be stable and present in the DOM before the `aria-describedby` reference is resolved by the AT. Fix: Always pair `role="tooltip"` with `aria-describedby="<tooltip-id>"` on the trigger element. For conditionally rendered tooltips, render the tooltip in the DOM but use CSS visibility rather than `display:none` / conditional rendering so the `id` reference can resolve.

**Gotcha G252: `aria-disabled="true"` on a button does NOT remove it from the tab order — the button remains focusable, which is intentional per ARIA spec, but teams testing with `expect(button).toBeDisabled()` in Playwright fail because `aria-disabled` does not set the HTML `disabled` property, causing false-positive passes**
HTML `disabled` removes the element from the tab order and prevents all interaction. ARIA `aria-disabled="true"` communicates disabled state to assistive technology while intentionally keeping the element focusable so users can discover the control and understand why it is disabled. Teams often use `aria-disabled` expecting it to behave identically to `disabled` — Playwright's `.isDisabled()` only returns `true` for HTML `disabled`, not `aria-disabled`. WHY: The two mechanisms are deliberately different: `disabled` removes capability; `aria-disabled` communicates state while preserving discoverability. Fix: In Playwright tests, use `await expect(button).toHaveAttribute('aria-disabled', 'true')` for ARIA-disabled controls. In implementation, intercept click and keypress events and call `event.preventDefault()` when `aria-disabled` is true to prevent accidental activation.

**Gotcha G253: Adding `aria-hidden="true"` to a focusable element (a button, link, or input) creates an accessibility tree orphan — the element receives focus when tabbing but has no accessible name or role, causing screen readers to announce the raw HTML tag or be completely silent**
`aria-hidden="true"` removes the element and all its descendants from the accessibility tree. When applied to a focusable element, the browser correctly removes it from the AT tree but does NOT remove it from the DOM tab order. Keyboard users tab to the element, but the AT cannot describe it — NVDA announces "blank", JAWS is silent, VoiceOver says "group". WHY: `aria-hidden` is designed for decorative containers, not interactive elements. The spec explicitly states that `aria-hidden` must not be applied to focusable elements. Fix: Before applying `aria-hidden`, add `tabindex="-1"` to remove the element from tab order, or use `disabled`/`inert` on its container to suppress both tab order and accessibility tree simultaneously.

**Gotcha G254: Playwright's `toMatchAriaSnapshot` with wildcards uses `...` for partial matching, but developers who use `*` (glob wildcard) instead get a literal string match failure — the aria snapshot DSL is distinct from shell globbing and standard regex**
`toMatchAriaSnapshot` uses a YAML-like DSL where `...` means "any children here" for partial subtree matching. Developers familiar with glob patterns reach for `*` or `**` to indicate partial matches and receive confusing assertion failures because `*` is a literal string in the ARIA snapshot DSL. WHY: The ARIA snapshot format was designed with YAML structural matching semantics, not shell or regex wildcards. The `...` token explicitly signals "I don't care about children here" in the tree diff. Fix: Replace `*` wildcards in `toMatchAriaSnapshot` strings with `/pattern/` regex literals for text matching, or `...` for structural omission. Consult the Playwright aria-snapshots documentation specifically rather than relying on general glob knowledge.

**Gotcha G255: When a modal dialog's backdrop `<div>` is placed after the dialog in the DOM but both are inside a `<div aria-modal="true">` container, VoiceOver on iOS reads content outside the modal because `aria-modal` is only reliably supported on the element with `role="dialog"` itself, not on wrapper containers**
`aria-modal="true"` signals to assistive technology that content outside the modal is inert. This works correctly when applied directly to `role="dialog"`. When developers wrap the dialog and backdrop in a container and apply `aria-modal` to the container, some screen readers — particularly VoiceOver on iOS Safari — fail to respect the inert boundary and allow reading of background content. WHY: The ARIA specification scopes `aria-modal` to the dialog role. Screen reader implementations differ in how they interpret `aria-modal` on non-dialog containers; VoiceOver iOS implements a strict reading of the spec. Fix: Apply `aria-modal="true"` directly on the element carrying `role="dialog"`. Use the `inert` HTML attribute on the background content as a complementary mechanism — `inert` is now broadly supported (Chrome 102+, Firefox 112+, Safari 15.5+) and provides a native fallback when `aria-modal` is mis-implemented.

## Cycle 56 — 2026-05-14

### New Patterns

**Pattern 311: WCAG 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced) — Verify focused element is fully visible, not just minimally unobscured** [official]
WCAG 2.4.12 (AA, new in 2.2) requires that no part of a focused component is hidden by author-created content. While 2.4.11 (AA) allows partial obscuring, 2.4.12 (AAA) demands full visibility. For sticky headers, floating chat widgets, and cookie banners, test that the entire focused element bounding box clears all sticky layers.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 2.4.12 — focused element fully unobscured by sticky layers', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Collect all sticky/fixed positioned layers
  const stickyRects = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('*'))
      .filter((el) => {
        const s = getComputedStyle(el);
        return (s.position === 'sticky' || s.position === 'fixed') && s.display !== 'none';
      })
      .map((el) => {
        const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        return { top: r.top, bottom: r.bottom, left: r.left, right: r.right };
      });
  });

  // Tab through all interactive elements and verify none are obscured
  const focusableSelector = 'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), select, textarea, [tabindex="0"]';
  const handles = await page.$$(focusableSelector);

  for (const handle of handles) {
    await handle.focus();
    const focused = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement;
      if (!el) return null;
      const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      return { top: r.top, bottom: r.bottom, left: r.left, right: r.right };
    });

    if (!focused) continue;

    for (const sticky of stickyRects) {
      const obscured =
        focused.top < sticky.bottom &&
        focused.bottom > sticky.top &&
        focused.left < sticky.right &&
        focused.right > sticky.left;
      expect(obscured, `Focused element at y=${focused.top} obscured by sticky layer at y=${sticky.top}–${sticky.bottom}`).toBe(false);
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Iterating every focusable element is expensive for large pages. Scope the test to critical flows (checkout, login, main nav) rather than whole-page traversal in CI. Also: elements that scroll off-screen during focus are not covered — add a `page.keyboard.press('Tab')` loop combined with `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` to handle scroll-triggered focus patterns.

**Pattern 312: WCAG 3.2.6 Consistent Help — Verify help mechanism appears in same DOM order across pages** [official]
WCAG 3.2.6 (A, new in 2.2) requires that if a help mechanism (live chat, phone number, support link, self-service portal) appears on multiple pages, it appears in the same relative order within page content. This is particularly relevant for SPAs where layout can drift across routes.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const HELP_PAGES = ['/', '/account', '/billing', '/support'];
const HELP_SELECTOR = '[data-testid="help-widget"], a[href*="support"], button[aria-label*="help" i]';

test('WCAG 3.2.6 — help mechanism has consistent DOM position across pages', async ({ page }) => {
  const positions: Record<string, number> = {};

  for (const path of HELP_PAGES) {
    await page.goto(path);
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const position = await page.evaluate((sel) => {
      const helpEl = document.querySelector(sel);
      if (!helpEl) return -1;
      // Count all interactive elements before this one in DOM order
      const allInteractive = Array.from(
        document.querySelectorAll('a[href], button, input, select, textarea, [tabindex]')
      );
      return allInteractive.indexOf(helpEl as HTMLElement);
    }, HELP_SELECTOR);

    expect(position, `Help mechanism not found on ${path}`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
    positions[path] = position;
  }

  // All help mechanisms should appear in last 20% of interactive elements
  // (or first — the key is consistency). Assert they are all roughly equivalent.
  const values = Object.values(positions);
  const min = Math.min(...values);
  const max = Math.max(...values);

  // Allow up to 5 position drift between pages (minor layout variance)
  expect(max - min, `Help mechanism DOM order drifts by ${max - min} positions across pages: ${JSON.stringify(positions)}`).toBeLessThanOrEqual(5);
});
```
Tradeoff: DOM position index is a proxy for "relative order" — minor layout changes like adding a new nav item will shift absolute counts. A more robust approach: assert that the help element is always in the `<footer>` or always in the header landmark by checking `closest('footer, header, [role="banner"], [role="contentinfo"]')`. Absolute index comparison will produce false positives during legitimate page structure evolution.

**Pattern 313: WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry — Multi-step form does not re-ask previously submitted information** [official]
WCAG 3.3.7 (A, new in 2.2) prohibits asking users to re-enter information they already provided in an earlier step of the same process, unless re-entry is essential (e.g., password confirmation) or due to security requirements. Test that checkout, onboarding, and multi-step wizards pre-populate or display previously submitted values.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 3.3.7 — shipping address not re-requested after billing step', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout/billing');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Fill billing address in step 1
  const billingData = {
    firstName: 'Test',
    lastName:  'User',
    address:   '123 Accessible Lane',
    city:      'Vienna',
    zip:       '1010',
  };

  await page.fill('[name="billing-first-name"]', billingData.firstName);
  await page.fill('[name="billing-last-name"]',  billingData.lastName);
  await page.fill('[name="billing-address"]',    billingData.address);
  await page.fill('[name="billing-city"]',       billingData.city);
  await page.fill('[name="billing-zip"]',        billingData.zip);
  await page.click('[data-testid="next-step"]');

  // Step 2: shipping — should pre-populate or offer "same as billing"
  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="shipping-step"]');

  // Option A: fields pre-populated
  const shippingAddressValue = await page.inputValue('[name="shipping-address"]').catch(() => '');
  const sameAsBillingChecked = await page.isChecked('[data-testid="same-as-billing"]').catch(() => false);

  const redundantEntryPrevented = shippingAddressValue === billingData.address || sameAsBillingChecked;
  expect(
    redundantEntryPrevented,
    'WCAG 3.3.7 violation: shipping step re-asks address already provided in billing step'
  ).toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: This test is tightly coupled to form field naming conventions. Parameterize step selectors via a page-object model so the test survives field renaming. Also: "same as billing" checkbox satisfies 3.3.7 even if fields are empty — the test must check both pre-population AND the presence of a re-use mechanism.

**Pattern 314: WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication — Verify CAPTCHA has accessible alternative and autocomplete is not blocked** [official]
WCAG 3.3.8 (AA, new in 2.2) prohibits authentication steps that rely on a cognitive function test (like solving a CAPTCHA) unless an alternative is provided, or `autocomplete` is allowed. Test that login fields carry appropriate `autocomplete` values and any CAPTCHA provides an audio alternative.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 3.3.8 — login form allows autocomplete and has accessible CAPTCHA alternative', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // 1. Check autocomplete attributes on credential fields
  const usernameAutocomplete = await page.getAttribute('input[type="email"], input[name*="user" i]', 'autocomplete');
  const passwordAutocomplete = await page.getAttribute('input[type="password"]', 'autocomplete');

  expect(
    ['username', 'email'].includes(usernameAutocomplete ?? ''),
    `Username field autocomplete="${usernameAutocomplete}" — should be "username" or "email"`
  ).toBe(true);

  expect(
    ['current-password', 'new-password'].includes(passwordAutocomplete ?? ''),
    `Password field autocomplete="${passwordAutocomplete}" — should be "current-password" or "new-password"`
  ).toBe(true);

  // 2. If CAPTCHA is present, verify audio alternative exists
  const hasCaptcha = await page.locator('iframe[src*="recaptcha"], [data-testid="captcha"]').count();
  if (hasCaptcha > 0) {
    // reCAPTCHA audio challenge button
    const audioChallenge = await page.locator('#recaptcha-audio-button, [aria-label*="audio" i]').count();
    expect(audioChallenge, 'CAPTCHA present but no audio alternative — WCAG 3.3.8 violation').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  }

  // 3. Verify autocomplete is not set to "off" on credential fields
  const autocompleteOff = await page.locator('input[autocomplete="off"][type="password"], input[autocomplete="off"][type="email"]').count();
  expect(autocompleteOff, 'Credential fields have autocomplete="off" — blocks password managers, violates 3.3.8').toBe(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Third-party CAPTCHA providers (reCAPTCHA v3, hCaptcha) are embedded in cross-origin iframes — `page.locator()` cannot pierce them without `frame()` access. Test for the presence of the iframe itself and separately verify in a headless environment with `--disable-web-security` if the CAPTCHA vendor provides a test key. Also: `autocomplete="off"` is widely ignored by modern browsers but is still a WCAG violation signal worth flagging.

**Pattern 315: Playwright `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage` — validate error message is programmatically associated** [official]
Playwright 1.50 introduced `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` which asserts the element's accessible error message via `aria-errormessage`. This is the programmatic equivalent of a screen reader announcing a form validation error — test it rather than only asserting the visible error text exists in the DOM.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('form validation error is programmatically associated via aria-errormessage', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/registration');

  // Submit with empty required email field to trigger validation
  await page.click('[data-testid="submit-registration"]');
  await page.waitForSelector('[aria-invalid="true"]');

  const emailInput = page.locator('input[type="email"]');

  // 1. Assert the field is marked invalid
  await expect(emailInput).toHaveAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true');

  // 2. Assert the accessible error message text content
  await expect(emailInput).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(/email.*required|please enter.*email/i);

  // 3. Verify the aria-errormessage target exists and is visible
  const errorId = await emailInput.getAttribute('aria-errormessage');
  expect(errorId, 'aria-errormessage attribute missing on invalid input').toBeTruthy();

  const errorEl = page.locator(`#${errorId}`);
  await expect(errorEl).toBeVisible();

  // 4. Verify error text is not hidden from AT (no aria-hidden on the error element)
  const ariaHidden = await errorEl.getAttribute('aria-hidden');
  expect(ariaHidden, `Error element #${errorId} has aria-hidden — invisible to screen readers`).not.toBe('true');
});
```
Tradeoff: `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage` resolves the full accessible description chain including `aria-errormessage`, `aria-describedby`, and title — it does NOT exclusively check `aria-errormessage`. If `aria-describedby` points to a hint text and `aria-errormessage` is absent, the assertion may still pass with the hint text. Use `toHaveAttribute('aria-errormessage', ...)` alongside `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage` for precise ARIA contract enforcement.

**Pattern 316: axe-core `resultTypes` performance optimization — only collect violations in hot CI paths** [official]
By default, `axe.run()` computes all four result categories: violations, passes, incomplete, inapplicable. On large pages this is expensive. In CI where only violations matter, pass `resultTypes: ['violations']` to axe to suppress the other three categories and achieve ~8× throughput improvement on complex pages.
```typescript
import { test, expect }   from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder        from '@axe-core/playwright';

// Utility: fast axe scan — violations only, no passes/incomplete/inapplicable
async function fastAxeScan(page: import('@playwright/test').Page, tags = ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa']) {
  const builder = new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(tags)
    // resultTypes reduces axe internal work for non-violation categories
    .options({ resultTypes: ['violations'] });
  return builder.analyze();
}

test.describe('Fast CI accessibility gate', () => {
  test('homepage — zero WCAG 2.1 AA violations', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    const { violations } = await fastAxeScan(page);
    expect(violations, JSON.stringify(violations, null, 2)).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('product listing — zero violations, tagged result for attachment', async ({ page, testInfo }) => {
    await page.goto('/products');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    const results = await fastAxeScan(page);
    // Attach full scan for debug even when no violations
    await testInfo.attach('axe-results', {
      body: JSON.stringify(results, null, 2),
      contentType: 'application/json',
    });
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `resultTypes: ['violations']` skips `passes` and `incomplete` — you lose visibility into needs-review items that may represent real issues not caught automatically. Use the full result set in nightly/extended runs and the fast variant in per-PR gates. Also note: `resultTypes` is an axe-core `RunOptions` field — it is passed via `.options({})` in `@axe-core/playwright`, not as a first-class `AxeBuilder` method.

**Pattern 317: Playwright `getByRole` with `description` parameter — assert accessible description separately from name** [official]
Playwright 1.60 added a `description` option to `getByRole()`, letting tests select elements by their accessible description (from `aria-describedby` or `title`). This is important for distinguishing multiple similar elements (e.g., multiple "Delete" buttons each described by the item name) without relying on fragile CSS selectors.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 4.1.2 — each Delete button has a unique accessible description', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/files');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Select specific delete button by its accessible description, not by index
  const deleteReport   = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete', description: 'Q4 Annual Report.pdf' });
  const deleteSummary  = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete', description: 'Executive Summary.docx' });

  await expect(deleteReport).toBeVisible();
  await expect(deleteSummary).toBeVisible();

  // Confirm each button is individually discoverable — count must be 1
  await expect(deleteReport).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(deleteSummary).toHaveCount(1);

  // Verify the accessible description maps to aria-describedby
  const describedBy = await deleteReport.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
  expect(describedBy, 'Delete button missing aria-describedby — description not programmatically associated').toBeTruthy();

  const descEl = page.locator(`#${describedBy}`);
  await expect(descEl).toContainText('Q4 Annual Report');
});
```
Tradeoff: `getByRole` with `description` matches the computed accessible description, which may include whitespace normalization and concatenation from multiple `aria-describedby` IDs. If the description text changes (e.g., file rename), the locator breaks. Prefer `aria-label` for fixed descriptions and `aria-describedby` for dynamic ones — and update test fixtures accordingly when the content model changes.

**Pattern 318: ARIA APG Accordion — full keyboard contract test including multi-expand and focus management** [official]
The ARIA APG accordion pattern defines a specific keyboard contract: Enter/Space on a header button toggles the panel; Arrow keys may move focus between headers (in roving-tabindex variants); Home/End jump to first/last header. Test all interactions including edge cases at first/last panels.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('ARIA accordion — full keyboard contract per APG pattern', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/faq');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const headers = page.locator('[role="button"][aria-expanded], button[aria-controls]');
  const count   = await headers.count();
  expect(count, 'No accordion header buttons found').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // 1. Enter expands the first panel
  await headers.first().focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(headers.first()).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

  const panelId = await headers.first().getAttribute('aria-controls');
  expect(panelId, 'aria-controls missing on accordion header').toBeTruthy();
  await expect(page.locator(`#${panelId}`)).toBeVisible();

  // 2. Space collapses the expanded panel
  await page.keyboard.press('Space');
  await expect(headers.first()).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

  // 3. Tab moves focus to next interactive element — not trapped
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  const focusedAfterTab = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role') ?? document.activeElement?.tagName);
  expect(focusedAfterTab).not.toBe(null);

  // 4. If ArrowDown supported (roving tabindex variant), verify it moves to next header
  await headers.first().focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  const focusedId = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.id ?? '');
  const secondId  = await headers.nth(1).getAttribute('id');
  if (secondId) {
    // Only assert if second header has an id — roving tabindex variant
    expect(focusedId).toBe(secondId);
  }

  // 5. Verify panel content is not accessible when collapsed (aria-hidden or removed)
  await headers.first().focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter'); // expand
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter'); // collapse
  const collapsedPanel = page.locator(`#${panelId}`);
  const isHiddenFromAT = (await collapsedPanel.getAttribute('aria-hidden') === 'true') ||
                         !(await collapsedPanel.isVisible());
  expect(isHiddenFromAT, 'Collapsed accordion panel content is still accessible to AT').toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: APG accordion patterns have two variants — a single-expand variant (opening one panel closes others) and a multi-expand variant. This test verifies multi-expand behavior. For single-expand accordions, extend the test to assert the previously open panel closes when a new header is activated. Arrow key navigation is optional per APG — the test uses a conditional assertion to avoid false failures on Tab-only implementations.

**Pattern 319: Forced-colors (High Contrast) mode emulation — assert UI remains usable in Windows High Contrast** [official]
Windows High Contrast mode (and CSS `forced-colors: active`) overrides all author colors with system palette colors. Components that rely on CSS `background-color` alone for visual distinction (e.g., active tab indicator, selected list item) lose their visual affordance. Playwright can emulate this mode to catch these regressions before users with visual impairments encounter them.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 1.4.3 / forced-colors — key UI indicators remain distinguishable in High Contrast', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext({
    forcedColors: 'active',
    colorScheme: 'dark',
  });
  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto('/navigation');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // In forced-colors mode, borders and outlines are preserved (mapped to ButtonText / Highlight).
  // Components must use border, outline, or text rather than background-color alone.

  const activeTab = page.locator('[role="tab"][aria-selected="true"]');
  await expect(activeTab).toBeVisible();

  // Verify active tab has a border or outline (not just background-color based distinction)
  const hasVisualIndicator = await activeTab.evaluate((el) => {
    const s = getComputedStyle(el);
    const hasBorder  = parseInt(s.borderWidth)  > 0 || parseInt(s.borderBottomWidth) > 0;
    const hasOutline = parseInt(s.outlineWidth) > 0;
    // In forced-colors mode, background is replaced — check for structural indicators
    return hasBorder || hasOutline;
  });
  expect(hasVisualIndicator, 'Active tab has no border/outline — relies on background-color alone, breaks in High Contrast').toBe(true);

  // Verify focus indicators are visible — outlines are preserved in forced-colors
  const focusableEl = page.locator('a[href], button').first();
  await focusableEl.focus();
  const outlineWidth = await focusableEl.evaluate((el) => parseInt(getComputedStyle(el).outlineWidth));
  expect(outlineWidth, 'Focus outline width is 0 — focus indicator invisible in High Contrast mode').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  await context.close();
});
```
Tradeoff: `forcedColors: 'active'` in Playwright emulates the CSS media query but does NOT replace system-level palette replacement on Windows. Components using SVG fill, box-shadow, or text-shadow for visual distinction are not affected by the CSS `forced-colors` emulation — they still render their author colors. Full verification requires manual testing on Windows with High Contrast mode enabled. Treat this test as a structural smoke test, not a complete regression guarantee.

**Pattern 320: `prefers-reduced-motion` emulation — verify animated components respect motion preferences** [official]
WCAG 2.3.3 (AAA) and real-world accessibility require that UI animations do not cause harm to users with vestibular disorders. Playwright can emulate `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` to assert that CSS transitions/animations are shortened or disabled and that JavaScript-driven animations check the media query before running.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 2.3.3 — animations disabled when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is set', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
  const page    = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto('/home');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // 1. Verify CSS transition durations are collapsed under reduced motion
  const heroTransitionDuration = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const hero = document.querySelector('[data-testid="hero-banner"]');
    return hero ? parseFloat(getComputedStyle(hero).transitionDuration) : null;
  });

  if (heroTransitionDuration !== null) {
    expect(
      heroTransitionDuration,
      `Hero banner transition duration is ${heroTransitionDuration}s — should be 0 under reduced-motion`
    ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0.01);
  }

  // 2. Verify CSS animation-duration is near-zero for animated elements
  const animatedDurations = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[class*="animate"], [class*="motion"]'))
      .map((el) => ({
        class:    el.className,
        duration: parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).animationDuration),
      }))
      .filter((e) => e.duration > 0.01);
  });
  expect(
    animatedDurations,
    `${animatedDurations.length} animated elements still have full duration under reduced-motion: ${JSON.stringify(animatedDurations)}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);

  // 3. Carousel auto-play should be paused
  const carouselPlaying = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const carousel = document.querySelector('[data-testid="carousel"][data-playing]');
    return carousel?.getAttribute('data-playing') === 'true';
  });
  expect(carouselPlaying, 'Carousel is auto-playing — must be paused when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce').toBe(false);

  await context.close();
});
```
Tradeoff: CSS `transition-duration: 0.001ms` satisfies the media query technically but may still cause perceptible flash on slow devices. Recommend using `transition-duration: 0s` explicitly. Also: JavaScript animation libraries (GSAP, Framer Motion) check the OS media query independently — `browser.newContext({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` only sets the CSS media query; verify the JS library's `prefersReducedMotion` flag separately.

**Pattern 321: Keyboard tab-order snapshot — detect unintended positive `tabindex` anti-patterns** [official]
Positive `tabindex` values (e.g., `tabindex="1"`, `tabindex="2"`) override the natural document tab order and create confusing navigation for keyboard and AT users. A tab-order snapshot test detects when positive `tabindex` values are introduced — usually accidentally via copy-paste or framework migration.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('tab order — no positive tabindex values override natural DOM order', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/app');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const positiveTabindexElements = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[tabindex]'))
      .filter((el) => {
        const val = parseInt(el.getAttribute('tabindex') ?? '0', 10);
        return val > 0;
      })
      .map((el) => ({
        tag:      el.tagName,
        id:       el.id,
        class:    el.className,
        tabindex: el.getAttribute('tabindex'),
        text:     (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.slice(0, 50),
      }));
  });

  expect(
    positiveTabindexElements,
    `Positive tabindex values found — these override natural tab order:\n${JSON.stringify(positiveTabindexElements, null, 2)}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);

  // Snapshot the full tab order sequence for regression comparison
  const tabOrder = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return Array.from(
      document.querySelectorAll('a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), select, [tabindex="0"]')
    ).map((el) => ({
      tag:  el.tagName,
      id:   el.id || undefined,
      role: el.getAttribute('role') || undefined,
      name: (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.trim().slice(0, 30) || el.getAttribute('aria-label') || undefined,
    }));
  });

  // Use toMatchSnapshot to catch order regressions between runs
  expect(tabOrder).toMatchSnapshot('tab-order.json');
});
```
Tradeoff: `toMatchSnapshot` will fail on first run — intentionally, to generate the baseline. Commit the generated snapshot and update it deliberately when intentional reordering occurs. Also: Shadow DOM components expose their internal `tabindex` through the composed tab order but are not enumerable by `querySelectorAll` from the light DOM — include Playwright's `locator.all()` with shadow DOM piercing for web-component-heavy pages.

**Pattern 322: Skip navigation link — verify first-focus, activation moves focus, and remains usable** [official]
Skip navigation links (WCAG 2.4.1, Level A) allow keyboard users to bypass repeated navigation blocks. Tests must verify the link is the first focusable element on the page, that pressing Enter moves focus to the main content landmark, and that the link is visually hidden until focused (not permanently hidden from sighted users who use keyboard).
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 2.4.1 — skip link is first-focused, functional, and visible on focus', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // 1. First Tab press should land on the skip link
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  const firstFocused = await page.evaluate(() => ({
    tag:   document.activeElement?.tagName,
    href:  document.activeElement?.getAttribute('href'),
    text:  (document.activeElement as HTMLElement)?.innerText,
  }));
  expect(firstFocused.tag, 'First focused element is not a link').toBe('A');
  expect(firstFocused.href, 'First focused link does not point to main content anchor').toMatch(/^#(main|content|maincontent)/i);

  // 2. Skip link is visible when focused (not clipped off-screen)
  const skipLink = page.locator(`a[href="${firstFocused.href}"]`).first();
  const boundingBox = await skipLink.boundingBox();
  // When focused, the link should be within the viewport (not at negative coordinates)
  expect(boundingBox?.x ?? -1, 'Skip link not within viewport when focused').toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
  expect(boundingBox?.y ?? -1, 'Skip link not within viewport when focused').toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);

  // 3. Activating the skip link moves focus to main content
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  const focusedAfterSkip = await page.evaluate(() => ({
    id:   document.activeElement?.id,
    tag:  document.activeElement?.tagName,
    role: document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role'),
  }));
  const href = firstFocused.href?.replace('#', '');
  expect(
    focusedAfterSkip.id === href || focusedAfterSkip.role === 'main',
    `Skip link activation did not move focus to main content — focused: ${JSON.stringify(focusedAfterSkip)}`
  ).toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: Some implementations show the skip link only on focus via `clip: rect(0,0,0,0)` or `transform: translateY(-100%)` — bounding box coordinates remain at 0,0 before focus is applied. If the `boundingBox()` check is unreliable, use `page.evaluate(() => getComputedStyle(el).clip)` to assert the clip resets on focus. Also: SPAs that use client-side routing may not re-render the skip link on route change — verify skip link behavior after navigating between pages, not just on initial load.

**Pattern 323: ARIA live region debounce — prevent announcement flooding for rapid DOM updates** [official]
ARIA live regions (`aria-live="polite"` or `"assertive"`) announce every DOM mutation. In UIs with high-frequency updates (search-as-you-type, real-time data streams), live regions can fire dozens of announcements per second, making screen readers unusable. The fix is to debounce updates into a single announcement. Test that a burst of updates produces exactly one announcement.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('ARIA live region — rapid updates produce a single debounced announcement', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const liveRegion = page.locator('[aria-live="polite"][data-testid="search-status"]');
  await expect(liveRegion).toBeAttached();

  // Track all text changes to the live region
  const announcements: string[] = [];
  await page.exposeFunction('trackAnnouncement', (text: string) => announcements.push(text));
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    const region = document.querySelector('[aria-live="polite"][data-testid="search-status"]');
    if (!region) return;
    const obs = new MutationObserver(() => {
      (window as any).trackAnnouncement(region.textContent?.trim() ?? '');
    });
    obs.observe(region, { childList: true, subtree: true, characterData: true });
  });

  // Type rapidly — simulates search-as-you-type burst
  const searchInput = page.locator('input[role="searchbox"], input[type="search"]');
  await searchInput.focus();
  await page.keyboard.type('typescript accessibility', { delay: 20 });

  // Wait for debounce to settle (assume 300ms debounce)
  await page.waitForTimeout(500);

  // Expect at most 3 announcements for 22 keystrokes (debounce collapsing rapid updates)
  expect(
    announcements.length,
    `Live region announced ${announcements.length} times for rapid typing — expected debounced to ≤3: ${JSON.stringify(announcements)}`
  ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(3);

  // Final announcement should describe the result count, not intermediate state
  const lastAnnouncement = announcements.at(-1) ?? '';
  expect(lastAnnouncement, 'Final live region announcement is empty').not.toBe('');
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.waitForTimeout(500)` is a fixed delay — if the debounce interval is configurable (e.g., via environment variable), retrieve the actual debounce duration from the app rather than hardcoding 500ms. Also: `MutationObserver` in the page context is disconnected on navigation — this pattern is safe only for single-page tests. The `exposeFunction` channel persists across navigations only if re-registered in a `page.addInitScript`.

**Pattern 324: `@axe-core/react` component unit scan — test accessibility in isolation with React Testing Library** [official]
Unit-level accessibility testing with `@axe-core/react` and jest-axe catches violations at the component level before they compound in integration tests. This is especially valuable for design system components (Button, Dialog, Input) where a single violation propagates to every consumer.
```typescript
import React from 'react';
import { render, screen, act } from '@testing-library/react';
import { axe, toHaveNoViolations } from 'jest-axe';
import { Dialog } from '../src/components/Dialog';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';

expect.extend(toHaveNoViolations);

describe('Dialog component — accessibility contract', () => {
  it('has no axe violations when open', async () => {
    const { container } = render(
      <Dialog open title="Confirm deletion" onClose={jest.fn()}>
        <p>Are you sure you want to delete this item?</p>
        <button>Cancel</button>
        <button>Delete</button>
      </Dialog>
    );

    // React 18 / act() flush required before axe scan
    let results: any;
    await act(async () => {
      results = await axe(container);
    });
    expect(results).toHaveNoViolations();
  });

  it('traps focus inside dialog — Tab cycles through interactive elements', async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(
      <Dialog open title="Settings" onClose={jest.fn()}>
        <input type="text" placeholder="Name" />
        <button>Save</button>
        <button>Cancel</button>
      </Dialog>
    );

    const dialog = screen.getByRole('dialog');
    expect(dialog).toBeInTheDocument();

    // Focus the first element and Tab through all interactive elements
    const firstInput = screen.getByPlaceholderText('Name');
    firstInput.focus();
    await user.tab();
    expect(screen.getByText('Save')).toHaveFocus();
    await user.tab();
    expect(screen.getByText('Cancel')).toHaveFocus();
    await user.tab();
    // Focus should wrap back to first focusable — not escape the dialog
    expect(firstInput).toHaveFocus();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: jest-axe runs axe-core in a jsdom environment, which lacks real layout computation — visual rules (contrast ratios, element visibility based on CSS) are not reliably detected. Use jest-axe for structural ARIA and role violations; use `@axe-core/playwright` for visual and layout-dependent rules. Also: React 18's concurrent rendering requires `act()` wrapping around `axe()` calls to avoid "not wrapped in act" warnings that mask real assertion failures.

**Pattern 325: Guidepup VoiceOver/NVDA automation — real screen reader smoke test in CI** [community]
Guidepup (`@guidepup/playwright`) allows driving macOS VoiceOver and Windows NVDA programmatically from Playwright tests. Unlike axe-core, Guidepup tests what the screen reader actually announces — catching announcements that are technically correct per ARIA but confusing in practice (e.g., role="group" with no label causing "group group group" announcements).
```typescript
import { test }      from '@playwright/test';
import { voiceOver } from '@guidepup/playwright';

test('VoiceOver announces correct page title and main landmark on load', async ({ page }) => {
  await voiceOver(async (vo) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    // Move VoiceOver cursor to Web content area
    await vo.interact();

    // Read the page title
    const pageTitle = await vo.itemText();
    expect(pageTitle).toContain('Dashboard');

    // Navigate to the main landmark
    await vo.press('J', { shift: true }); // VO+Shift+J navigates to next landmark
    const landmarkText = await vo.itemText();
    expect(landmarkText).toMatch(/main|navigation/i);

    // Confirm the first heading is announced correctly
    await vo.press('H');
    const headingText = await vo.itemText();
    expect(headingText).toBeTruthy();
    expect(headingText.length, 'Heading text is suspiciously short — may be announcing role only').toBeGreaterThan(3);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Guidepup requires macOS for VoiceOver tests and Windows for NVDA tests — it cannot run in Linux CI containers. Restrict these tests to dedicated macOS/Windows CI runners using `test.skip(!process.platform.startsWith('darwin'))` guards. Also: VoiceOver keyboard navigation commands vary between Safari and Chrome on macOS — specify the target browser explicitly and document which browser the VoiceOver tests are validated against.

---

### Community Gotchas

**Gotcha G256: `role="presentation"` on a `<table>` used for layout removes ALL semantic structure from descendants — child `<th>` and `<caption>` elements silently lose their semantics, breaking any axe rule that relies on the table's accessible name**
Layout tables often receive `role="presentation"` to suppress screen reader table navigation. However, the presentational role propagates to all owned descendants — `<th>` elements become generic text, `<caption>` is ignored, and `<tr>`/`<td>` structure is flattened. If the table later evolves to include real data columns (a common refactor), all descendant semantics must be explicitly re-added. WHY: The ARIA specification's "presentational role" propagation rule strips semantic roles from all owned children when the owner is presentational — this is intentional to prevent a partially-semantic layout table from being announced with confusing mixed semantics. Fix: Use `role="none"` instead of `role="presentation"` (they are synonyms, but `role="none"` is the modern name) and audit all descendants. For genuinely data-containing tables, remove the presentational role entirely and use `<caption>` + `<th scope>` to convey structure. Never apply presentational role to a table that has `<thead>`, `<th>`, or sorted columns.

**Gotcha G257: `aria-label` on a `<div>` or `<span>` with no ARIA role has no effect — the accessible name is computed but never exposed because nameless elements have no accessible node in the tree**
Developers add `aria-label="Loading spinner"` to a `<div>` thinking the label is announced, but `aria-label` only has meaning on elements with a role in the accessibility tree. A `<div>` with no ARIA role has `role="generic"` (Chrome/Firefox) or is stripped from the tree (older Safari) — either way, `aria-label` is silently ignored. WHY: The accessible name computation algorithm only runs for elements that have an accessible role. Generic containers (`<div>`, `<span>`) are mapped to `role="generic"` in ARIA 1.2, which is not a named role — browsers do not compute accessible names for `role="generic"`. Fix: Add an explicit `role` to the element (e.g., `role="status"` for loading regions, `role="img"` for decorative groupings that need description) before adding `aria-label`. Alternatively, wrap the content in a semantic element that has an implicit role.

**Gotcha G258: Using `display: contents` in CSS causes the element to be removed from the layout box tree, but NOT from the accessibility tree — resulting in elements with roles and names that have no visual position, causing axe's color contrast rule to report false-positive passes because contrast cannot be computed for visually-absent elements**
`display: contents` is used to flatten CSS grid containers without adding wrapper `<div>` elements. The element's box is removed from layout, but its role, name, and state remain in the accessibility tree. For AT users, the element is announced but cannot be visually located — sighted keyboard users see the focus indicator jump to an "invisible" element. WHY: The CSS display rendering model and the accessibility tree are maintained separately — CSS `display: contents` is purely a layout instruction and has no specified effect on the AT mapping. The ARIA spec does not define what should happen. Chromium, Firefox, and Safari all handle this differently. Fix: Avoid `display: contents` on elements that carry ARIA roles or are interactive. Use CSS grid / `subgrid` on semantic landmarks directly, or replace `display: contents` wrappers with dedicated grid context elements that use `role="none"` if they must be invisible to AT.

**Gotcha G259: When a combobox input uses `aria-autocomplete="list"` with a detached `role="listbox"` (in a portal/teleport), some screen readers fail to associate the listbox with the input because the `aria-owns` relationship requires the owned element to be in the same ARIA tree root (i.e., no intervening `aria-modal` or `role="dialog"` boundary)**
Combobox implementations often render the listbox in a portal (`document.body` child) for z-index reasons. The combobox input uses `aria-controls` or `aria-owns` to reference the listbox `id`. When the input is inside a modal dialog that has `aria-modal="true"`, the ARIA tree boundary created by `aria-modal` can prevent screen readers from following the `aria-owns` reference outside the modal boundary. NVDA and JAWS both exhibit this; VoiceOver on macOS also fails silently. WHY: `aria-modal="true"` signals to AT that everything outside the modal is inert — some AT implementations interpret this as also invalidating `aria-owns` references that cross the boundary. Fix: Render the combobox listbox inside the modal DOM subtree (inside the `role="dialog"` element) even if it appears visually outside via CSS `overflow: visible` or `position: fixed`. Use the CSS approach for visual positioning rather than DOM portals. If a portal is unavoidable, test with both NVDA+Firefox and VoiceOver+Safari to verify cross-tree `aria-owns` behavior.

**Gotcha G260: `inert` HTML attribute on a container element prevents keyboard navigation and AT access, but does NOT prevent `focus()` calls from JavaScript — programmatic focus via `element.focus()` succeeds even on inert elements, causing screen readers to announce content in an "inaccessible" region**
The `inert` attribute (now broadly supported: Chrome 102+, Firefox 112+, Safari 15.5+) is used to suppress focus and AT access for background content during modal overlays. It is more reliable than `aria-hidden` for focus suppression — but it does not block programmatic `element.focus()` calls from JavaScript. Auto-focus logic (`autofocus` attribute, framework lifecycle hooks, or `useEffect(() => ref.current.focus(), [])`) can still pull focus into an inert container if the JavaScript runs after the `inert` attribute is set. WHY: The `inert` attribute is a rendering and interaction hint — it removes elements from the tab order and the accessibility tree, but the DOM method `focus()` operates at a lower level and respects the browser's focus model, which does not block programmatic focus. Fix: After setting `inert` on a container, audit all JavaScript `focus()` calls and `autofocus` usages inside that container. Add a guard: `if (!el.closest('[inert]')) el.focus();` before any programmatic focus. In Playwright tests, assert `expect(page.locator('[inert] :focus')).toHaveCount(0)` after modal open/close transitions.
