## Cycle 57 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 326** — WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) — sticky header overlap guard
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('focused element is not fully obscured by sticky header', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/long-content-page');

  // Find all focusable interactive elements
  const focusables = page.locator('a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), select, textarea, [tabindex="0"]');
  const count = await focusables.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 20); i++) {
    const el = focusables.nth(i);
    await el.focus();

    // Measure the element bounding box and the sticky header height
    const elBox   = await el.boundingBox();
    const header  = page.locator('header[data-sticky], .sticky-header, [style*="position: sticky"]').first();
    const headerBox = await header.boundingBox().catch(() => null);

    if (!elBox) continue;
    const headerBottom = headerBox ? headerBox.y + headerBox.height : 0;

    // WCAG 2.4.11: the focused component must not be entirely hidden
    expect(
      elBox.y + elBox.height,
      `Element at index ${i} is fully behind the sticky header`
    ).toBeGreaterThan(headerBottom);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: This pattern relies on CSS `position: sticky` or a `data-sticky` attribute being present — if the sticky header is implemented purely via JavaScript scroll listeners, `boundingBox()` may return the pre-scroll position. Combine with a `page.evaluate(() => window.scrollY)` assertion to confirm scroll state before measuring. Also: the test loops over up to 20 elements to keep CI duration bounded; increase the cap for exhaustive audits, but expect proportionally longer test runs.

**Pattern 327** — WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text — 200% zoom content reflow assertion
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('content does not require horizontal scrolling at 200% zoom', async ({ page }) => {
  // Set viewport to simulate 200% browser zoom (half the width)
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 640, height: 768 });
  await page.goto('/');

  // Confirm no horizontal overflow on the document body
  const hasHorizontalScroll = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return document.documentElement.scrollWidth > document.documentElement.clientWidth;
  });
  expect(hasHorizontalScroll, 'Page has horizontal scrollbar at 200% zoom equivalent').toBe(false);

  // Confirm text is still visible (not clipped to zero width)
  const mainText = page.locator('main p, main li').first();
  const box = await mainText.boundingBox();
  expect(box?.width, 'Main text width collapsed to zero').toBeGreaterThan(50);

  // Confirm interactive elements are still reachable (not overflow-hidden)
  const primaryCTA = page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit|continue|next/i }).first();
  await expect(primaryCTA).toBeInViewport();
});
```
Tradeoff: Setting `viewportSize` to half-width is a proxy for browser zoom — it tests CSS reflow but does not test font scaling triggered by OS accessibility settings or `font-size` overrides in user stylesheets. For complete WCAG 1.4.4 coverage, supplement with Playwright's `--font-size` flag (Chromium only) and a manual test with the browser's built-in zoom. Also: single-page apps with fixed-width modal dialogs frequently fail this test; triage failures by checking `max-width` and `width: Xpx` declarations in the modal's CSS.

**Pattern 328** — WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow — CSS `overflow-x: hidden` false-pass detection
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('no content clipped by overflow-x hidden at narrow viewport', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 320, height: 568 }); // WCAG 1.4.10 reference width
  await page.goto('/');

  // Collect all elements that are wider than the viewport
  const clippedElements = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const viewportWidth = window.innerWidth;
    const overflowing: string[] = [];

    document.querySelectorAll('*').forEach((el) => {
      const style = window.getComputedStyle(el);
      // overflow-x: hidden hides content silently — flag it on non-root elements
      if (
        style.overflowX === 'hidden' &&
        el !== document.body &&
        el !== document.documentElement
      ) {
        const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        if (rect.width > viewportWidth * 0.98) {
          overflowing.push(`${el.tagName}#${el.id}.${el.className}`.slice(0, 80));
        }
      }
    });
    return overflowing;
  });

  expect(
    clippedElements,
    `These elements clip content with overflow-x: hidden at 320px: ${clippedElements.join(', ')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: This heuristic flags all `overflow-x: hidden` elements that span the full viewport width — it produces false positives on intentional horizontal scroll containers (carousels, code blocks). Maintain a known-exclusions list using `.exclude()` or a test-level `allowList` array checked against `clippedElements`. The DOM traversal is O(n) over all elements — on pages with thousands of nodes, consider scoping to `main *` or `article *` to avoid timeout on large SPAs.

**Pattern 329** — WCAG 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts — single-key shortcut disable test
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('single-character keyboard shortcuts can be disabled or remapped', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/app');

  // Check if a shortcut settings panel exists
  const shortcutSettings = page.locator('[aria-label*="keyboard shortcut"], [data-testid="shortcut-settings"]');
  const hasSettings = await shortcutSettings.count() > 0;

  if (hasSettings) {
    await expect(shortcutSettings.first()).toBeVisible();
  } else {
    // Alternative: verify shortcuts only activate when a component has focus
    // Press 's' globally — should NOT trigger a search shortcut when no input is focused
    await page.keyboard.press('s');
    const searchModal = page.locator('[role="dialog"][aria-label*="search" i]');
    const modalVisible = await searchModal.isVisible().catch(() => false);

    // If a search modal appeared from a bare 's' press, WCAG 2.1.4 requires a disable mechanism
    if (modalVisible) {
      // Look for the disable/remap affordance
      const escapeClose = async () => { await page.keyboard.press('Escape'); };
      await escapeClose();
      const disableHint = page.locator('[aria-label*="disable shortcut"], [data-shortcut-off]');
      expect(
        await disableHint.count(),
        'Single-char shortcut opened modal but no disable mechanism was found (WCAG 2.1.4)'
      ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: This test only catches globally-scoped single-character shortcuts and relies on visible shortcut-settings affordances or a testid hook. Shortcuts implemented via `keydown` listeners on `document` with no AT-discoverable disable path will be missed unless the test enumerates known shortcut keys. Supplement with a static analysis step that greps the codebase for `document.addEventListener('keydown'` and audits each handler for WCAG 2.1.4 compliance.

**Pattern 330** — WCAG 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions — placeholder-only label detection
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('form inputs are not labelled by placeholder text alone', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/signup');

  // axe-core's label rule catches missing labels, but not placeholder-only labels
  // Supplement with a custom DOM scan
  const placeholderOnlyInputs = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const inputs = Array.from(
      document.querySelectorAll<HTMLInputElement>('input:not([type="hidden"]):not([type="submit"]):not([type="button"]), textarea')
    );
    return inputs
      .filter((input) => {
        const hasLabel       = !!document.querySelector(`label[for="${input.id}"]`);
        const hasAriaLabel   = input.hasAttribute('aria-label');
        const hasAriaLabelledBy = input.hasAttribute('aria-labelledby');
        const hasPlaceholder = input.hasAttribute('placeholder');
        // Placeholder-only: has placeholder but no proper label
        return hasPlaceholder && !hasLabel && !hasAriaLabel && !hasAriaLabelledBy;
      })
      .map((input) => input.placeholder || input.name || input.id);
  });

  expect(
    placeholderOnlyInputs,
    `These inputs rely on placeholder text as their only label: [${placeholderOnlyInputs.join(', ')}]`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: This pattern does not detect visually-visible-but-non-programmatic labels (e.g., a `<p>` tag adjacent to the input acting as a visual label with no `for`/`aria-labelledby` association). Combine with axe-core's `label` rule and manual review of form layouts that use CSS Grid or Flexbox to position text-next-to-input without semantic association. Note that `placeholder` text also fails WCAG 1.4.3 contrast in many browser default styles — run a contrast scan on placeholder pseudo-elements separately.

**Pattern 331** — WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible — custom component focus ring regression test
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const CUSTOM_COMPONENTS = [
  { selector: '[data-component="dropdown-trigger"]', label: 'Dropdown trigger' },
  { selector: '[data-component="chip"]',              label: 'Chip/tag component' },
  { selector: '[data-component="toggle-switch"]',     label: 'Toggle switch' },
  { selector: '[data-component="date-picker-input"]', label: 'Date picker input' },
];

for (const { selector, label } of CUSTOM_COMPONENTS) {
  test(`${label} has visible focus ring when focused`, async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/components/preview');
    const el = page.locator(selector).first();
    await el.focus();

    // Capture computed outline/box-shadow that constitute the focus ring
    const focusStyles = await el.evaluate((node) => {
      const style = window.getComputedStyle(node);
      return {
        outline:      style.outline,
        outlineWidth: style.outlineWidth,
        boxShadow:    style.boxShadow,
      };
    });

    const hasOutline    = focusStyles.outlineWidth !== '0px' && focusStyles.outline !== 'none';
    const hasBoxShadow  = focusStyles.boxShadow !== 'none';

    expect(
      hasOutline || hasBoxShadow,
      `${label} has no visible focus indicator (outline: ${focusStyles.outline}, box-shadow: ${focusStyles.boxShadow})`
    ).toBe(true);
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: Computed `outline` and `box-shadow` detection does not cover all visible focus techniques — some components use `::before` pseudo-element rings or SVG `stroke` animations that are invisible to `getComputedStyle` on the host element. Supplement with a visual screenshot diff: take `page.screenshot()` before and after `.focus()` and assert that pixel content changed within the element's bounding box. Also: `outline: none` combined with a replacement `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px` passes this test but may fail under Windows High Contrast Mode where `box-shadow` is suppressed — pair with the `forcedColors` emulation test.

**Pattern 332** — WCAG 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose — `autocomplete` attribute completeness audit
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// WCAG 1.3.5 requires autocomplete tokens on inputs collecting personal info
const REQUIRED_AUTOCOMPLETE_MAP: Record<string, string> = {
  'input[name*="email" i]':      'email',
  'input[name*="phone" i]':      'tel',
  'input[name*="first" i]':      'given-name',
  'input[name*="last" i]':       'family-name',
  'input[name*="address" i]':    'street-address',
  'input[name*="zip" i]':        'postal-code',
  'input[name*="city" i]':       'address-level2',
  'input[name*="country" i]':    'country',
  'input[name*="username" i]':   'username',
  'input[type="password"]':       'current-password',
};

test('personal-info inputs declare correct autocomplete tokens (WCAG 1.3.5)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/account/profile');

  const failures: string[] = [];

  for (const [selector, expectedToken] of Object.entries(REQUIRED_AUTOCOMPLETE_MAP)) {
    const inputs = page.locator(selector);
    const count  = await inputs.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const autocomplete = await inputs.nth(i).getAttribute('autocomplete');
      if (!autocomplete || !autocomplete.includes(expectedToken)) {
        const name = await inputs.nth(i).getAttribute('name') ?? selector;
        failures.push(`"${name}": expected autocomplete to include "${expectedToken}", got "${autocomplete}"`);
      }
    }
  }

  expect(failures, failures.join('\n')).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Name-based heuristics (`name*="email"`) have both false positives (newsletter checkbox named `email_opt_in`) and false negatives (inputs with generic names like `field1`). Run this test as a signal-generating audit rather than a hard gate — review the failure list and add per-input override comments in source before blocking CI. Also: WCAG 1.3.5 only applies to inputs "that collect information about the user" — apply the `autocomplete` audit selectively to profile, checkout, and registration forms, not to generic search or filter inputs.

**Pattern 333** — ARIA APG Tabs pattern — keyboard contract full coverage test
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('Tab widget satisfies ARIA APG keyboard contract', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/components/tabs');

  const tablist = page.getByRole('tablist');
  const tabs    = tablist.getByRole('tab');
  const firstTab = tabs.first();

  // 1. ArrowRight moves focus to next tab (not activating unless automatic activation)
  await firstTab.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
  const secondTab = tabs.nth(1);
  await expect(secondTab).toBeFocused();

  // 2. ArrowLeft wraps back
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft');
  await expect(firstTab).toBeFocused();

  // 3. Home / End jump to first / last tab
  await page.keyboard.press('End');
  const lastTab = tabs.last();
  await expect(lastTab).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('Home');
  await expect(firstTab).toBeFocused();

  // 4. Space/Enter activates the focused tab
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(firstTab).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');

  // 5. Tab key moves focus OUT of the tablist into the associated tabpanel
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  const activePanel = page.getByRole('tabpanel');
  const panelOrDescendant = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const panel = document.querySelector('[role="tabpanel"]');
    return panel?.contains(document.activeElement) || document.activeElement === panel;
  });
  expect(panelOrDescendant, 'Tab key should move focus into the active tabpanel').toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: The APG tabs pattern supports both manual-activation (Enter/Space activates) and automatic-activation (ArrowKey immediately activates) — this test assumes manual activation. If your implementation uses automatic activation, remove the `Enter` press assertion and instead assert `aria-selected` after each `ArrowRight`. Also: the `Home`/`End` keys are not universally implemented in older tab widget libraries — this test will correctly flag the gap but may require a library upgrade rather than a simple bug fix.

**Pattern 334** — WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages — `role="status"` announcement timing test
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('form save success message is announced as a status (WCAG 4.1.3)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings/profile');

  // Set up a listener to capture announced live region updates
  const announcements: string[] = [];
  await page.exposeFunction('captureAnnouncement', (text: string) => {
    announcements.push(text);
  });

  // Inject a MutationObserver to watch live regions before triggering the action
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    const observer = new MutationObserver((mutations) => {
      mutations.forEach((m) => {
        m.addedNodes.forEach((node) => {
          if (node.nodeType === Node.TEXT_NODE || node instanceof Element) {
            const text = (node as Element).textContent ?? (node as Text).textContent ?? '';
            if (text.trim()) (window as any).captureAnnouncement(text.trim());
          }
        });
        if (m.type === 'characterData' && m.target.textContent?.trim()) {
          (window as any).captureAnnouncement(m.target.textContent.trim());
        }
      });
    });
    document.querySelectorAll('[role="status"],[role="alert"],[aria-live]').forEach((el) =>
      observer.observe(el, { childList: true, characterData: true, subtree: true })
    );
  });

  // Trigger the save action
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /save/i }).click();

  // Wait for the announcement to appear
  await page.waitForFunction(() => (window as any).__announcements?.length > 0 || true, { timeout: 3000 }).catch(() => {});
  await page.waitForTimeout(500); // allow DOM mutation to propagate

  const hasSuccessAnnouncement = announcements.some((a) => /saved|success|updated/i.test(a));
  expect(hasSuccessAnnouncement, `No status announcement detected. Captured: [${announcements.join(', ')}]`).toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: The MutationObserver approach captures live region DOM mutations but cannot verify the actual text that a screen reader announced — screen readers queue and deduplicate announcements in ways that differ from the raw DOM content. For ground-truth announcement testing, use Guidepup (Pattern 325). This pattern is useful for fast CI verification that a live region exists and receives content; treat it as a structural check, not a screen-reader fidelity check. Also: if the status message is injected by clearing and re-setting the same text node (a common React pattern), MutationObserver may only capture one mutation — use `characterData: true` alongside `childList: true`.

**Pattern 335** — WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name — button/link visible text matches accessible name
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('interactive element accessible names contain their visible label text (WCAG 2.5.3)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const interactives = page.locator('a[href], button');
  const count = await interactives.count();
  const failures: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 50); i++) {
    const el = interactives.nth(i);
    const visibleText  = (await el.innerText()).trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ');
    const accessibleName = await el.evaluate((node) =>
      (node as HTMLElement).getAttribute('aria-label') ??
      (node as HTMLElement).getAttribute('aria-labelledby') ??
      ''
    );

    // If an aria-label or aria-labelledby overrides the visible text, the visible text
    // must be a substring of the accessible name (WCAG 2.5.3)
    if (accessibleName && visibleText && !accessibleName.toLowerCase().includes(visibleText.toLowerCase())) {
      failures.push(
        `Element ${i}: visible="${visibleText}" accessible="${accessibleName}" — visible text not contained in accessible name`
      );
    }
  }

  expect(failures, failures.join('\n')).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `innerText` is sensitive to CSS `text-transform` — a button with `text-transform: uppercase` in CSS returns uppercase `innerText`, but the `aria-label` may use mixed case, causing a false positive. Normalize both strings to lowercase before comparison. Also: icon-only buttons (`<button aria-label="Close"><svg>…</svg></button>`) have empty `innerText` and should be excluded from this check — add `if (!visibleText) continue;` to skip them. Accessible names computed via `aria-labelledby` require dereferencing the referenced element's text, which this pattern does not do — use the Accessibility Tree API (`page.accessibility.snapshot()`) for full name resolution.

**Pattern 336** — WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color — color-only state change detection via computed styles
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('error state is not conveyed by color change alone (WCAG 1.4.1)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout/payment');

  const emailInput = page.getByLabel(/email/i);

  // Capture baseline border and background before error
  const baselineStyle = await emailInput.evaluate((el) => {
    const s = window.getComputedStyle(el);
    return { border: s.borderColor, background: s.backgroundColor, outline: s.outline };
  });

  // Trigger validation error
  await emailInput.fill('not-an-email');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next|continue|submit/i }).click();

  // Capture post-error style
  const errorStyle = await emailInput.evaluate((el) => {
    const s = window.getComputedStyle(el);
    return { border: s.borderColor, background: s.backgroundColor, outline: s.outline };
  });

  // If color changed, a non-color indicator MUST also exist
  const colorChanged = baselineStyle.border !== errorStyle.border || baselineStyle.background !== errorStyle.background;
  if (colorChanged) {
    // Non-color indicators: error icon, error text, aria-invalid, aria-describedby
    const hasAriaInvalid     = await emailInput.getAttribute('aria-invalid');
    const hasErrorText       = await page.locator('[role="alert"], .error-message, [data-error]').count() > 0;
    expect(
      hasAriaInvalid === 'true' || hasErrorText,
      'Input error is conveyed by color change only — no aria-invalid or visible error text found (WCAG 1.4.1)'
    ).toBe(true);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: This test only inspects `borderColor` and `backgroundColor` — some designs use icon changes (a red X replacing a neutral icon) or text weight changes as non-color error indicators that are invisible to style comparisons. Supplement with a screenshot diff and a manual review checklist for color-only state changes. Also: the pattern fires a click on a submit button to trigger validation — in SPAs where validation is triggered on `blur` rather than submit, replace the click with `emailInput.blur()` to match the actual validation lifecycle.

**Pattern 337** — axe-core `AxeBuilder.withTags` — scoped WCAG 2.2 AA full-page scan fixture
```typescript
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

// Shared fixture: pre-configured axe builder for WCAG 2.2 AA
const test = base.extend<{ axe: AxeBuilder }>({
  axe: async ({ page }, use) => {
    const builder = new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
      .options({ resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'] });
    await use(builder);
  },
});

test('home page passes WCAG 2.2 AA scan', async ({ page, axe }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  const results = await axe.analyze();

  // Attach full results to the test report for triage
  await test.info().attach('axe-results', {
    body:        JSON.stringify(results, null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  expect(results.violations, formatViolations(results.violations)).toHaveLength(0);
});

function formatViolations(violations: any[]): string {
  return violations
    .map((v) => `[${v.id}] ${v.description}\n  Nodes: ${v.nodes.map((n: any) => n.target.join(', ')).join(' | ')}`)
    .join('\n');
}
```
Tradeoff: Including `'incomplete'` in `resultTypes` surfaces "needs review" items that axe-core cannot automatically determine — these require manual triage and will cause the test to fail on every run until suppressed. Use `incomplete` results during initial audit runs to discover grey-area items, then switch to `resultTypes: ['violations']` for the gating CI check. Also: `wcag22aa` tag in axe-core 4.9+ adds checks for WCAG 2.2 new success criteria (2.4.11, 2.4.12, 3.2.6, 3.3.7, 3.3.8) — verify your version of `@axe-core/playwright` includes this tag before relying on it.

**Pattern 338** — WCAG 2.4.6 Headings and Labels — heading hierarchy snapshot test
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('page heading hierarchy is sequential without skipped levels', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const headings = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6')).map((el) => ({
      level: parseInt(el.tagName.slice(1), 10),
      text:  (el.textContent ?? '').trim().slice(0, 60),
    }));
  });

  // Verify there is exactly one h1
  const h1Count = headings.filter((h) => h.level === 1).length;
  expect(h1Count, `Page must have exactly one <h1>, found ${h1Count}`).toBe(1);

  // Verify no level is skipped (e.g., h2 → h4 is a skip)
  const skips: string[] = [];
  for (let i = 1; i < headings.length; i++) {
    const prev = headings[i - 1];
    const curr = headings[i];
    if (curr.level > prev.level + 1) {
      skips.push(`"${prev.text}" (h${prev.level}) → "${curr.text}" (h${curr.level}) skips level h${prev.level + 1}`);
    }
  }

  expect(skips, `Heading level skips detected:\n${skips.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Heading level skips are technically a WCAG advisory technique (H42), not a hard failure — this test enforces a best practice that some legitimate designs violate intentionally (e.g., a visually prominent h2-styled element that is semantically h3 for outline reasons). Treat failures as warnings in first-run audits rather than blocking CI. Also: this test counts all headings in the DOM including those inside `display: none` containers — filter to only visible headings by adding `if (window.getComputedStyle(el).display === 'none') return null` and filtering out nulls.

**Pattern 339** — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) — interactive element 24×24 px target audit
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('interactive elements meet WCAG 2.5.8 24×24px minimum target size', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const smallTargets = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const MIN_SIZE = 24;
    const interactives = Array.from(
      document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('a[href], button, [role="button"], input, select, [role="checkbox"], [role="radio"]')
    );

    return interactives
      .filter((el) => {
        if (window.getComputedStyle(el).display === 'none') return false;
        const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        // WCAG 2.5.8 exception: element is inline in a sentence of text
        const isInlineText = window.getComputedStyle(el).display === 'inline';
        return !isInlineText && (rect.width < MIN_SIZE || rect.height < MIN_SIZE);
      })
      .map((el) => {
        const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        return `${el.tagName}[${el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? el.textContent?.trim().slice(0, 20)}] ${Math.round(rect.width)}×${Math.round(rect.height)}px`;
      });
  });

  expect(
    smallTargets,
    `These elements are below the 24×24px WCAG 2.5.8 minimum target size:\n${smallTargets.join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `getBoundingClientRect()` returns the element's clickable area in CSS pixels — this is correct for WCAG 2.5.8 compliance which specifies CSS pixel measurements. However, on high-DPI screens (2× retina), the visual target size perceived by users is determined by physical pixels, which may feel smaller than the CSS pixel calculation implies. The WCAG 2.5.8 exception for inline text links (hyperlinks in a paragraph) is handled by the `display === 'inline'` check — but some inline elements use `display: inline-flex`, which this check misses. Extend the inline exclusion to cover `inline-flex` and `inline-block` elements whose adjacent siblings are text nodes.

**Pattern 340** — WCAG 3.1.2 Language of Parts — `lang` attribute on non-default-language content
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('page root has a valid lang attribute and non-English content uses lang overrides', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // 1. Root lang attribute must be present and BCP 47 valid
  const rootLang = await page.locator('html').getAttribute('lang');
  expect(rootLang, '<html> must have a lang attribute').toBeTruthy();
  expect(rootLang, 'lang must be a valid BCP 47 language tag (e.g., "en", "en-US", "fr")').toMatch(
    /^[a-zA-Z]{2,3}(-[a-zA-Z]{2,4}(-[a-zA-Z0-9]{1,8})*)?$/
  );

  // 2. Elements with a different language must declare lang
  // This checks for common multilingual UI patterns (language selector, translated quotes, etc.)
  const langSwitchLinks = page.locator('[data-lang], [hreflang]');
  const count = await langSwitchLinks.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const el = langSwitchLinks.nth(i);
    const lang      = await el.getAttribute('lang') ?? await el.getAttribute('hreflang');
    const innerText = (await el.innerText()).trim();

    if (lang && lang !== rootLang && innerText) {
      // The element declares a different language — verify the lang value is also BCP 47 valid
      expect(
        lang,
        `Element with text "${innerText.slice(0, 30)}" has invalid lang="${lang}"`
      ).toMatch(/^[a-zA-Z]{2,3}(-[a-zA-Z]{2,4})?$/);
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: This test checks structural `lang` presence but cannot verify semantic accuracy — a page with `lang="en"` that contains a French blockquote without `lang="fr"` will pass this test if no `data-lang` or `hreflang` attribute is present. For multilingual apps, supplement with a translation-key audit that maps known non-English strings to their source locale and asserts the containing element carries the correct `lang` override. Also: the BCP 47 regex used here is a simplified approximation — edge-case tags like `zh-Hant-TW` (Traditional Chinese, Taiwan) require a full BCP 47 parser for strict validation.

---

### Community Gotchas

**G261** — `aria-expanded` on a trigger element is not enough — the controlled region must also be programmatically discoverable via `aria-controls`
Why this matters: Screen readers announce "button, collapsed, Filters" from `aria-expanded="false"` but many users then press Enter/Space expecting to navigate to the expanded content. If the trigger lacks `aria-controls="panelId"`, AT cannot programmatically jump to the newly revealed panel — users must manually hunt for the expanded content. JAWS's virtual cursor jumps to the first newly-visible element in DOM order, which may be unrelated content if the panel is appended to `document.body` via a portal. NVDA simply leaves the cursor on the button. The ARIA authoring spec requires the relationship to be explicit via `aria-controls`.
Fix: Add `aria-controls="<panel-id>"` on every trigger that uses `aria-expanded`. Verify with `expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-controls')` and confirm the referenced `id` exists in the DOM: `expect(page.locator(`#${panelId}`)).toBeAttached()`.

**G262** — Tooltip content associated via `aria-describedby` is NOT announced on focus in all screen reader/browser combinations — VoiceOver on iOS and TalkBack on Android both suppress `aria-describedby` content on initial focus
Why this matters: Developers rely on `aria-describedby` to associate tooltips, additional hints, and character count messages with form inputs. The ARIA spec mandates that `aria-describedby` content is included in the accessible description, but iOS VoiceOver reads the description only after a 2-second delay (or not at all if the user moves on quickly). TalkBack on Android omits descriptions entirely on first focus — users must swipe-right a second time to hear the description. This affects password-hint text, input format instructions, and error-helper text that is inside a tooltip rather than directly below the input.
Fix: Use `aria-describedby` to reference visible helper text rendered directly in the DOM adjacent to the input (not in a tooltip overlay). For mobile AT coverage, assert that the referenced element is both in the DOM and visible: `await expect(page.locator('#hint-text')).toBeVisible()`. Do not hide helper text behind `display: none` or `visibility: hidden` — both remove the element from the accessibility tree, silently breaking the description association.

**G263** — `role="dialog"` without `aria-modal="true"` allows screen reader virtual cursors to wander outside the dialog boundaries — content behind the modal remains navigable
Why this matters: When a dialog opens and `aria-modal="true"` is absent, JAWS and NVDA's virtual cursor (document reading mode) ignores the dialog boundary and continues reading all background DOM content as if the modal were not present. This exposes partially-obscured controls (buttons, links behind the overlay) to AT users. The fix appears simple but has a critical nuance: adding `aria-modal="true"` without also managing `inert` on background content causes VoiceOver on macOS to still escape the dialog — VoiceOver does not fully honor `aria-modal` and requires the background DOM to be `inert`.
Fix: Apply both `aria-modal="true"` on `role="dialog"` AND `inert` on all sibling containers that are not the dialog. Use a focus-trap library (e.g., `focus-trap-react`) that handles both attributes. In Playwright, assert: `await expect(page.locator('[role="dialog"]')).toHaveAttribute('aria-modal', 'true')` and `await expect(page.locator('main')).toHaveAttribute('inert')` when the modal is open.

**G264** — Lazy-loaded images that use `loading="lazy"` and no explicit `width`/`height` attributes cause Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), and also break `alt` text association in some screen readers when the image swaps from a blank placeholder to the real `src`
Why this matters: When `<img loading="lazy">` lacks explicit `width` and `height` attributes, browsers cannot reserve layout space before the image loads — the page reflows when the image enters the viewport. For AT users, the reflow causes the focus position to shift unexpectedly. More critically: some screen reader + browser combinations (older NVDA + Chrome) re-announce the image's `alt` text when the `src` attribute is swapped by the lazy-load intersection observer, causing a duplicate or out-of-context announcement mid-read. The layout shift also invalidates axe-core's color contrast measurements taken before the image loaded (the background color under a lazy image may be white before load and a dark hero-image afterward).
Fix: Always include `width` and `height` attributes on lazy-loaded images. Add `aspect-ratio: attr(width) / attr(height)` in CSS as a progressive enhancement. In Playwright tests, call `await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')` before running axe-core to ensure lazy images have settled. Assert: `await expect(page.locator('img[loading="lazy"]')).each((img) => expect(img).toHaveAttribute('width'))`.

**G265** — Using `tabindex="-1"` to remove an element from the tab order does NOT remove it from the accessibility tree — screen reader virtual cursor (document browse mode) still reaches it, so `tabindex="-1"` alone is not a substitute for `aria-hidden="true"` when hiding decorative content from AT
Why this matters: Developers use `tabindex="-1"` on decorative icons, duplicate text badges, and redundant skip-link anchors to prevent them from appearing in the keyboard tab sequence. However, NVDA, JAWS, and VoiceOver virtual cursors navigate the DOM in document order using arrow keys — `tabindex="-1"` does not affect this. Users in browse/read mode encounter the decorative element, hear its (often empty or confusing) accessible name, and must manually skip past it. This is especially problematic for icon fonts (`<i class="icon-chevron">`) where the Unicode glyph is announced as "right-pointing angle bracket" by some AT.
Fix: For purely decorative elements that contribute no information: add both `tabindex="-1"` (removes from tab order) AND `aria-hidden="true"` (removes from accessibility tree). For icon fonts, always add `aria-hidden="true"` unless the icon is the sole content of a button/link, in which case add an accessible name via `aria-label` on the parent. Verify with: `await expect(page.locator('.icon-decorative')).toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true')`.

## Cycle 58 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 341** — WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast Minimum — automated contrast audit for all text nodes using axe-core and getComputedStyle fallback
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('all visible text meets WCAG 1.4.3 AA contrast ratio (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large text)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Run axe-core targeting only color-contrast rules
  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withRules(['color-contrast'])
    .withTags(['wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa'])
    .analyze();

  // Attach full results to test report for debugging
  await test.info().attach('contrast-axe-results', {
    body: JSON.stringify(results.violations, null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  // Zero violations expected
  expect(
    results.violations,
    `Color contrast violations:\n${results.violations.map(v => `  [${v.id}] ${v.description}\n    Nodes: ${v.nodes.map(n => n.html).join(', ')}`).join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: axe-core's color-contrast rule resolves computed CSS colors — it correctly handles CSS custom properties and `color-mix()` in modern browsers, but cannot detect contrast failures inside canvas elements, SVG `<text>` rendered via `fill` property on non-white backgrounds, or text rendered inside `<video>` captions. For SVG text, supplement with a targeted `getComputedStyle` check: retrieve `fill` and the parent background, then compute the contrast ratio manually using the WCAG relative-luminance formula. Also, axe's contrast check is synchronous with the DOM snapshot — dynamic text color changes on hover/focus require separate interaction-state tests.

**Pattern 342** — WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible — computed outline detection after `:focus-visible` pseudo-class activation
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('interactive elements display a visible focus ring when focused via keyboard', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

  // Collect all focusable interactive elements
  const focusableSelectors = 'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';
  const elements = page.locator(focusableSelectors);
  const count = await elements.count();

  const failures: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 30); i++) {
    const el = elements.nth(i);
    await el.focus();

    // Read computed outline after focus (resolves :focus-visible styles)
    const outlineWidth = await el.evaluate(node => {
      const style = window.getComputedStyle(node);
      return parseFloat(style.outlineWidth);
    });
    const outlineStyle = await el.evaluate(node =>
      window.getComputedStyle(node).outlineStyle
    );
    const boxShadow = await el.evaluate(node =>
      window.getComputedStyle(node).boxShadow
    );

    const hasFocusRing =
      (outlineWidth > 0 && outlineStyle !== 'none') ||
      (boxShadow !== 'none' && boxShadow !== '');

    if (!hasFocusRing) {
      const tagName = await el.evaluate(n => n.tagName.toLowerCase());
      const label   = await el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? await el.textContent();
      failures.push(`<${tagName}> "${(label ?? '').trim().slice(0, 40)}" — no visible focus ring`);
    }
  }

  expect(failures, `Elements without visible focus ring:\n${failures.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `getComputedStyle` resolves the final painted style but does NOT trigger browser-native `:focus-visible` heuristics in all headless Chromium versions — Playwright's `el.focus()` programmatic focus may not activate `:focus-visible` the same way a real Tab keypress does. Use `page.keyboard.press('Tab')` in a loop instead of `el.focus()` if you observe false-negatives. This test caps at 30 elements to keep runtime bounded; for a full audit adjust the cap or split across multiple test files.

**Pattern 343** — WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value — ARIA attribute completeness audit for custom interactive components
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('custom interactive components expose correct ARIA name, role, and state', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // 1. Axe-core aria-required-attr + aria-valid-attr rules
  const axeResults = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withRules(['aria-required-attr', 'aria-valid-attr', 'aria-valid-attr-value', 'button-name', 'link-name'])
    .analyze();

  expect(axeResults.violations).toHaveLength(0);

  // 2. Assert every toggle button exposes aria-pressed
  const toggleButtons = page.locator('button[aria-pressed]');
  const toggleCount = await toggleButtons.count();
  for (let i = 0; i < toggleCount; i++) {
    const pressed = await toggleButtons.nth(i).getAttribute('aria-pressed');
    expect(['true', 'false'], `aria-pressed must be "true" or "false", got "${pressed}"`).toContain(pressed);
  }

  // 3. Assert every expandable section has aria-expanded on its trigger
  const expandTriggers = page.locator('[aria-controls]');
  const expandCount = await expandTriggers.count();
  for (let i = 0; i < expandCount; i++) {
    await expect(expandTriggers.nth(i)).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', /^(true|false)$/);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: axe-core checks ARIA attribute syntax but does not validate that `aria-controls` values reference existing DOM IDs at runtime (the referenced element may be injected asynchronously). Add a manual assertion: `const controlledId = await trigger.getAttribute('aria-controls'); await expect(page.locator(`#${controlledId}`)).toBeAttached()` after each expandable trigger check to catch broken cross-references.

**Pattern 344** — WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard — full keyboard navigation smoke test with tab-order recording
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('all critical actions are reachable via keyboard Tab/Enter/Space without a mouse', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

  const tabOrder: string[] = [];
  const MAX_TABS = 50;

  for (let i = 0; i < MAX_TABS; i++) {
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focused = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement;
      if (!el || el === document.body) return null;
      const tag  = el.tagName.toLowerCase();
      const role = el.getAttribute('role') ?? '';
      const name = el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? el.textContent?.trim().slice(0, 30) ?? '';
      return `${tag}[${role}] "${name}"`;
    });
    if (focused) tabOrder.push(focused);
  }

  // Verify key landmarks are reachable
  const hasMainNav   = tabOrder.some(e => e.includes('nav') || e.includes('navigation'));
  const hasMainCTA   = tabOrder.some(e => e.toLowerCase().includes('submit') || e.toLowerCase().includes('save'));
  const hasSkipLink  = tabOrder[0]?.toLowerCase().includes('skip') ?? false;

  expect(hasSkipLink, 'First Tab stop should be a skip navigation link').toBe(true);
  expect(hasMainNav,  'Main navigation must be reachable via keyboard').toBe(true);
  expect(hasMainCTA,  'Primary action (submit/save) must be reachable via keyboard').toBe(true);

  // No element should appear twice (positive tabindex anti-pattern)
  const duplicates = tabOrder.filter((e, i) => tabOrder.indexOf(e) !== i);
  expect(duplicates, `Duplicate tab stops detected (positive tabindex?): ${duplicates.join(', ')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `document.activeElement` in `page.evaluate()` is synchronous with the DOM frame — there is a small race window if focus transitions via JavaScript animation. Wrapping in `await page.waitForFunction(() => document.activeElement !== document.body)` after each Tab press eliminates false `null` readings in animated SPAs. The MAX_TABS cap prevents infinite loops on pages with cyclic focus traps, but means deep pages with many controls won't be fully audited; split into section-level tests for thoroughness.

**Pattern 345** — WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content — image alt text completeness and quality audit
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('all meaningful images have non-empty alt text; decorative images have alt=""', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const images = page.locator('img');
  const count  = await images.count();
  const failures: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const img = images.nth(i);
    const alt  = await img.getAttribute('alt');
    const src  = (await img.getAttribute('src') ?? '').slice(0, 60);
    const role = await img.getAttribute('role');

    // alt attribute must always be present (even for decorative images)
    if (alt === null) {
      failures.push(`MISSING alt attr: <img src="${src}">`);
      continue;
    }

    // Decorative images: role="presentation" or role="none" with alt=""
    if (role === 'presentation' || role === 'none') {
      if (alt !== '') {
        failures.push(`Decorative img (role="${role}") should have alt="": <img src="${src}" alt="${alt}">`);
      }
      continue;
    }

    // Meaningful images must have non-empty, non-generic alt text
    const genericAlt = /^(image|photo|picture|icon|logo|img|graphic|\s*)$/i;
    if (genericAlt.test(alt)) {
      failures.push(`Generic/empty alt text on meaningful image: <img src="${src}" alt="${alt}">`);
    }
  }

  expect(failures, `Image alt text failures:\n${failures.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: This test can only catch structurally bad alt text (missing, empty, or regex-matched generic strings) — it cannot assess semantic quality. An alt text of "A smiling person" on an e-commerce product image that should read "Blue cotton T-shirt, front view" will pass this test. For quality audits, export all alt texts to a CSV and review manually, or use an LLM-based alt text quality scorer as a supplementary step. Also: SVG `<use>` elements referencing external sprites inherit their accessible name from the symbol's `<title>` inside the sprite sheet, which may not be loaded in the page DOM — test these separately.

**Pattern 346** — WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order — logical DOM order verification against visual reading order via bounding-rect comparison
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('DOM order of focusable elements matches top-to-bottom, left-to-right visual reading order', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

  const focusable = page.locator('a[href], button:not([disabled]), [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])');
  const count = await focusable.count();

  type Rect = { index: number; top: number; left: number; tag: string; label: string };
  const rects: Rect[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const el = focusable.nth(i);
    const box = await el.boundingBox();
    if (!box) continue; // Skip hidden elements
    const tag   = await el.evaluate(n => n.tagName.toLowerCase());
    const label = (await el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? await el.textContent() ?? '').trim().slice(0, 30);
    rects.push({ index: i, top: box.y, left: box.x, tag, label });
  }

  // Check that DOM order (index) follows visual top-to-bottom order
  // Allow 10px tolerance for elements on the same visual line
  const outOfOrder: string[] = [];
  for (let i = 1; i < rects.length; i++) {
    const prev = rects[i - 1];
    const curr = rects[i];
    const sameRow = Math.abs(curr.top - prev.top) < 10;
    const domOrderMatchesVisual = sameRow
      ? curr.left >= prev.left        // Same row: left-to-right
      : curr.top  >= prev.top;        // Different rows: top-to-bottom
    if (!domOrderMatchesVisual) {
      outOfOrder.push(`DOM[${i}] <${curr.tag}> "${curr.label}" (top:${curr.top}, left:${curr.left}) appears before DOM[${i-1}] visually`);
    }
  }

  expect(outOfOrder, `Focus order mismatches:\n${outOfOrder.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: This test assumes a standard LTR reading grid. For RTL (`dir="rtl"`) pages, reverse the left-to-right directional logic. Absolutely-positioned elements (tooltips, popovers, sticky headers) will generate false positives because their `boundingBox()` top/left reflects painted position, not DOM insertion point. Exclude absolutely-positioned elements with: `await el.evaluate(n => getComputedStyle(n).position !== 'absolute')` as a filter before adding to `rects`.

**Pattern 347** — WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification — form validation error messages are programmatically associated and announced
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('form validation errors are associated with inputs via aria-describedby and announced via role="alert"', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/contact');
  await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

  // Submit empty form to trigger validation
  await page.locator('button[type="submit"]').click();
  await page.waitForSelector('[role="alert"], .error-message, [aria-live]', { timeout: 3000 });

  // 1. Every required input must have aria-describedby pointing to its error
  const requiredInputs = page.locator('input[required], select[required], textarea[required]');
  const inputCount = await requiredInputs.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < inputCount; i++) {
    const input = requiredInputs.nth(i);
    const describedBy = await input.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
    if (describedBy) {
      const errorEl = page.locator(`#${describedBy}`);
      await expect(errorEl, `Error element #${describedBy} must be visible`).toBeVisible();
      const errorText = await errorEl.textContent();
      expect(errorText?.trim().length ?? 0, 'Error message must not be empty').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  }

  // 2. axe-core scan to catch aria-label and form-related violations
  const axeResults = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withRules(['label', 'aria-required-attr', 'form-field-multiple-labels'])
    .analyze();
  expect(axeResults.violations).toHaveLength(0);

  // 3. Playwright built-in: error messages must have accessible error role
  const alerts = page.locator('[role="alert"]');
  const alertCount = await alerts.count();
  expect(alertCount, 'At least one role="alert" must be present after invalid submission').toBeGreaterThan(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.waitForSelector` with a 3-second timeout covers most async validation pipelines, but server-side validation that requires a network round-trip may take longer — increase the timeout or use `page.waitForResponse()` to gate on the API response. Also, `aria-describedby` associations are set at input render time; frameworks that re-create input elements during re-renders (React strict mode double-invocation) may break the ID association if error elements are injected before the input re-mounts. Use `aria-errormessage` (ARIA 1.1+) as a more semantically explicit alternative, though axe-core support for `aria-errormessage` validation arrived in version 4.9.

**Pattern 348** — WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow — 320px viewport horizontal scroll absence test
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('page content reflows to single column at 320px width without horizontal scrolling (WCAG 1.4.10)', async ({ page }) => {
  // 320px CSS width at 1× device pixel ratio = WCAG 1.4.10 reference viewport
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 320, height: 256 });
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Check for horizontal overflow on the body/html
  const horizontalOverflow = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const body = document.body;
    const html = document.documentElement;
    return {
      bodyScrollWidth:   body.scrollWidth,
      htmlScrollWidth:   html.scrollWidth,
      viewportWidth:     window.innerWidth,
      bodyOverflows:     body.scrollWidth > window.innerWidth + 2,   // 2px tolerance
      htmlOverflows:     html.scrollWidth > window.innerWidth + 2,
    };
  });

  expect(
    horizontalOverflow.bodyOverflows || horizontalOverflow.htmlOverflows,
    `Horizontal overflow at 320px: body.scrollWidth=${horizontalOverflow.bodyScrollWidth}px, html.scrollWidth=${horizontalOverflow.htmlScrollWidth}px, viewport=${horizontalOverflow.viewportWidth}px`
  ).toBe(false);

  // Also check that no element has a fixed width wider than the viewport
  const wideElements = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const all = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('*'));
    return all
      .filter(el => el.getBoundingClientRect().width > window.innerWidth + 2)
      .map(el => `<${el.tagName.toLowerCase()}> class="${el.className}" w=${Math.round(el.getBoundingClientRect().width)}px`);
  });

  expect(wideElements, `Elements wider than 320px viewport:\n${wideElements.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `scrollWidth > innerWidth` correctly detects overflow caused by fixed-width containers, but does NOT detect overflow hidden by `overflow: hidden` on a parent — content is clipped rather than triggering a scrollbar, which technically passes this numeric check while still failing WCAG 1.4.10 intent. Supplement with a visual snapshot comparison at 320px to catch hidden-overflow clipping. Also: some third-party embeds (maps, payment widgets) are exempt from WCAG 1.4.10 if the content "requires two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning" (e.g., a data grid); add explicit exclusions for such iframes using `AxeBuilder.exclude()` or skip the wide-element check for `<iframe>` tags.

**Pattern 349** — WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages — live region announcement test using MutationObserver interception
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('dynamic status messages are announced via aria-live regions without moving keyboard focus', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

  // Intercept MutationObserver-level changes to aria-live regions
  const liveRegionUpdates: string[] = [];
  await page.exposeFunction('recordLiveUpdate', (text: string) => {
    liveRegionUpdates.push(text);
  });

  await page.evaluate(() => {
    const regions = document.querySelectorAll('[aria-live], [role="alert"], [role="status"]');
    regions.forEach(region => {
      const observer = new MutationObserver(mutations => {
        mutations.forEach(m => {
          const text = (m.target as Element).textContent?.trim();
          if (text) (window as any).recordLiveUpdate(text);
        });
      });
      observer.observe(region, { childList: true, subtree: true, characterData: true });
    });
  });

  // Trigger an action that produces a status message
  const focusBefore = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.tagName);
  await page.locator('button[data-action="save"], button:has-text("Save")').first().click();
  await page.waitForTimeout(500); // Allow async announcement to propagate

  // Verify a live region was updated
  expect(liveRegionUpdates.length, 'At least one aria-live region must have been updated after the action').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Verify focus was NOT moved (status message must not steal focus)
  const focusAfter = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.tagName);
  expect(focusAfter, 'Focus must not move when a status message is announced').toBe(focusBefore);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.exposeFunction` bridges Node.js and browser contexts synchronously — the `recordLiveUpdate` callback is reliable but introduces a small overhead per mutation event. On pages with high-frequency live region updates (e.g., a live sports score ticker), this can generate thousands of callbacks and slow the test. Scope the MutationObserver to a specific region ID rather than all `[aria-live]` selectors when the target region is known. Also: `role="alert"` regions fire immediately regardless of `aria-live` value — inserting content into an alert region that already has content may not re-announce in NVDA. Use `innerHTML = ''` then set content to force re-announcement; test this with Guidepup if screen-reader-level verification is required.

**Pattern 350** — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size Minimum — bounding-rect geometry audit for all interactive touch targets
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const MIN_TARGET_SIZE = 24; // px — WCAG 2.5.8 AA minimum
const SPACING_OFFSET  = 24; // px — acceptable via spacing mechanism

test('all interactive touch targets meet WCAG 2.5.8 24×24px minimum (with spacing offset)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 390, height: 844 }); // iPhone 14 Pro
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const interactive = page.locator('a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([type="hidden"]):not([disabled]), select, [role="button"], [role="link"]');
  const count = await interactive.count();
  const undersized: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const el  = interactive.nth(i);
    const box = await el.boundingBox();
    if (!box) continue; // Hidden element

    const tooSmall = box.width < MIN_TARGET_SIZE || box.height < MIN_TARGET_SIZE;
    if (tooSmall) {
      // Check if spacing offset exemption applies — nearest interactive neighbor must be >= 24px away
      const tag   = await el.evaluate(n => n.tagName.toLowerCase());
      const label = (await el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? await el.textContent() ?? '').trim().slice(0, 30);
      undersized.push(`<${tag}> "${label}" — ${Math.round(box.width)}×${Math.round(box.height)}px (min ${MIN_TARGET_SIZE}×${MIN_TARGET_SIZE}px)`);
    }
  }

  // WCAG 2.5.8 allows failure if offset from nearest target provides equivalent activation area
  // For automated testing, flag all undersized targets for manual spacing review
  if (undersized.length > 0) {
    console.warn(`[WCAG 2.5.8] Targets below ${MIN_TARGET_SIZE}px requiring manual spacing review:\n${undersized.join('\n')}`);
  }
  // Hard-fail if any target is below 16px (no spacing offset can compensate)
  const criticallySmall = undersized.filter(s => /— \d×/.test(s) && parseInt(s.match(/— (\d+)×/)![1]) < 16);
  expect(criticallySmall, `Critically undersized targets (< 16px):\n${criticallySmall.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `boundingBox()` returns the element's CSS layout box, not the visual painted area — CSS `padding` is included, but `::before`/`::after` pseudo-elements that extend the clickable area via `content: ""` are not. This means icon buttons with a small SVG surrounded by generous padding will show the SVG's intrinsic size, not the padded click target. Use `el.evaluate(n => n.getBoundingClientRect())` and compare against the parent padding if icon buttons are common in your design system. The hard-fail threshold of 16px is a pragmatic engineering choice — adjust to 20px for products targeting users with motor impairments as a primary audience.

**Pattern 351** — WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships — heading hierarchy snapshot and sequential order validation
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('heading hierarchy is sequential (no skipped levels) and matches page structure (WCAG 1.3.1)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

  const headings = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const els = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6'));
    return els.map(el => ({
      level: parseInt(el.tagName[1]),
      text:  el.textContent?.trim().slice(0, 60) ?? '',
      id:    el.id ?? '',
    }));
  });

  // Must have exactly one h1
  const h1s = headings.filter(h => h.level === 1);
  expect(h1s, 'Page must contain exactly one <h1>').toHaveLength(1);

  // No heading level must skip more than one level down
  const skips: string[] = [];
  for (let i = 1; i < headings.length; i++) {
    const prev = headings[i - 1];
    const curr = headings[i];
    if (curr.level > prev.level + 1) {
      skips.push(`Skipped from h${prev.level} "${prev.text}" → h${curr.level} "${curr.text}"`);
    }
  }
  expect(skips, `Heading level skips detected:\n${skips.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);

  // Snapshot heading structure for regression detection
  const snapshot = headings.map(h => `${'  '.repeat(h.level - 1)}h${h.level}: ${h.text}`).join('\n');
  expect(snapshot).toMatchSnapshot('heading-hierarchy.txt');
});
```
Tradeoff: Heading level skips are a WCAG advisory technique, not a hard failure — the test above treats them as failures for tighter quality gates, which is appropriate for new development but may be too strict for legacy codebases. Use `test.soft()` assertions for the skip check when running against inherited content. The `toMatchSnapshot` call creates a regression guard but will fail on any content update — use named snapshots with a `--update-snapshots` flag in CI when intentional heading structure changes are merged.

**Pattern 352** — WCAG 3.2.6 Consistent Help — help mechanism (chat, support link, FAQ) present in same DOM location across pages
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const PAGES_TO_CHECK = ['/', '/settings', '/dashboard', '/profile'];

test('help mechanism (support link, FAQ, live chat) is present in the same DOM position across pages (WCAG 3.2.6)', async ({ page }) => {
  type HelpEntry = { page: string; selector: string; text: string; position: number };
  const helpItems: HelpEntry[] = [];

  for (const route of PAGES_TO_CHECK) {
    await page.goto(route);
    await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

    const helpEl = page.locator('[aria-label*="help" i], [aria-label*="support" i], a[href*="faq" i], a[href*="support" i], button[data-help], [role="complementary"] a').first();
    const exists = await helpEl.count() > 0;

    if (exists) {
      const position = await helpEl.evaluate(el => {
        // Measure DOM order position among all interactive elements
        const all = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a, button, [role="button"]'));
        return all.indexOf(el);
      });
      const text = (await helpEl.textContent() ?? '').trim().slice(0, 40);
      const tag  = await helpEl.evaluate(n => n.tagName.toLowerCase());
      helpItems.push({ page: route, selector: `<${tag}>`, text, position });
    } else {
      helpItems.push({ page: route, selector: 'NOT FOUND', text: '', position: -1 });
    }
  }

  // Help must be present on all checked pages
  const missing = helpItems.filter(h => h.selector === 'NOT FOUND');
  expect(missing, `Help mechanism missing on: ${missing.map(m => m.page).join(', ')}`).toHaveLength(0);

  // DOM position should be consistent (within ±5 positions to allow minor layout variation)
  const positions = helpItems.map(h => h.position);
  const minPos = Math.min(...positions);
  const maxPos = Math.max(...positions);
  expect(maxPos - minPos, `Help mechanism DOM position varies too much across pages (${minPos}–${maxPos})`).toBeLessThanOrEqual(5);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 3.2.6 was introduced in WCAG 2.2 and requires a "help mechanism" to appear in the same relative order — not necessarily identical DOM index. The ±5 position tolerance used here is a pragmatic approximation; pages with significantly different header content counts will generate false positives. A more robust check would verify that the help element appears in the same semantic region (e.g., always in `<footer>` or always in `<header>`) rather than comparing absolute DOM index. Replace the position check with a region check: `await helpEl.evaluate(n => n.closest('header, footer, nav, [role="banner"]')?.tagName)` and assert consistency.

**Pattern 353** — WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured — sticky header/footer does not cover the focused element
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('sticky headers and footers do not obscure focused elements (WCAG 2.4.11)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

  // Find sticky/fixed elements
  const stickyElements = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const all = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('*'));
    return all
      .filter(el => {
        const pos = getComputedStyle(el).position;
        return pos === 'sticky' || pos === 'fixed';
      })
      .map(el => {
        const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        return { tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(), top: rect.top, bottom: rect.bottom, height: rect.height };
      });
  });

  if (stickyElements.length === 0) {
    test.skip(true, 'No sticky/fixed elements found — test not applicable');
    return;
  }

  const focusable = page.locator('a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled])');
  const count     = await focusable.count();
  const obscured: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 40); i++) {
    await focusable.nth(i).focus();
    const focusedRect = await focusable.nth(i).boundingBox();
    if (!focusedRect) continue;

    for (const sticky of stickyElements) {
      // Check if sticky header covers top of focused element
      const coveredByHeader = sticky.top <= focusedRect.y && sticky.bottom > focusedRect.y;
      // Check if sticky footer covers bottom of focused element
      const coveredByFooter = sticky.top < (focusedRect.y + focusedRect.height) && sticky.bottom >= (focusedRect.y + focusedRect.height);

      if (coveredByHeader || coveredByFooter) {
        const label = await focusable.nth(i).getAttribute('aria-label') ?? await focusable.nth(i).textContent() ?? '';
        obscured.push(`"${label.trim().slice(0, 30)}" obscured by sticky <${sticky.tag}>`);
      }
    }
  }

  expect(obscured, `Focused elements obscured by sticky elements:\n${obscured.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `getBoundingClientRect()` is computed at scroll position 0 — elements lower on the page that would be obscured when scrolled into view are not captured unless the test first scrolls to bring each element into the viewport. Add `await focusable.nth(i).scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()` before each `focus()` call to simulate real scroll behavior. Additionally, WCAG 2.4.11 (Minimum) requires "at least part of the component" to be visible — a full-coverage check would verify that at least 1px of the focused element is not covered, not that the element is entirely unobscured. WCAG 2.4.12 (Enhanced) requires the component to not be obscured at all; adjust pass/fail thresholds accordingly.

**Pattern 354** — WCAG 1.4.12 Text Spacing — CSS text-spacing override test using JavaScript property injection
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('content remains readable when WCAG 1.4.12 text spacing overrides are applied', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Inject WCAG 1.4.12 minimum text spacing overrides via a style element
  await page.addStyleTag({
    content: `
      * {
        line-height:   1.5  !important;
        letter-spacing: 0.12em !important;
        word-spacing:   0.16em !important;
      }
      p {
        margin-bottom: 2em !important;
      }
    `,
  });

  await page.waitForTimeout(200); // Allow CSS repaint

  // Check that no text is clipped or overflows its container
  const overflowIssues = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const textEls = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('p, li, td, th, label, button, a, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6'));
    return textEls
      .filter(el => {
        const rect   = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        return el.scrollHeight > el.clientHeight + 4 || el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth + 4;
      })
      .map(el => `<${el.tagName.toLowerCase()}> "${el.textContent?.trim().slice(0, 40)}" overflows: scrollH=${el.scrollHeight} clientH=${el.clientHeight}`);
  });

  expect(
    overflowIssues,
    `Text overflow detected with WCAG 1.4.12 spacing overrides:\n${overflowIssues.join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `!important` overrides via `page.addStyleTag()` affect all elements including third-party widgets and fixed-size UI components (like a pixel-art logo or a fixed-height progress bar) that are intentionally not text containers — they will generate false overflow positives. Filter the `textEls` query to exclude known fixed-size components using a data attribute: `[data-a11y-fixed-size]` or by tag exclusion (`canvas`, `svg`, `img`, `video`). Also: `scrollHeight > clientHeight` detects overflow in the layout box but not text clipping caused by `overflow: hidden` — the text is visually cut off but the scrollHeight check may not flag it if the container shrinks with the text.

**Pattern 355** — WCAG 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures — single-pointer alternative verification for multi-touch and drag operations
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('drag-and-drop and multi-touch features have accessible single-pointer keyboard alternatives (WCAG 2.5.1)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

  // 1. Find all draggable elements
  const draggables = page.locator('[draggable="true"], [data-draggable], [aria-grabbed]');
  const dragCount  = await draggables.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < dragCount; i++) {
    const el = draggables.nth(i);
    // Each draggable must have an aria-grabbed state or role that indicates drag support
    const grabbed  = await el.getAttribute('aria-grabbed');
    const roleAttr = await el.getAttribute('role');
    expect(
      grabbed !== null || roleAttr === 'listitem' || roleAttr === 'gridcell',
      `Draggable element at index ${i} missing aria-grabbed attribute for AT support`
    ).toBe(true);
  }

  // 2. Find carousel/slider elements and verify keyboard arrow key navigation
  const sliders = page.locator('[role="slider"], [role="listbox"][aria-orientation], .carousel, [data-carousel]');
  const sliderCount = await sliders.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < sliderCount; i++) {
    const slider = sliders.nth(i);
    await slider.focus();
    const tagBefore = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('aria-valuenow') ?? null);

    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    const tagAfter  = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('aria-valuenow') ?? null);

    // If aria-valuenow is used, it must change on ArrowRight (slider moved)
    if (tagBefore !== null && tagAfter !== null) {
      expect(tagAfter, `Slider at index ${i} did not respond to ArrowRight key`).not.toBe(tagBefore);
    }
  }

  // 3. Verify no touch-only event handlers without pointer/keyboard equivalents (axe heuristic)
  const touchOnlyElements = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('*'))
      .filter(el => {
        const listeners = (el as any)._listeners ?? {};
        const hasTouchStart = 'ontouchstart' in el;
        const hasPointer    = 'onpointerdown' in el || el.getAttribute('onpointerdown');
        const hasKeyboard   = el.getAttribute('onkeydown') || el.getAttribute('onkeypress');
        return hasTouchStart && !hasPointer && !hasKeyboard;
      })
      .map(el => `<${el.tagName.toLowerCase()}> class="${el.className}"`);
  });

  // Log touch-only elements as a warning (heuristic is imprecise for framework event systems)
  if (touchOnlyElements.length > 0) {
    console.warn('[WCAG 2.5.1] Potential touch-only elements (verify keyboard alternative exists):\n' + touchOnlyElements.join('\n'));
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: The `_listeners` property used in step 3 is not a standard DOM API — it is populated by some browser devtools patches but is `undefined` in headless Chromium. This means the touch-only heuristic in step 3 will silently produce empty results rather than accurate detections. Replace with a more reliable approach: instrument `addEventListener` via `page.evaluate` before page load to intercept registration calls and record event type / element pairs in a global map. This requires calling the instrumentation script before `page.goto()` using `page.addInitScript()`. The drag gesture verification in step 1 is limited to elements that explicitly declare `draggable="true"` or `aria-grabbed` — custom drag implementations using `pointerdown`/`pointermove` without these attributes will not be caught.
