## Cycle 63 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 415** — WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance — Assert Minimum Focus Indicator Dimensions and Contrast
```typescript
test('focused elements meet WCAG 2.4.13 focus appearance', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Collect all focusable elements via Tab traversal
  const focusIndicators: { selector: string; width: number; area: number }[] = [];
  let prevFocused = '';

  for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focused = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement;
      if (!el || el === document.body) return null;
      const style = window.getComputedStyle(el);
      const outlineWidth = parseFloat(style.outlineWidth) || 0;
      // WCAG 2.4.13 requires outline area >= perimeter × 2 (≥2px width suffices for simple rects)
      return {
        tag: el.tagName,
        id: el.id,
        outlineWidth,
        outlineColor: style.outlineColor,
        outlineStyle: style.outlineStyle,
      };
    });
    if (!focused || JSON.stringify(focused) === prevFocused) break;
    prevFocused = JSON.stringify(focused);
    // Minimum 2px outline width per WCAG 2.4.13
    expect(
      focused.outlineWidth,
      `${focused.tag}#${focused.id} outline-width ${focused.outlineWidth}px < 2px`
    ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
    expect(focused.outlineStyle).not.toBe('none');
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: This test checks `outline-width` against the 2px minimum from WCAG 2.4.13 but cannot validate the contrast ratio of the focus indicator against adjacent colours — contrast testing requires pixel-level colour sampling (e.g., via `page.screenshot()` and an image analysis library) which is expensive and fragile across themes; additionally, WCAG 2.4.13 allows focus indicators implemented via `box-shadow` or `border` changes instead of `outline`, none of which are captured by `style.outlineWidth` — a complete test must also check `box-shadow` spread and `border-width` changes on focus; this pattern is a fast first-pass gate for the most common violation (outline removal via `outline: none`).

**Pattern 416** — WCAG 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced) — Verify Focus Is Fully Visible With Sticky Headers
```typescript
test('keyboard focus is never fully or partially obscured by sticky header', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  const stickyHeaderHeight = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const header = document.querySelector('header[data-sticky], .sticky-header, [style*="position: sticky"]');
    return header ? header.getBoundingClientRect().height : 0;
  });

  // Tab through interactive elements and assert each focused element is
  // fully visible below the sticky header
  for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const overlap = await page.evaluate((headerH) => {
      const el = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;
      if (!el || el === document.body) return -1;
      const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      // Element top must be below sticky header bottom
      return rect.top - headerH;
    }, stickyHeaderHeight);

    if (overlap === -1) break; // No more focusable elements

    expect(
      overlap,
      `Focused element top (${overlap}px below header) is obscured by sticky header`
    ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: This pattern detects full obscuring (element top is above header bottom) satisfying WCAG 2.4.11, and partial obscuring (any portion hidden) satisfying the Enhanced 2.4.12 — but it only checks vertical (top) obscuring by a top-sticky header; fixed footers, side drawers, cookie banners, or chat widgets that obscure elements from the bottom or sides are not detected; the `data-sticky` selector heuristic may miss dynamically positioned headers that become sticky only after scroll — add `await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollBy(0, 200))` before the loop if the page has a scroll-activated sticky header.

**Pattern 417** — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size Minimum — Measure Interactive Element Bounding Boxes
```typescript
test('interactive elements meet 24x24px minimum target size (WCAG 2.5.8)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const tooSmall = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const interactive = Array.from(
      document.querySelectorAll('a, button, input, select, textarea, [role="button"], [role="link"]')
    );
    return interactive
      .map(el => {
        const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        return { tag: el.tagName, text: (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.slice(0, 40), w: r.width, h: r.height };
      })
      .filter(({ w, h }) => (w < 24 || h < 24) && w > 0 && h > 0); // exclude display:none
  });

  // Report all violations in the failure message for actionable output
  expect(
    tooSmall,
    `Elements below 24×24px target size:\n${JSON.stringify(tooSmall, null, 2)}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.5.8 allows an exception when the target is inline (e.g., a link within a sentence) or when adjacent spacing ensures the total 24px activation zone is met through offset — `getBoundingClientRect()` measures the visual bounding box only, not the activation zone including padding or click area extension via CSS `padding`; an icon button with `width: 16px; padding: 4px` has a 16px bounding box but a 24px click target via padding, causing false positives in this test; to reduce false positives, use `getComputedStyle` to sum `paddingTop + height + paddingBottom` rather than `getBoundingClientRect().height` for elements where the visible content is smaller than the touch target.

**Pattern 418** — WCAG 3.2.6 Consistent Help — Assert Help Link Appears in Same Relative Position Across Pages
```typescript
test('help mechanism appears in consistent position across key pages', async ({ page }) => {
  const pages = ['/home', '/settings', '/checkout', '/profile'];
  const helpPositions: { path: string; position: 'header' | 'footer' | 'main' | 'none' }[] = [];

  for (const path of pages) {
    await page.goto(path);
    const position = await page.evaluate(() => {
      // Find help link by common patterns: text "Help", aria-label "help", role="complementary"
      const helpEl = document.querySelector(
        '[aria-label*="help" i], [href*="help"], a:has-text("Help"), button:has-text("Help")'
      ) as HTMLElement | null;
      if (!helpEl) return 'none';
      // Determine landmark ancestor
      const inHeader = !!helpEl.closest('header, [role="banner"]');
      const inFooter = !!helpEl.closest('footer, [role="contentinfo"]');
      return inHeader ? 'header' : inFooter ? 'footer' : 'main';
    });
    helpPositions.push({ path, position });
  }

  const positions = helpPositions.map(p => p.position).filter(p => p !== 'none');
  const allSame = positions.every(p => p === positions[0]);

  expect(
    allSame,
    `Help mechanism is not in a consistent position:\n${JSON.stringify(helpPositions, null, 2)}`
  ).toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 3.2.6 (new in WCAG 2.2) requires help mechanisms to appear in the same relative order when present on multiple pages — "relative order" means order within a set of repeated components (header, footer), not pixel coordinates; this pattern classifies by landmark region which correctly captures relative consistency, but will pass even if the help link is in the header on three pages and absent on one page (`'none'` entries are excluded from the consistency check); if the help link is only conditionally shown on authenticated pages, adjust the test to only include pages where the user is expected to be authenticated.

**Pattern 419** — axe-core `AxeBuilder.exclude()` for Third-Party Widgets — Isolate First-Party Violations
```typescript
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('first-party content has no axe violations (third-party widgets excluded)', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Wait for all async content to settle
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const { violations } = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
    // Exclude known third-party embeds: chat widget, analytics badge, ad iframes
    .exclude('#intercom-container')
    .exclude('[id^="google_ads"]')
    .exclude('iframe[src*="doubleclick"]')
    .exclude('[class*="hubspot"]')
    .analyze();

  await testInfo.attach('axe-first-party-violations', {
    body: JSON.stringify(violations, null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  const summary = violations.map(v => `${v.id} (${v.impact}): ${v.nodes.length} node(s) — ${v.helpUrl}`);
  expect(violations, summary.join('\n')).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Excluding third-party widgets prevents failing the build on violations that the team cannot fix, but it also creates a maintenance burden — exclusion selectors must be audited regularly because third-party vendors change their DOM structure; if a third-party selector becomes stale (the element no longer exists), the exclusion silently has no effect (axe-core does not warn on empty `exclude()` targets); document each exclusion with a comment explaining why it is excluded, which team owns remediation, and a review date; team-authored widgets that are added to the exclusion list to defer work should have a corresponding Jira ticket reference in the comment.

**Pattern 420** — ARIA Live Region Announcement Timing — Assert AT Announcements With `aria-live` Polling
```typescript
test('form submission status message is announced via aria-live region', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/contact');

  // Locate the live region before interaction — it must exist in the DOM before content is injected
  const liveRegion = page.locator('[aria-live="polite"], [role="status"]').first();
  await expect(liveRegion).toBeAttached();

  // Capture initial text to detect change
  const initialText = await liveRegion.textContent();

  // Submit the form
  await page.fill('[name="email"]', 'test@example.com');
  await page.fill('[name="message"]', 'Hello from Playwright test');
  await page.click('button[type="submit"]');

  // Wait for the live region to be updated with non-empty, changed content
  await expect(liveRegion).not.toHaveText(initialText ?? '');
  await expect(liveRegion).not.toBeEmpty();

  // Verify the content is a meaningful status message
  const announcedText = await liveRegion.textContent();
  expect(announcedText?.length).toBeGreaterThan(5);
});
```
Tradeoff: Playwright assertions on `aria-live` region text content verify that the DOM is updated with a status message, but they do not verify that AT actually announced the message — AT announcement depends on the live region being in the DOM *before* content is injected (not dynamically created), on the `aria-live` value being `polite` or `assertive` (not `off`), and on AT-specific processing delays; if the live region is created dynamically at announcement time (a common mistake), AT ignores the announcement entirely even though the Playwright assertion passes; this pattern correctly validates the prerequisite (region exists before injection) by asserting `toBeAttached()` before the form submission.

**Pattern 421** — WCAG 2.2.6 Timeouts — Assert Timeout Warning Dialog Appears Before Session Expiry
```typescript
test('session timeout warning appears with at least 20 seconds remaining', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/app');

  // Simulate near-expiry by advancing application session timer
  // (requires a test-only endpoint or cookie override to set short session)
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    // Trigger the timeout warning callback that normally fires at T-20s
    const event = new CustomEvent('session-expiry-warning', { detail: { secondsRemaining: 20 } });
    window.dispatchEvent(event);
  });

  // WCAG 2.2.6 requires warning of data loss before expiry, with option to extend
  const dialog = page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /session|timeout|expire/i });
  await expect(dialog).toBeVisible({ timeout: 3000 });

  // Warning must include time remaining and an extend button
  await expect(dialog).toContainText(/\d+\s*(second|minute)/i);
  const extendButton = dialog.getByRole('button', { name: /extend|continue|stay/i });
  await expect(extendButton).toBeVisible();

  // Extend the session and verify dialog closes
  await extendButton.click();
  await expect(dialog).not.toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.2.6 requires that users are warned before a data-loss timeout occurs (session timeouts that discard form data) and are given the option to extend — this test uses a synthetic `CustomEvent` to trigger the warning, which only works if the application's timeout logic listens on `window`; production implementations using `setTimeout` callbacks or server-side session expiry notifications (via WebSocket or SSE) require a different trigger mechanism; the test also cannot verify the exact timing (that the warning fires 20+ seconds before expiry) without mocking `Date.now()` or using a test-mode session configuration — treat this as a functional existence test, not a timing precision test.

**Pattern 422** — ARIA Combobox Pattern — Validate ARIA State Machine Through Search Interaction
```typescript
test('combobox search widget follows ARIA combobox pattern states', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');

  const combobox = page.getByRole('combobox');
  await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-autocomplete');
  await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-controls');

  // Type to expand
  await combobox.fill('acc');
  await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

  // Verify the controlled listbox is visible
  const listboxId = await combobox.getAttribute('aria-controls');
  const listbox = page.locator(`#${listboxId}`);
  await expect(listbox).toBeVisible();
  await expect(listbox).toHaveAttribute('role', 'listbox');

  // Arrow down moves active descendant
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  const activeDescendant = await combobox.getAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
  expect(activeDescendant).toBeTruthy();

  // Escape collapses and clears active descendant
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
});
```
Tradeoff: This test validates the ARIA combobox state machine (expanded/collapsed transitions, activedescendant management) against the APG combobox pattern — however, ARIA combobox has two incompatible patterns in the wild: the ARIA 1.1 pattern (uses `aria-owns` on the combobox itself wrapping a listbox) and the ARIA 1.2 pattern (combobox is an `<input>`, listbox is a sibling controlled via `aria-controls`); this test assumes the ARIA 1.2 pattern; implementing the ARIA 1.1 pattern will cause `aria-controls` assertions to fail even if the widget is functionally accessible — check which pattern your library uses before applying this test verbatim.

**Pattern 423** — WCAG 1.3.6 Identify Purpose — Assert Landmark and Icon Purpose Annotations
```typescript
test('page regions and icons have programmatic purpose annotations (WCAG 1.3.6)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Verify all landmark regions have accessible names distinguishing them
  const landmarks = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const roles = ['navigation', 'main', 'complementary', 'form', 'search', 'region'];
    return roles.flatMap(role =>
      Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(`[role="${role}"], ${role === 'navigation' ? 'nav' : role === 'main' ? 'main' : ''}`))
        .filter(el => el.tagName !== 'UNDEFINED')
        .map(el => ({
          role,
          label: el.getAttribute('aria-label') || el.getAttribute('aria-labelledby') || '',
          tag: el.tagName,
        }))
    );
  });

  // Pages with multiple instances of the same landmark require unique labels
  const byRole = landmarks.reduce<Record<string, typeof landmarks>>((acc, l) => {
    (acc[l.role] = acc[l.role] || []).push(l);
    return acc;
  }, {});

  for (const [role, instances] of Object.entries(byRole)) {
    if (instances.length > 1) {
      instances.forEach(inst =>
        expect(inst.label, `Duplicate ${role} landmark has no distinguishing label`).not.toBe('')
      );
    }
  }

  // Verify decorative icons have aria-hidden and functional icons have accessible names
  const icons = await page.locator('svg, [class*="icon"], [class*="Icon"]').all();
  for (const icon of icons.slice(0, 50)) {
    const isHidden = await icon.getAttribute('aria-hidden');
    const label = await icon.getAttribute('aria-label');
    const labelledby = await icon.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    const hasAccessibleName = label || labelledby;
    // Icon must be either hidden (decorative) or have an accessible name (functional)
    expect(isHidden === 'true' || !!hasAccessibleName).toBe(true);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.3.6 (AAA) requires that the purpose of user interface components can be programmatically determined — this test approximates that criterion by checking landmark labels and icon accessibility, but 1.3.6 also requires purpose annotations for links, buttons, and form fields beyond what WCAG 2.1 AA already mandates; the icon loop is limited to 50 elements to avoid test timeouts on icon-heavy pages; `[class*="icon"]` is a heuristic selector that may miss icon systems using web fonts (e.g., Font Awesome `<i>` elements) or custom icon components with non-standard class names — supplement with a search for `<i>` elements with empty text content.

**Pattern 424** — WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions — Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` in CSS Transitions
```typescript
test('animations are suppressed when prefers-reduced-motion is set', async ({ browser }) => {
  // Launch a context with the reduced-motion media query emulated
  const context = await browser.newContext({
    reducedMotion: 'reduce',
  });
  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto('/');

  // Verify the CSS variable or class that drives animations is set correctly
  const motionPreference = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
  });
  expect(motionPreference).toBe(true);

  // Check that animated elements have duration of 0 or very short transitions
  const animatedElements = await page.locator('[class*="animate"], [class*="transition"], [class*="fade"]').all();
  for (const el of animatedElements.slice(0, 20)) {
    const duration = await el.evaluate(node => {
      const style = window.getComputedStyle(node);
      return parseFloat(style.animationDuration) + parseFloat(style.transitionDuration);
    });
    // With reduced motion, total animation + transition duration should be ≤ 0.01s
    expect(duration, `Element has ${duration}s duration under prefers-reduced-motion`).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0.01);
  }

  await context.close();
});
```
Tradeoff: Playwright's `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` context option correctly sets the `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` CSS media query at the browser level, ensuring the test faithfully emulates user preference — however, the duration threshold of 0.01s may produce false positives for intentional "instant" transitions (e.g., opacity snap from 0 to 1 with `transition-duration: 0.001s`) that are technically not zero but are perceptually instant; additionally, some libraries implement reduced motion by replacing `animation` with `transition` at a very short duration rather than removing motion entirely, which is WCAG-compliant but will still trigger this assertion; adjust the threshold to 0.05s (50ms) to accommodate deliberate instant-feedback transitions.

**Pattern 425** — ARIA Tabs Pattern — Assert Keyboard Navigation With Arrow Keys and Selection State
```typescript
test('tab widget follows ARIA tabs keyboard navigation pattern', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  const tablist = page.getByRole('tablist');
  await expect(tablist).toBeVisible();

  const tabs = tablist.getByRole('tab');
  const tabCount = await tabs.count();
  expect(tabCount).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);

  // Focus first tab
  await tabs.first().focus();
  await expect(tabs.first()).toBeFocused();

  // ArrowRight moves focus to next tab (roving tabindex pattern)
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
  await expect(tabs.nth(1)).toBeFocused();

  // Space or Enter selects the focused tab
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(tabs.nth(1)).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');
  await expect(tabs.first()).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'false');

  // Verify the controlled tabpanel is shown
  const panelId = await tabs.nth(1).getAttribute('aria-controls');
  if (panelId) {
    const panel = page.locator(`#${panelId}`);
    await expect(panel).toBeVisible();
    await expect(panel).toHaveAttribute('role', 'tabpanel');
  }

  // Home key moves focus to first tab
  await page.keyboard.press('Home');
  await expect(tabs.first()).toBeFocused();
});
```
Tradeoff: The APG Tabs pattern supports two keyboard interaction models: "automatic activation" (ArrowRight both moves focus and selects the tab) and "manual activation" (ArrowRight moves focus only; Enter/Space selects) — this test presses Enter after ArrowRight, which works for both models; however, if the implementation uses automatic activation, the `Enter` press after arrow navigation will do nothing (the tab was already selected on ArrowRight), making the assertion on the previous tab's `aria-selected="false"` unreliable; check which activation model the implementation uses and write separate test branches or use `page.waitForTimeout(100)` to detect auto-activation; also, `aria-controls` on tab elements is optional in ARIA 1.2 — some implementations use DOM proximity instead, causing `panelId` to be null.

**Pattern 426** — axe-core `resultTypes` API — Separate Violations from Incomplete (Needs Review) Items
```typescript
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('axe scan with incomplete items separated for manual triage', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
    .options({ resultTypes: ['violations', 'incomplete'] })
    .analyze();

  // Hard fail on violations — these are confirmed issues
  await testInfo.attach('axe-violations', {
    body: JSON.stringify(results.violations, null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });
  expect(results.violations, `${results.violations.length} violations found`).toHaveLength(0);

  // Soft warn on incomplete — these need manual review but should not block CI
  if (results.incomplete.length > 0) {
    const incompleteIds = results.incomplete.map(r => `${r.id} (${r.impact}): ${r.nodes.length} node(s)`);
    console.warn('axe incomplete items requiring manual review:\n' + incompleteIds.join('\n'));
    await testInfo.attach('axe-incomplete', {
      body: JSON.stringify(results.incomplete, null, 2),
      contentType: 'application/json',
    });
  }

  // Track incomplete count in test annotations for trending
  testInfo.annotations.push({ type: 'axe-incomplete-count', description: String(results.incomplete.length) });
});
```
Tradeoff: The `resultTypes` option limits axe-core result processing to only the specified categories (`violations` and `incomplete`), which measurably reduces analysis time on large pages by skipping `passes` and `inapplicable` computation — however, `incomplete` results (also called "needs review") represent items where axe-core detected a potential issue but could not algorithmically determine a pass/fail, such as colour contrast on elements with background images; these are soft-failing: the test logs them as warnings but does not fail the build; over time, incomplete items that are never triaged accumulate into a noise floor; set a policy to review incomplete items monthly and either file them as violations or add a justified `.disableRules()` exclusion with a comment.

**Pattern 427** — WCAG 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) — Assert Video Elements Have Associated Track Elements
```typescript
test('all prerecorded video elements have at least one captions track', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/media');

  const videoViolations = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const videos = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('video'));
    return videos
      .filter(video => {
        // Only check videos with audio (muted videos are exempt from 1.2.2)
        if (video.muted) return false;
        // Check for captions or subtitles track in <track> elements
        const tracks = Array.from(video.querySelectorAll('track'));
        const hasCaptions = tracks.some(t =>
          t.kind === 'captions' || t.kind === 'subtitles'
        );
        // Also check TextTrack API for programmatically added tracks
        const hasApiTrack = Array.from(video.textTracks).some(
          t => t.kind === 'captions' || t.kind === 'subtitles'
        );
        return !hasCaptions && !hasApiTrack;
      })
      .map(video => ({
        src: video.currentSrc || video.src || video.querySelector('source')?.src || 'unknown',
        id: video.id,
        trackCount: video.querySelectorAll('track').length,
      }));
  });

  expect(
    videoViolations,
    `Videos missing captions track:\n${JSON.stringify(videoViolations, null, 2)}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.2.2 requires captions for prerecorded audio content in synchronised media — this test checks for the presence of `<track kind="captions">` or `kind="subtitles"` elements and TextTrack API entries but cannot verify caption *quality* (accuracy, timing synchronisation, or speaker identification); it also cannot detect videos loaded via JavaScript after initial page load unless the test waits for all media to initialise; the `video.muted` check is an approximation of "no audio" — a video with `muted` attribute may still have an audio track that users can unmute, in which case captions remain a legal requirement; supplement with manual review of caption quality using the WebVTT file directly.

**Pattern 428** — WCAG 2.5.4 Motion Actuation — Assert Device Motion API Has a UI Alternative
```typescript
test('features using device motion have equivalent UI controls', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Check if the page registers devicemotion or deviceorientation listeners
  const usesMotion = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const listeners: string[] = [];
    const origAddEventListener = window.addEventListener.bind(window);
    window.addEventListener = function (type: string, ...args) {
      if (type === 'devicemotion' || type === 'deviceorientation') {
        listeners.push(type);
      }
      return origAddEventListener(type, ...(args as [EventListenerOrEventListenerObject]));
    };
    // Re-run page initialization scripts by dispatching DOMContentLoaded
    // This is a heuristic — check window.__motionFeatures if the app exposes it
    return (window as unknown as Record<string, unknown>).__motionFeatures ?? listeners;
  });

  if (!usesMotion || (Array.isArray(usesMotion) && (usesMotion as unknown[]).length === 0)) {
    // No motion features detected — test passes
    return;
  }

  // If motion features are used, assert a UI disable/alternative control exists
  const motionToggle = page.locator(
    '[aria-label*="motion" i], [aria-label*="shake" i], button:has-text("Disable motion")'
  );
  await expect(motionToggle).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.5.4 requires that functionality triggered by device motion (shaking, tilting) must also be operable via UI components unless the motion is essential — this test uses a `window.addEventListener` monkey-patch heuristic to detect motion listener registration, which only works if listeners are added synchronously during page load; listeners added in response to user interaction, lazy loading, or dynamic imports will not be captured; for React/Vue SPAs where event binding happens after hydration, use `page.waitForFunction(() => window.__motionListenerCount > 0)` if the app exposes a debug flag, or rely on code review to identify `devicemotion` usage rather than runtime detection.

**Pattern 429** — ARIA Switch Pattern — Validate Toggle State Announcement With `role="switch"`
```typescript
test('toggle switches use role="switch" with correct aria-checked state transitions', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings');

  const switches = page.getByRole('switch');
  const switchCount = await switches.count();
  expect(switchCount).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  for (let i = 0; i < switchCount; i++) {
    const sw = switches.nth(i);
    const initialChecked = await sw.getAttribute('aria-checked');
    expect(['true', 'false']).toContain(initialChecked);

    // Verify accessible name is present
    const name = await sw.getAttribute('aria-label')
      || await sw.getAttribute('aria-labelledby')
      || await page.evaluate(el => el.closest('label')?.textContent?.trim() || '', await sw.elementHandle());
    expect(name, `Switch at index ${i} has no accessible name`).toBeTruthy();

    // Click and verify state toggles
    await sw.click();
    const afterChecked = await sw.getAttribute('aria-checked');
    expect(afterChecked).toBe(initialChecked === 'true' ? 'false' : 'true');

    // Space key also toggles (keyboard operability)
    await sw.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
    const afterSpace = await sw.getAttribute('aria-checked');
    expect(afterSpace).toBe(afterChecked === 'true' ? 'false' : 'true');
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `role="switch"` is semantically distinct from `role="checkbox"` — a switch represents a binary on/off state for a setting that takes immediate effect (no form submission required), while a checkbox represents a selection that may be applied later; AT (including JAWS, NVDA, and VoiceOver) all announce `role="switch"` as "switch" followed by "on" or "off" (derived from `aria-checked: true/false`), which provides a better UX than "checkbox" for immediate-effect toggles; however, Safari iOS VoiceOver does not fully support `role="switch"` and falls back to announcing it as "checkbox" — for maximum AT compatibility on iOS, some teams use `<input type="checkbox">` with a custom visual design instead of `role="switch"`, accepting the semantic imprecision.

### Community Gotchas

**G291** — `aria-describedby` pointing to a hidden element (`display:none` or `visibility:hidden`) provides no description to AT — the referenced element must be visible or use `clip` / `sr-only` hiding, not `display:none`
Why this matters: `aria-describedby` resolves its accessible description by reading the `textContent` of the referenced element. The ARIA specification states that elements with `display:none` or `visibility:hidden` are excluded from the accessibility tree, and their text content is therefore not exposed to AT — `aria-describedby` pointing to such an element yields an empty description as if the attribute were absent. This is a widely misunderstood behaviour: developers frequently place helper text in a `<span aria-describedby="hint">` and then hide the hint `<span>` with `display:none` for non-screen-reader users, believing the hint will still be read aloud. All major screen readers (JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver) confirm the description is empty in this configuration. axe-core's `aria-valid-attr-value` rule does not flag `aria-describedby` pointing to hidden elements because the element *id* is valid — the content visibility issue is not detected by automated tools.
Fix: To hide helper text visually while keeping it accessible to AT, use the `.sr-only` (visually hidden) CSS pattern instead of `display:none`: `.sr-only { position:absolute; width:1px; height:1px; padding:0; margin:-1px; overflow:hidden; clip:rect(0,0,0,0); white-space:nowrap; border:0; }`. This removes the element from visual flow without removing it from the accessibility tree. Playwright verification: `const desc = await page.evaluate(id => document.getElementById(id)?.textContent?.trim(), hintId); expect(desc?.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` — if this returns empty, the referenced element is either absent or hidden with `display:none`.

**G292** — `role="tooltip"` must be triggered only by keyboard focus and pointer hover — attaching tooltip content to `click` events violates WCAG 1.4.13 (Content on Hover or Focus) because click-triggered tooltips cannot be dismissed without moving focus or losing the interaction
Why this matters: WCAG 1.4.13 requires that content appearing on hover or focus is dismissable (typically via Escape), hoverable (the pointer can move over the tooltip without it disappearing), and persistent (it remains until dismissed). A tooltip triggered by a `click` event satisfies none of these: it is not triggered by hover/focus, so 1.4.13 does not apply — but the pattern fails users who navigate with keyboard only, because clicking to reveal additional information is not a keyboard-available interaction unless the element is also focusable. Teams compound the error by giving the trigger `tabindex="0"` and `role="button"` but implementing only `onclick`, so keyboard users pressing Enter/Space do get the tooltip — but it still cannot be dismissed via Escape (another common omission). JAWS users in Forms Mode navigate by Tab key only, so non-focusable tooltip triggers are entirely inaccessible. axe-core does not test tooltip trigger mechanisms.
Fix: Implement tooltips with both `mouseover`/`mouseout` (pointer) and `focus`/`blur` (keyboard) event pairs on the trigger element. Add an `onkeydown` handler that closes the tooltip on Escape. The referenced tooltip element must have `role="tooltip"` and the trigger must reference it via `aria-describedby`. Reference the APG Tooltip pattern: `https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tooltip/`. Playwright test: focus the trigger via `Tab`, verify tooltip appears, press `Escape`, verify tooltip is hidden.

**G293** — `<select>` elements styled with custom CSS dropdowns often replace the native `<select>` with a `<div role="listbox">` — this requires the full ARIA listbox keyboard contract (Up/Down arrows, Home, End, type-ahead selection) or AT users lose access to the options
Why this matters: Native `<select>` elements have full AT support across all platforms with no JavaScript required. Custom dropdown implementations using `<div role="combobox">` or `<div role="listbox">` must reimplement the complete keyboard interaction contract specified in the ARIA APG Listbox and Combobox patterns. Common omissions include: (1) type-ahead character search (pressing "C" jumps to the first option starting with "C"), which is part of the ARIA listbox contract; (2) `aria-selected` state management on individual `<li role="option">` elements; (3) `aria-activedescendant` updates on the combobox input as options are highlighted; (4) correct focus management when the listbox closes (focus must return to the trigger). Teams using UI libraries (MUI Select, Headless UI Listbox, Radix Select) generally handle this correctly but often have version-specific bugs — always run the APG keyboard tests manually after a library upgrade. axe-core detects missing `aria-selected` on `role="option"` elements but not missing type-ahead or keyboard navigation.
Fix: Run the APG Combobox or Listbox keyboard interaction checklist manually against every custom select implementation. Add a Playwright keyboard test that cycles through options with ArrowDown, jumps to the last option with End, and verifies a type-ahead keystroke focuses the correct option: `await page.keyboard.press('c'); await expect(page.locator('[role="option"][aria-selected="true"]')).toContainText(/^c/i)`.

**G294** — Images of text inside `<canvas>` elements are completely invisible to AT — `<canvas>` has no native accessibility tree, and text rendered via `ctx.fillText()` is not exposed as text content to screen readers; every canvas that displays meaningful text requires a text alternative or must be replaced with HTML
Why this matters: `<canvas>` renders as a bitmap image from the accessibility tree perspective. The HTML5 specification defines a fallback content mechanism (content inside the `<canvas>` open/close tags) that AT should expose when canvas is not supported or when the canvas has no accessible alternative — but screen readers do not consistently expose canvas fallback content in modern browsers. Chrome and Firefox both expose the canvas fallback content subtree, but only if the canvas itself has a valid accessible name (via `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`). Safari VoiceOver ignores canvas fallback content entirely in most configurations. Charts, data visualisations, signature pads, interactive maps, and game UIs built entirely in canvas are among the most common WCAG 1.1.1 violations found in enterprise audits. axe-core rule `canvas-has-accessible-name` flags canvases with meaningful roles that lack accessible names, but it does not detect canvases that contain text rendered via `fillText()` without any accessible name.
Fix: For informational canvas content (charts, graphs): render an equivalent HTML table or `<figure>` with `<figcaption>` as a visually-hidden sibling; use `role="img"` on the canvas with `aria-label` describing the data in a sentence. For interactive canvas content: use an HTML overlay of focusable elements positioned over the canvas for keyboard and AT interaction — this is the pattern used by Google Maps (HTML button overlays on a canvas map). For text specifically: replace `ctx.fillText()` with positioned HTML `<span>` elements whenever possible. Test with `expect(await page.locator('canvas').getAttribute('aria-label')).toBeTruthy()`.

**G295** — `aria-live="assertive"` should only be used for urgent, time-sensitive announcements — using `assertive` for routine status updates (form saved, item added to cart) interrupts and overwrites whatever AT was currently reading, causing disorientation for screen reader users
Why this matters: `aria-live="assertive"` instructs AT to immediately interrupt its current speech and announce the new live region content, regardless of what the user was reading or typing. This is the correct behaviour for genuinely urgent messages: session expiry warnings, critical errors, authentication failures, or security alerts that require immediate attention. For all other asynchronous updates — success confirmations, progress indicators, item counts, background sync notifications — `aria-live="polite"` is the correct value: it queues the announcement until AT finishes the current utterance, preserving reading context. Teams commonly use `assertive` because they observe that `polite` announcements are sometimes delayed by a few seconds, and they want the update to be noticeable — but the correct fix for delayed `polite` announcements is to ensure the live region is already in the DOM before content is injected (not created dynamically), and to verify the region is not inside a dialog that consumes all focus. axe-core does not audit `aria-live` values at all — the choice between `polite` and `assertive` is never flagged.
Fix: Audit every `aria-live` attribute in the codebase and reclassify: use `assertive` only for errors/warnings that require immediate action; use `polite` (or equivalently `role="status"`) for all other asynchronous notifications. Create a shared `StatusAnnouncer` component that defaults to `polite` and requires an explicit `urgent` prop to use `assertive`, preventing accidental escalation. Playwright test: observe that after a form save, AT is not interrupted mid-sentence by asserting the live region has `aria-live="polite"` and not `"assertive"`: `await expect(page.locator('[role="status"]')).toHaveAttribute('aria-live', 'polite')`.

## Cycle 64 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 430** — ARIA Accordion — Validate Keyboard Expand/Collapse and `aria-expanded` State
```typescript
test('accordion headers expose aria-expanded and toggle on Enter/Space', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/faq');

  const headers = page.locator('[role="button"][aria-expanded], button[aria-controls]');
  const count = await headers.count();
  expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const header = headers.nth(i);
    const expanded = await header.getAttribute('aria-expanded');
    expect(['true', 'false']).toContain(expanded);

    const controlsId = await header.getAttribute('aria-controls');
    if (controlsId) {
      const panel = page.locator(`#${controlsId}`);
      if (expanded === 'false') {
        await header.focus();
        await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
        await expect(header).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
        await expect(panel).toBeVisible();
        await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
        await expect(header).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
      }
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: The APG Accordion pattern permits two keyboard models — pressing Enter/Space on a focused header always toggles that panel — but does not mandate Up/Down arrow navigation between headers (unlike the Tabs pattern); teams that implement arrow-key navigation between accordion headers create an unexpected keyboard interaction that contradicts the list-of-buttons model (each header is an independent button, not a roving-tabindex widget), causing keyboard users who learned the standard pattern to overshoot by pressing arrow keys expecting no movement.

**Pattern 431** — WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry — Verify Previously Entered Data Is Pre-Populated in Multi-Step Forms
```typescript
test('checkout step 3 pre-populates shipping address entered in step 1', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout/step-1');

  const firstName = 'Accessibility';
  const lastName = 'Tester';
  await page.getByLabel('First name').fill(firstName);
  await page.getByLabel('Last name').fill(lastName);
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('a11y@example.com');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next/i }).click();

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next/i }).click(); // step 2

  // Step 3 — billing address
  await expect(page.getByLabel('First name')).toHaveValue(firstName);
  await expect(page.getByLabel('Last name')).toHaveValue(lastName);

  // Verify the pre-populated values are not just placeholder text
  const firstNameInput = page.getByLabel('First name');
  const valueProp = await firstNameInput.inputValue();
  expect(valueProp).toBe(firstName);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 3.3.7 (Redundant Entry) only applies to information required in the same session — pre-population satisfies the criterion, but so does providing a "same as shipping" checkbox; the checkbox approach is lower risk because silently pre-populating billing fields can cause errors when shipping and billing addresses differ, and some payment processors flag pre-filled billing forms for fraud review; choose pre-population only when the UX research confirms users predominantly use the same address for both.

**Pattern 432** — WCAG 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose — Validate `autocomplete` Attribute Coverage on Personal Data Fields
```typescript
test('personal data form fields expose correct autocomplete tokens', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/profile/edit');

  const expectedTokens: Record<string, string> = {
    'Given name':        'given-name',
    'Family name':       'family-name',
    'Email':             'email',
    'Phone':             'tel',
    'Street address':    'street-address',
    'Postal code':       'postal-code',
    'Country':           'country-name',
    'Current password':  'current-password',
    'New password':      'new-password',
  };

  for (const [label, token] of Object.entries(expectedTokens)) {
    const field = page.getByLabel(new RegExp(label, 'i'));
    if (await field.count() > 0) {
      const autocomplete = await field.getAttribute('autocomplete');
      expect(autocomplete, `Field "${label}" is missing autocomplete="${token}"`).toBe(token);
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.3.5 applies to inputs that collect personal information about the user — it explicitly does not apply to fields collecting information about other people (e.g., a "send gift to" address form), so applying `autocomplete` tokens to third-party address fields causes browsers to incorrectly offer the user's own saved addresses for data intended for someone else; always check field intent before applying tokens.

**Pattern 433** — WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured — Detect Sticky Headers Covering Focused Elements
```typescript
test('sticky header does not obscure focused interactive elements when scrolled', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/long-form');
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 1280, height: 720 });

  const stickyHeader = page.locator('header[style*="sticky"], header[style*="fixed"], [data-sticky]');
  const headerBox = await stickyHeader.first().boundingBox();
  const stickyHeight = headerBox?.height ?? 0;

  const inputs = page.locator('input, select, textarea, a, button');
  const count = Math.min(await inputs.count(), 20);

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const el = inputs.nth(i);
    if (!await el.isVisible()) continue;
    await el.focus();
    const box = await el.boundingBox();
    if (!box) continue;
    // WCAG 2.4.11: focused element must not be fully covered by the sticky header
    const fullyObscured = box.y + box.height <= stickyHeight;
    expect(fullyObscured, `Element at index ${i} is fully obscured by sticky header`).toBe(false);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.4.11 (AA) requires only that the focused component is not *entirely* hidden, while 2.4.12 (AAA) requires it is not hidden at all — this test enforces 2.4.11 by checking full obscurement only; for 2.4.12 compliance, change the assertion to check that `box.y >= stickyHeight`, which is a stricter requirement that will fail even when a single pixel of the element is behind the header; most production sites cannot meet 2.4.12 with sticky headers taller than 60px without adding `scroll-padding-top` equal to the header height.

**Pattern 434** — ARIA Feed Pattern — Validate Infinite Scroll With `role="feed"`, `aria-busy`, and Article Labelling
```typescript
test('infinite scroll feed uses role="feed" with correct article labelling and aria-busy during load', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/news');

  const feed = page.locator('[role="feed"]');
  await expect(feed).toBeVisible();

  // Each child article must have an accessible name
  const articles = feed.locator('[role="article"], article');
  const initial = await articles.count();
  expect(initial).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(initial, 3); i++) {
    const article = articles.nth(i);
    const labelAttr = await article.getAttribute('aria-label')
      || await article.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    expect(labelAttr, `Article ${i} has no accessible name`).toBeTruthy();
  }

  // Scroll to trigger next page load
  await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight));
  // aria-busy should be true while loading
  await expect(feed).toHaveAttribute('aria-busy', 'true');
  await expect(feed).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-busy', 'true', { timeout: 5000 });
  const afterCount = await articles.count();
  expect(afterCount).toBeGreaterThan(initial);
});
```
Tradeoff: The APG Feed pattern requires each article to expose `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` on the `role="article"` element so AT can announce "article 7 of 23" — but `aria-setsize=-1` is valid when total count is unknown (typical for infinite scroll); setting `aria-setsize` to the count of *currently loaded* articles is incorrect because it changes on every load batch and misleads AT into thinking the feed has ended, causing JAWS to announce "article 7 of 7" before new articles load.

**Pattern 435** — WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard — Custom Drag-and-Drop Lists Must Have a Keyboard Reorder Alternative
```typescript
test('sortable list provides keyboard reorder mechanism for all items', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/tasks/reorder');

  const listItems = page.locator('[role="listitem"][draggable="true"], [role="option"]');
  const count = await listItems.count();
  expect(count).toBeGreaterThan(1);

  const first = listItems.nth(0);
  const firstLabel = await first.getAttribute('aria-label') || await first.textContent();

  // Verify a keyboard mechanism exists: either aria-grabbed or a reorder button
  const hasAriaGrabbed = await first.getAttribute('aria-grabbed') !== null;
  const hasReorderButton = await page.locator('button[aria-label*="Move up"], button[aria-label*="Move down"]').count() > 0;
  expect(hasAriaGrabbed || hasReorderButton,
    'Sortable list has no keyboard-accessible reorder mechanism'
  ).toBe(true);

  if (hasReorderButton) {
    const moveDownBtn = first.locator('button[aria-label*="Move down"]');
    const secondLabelBefore = await listItems.nth(1).textContent();
    await moveDownBtn.click();
    const firstLabelAfter = await listItems.nth(0).textContent();
    expect(firstLabelAfter?.trim()).toBe(secondLabelBefore?.trim());
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `aria-grabbed` was deprecated in ARIA 1.1 and removed from ARIA 1.2 — the ARIA 1.2 drag-and-drop model uses `aria-dropeffect` removal and keyboard reorder buttons instead; code that still sets `aria-grabbed` will not cause AT failures in JAWS 2025 or NVDA (both ignore the deprecated attribute gracefully), but it signals the implementation is using a pre-ARIA-1.2 pattern that will not work with any AT that has fully adopted the 1.2 specification.

**Pattern 436** — Playwright ARIA Snapshot — Component-Level Regression Testing With `toMatchAriaSnapshot`
```typescript
test('navigation menu aria snapshot matches baseline on re-render', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const nav = page.locator('nav[aria-label="Main"]');
  await expect(nav).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - navigation "Main":
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - link "Home"
        - listitem:
          - link "Products"
        - listitem:
          - link "About"
        - listitem:
          - link "Contact"
  `);

  // After a client-side route change, verify the nav structure is preserved
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Products' }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('**/products');
  await expect(nav).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - navigation "Main":
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - link "Home"
        - listitem:
          - link "Products" [current=page]
        - listitem:
          - link "About"
        - listitem:
          - link "Contact"
  `);
});
```
Tradeoff: `toMatchAriaSnapshot` (introduced in Playwright v1.49) uses partial matching by default — the snapshot passes as long as every node listed in the YAML is present, even if the actual tree has additional nodes; this is ideal for component regression tests that should not break when new items are added, but it means the test will not catch *removed* items unless the snapshot is exhaustive and uses the `/children` deep-equal modifier (e.g., `- list /children:`) to require exact child sets.

**Pattern 437** — WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast Ratio — Programmatic Luminance Calculation for Dynamic Theme Colors
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

function relativeLuminance(r: number, g: number, b: number): number {
  const [rs, gs, bs] = [r, g, b].map(c => {
    const s = c / 255;
    return s <= 0.03928 ? s / 12.92 : Math.pow((s + 0.055) / 1.055, 2.4);
  });
  return 0.2126 * rs + 0.7152 * gs + 0.0722 * bs;
}

function contrastRatio(l1: number, l2: number): number {
  const [lighter, darker] = l1 > l2 ? [l1, l2] : [l2, l1];
  return (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05);
}

test('primary button text meets WCAG 1.4.3 AA contrast ratio >= 4.5:1', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  const button = page.getByRole('button', { name: /primary|submit|save/i }).first();
  const styles = await button.evaluate(el => {
    const s = window.getComputedStyle(el);
    return { color: s.color, background: s.backgroundColor };
  });

  const parse = (css: string) =>
    css.match(/\d+/g)!.slice(0, 3).map(Number) as [number, number, number];

  const [fr, fg, fb] = parse(styles.color);
  const [br, bg, bb] = parse(styles.background);
  const ratio = contrastRatio(
    relativeLuminance(fr, fg, fb),
    relativeLuminance(br, bg, bb)
  );
  expect(ratio, `Contrast ratio ${ratio.toFixed(2)}:1 below AA minimum 4.5:1`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4.5);
});
```
Tradeoff: This programmatic contrast check reads `getComputedStyle` at runtime, which handles CSS custom properties and dark-mode overrides correctly — but it only tests the *computed* color at the time of the snapshot; if the page uses `background: transparent` or layered gradients, `getComputedStyle` returns the transparent value rather than the effective rendered color, yielding a false pass; for gradient or semi-transparent backgrounds, use a screenshot pixel-color extraction approach or Chromium DevTools Protocol `DOM.getComputedStyle` with a known opaque parent background.

**Pattern 438** — WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order — Tab Order Snapshot and Regression With Sequential Index Assertion
```typescript
test('tab order follows logical visual sequence through the main form', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/apply');
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab'); // move focus into page

  const tabOrder: string[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
    const focused = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement;
      if (!el || el === document.body) return null;
      return el.getAttribute('aria-label')
        || el.getAttribute('name')
        || (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.slice(0, 40).trim()
        || el.tagName.toLowerCase();
    });
    if (!focused) break;
    tabOrder.push(focused);
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  }

  // Verify critical ordering: name fields appear before date-of-birth, which appears before signature
  const nameIdx    = tabOrder.findIndex(l => /name/i.test(l));
  const dobIdx     = tabOrder.findIndex(l => /birth|dob/i.test(l));
  const signIdx    = tabOrder.findIndex(l => /sign/i.test(l));

  expect(nameIdx).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
  expect(dobIdx).toBeGreaterThan(nameIdx);
  if (signIdx >= 0) expect(signIdx).toBeGreaterThan(dobIdx);
});
```
Tradeoff: Tab-order snapshot tests catch regressions in focus sequence caused by CSS `order` property changes, DOM reordering, or `tabindex` mutations, but they are brittle to label text changes — any rewording of a field label breaks the `findIndex` match; prefer matching by `name` attribute or a stable `data-testid` fallback rather than visible text to reduce maintenance burden without sacrificing regression coverage.

**Pattern 439** — WCAG 3.3.1 + 3.3.3 Error Identification and Suggestion — Validate `aria-invalid` and `aria-errormessage` Linkage Post-Submit
```typescript
test('form shows linked error messages with aria-invalid and aria-errormessage after failed submit', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/register');

  // Submit without filling required fields
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit|register|sign up/i }).click();

  const invalidFields = page.locator('[aria-invalid="true"]');
  const invalidCount = await invalidFields.count();
  expect(invalidCount, 'No fields marked aria-invalid after failed submit').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  for (let i = 0; i < invalidCount; i++) {
    const field = invalidFields.nth(i);
    const errId = await field.getAttribute('aria-errormessage');
    expect(errId, `Field ${i} has aria-invalid but no aria-errormessage`).toBeTruthy();

    const errEl = page.locator(`#${errId}`);
    await expect(errEl).toBeVisible();
    const errText = await errEl.textContent();
    expect(errText?.trim().length, `Error message for field ${i} is empty`).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    // WCAG 3.3.3: error should suggest a valid value, not just say "invalid"
    expect(errText?.toLowerCase()).not.toMatch(/^(invalid|error|required)\.?$/);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `aria-errormessage` requires the referenced element to be currently visible — unlike `aria-describedby`, `aria-errormessage` is only valid when the field has `aria-invalid="true"` *and* the error element is visible in the accessibility tree; setting `aria-errormessage` on all fields at page load (even before submission) with initially hidden error elements causes axe-core's `aria-errormessage` rule to flag the elements as invalid even though this is a timing issue rather than a structural defect — only set `aria-errormessage` when the field is actually in an error state.

**Pattern 440** — WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name — Verify Accessible Name Contains the Visible Button Label
```typescript
test('icon buttons and labelled controls have accessible names containing their visible text', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Find all buttons that have visible text
  const buttons = page.getByRole('button');
  const count = await buttons.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const btn = buttons.nth(i);
    if (!await btn.isVisible()) continue;
    const visibleText = (await btn.textContent() ?? '').trim().toLowerCase();
    if (!visibleText || visibleText.length === 0) continue;

    const accessibleName = await btn.evaluate(el => {
      return (el as HTMLElement).getAttribute('aria-label')
        || (el as HTMLElement).getAttribute('aria-labelledby')
           ? document.getElementById(
               (el as HTMLElement).getAttribute('aria-labelledby')!
             )?.textContent?.trim().toLowerCase()
           : '';
    }) || visibleText;

    // WCAG 2.5.3: accessible name must *contain* the visible label string
    expect(
      accessibleName.toLowerCase().includes(visibleText),
      `Button visible text "${visibleText}" not contained in accessible name "${accessibleName}"`
    ).toBe(true);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.5.3 only applies when the control has *both* a visible text label and an overriding ARIA name — a button with no `aria-label` and only text content automatically has its text as the accessible name (via the accname algorithm), so 2.5.3 is satisfied implicitly; the common violation occurs when a developer adds `aria-label="Submit form"` to a button whose visible text is "Submit" — the accessible name "Submit form" contains "Submit", so this technically passes 2.5.3, but voice control users who say "Click Submit" may not activate it because voice recognition software matches on the full accessible name token, not a substring.

**Pattern 441** — WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text — Verify Layout Integrity at 200% Text-Only Zoom
```typescript
test('page remains operable and no content is clipped at 200% text zoom', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 1280, height: 720 });

  // Simulate 200% text-only zoom via CSS font-size override on root
  await page.addStyleTag({ content: 'html { font-size: 200% !important; }' });
  await page.waitForTimeout(300); // allow reflow

  // Check that primary CTA is still visible and not overflow-hidden
  const cta = page.getByRole('button', { name: /proceed|continue|checkout/i });
  await expect(cta).toBeVisible();
  const box = await cta.boundingBox();
  expect(box, 'CTA button has no bounding box at 200% text zoom').toBeTruthy();
  expect(box!.width).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(box!.height).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Verify no horizontal scrollbar (overflow clipping check)
  const hasHorizScroll = await page.evaluate(
    () => document.documentElement.scrollWidth > document.documentElement.clientWidth
  );
  expect(hasHorizScroll, 'Horizontal scrollbar appears at 200% text zoom').toBe(false);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.4.4 requires text can be resized up to 200% "without loss of content or functionality" but does not prohibit *all* horizontal scrolling — the criterion is violated only when content or controls become inaccessible; injecting `font-size: 200%` via `addStyleTag` tests reflow behaviour but does not faithfully replicate browser text-only zoom (Ctrl+scroll in Firefox), which also scales `em`-based paddings, margins, and SVG font sizes; for higher fidelity, combine `addStyleTag` with a screenshot diff or use a real browser zoom command via CDP.

**Pattern 442** — ARIA Tree View — Validate Keyboard Navigation Contract: Arrows, Enter, Space, Home, End
```typescript
test('tree view implements full APG keyboard navigation contract', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/file-explorer');

  const tree = page.locator('[role="tree"]');
  await expect(tree).toBeVisible();

  const firstItem = tree.locator('[role="treeitem"]').first();
  await firstItem.focus();

  // Right arrow expands a collapsed node
  const isExpanded = await firstItem.getAttribute('aria-expanded');
  if (isExpanded === 'false') {
    await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
    await expect(firstItem).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
  }

  // Down arrow moves to next visible item
  const beforeDown = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? document.activeElement?.textContent);
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  const afterDown = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? document.activeElement?.textContent);
  expect(afterDown).not.toBe(beforeDown);

  // End key moves focus to last visible item
  await page.keyboard.press('End');
  const lastFocused = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.textContent?.trim());
  const allItems = tree.locator('[role="treeitem"]');
  const lastItem = allItems.last();
  const lastText = await lastItem.textContent();
  expect(lastFocused?.trim()).toBe(lastText?.trim());
});
```
Tradeoff: The APG Tree pattern uses a single-tabstop roving-tabindex model — only one tree item receives `tabindex="0"` at a time; trees that give all items `tabindex="0"` allow Tab to move through every item, which conflicts with the ARIA pattern's expectation that Tab exits the tree entirely and arrow keys navigate within it; this dual-tabstop anti-pattern is frequently introduced when migrating from a list-based UI to a tree, because the original list items each had `tabindex="0"` and the migration only adds `role="treeitem"` without fixing the tabindex model.

**Pattern 443** — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size — Measure Touch Target Geometry Including CSS Spacing Offset
```typescript
test('all interactive controls meet 24x24px minimum target size including offset', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/mobile-nav');
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 390, height: 844 }); // iPhone 14 Pro

  const MIN_PX = 24;
  const interactives = page.locator('a, button, [role="button"], input[type="checkbox"], input[type="radio"]');
  const count = await interactives.count();
  const failures: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const el = interactives.nth(i);
    if (!await el.isVisible()) continue;
    const box = await el.boundingBox();
    if (!box) continue;

    // WCAG 2.5.8 offset exception: if spacing around a smaller element brings total to 24px each axis
    if (box.width < MIN_PX || box.height < MIN_PX) {
      const offset = await el.evaluate(e => {
        const s = window.getComputedStyle(e);
        return {
          top: parseFloat(s.marginTop),
          bottom: parseFloat(s.marginBottom),
          left: parseFloat(s.marginLeft),
          right: parseFloat(s.marginRight),
        };
      });
      const totalW = box.width  + offset.left + offset.right;
      const totalH = box.height + offset.top  + offset.bottom;
      if (totalW < MIN_PX || totalH < MIN_PX) {
        const label = await el.getAttribute('aria-label') || await el.textContent() || `index ${i}`;
        failures.push(`"${label?.trim()}" — ${box.width.toFixed(0)}x${box.height.toFixed(0)}px (with offset: ${totalW.toFixed(0)}x${totalH.toFixed(0)}px)`);
      }
    }
  }

  expect(failures, `Target size failures:\n${failures.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.5.8 includes an inline exception — targets within a sentence or whose size is otherwise constrained by the line-height of text are exempt; this test does not apply the inline exception because detecting whether an element is inline within flowing text requires inspecting computed `display`, `position`, and surrounding sibling elements, which is computationally expensive at scale; for inline links within paragraphs, suppress failures by excluding `a:not([role])` elements whose `display` resolves to `inline` and whose parent is a `<p>` or `<li>`.

**Pattern 444** — WCAG 2.4.6 Headings and Labels — Verify Heading Hierarchy Has No Skipped Levels
```typescript
test('page heading hierarchy has no skipped levels and every section has a heading', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/article');

  const headings = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const els = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6'));
    return els.map(el => ({
      level: parseInt(el.tagName[1]),
      text:  (el as HTMLElement).innerText.trim().slice(0, 60),
    }));
  });

  expect(headings.length, 'Page has no headings').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  const h1Count = headings.filter(h => h.level === 1).length;
  expect(h1Count, 'Page must have exactly one <h1>').toBe(1);

  for (let i = 1; i < headings.length; i++) {
    const prev = headings[i - 1].level;
    const curr = headings[i].level;
    expect(
      curr <= prev + 1,
      `Heading level skipped: h${prev} -> h${curr} ("${headings[i].text}")`
    ).toBe(true);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: This test enforces the "no skipped levels" rule derived from WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) advisory technique H69, which is a best practice but not a strict WCAG 2.2 AA failure on its own — screen reader users can still navigate headings with the H key even if a level is skipped; however, skipped levels consistently appear in WebAIM Million audit data as one of the top five most common structural issues, and they indicate copy-paste from another page or use of heading level for visual styling rather than document structure.

### Community Gotchas

**G296** — `role="presentation"` and `role="none"` on elements with focusable descendants do not remove the child from the accessibility tree — interactive children retain their roles and receive focus independently
Why this matters: The ARIA specification states that `role="none"` (and its synonym `role="presentation"`) removes the element's own semantics from the accessibility tree, but the effect does not cascade to focusable descendants. A `<table role="none">` loses its table semantics, but any `<a>` or `<button>` inside it remains focusable and retains its link/button role. Teams apply `role="none"` to layout tables believing it makes the entire subtree invisible to AT — this is correct for static content but false for any table that contains interactive elements such as action links in the last column. JAWS and NVDA both confirm that focusable children of `role="none"` elements are announced normally. axe-core's `presentational-children-not-owned` rule catches some cases of this misuse but does not cover every element type.
Fix: Do not apply `role="none"` to any container that holds focusable descendants — the spec-required behaviour is to ignore the `none`/`presentation` role and treat the element as if the role were not present when focusable children are detected. For layout tables with interactive content, use `<table>` with `aria-hidden="true"` on purely decorative cells, or restructure the layout using CSS Grid/Flexbox instead of tables, eliminating the need for `role="none"` entirely.

**G297** — `aria-hidden="true"` on a focusable element does not prevent keyboard focus from landing on it — the element is hidden from the AT tree but still receives `Tab` focus, causing a "ghost focus" where keyboard users Tab to an element that AT does not announce
Why this matters: `aria-hidden="true"` removes an element and all its descendants from the accessibility tree — AT will not read its content. However, `aria-hidden` has no effect on keyboard focus: if the element has `tabindex="0"` or is a natively focusable element (`<a href>`, `<button>`, `<input>`), it will still receive focus when the user tabs through the page. The result is a "ghost focus" state where the visible focus indicator moves to an element but the screen reader reads nothing (or reads the previously focused element's context), disorienting keyboard-and-AT users. This pattern commonly appears in decorative icon buttons where the developer adds `aria-hidden="true"` to the `<button>` instead of its inner `<svg>` or `<span>`, intending to hide the icon from AT but accidentally hiding the entire button.
Fix: Never apply `aria-hidden="true"` to a focusable element. To hide purely decorative icon content inside a button from AT, apply `aria-hidden="true"` to the inner `<svg>` or `<img>` only, and give the `<button>` an accessible name via `aria-label`. To completely remove a control from both AT and keyboard navigation, use `display:none` or `visibility:hidden` (which removes it from both), or use `disabled` for form controls. Playwright detection: `await expect(page.locator('[aria-hidden="true"]:is(a, button, input, select, textarea)')).toHaveCount(0)`.

**G298** — Placeholder text is not a substitute for a visible `<label>` — placeholder disappears on input and is never announced as a persistent label by any screen reader, violating WCAG 1.3.1 and WCAG 2.4.6
Why this matters: `placeholder` attribute text is defined by the HTML spec as "a hint" — short example text or format guidance shown before the user types. It is not a label, and all major AT treat it differently from a label: JAWS announces the placeholder as part of the field description (not the name) and stops announcing it once the user begins typing; NVDA may announce it as the accessible name if no `<label>` is present, but only before text is entered; VoiceOver on iOS announces placeholder as the accessible name when no label exists, but once the user types any character the accessible name becomes empty. Designs that rely solely on placeholder text fail WCAG 1.3.1 (form labels are structural information) and WCAG 2.4.6 (labels must be descriptive). axe-core's `label` rule flags inputs with no accessible name, but it accepts placeholder-derived accessible names as valid — this is a known axe-core limitation.
Fix: Every form input must have a persistent `<label>` element (or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` when a visible label cannot be shown). Placeholder text may additionally be used as format guidance (e.g., `placeholder="DD/MM/YYYY"`), but it must not be the sole label. If visual design constraints prevent a visible label, use the `.sr-only` CSS class to visually hide the `<label>` while keeping it in the accessibility tree.

**G299** — Modal dialogs that do not trap focus allow keyboard and AT users to navigate into the obscured background content, violating WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
Why this matters: When a modal dialog opens, WCAG requires that focus is moved into the dialog and that keyboard navigation cannot escape the dialog boundary until it is dismissed — this is the "focus trap" contract. Implementations that call `dialog.focus()` but do not intercept Tab/Shift-Tab keystrokes allow users to Tab through all focusable elements in the document, including controls hidden behind the modal overlay. Screen reader users navigating with arrow keys can also escape an improperly trapped dialog because AT virtual cursor mode (JAWS Browse Mode, NVDA Browse Mode) reads the DOM sequentially and ignores visual overlays. The `<dialog>` HTML element (with `showModal()`) provides native focus trapping in Chromium 107+, Firefox 98+, and Safari 15.4+ — but polyfilled dialogs using `<div role="dialog">` require a manual focus trap implementation. axe-core's `dialog-name` rule checks accessible names but does not test focus trapping.
Fix: Use the native `<dialog>` element with `dialog.showModal()` to get browser-native focus trapping, `Escape` key dismissal, and the top-layer rendering that prevents background interaction. For `<div role="dialog">` implementations, use a focus-trap library (e.g., `focus-trap` npm package) that intercepts Tab/Shift-Tab within the dialog boundary and moves focus to the first or last focusable descendant. Playwright test: open a dialog, then press Tab enough times to wrap around — assert focus never leaves the dialog by evaluating `document.activeElement?.closest('[role="dialog"]') !== null`.

**G300** — SVG elements used as images without `role="img"` and `<title>` are announced inconsistently across browsers and AT — Chrome exposes inline SVG content as a group of paths, Firefox reads SVG `<title>` automatically, Safari ignores both
Why this matters: Inline `<svg>` elements that serve as informational images (logos, charts, icons with meaning) have no single universally correct accessibility treatment because AT and browser accessibility tree implementations for SVG diverge significantly. Chrome (as of 2025) exposes inline SVG as a generic container and reads child `<text>` and `<title>` elements directly into the accessibility tree; Firefox reads the first `<title>` child as the accessible name of the SVG; Safari VoiceOver on macOS ignores the SVG entirely unless it has `role="img"` on the `<svg>` element. The safest cross-platform treatment is `<svg role="img" aria-label="...">` with a `<title>` as the first child — the `aria-label` overrides AT name computation uniformly while `<title>` provides a browser tooltip. Purely decorative SVGs must have `aria-hidden="true"` to prevent all three browsers from attempting to read their path data.
Fix: For informational SVGs: add `role="img"` to the `<svg>` element, add a `<title>` as the first child with a descriptive text, and also add `aria-labelledby` pointing to the `<title>` id — this three-part treatment has the broadest AT support. For decorative SVGs: add `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"` (the latter prevents IE11/Edge Legacy focus on SVG elements). Playwright test: `await expect(page.locator('svg:not([aria-hidden="true"])')).each(s => expect(s.getAttribute('aria-label') || s.locator('title').count()).toBeTruthy())`.
