## Cycle 66 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 445** — WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible — Detect Elements That Suppress the Default Focus Ring Without Providing a Custom Indicator
```typescript
test('no focusable element suppresses focus indicator without replacement', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Collect all focusable elements
  const focusableHandles = await page.locator(
    'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])'
  ).all();

  const failures: string[] = [];

  for (const el of focusableHandles) {
    await el.focus();

    const hasVisibleFocus = await el.evaluate((node: Element) => {
      const style = window.getComputedStyle(node);
      const outlineWidth = parseFloat(style.outlineWidth);
      const boxShadow   = style.boxShadow;
      // Accept: non-zero outline, or non-none box-shadow as custom focus style
      if (outlineWidth > 0) return true;
      if (boxShadow && boxShadow !== 'none') return true;
      return false;
    });

    if (!hasVisibleFocus) {
      const label = await el.getAttribute('aria-label') || await el.innerText() || await el.getAttribute('name');
      failures.push(`No focus indicator on: <${(await el.evaluate(n => n.tagName)).toLowerCase()}> "${label?.trim().slice(0, 40)}"`);
    }
  }

  expect(failures, `Focus indicator missing:\n${failures.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Computing `getComputedStyle` inside a `page.evaluate` loop serialises focus changes over CDP one element at a time — on pages with 200+ focusable elements this test can take 30–60 seconds; scope the test to a single critical route or use sampling on pages where complete coverage is not feasible. Additionally, custom `:focus-visible` polyfills applied via JavaScript class toggling will not be detected unless you also check for the presence of a CSS class with a non-zero outline or box-shadow in the computed style.

**Pattern 446** — WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow — Assert No Horizontal Scrollbar Appears at 320 CSS px Viewport Width
```typescript
test('content reflows at 320 CSS px width with no horizontal scroll', async ({ page }) => {
  // 320 CSS px at 1x device scale; WCAG 1.4.10 mandates no 2D scrolling at this width
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 320, height: 780 });
  await page.goto('/');

  const hasHorizontalScroll = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return document.documentElement.scrollWidth > document.documentElement.clientWidth;
  });

  expect(hasHorizontalScroll, 'Horizontal scroll bar present at 320px viewport').toBe(false);

  // Also check that no element overflows the viewport boundary
  const overflowingElements = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const vw = document.documentElement.clientWidth;
    return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('*'))
      .filter(el => {
        const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        return rect.right > vw + 1; // 1px tolerance for sub-pixel rounding
      })
      .map(el => `<${el.tagName.toLowerCase()}> class="${el.className}" right=${el.getBoundingClientRect().right.toFixed(0)}`);
  });

  expect(overflowingElements, `Overflowing elements at 320px:\n${overflowingElements.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: The WCAG 1.4.10 exception explicitly excludes content that "requires two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning" (e.g., complex data tables, maps, diagrams) — this test will produce false positives for those elements; suppress them by filtering elements matching `table`, `canvas`, `svg`, `[data-reflow-exempt]`, or a project-specific selector list before asserting overflow. Running at 320 device pixels (not CSS px) by omitting `deviceScaleFactor` is a common mistake — always set the viewport in CSS px with `deviceScaleFactor: 1` (the default).

**Pattern 447** — ARIA 1.2 Combobox — Verify `role="combobox"` Has Correct `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, and `aria-activedescendant` Lifecycle
```typescript
test('combobox ARIA 1.2 state lifecycle is correct during interaction', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');
  const input = page.locator('[role="combobox"]').first();

  // Initial state: collapsed
  await expect(input).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  await expect(input).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-activedescendant');

  // Open the listbox by typing
  await input.fill('ap');
  await expect(input).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

  // aria-controls must point to the visible listbox
  const controlsId = await input.getAttribute('aria-controls');
  expect(controlsId, 'aria-controls must be set when expanded').toBeTruthy();
  const listbox = page.locator(`#${controlsId}`);
  await expect(listbox).toHaveAttribute('role', 'listbox');
  await expect(listbox).toBeVisible();

  // Arrow down: first option becomes active descendant
  await input.press('ArrowDown');
  const activeDescendant = await input.getAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
  expect(activeDescendant, 'aria-activedescendant must be set after ArrowDown').toBeTruthy();
  const activeOption = page.locator(`#${activeDescendant}`);
  await expect(activeOption).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true');

  // Escape: collapse and clear active descendant
  await input.press('Escape');
  await expect(input).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
  const adAfterEscape = await input.getAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
  expect(adAfterEscape, 'aria-activedescendant must be absent or empty after Escape').toBeFalsy();
});
```
Tradeoff: ARIA 1.2 deprecated the pattern of placing `role="combobox"` on a wrapping `<div>` and changed the popup relationship from `aria-owns` on the container to `aria-controls` on the `<input>` itself — if you test a legacy ARIA 1.0 combobox (common in older MUI or Kendo implementations), this test will fail because the `<input>` element does not carry `role="combobox"` and the popup relationship is expressed differently; detect the pattern version before running assertions by checking whether the nearest ancestor `[role="combobox"]` is an `input` or a `div`.

**Pattern 448** — axe-core in Playwright — Configure `runOnly` to Target WCAG 2.2 AA Rules Exclusively and Surface Violations with Source Context
```typescript
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WCAG 2.2 AA axe-core full-page scan with source context', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Wait for dynamic content to settle before scanning
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
    .exclude('.third-party-widget, [data-axe-ignore]')
    .analyze();

  // Annotate each violation with the failing HTML for rapid triage
  const report = results.violations.map(v => ({
    id:          v.id,
    impact:      v.impact,
    description: v.description,
    help:        v.helpUrl,
    nodes:       v.nodes.map(n => n.html).slice(0, 3),
  }));

  expect(
    report,
    `axe violations found:\n${JSON.stringify(report, null, 2)}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});

test('axe-core component-scoped scan for modal dialog', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.locator('[data-testid="open-dialog"]').click();
  await page.waitForSelector('[role="dialog"]');

  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .include('[role="dialog"]')
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag22aa'])
    .analyze();

  expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: axe-core's `wcag22aa` tag covers only the subset of WCAG 2.2 AA criteria that axe-core has implemented automated rules for — as of axe-core 4.9, rules for WCAG 2.5.8 (Target Size Minimum) and WCAG 2.4.11 (Focus Not Obscured) are either incomplete or not yet implemented, meaning a zero-violation scan does not constitute a full WCAG 2.2 AA audit; always supplement axe-core with Playwright geometry checks (Patterns 443 and 433) and manual screen reader testing.

**Pattern 449** — WCAG 2.5.6 Concurrent Input Mechanisms — Assert Pointer-Only Event Handlers Are Paired with Keyboard Equivalents
```typescript
test('interactive elements do not rely solely on pointer-specific event handlers', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');

  // Detect elements with pointer-only inline handlers (no keyboard handler present)
  const pointerOnlyElements = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const candidates: string[] = [];
    document.querySelectorAll('[onmousedown]:not([onclick]):not([onkeydown]):not([onkeyup])').forEach(el => {
      candidates.push(`<${el.tagName.toLowerCase()}> onmousedown only: "${(el as HTMLElement).innerText?.trim().slice(0, 40)}"`);
    });
    document.querySelectorAll('[ontouchstart]:not([onclick]):not([onkeydown])').forEach(el => {
      candidates.push(`<${el.tagName.toLowerCase()}> ontouchstart only: "${(el as HTMLElement).innerText?.trim().slice(0, 40)}"`);
    });
    return candidates;
  });

  expect(
    pointerOnlyElements,
    `Elements with pointer-only event handlers (no keyboard equivalent):\n${pointerOnlyElements.join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);

  // Verify drag-and-drop sortable items expose a keyboard reorder mechanism
  const sortableItems = page.locator('[aria-grabbed], [draggable="true"]');
  const count = await sortableItems.count();
  if (count > 0) {
    for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 5); i++) {
      const item = sortableItems.nth(i);
      const describedBy = await item.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
      const hasKeyboardButton = await item.locator('..').locator('button[aria-label*="move"], button[aria-label*="reorder"]').count();
      expect(
        describedBy || hasKeyboardButton > 0,
        `Draggable item ${i} has no keyboard reorder mechanism`
      ).toBeTruthy();
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Inline event handler attributes (`onmousedown`, `ontouchstart`) are detectable via DOM attribute inspection, but event listeners added via `addEventListener` are invisible to DOM attribute queries — a page that uses `addEventListener` exclusively for pointer-only drag interactions will pass this attribute-based test while still violating WCAG 2.5.6; for complete coverage, pair this test with manual keyboard testing of all interactive widgets and a code review policy that bans `addEventListener('mousedown', ...)` without a paired `addEventListener('keydown', ...)` on the same element.

**Pattern 450** — WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast — Measure UI Component Boundary Color Against Adjacent Background
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

function relativeLuminance(r: number, g: number, b: number): number {
  const [rs, gs, bs] = [r, g, b].map(c => {
    const sRGB = c / 255;
    return sRGB <= 0.04045 ? sRGB / 12.92 : Math.pow((sRGB + 0.055) / 1.055, 2.4);
  });
  return 0.2126 * rs + 0.7151 * gs + 0.0722 * bs;
}

function contrastRatio(l1: number, l2: number): number {
  const lighter = Math.max(l1, l2);
  const darker  = Math.min(l1, l2);
  return (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05);
}

test('form input borders meet WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 non-text contrast requirement', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/contact');

  const inputs = page.locator('input[type="text"], input[type="email"], input[type="tel"], textarea, select');
  const count  = await inputs.count();
  const failures: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const el = inputs.nth(i);
    const colors = await el.evaluate((node: HTMLElement) => {
      const style  = window.getComputedStyle(node);
      const parent = window.getComputedStyle(node.parentElement!);
      return {
        borderColor: style.borderColor,
        bgColor:     parent.backgroundColor || 'rgb(255,255,255)',
        name:        node.getAttribute('name') || node.getAttribute('aria-label') || node.id,
      };
    });

    const parseRGB = (s: string) => s.match(/\d+/g)!.map(Number);
    const [br, bg, bb]    = parseRGB(colors.borderColor);
    const [bgr, bgg, bgb] = parseRGB(colors.bgColor);

    const ratio = contrastRatio(relativeLuminance(br, bg, bb), relativeLuminance(bgr, bgg, bgb));
    if (ratio < 3.0) {
      failures.push(`Input "${colors.name}" border contrast ${ratio.toFixed(2)}:1 < 3:1 required`);
    }
  }

  expect(failures, `Non-text contrast failures:\n${failures.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `getComputedStyle` returns `borderColor` as a single value only when all four border sides share the same color — inputs styled with per-side borders require individual side extraction; additionally, `borderColor` resolves to `rgba(0,0,0,0)` (transparent) for inputs that rely on `outline` as their visible boundary instead of `border`, causing a false pass; before asserting, verify that `borderStyle` is not `none` and `borderWidth` is non-zero, otherwise fall back to checking `outlineColor` instead.

**Pattern 451** — WCAG 3.3.4 Error Prevention — Assert Destructive Form Actions Have a Confirmation Step Before Submission
```typescript
test('destructive actions require explicit confirmation before data is deleted', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/account/settings');

  const destructiveButtons = page.locator(
    'button:has-text("Delete"), button:has-text("Remove"), button:has-text("Cancel subscription"), button[data-destructive]'
  );
  const count = await destructiveButtons.count();
  expect(count, 'No destructive action buttons found — verify selector').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const btn   = destructiveButtons.nth(i);
    const label = (await btn.innerText()).trim();

    await btn.click();

    // Must open a confirmation dialog OR show an undo mechanism
    const confirmDialog = page.locator('[role="dialog"], [role="alertdialog"]');
    const undoBanner    = page.locator('[aria-label*="undo"], [data-testid="undo-action"]');

    const dialogVisible = await confirmDialog.isVisible().catch(() => false);
    const undoVisible   = await undoBanner.isVisible().catch(() => false);

    expect(
      dialogVisible || undoVisible,
      `Destructive button "${label}" performed action without confirmation dialog or undo mechanism`
    ).toBe(true);

    // Dismiss without confirming to restore state for next iteration
    if (dialogVisible) {
      const cancelBtn = confirmDialog.locator('button:has-text("Cancel"), button:has-text("No")');
      if (await cancelBtn.isVisible()) await cancelBtn.click();
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 3.3.4 (AA) applies to legal, financial, and data-modifying submissions — it does not apply to every button; this test's selector matches any button with "Delete" or "Remove" text, which may include non-destructive UI actions (e.g., "Remove filter") that do not require confirmation under WCAG 3.3.4; scope the selector to `[data-destructive="true"]` and enforce that attribute via code review for actions that permanently delete user data, making the test authoritative rather than heuristic.

**Pattern 452** — WCAG 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced) — Assert Focused Elements Are Fully Visible in the Viewport
```typescript
test('WCAG 2.4.12 — focused elements are fully (not just partially) visible in viewport', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/long-page-with-sticky-header');

  const focusableSelector = 'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), [tabindex="0"]';
  const focusables = await page.locator(focusableSelector).all();
  const failures: string[] = [];

  // Get sticky header height once
  const stickyHeaderHeight = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const header = document.querySelector('header[style*="sticky"], header[style*="fixed"], [data-sticky]') as HTMLElement;
    return header ? header.getBoundingClientRect().height : 0;
  });

  for (const el of focusables.slice(0, 50)) { // sample first 50 for performance
    await el.focus();
    const visibility = await el.evaluate((node: Element, headerH: number) => {
      const rect = node.getBoundingClientRect();
      const vw   = window.innerWidth;
      const vh   = window.innerHeight;
      return {
        topClear:    rect.top    >= headerH,
        bottomClear: rect.bottom <= vh,
        leftClear:   rect.left   >= 0,
        rightClear:  rect.right  <= vw,
        label:       (node as HTMLElement).innerText?.trim().slice(0, 40) || node.getAttribute('aria-label') || node.tagName,
      };
    }, stickyHeaderHeight);

    if (!visibility.topClear || !visibility.bottomClear || !visibility.leftClear || !visibility.rightClear) {
      failures.push(
        `"${visibility.label}" obscured: top=${visibility.topClear} bottom=${visibility.bottomClear} left=${visibility.leftClear} right=${visibility.rightClear}`
      );
    }
  }

  expect(failures, `Fully-obscured focused elements (WCAG 2.4.12):\n${failures.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.4.11 (AA) requires that focused elements are not *entirely* obscured, while WCAG 2.4.12 (AAA) requires they are *not obscured at all* — this test enforces the stricter AAA criterion, which may produce failures on legitimate designs where a small portion of the focus indicator extends under a sticky footer; if targeting only AA conformance, change the assertion to check that the element's bounding rect does not have zero intersection with the unobscured viewport area, rather than requiring full containment.

**Pattern 453** — `aria-live` Region Timing — Assert Live Regions Are Present in the DOM Before Dynamic Content Is Injected Into Them
```typescript
test('aria-live regions are present in DOM before dynamic content is injected', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Live regions must exist on page load — not created dynamically at announcement time
  const liveRegions = page.locator('[aria-live], [role="status"], [role="alert"], [role="log"]');
  const regionCount = await liveRegions.count();
  expect(regionCount, 'No aria-live regions found on checkout page').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  for (let i = 0; i < regionCount; i++) {
    const region = liveRegions.nth(i);
    await expect(region).toBeAttached();

    const role = await region.getAttribute('role');
    const politeness = await region.getAttribute('aria-live') ||
      (role === 'alert' ? 'assertive' : 'polite');

    // Flag pages with more than 2 assertive regions — assertive should be used sparingly
    if (politeness === 'assertive') {
      const assertiveCount = await page.locator('[aria-live="assertive"], [role="alert"]').count();
      expect(
        assertiveCount,
        `Too many assertive live regions (${assertiveCount}) — use aria-live="polite" unless genuinely urgent`
      ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(2);
    }
  }

  // Trigger a live region update and verify content appears within 3s
  await page.locator('[data-testid="apply-coupon"]').click().catch(() => {});
  const statusRegion = page.locator('[role="status"]').first();
  if (await statusRegion.count() > 0) {
    await expect(statusRegion).not.toBeEmpty({ timeout: 3000 });
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: AT only registers `aria-live` regions that are already in the DOM when the page loads — content injected *into* a live region that is itself injected dynamically will not be announced by NVDA or JAWS because the AT has not yet registered the region as a live container; this test asserts the region is attached at page load, but cannot verify the AT registration timing; for single-page app route transitions, live regions attached after the initial paint may not be registered if added after AT finishes its initial DOM scan.

**Pattern 454** — WCAG 1.1.1 Complex Images — Assert `<figure>` Elements Containing Charts Have `aria-describedby` Pointing to a Long Description
```typescript
test('chart and graph figures have accessible long descriptions via aria-describedby', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/analytics');

  const figures = page.locator('figure:has(canvas), figure:has(svg[role="img"]), [data-chart-container]');
  const count   = await figures.count();

  if (count === 0) {
    console.log('No chart figures found — skipping');
    return;
  }

  const failures: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const fig = figures.nth(i);

    const describedBy = await fig.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
    const figcaption  = fig.locator('figcaption');

    if (describedBy) {
      const descEl   = page.locator(`#${describedBy}`);
      await expect(descEl, `aria-describedby target #${describedBy} not found`).toBeAttached();
      const descText = await descEl.innerText();
      expect(
        descText.length,
        `Long description for chart ${i} is too short (${descText.length} chars)`
      ).toBeGreaterThan(50);
    } else if (await figcaption.count() > 0) {
      const captionText = await figcaption.innerText();
      if (captionText.length < 50) {
        failures.push(`Chart figure ${i} has only a short figcaption ("${captionText.trim()}") — needs a long description`);
      }
    } else {
      failures.push(`Chart figure ${i} has neither aria-describedby nor figcaption`);
    }
  }

  expect(failures, `Complex image accessibility failures:\n${failures.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.1.1 requires that complex images have both a short text alternative (accessible name) and a long description conveying the same information — the 50-character threshold used in this test is a heuristic, not a WCAG requirement; a genuinely descriptive caption of 30 characters ("Bar chart: Q1 sales by region") may satisfy WCAG while a 200-character description that only restates the chart title does not; treat character-length checks as a signal for human review rather than a definitive pass/fail.

**Pattern 455** — WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks — Verify a Skip Navigation Link Is the First Focusable Element, Is Visible on Focus, and Navigates to Main Content
```typescript
test('skip navigation link is present, keyboard-reachable, and functional', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // The skip link must be the first focusable element on the page
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  const isFocused = await page.evaluate(() =>
    document.activeElement?.matches('a[href="#main"], a[href="#main-content"], a[href="#content"], a.skip-link, a[data-skip-link]')
  );
  expect(isFocused, 'Skip navigation link is not the first focusable element (Tab did not reach it first)').toBe(true);

  // Skip link must exist and be attached
  const skipLink = page.locator('a[href="#main"], a[href="#main-content"], a[href="#content"], a.skip-link').first();
  await expect(skipLink).toBeAttached();

  // Must be visible when focused (may be CSS-offscreen until focused)
  await skipLink.focus();
  const isVisible = await skipLink.isVisible();
  expect(isVisible, 'Skip link is not visible when focused — check CSS :focus styles').toBe(true);

  // Clicking skip link must move focus to main landmark
  await skipLink.click();
  const focusedAfterSkip = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const el = document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
    return { tag: el?.tagName.toLowerCase(), id: el?.id, role: el?.getAttribute('role') };
  });

  const landedOnMain =
    focusedAfterSkip.id   === 'main'         ||
    focusedAfterSkip.id   === 'main-content' ||
    focusedAfterSkip.id   === 'content'      ||
    focusedAfterSkip.role === 'main'         ||
    focusedAfterSkip.tag  === 'main';

  expect(landedOnMain, `Skip link click did not move focus to main content — landed on <${focusedAfterSkip.tag}#${focusedAfterSkip.id}>`).toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: Some implementations make the skip link visible only when it receives focus via CSS (`position: absolute; top: -9999px` moving to `top: 0` on `:focus`) — these are legitimate and satisfy WCAG 2.4.1, but Playwright's `isVisible()` returns `false` before `focus()` is called; this test calls `focus()` before `isVisible()` to handle the common CSS-offscreen pattern, but skip links hidden with `display:none` (which prevents `focus()` from working) will be silently skipped by the browser's Tab traversal — verify these styles if the `isFocused` assertion unexpectedly fails on a page that visually shows a skip link.

**Pattern 456** — WCAG 3.1.2 Language of Parts — Verify Foreign-Language Phrases Have a `lang` Attribute on Their Containing Element
```typescript
test('lang attributes on foreign-language phrases are valid BCP 47 subtags', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/glossary');

  const langgedElements = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[lang]'))
      .filter(el => el !== document.documentElement)
      .map(el => ({
        lang:  el.getAttribute('lang'),
        tag:   el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
        text:  (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.trim().slice(0, 60),
        // BCP 47 two-letter or three-letter language tag, optionally with region subtag
        valid: /^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Z]{2,3})?$/.test(el.getAttribute('lang') || ''),
      }));
  });

  // All present lang attributes must use valid BCP 47 syntax
  const invalidLangs = langgedElements.filter(el => !el.valid);
  expect(
    invalidLangs,
    `Invalid lang attribute values (must be BCP 47):\n${invalidLangs.map(e => `<${e.tag} lang="${e.lang}">`).join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);

  // All lang-tagged elements must contain non-empty text (no orphaned lang attributes)
  const emptyLangElements = langgedElements.filter(el => !el.text || el.text.length === 0);
  expect(
    emptyLangElements,
    'Elements with lang attribute must contain visible text'
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 3.1.2 (AA) requires `lang` attributes only when language changes would affect pronunciation by screen readers — common English proper nouns (e.g., "ARIA", "WCAG") do not require `lang` tags even in documents with a different base language; this test validates that existing `lang` attributes are well-formed BCP 47 codes but does not detect *missing* `lang` attributes on unlabelled foreign phrases, which requires natural language detection beyond static DOM analysis; a manual review step for pages with multilingual content is necessary to supplement automated testing.

**Pattern 457** — Accessible Date Picker — Assert ARIA Grid Navigation and `aria-selected` State Are Correct During Keyboard Interaction
```typescript
test('date picker calendar grid responds to arrow key navigation and updates aria-selected', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/booking');

  const dateInput = page.locator('[data-testid="date-picker-input"], input[aria-haspopup]').first();
  await dateInput.click();

  // Calendar popup must appear with a grid structure
  const calendar = page.locator('[role="dialog"] [role="grid"], [data-testid="calendar-grid"]').first();
  await expect(calendar).toBeVisible({ timeout: 3000 });

  // Initial state: exactly one date cell has aria-selected="true"
  const selectedCell = calendar.locator('[aria-selected="true"]');
  await expect(selectedCell).toHaveCount(1);

  // Arrow key navigation: ArrowRight should advance selection by one day
  const initialDate = await selectedCell.getAttribute('data-date') || await selectedCell.innerText();
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');

  const newSelected = calendar.locator('[aria-selected="true"]');
  await expect(newSelected).toHaveCount(1);

  const updatedDate = await newSelected.getAttribute('data-date') || await newSelected.innerText();
  expect(updatedDate, 'ArrowRight did not change the selected date').not.toBe(initialDate);

  // Each gridcell must have an aria-label with the full date string (not just the day number)
  const firstCell      = calendar.locator('[role="gridcell"]').first();
  const firstCellLabel = await firstCell.getAttribute('aria-label');
  expect(firstCellLabel, 'Date grid cells must have aria-label with full date (e.g., "January 15, 2026")').toBeTruthy();
  expect(firstCellLabel!.length, 'aria-label on date cell is too short to be a full date').toBeGreaterThan(4);
});
```
Tradeoff: The ARIA APG Date Picker pattern specifies `role="grid"` with `role="gridcell"` for individual dates and arrow key navigation — third-party date picker libraries (Pikaday, Flatpickr, React Day Picker) implement this inconsistently; Flatpickr before version 4.6.10 uses a `<div>` grid without ARIA roles, which will cause this test to fail with a legitimate accessibility bug rather than a test setup error; confirm which library is in use before running and add the library-specific selector as a fallthrough if the primary selector finds no matching element.

**Pattern 458** — WCAG 2.3.1 Three Flashes — Detect CSS Animations That Loop at a Rate Exceeding Three Times per Second
```typescript
test('no animated elements flash at a rate exceeding 3 Hz via CSS animation duration', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // CSS animation or transition with period < 333ms (= frequency > 3 Hz) and looping
  const flashingElements = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const THRESHOLD_MS = 333; // 1000ms / 3Hz = 333ms
    return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('*'))
      .filter(el => {
        const style           = window.getComputedStyle(el);
        const animDurationMs  = parseFloat(style.animationDuration) * 1000;
        const transDurationMs = parseFloat(style.transitionDuration) * 1000;
        const iterations      = style.animationIterationCount;

        // Only flag looping animations (infinite or repeating > 3 times)
        const isLooping  = iterations === 'infinite' || parseFloat(iterations) > 3;
        const isFlashing = (animDurationMs > 0 && animDurationMs < THRESHOLD_MS && isLooping) ||
                           (transDurationMs > 0 && transDurationMs < THRESHOLD_MS);

        return isFlashing;
      })
      .map(el => {
        const s = window.getComputedStyle(el);
        return `<${el.tagName.toLowerCase()}> class="${el.className.toString().trim().slice(0, 40)}" animDur=${s.animationDuration} transDur=${s.transitionDuration}`;
      });
  });

  expect(
    flashingElements,
    `Potentially flashing elements (animation/transition < 333ms looping):\n${flashingElements.join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.3.1 defines a flash as a "pair of opposing changes in relative luminance" — a fast CSS animation that cycles through hues without a luminance change (e.g., a rainbow color rotation) may trigger this test but not constitute a flash under WCAG's photosensitive seizure definition; conversely, a JavaScript-driven animation that swaps between near-white and near-black at 4 Hz will not be caught by CSS property inspection at all; treat this test as a proxy signal requiring follow-up with the Trace Center's PEAT tool for pages with known animation-heavy content.

**Pattern 459** — Accessible Notification Toast — Assert Toasts Use an `aria-live` Role, Are Keyboard-Dismissible, and Persist Long Enough to Be Read
```typescript
test('notification toasts are announced by AT, keyboard-dismissible, and persist adequately', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // Trigger a toast notification via a form save action
  await page.locator('[data-testid="save-settings"]').click().catch(async () => {
    await page.locator('form button[type="submit"]').first().click();
  });

  // Toast must appear with appropriate ARIA live region role
  const toast = page.locator('[role="status"], [role="alert"], [aria-live="polite"], [aria-live="assertive"]').last();
  await expect(toast).toBeVisible({ timeout: 3000 });

  const role = await toast.getAttribute('role');
  const live = await toast.getAttribute('aria-live');
  const validRole = role === 'status' || role === 'alert' || live === 'polite' || live === 'assertive';
  expect(validRole, 'Toast has invalid or missing ARIA live announcement role/attribute').toBe(true);

  // Keyboard dismissibility: visible close button OR Escape key must dismiss the toast
  const closeBtn = toast.locator('button[aria-label*="close"], button[aria-label*="dismiss"], button:has-text("×")');
  const hasCloseBtn = await closeBtn.count() > 0;

  if (hasCloseBtn) {
    await expect(closeBtn.first()).toBeVisible();
  } else {
    // Fall back to Escape key as dismiss mechanism
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(toast).not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 2000 });
  }

  // Verify toast persists for at least 1 second (not immediately auto-dismissed)
  // WCAG 2.2.1 requires >= 20s for timed content, or a pause/extend/disable mechanism
  if (hasCloseBtn) {
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000);
    const stillVisible = await toast.isVisible().catch(() => false);
    expect(stillVisible, 'Toast auto-dismissed in under 1 second — not enough time for AT users to read it').toBe(true);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable) requires that timed content persisting for less than 20 seconds either allows the user to turn off, adjust, or extend the time limit — many toast library defaults (3–5 seconds) violate this criterion; this test checks persistence at the 1-second mark rather than 20 seconds to remain fast, making it a minimum-bar check rather than a full WCAG 2.2.1 verification; supplement with a manual check that the toast duration is configurable by the user and enforce a minimum of 10 seconds in the toast library default configuration.

### Community Gotchas

**G301** — `aria-label` on a `<div role="group">` is silently ignored by JAWS when the group contains no focusable descendant — the group label is announced by NVDA but invisible to JAWS users navigating static grouped content
Why this matters: `role="group"` is intended to create a nameable container for a set of related controls, with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` providing the group's accessible name. NVDA (all recent versions) reads the group label when the user navigates into the group. However, JAWS (versions 2021–2024) silently suppresses the `aria-label` on `role="group"` elements when the group contains no interactive descendant — the label is never announced, and there is no error or warning. Groups used for purely structural organisation (e.g., wrapping a set of read-only `<p>` elements) need `role="region"` with `aria-label` instead, as `role="region"` has broader AT support for named landmarks over static content.
Fix: Use `role="group"` only for groups that contain at least one interactive control (`<input>`, `<button>`, `<select>`, or an element with `tabindex`). For grouping read-only content that needs a label, use `<section aria-label="...">` or `role="region"` with `aria-labelledby` pointing to a visible heading. Playwright smoke test: `await page.locator('[role="group"]').each(async g => expect(await g.locator('button, input, select, [tabindex]').count()).toBeGreaterThan(0))`.

**G302** — Positive `tabindex` values (tabindex="1", "2", etc.) create a priority tab order that runs before natural DOM order, causing keyboard users to jump to visually unrelated page sections on their first Tab keystrokes
Why this matters: HTML's `tabindex` attribute accepts `-1` (remove from tab order), `0` (add to natural DOM tab order), and any positive integer (insert into a priority sequence that precedes all `tabindex="0"` elements). Any element with `tabindex="1"` receives focus before any `tabindex="0"` element in the DOM, regardless of visual position. A `<footer>` link with `tabindex="1"` will receive the very first Tab keystroke on the page. Developers add positive `tabindex` values as a quick fix when component refactors move elements out of their visual sequence — the result is a fragmented focus order that is extremely difficult for keyboard-only users to predict or memorise, violating WCAG 2.4.3. axe-core's `tabindex` rule flags `tabindex` values greater than 0.
Fix: Remove all `tabindex` values greater than 0 from the codebase. Restore the intended focus order by reordering DOM elements to match the visual sequence, using CSS for visual reordering (Flexbox `order`, CSS Grid placement) while keeping the DOM in logical order. Use `tabindex="0"` to add non-interactive elements to the tab order only when they genuinely need to be reachable by keyboard navigation.

**G303** — `autocomplete="off"` on password and username fields breaks WCAG 1.3.5 (Identify Input Purpose) and is partially ignored by modern browsers, which preserve password manager autofill as an accessibility accommodation
Why this matters: `autocomplete="off"` was historically used to prevent browsers and password managers from pre-filling login forms. Modern browsers (Chrome 34+, Firefox 38+, Safari since iOS 8) explicitly ignore `autocomplete="off"` on `type="password"` fields to preserve password manager functionality, which benefits users with memory or motor impairments. Applying `autocomplete="off"` to `type="username"` or `type="email"` breaks the `autocomplete` token mapping required by WCAG 1.3.5 (AA), which mandates that login inputs carry the correct token (`username`, `email`, `current-password`) so AT and browser autofill can pre-populate them without the user needing to type. Security teams that add `autocomplete="off"` to suppress browser-stored credentials inadvertently break assistive technology for users who cannot type.
Fix: Replace `autocomplete="off"` on login fields with the correct WCAG 1.3.5 tokens: `autocomplete="username"` for the username field, `autocomplete="current-password"` for the login password field, and `autocomplete="new-password"` for registration or change-password flows. If the security requirement is to prevent credential caching on shared-computer kiosks, implement session-level credential clearing server-side rather than relying on `autocomplete="off"`.

**G304** — `aria-expanded` must be placed on the triggering control element, not on the expandable panel — placing it on the panel causes AT to report the panel's open/closed state while the button is announced as a plain unlabelled control with no state
Why this matters: The ARIA specification places `aria-expanded` on the element that controls the expansion — the trigger (`<button>`, link, or custom role) — not on the content region that expands and collapses. `aria-expanded="true"` on the triggering `<button>` causes AT to announce "button, expanded" when the panel is open. If `aria-expanded` is placed on the `<div>` panel instead, the button is announced as a plain button with no expansion state, and the panel (typically not focusable) carries a state attribute that keyboard users never reach. This is one of the most common ARIA misplacements found in component library audits, often introduced when developers conflate "the expanded element" with "the element that expands".
Fix: Always place `aria-expanded` on the interactive trigger element (`<button>`, an element with `role="button"`, or `role="tab"`), not on the content panel. The panel should be associated to the trigger via `aria-controls="[panel-id]"`. Correct example: `<button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="panel1">Show details</button><div id="panel1" hidden>...</div>`. Update `aria-expanded` in the same event handler that toggles the panel's `hidden` attribute or CSS `display` state.

**G305** — Form validation error messages and required-field indicators rendered via CSS `::before`/`::after` pseudo-elements are completely invisible to AT — pseudo-element `content` is not in the accessibility tree and is never announced by any screen reader
Why this matters: CSS `::before` and `::after` pseudo-elements inject text content into the visual page via the `content` property. This technique is sometimes used to display validation error messages (`content: "This field is required"`) or required-field asterisks (`content: "*"`) adjacent to form labels. While this content is visually rendered, it is not part of the DOM and is not exposed in the accessibility tree in any browser — JAWS, NVDA, and VoiceOver do not read pseudo-element `content` text. A form that relies on `::before`/`::after` for error messaging will show errors to sighted users while providing zero feedback to screen reader users, violating WCAG 3.3.1 (Error Identification) and 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships). This pattern is common in older CSS-heavy frameworks and themes.
Fix: Move all error messages and required-field indicators from CSS pseudo-elements into actual DOM text nodes. Use `<span class="error-message" role="alert">This field is required</span>` inserted adjacent to the input when validation fails, and reference it from the input via `aria-errormessage="[span-id]"`. For required-field asterisks, use `<abbr title="required" aria-hidden="true">*</abbr>` in the visible label and add `aria-required="true"` on the input. Playwright detection: `await expect(page.locator('input + .error-message, input ~ [role="alert"]')).not.toHaveCount(0)` after triggering form validation.
