## Cycle 65 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 445** — WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance — Verify Focus Indicator Area and Contrast Meet AAA Threshold
```typescript
test('focus indicators meet WCAG 2.4.13 AAA area and contrast requirements', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  const focusables = page.locator(
    'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), [tabindex="0"]'
  );
  const count = await focusables.count();
  const failures: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 40); i++) {
    const el = focusables.nth(i);
    await el.focus();
    const styles = await el.evaluate((node: Element) => {
      const cs = getComputedStyle(node);
      return {
        outlineWidth:  parseFloat(cs.outlineWidth)  || 0,
        outlineOffset: parseFloat(cs.outlineOffset) || 0,
        outlineColor:  cs.outlineColor,
        outlineStyle:  cs.outlineStyle,
        boxShadow:     cs.boxShadow,
        tag:           node.tagName,
        text:          (node as HTMLElement).innerText?.slice(0, 40) || node.getAttribute('aria-label') || '',
      };
    });
    const hasRealOutline = styles.outlineStyle !== 'none' && styles.outlineWidth >= 2;
    const hasBoxShadowFocus = styles.boxShadow !== 'none' && styles.boxShadow !== '';
    if (!hasRealOutline && !hasBoxShadowFocus) {
      failures.push(`${styles.tag} "${styles.text}" — no visible focus indicator (outline or box-shadow)`);
    }
  }

  expect(failures, `Focus appearance failures:\n${failures.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.4.13 is AAA — it requires the focus indicator area to be at least as large as a 2px perimeter of the unfocused component AND maintain a 3:1 contrast ratio against adjacent colors; this test approximates the area requirement by checking `outlineWidth >= 2` and falls back to any non-`none` `box-shadow`, but it cannot compute the actual closed perimeter area or read contrast ratio without extracting computed colors and running the relative-luminance formula at runtime, meaning box-shadow implementations that use a 1px spread with a bright color will pass this test but would fail the full 2.4.13 calculation — supplement with a manual Colour Contrast Analyser pass on the focused state of each interactive component.

**Pattern 446** — WCAG 2.5.7 Dragging Movements — Assert Every Drag Interaction Has a Single-Pointer Alternative
```typescript
test('draggable components expose single-pointer path alternative', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Collect all elements with drag role or HTML draggable attribute
  const draggables = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const els = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[draggable="true"], [role="slider"], [aria-grabbed]'));
    return els.map(el => ({
      tag:   el.tagName,
      role:  el.getAttribute('role') || '',
      label: (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.slice(0, 50) || el.getAttribute('aria-label') || '',
      id:    el.id || '',
    }));
  });

  for (const draggable of draggables) {
    if (draggable.role === 'slider') {
      // Sliders must support arrow key adjustment — that IS the single-pointer alternative
      const slider = draggable.id
        ? page.locator(`#${draggable.id}`)
        : page.locator(`[role="slider"]`).first();
      await slider.focus();
      const before = await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow');
      await slider.press('ArrowRight');
      const after = await slider.getAttribute('aria-valuenow');
      expect(after, `Slider "${draggable.label}" did not change value on ArrowRight`).not.toBe(before);
    } else {
      // Non-slider draggables must expose a button/menu alternative in their DOM region
      const parent = draggable.id
        ? page.locator(`#${draggable.id}`).locator('..')
        : page.locator(`[draggable="true"]`).first().locator('..');
      const altCount = await parent.locator('button, [role="button"], [role="menuitem"]').count();
      expect(
        altCount,
        `Draggable "${draggable.label}" has no single-pointer alternative (button/menu) in its parent region`
      ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.5.7 (AA, new in 2.2) requires that any functionality using dragging can also be operated with a single pointer without dragging, such as a click-to-place or button-activated reorder menu; this test checks that `[role="slider"]` responds to `ArrowRight` and that non-slider draggables have at least one button in their immediate parent, but it cannot verify that the button-based alternative is functionally equivalent to the drag operation — a "move up/down" button set next to a draggable list item satisfies the criterion even if it moves only one position per click, so supplement with a manual check of equivalence for complex sorting surfaces.

**Pattern 447** — WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication — Verify Login Does Not Require Cognitive Function Test
```typescript
test('login page satisfies WCAG 3.3.8 — no unsupported cognitive function test', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');

  // Check that no CAPTCHA image-recognition challenge is required with no alternative
  const captchaFrames = page.frameLocator('iframe[src*="recaptcha"], iframe[src*="hcaptcha"]');
  const captchaVisible = await page.locator(
    '[class*="captcha"], [id*="captcha"], [data-sitekey]'
  ).count();

  if (captchaVisible > 0) {
    // An audio or object-recognition-free alternative must exist
    const audioAlt = await page.locator(
      'button[aria-label*="audio"], a[aria-label*="audio"], [class*="audio-challenge"]'
    ).count();
    const passkeyOrWebAuthn = await page.locator(
      'button[id*="passkey"], button[id*="webauthn"], [data-method="passkey"]'
    ).count();
    expect(
      audioAlt + passkeyOrWebAuthn,
      'CAPTCHA present without audio alternative or passkey — violates WCAG 3.3.8'
    ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  }

  // Verify password field allows paste (pasting from a password manager is a 3.3.8 exception)
  const passwordInput = page.locator('input[type="password"]').first();
  await passwordInput.fill('');
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    const input = document.querySelector('input[type="password"]') as HTMLInputElement;
    if (input) {
      const event = new ClipboardEvent('paste', {
        clipboardData: new DataTransfer(),
        bubbles: true,
        cancelable: true,
      });
      input.dispatchEvent(event);
    }
  });
  const isPasteBlocked = await passwordInput.evaluate(
    (el: HTMLInputElement) => el.getAttribute('onpaste') === 'return false;' || el.getAttribute('onpaste')?.includes('false')
  );
  expect(isPasteBlocked, 'Password field blocks paste — prevents password manager use, violates WCAG 3.3.8').toBe(false);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 3.3.8 AA prohibits requiring a cognitive function test (such as transcribing distorted text or solving a puzzle) during authentication unless an alternative method or auto-fill is available; this test detects CAPTCHAs by class/id patterns and checks for audio alternatives and passkey buttons, but custom CAPTCHA implementations (canvas-drawn, CSS-only) will evade detection — run this test against a staging environment where you control the CAPTCHA presentation, and supplement with a manual login walkthrough using a screen reader and a keyboard-only user session to confirm the full path is accessible.

**Pattern 448** — WCAG 3.2.6 Consistent Help — Assert Help Links Appear in the Same Relative Order Across Pages
```typescript
test('help mechanisms appear in consistent position across application pages', async ({ page }) => {
  const routes = ['/', '/settings', '/profile', '/dashboard'];
  const helpPositions: Array<{ route: string; index: number; text: string }> = [];

  for (const route of routes) {
    await page.goto(route);
    const links = await page.evaluate(() => {
      return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a[href], button')).map((el, idx) => ({
        text: (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.toLowerCase().trim() || '',
        index: idx,
      }));
    });

    const helpLink = links.find(
      l => l.text.includes('help') || l.text.includes('support') || l.text.includes('contact')
    );

    if (helpLink) {
      helpPositions.push({ route, index: helpLink.index, text: helpLink.text });
    }
  }

  // Verify all found help links are in a consistent relative position (all near the end or all near start)
  if (helpPositions.length > 1) {
    const positions = helpPositions.map(p => p.index);
    const max = Math.max(...positions);
    const min = Math.min(...positions);
    // Allow up to 10 index positions of drift across templates
    expect(
      max - min,
      `Help link position varies too widely across pages:\n${helpPositions.map(p => `  ${p.route}: index ${p.index} "${p.text}"`).join('\n')}`
    ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(10);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 3.2.6 (Level A, new in 2.2) requires that help mechanisms — when present on multiple pages — appear in the same relative order within the page layout; this test measures DOM index drift across four routes using a tolerance of 10 positions, which is a pragmatic proxy for "same relative order" but is DOM-order sensitive rather than visual-order sensitive — a sticky footer help link might have the same visual position on every page but wildly different DOM indices if the footer is rendered after a variable-length main content region; for accurate 3.2.6 testing, compare the help link's membership in a named landmark (`<footer>`, `role="navigation"`) across pages rather than its raw DOM index.

**Pattern 449** — axe-core AxeBuilder Fixture — Scoped WCAG 2.2 AA Scan with Violation Fingerprinting
```typescript
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

type A11yFixtures = { checkA11y: (selector?: string) => Promise<void> };

export const test = base.extend<A11yFixtures>({
  checkA11y: async ({ page }, use) => {
    await use(async (selector = 'document') => {
      const builder = new AxeBuilder({ page })
        .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
        .exclude('[data-axe-ignore]');

      if (selector !== 'document') {
        builder.include(selector);
      }

      const results = await builder.analyze();

      const fingerprints = results.violations.map(v => ({
        id:       v.id,
        impact:   v.impact,
        nodes:    v.nodes.map(n => n.target.join(' ')).slice(0, 3),
        help:     v.help,
        helpUrl:  v.helpUrl,
      }));

      expect(
        fingerprints,
        `axe-core WCAG 2.2 AA violations:\n${JSON.stringify(fingerprints, null, 2)}`
      ).toHaveLength(0);
    });
  },
});
```
Tradeoff: The `withTags(['wcag22aa'])` tag enables axe-core rules mapped to WCAG 2.2 AA criteria (including `target-size` and `dragging-movements` rules where axe implements them), and the `[data-axe-ignore]` exclusion provides a per-element escape hatch for known false positives — but fingerprinting by `v.id` and `n.target` means a change in the number of violating nodes (e.g., 3 buttons → 4 buttons with the same missing label) will still appear as one fingerprint entry rather than four separate failures; use `nodes.length` in the fingerprint if you need to catch regressions in violation count per rule.

**Pattern 450** — ARIA Carousel — Verify Rotation Controls, Auto-Rotation Pause, and Live Region Announcement
```typescript
test('carousel meets ARIA APG requirements — controls, pause, and live region', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/home');
  const carousel = page.locator('[role="region"][aria-roledescription="carousel"]').first();

  // 1. Auto-rotation must pause on hover
  await carousel.hover();
  const slidesBefore = await carousel.locator('[role="group"][aria-roledescription="slide"]').count();
  await page.waitForTimeout(3500); // typical slide interval is 3s
  const slidesAfter = await carousel.locator('[aria-current="true"], [aria-hidden="false"]').count();
  // We cannot easily detect "current slide changed", so assert live region exists instead
  const liveRegion = carousel.locator('[aria-live="polite"], [aria-live="assertive"]');
  await expect(liveRegion, 'Carousel must have an aria-live region for slide announcements').toHaveCount(1);

  // 2. Previous/Next buttons must be present and labeled
  const prevBtn = carousel.locator('button[aria-label*="previous" i], button[aria-label*="prev" i]');
  const nextBtn = carousel.locator('button[aria-label*="next" i]');
  await expect(prevBtn.first(), 'Carousel must have a labeled "previous" button').toBeVisible();
  await expect(nextBtn.first(), 'Carousel must have a labeled "next" button').toBeVisible();

  // 3. Pause/Stop button must exist when rotation is automatic
  const pauseBtn = carousel.locator(
    'button[aria-label*="pause" i], button[aria-label*="stop" i], button[aria-label*="play" i]'
  );
  await expect(pauseBtn.first(), 'Auto-rotating carousel must have a pause/stop control').toBeVisible();
  await pauseBtn.first().click();
  // After pause, aria-label should change to "play" or button should now say "play"
  const playBtn = carousel.locator('button[aria-label*="play" i]');
  await expect(playBtn.first()).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: The ARIA APG Carousel Pattern requires `aria-roledescription="carousel"` on the outer region, `aria-roledescription="slide"` on each slide, and a pause mechanism if rotation is automatic; this test fails if the implementation uses non-standard attribute names (e.g., `data-carousel` instead of `role="region"`) or if the pause button uses an icon with a tooltip instead of an `aria-label` — the selector `button[aria-label*="pause" i]` misses icon-only buttons that rely on `title` or `aria-describedby`, so supplement with an AT manual test to confirm the pause control is announced correctly.

**Pattern 451** — ARIA Combobox — Verify Popup Role, aria-expanded Lifecycle, and Selection Announcement
```typescript
test('combobox follows ARIA 1.2 pattern — popup role, expansion, and selection', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');
  const combobox = page.locator('[role="combobox"]').first();

  // 1. aria-expanded must be "false" before interaction
  await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

  // 2. Typing must expand the combobox and reveal a listbox or grid
  await combobox.fill('a');
  await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

  const controlsId = await combobox.getAttribute('aria-controls');
  expect(controlsId, 'combobox must have aria-controls pointing to its popup').toBeTruthy();
  const popup = page.locator(`#${controlsId}`);
  const popupRole = await popup.getAttribute('role');
  expect(
    ['listbox', 'grid', 'tree', 'dialog'].includes(popupRole ?? ''),
    `combobox popup role must be listbox/grid/tree/dialog, got "${popupRole}"`
  ).toBe(true);

  // 3. ArrowDown moves focus to first option; Enter selects and collapses
  await combobox.press('ArrowDown');
  const focused = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role'));
  expect(['option', 'gridcell', 'treeitem'].includes(focused ?? ''), 'ArrowDown must move focus to a popup item').toBe(true);

  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(combobox).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
});
```
Tradeoff: ARIA 1.2 (which supersedes 1.1) changed the combobox pattern significantly — in ARIA 1.1 the combobox wrapped both the input and popup in a container with `role="combobox"`, while in ARIA 1.2 the `role="combobox"` is placed directly on the `<input>` with `aria-controls` pointing to the separate popup element; this test targets the ARIA 1.2 pattern, and legacy components built against the ARIA 1.1 pattern (still common in older design systems) will fail the `aria-expanded` check on the input because the attribute lives on the wrapper div — detect the pattern in use before running this test by checking `page.locator('[role="combobox"] input').count()` (ARIA 1.1) vs `page.locator('input[role="combobox"]').count()` (ARIA 1.2).

**Pattern 452** — WCAG 1.4.12 Text Spacing — Verify No Content Clipping or Overlap at Override Values
```typescript
test('text spacing overrides do not cause content loss or overlap (WCAG 1.4.12)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/article');

  // Inject the WCAG 1.4.12 text-spacing bookmarklet overrides via a style tag
  await page.addStyleTag({
    content: `
      * {
        line-height: 1.5 !important;
        letter-spacing: 0.12em !important;
        word-spacing: 0.16em !important;
      }
      p, li, dt, dd, figcaption, blockquote {
        margin-bottom: 2em !important;
      }
    `,
  });

  // Scan for clipping: elements where scrollHeight > clientHeight (content overflow hidden)
  const clipped = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const elements = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('p, li, h1, h2, h3, h4, label, button, a'));
    return elements
      .filter(el => {
        const s = getComputedStyle(el);
        const overflowHidden = s.overflow === 'hidden' || s.overflowY === 'hidden';
        const isClipped = (el as HTMLElement).scrollHeight > (el as HTMLElement).clientHeight + 2;
        return overflowHidden && isClipped;
      })
      .map(el => ({
        tag:  el.tagName,
        text: (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.slice(0, 60) || '',
        scrollH: (el as HTMLElement).scrollHeight,
        clientH: (el as HTMLElement).clientHeight,
      }));
  });

  expect(clipped, `Text spacing override caused content clipping:\n${JSON.stringify(clipped, null, 2)}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.4.12 specifies exact override values (line-height 1.5x, letter-spacing 0.12em, word-spacing 0.16em, paragraph spacing 2em) and requires that no content is lost or clipped — this test injects those values via `addStyleTag` and checks `scrollHeight > clientHeight` on `overflow:hidden` elements, which catches the most common failure (fixed-height containers with hidden overflow); it does not detect text overlap (two elements visually colliding) because measuring overlap requires comparing bounding-box coordinates of every pair of text elements, which is O(n²) and prohibitively slow — use the Accessibility Insights for Web "Text Spacing" bookmarklet for visual overlap verification during manual review.

**Pattern 453** — ARIA Live Region Politeness — Verify Status and Alert Announcements Use Correct aria-live Values
```typescript
test('live regions use correct politeness levels for their content type', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Status messages (success, info, count updates) must use aria-live="polite" or role="status"
  const statusRegions = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const els = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[role="status"], [role="log"], [aria-live="polite"]'));
    return els.map(el => ({
      tag:   el.tagName,
      role:  el.getAttribute('role'),
      live:  el.getAttribute('aria-live'),
      text:  (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.slice(0, 80),
    }));
  });

  // Alert messages (errors, time-sensitive warnings) must use aria-live="assertive" or role="alert"
  const alertRegions = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const els = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[role="alert"], [aria-live="assertive"]'));
    return els.map(el => ({
      tag:   el.tagName,
      role:  el.getAttribute('role'),
      live:  el.getAttribute('aria-live'),
      text:  (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.slice(0, 80),
    }));
  });

  // Validate no alert regions accidentally use aria-live="polite" (would delay urgent error announcements)
  const misusedAlerts = alertRegions.filter(r => r.live === 'polite');
  expect(
    misusedAlerts,
    `These elements use role="alert" but also set aria-live="polite" — the role already implies assertive:\n${JSON.stringify(misusedAlerts, null, 2)}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);

  // Validate live regions are not also aria-atomic="false" when they are counters or single-value regions
  const nonAtomicCounters = statusRegions.filter(r => r.text?.match(/\d+ item/i) && r.role !== 'log');
  for (const region of nonAtomicCounters) {
    const el = page.locator(`[role="${region.role}"]`).first();
    const atomic = await el.getAttribute('aria-atomic');
    expect(
      atomic,
      `Counter live region "${region.text}" should use aria-atomic="true" so the full value is re-read on update`
    ).toBe('true');
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `role="alert"` implies `aria-live="assertive"` and `aria-atomic="true"` — adding an explicit `aria-live="polite"` on the same element creates a conflict that different AT resolve differently (JAWS respects the role, NVDA may respect the explicit attribute), and this conflict is the root cause of inconsistent announcement timing across AT; this test catches the conflict but cannot test timing empirically because Playwright runs in a headless Chromium process with no AT attached — actual announcement ordering must be verified with NVDA + Firefox or JAWS + Chrome in a manual test pass.

**Pattern 454** — WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured — Detect Sticky Headers and Footers That Cover Focused Elements
```typescript
test('focused elements are not fully obscured by sticky headers or footers (WCAG 2.4.11)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/long-page');

  const stickyElements = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('*'))
      .filter(el => {
        const s = getComputedStyle(el);
        return (s.position === 'fixed' || s.position === 'sticky') && (el as HTMLElement).offsetHeight > 0;
      })
      .map(el => {
        const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        return { top: rect.top, bottom: rect.bottom, height: rect.height };
      });
  });

  if (stickyElements.length === 0) return; // No sticky elements — criterion trivially satisfied

  const focusables = page.locator('a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), [tabindex="0"]');
  const count = await focusables.count();
  const failures: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 30); i++) {
    const el = focusables.nth(i);
    await el.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded();
    await el.focus();
    const elBox = await el.boundingBox();
    if (!elBox) continue;

    for (const sticky of stickyElements) {
      // Full obscurement: focused element top >= sticky top AND focused element bottom <= sticky bottom
      const fullyObscuredByHeader = elBox.y >= sticky.top && elBox.y + elBox.height <= sticky.bottom;
      const fullyObscuredByFooter = sticky.top > 0 && elBox.y >= sticky.top;
      if (fullyObscuredByHeader || fullyObscuredByFooter) {
        const label = await el.getAttribute('aria-label') || await el.textContent() || '';
        failures.push(`Element "${label.trim().slice(0, 50)}" at y=${elBox.y.toFixed(0)} fully obscured by sticky element`);
      }
    }
  }

  expect(failures, `WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured failures:\n${failures.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.4.11 AA (new in 2.2) prohibits *full* obscurement of a focused component — partial obscurement is acceptable at AA level (only AAA 2.4.12 requires zero obscurement); this test correctly tests full obscurement by comparing the focused element's bounding box against every sticky element's bounding box, but it does not account for `scroll-padding-top` or `scroll-margin-top` CSS properties that browsers use to offset scroll position for sticky headers — if the application correctly uses `scroll-padding`, the element will never actually be obscured during keyboard navigation, meaning this test may report false positives on pages that use `scroll-padding` correctly; suppress by checking `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).scrollPaddingTop` before asserting.

**Pattern 455** — Playwright `toMatchAriaSnapshot` — Regression-Test ARIA Tree for a Navigation Component
```typescript
test('primary navigation ARIA tree matches expected snapshot', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  const nav = page.locator('nav[aria-label="Primary navigation"]');

  // First run: generate snapshot with --update-snapshots flag
  // Subsequent runs: assert structural regression
  await expect(nav).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - navigation "Primary navigation":
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - link "Home" [href="/"]
        - listitem:
          - link "Products" [href="/products"] [expanded=false]
          - list /[aria-label="Products submenu"]/: []
        - listitem:
          - link "About" [href="/about"]
        - listitem:
          - link "Contact" [href="/contact"]
  `);
});
```
Tradeoff: Playwright's `toMatchAriaSnapshot` (available from Playwright 1.46) uses the Accessibility Tree computed by the browser's accessibility API — not the DOM — so it catches regressions in ARIA role assignments, accessible names, and structural hierarchy that DOM snapshots miss; however, it is brittle to any localization change (a translated `aria-label` will break the snapshot) and to intentional restructuring (adding a menu item requires updating all navigation snapshots), meaning it adds maintenance overhead proportional to the rate of UI change; use partial YAML matching with `/regex/` patterns for labels that are dynamic (e.g., badge counts or user names) to reduce snapshot churn.

**Pattern 456** — WCAG 1.3.4 Orientation — Verify No Content or Functionality Is Locked to a Single Orientation
```typescript
test('application does not restrict content to portrait or landscape orientation', async ({ page, browser }) => {
  const portraitContext = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 } });
  const landscapeContext = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 844, height: 390 } });

  const portraitPage = await portraitContext.newPage();
  const landscapePage = await landscapeContext.newPage();

  try {
    await portraitPage.goto('/dashboard');
    await landscapePage.goto('/dashboard');

    // Both orientations must render the main content landmark
    const portraitMain = await portraitPage.locator('main, [role="main"]').count();
    const landscapeMain = await landscapePage.locator('main, [role="main"]').count();

    expect(portraitMain, 'Portrait orientation must render main content').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(landscapeMain, 'Landscape orientation must render main content').toBeGreaterThan(0);

    // Neither orientation should show an orientation-lock message
    const lockMessages = [/rotate your (device|phone|screen)/i, /only (works?|available) in (portrait|landscape)/i];
    for (const pattern of lockMessages) {
      await expect(portraitPage.getByText(pattern)).toHaveCount(0);
      await expect(landscapePage.getByText(pattern)).toHaveCount(0);
    }

    // Both orientations must show the same number of primary nav links
    const portraitNavLinks = await portraitPage.locator('nav a').count();
    const landscapeNavLinks = await landscapePage.locator('nav a').count();
    expect(
      Math.abs(portraitNavLinks - landscapeNavLinks),
      `Navigation has ${portraitNavLinks} links in portrait but ${landscapeNavLinks} in landscape — some may be hidden`
    ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1); // allow for hamburger vs expanded nav (at most 1 difference)
  } finally {
    await portraitContext.close();
    await landscapeContext.close();
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.3.4 forbids restricting content to a single viewport orientation unless the restriction is essential (e.g., a piano app that requires landscape); this test simulates both orientations by resizing the Playwright viewport, which exercises CSS `@media (orientation: portrait/landscape)` rules correctly but does not test the device `screen.orientation` API or CSS `transform: rotate()` used by some hybrid apps that physically rotate the rendered content rather than reflow it — apps using CSS rotation will appear in both orientations in Playwright but will be unusable in one orientation for real device users; supplement with a physical device test or a BrowserStack/Sauce Labs real device session.

**Pattern 457** — ARIA APG Tab Panel — Verify Selection-Follows-Focus vs Manual Activation Modes and roving tabindex
```typescript
test('tab widget implements roving tabindex and correct activation mode', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings');
  const tabList = page.locator('[role="tablist"]').first();
  const tabs = tabList.locator('[role="tab"]');

  const tabCount = await tabs.count();
  expect(tabCount, 'Settings tablist must have at least 2 tabs').toBeGreaterThan(1);

  // Verify roving tabindex: only one tab has tabindex="0", rest have tabindex="-1"
  let zeroCount = 0;
  let negOneCount = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < tabCount; i++) {
    const ti = await tabs.nth(i).getAttribute('tabindex');
    if (ti === '0') zeroCount++;
    if (ti === '-1') negOneCount++;
  }
  expect(zeroCount, 'Exactly one tab must have tabindex="0"').toBe(1);
  expect(negOneCount, 'All non-selected tabs must have tabindex="-1"').toBe(tabCount - 1);

  // Verify selected tab has aria-selected="true" and its panel is visible
  const selectedTab = tabList.locator('[role="tab"][aria-selected="true"]');
  await expect(selectedTab).toHaveCount(1);
  const panelId = await selectedTab.getAttribute('aria-controls');
  if (panelId) {
    const panel = page.locator(`#${panelId}`);
    await expect(panel).toBeVisible();
  }

  // Verify ArrowRight moves focus and updates aria-selected (selection-follows-focus mode)
  await tabs.first().focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
  const newSelected = tabList.locator('[role="tab"][aria-selected="true"]');
  const newSelectedText = await newSelected.textContent();
  const secondTabText = await tabs.nth(1).textContent();
  expect(newSelectedText?.trim()).toBe(secondTabText?.trim());
});
```
Tradeoff: The ARIA APG Tab Pattern supports two activation modes — "selection follows focus" (arrow key immediately activates the tab) and "manual activation" (arrow key moves focus but requires Enter/Space to activate); this test assumes selection-follows-focus because it is the simpler and more common implementation and is the mode recommended by the APG for tabs containing form controls (to avoid data loss from accidental tab switches), but manual-activation tabs will fail the final `aria-selected` assertion — detect the mode before asserting by pressing `ArrowRight` and checking whether `aria-selected` changed; if it did not, skip the final assertion and instead test that `Enter` activates the tab.

**Pattern 458** — WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard — Detect Date Pickers That Trap Focus Without Escape Route
```typescript
test('date picker does not create an inescapable keyboard trap', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/booking');

  const dateInput = page.locator('input[type="date"], input[aria-haspopup="dialog"], input[aria-haspopup="grid"]').first();
  await dateInput.focus();

  // Open the picker
  await dateInput.press('Enter');
  await page.waitForTimeout(300);

  const pickerVisible = await page.locator(
    '[role="dialog"][aria-label*="date" i], [role="grid"][aria-label*="date" i], [role="listbox"][aria-label*="month" i]'
  ).isVisible().catch(() => false);

  if (pickerVisible) {
    // Escape must close the picker and return focus to the input
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await page.waitForTimeout(200);

    const pickerGone = !(await page.locator(
      '[role="dialog"][aria-label*="date" i], [role="grid"][aria-label*="date" i]'
    ).isVisible().catch(() => false));

    expect(pickerGone, 'Date picker did not close on Escape — keyboard trap').toBe(true);

    const focusedTag = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.tagName.toLowerCase());
    const focusedType = await page.evaluate(() => (document.activeElement as HTMLInputElement)?.type);
    expect(
      focusedTag === 'input' && (focusedType === 'date' || focusedType === 'text'),
      `Focus did not return to date input after Escape — landed on "${focusedTag}"`
    ).toBe(true);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.1.1 requires that all functionality is operable via keyboard, and the ARIA APG Dialog Pattern requires that Escape closes a modal dialog and returns focus to the triggering element — custom date pickers that implement a popup grid frequently fail this by closing on Escape but returning focus to the document body rather than the trigger input, breaking the keyboard user's navigation position; this test verifies both the close behavior and the focus return, but it opens the picker with `Enter` which is not universally supported by custom picker implementations that only open on click — add a fallback that clicks the calendar icon (`[aria-label*="calendar" i]`) if Enter does not reveal the picker.

**Pattern 459** — WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages — Verify Success and Error Toasts Are Announced Without Receiving Focus
```typescript
test('status message toasts are announced via aria-live without receiving focus (WCAG 4.1.3)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/profile');

  // Record the element that has focus before the action that triggers a toast
  const focusBeforeAction = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.id || document.activeElement?.tagName);

  // Submit a form to trigger a success toast
  await page.locator('button[type="submit"], button:has-text("Save")').first().click();
  await page.waitForTimeout(800);

  // Find the toast / status message
  const toasts = page.locator('[role="status"], [role="alert"], [aria-live="polite"], [aria-live="assertive"]');
  const toastCount = await toasts.count();
  expect(toastCount, 'No live-region element found for status messages').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Focus must NOT have moved to the toast
  const focusAfterToast = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.id || document.activeElement?.tagName);
  expect(
    focusAfterToast,
    `Focus moved to the toast/status region — WCAG 4.1.3 requires status messages not to receive focus`
  ).toBe(focusBeforeAction);

  // Toast must not be a focusable element itself
  const toastEl = toasts.first();
  const tabindex = await toastEl.getAttribute('tabindex');
  expect(
    tabindex,
    'Toast element must not have tabindex="0" — status messages must not be reachable via Tab'
  ).not.toBe('0');
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 4.1.3 (AA, added in WCAG 2.1) requires that status messages — informational updates that do not receive focus — are programmatically determinable so AT can announce them; the criterion is violated when a toast library moves focus to the toast container to ensure AT reads it, because this disrupts the user's current position; this test asserts focus does not move and the container is not in the tab order, but it cannot verify that AT actually announced the message because Playwright has no AT attached — a toast with `aria-live="polite"` on a container that is `display:none` when empty and `display:block` when shown will trigger a live region announcement in real AT, but only if the text is inserted *after* the element is already in the DOM; test this injection pattern explicitly by asserting the container exists in the DOM before the form submit.

### Community Gotchas

**G301** — `aria-describedby` pointing to a hidden element silently fails to provide a description — all major AT ignore descriptions from elements with `display:none` or `visibility:hidden`
Why this matters: `aria-describedby` provides supplementary description text, announced after the accessible name, for form fields, buttons, and complex widgets. Developers frequently place the description text in a `<span>` that is visually hidden using `display:none` (e.g., to avoid cluttering the visual layout) and reference it via `aria-describedby`. However, the ARIA specification states that AT must ignore `aria-describedby` references to elements that are not exposed in the accessibility tree — elements with `display:none` or `visibility:hidden` are removed from the accessibility tree, so the description is silently dropped. The element with `aria-describedby` will report an empty or absent description in all AT, and the associated description text will never be read. This differs from `aria-labelledby`, which shares the same behavior but is more commonly tested because accessible-name failures are flagged by axe-core's `label` rule — `aria-describedby` failures are not flagged unless you use the `aria-required-attr` rule with manual inspection.
Fix: Use the `.sr-only` (visually hidden) CSS technique instead of `display:none` — `.sr-only` positions the element off-screen using `position:absolute; clip:rect(0,0,0,0); width:1px; height:1px; overflow:hidden` which keeps the element in both the DOM and the accessibility tree. Playwright detection: `const ids = await el.getAttribute('aria-describedby'); const described = page.locator('#' + ids); expect(await described.evaluate(n => getComputedStyle(n).display)).not.toBe('none')`.

**G302** — `aria-label` overrides the visible text label entirely — voice control users who read the screen and speak the visible text cannot activate the control if `aria-label` differs from visible text, violating WCAG 2.5.3
Why this matters: WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name, Level A) requires that the accessible name of a UI component contains the visible text label as a substring. When developers add an `aria-label` to a button that already has visible text — commonly to provide more context (e.g., button text "Edit" + `aria-label="Edit billing address"`) — the `aria-label` completely overrides the accessible name. Voice control software (Dragon NaturallySpeaking, Voice Control on iOS/macOS) derives activation targets from the accessible name, so a user who sees "Edit" and says "click Edit" will fail to activate the button because the accessible name is "Edit billing address". axe-core's `label-content-name-mismatch` rule detects this when the visible text is entirely absent from the `aria-label`, but it does not flag cases where the text is present but in a different order or truncated.
Fix: Always include the visible text verbatim as a prefix or substring in the `aria-label` — for example, `aria-label="Edit billing address"` on a button with visible text "Edit" satisfies 2.5.3 because "Edit" appears as a substring of the accessible name. Alternatively, use `aria-label` only when there is no visible text (icon buttons), and use `aria-describedby` when you need to add supplementary context beyond the visible label.

**G303** — `role="button"` on a `<div>` or `<span>` does not automatically provide keyboard operability — without `tabindex="0"` the element is not focusable, and without keydown handlers it does not fire on Space and Enter
Why this matters: The ARIA specification defines role semantics (what the element *is*) but does not polyfill native HTML behavior — a `<div role="button">` tells AT it is a button, but the browser will not make it focusable (no native tab stop), will not fire a `click` event on Space or Enter keydown, and will not provide the button's default styling. This is the "ARIA does not add behavior" principle. A `<div role="button">` without `tabindex="0"` is invisible to keyboard-only users entirely; with `tabindex="0"` but without keydown handlers it can be focused but not activated by keyboard. axe-core's `button-name` rule checks accessible names on `[role="button"]` elements but does not check keyboard operability. The issue is pervasive in custom component libraries built before native `<button>` theming was widely understood.
Fix: Use a native `<button>` element — it provides tabindex, keyboard activation (Space/Enter), accessible role, and browser default styles with `appearance:none` for custom theming, all without JavaScript. If a `<div role="button">` must be used (e.g., in a third-party component), add `tabindex="0"` and attach a `keydown` handler that calls `event.currentTarget.click()` when `event.key === ' ' || event.key === 'Enter'`, and call `event.preventDefault()` for Space to prevent page scroll.

**G304** — `aria-expanded` on a disclosure button reflects the state of a menu that renders lazily — if the menu DOM does not exist yet when `aria-expanded="false"`, AT may read the correct state but users find an empty container on expand
Why this matters: Single-page application navigation menus commonly render the dropdown submenu DOM only after the toggle button is first clicked (lazy rendering for performance). The toggle button correctly starts with `aria-expanded="false"`, and the AT announces "collapsed". When the user expands the menu for the first time, the `aria-expanded` is set to `"true"` before the menu DOM is fully rendered, causing a race condition where AT immediately reads the focus destination inside the menu before the menu items are painted. The focus lands inside an empty or partially rendered `<ul>` and AT announces nothing or announces stale content. This pattern is reproducible when the menu content is fetched from an API or rendered asynchronously via `requestAnimationFrame`. axe-core does not test async rendering timing.
Fix: Set `aria-expanded="true"` and move focus into the menu *after* the menu content is fully rendered and visible — use `await` on the data fetch, or use a `MutationObserver` that watches for the first `<li>` child of the menu container before triggering focus movement. In Playwright: `await page.locator('[aria-expanded="true"] + [role="menu"] li').first().waitFor({ state: 'visible' })` before asserting focus.

**G305** — Reading order in the accessibility tree diverges from visual reading order when CSS Grid or Flexbox uses `order` property — AT reads DOM source order, not visual order, causing a disorienting mismatch for AT users
Why this matters: CSS Grid and Flexbox `order` property changes the visual rendering sequence of child elements without changing DOM order — a sidebar visually positioned before a main article can be last in the DOM and receive AT focus last, while a CTA button visually at the top of a card grid may be last in the DOM and accessed last by keyboard. WCAG 1.3.2 (Meaningful Sequence, A) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order, A) both require that reading and navigation order matches the meaningful sequence of content. The `order` property is the most common source of DOM-visual order divergence in modern CSS layouts, followed by `float` and absolute positioning. axe-core does not detect `order`-based divergence because it would require layout computation.
Fix: Maintain logical DOM order that matches the intended reading order, and use CSS Grid/Flexbox for visual presentation only without relying on `order` to invert meaning. When visual reordering is necessary (e.g., a "featured" item that appears first visually but is third in the data set), reorder the data array before rendering rather than reordering with CSS. Playwright audit: `await page.evaluate(() => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[style*="order"]')).map(el => ({ tag: el.tagName, order: getComputedStyle(el).order, text: el.innerText.slice(0, 40) })))` — review any non-zero `order` value for reading order impact.
