## Cycle 68 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 460** — WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size Minimum — Verify Interactive Controls Are at Least 24×24 CSS Pixels or Have Adequate Spacing
```typescript
test('interactive controls meet 24x24 CSS pixel minimum target size (WCAG 2.5.8)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Collect all interactive controls (buttons, links, inputs, checkboxes, radios)
  const interactiveSelectors = 'button, a[href], input[type="checkbox"], input[type="radio"], [role="button"], [role="link"], [role="checkbox"], [role="radio"], [role="switch"]';
  const controls = page.locator(interactiveSelectors);
  const count = await controls.count();

  const undersizedTargets: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 80); i++) {
    const el = controls.nth(i);

    // Skip invisible or disabled elements
    if (!(await el.isVisible())) continue;
    const disabled = await el.getAttribute('disabled');
    const ariaDisabled = await el.getAttribute('aria-disabled');
    if (disabled !== null || ariaDisabled === 'true') continue;

    const box = await el.boundingBox();
    if (!box) continue;

    // Inline elements (links in prose) are exempt — check display type
    const display = await el.evaluate((n: Element) => getComputedStyle(n).display);
    if (display === 'inline') continue;

    if (box.width < 24 || box.height < 24) {
      const label = await el.getAttribute('aria-label') || await el.textContent() || await el.getAttribute('type') || 'unlabeled';
      undersizedTargets.push(`[${label.trim().slice(0, 40)}] ${Math.round(box.width)}x${Math.round(box.height)}px at (${Math.round(box.x)},${Math.round(box.y)})`);
    }
  }

  expect(
    undersizedTargets,
    `Controls below 24x24 CSS px minimum (WCAG 2.5.8) — verify spacing exception or add padding:\n${undersizedTargets.join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.5.8 (AA, WCAG 2.2) requires controls to be at least 24×24 CSS pixels or have sufficient spacing so a 24px-diameter circle around each target does not intersect adjacent targets — inline text links, disabled controls, and user-agent-native widgets are exempt; this test checks bounding-box dimensions and skips `display:inline` elements but cannot automatically verify the spacing exception path, so any control below 24×24 that the team claims passes via spacing must be manually verified using the circle-center offset formula from the Understanding document; padding added to meet the size requirement must not push adjacent controls so close that the spacing exception is violated for their neighbors.

**Pattern 461** — WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry — Verify Multi-step Forms Auto-populate or Offer Pre-filled Selections for Previously Entered Data
```typescript
test('multi-step checkout does not require redundant re-entry of contact information (WCAG 3.3.7)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout/contact');

  // Step 1: enter contact information
  await page.locator('input[autocomplete="given-name"], input[name*="first"]').first().fill('Jane');
  await page.locator('input[autocomplete="family-name"], input[name*="last"]').first().fill('Smith');
  await page.locator('input[autocomplete="email"], input[type="email"]').first().fill('jane.smith@example.com');
  await page.locator('button[type="submit"], button:has-text("Continue"), button:has-text("Next")').first().click();

  // Step 2: billing page — name/email from contact must not require manual re-entry
  await page.waitForURL(/billing|payment|step-?2/i);

  // Verify that first name is auto-populated or a matching pre-fill checkbox exists
  const firstNameInput = page.locator('input[autocomplete="given-name"], input[name*="first"]').first();
  const billingCheckbox = page.locator('[id*="same"], [name*="same"], label:has-text("same as")').first();

  const firstNamePopulated = await firstNameInput.count() > 0
    ? (await firstNameInput.inputValue()).toLowerCase().includes('jane')
    : false;
  const sameAsCheckboxVisible = await billingCheckbox.count() > 0 && await billingCheckbox.isVisible();

  expect(
    firstNamePopulated || sameAsCheckboxVisible,
    'WCAG 3.3.7: Contact name must be auto-populated on billing step or a "same as contact" checkbox must be provided'
  ).toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 3.3.7 (A, WCAG 2.2) protects users with cognitive disabilities from the memory burden of re-entering data across steps in the same process; the criterion allows three exceptions — security-critical re-entry (e.g., password confirmation), essential re-entry (e.g., CAPTCHA, quiz answers), and invalid data requiring correction — but this test cannot distinguish intent from implementation and will flag a password-confirm field as a false positive unless the selector is scoped to non-security fields; for processes where the same data appears in three or more distinct steps, audit each transition individually rather than only the second step.

**Pattern 462** — WCAG 2.2.6 Timeouts — Verify Session Timeout Warning Is Present Before Inactivity Causes Data Loss
```typescript
test('session timeout warning is present before inactivity causes data loss (WCAG 2.2.6)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/application/form');

  // Fill in form data that would be lost on timeout
  await page.locator('input[type="text"], textarea').first().fill('Draft content that must not be silently lost');

  // Detect whether a session timeout warning element exists in the DOM (hidden initially, shown before timeout)
  const timeoutWarning = page.locator(
    '[role="alertdialog"][aria-label*="session" i], [role="alertdialog"][aria-label*="timeout" i], ' +
    '[role="dialog"][aria-label*="session" i], [aria-live][id*="timeout" i], ' +
    'dialog:has-text("session"), dialog:has-text("expire")'
  );

  const warningExists = await timeoutWarning.count() > 0;

  // Check for a data-preservation indicator: auto-save, draft save, or explicit preserve policy text
  const preservesData = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const body = document.body.innerText.toLowerCase();
    return body.includes('auto-save') || body.includes('saved automatically') ||
           body.includes('draft saved') || body.includes('progress is saved');
  });

  expect(
    warningExists || preservesData,
    'WCAG 2.2.6: Either a session timeout warning dialog must exist in the DOM, or the page must indicate data is preserved for 20+ hours of inactivity'
  ).toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.2.6 (AAA) requires that users are warned at the start of a process about inactivity timeout duration if data is not preserved for at least 20 hours — this test provides coverage by detecting either a timeout-warning dialog element or auto-save language, but it cannot verify the actual timeout duration or that the warning appears at process start rather than mid-step; a page that displays the warning only 30 seconds before expiry when the form takes 45 minutes to complete satisfies the DOM-presence check but fails the criterion's spirit; supplement this test with a manual review of the timeout configuration and warning timing.

**Pattern 463** — ARIA APG Tree View — Verify ArrowRight/Left Expand/Collapse and Home/End Navigation in role="tree"
```typescript
test('tree view implements APG keyboard contract: ArrowRight/Left expand/collapse, Home/End boundary navigation', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/file-explorer');

  const tree = page.locator('[role="tree"]').first();
  await expect(tree, 'No role="tree" found on page').toBeVisible();

  await tree.focus();

  // Identify a collapsed parent node
  const collapsedNode = tree.locator('[role="treeitem"][aria-expanded="false"]').first();
  await expect(collapsedNode, 'No collapsed treeitem (aria-expanded="false") found').toBeVisible();
  await collapsedNode.focus();

  // ArrowRight should expand the node
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
  await expect(collapsedNode, 'ArrowRight did not set aria-expanded to true on collapsed node').toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

  // ArrowRight on open node moves focus to first child
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight');
  const focusedAfterChildMove = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('role'));
  expect(focusedAfterChildMove, 'ArrowRight on open node did not move focus to first child treeitem').toBe('treeitem');

  // ArrowLeft should collapse or move to parent
  await collapsedNode.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowLeft');
  const ariaExpandedAfterLeft = await collapsedNode.getAttribute('aria-expanded');
  expect(['false', null], 'ArrowLeft did not close the open node').toContain(ariaExpandedAfterLeft);

  // Home key should move to first treeitem
  await page.keyboard.press('Home');
  const firstNode = tree.locator('[role="treeitem"]').first();
  await expect(firstNode, 'Home key did not move focus to first treeitem').toBeFocused();

  // End key should move to last visible treeitem
  await page.keyboard.press('End');
  const lastVisible = tree.locator('[role="treeitem"]:visible').last();
  await expect(lastVisible, 'End key did not move focus to last visible treeitem').toBeFocused();
});
```
Tradeoff: The ARIA APG Tree View pattern defines a keyboard contract where ArrowRight on an open node moves focus to the first child, and ArrowLeft on a leaf node moves focus to the parent — this test exercises the expand/collapse contract and Home/End boundaries, but it focuses each node by calling `.focus()` programmatically rather than navigating by ArrowUp/ArrowDown from the tree root, which can mask implementations that apply focus management only to nodes navigated from the roving-tabindex path; if a treeitem has `tabindex="-1"` and is programmatically focusable but excluded from the roving-tabindex cycle, ArrowDown navigation from the root will never reach it and the tree will silently omit content for keyboard users.

**Pattern 464** — ARIA APG Feed Pattern — Verify role="feed" Sets aria-busy During Load and Articles Have aria-labelledby
```typescript
test('feed pattern sets aria-busy during load and articles have accessible names (ARIA APG Feed)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/activity-feed');

  const feed = page.locator('[role="feed"]').first();
  await expect(feed, 'No role="feed" element found').toBeVisible();

  // Trigger a load-more action if a button exists
  const loadMoreBtn = page.locator('button:has-text("Load more"), button:has-text("Show more"), [aria-label*="load" i]').first();
  if (await loadMoreBtn.count() > 0 && await loadMoreBtn.isVisible()) {
    let busyDuringLoad = false;
    const checkBusy = page.waitForFunction(
      () => document.querySelector('[role="feed"]')?.getAttribute('aria-busy') === 'true',
      { timeout: 2000 }
    ).then(() => { busyDuringLoad = true; }).catch(() => {});

    await loadMoreBtn.click();
    await checkBusy;
    await page.waitForFunction(
      () => document.querySelector('[role="feed"]')?.getAttribute('aria-busy') !== 'true',
      { timeout: 8000 }
    );

    expect(busyDuringLoad, 'Feed did not set aria-busy="true" during article load — AT users cannot detect content loading').toBe(true);
  }

  // Verify feed articles have accessible names via aria-labelledby or aria-label
  const articles = feed.locator('[role="article"]');
  const articleCount = await articles.count();
  expect(articleCount, 'Feed contains no role="article" children').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(articleCount, 5); i++) {
    const article = articles.nth(i);
    const labelledBy = await article.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    const ariaLabel = await article.getAttribute('aria-label');
    expect(
      labelledBy || ariaLabel,
      `Article ${i + 1} in feed lacks aria-labelledby or aria-label — screen reader users cannot distinguish articles`
    ).toBeTruthy();
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: The ARIA APG Feed pattern requires `aria-busy="true"` on the feed container during multi-DOM-operation updates so AT does not announce partial content, and requires each `role="article"` to have an accessible name via `aria-labelledby` so screen reader users can skim the feed using browse-mode navigation — this test's `aria-busy` detection depends on the update being slow enough for the transient state to be observable, which can fail on fast connections where the DOM update completes within a single microtask queue flush; for reliable testing inject a network intercept that delays the feed API response by 500ms to guarantee the `aria-busy` transition is detectable.

**Pattern 465** — WCAG 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus — Verify Tooltips Are Dismissible via Escape, Hoverable, and Persistent
```typescript
test('tooltip content is dismissible via Escape, hoverable by mouse, and persistent (WCAG 1.4.13)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/help-center');

  const trigger = page.locator('[aria-describedby]').filter({
    has: page.locator('~ [role="tooltip"], + [role="tooltip"]')
  }).first();

  const tooltipTrigger = await trigger.count() > 0
    ? trigger
    : page.locator('[data-tooltip], [title]:not(html):not(head)').first();

  await tooltipTrigger.hover();
  await page.waitForTimeout(600);

  const tooltip = page.locator('[role="tooltip"]').first();
  const tooltipVisible = await tooltip.count() > 0 && await tooltip.isVisible();

  if (!tooltipVisible) {
    console.warn('No role="tooltip" visible after hover; skipping WCAG 1.4.13 tooltip check');
    return;
  }

  // 1. Dismissible: Escape must close the tooltip
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await page.waitForTimeout(200);
  await expect(tooltip, 'WCAG 1.4.13: Tooltip is not dismissible via Escape key').not.toBeVisible();

  // Re-trigger for hoverability check
  await tooltipTrigger.hover();
  await page.waitForTimeout(600);

  // 2. Hoverable: moving cursor onto tooltip must not close it
  await tooltip.hover();
  await page.waitForTimeout(300);
  await expect(tooltip, 'WCAG 1.4.13: Tooltip closes when hovered — pointer must be able to move over it without dismissal').toBeVisible();

  // 3. Persistent: tooltip must remain while hovered
  await page.waitForTimeout(1500);
  await expect(tooltip, 'WCAG 1.4.13: Tooltip auto-dismissed while pointer was still over it — content must persist until intentionally dismissed').toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.4.13 (AA) requires hover-triggered content to be dismissible (Escape), hoverable (mouse can move onto it), and persistent (stays until user dismisses it) — this test uses a 600ms wait to allow hover-delay timers to fire, but tooltip implementations with longer delays (>1 second) or animated entry will produce false failures; the `role="tooltip"` locator misses tooltips implemented as CSS `:hover` pseudo-elements on `::after` pseudo-elements since these have no DOM node for Playwright to locate, and the Escape dismissal check will silently pass for those invisible implementations — use screenshot comparison or a pixel-color assertion at the tooltip coordinates to verify CSS-only tooltips.

**Pattern 466** — WCAG 2.4.6 Headings and Labels — Verify All Form Labels Are Descriptive and Headings Describe Their Section
```typescript
test('form labels and page headings are descriptive and not generic placeholder text (WCAG 2.4.6)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings/account');

  const nonDescriptivePatterns = /^(field|input|text|enter|type here|label|value|data|\d+)$/i;

  // Check form labels
  const labels = page.locator('label');
  const labelCount = await labels.count();
  const genericLabels: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < labelCount; i++) {
    const labelText = (await labels.nth(i).textContent() || '').trim();
    if (labelText && nonDescriptivePatterns.test(labelText)) {
      genericLabels.push(`label: "${labelText}"`);
    }
    if (labelText === '') {
      const forAttr = await labels.nth(i).getAttribute('for');
      genericLabels.push(`empty label (for="${forAttr}")`);
    }
  }

  // Check aria-label values on form controls
  const ariaLabeled = page.locator('[aria-label]');
  const ariaCount = await ariaLabeled.count();
  for (let i = 0; i < ariaCount; i++) {
    const ariaText = (await ariaLabeled.nth(i).getAttribute('aria-label') || '').trim();
    if (nonDescriptivePatterns.test(ariaText)) {
      genericLabels.push(`aria-label: "${ariaText}"`);
    }
  }

  expect(
    genericLabels,
    `WCAG 2.4.6: Generic or empty labels found — labels must describe field purpose:\n${genericLabels.join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);

  // Check headings: h1–h4 must not be generic
  const headings = page.locator('h1, h2, h3, h4, [role="heading"]');
  const headingCount = await headings.count();
  const genericHeadings: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < headingCount; i++) {
    const hText = (await headings.nth(i).textContent() || '').trim();
    if (hText === '' || /^(heading|title|section|untitled)$/i.test(hText)) {
      genericHeadings.push(`heading: "${hText}"`);
    }
  }

  expect(
    genericHeadings,
    `WCAG 2.4.6: Generic or empty headings found — headings must describe their section:\n${genericHeadings.join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.4.6 (AA) requires that headings and labels describe topic or purpose, but the criterion does not require labels to be present — 2.4.6 only applies when labels exist, while 3.3.2 separately mandates that labels are provided; this test catches generically named labels and headings but cannot evaluate semantic quality of plausible-sounding text (e.g., a label reading "Value" that contextually means a financial instrument symbol is not caught as generic by regex), so complement automated detection with a manual pass that reads each label aloud and asks whether a user unfamiliar with the page would understand the field's purpose.

**Pattern 467** — WCAG 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose — Verify autocomplete Attributes Are Present and Use Valid Token Values on Personal-Data Fields
```typescript
test('personal data inputs carry valid HTML autocomplete attribute values (WCAG 1.3.5)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/profile/edit');

  const inputs = page.locator('input:not([type="hidden"]):not([type="submit"]):not([type="button"])');
  const count = await inputs.count();
  const missingAutocomplete: string[] = [];

  // Personal-data field detection by name/type pattern
  const personalFieldPatterns = ['first', 'last', 'given', 'family', 'email', 'phone', 'tel', 'address', 'postal', 'zip', 'country', 'password'];

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const input = inputs.nth(i);
    const nameAttr = (await input.getAttribute('name') || '').toLowerCase();
    const typeAttr = (await input.getAttribute('type') || 'text').toLowerCase();
    const autocomplete = await input.getAttribute('autocomplete');

    const isPersonalField = personalFieldPatterns.some(p => nameAttr.includes(p)) || typeAttr === 'email' || typeAttr === 'tel';
    if (!isPersonalField) continue;

    // autocomplete="on" and "off" do not convey purpose — specific tokens required
    if (!autocomplete || autocomplete === 'on' || autocomplete === 'off') {
      missingAutocomplete.push(
        `input[name="${nameAttr}" type="${typeAttr}"] — autocomplete="${autocomplete ?? 'missing'}" (needs specific token e.g. "email", "given-name", "postal-code")`
      );
    }
  }

  expect(
    missingAutocomplete,
    `WCAG 1.3.5: Personal-data inputs lack specific autocomplete tokens:\n${missingAutocomplete.join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.3.5 (AA) requires that inputs collecting user personal information have their purpose programmatically determinable using the HTML autocomplete attribute — this test infers "personal data" fields from name-attribute patterns, which misses fields where the name is opaque (e.g., `name="field_34"`) and over-matches fields in admin UIs where staff enter other people's data rather than their own; the criterion only applies to inputs collecting information about the current user, not arbitrary data-entry fields, so scope the selector to forms within authenticated profile, billing, and registration pages rather than running globally across all inputs.

**Pattern 468** — ARIA APG Tooltip Pattern — Verify role="tooltip" Is Reference-Linked via aria-describedby and Does Not Receive Focus
```typescript
test('tooltip role and aria-describedby wiring are correct, tooltip is not in tab order (ARIA APG Tooltip)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  const tooltips = page.locator('[role="tooltip"]');
  const tooltipCount = await tooltips.count();
  if (tooltipCount === 0) {
    console.warn('No role="tooltip" elements found; skipping ARIA APG tooltip wiring check');
    return;
  }

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(tooltipCount, 10); i++) {
    const tooltip = tooltips.nth(i);
    const tooltipId = await tooltip.getAttribute('id');

    expect(tooltipId, `Tooltip ${i + 1} lacks an id — cannot be referenced by aria-describedby`).toBeTruthy();

    if (tooltipId) {
      const triggers = page.locator(`[aria-describedby~="${tooltipId}"]`);
      expect(
        await triggers.count(),
        `Tooltip id="${tooltipId}" is not referenced by any element via aria-describedby`
      ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }

    // Tooltip must not be in the tab order
    const tabindex = await tooltip.getAttribute('tabindex');
    expect(
      tabindex,
      `Tooltip ${i + 1} has tabindex="${tabindex}" — tooltips must not receive keyboard focus; use a non-modal dialog for interactive content`
    ).not.toBe('0');

    // Tooltip must not use a natively focusable element tag
    const tooltipTag = await tooltip.evaluate(n => n.tagName.toLowerCase());
    const focusableTags = ['a', 'button', 'input', 'select', 'textarea'];
    expect(
      focusableTags,
      `Tooltip uses <${tooltipTag}> which is natively focusable — tooltips must use a non-interactive element like <div role="tooltip">`
    ).not.toContain(tooltipTag);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: The ARIA APG Tooltip pattern requires the trigger to reference the tooltip via `aria-describedby` (supplementary description, announced after accessible name) and prohibits the tooltip from receiving focus — if interactive content is needed inside the hovering container, the pattern mandates a non-modal dialog instead; this test checks that `aria-describedby` references match tooltip IDs but does not verify the tooltip is visible when the trigger is hovered or focused, which is the condition under which AT announces the description — a tooltip with correct wiring but `display:none` at all times will pass this test but provide no AT announcement; pair with a hover/focus visibility assertion to confirm the tooltip is shown to AT under the right trigger conditions.

**Pattern 469** — WCAG 3.2.1 On Focus — Verify That Receiving Focus Does Not Initiate a Context Change
```typescript
test('receiving focus on interactive elements does not trigger unexpected context changes (WCAG 3.2.1)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/navigation');

  const focusableEls = page.locator(
    'a[href], button:not([type="submit"]):not([aria-haspopup]), input[type="text"], input[type="search"], select'
  );
  const count = await focusableEls.count();
  const contextChanges: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 30); i++) {
    const el = focusableEls.nth(i);
    if (!(await el.isVisible())) continue;

    const urlBefore = page.url();
    const titleBefore = await page.title();

    await el.focus();
    await page.waitForTimeout(250);

    const urlAfter = page.url();
    const titleAfter = await page.title();

    if (urlAfter !== urlBefore) {
      const label = await el.getAttribute('aria-label') || await el.textContent() || await el.getAttribute('name') || `element ${i}`;
      contextChanges.push(`Focus on "${label.trim().slice(0, 40)}" navigated from ${urlBefore} to ${urlAfter}`);
      await page.goto(urlBefore);
    } else if (titleAfter !== titleBefore) {
      const label = await el.getAttribute('aria-label') || await el.textContent() || `element ${i}`;
      contextChanges.push(`Focus on "${label.trim().slice(0, 40)}" changed page title from "${titleBefore}" to "${titleAfter}"`);
    }
  }

  expect(
    contextChanges,
    `WCAG 3.2.1: Context changes triggered by focus:\n${contextChanges.join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 3.2.1 (A) prohibits context changes (navigation, focus shift, form submission, new window) triggered by focus alone — this test detects URL changes and title changes but cannot detect context changes that are single-page application view transitions where the URL stays the same while the main content area is replaced, nor can it detect focus being silently moved to a different element as a side effect; extend the test by capturing `document.activeElement` before and after focus events to catch focus-on-focus redirection, which is a common failure in custom megamenu implementations that move focus to the first menu item when the parent navigation item is focused rather than when it is activated.

**Pattern 470** — WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap — Verify That Focus Cannot Become Stranded Inside a Widget or Embedded Component
```typescript
test('keyboard focus cannot be trapped inside widgets or iframes (WCAG 2.1.2)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/embed-demo');

  const potentialTraps = page.locator('iframe, [contenteditable="true"], [role="grid"], [role="treegrid"], .ql-editor, .ProseMirror, .CodeMirror');
  const count = await potentialTraps.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 5); i++) {
    const trap = potentialTraps.nth(i);
    if (!(await trap.isVisible())) continue;

    const tag = await trap.evaluate(n => n.tagName.toLowerCase());

    if (tag === 'iframe') {
      await trap.focus();
      // Tab five times and verify focus eventually exits the iframe back to main frame
      for (let t = 0; t < 5; t++) {
        await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
      }
      const activeInMain = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.tagName !== 'IFRAME');
      expect(
        activeInMain,
        `WCAG 2.1.2: Focus may be trapped in iframe ${i + 1} — tabbing 5 times did not return focus to main frame`
      ).toBe(true);
    }

    // For contenteditable rich editors: Tab should exit, not insert a tab character
    if (await trap.getAttribute('contenteditable') === 'true') {
      await trap.focus();
      await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
      const focusLeftEditor = await trap.evaluate(n => document.activeElement !== n && !n.contains(document.activeElement));
      expect(
        focusLeftEditor,
        `WCAG 2.1.2: Tab key did not exit contenteditable editor — keyboard users are trapped; provide a documented Escape-based exit mechanism`
      ).toBe(true);
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.1.2 (A) allows focus containment when users are informed of the exit mechanism (e.g., "press Escape to exit the editor") — a rich text editor that uses Tab for indentation is permitted to trap Tab but must provide an alternative exit mechanism; this test tabs five times and checks whether focus exits, which will trigger a false positive on intentionally focus-managed editors like CodeMirror and ProseMirror that intercept Tab for indentation; scope the test to verify the editor's documented exit mechanism (usually Escape or a custom shortcut) rather than asserting Tab exits, and check that the exit instruction is programmatically announced when the editor gains focus.

**Pattern 471** — ARIA APG Switch Pattern — Verify role="switch" Uses aria-checked and Activates on Space Key
```typescript
test('switch widget uses role="switch" with aria-checked and toggles on Space key (ARIA APG Switch)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings/notifications');

  const switches = page.locator('[role="switch"]');
  const switchCount = await switches.count();
  expect(switchCount, 'No role="switch" elements found on notification settings page').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(switchCount, 5); i++) {
    const sw = switches.nth(i);
    await expect(sw, `Switch ${i + 1} is not visible`).toBeVisible();

    // aria-checked must be "true" or "false" — switches are binary, no "mixed" state
    const ariaChecked = await sw.getAttribute('aria-checked');
    expect(
      ['true', 'false'],
      `Switch ${i + 1} aria-checked="${ariaChecked}" — must be "true" or "false", not mixed or absent`
    ).toContain(ariaChecked);

    // Accessible name must exist
    const ariaLabel = await sw.getAttribute('aria-label');
    const ariaLabelledBy = await sw.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    const innerText = (await sw.textContent() || '').trim();
    expect(
      ariaLabel || ariaLabelledBy || innerText,
      `Switch ${i + 1} has no accessible name — requires aria-label, aria-labelledby, or inner text`
    ).toBeTruthy();

    // Activate with Space and verify state toggles
    await sw.focus();
    const stateBefore = await sw.getAttribute('aria-checked');
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
    await page.waitForTimeout(150);
    const stateAfter = await sw.getAttribute('aria-checked');

    const expectedAfter = stateBefore === 'true' ? 'false' : 'true';
    expect(
      stateAfter,
      `Switch ${i + 1} did not toggle aria-checked from "${stateBefore}" to "${expectedAfter}" on Space key`
    ).toBe(expectedAfter);

    // Restore original state
    await page.keyboard.press('Space');
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: The ARIA APG Switch pattern uses `role="switch"` with `aria-checked="true/false"` (binary only — no mixed state) and activates on Space, with Enter as an optional alternative — this diverges from `role="checkbox"` which uses `aria-checked` including "mixed" for tri-state; this test toggles each switch and immediately restores it, which produces a side-effect on notification settings that could trigger server-side emails or notifications during the test run; run this test in an environment with mocked API responses or a test account where notification side effects are acceptable, and add an `afterEach` teardown that restores notification defaults if server mutations cannot be avoided.

**Pattern 472** — WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose in Context — Verify Duplicate Link Text Points to Unique Destinations or Has Disambiguating Context
```typescript
test('links with identical visible text either share a destination or have disambiguating accessible names (WCAG 2.4.4)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/blog');

  const links = page.locator('a[href]');
  const count = await links.count();
  const linkMap = new Map<string, Set<string>>();

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const link = links.nth(i);
    if (!(await link.isVisible())) continue;

    // Build accessible name: aria-label > aria-labelledby text > inner text
    const ariaLabel = await link.getAttribute('aria-label');
    const ariaLabelledBy = await link.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
    let accessibleName = ariaLabel || '';

    if (!accessibleName && ariaLabelledBy) {
      const referenced = page.locator(`#${ariaLabelledBy}`);
      accessibleName = (await referenced.textContent() || '').trim();
    }
    if (!accessibleName) {
      accessibleName = (await link.textContent() || '').trim();
    }

    const href = await link.getAttribute('href') || '';
    const normalizedName = accessibleName.toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, ' ');
    const normalizedHref = href.split('?')[0];

    if (!linkMap.has(normalizedName)) linkMap.set(normalizedName, new Set());
    linkMap.get(normalizedName)!.add(normalizedHref);
  }

  // Flag names that map to multiple different destinations
  const ambiguous: string[] = [];
  for (const [name, destinations] of linkMap) {
    if (destinations.size > 1 && !['', '#', '/'].includes(name)) {
      ambiguous.push(`"${name}" -> ${[...destinations].join(', ')}`);
    }
  }

  expect(
    ambiguous,
    `WCAG 2.4.4: Same link text points to different destinations — add aria-label with destination context:\n${ambiguous.join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.4.4 (A) permits identical link text when links share the same destination or when context (enclosing paragraph, list item, table cell, or `aria-label`) disambiguates them — this test flags duplicate names with divergent hrefs but does not evaluate whether the surrounding context resolves ambiguity for a screen reader user; a page with 12 "Read more" links each inside a unique `<article>` element satisfies 2.4.4 because the list-item context is available programmatically, but this test will incorrectly flag it as a violation; filter false positives by checking whether the link's immediate parent block has unique text content that distinguishes each instance before reporting.

**Pattern 473** — WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast — Verify UI Component Boundaries Have 3:1 Contrast Against Adjacent Background
```typescript
test('form control boundaries meet 3:1 non-text contrast ratio against adjacent background (WCAG 1.4.11)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout/payment');

  const uiComponents = page.locator('input[type="text"], input[type="email"], input[type="tel"], select, textarea, input[type="checkbox"], input[type="radio"]');
  const count = await uiComponents.count();
  const lowContrastComponents: string[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(count, 15); i++) {
    const el = uiComponents.nth(i);
    if (!(await el.isVisible())) continue;

    const contrastInfo = await el.evaluate((node: Element) => {
      const style = getComputedStyle(node);
      const parentStyle = getComputedStyle(node.parentElement || document.body);
      return {
        borderColor: style.borderColor,
        borderWidth: style.borderTopWidth,
        backgroundColor: style.backgroundColor,
        parentBackground: parentStyle.backgroundColor,
        tagName: node.tagName.toLowerCase(),
        inputType: (node as HTMLInputElement).type || '',
      };
    });

    const borderWidth = parseFloat(contrastInfo.borderWidth);

    // Zero-width border means the component relies on background differentiation alone
    if (borderWidth === 0) {
      lowContrastComponents.push(
        `<${contrastInfo.tagName} type="${contrastInfo.inputType}"> — border-width is 0; component boundary may not meet 3:1 contrast (WCAG 1.4.11)`
      );
      continue;
    }

    // Flag transparent borders
    if (contrastInfo.borderColor === 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)' || contrastInfo.borderColor === 'transparent') {
      lowContrastComponents.push(
        `<${contrastInfo.tagName} type="${contrastInfo.inputType}"> — border-color is transparent; verify background-based boundary meets 3:1 contrast`
      );
    }
  }

  expect(
    lowContrastComponents,
    `WCAG 1.4.11: Components with invisible or missing boundaries — verify 3:1 non-text contrast manually:\n${lowContrastComponents.join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.4.11 (AA) requires that the visual indicator of a UI component (typically its border or background fill) has a 3:1 contrast ratio against the adjacent color — this test detects missing or zero-width borders as a proxy for contrast failure, but the actual contrast ratio requires color sampling and relative luminance calculation using the WCAG formula, which getComputedStyle alone cannot provide for anti-aliased or gradient borders; the definitive test is a manual check using the browser DevTools Accessibility panel or a tool like the Colour Contrast Analyser on the actual rendered screenshot, not getComputedStyle; use this test as a fast CI filter for obviously missing borders and escalate to manual review any component flagged.

**Pattern 474** — WCAG 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts — Verify Single-character Keyboard Shortcuts Can Be Remapped or Disabled
```typescript
test('single-character keyboard shortcuts can be turned off or remapped (WCAG 2.1.4)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/inbox');

  // Common single-character shortcut keys used in email/productivity UIs
  const singleCharKeys = ['j', 'k', 'n', 'p', 'r', 'e', 'd', 'c', 'g'];
  const triggeredShortcuts: string[] = [];
  const urlBefore = page.url();

  for (const key of singleCharKeys) {
    // Ensure focus is on a non-input element to trigger global shortcuts
    await page.locator('body').click({ position: { x: 200, y: 200 } });
    await page.waitForTimeout(100);

    // Watch for DOM mutations in main content area
    const contentArea = page.locator('main, [role="main"], #content, .content').first();
    const selectorToWatch = await contentArea.count() > 0 ? 'main' : 'body';

    const mutationObserved = page.evaluate((sel) => {
      return new Promise<boolean>(resolve => {
        const target = document.querySelector(sel) || document.body;
        const obs = new MutationObserver(() => { obs.disconnect(); resolve(true); });
        obs.observe(target, { childList: true, subtree: true });
        setTimeout(() => { obs.disconnect(); resolve(false); }, 350);
      });
    }, selectorToWatch);

    await page.keyboard.press(key);
    const mutated = await mutationObserved;
    if (mutated) triggeredShortcuts.push(key);

    if (page.url() !== urlBefore) {
      triggeredShortcuts.push(`${key} (caused navigation)`);
      await page.goto(urlBefore);
    }
  }

  if (triggeredShortcuts.length > 0) {
    const shortcutSettings = page.locator(
      '[href*="shortcut" i], [href*="keyboard" i], button:has-text("Shortcuts"), [aria-label*="shortcut" i]'
    );
    const settingsExist = await shortcutSettings.count() > 0 && await shortcutSettings.first().isVisible();

    expect(
      settingsExist,
      `WCAG 2.1.4: Single-character shortcuts detected (${triggeredShortcuts.join(', ')}) but no shortcut settings link found — users with speech input must be able to turn off or remap these`
    ).toBe(true);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.1.4 (A) requires that single-character shortcuts (letter, number, punctuation, or symbol with no modifier) can be turned off, remapped to a modifier+key combination, or are only active when a specific component has focus — this test uses a MutationObserver-based heuristic to detect DOM changes triggered by key presses, which will false-positive on any animation, lazy-load, or analytics event that coincidentally fires within 350ms of a keypress; reduce false positives by narrowing the observation scope to the main content region, snapshotting the focused element before and after, and comparing `aria-selected` or `aria-activedescendant` state changes as a more targeted shortcut-effect signal.

### Community Gotchas

**G306** — `aria-live="assertive"` on a container that persists in the DOM causes AT to re-announce its contents on every page navigation in single-page applications
Why this matters: `aria-live="assertive"` instructs AT to immediately interrupt the current announcement to read the region's content whenever the DOM text inside it changes. In single-page applications, a persistent notification container with `aria-live="assertive"` placed in a layout shell that persists across route changes will re-announce its last content every time the user navigates — because React, Vue, and Angular route transitions trigger DOM reconciliation that temporarily clears and re-inserts the container's text, making AT treat the re-insertion as a new assertive announcement. Users navigating between pages hear the previous error message or toast spoken over the new page's content unprompted. This is one of the most disorienting SPA accessibility patterns and is invisible to automated axe-core scans because the issue is temporal, not structural.
Fix: Move `aria-live` containers inside the route view component so they are mounted and unmounted with the route, not persisted across navigation. Alternatively, clear the live region content programmatically on each route change using a router `beforeEach` guard that sets the container's `textContent` to an empty string before injecting the new message, ensuring AT only hears the current route's announcements.

**G307** — Form inputs inside a `<table>` without `<th>` column headers lose their label association when AT reads the cell — `aria-labelledby` pointing to a `<td>` is not reliably announced as a column header by all AT
Why this matters: Data-entry grids frequently render form controls (text inputs, selects, checkboxes) inside `<td>` cells, relying on `<th>` column headers to provide the field label via table context. When the column headers are implemented as `<td>` elements with `role="columnheader"` (or no semantic role at all), AT in table-reading mode does not announce them as headers, so each input cell appears to have no label. JAWS and NVDA in "browse mode" and "forms mode" both derive input labels from associated `<label>` elements or `aria-labelledby`, not from table column positions, so the column-header-as-label technique only works when using native `<th scope="col">` markup combined with a proper table `<caption>` or `aria-label`. axe-core's `th-has-data-cells` rule checks the reverse (headers must have data cells) but does not flag inputs inside `<td>` cells that lack `<th>` column headers.
Fix: Add explicit `<th scope="col">` headers for every column in the grid table, or add `aria-labelledby` directly on each input referencing both the column header id and a row identifier id to form a compound label. For programmatically generated grids, the `headers` attribute on `<td>` elements provides the most explicit and AT-reliable column-header association: `<td headers="col-name row-3"><input ...></td>`.

**G308** — Custom `<select>`-replacement widgets built as `role="listbox"` fail WCAG 2.5.3 when the selected option's visible text diverges from the button's accessible name after selection
Why this matters: Custom select menus commonly render a toggle button displaying the currently selected option's text, with a `role="listbox"` popup containing `role="option"` children. When the option is selected, the button's visible text is updated, but many implementations also carry a static `aria-label` on the button from the initial placeholder state (e.g., `aria-label="Select country"`) that is never updated. After the user selects "Germany", the visible text reads "Germany" but the accessible name remains "Select country", violating WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name, A) because the accessible name no longer contains the visible text as a substring. Voice control users who say "click Germany" cannot activate the button because its accessible name is "Select country". axe-core's `label-content-name-mismatch` rule will flag this in static analysis but only on the initial render — a post-interaction scan is required to catch the post-selection divergence.
Fix: Either remove the `aria-label` from the toggle button entirely and rely solely on its visible text content (which automatically becomes the accessible name when no `aria-label` is present), or synchronize the `aria-label` with the displayed option text on every selection event: `button.setAttribute('aria-label', selectedOption.textContent)`.

**G309** — `prefers-reduced-motion` media query is respected in CSS but ignored in JavaScript-driven animations — WCAG 2.3.3 and user expectation require JS animations to honor the preference
Why this matters: Developers commonly add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` to CSS to disable transitions and animations for users who have enabled "Reduce Motion" in their OS accessibility settings. However, JavaScript-driven animations — created via the Web Animations API, GreenSock (GSAP), Framer Motion, or `setInterval`-based canvas animations — run independently of CSS media queries and will still play at full motion even when CSS animations are suppressed. Users who experience vestibular disorders, vertigo, or epilepsy triggers may have configured the OS preference specifically to avoid these animations; bypassing the preference through JS is a critical accessibility regression. WCAG 2.3.3 (AAA) addresses animation from interactions, but the preference should be honored as a best practice even at AA compliance targets per the WCAG Understanding document guidance.
Fix: Read the `prefers-reduced-motion` preference in JavaScript using `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` before starting any JS-driven animation, and either skip the animation, use an instantaneous alternative, or halve the duration. Register a change listener with `matchMedia.addEventListener('change', ...)` to respond dynamically if the user toggles the setting while the page is open.

**G310** — `role="presentation"` and `role="none"` on a table remove the table's semantic structure from the accessibility tree, but child `<th>` and `<td>` elements may retain their roles in some AT — producing orphaned header and data cell announcements with no table context
Why this matters: To suppress AT from reading layout tables as data structures, developers add `role="presentation"` or `role="none"` to the `<table>` element. The ARIA specification defines that `role="presentation"` is inherited by required-owned children — `<tr>`, `<td>`, `<th>` — removing their native roles from the accessibility tree in compliant AT. However, Firefox + NVDA and older versions of JAWS do not fully propagate the presentation role to child elements, leaving `<th>` cells announced as "column header" with no table context, creating a disorienting stream of unstructured header announcements. The bug is particularly common with layout tables used for email-style multi-column forms. The axe-core rules `table-duplicate-name` and `td-headers-attr` do not fire for `role="none"` tables because the table is logically absent from the tree.
Fix: Replace layout tables with CSS Grid or Flexbox to eliminate the semantic ambiguity entirely. If a layout table must be kept, audit AT behavior in Firefox + NVDA and JAWS 2023+ specifically to confirm child role suppression is working — do not rely solely on Chrome + NVDA which has historically had more consistent presentation-role inheritance. As a belt-and-suspenders measure, add `role="none"` to every `<tr>`, `<td>`, and `<th>` child explicitly rather than relying on inheritance.
