## Cycle 67 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 475** — WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast Minimum — Programmatic Luminance Calculation for Dynamic Text on Gradient Backgrounds
```typescript
test('text on gradient backgrounds meets 4.5:1 contrast minimum (WCAG 1.4.3)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/hero-section');

  // Use axe-core to catch bulk contrast violations first
  const { AxeBuilder } = await import('@axe-core/playwright');
  const axeResults = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .withTags(['wcag2aa'])
    .analyze();

  const contrastViolations = axeResults.violations.filter(v => v.id === 'color-contrast');
  if (contrastViolations.length > 0) {
    const nodes = contrastViolations.flatMap(v => v.nodes.map(n => n.target.join(' ')));
    expect.soft(contrastViolations, `Color contrast violations:\n${nodes.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
  }

  // For gradient backgrounds, axe-core computes contrast against a single color sample point.
  // Manually check text that sits at the light end of a gradient.
  const heroText = page.locator('.hero h1, .hero-title, [class*="hero"] h1').first();
  if (await heroText.count() > 0) {
    const contrastInfo = await heroText.evaluate((el: HTMLElement) => {
      const style = getComputedStyle(el);
      const bg = getComputedStyle(el.closest('[class*="hero"]') ?? el).background;
      return { color: style.color, background: bg, fontSize: style.fontSize, fontWeight: style.fontWeight };
    });
    // If background is a gradient, flag for manual verification
    if (contrastInfo.background.includes('gradient')) {
      console.warn(`Manual contrast check required: hero text color "${contrastInfo.color}" sits on a gradient background — axe-core may have sampled only the darkest color; verify contrast at the lightest gradient point`);
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.4.3 (Contrast Minimum, AA) requires at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio for normal text and 3:1 for large text (18pt or 14pt bold) against the background color — axe-core computes contrast by sampling the background color at a single point beneath the text's bounding box, which means text overlaid on a gradient will only be tested against the sampled color and not against the full gradient range; a gradient that is dark purple at left and light yellow at right may pass axe-core if the sample hits the dark end, while the same text drawn over the light end of the gradient fails 4.5:1; this test logs a manual verification warning when a gradient background is detected but cannot automate the full gradient sweep without iterating pixel coordinates.

**Pattern 476** — WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order — Tab Order Matches Logical Reading Order via Bounding-Rect Comparison
```typescript
test('tab order follows top-to-bottom, left-to-right reading order (WCAG 2.4.3)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Record every element that receives focus as we Tab through the page
  const focusSequence: Array<{ tag: string; id: string; y: number; x: number }> = [];
  const maxTabs = 30;

  for (let i = 0; i < maxTabs; i++) {
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const info = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
      if (!el || el === document.body) return null;
      const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      return { tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(), id: el.id, y: Math.round(rect.top), x: Math.round(rect.left) };
    });
    if (!info) break;
    // Stop if we looped back to the first element
    if (focusSequence.length > 1 && info.y === focusSequence[0].y && info.x === focusSequence[0].x) break;
    focusSequence.push(info);
  }

  expect(focusSequence.length, 'No focusable elements found on the page').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Detect order inversions: a later Tab stop that is visually above and to the left of the previous one
  const inversions: string[] = [];
  for (let i = 1; i < focusSequence.length; i++) {
    const prev = focusSequence[i - 1];
    const curr = focusSequence[i];
    // Allow 20px vertical tolerance (same visual row)
    const sameRow = Math.abs(curr.y - prev.y) < 20;
    if (sameRow && curr.x < prev.x - 10) {
      inversions.push(`Tab ${i}: <${prev.tag}#${prev.id}> (x=${prev.x}) → <${curr.tag}#${curr.id}> (x=${curr.x}) — right-to-left jump on same row`);
    } else if (!sameRow && curr.y < prev.y - 20) {
      inversions.push(`Tab ${i}: <${prev.tag}#${prev.id}> (y=${prev.y}) → <${curr.tag}#${curr.id}> (y=${curr.y}) — upward focus jump`);
    }
  }
  expect(inversions, `Tab order inversions detected:\n${inversions.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order, A) requires that if a web page can be navigated sequentially and the navigation sequences affect meaning or operation, focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability — this test uses bounding-rect Y/X coordinates to detect upward and right-to-left focus jumps, which identifies the most common focus order violations caused by CSS `order`, `position: absolute`, and `float`; however, it does not detect logical order errors where Tab moves forward-sequentially in the DOM but the visual layout places unrelated groups of controls interleaved, which requires manual inspection of the focus sequence against the page's information architecture.

**Pattern 477** — WCAG 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics — Verify Instructions Do Not Rely on Shape, Color, or Position Alone
```typescript
test('instructions reference controls by name, not solely by shape, color, or position (WCAG 1.3.3)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/onboarding');

  // Collect all visible instruction text: paragraphs, list items, labels, headings
  const instructionText = await page.locator('p, li, label, h1, h2, h3, h4, [role="note"]').allInnerTexts();
  const combined = instructionText.join(' ').toLowerCase();

  // Patterns that indicate sole reliance on sensory characteristics
  const positionOnlyPatterns = [
    /click the button (on the right|on the left|above|below)/i,
    /use the (red|green|blue|yellow) button/i,
    /press the (round|square|circular) icon/i,
    /the (top|bottom|left|right) link/i,
  ];

  const violations: string[] = [];
  for (const pattern of positionOnlyPatterns) {
    const match = combined.match(pattern);
    if (match) {
      violations.push(`Sensory-only instruction detected: "${match[0]}" — WCAG 1.3.3 requires a textual name or label, not just shape/color/position`);
    }
  }

  expect(violations, `Sensory characteristic violations:\n${violations.join('\n')}`).toHaveLength(0);

  // Additionally check that form error messages identify the field by name, not just position
  const errorMessages = page.locator('[role="alert"], .error, [aria-live="assertive"]');
  const errorCount = await errorMessages.count();
  for (let i = 0; i < errorCount; i++) {
    const errorText = await errorMessages.nth(i).innerText();
    const positionOnly = /^(above|below|to the (left|right)|the (first|second|third)) field/i.test(errorText);
    expect(
      positionOnly,
      `Error message "${errorText}" uses position-only reference — WCAG 1.3.3 requires identifying the field by its label name`
    ).toBe(false);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.3.3 (Sensory Characteristics, A) requires that instructions for understanding and operating content do not rely solely on sensory characteristics of components such as shape, color, size, visual location, orientation, or sound — this test uses regex pattern matching against visible text to detect common positional phrasings, but its effectiveness is limited to the patterns enumerated; instructions phrased as "click the arrow icon" or "select the highlighted option" also violate 1.3.3 but are not caught by the current patterns; expand the pattern list incrementally as new violations are found during manual review.

**Pattern 478** — WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable — Verify Session Timeout Warning Appears Before Expiry and Can Be Extended
```typescript
test('session timeout warning appears with sufficient time to extend and announces via aria-live (WCAG 2.2.1)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Inject a shortened timeout warning to test the mechanism without waiting
  // Most apps expose a session timeout config — alternatively, mock the timer
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    // Simulate what the app would do: show a timeout modal with a countdown
    const mockWarning = document.createElement('div');
    mockWarning.setAttribute('role', 'alertdialog');
    mockWarning.setAttribute('aria-labelledby', 'timeout-title');
    mockWarning.setAttribute('aria-describedby', 'timeout-desc');
    mockWarning.id = 'session-timeout-warning';
    mockWarning.innerHTML = `
      <h2 id="timeout-title">Session Expiring Soon</h2>
      <p id="timeout-desc">Your session will expire in <span id="countdown">60</span> seconds.</p>
      <button id="extend-session">Extend Session</button>
      <button id="logout-now">Log Out Now</button>
    `;
    document.body.appendChild(mockWarning);
  });

  const warningDialog = page.locator('#session-timeout-warning');
  await expect(warningDialog).toBeVisible();

  // Warning must be an alertdialog with an accessible name
  await expect(warningDialog).toHaveAttribute('role', 'alertdialog');
  const labelId = await warningDialog.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
  expect(labelId, 'Timeout warning must have aria-labelledby').not.toBeNull();

  // Must have an "extend session" mechanism
  const extendButton = warningDialog.locator('button:has-text("Extend"), button:has-text("Continue"), button:has-text("Keep")');
  await expect(extendButton.first(), 'Timeout warning must include a button to extend the session (WCAG 2.2.1)').toBeVisible();

  // Activating extend must dismiss the warning
  await extendButton.first().click();
  await expect(warningDialog).not.toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.2.1 (Timing Adjustable, A) requires that for any time limit set by the content, users must be able to turn off, adjust, or extend the time limit — the testing challenge is that session timeouts are typically 15-30 minutes and cannot be waited out in a test suite; this test injects a mock warning dialog to verify the warning mechanism's ARIA structure and extend button, but it does not verify that the real application shows the warning with sufficient advance notice (WCAG requires at least 20 seconds to respond) or that the server-side session is actually extended when the button is clicked; supplement with a backend integration test that calls the session-extend endpoint and verifies the session expiry timestamp is updated.

**Pattern 479** — WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text — Verify Layout Integrity at 200% Browser Zoom (Not Text-Only Zoom)
```typescript
test('page layout remains functional and no content is clipped at 200% browser zoom (WCAG 1.4.4)', async ({ page }) => {
  // Set viewport to simulate 200% zoom effect: halve the logical viewport
  // 1280x720 at 200% zoom behaves like 640x360 logical pixels
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 640, height: 360 });
  await page.goto('/home');

  // No horizontal scrollbar should appear at 200% zoom
  const hasHorizontalScroll = await page.evaluate(() =>
    document.documentElement.scrollWidth > document.documentElement.clientWidth
  );
  expect(hasHorizontalScroll, 'Horizontal scrollbar appears at 200% zoom (640px viewport) — WCAG 1.4.4 requires no horizontal scroll at 200% zoom in a maximized browser').toBe(false);

  // All primary navigation links must still be visible (not hidden by overflow:hidden)
  const navLinks = page.locator('nav a').first();
  if (await navLinks.count() > 0) {
    await expect(navLinks).toBeVisible();
  }

  // Form elements must not overflow their containers
  const inputs = page.locator('input[type="text"], input[type="email"], textarea');
  const inputCount = await inputs.count();
  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(inputCount, 5); i++) {
    const box = await inputs.nth(i).boundingBox();
    expect(box, `Input ${i} has no bounding box at 200% zoom — may be clipped`).not.toBeNull();
    expect(box!.width, `Input ${i} is excessively wide at 200% zoom, causing overflow`).toBeLessThan(700);
  }

  // Headings must not be cut off
  const h1 = page.locator('h1').first();
  if (await h1.count() > 0) {
    const h1Text = await h1.innerText();
    expect(h1Text.trim().length, 'h1 heading is empty at 200% zoom — text may be hidden by overflow').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text, AA) requires that text can be resized up to 200% without loss of content or functionality — this test simulates 200% zoom by halving the viewport to 640x360 px, which approximates the logical pixel space available at 200% zoom in a 1280x720 window; however, some layout bugs only manifest at the actual 200% browser zoom level (where CSS pixels are doubled but the viewport reports a narrower logical width) rather than a halved viewport — the distinction matters for `min-width` media query breakpoints that may trigger at 640 px but not at native 200% zoom; supplement with Playwright's `--scale-factor 2` browser launch option or a real-device zoom test.

**Pattern 480** — ARIA Listbox — Verify Type-Ahead Selection and `aria-selected` State Updates
```typescript
test('listbox supports type-ahead character navigation and aria-selected updates (ARIA APG)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/country-selector');

  const listbox = page.locator('[role="listbox"]').first();
  await expect(listbox).toBeVisible();
  await listbox.focus();

  // Verify the listbox has at least one option
  const options = listbox.locator('[role="option"]');
  const optionCount = await options.count();
  expect(optionCount, 'Listbox must have at least one option').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Verify initial state: exactly one option has aria-selected="true" OR none do (for unselected listbox)
  const selectedOptions = listbox.locator('[role="option"][aria-selected="true"]');
  const selectedCount = await selectedOptions.count();
  expect(selectedCount, 'Listbox must have at most one option selected initially').toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);

  // Type-ahead: press "C" to jump to the first option starting with C
  await page.keyboard.press('KeyC');
  const focusedOption = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.textContent?.trim() ?? '');
  if (focusedOption) {
    expect(
      focusedOption.toLowerCase().startsWith('c'),
      `Type-ahead: pressing "C" should focus first option starting with C, but focused "${focusedOption}"`
    ).toBe(true);
  }

  // Press Enter or Space to select the focused option
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

  // The selected option must now have aria-selected="true"
  const nowSelected = await page.evaluate(() =>
    document.querySelector('[role="listbox"] [role="option"][aria-selected="true"]')?.textContent?.trim()
  );
  expect(nowSelected, 'After Enter, the focused option must have aria-selected="true"').not.toBeNull();
});
```
Tradeoff: The ARIA APG Listbox pattern requires type-ahead navigation where pressing a character moves focus to the next option starting with that character — this test verifies type-ahead by pressing "C" and checking that focus lands on an option starting with "C", but it will produce a false pass if the listbox happens to have no options starting with "C" (focusedOption will be empty and the assertion is skipped); add a pre-condition that reads the first character of the first option and types that character, then asserts focus is on an option with that initial character — this is resilient regardless of the option list content.

**Pattern 481** — WCAG 3.3.3 Error Suggestion — Verify Validation Errors Include Specific Fix Guidance
```typescript
test('form validation errors include specific fix suggestions, not just "invalid input" (WCAG 3.3.3)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/registration');

  // Deliberately submit the form with invalid data
  await page.locator('input[type="email"]').fill('not-an-email');
  await page.locator('input[type="password"]').fill('abc'); // too short
  await page.locator('button[type="submit"]').click();

  // Wait for validation errors to appear
  await page.waitForSelector('[role="alert"], .error-message, [aria-live="assertive"]', { timeout: 3000 })
    .catch(() => {});

  // Collect all error messages
  const errorElements = page.locator('[role="alert"], .field-error, [aria-describedby] + .error, [aria-errormessage]');
  const errorCount = await errorElements.count();
  expect(errorCount, 'No error messages appeared after submitting invalid form data').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Each error message must contain specific guidance, not just "invalid" or "error"
  for (let i = 0; i < errorCount; i++) {
    const errorText = await errorElements.nth(i).innerText();
    const isTooVague = /^(invalid|error|required|wrong|incorrect)\.*$/i.test(errorText.trim());
    expect(
      isTooVague,
      `Error message "${errorText}" is too vague — WCAG 3.3.3 requires specific suggestions, e.g., "Enter a valid email address like name@example.com"`
    ).toBe(false);
    // Verify the error message has meaningful length (at least 20 chars for a suggestion)
    expect(
      errorText.trim().length,
      `Error message at index ${i} is too short to contain actionable guidance: "${errorText}"`
    ).toBeGreaterThan(15);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 3.3.3 (Error Suggestion, AA) requires that if an input error is automatically detected and suggestions for correction are known, the suggestion is provided to the user — this test catches single-word vague errors by checking that error text is longer than 15 characters and does not match a short generic pattern, but it cannot evaluate the semantic quality of the suggestion text; an error message "This field is required." is 25 characters and passes the length check but provides no fix guidance; supplement with a manual review of each error template and a label-content audit ensuring every error references the field's expected format.

**Pattern 482** — WCAG 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures — Verify Swipe-Based Carousels Have Single-Pointer Button Alternatives
```typescript
test('carousel swipe gesture has single-pointer prev/next button alternatives (WCAG 2.5.1)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/marketing-carousel');

  // Locate the carousel
  const carousel = page.locator('[role="region"][aria-roledescription="carousel"], [aria-label*="carousel" i]').first();
  if (await carousel.count() === 0) {
    test.skip(); // No carousel on this page
    return;
  }
  await expect(carousel).toBeVisible();

  // WCAG 2.5.1: multipoint gestures (swipe) must have single-pointer alternatives
  // Verify there are Previous and Next buttons
  const prevButton = carousel.locator('button[aria-label*="previous" i], button[aria-label*="prev" i], button[aria-label*="back" i]');
  const nextButton = carousel.locator('button[aria-label*="next" i], button[aria-label*="forward" i]');
  await expect(prevButton.first(), 'Carousel must have a single-pointer Previous button as an alternative to swipe (WCAG 2.5.1)').toBeVisible();
  await expect(nextButton.first(), 'Carousel must have a single-pointer Next button as an alternative to swipe (WCAG 2.5.1)').toBeVisible();

  // Clicking Next must advance the carousel to a different slide
  const firstSlide = await carousel.locator('[role="group"], [aria-label*="slide" i]').first().getAttribute('aria-label');
  await nextButton.first().click();
  await page.waitForTimeout(500); // allow transition
  const secondSlide = await carousel.locator('[role="group"], [aria-label*="slide" i]').first().getAttribute('aria-label');
  expect(secondSlide, 'Clicking Next must change the active slide').not.toBe(firstSlide);
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.5.1 (Pointer Gestures, A) requires that all functionality using multipoint or path-based gestures (e.g., swipe, pinch-zoom) can be operated with a single pointer without requiring a path — carousels that rely solely on touch swipe gestures with no prev/next buttons fail this criterion for keyboard and single-switch users; this test verifies buttons exist and function, but it does not test whether the swipe gesture itself is still operational after the buttons are added, nor does it verify that the button labels are sufficiently descriptive for screen reader users who need to understand what "Previous" and "Next" navigate to — add aria-label="Previous slide" or aria-label="Next: [slide title]" to provide context.

**Pattern 483** — WCAG 1.2.1 Audio-Only and Video-Only — Verify Pre-Recorded Audio Has a Transcript
```typescript
test('pre-recorded audio-only content has an accessible transcript (WCAG 1.2.1)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/podcast-episode');

  // Find audio elements on the page
  const audioElements = page.locator('audio');
  const audioCount = await audioElements.count();
  if (audioCount === 0) {
    test.skip(); // No audio on this page
    return;
  }

  for (let i = 0; i < audioCount; i++) {
    const audio = audioElements.nth(i);
    await expect(audio).toBeVisible();

    // Method 1: A <track kind="descriptions"> or a transcript link near the audio element
    const trackElement = audio.locator('track[kind="descriptions"], track[kind="subtitles"]');
    const hasTrack = await trackElement.count() > 0;

    // Method 2: A nearby transcript link within a reasonable DOM proximity
    const parent = audio.locator('xpath=ancestor::section | ancestor::article | ancestor::div[contains(@class,"player")]').first();
    const transcriptLink = parent.locator('a:has-text("transcript"), a:has-text("Transcript"), [aria-label*="transcript" i]');
    const hasTranscriptLink = await transcriptLink.count() > 0;

    expect(
      hasTrack || hasTranscriptLink,
      `Audio element ${i} has no associated transcript — WCAG 1.2.1 requires a text alternative (transcript) for pre-recorded audio-only content`
    ).toBe(true);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.2.1 (Audio-only and Video-only, A) requires that pre-recorded audio-only content has either a text transcript or a text alternative — this test checks for the presence of a `<track>` element or a nearby transcript link in the DOM, which is a structural heuristic rather than a semantic guarantee; a transcript link that is present but points to a 404 page or a page with empty content would still pass this test; supplement with a link-checker that verifies transcript URLs resolve to non-empty pages, and with a content audit that confirms the transcript covers all spoken content including speaker identification and relevant non-speech audio.

**Pattern 484** — WCAG 2.4.2 Page Titled — Verify SPA Route Changes Update `document.title`
```typescript
test('SPA route changes update document.title with a descriptive, unique page title (WCAG 2.4.2)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');
  const homeTitle = await page.title();
  expect(homeTitle.trim().length, 'Homepage must have a non-empty document title (WCAG 2.4.2)').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Navigate to another route via client-side navigation
  await page.locator('nav a').nth(1).click();
  await page.waitForTimeout(500); // allow SPA router to update

  const secondPageTitle = await page.title();
  expect(secondPageTitle.trim().length, 'Second page must have a non-empty document title').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(
    secondPageTitle,
    'SPA route change must update document.title — identical titles on different pages violate WCAG 2.4.2 and prevent AT users from orienting themselves'
  ).not.toBe(homeTitle);

  // Navigate to a third route
  await page.locator('nav a').nth(2).click();
  await page.waitForTimeout(500);
  const thirdPageTitle = await page.title();
  expect(thirdPageTitle.trim().length, 'Third page must have a non-empty document title').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(thirdPageTitle, 'Third page title must differ from both homepage and second page title').not.toBe(homeTitle);
  expect(thirdPageTitle, 'Third page title must differ from second page title').not.toBe(secondPageTitle);

  // Titles should contain the site name as a consistent suffix (best practice)
  const siteName = homeTitle.split(/[-|—]/).pop()?.trim() ?? '';
  if (siteName.length > 2) {
    expect(secondPageTitle, `Second page title should contain the site name "${siteName}"`).toContain(siteName);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.4.2 (Page Titled, A) requires that web pages have titles that describe their topic or purpose — SPA frameworks that update view content via JavaScript router without updating `document.title` are a common source of this failure; screen readers announce `document.title` to users when a page loads, and in SPAs this happens only once (initial load) unless `document.title` is explicitly updated on each route change; this test detects title stagnation by asserting uniqueness across three routes, but it cannot verify that the title update fires synchronously with the route change — if title update is delayed, AT may announce the old title before the new one is set; use Playwright's `page.waitForFunction(() => document.title !== oldTitle)` to wait for the update rather than a fixed timeout.

**Pattern 485** — WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships — Verify Required Field Indicators Are Programmatically Determinable
```typescript
test('required form fields use aria-required and visual indicator is not color-alone (WCAG 1.3.1)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/application-form');

  // Find all required fields — both natively required and ARIA required
  const requiredInputs = page.locator('input[required], input[aria-required="true"], select[required], textarea[required], select[aria-required="true"], textarea[aria-required="true"]');
  const requiredCount = await requiredInputs.count();
  expect(requiredCount, 'Application form must have at least one required field').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  for (let i = 0; i < requiredCount; i++) {
    const input = requiredInputs.nth(i);
    const id = await input.getAttribute('id');
    const ariaRequired = await input.getAttribute('aria-required');
    const nativeRequired = await input.getAttribute('required');

    // Must have programmatic required indicator (WCAG 1.3.1)
    expect(
      ariaRequired === 'true' || nativeRequired !== null,
      `Required field ${id ?? i} has no programmatic required indicator — use required or aria-required="true" (WCAG 1.3.1)`
    ).toBe(true);

    // Find the associated label and verify it visually indicates required (asterisk, text)
    if (id) {
      const label = page.locator(`label[for="${id}"]`);
      if (await label.count() > 0) {
        const labelText = await label.innerText();
        const hasVisualIndicator = labelText.includes('*') || labelText.toLowerCase().includes('required');
        expect.soft(
          hasVisualIndicator,
          `Label for required field "${id}" has no visual indicator (asterisk or "required" text) — WCAG 1.3.3 also requires non-color-alone indication`
        ).toBe(true);
      }
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships, A) requires that information conveyed through visual presentation — including required field status — is programmatically determinable; using only a red asterisk (*) without accessible text ("* indicates required" in a legend or visible label) violates 1.3.1 because the asterisk's meaning is conveyed by convention and color, not programmatic semantics; this test verifies programmatic required attributes and checks for an asterisk or "required" text in the label, but it does not verify that a legend explaining the asterisk convention is present on the form — without the legend, low-literacy users and AT users who do not encounter the convention may not understand the indicator.

**Pattern 486** — WCAG 2.5.4 Motion Actuation — Verify Device-Motion-Activated Features Have UI Alternatives
```typescript
test('device motion features (shake to undo) have an accessible UI alternative (WCAG 2.5.4)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/drawing-canvas');

  // Detect if the page registers devicemotion or deviceorientation event listeners
  const hasMotionListeners = await page.evaluate(() => {
    // Intercept addEventListener to detect motion listeners
    const originalAdd = EventTarget.prototype.addEventListener;
    let motionListenerRegistered = false;
    EventTarget.prototype.addEventListener = function(type, ...args) {
      if (type === 'devicemotion' || type === 'deviceorientation') {
        motionListenerRegistered = true;
      }
      return originalAdd.call(this, type, ...args);
    };
    // Re-run any inline scripts — this is a best-effort detection
    // Return current registration status
    return motionListenerRegistered;
  });

  if (hasMotionListeners) {
    // If device motion is used, there must be a UI button alternative (WCAG 2.5.4)
    const undoButton = page.locator('button:has-text("Undo"), button[aria-label*="undo" i], button[title*="undo" i]');
    const shakeAlternative = page.locator('[aria-label*="shake" i], button:has-text("Reset"), button:has-text("Clear")');
    const hasUIAlternative = (await undoButton.count() > 0) || (await shakeAlternative.count() > 0);
    expect(
      hasUIAlternative,
      'Device motion event listener detected — WCAG 2.5.4 requires a UI button alternative for shake-to-undo or tilt-to-rotate functionality'
    ).toBe(true);
  } else {
    // Verify no motion-only interactions exist in the page's documented help text
    const helpText = await page.locator('[aria-label*="help" i], [class*="tooltip"], details').allInnerTexts();
    const mentionsShake = helpText.some(t => /shake|tilt|motion|accelerom/i.test(t));
    if (mentionsShake) {
      const undoButton = page.locator('button:has-text("Undo"), button[aria-label*="undo" i]');
      expect(await undoButton.count(), 'Motion-actuation mentioned in help text — must have a UI button alternative (WCAG 2.5.4)').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.5.4 (Motion Actuation, A) requires that functionality triggered by device motion or user motion can also be operated through user interface components and can be disabled to prevent accidental actuation — this test attempts to intercept addEventListener calls to detect devicemotion listeners, but the interception runs before the page's own event registration only if injected at document_start (use Playwright's addInitScript); event listeners added via third-party libraries may be registered under obfuscated event names; the most reliable approach is to request the development team to annotate motion-actuated features with data-motion-feature attributes and test for matching UI controls.

**Pattern 487** — WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value — Verify Custom Toggle Switches Expose Correct Role and State
```typescript
test('custom toggle switch exposes role="switch" and aria-checked state (WCAG 4.1.2)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings/notifications');

  // Find toggle switches — both native checkboxes styled as toggles and custom ARIA switches
  const switches = page.locator('[role="switch"], input[type="checkbox"][class*="toggle" i], input[type="checkbox"][aria-label*="toggle" i]');
  const switchCount = await switches.count();
  if (switchCount === 0) {
    test.skip(); // No toggle switches on this page
    return;
  }

  for (let i = 0; i < switchCount; i++) {
    const sw = switches.nth(i);
    const role = await sw.getAttribute('role');

    if (role === 'switch') {
      // Custom switch: must have aria-checked
      const ariaChecked = await sw.getAttribute('aria-checked');
      expect(
        ariaChecked === 'true' || ariaChecked === 'false',
        `Custom switch ${i} has invalid or missing aria-checked="${ariaChecked}" — WCAG 4.1.2 requires aria-checked to be "true" or "false"`
      ).toBe(true);

      // Must have an accessible name
      const name = await sw.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? await sw.getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
      expect(name, `Custom switch ${i} has no accessible name — add aria-label or aria-labelledby`).not.toBeNull();

      // Toggle the switch and verify aria-checked changes
      const checkedBefore = ariaChecked;
      await sw.click();
      const checkedAfter = await sw.getAttribute('aria-checked');
      expect(checkedAfter, `After clicking, aria-checked must toggle from "${checkedBefore}" to "${checkedBefore === 'true' ? 'false' : 'true'}"`).toBe(checkedBefore === 'true' ? 'false' : 'true');
    } else {
      // Native checkbox: must have a visible label
      const id = await sw.getAttribute('id');
      if (id) {
        const label = page.locator(`label[for="${id}"]`);
        expect(await label.count(), `Native checkbox toggle ${i} has no associated label`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      }
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value, Level A) requires that all user interface components have accessible names, roles, and states — toggle switches designed with CSS that repurpose `<input type="checkbox">` as a visual toggle do not need `role="switch"` because their native checkbox role accurately communicates the binary on/off state; however, custom `<div>` or `<span>` toggle switches that use `role="switch"` must maintain `aria-checked` in sync with the visual state on every toggle; this test detects the common bug where `aria-checked` is set to its initial value but never updated when the switch is clicked because the click handler updates only a CSS class and forgets to update the ARIA attribute.

**Pattern 488** — WCAG 2.4.10 Section Headings — Verify Content Sections Are Organized With Accessible Headings
```typescript
test('major content sections use heading elements to organize structure (WCAG 2.4.10 AAA)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/product-listing');

  // Collect all headings and their levels on the page
  const headings = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const els = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, [role="heading"]'));
    return els.map(el => ({
      tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
      level: el.getAttribute('aria-level') ?? el.tagName.replace('H', ''),
      text: el.textContent?.trim().slice(0, 60) ?? '',
      visible: (el as HTMLElement).offsetParent !== null,
    }));
  });

  // Page must have at least one heading
  expect(headings.length, 'Page has no heading elements — WCAG 2.4.10 requires sections to be organized with headings').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Page must have exactly one h1
  const h1Count = headings.filter(h => h.tag === 'h1' || h.level === '1').length;
  expect(h1Count, 'Page must have exactly one h1 heading').toBe(1);

  // Heading levels must not skip (e.g., h1 → h3 without h2)
  const visibleHeadings = headings.filter(h => h.visible);
  for (let i = 1; i < visibleHeadings.length; i++) {
    const prevLevel = parseInt(visibleHeadings[i - 1].level, 10);
    const currLevel = parseInt(visibleHeadings[i].level, 10);
    if (currLevel > prevLevel) {
      expect(
        currLevel - prevLevel,
        `Heading level skipped: h${prevLevel} ("${visibleHeadings[i - 1].text}") → h${currLevel} ("${visibleHeadings[i].text}") — heading levels must increment by 1 only`
      ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 2.4.10 (Section Headings, AAA) requires that section headings are used to organize content — the AAA level means it is not required for conformance but is a strong best practice; the level-skip detection in this test will produce false positives for valid structural patterns like a page where a sidebar begins with an h3 that is semantically under the h1 but not under any h2 in the main content flow; use `aria-level` to assign logical heading levels in components rendered outside the main content flow, and consider excluding sidebar/aside elements from the level-skip check by scoping the heading query to `main` rather than the full document.

**Pattern 489** — WCAG 3.1.1 Language of Page — Verify `lang` Attribute Is Present and Contains a Valid BCP 47 Tag
```typescript
test('html element has a valid lang attribute identifying the primary language (WCAG 3.1.1)', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  // WCAG 3.1.1: the default language of the page must be programmatically determinable
  const htmlLang = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.lang);
  expect(htmlLang, 'html element must have a lang attribute — WCAG 3.1.1 requires the page language to be programmatically determinable').toBeTruthy();
  expect(htmlLang.trim().length, 'lang attribute must not be empty').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Validate BCP 47 format: at least a 2-letter primary language subtag
  const validLangPattern = /^[a-zA-Z]{2,3}(-[a-zA-Z0-9]{2,8})*$/;
  expect(
    validLangPattern.test(htmlLang.trim()),
    `lang="${htmlLang}" does not match BCP 47 format (e.g., "en", "en-US", "fr-CA") — invalid lang values are ignored by AT, making the language undetermined`
  ).toBe(true);

  // Check all iframes also have a lang attribute or inherit correctly
  const iframes = page.locator('iframe');
  const iframeCount = await iframes.count();
  for (let i = 0; i < iframeCount; i++) {
    const iframeEl = iframes.nth(i);
    try {
      const iframeFrame = await iframeEl.contentFrame();
      if (iframeFrame) {
        const iframeLang = await iframeFrame.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.lang);
        // Iframes should specify their own lang; absence is not a blocker if same-language app
        if (!iframeLang) {
          console.warn(`iframe ${i} does not have a lang attribute — if it contains non-primary-language content, add lang attribute`);
        }
      }
    } catch {
      // Cross-origin iframes are not accessible — skip
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: WCAG 3.1.1 (Language of Page, A) requires that the default human language of each web page can be programmatically determined — AT uses the `lang` attribute to select the correct pronunciation rules, dictionary, and voice for text-to-speech; a missing `lang` attribute causes AT to fall back to the user's system language, which may be incorrect for multilingual users; this test validates BCP 47 format with a permissive regex but does not verify that the language tag accurately describes the page's actual primary language content — a page with `lang="en"` that contains primarily French text violates the spirit of 3.1.1 even though the attribute is syntactically valid; combine with a human language detection library or a manual content review to validate correctness.

### Community Gotchas

**G311** — `aria-activedescendant` requires the referenced element to be a DOM descendant of the element with `aria-activedescendant` — referencing an element outside the composite widget causes AT to ignore the active descendant and announce nothing
Why this matters: `aria-activedescendant` is the focus-management alternative to moving DOM focus inside a composite widget (listbox, tree, grid) — it allows the container element (e.g., a combobox input) to retain DOM focus while AT reads the "active" descendant element. The ARIA specification requires that the element referenced by `aria-activedescendant` must be owned by the element with the attribute (either a DOM descendant or owned via `aria-owns`). Developers who render the dropdown popup as a direct child of `<body>` (for z-index stacking reasons) and reference it via `aria-activedescendant` from an `<input>` in the header create a cross-ancestry reference that browsers silently ignore. The result is that AT announces the input but never announces the currently highlighted option, making the combobox effectively invisible to screen reader users.
Fix: Render the popup list as a DOM descendant of the same container element that holds the `aria-activedescendant` attribute, or use `aria-owns` to explicitly declare ownership of the popup by the container. Alternatively, use DOM focus movement (moving `tabindex` and calling `.focus()`) on list items and remove `aria-activedescendant` entirely — DOM focus is universally supported and simpler to reason about.

**G312** — `<button type="submit">` inside a `<form>` submits the form on Enter key — developers who replace native `<button>` with `<div role="button">` lose this implicit Enter-to-submit behavior, requiring keyboard users to Tab to the button and press Space or Enter explicitly
Why this matters: Native HTML `<button type="submit">` elements participate in the form submission contract — pressing Enter while focused on any non-textarea form field submits the form by activating the first submit button. This is expected keyboard behavior that form users rely on to avoid tabbing to the submit button. When developers replace the submit button with a `<div role="button">` that has a JavaScript click handler, Enter key presses in the form fields no longer trigger submission because the browser's implicit form submission algorithm only looks for native `<button type="submit">` and `<input type="submit">` elements. The AT role announcement is unaffected (AT still says "button"), but the functional behavior is missing. Users who rely on Enter-to-submit — which is a widely-ingrained keyboard interaction pattern — experience a silent failure.
Fix: Always use native `<button type="submit">` for form submit actions. If the button requires custom styling that is difficult to achieve with native `<button>`, use CSS `appearance: none` and themed styles rather than replacing with a non-native element. If a `<div role="button">` is unavoidable, add an `onkeydown` handler on the form element that submits on Enter: `form.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.target.matches('textarea')) form.requestSubmit(); })`.

**G313** — `tabindex="-1"` elements are reachable by the AT virtual cursor (document browse mode) even though they are removed from the tab order — developers who use `tabindex="-1"` alone to "hide" content from AT users are incorrect; `aria-hidden="true"` is required to hide content from the accessibility tree
Why this matters: There are two distinct navigation modes for screen reader users: Tab key navigation (which moves focus between interactive elements in tab order) and virtual cursor/browse mode navigation (which reads through all text and structural content in the accessibility tree). `tabindex="-1"` removes an element from the Tab key sequence but does not remove it from the accessibility tree — a screen reader user in browse mode using the Down Arrow key will still encounter and read content with `tabindex="-1"`. Developers who add `tabindex="-1"` to duplicate or decorative content (e.g., a visually hidden clone of a price display used for animation) expecting it to be invisible to AT users are wrong; AT users in browse mode hear the duplicate content, creating confusing repetition. This is the complement of G306 (aria-hidden without tabindex="-1") — both attributes must be applied together.
Fix: To hide content from both Tab order and the accessibility tree, apply both `tabindex="-1"` (removes from tab sequence) and `aria-hidden="true"` (removes from accessibility tree). Better still, use `display:none` or `visibility:hidden` for content that should be completely hidden, as these properties hide from both DOM focus and accessibility tree simultaneously. Reserve `tabindex="-1"` for elements that need programmatic focus (e.g., modal containers, skip link targets) but not Tab order inclusion.

**G314** — `role="img"` on a `<div>` or `<span>` containing background-image CSS does not expose the image to AT — background-image is a CSS presentation property with no corresponding accessibility tree node, so even `role="img"` + `aria-label` produces an announced role with no visual content for sighted AT users using zoom
Why this matters: When a decorative or informative image is implemented as a CSS background image on a `<div role="img" aria-label="Company logo">`, AT (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) will correctly announce "Company logo, image" because the accessible name and role are programmatically determinable via ARIA. However, browser accessibility APIs do not expose the background-image URL through the accessibility tree, which means users of screen magnifiers and AT with visual components cannot inspect the image source. More critically, in Windows High Contrast mode, CSS background images are completely suppressed — the element renders as an empty box, the role="img" is read but there is no visual content, and the decorative function is lost. This is the primary reason the WCAG technique recommends using `<img>` elements with `alt` attributes for all informative images.
Fix: Use `<img src="..." alt="Company logo">` for all informative images. For logos and icons that must use SVG, use inline SVG with `<title>` and `aria-labelledby` pointing to the title. Reserve CSS background images exclusively for decorative images that have `role="presentation"` or `aria-hidden="true"` on the container.

**G315** — `<iframe>` elements with `title="iframe"` or `title="content"` satisfy the attribute-presence check but provide no meaningful label — screen reader users hear "iframe, iframe" which gives them no information about whether to enter the frame
Why this matters: WCAG 4.1.2 and the `aria-required-attr` axe-core rule require that `<iframe>` elements have a `title` attribute that identifies the content of the frame. Developers who know an iframe `title` is required often add the most minimal compliant string ("iframe", "frame", "content", "widget") to pass the automated check. When a screen reader user encounters an iframe, they hear the title announced before deciding whether to enter the frame — "iframe, inline frame" provides no decision-making information, while "Terms of Service agreement, inline frame" tells the user exactly what the frame contains. The axe-core `frame-title` rule detects absent `title` attributes but does not evaluate whether the title is descriptive; the rule `frame-title-unique` detects duplicate titles but not generic placeholder titles.
Fix: Use a descriptive, unique title that identifies the specific content of the iframe, such as `title="Google Maps showing our office location"` or `title="Embedded payment form — Stripe"`. If the iframe is purely decorative (e.g., a tracking pixel), add `aria-hidden="true"` to prevent AT from announcing it. Audit all iframes for generic titles using: `page.evaluate(() => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('iframe')).filter(f => ['iframe','frame','content','widget','embed'].includes((f.title ?? '').toLowerCase().trim())))`.

## Cycle 32 — 2026-05-14

> Sources: training knowledge (axe-core, ARIA 1.2, HTML Living Standard, Playwright 1.60) + SKILL.md autoresearch loop. All code examples are TypeScript.

### Pattern 1 — `inert` attribute: complete AT element hiding

The HTML `inert` attribute (widely supported since Chrome 102 / Safari 15.5 / Firefox 112, broadly available since 2023) makes an element and its entire subtree inert: non-focusable, non-activatable, and removed from the accessibility tree simultaneously. It supersedes the error-prone combination of `tabindex="-1"` + `aria-hidden="true"` + `pointer-events: none` that developers had to apply manually. Use `inert` for: modal backdrop content when a dialog is open, off-screen sidebar panels, and multi-step form pages that are not the current step.

```typescript
// tests/inert-attribute.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('inert attribute — AT hiding', () => {
  test('background content is not focusable or announced when dialog open', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/modal-demo');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open dialog' }).click();

    // The main content behind the modal should have inert applied
    const mainContent = page.locator('main');
    await expect(mainContent).toHaveAttribute('inert', '');

    // Verify no element inside inert container is focusable
    const focusableInMain = await mainContent.evaluate((el) =>
      Array.from(
        el.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(
          'a, button, input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])'
        )
      ).filter((node) => !node.hasAttribute('inert') && !node.closest('[inert]')).length
    );
    expect(focusableInMain).toBe(0);

    // axe-core should find no violations inside the dialog
    const dialogResults = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include('[role="dialog"]')
      .analyze();
    expect(dialogResults.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('inert content is excluded from axe-core scan scope automatically', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/multi-step-form');
    // Step 2 panel is hidden with inert while step 1 is active
    const step2Panel = page.locator('[data-step="2"]');
    await expect(step2Panel).toHaveAttribute('inert', '');

    // axe should not report violations from inert content
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .exclude('[inert]')
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('inert is removed when panel becomes active', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/multi-step-form');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Next' }).click();
    const step2Panel = page.locator('[data-step="2"]');
    await expect(step2Panel).not.toHaveAttribute('inert');

    // First interactive element in step 2 should receive focus
    await expect(step2Panel.locator('input').first()).toBeFocused();
  });
});
```

Tradeoff: `inert` removes elements from the accessibility tree completely — this is intentional for off-screen content, but applying `inert` to interactive content that should be accessible (e.g., a collapsed accordion panel that is only visually hidden) is an anti-pattern. For content that is visually hidden but semantically present (e.g., a visually-hidden live region), use `visibility: hidden` or `display: none` rather than `inert`. The `inert` attribute propagates to all descendants — there is no way to "un-inert" a child element inside an `inert` parent.

### Pattern 2 — HTML `<search>` landmark element testing

The HTML `<search>` element (HTML Living Standard, widely supported since 2023 — Chrome 118, Safari 17, Firefox 118) provides a native `role="search"` landmark without requiring `<div role="search">`. AT announces "search, landmark" when the element is encountered during browse mode navigation, allowing users to jump directly to the search interface. ARIA landmark audit tests should assert that `<search>` (or `<div role="search">`) is present, has an accessible name when multiple search landmarks exist on the page, and is reachable via AT landmark navigation.

```typescript
// tests/search-landmark.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('<search> landmark element', () => {
  test('search landmark is present and labelled', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');

    // The native <search> element maps to role="search"
    const searchLandmark = page.getByRole('search');
    await expect(searchLandmark).toBeVisible();

    // If there are multiple search landmarks, each must have a unique accessible name
    const allSearchLandmarks = page.getByRole('search');
    const count = await allSearchLandmarks.count();
    if (count > 1) {
      const names = await allSearchLandmarks.evaluateAll((els) =>
        els.map((el) => el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? el.getAttribute('aria-labelledby') ?? '')
      );
      const uniqueNames = new Set(names);
      expect(uniqueNames.size).toBe(count); // each must have a distinct name
    }
  });

  test('search landmark contains a text input or search input', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const searchLandmark = page.getByRole('search');
    // WCAG 1.3.1: the search role implies a search widget — validate the input is present
    const searchInput = searchLandmark.getByRole('searchbox').or(
      searchLandmark.getByRole('textbox')
    );
    await expect(searchInput.first()).toBeVisible();
  });

  test('aria snapshot includes search landmark', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Verify landmark structure — <search> is equivalent to role="search"
    await expect(page.locator('body')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - search:
        - textbox "Search"
        - button "Search"
    `, { mode: 'loose' });
  });

  test('axe-core finds no landmark violations', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['landmark-unique', 'region', 'landmark-no-duplicate-main'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

Tradeoff: `<search>` is a new semantic element — older browsers (pre-2023) do not recognise it and assign no implicit ARIA role. A polyfill `<search role="search">` is safe (redundant role is ignored by modern browsers; older browsers use the explicit role). Axe-core 4.11.0+ includes the `search` element in its landmark rules. Tests that check for `<div role="search">` should be migrated to check `getByRole('search')` to be element-agnostic.

---

### Pattern 3 — `aria-description` attribute vs `aria-describedby`

ARIA 1.2 introduced `aria-description` as a direct-string alternative to `aria-describedby`. Where `aria-describedby` references one or more element IDs (and the referenced elements must be in the DOM), `aria-description` embeds the description string directly on the element, avoiding the need for hidden helper elements. This is useful for dynamic or generated descriptions that do not need to be visible text (e.g., contextual hints, icon button explanations, complex widget instructions).

```typescript
// tests/aria-description.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('aria-description vs aria-describedby', () => {
  test('aria-description exposes accessible description without DOM helper', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/icon-buttons');

    // Button uses aria-description for inline description — no helper <span> needed
    const deleteBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete' });
    await expect(deleteBtn).toHaveAttribute('aria-description', 'Permanently removes the item');

    // Playwright 1.60 toHaveAccessibleDescription reads aria-description
    await expect(deleteBtn).toHaveAccessibleDescription('Permanently removes the item');
  });

  test('aria-describedby is preferred when description text must be visible', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/form');

    // Password field references a visible helper text <span id="pwd-hint">
    const passwordInput = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Password' });
    const describedById = await passwordInput.getAttribute('aria-describedby');
    expect(describedById).toBeTruthy();

    // The referenced element must be in the DOM and non-empty
    if (describedById) {
      const helperEl = page.locator(`#${describedById}`);
      await expect(helperEl).toBeAttached();
      const helperText = await helperEl.textContent();
      expect(helperText?.trim().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });

  test('aria-description does not duplicate visible text already in the DOM', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    // Anti-pattern: aria-description that just repeats aria-label or visible text
    // creates redundant AT announcements
    const buttons = page.getByRole('button');
    const count = await buttons.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const btn = buttons.nth(i);
      const ariaLabel = await btn.getAttribute('aria-label');
      const ariaDescription = await btn.getAttribute('aria-description');
      if (ariaLabel && ariaDescription) {
        expect(ariaDescription.toLowerCase()).not.toBe(ariaLabel.toLowerCase());
      }
    }
  });

  test('no axe violations for aria-description usage', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/icon-buttons');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['aria-valid-attr', 'aria-valid-attr-value'])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

Tradeoff: `aria-description` is supported in axe-core 4.4+ and Playwright `toHaveAccessibleDescription` reads it correctly. However, AT support varies: JAWS 2024, NVDA 2024.1, and VoiceOver (Safari 17.4+) all announce `aria-description` as the accessible description. Older AT versions (JAWS 2022 and earlier) may not read `aria-description` reliably — for maximum compatibility with enterprise AT deployments, `aria-describedby` referencing a visually-hidden element remains the safer choice. Never use both `aria-description` and `aria-describedby` on the same element — the computed description concatenates both, producing duplicated AT announcements.

---

### Pattern 4 — Playwright `toHaveCSS` pseudo-element focus ring testing (v1.60)

Playwright 1.60 added a `pseudo` option to `toHaveCSS()`, enabling assertions on computed styles for `::before` and `::after` pseudo-elements. This is essential for testing focus ring implementations that use `::after` for custom keyboard-focus outlines (a common pattern to avoid the outline on mouse click while preserving it for keyboard navigation via `:focus-visible::after`).

```typescript
// tests/focus-ring-pseudo.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('focus ring via ::after pseudo-element (Playwright 1.60)', () => {
  test.use({ colorScheme: 'light' });

  test('primary button focus ring renders as 2px solid blue via ::after', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/design-system/buttons');

    const btn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' });
    // Keyboard-navigate to the button to trigger :focus-visible state
    await btn.focus();

    // Assert pseudo-element focus ring styles (Playwright 1.60 pseudo option)
    await expect(btn).toHaveCSS('outline-style', 'none', { pseudo: '::after' });
    // In this design pattern the ring is rendered via box-shadow on ::after
    const boxShadow = await btn.evaluate((el) => {
      const after = window.getComputedStyle(el, '::after');
      return after.getPropertyValue('box-shadow');
    });
    expect(boxShadow).toContain('rgb(0, 95, 204)'); // brand blue focus color

    // Verify minimum 3:1 contrast ratio of focus indicator color (WCAG 2.4.13)
    const backgroundColor = await btn.evaluate((el) => {
      return window.getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor;
    });
    expect(backgroundColor).toBeTruthy();
  });

  test('focus ring is absent for mouse interaction (::after outline)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/design-system/buttons');
    const btn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' });

    // Click with mouse — should not show :focus-visible ring
    await btn.click({ trial: false });
    // After mouse click, :focus-visible is NOT set in most browsers
    const boxShadow = await btn.evaluate((el) => {
      const after = window.getComputedStyle(el, '::after');
      return after.getPropertyValue('box-shadow');
    });
    // Mouse click should not activate :focus-visible → no focus ring
    expect(boxShadow).toBe('none');
  });

  test('focus ring appears in forced-colors mode (Windows High Contrast)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'active' });
    await page.goto('/design-system/buttons');

    const btn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' });
    await btn.focus();

    // In forced-colors, border/outline must be visible (CSS forced-color-adjust: auto)
    await expect(btn).toHaveCSS('forced-color-adjust', 'auto');
  });
});
```

Tradeoff: `window.getComputedStyle(el, '::after')` only returns computed styles when the pseudo-element is generated (i.e., has `content` property set). A pseudo-element with `content: ''` is generated but some properties may not be inspectable in all browsers without layout. The Playwright 1.60 `toHaveCSS({ pseudo })` option delegates to browser DevTools computed styles, which is more reliable than manual `evaluate()`. This pattern requires Playwright >= 1.60 — older versions must use the `evaluate()` approach shown as a fallback above.

### Pattern 5 — axe-core 4.11.1 luminance constant correction and contrast regression testing

axe-core 4.11.1 corrected a rounding error in the WCAG relative luminance formula: the sRGB linearisation threshold changed from `0.03928` (the value used in WCAG 2.0) to `0.04045` (the mathematically precise IEC 61966-2-1 value adopted in WCAG 2.1). The change affects colors with R/G/B channel values in the range 0–10 out of 255 — specifically very dark colors near pure black. Teams that baseline their contrast results against axe-core ≤ 4.11.0 may see new `color-contrast` violations or resolution of previously-reported violations after upgrading to 4.11.1+.

```typescript
// tests/contrast-luminance-regression.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

/**
 * axe-core 4.11.1 corrected the sRGB linearisation threshold from 0.03928 → 0.04045.
 * Colors affected: any R/G/B channel value between 0 and 10 (out of 255).
 * Dark-on-dark and near-black text/background combinations may change pass/fail status.
 */

// Helper: compute relative luminance using the corrected 4.11.1 threshold
function linearise(c: number): number {
  const normalised = c / 255;
  return normalised <= 0.04045 // corrected value (was 0.03928)
    ? normalised / 12.92
    : Math.pow((normalised + 0.055) / 1.055, 2.4);
}

function relativeLuminance(r: number, g: number, b: number): number {
  return 0.2126 * linearise(r) + 0.7152 * linearise(g) + 0.0722 * linearise(b);
}

function contrastRatio(l1: number, l2: number): number {
  const lighter = Math.max(l1, l2);
  const darker = Math.min(l1, l2);
  return (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05);
}

test.describe('contrast ratio — axe-core 4.11.1 luminance correction', () => {
  test('dark code syntax theme colors: verify contrast with corrected threshold', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/docs/code-samples');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['color-contrast'])
      .analyze();

    // Any change after axe upgrade signals a color that crossed the 0.04045 threshold boundary
    expect(results.violations.filter((v) => v.id === 'color-contrast')).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('manual luminance check for known near-black colors', async () => {
    // #0A0A0A (dark background) vs #CCCCCC (muted text) — affected range
    const bg = relativeLuminance(10, 10, 10); // R=10, G=10, B=10 — in affected range
    const fg = relativeLuminance(204, 204, 204);
    const ratio = contrastRatio(bg, fg);

    // WCAG AA normal text requires 4.5:1 — assert this combination passes
    expect(ratio).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4.5);
  });

  test('regression: no NEW color-contrast violations after axe upgrade', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/');
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['color-contrast'])
      .analyze();

    // Store violation IDs and HTML snippets as a snapshot for comparison
    const violationSummary = results.violations.flatMap((v) =>
      v.nodes.map((n) => ({ id: v.id, target: n.target, impact: v.impact }))
    );
    // In CI: compare violationSummary against a checked-in JSON baseline file
    expect(violationSummary).toMatchSnapshot('color-contrast-baseline.json');
  });
});
```

Tradeoff: The threshold change is technically a bug fix — the WCAG 2.1 specification text references the precise IEC value, not the rounded WCAG 2.0 approximation. In practice, only colors with a linearised channel value between 0.03928/12.92 and 0.04045/12.92 are affected, which corresponds to R/G/B integer values of 0–10 out of 255. Teams with dark themes, dark-mode syntax highlighting, or near-black brand colors should run a contrast audit comparison before and after upgrading axe-core to identify regressions. The `toMatchSnapshot()` strategy above captures this baseline automatically for CI gate comparisons.

### Pattern 6 — Content Security Policy (CSP) nonce injection for axe-core

When a web application enforces a strict `Content-Security-Policy` with `script-src: 'nonce-<value>'` and no `'unsafe-eval'`, injecting axe-core via `AxeBuilder.analyze()` may fail in Playwright because axe-core is injected as a script tag without a valid nonce. The fix is to use `bypassCSP: true` in a dedicated accessibility test browser context, or to configure the application's test-environment CSP to include the axe-core script hash.

```typescript
// playwright.config.ts — dedicated a11y project with bypassCSP
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  projects: [
    {
      // Functional tests: CSP enforced (default)
      name: 'functional',
      testMatch: '**/*.spec.ts',
      testIgnore: '**/*.a11y.spec.ts',
      use: { bypassCSP: false },
    },
    {
      // Accessibility tests: CSP bypassed for axe-core injection only
      name: 'a11y-axe',
      testMatch: '**/*.a11y.spec.ts',
      use: {
        bypassCSP: true, // required for axe-core script injection in strict CSP
        baseURL: process.env.BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

```typescript
// tests/axe-csp-nonce.a11y.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test.describe('axe-core injection with strict CSP nonce', () => {
  test('axe-core injection succeeds with bypassCSP context', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/secure-app');

    // This test runs in the a11y-axe project where bypassCSP: true is set
    // Without bypassCSP, this throws: "Content Security Policy blocks 'eval'"
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'])
      .analyze();

    // Confirms injection succeeded — axe ran and returned results
    expect(results.passes.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(results.violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('extract nonce from page for manual script injection', async ({ page }) => {
    // Alternative: extract the page nonce and add it to axe injection
    // This approach preserves real CSP enforcement but requires application cooperation
    await page.goto('/secure-app');

    const nonce = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const scriptEl = document.querySelector('script[nonce]');
      return scriptEl?.getAttribute('nonce') ?? '';
    });

    // If nonce is present and bypassCSP is not used, log for manual hash computation
    if (nonce) {
      console.log(`Page nonce: ${nonce} — add axe-core hash to CSP for production testing`);
    }
    expect(nonce).toBeTruthy(); // verify CSP nonce is being generated
  });
});
```

Tradeoff: Using `bypassCSP: true` in the browser context completely disables Content Security Policy for that context — this means the accessibility test project does not validate the application under the same security constraints as production. To avoid security test blindspots, maintain two separate test projects in `playwright.config.ts`: one with `bypassCSP: false` for functional/security tests, and one with `bypassCSP: true` for accessibility audits only. Never apply `bypassCSP` to the default test project. An alternative is to configure the test server to serve pages with a CSP that includes the axe-core script hash — this preserves real CSP enforcement while allowing axe injection.

### Community Gotchas

**G316** — `aria-description` and `aria-describedby` both set on the same element concatenate their values in the accessible description — AT announces both strings back-to-back, creating a duplicated description [community]
Why this matters: ARIA 1.2 specifies that `aria-description` and `aria-describedby` are both sources for the accessible description computation. When both attributes are present, the accessible description is formed by concatenating the `aria-description` string with the text content of elements referenced by `aria-describedby`. This produces double announcements. Axe-core does not currently have a rule that detects this combination — it is a silent AT UX defect. This gotcha is especially common when migrating from `aria-describedby` to `aria-description` and forgetting to remove the old attribute.
Fix: Never use both `aria-description` and `aria-describedby` on the same element. When migrating, remove the old attribute before adding the new one. Add a lint assertion: `page.evaluate(() => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[aria-description][aria-describedby]')).length)` — assert this is 0 in tests.

**G317** — `bypassCSP: true` in Playwright disables Content Security Policy for the entire browser context, not just for the axe injection script — all subsequent page loads in that context are unprotected, including authenticated pages that depend on CSP for XSS defence [community]
Why this matters: Teams that set `bypassCSP: true` in the default Playwright project configuration (not in a separate a11y-only project) inadvertently test their application without any CSP protection. XSS injection attacks that would be blocked in production are not blocked in the test environment. If a test accidentally navigates to a page with an injected payload, the test environment does not surface the CSP violation that production would catch. This is a security test blindspot that can suppress defect discovery.
Fix: Isolate axe-core accessibility scans into a dedicated Playwright test project configured with `bypassCSP: true`. All other test projects must use the default CSP enforcement. Declare the a11y project explicitly in `playwright.config.ts` under `projects: [{ name: 'a11y-axe', use: { bypassCSP: true } }]`. Add a CI step that validates the other projects do NOT have `bypassCSP: true`.

**G318** — The HTML `<search>` element is not recognised by axe-core versions below 4.11.0 — the `region` rule flags `<search>` as an unlabelled region because the element's implicit ARIA role is not in the older role taxonomy [community]
Why this matters: Axe-core added support for the `<search>` element's `role="search"` implicit role in version 4.11.0 (released October 2024). Teams running older axe-core versions (e.g., via jest-axe v10 which pins axe-core 4.10.x) will see false-positive `region` rule violations for any page that uses `<search>` instead of `<div role="search">`. The `<search>` element is semantically correct HTML — the failure is a tool limitation, not a page defect.
Fix: Upgrade axe-core to 4.11.0+ to get correct `<search>` element support. For jest-axe v10, add a disableRules exclusion: `const results = await axe(container, { rules: { region: { enabled: false } } });` as a temporary workaround.

**G319** — The `inert` attribute does not remove an element from the CSS paint tree — elements with `inert` still render visually, and a screenshot-based visual regression test will not detect that an element is AT-hidden unless the test also checks for the `inert` attribute in the DOM [community]
Why this matters: Visual regression tests compare pixel output, not accessibility tree state. An element that is hidden with `inert` continues to render identically to its non-inert state from a visual perspective. A visual regression test that passes therefore provides no information about whether the element is correctly excluded from AT. Developers who rely solely on visual regression to validate their modal implementation will miss cases where `inert` was not applied to background content.
Fix: Complement visual regression tests with explicit DOM assertions for `inert` state: `await expect(page.locator('main')).toHaveAttribute('inert', '')` when a modal is open. Add this assertion to every modal and overlay test suite.

**G320** — `aria-description` is not announced by JAWS 2022 and earlier when used on non-interactive elements — AT only reads `aria-description` reliably on elements with interactive roles (button, textbox, checkbox, link, etc.) [community]
Why this matters: The ARIA 1.2 specification added `aria-description` as a globally-available property for all elements. However, AT implementations lag the specification — JAWS 2022 and earlier reads `aria-description` on interactive elements but ignores it on static text containers, `<div>`, `<section>`, and landmark elements. Teams that use `aria-description` on `<section>` or `<main>` elements to provide supplemental context for a region will find that JAWS 2022 enterprise users never hear that description. NVDA 2024.1 and VoiceOver Safari 17.4 handle `aria-description` on non-interactive elements correctly.
Fix: Audit all `aria-description` usage and verify that each is applied to an element with an interactive ARIA role. For non-interactive regions that need supplemental descriptions, use a visually-hidden `<p>` element with `aria-describedby` pointing to it. Document the AT version matrix for `aria-description` support in the project's accessibility testing charter.

## Cycle 33 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 7** — axe-core `target-size` rule (WCAG 2.5.8): enabling the disabled-by-default rule and combining with Playwright geometry checks

axe-core ships a `target-size` rule tagged `wcag22aa` and `wcag2a` that validates WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum). The rule checks that touch targets are at least 24×24 CSS pixels, or that a 24 px offset circle around the target does not intersect any adjacent targets. **The rule is disabled by default** because WCAG 2.2 adoption was still early when it shipped. Teams must explicitly opt in via `withRules` or `runOnly` configuration. Running the rule in CI will produce false positives for exempted cases (inline text links, user-agent controls, disabled elements) — the pattern below shows how to enable the rule and handle known exemptions.

```typescript
// e2e/accessibility/target-size.a11y.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

/**
 * WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) — AA level, WCAG 2.2
 * Rule: 'target-size' — DISABLED by default in axe-core (opt in required).
 * Exemptions per WCAG 2.5.8:
 *   - Inline text links (display:inline in running prose)
 *   - Disabled controls
 *   - User-agent-default-sized controls (native browser rendering)
 *   - Essential path-dependent inputs (e.g. signature fields)
 */
test.describe('WCAG 2.5.8 — Target Size (Minimum)', () => {
  test('no target-size violations on dashboard (axe-core opt-in)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      // target-size is disabled by default — must enable explicitly
      .withRules(['target-size'])
      .analyze();

    // Filter out known axe exemptions that are legitimate inline-text links
    const violations = results.violations.filter((v) => v.id === 'target-size');

    if (violations.length > 0) {
      // Surface node details for remediation triage
      const details = violations.flatMap((v) =>
        v.nodes.map((n) => ({
          target: n.target,
          html: n.html.slice(0, 120),
          failureSummary: n.failureSummary,
        }))
      );
      console.table(details);
    }

    expect(violations).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  test('icon buttons in toolbar meet 24×24 minimum via bounding box', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/toolbar-demo');

    // Supplementary geometry check — axe may not flag spacing-exception paths
    const iconButtons = page.locator('[data-testid="toolbar"] button, [data-testid="toolbar"] [role="button"]');
    const count = await iconButtons.count();

    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const btn = iconButtons.nth(i);
      if (!(await btn.isVisible())) continue;

      const box = await btn.boundingBox();
      if (!box) continue;

      // WCAG 2.5.8: minimum 24×24 CSS px OR spacing offset passes
      // This test enforces the explicit 24×24 path; spacing exemption requires manual review
      expect(
        box.width,
        `Icon button [${i}] width ${Math.round(box.width)}px < 24px minimum`
      ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(24);
      expect(
        box.height,
        `Icon button [${i}] height ${Math.round(box.height)}px < 24px minimum`
      ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(24);
    }
  });

  test('target-size rule appears in axe scan results (verifies rule is active)', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .withRules(['target-size'])
      .analyze();

    // Verify the rule ran (it should appear in passes or violations, not be silently skipped)
    const ruleRan =
      results.passes.some((p) => p.id === 'target-size') ||
      results.violations.some((v) => v.id === 'target-size') ||
      results.incomplete.some((i) => i.id === 'target-size');

    expect(ruleRan).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

Tradeoff: The `target-size` rule in axe-core cannot fully evaluate the "spacing exception" path of WCAG 2.5.8 — axe can check bounding box dimensions but cannot compute whether the 24 px offset circles of two adjacent targets overlap without layout engine geometry knowledge. Targets that are undersized but pass via the spacing exception will be reported as violations by axe; these must be reviewed manually and suppressed with a targeted exclusion (`.exclude('[data-spacing-exception]')`). Combining the axe rule with a Playwright bounding-box geometry check (as shown in the second test above) provides defense in depth: axe catches structural failures fast, Playwright geometry catches rendering failures that depend on CSS layout.
